  a document from HTML (see rich_html.rs); a fragment of a richtext's clipboard is
  taken exactly

#### `ui/rich_edit.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/rich_edit.rs`](../lib/ui/rich_edit.rs)

```text
rich_edit -- ui.richtext: a rich-text editor over a RichDoc (rich_doc.rs), and its toolbar

  ui.richtext(id, &mut doc, RT_*) -> EV_*   the editor, filling the place it gets (natural
       480 x 240 DIP; next_size(-1, -1) fills): the paragraphs wrapped at the width
       (text::segment line breaks, grapheme clusters inside a word too long), runs in their
       fonts (bold / italic: the family's faces, else synthetic), colours, highlight,
       underline / strike, links in the accent colour, alignment (justify spreads the
       blanks), bulleted / numbered lists by level, headings, quotations; a scroll bar.
       EV_ACT: the content changed this frame; EV_FOCUS while focused; EV_COMMIT: the focus
       left.  Ids id .. id + 5 (id + 1 the scroll bar, id + 2 .. 5 the link flyout).
       RT_READONLY: select and copy only (a click opens a link); RT_NO_FRAME: no box;
       RT_OPEN_LINKS: the editor opens an activated link with open_url itself; RT_TAB: Tab
       outside a list inserts a tab (else Tab moves the focus on); RT_PLAIN_PASTE: paste
       only text.
  ui.richtext_toolbar(id, editor, &mut doc, RTB_*) -> EV_ACT when it changed doc
       undo / redo, paragraph style, font family (registered families: font_register),
       size, bold / italic / underline / strike, text and highlight colour, link, alignment,
       lists, indent, clear format; the buttons show the state at the caret and give the
       focus back to the editor (ids id .. id + 149)
  ui.richtext_link(id) -> Option<String>   a link the user activated (Ctrl+click, a click
       when read-only, Ctrl+Enter on it), taken once
  ui.richtext_link_dialog(id)              open the editor's link flyout (as Ctrl+K)

Keys (besides those of ed_core.rs): Ctrl+B / I / U bold, italic, underline, Ctrl+Shift+X
strike, Ctrl+Space clear format, Ctrl+K link, Ctrl+L / E / R / J alignment, Ctrl+Shift+8 /
Ctrl+Shift+L bullets, Ctrl+Shift+7 numbers, Ctrl+1 / 2 / 3 headings, Ctrl+0 body text,
Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ size up / down, Tab / Shift+Tab a list level in / out, Enter a new
paragraph (in an empty list item: the list ends), Backspace at the start of a list item:
the item becomes body text, Ctrl+Shift+V paste text only, Esc drops the focus.  With no
selection a format applies to what is typed next.
Clipboard: CLIP_TEXT (list markers when several paragraphs are copied) and CLIP_HTML
(rich_html.rs: HTML with the exact fragment as JSON in a comment); a paste takes HTML when
there is some (any program's), else the text.  Undo: the document's History (rich_doc.rs).
Accessibility: a K_TEXTBOX record (label: the text, value / max: caret / anchor as byte
offsets into it) as text boxes have, a K_LINK record per visible link; the caret goes to
ime_pos (IME, magnifiers); the editor takes the text boxes' edit state while focused
(ed_hold), so a screen reader can select.  Right-to-left the text keeps its order (as in
text boxes); bidirectional reordering inside a paragraph is not done.

Layout: a paragraph is laid out once per version (Para::version, its attributes, the
width, dpi, text scale and document font); the rows are cached per editor.  Only the
visible paragraphs are drawn.
```

```rust
/// richtext flags: select and copy only
RT_READONLY: u32 = 1
/// no text box frame
RT_NO_FRAME: u32 = 2
/// the editor opens activated links itself (open_url)
RT_OPEN_LINKS: u32 = 4
/// Tab outside a list inserts a tab
RT_TAB: u32 = 8
/// a paste takes only the text
RT_PLAIN_PASTE: u32 = 16
/// richtext_toolbar groups: undo / redo
RTB_HISTORY: u32 = 1
/// paragraph style, font family, size
RTB_STYLE: u32 = 2
/// bold, italic, underline, strike
RTB_CHARS: u32 = 4
/// text and highlight colour
RTB_COLOR: u32 = 8
/// link
RTB_LINK: u32 = 16
/// alignment
RTB_ALIGN: u32 = 32
/// lists and indent
RTB_LISTS: u32 = 64
/// clear format
RTB_CLEAR: u32 = 128
/// every group
RTB_ALL: u32 = 255
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn richtext(&mut self, id: u32, doc: &mut RichDoc, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  ui_richtext(id, doc, RT_\*) -> EV_\* (see the module header)
- **`fn richtext_link(&mut self, id: u32) -> Option<String>`**
  a link the user activated in richtext `id` (Ctrl+click, a click when read-only,
  Ctrl+Enter), taken once
- **`fn richtext_link_dialog(&mut self, id: u32, doc: &RichDoc)`**
  open the link flyout of richtext `id` (as Ctrl+K does): the url of the link at the
  caret or "https://"; OK sets it on the selection (without one: inserts it as linked
  text), "Entfernen" removes the link
- **`fn richtext_toolbar(&mut self, id: u32, editor: u32, doc: &mut RichDoc, groups: u32) -> u32`**
  ui_richtext_toolbar(id, editor, doc, RTB_\*) -> EV_ACT when it changed doc (see the
  module header)

#### `ui/code_doc.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/code_doc.rs`](../lib/ui/code_doc.rs)

```text
code_doc -- the document of ui.code_editor: lines of text, the selection, undo (ui::History),
the indentation settings and the edits of a code editor

  CodeDoc::new() / from_text(s)       ('\r\n', '\r' and '\n' end lines)
  doc.text() / line_count() / line(i) / lines() / selection() / set_selection(sel)
  doc.revision()                      counts content changes (edits, undo, redo)
  edits (each one undoable step; typing and repeated Backspace / Delete merge):
    replace(a, b, s) / insert(s) / delete(a, b) / newline(openers) (auto-indent: the line's
    indentation, one level more after an opener, a closer right of the caret on a line of
    its own) / type_text(s) (a closer typed on a blank line goes one level out) / indent(delta)
    (block indent / unindent of the selected lines) / tab() / back_tab() /
    toggle_comment(prefix) / replace_all(q, rep, FIND_*) / replace_next(q, rep, FIND_*)
  find: find_all(q, FIND_*) / find_next(from, q, FIND_*, backwards) (FIND_CASE matches the
    case, FIND_WORD whole words)
  doc.undo() / redo() / can_undo() / can_redo() / undo_label() / is_dirty() / mark_saved()
  tab_width (1..16, default 4), use_tabs (indent with tabs instead of blanks)
  col_of(line, byte) / byte_at_col(line, col)   visual columns (tabs to the next stop,
  wide East Asian characters two)
  diagnostics (a checker's or compiler's messages, drawn by the editor):
    set_diagnostics(&[Diag]) / clear_diagnostics() / diagnostics() -> Vec<Diag> /
    diagnostic(i) / diagnostic_count() / diagnostic_counts() -> [errors, warnings, infos] /
    diagnostics_at(pos) (most severe first) / next_diagnostic(pos, back) (wrapping)

An edit replaces a range of whole lines (LineEdit: old and new lines, the selection before
and after); each change is also kept in a short journal (changes_since) that the editor's
highlighting states and the find results follow without starting again from the top.

Diagnostics follow every change of the text (edits, undo, redo) until the app sets new
ones: when lines change, the old and new lines are compared -- the same number of lines
line by line (one line moved by Alt+Up / Down: as a move), else as one replaced part from
the first to the last difference.  Text before a change keeps its positions, text after it
shifts; a diagnostic whose text was replaced shrinks to what is left of it and is dropped
when nothing is (one that marks a point stays at the change).  Typed text at a diagnostic's
edge stays outside it.  So squiggles stay under their words while the user types, until
the next check replaces them.
```

```rust
/// find: match the case
FIND_CASE: u8 = 1
/// find: whole words only
FIND_WORD: u8 = 2
/// find_all stops after this many matches
FIND_MAX: usize = 100_000
```

- **`struct LineChange`**
  a change of the lines: first .. first + old became first .. first + new (at revision rev)
  - `rev: u64`
  - `first: usize`
  - `old: usize`
  - `new: usize`

```rust
/// Diag::severity: an error
DIAG_ERROR: u8 = 0
/// a warning
DIAG_WARNING: u8 = 1
/// a note, a hint (higher values count as this too)
DIAG_INFO: u8 = 2
```

- **`struct Diag`**
  a diagnostic of a code editor: a part of the text in lines and columns from 1 as compilers
  report them (columns count characters, a tab is one; the end is exclusive, an end at or
  before the start marks the one character at the start, past a line's end the end of the
  line), a severity DIAG_\* and the message (see the module header)
  - `line: usize` -- where it starts (from 1)
  - `col: usize`
  - `end_line: usize` -- where it ends (exclusive)
  - `end_col: usize`
  - `severity: u8` -- DIAG_ERROR, DIAG_WARNING, DIAG_INFO
  - `msg: String`

**`impl Diag`**

- **`fn new(line: usize, col: usize, end_col: usize, severity: u8, msg: &str) -> Diag`**
  a part of one line: line:col .. line:end_col
- **`fn span(line: usize, col: usize, end_line: usize, end_col: usize, severity: u8, msg: &str) -> Diag`**
  line:col .. end_line:end_col

- **`struct CodeDoc`**
  the document of ui.code_editor (see the module header)
  - `tab_width: u8` -- columns between tab stops (1..16)
  - `use_tabs: bool` -- indent with tabs (else with blanks)

**`impl CodeDoc`**

- **`fn new() -> CodeDoc`**
  one empty line
- **`fn from_text(s: &str) -> CodeDoc`**
  a text: a line per '\\n' ('\\r\\n' and '\\r' too)

  lines (an empty list: one empty line); they must not hold '\\n'
- **`fn text(&self) -> String`**
  the text: the lines joined by '\\n'
- **`fn line_count(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of lines (at least 1)
- **`fn line(&self, i: usize) -> &str`**
  line i (clamped to the last one), without its '\\n'
- **`fn lines(&self) -> &[String]`**
  every line
- **`fn revision(&self) -> u64`**
  counts the content changes (edits, undo, redo)
- **`fn changes_since(&self, rev: u64) -> Option<&[LineChange]>`**
  the changes after revision rev, oldest first (None: the journal no longer reaches back
  that far -- start again)
- **`fn selection(&self) -> TextSel`**
  the selection (the caret: anchor == caret)
- **`fn set_selection(&mut self, sel: TextSel)`**
  move the selection (clamped, not undoable)
- **`fn clamp(&self, p: TextPos) -> TextPos`**
  p inside the document, on a character boundary
- **`fn end(&self) -> TextPos`**
  the end of the document
- **`fn text_range(&self, a: TextPos, b: TextPos) -> String`**
  the text between a and b
- **`fn selected_text(&self) -> String`**
  the selected text (lines joined by '\\n')
- **`fn flat(&self, p: TextPos) -> usize`**
  the byte offset of p in text()
- **`fn unflat(&self, f: usize) -> TextPos`**
  the position of byte offset f of text()
- **`fn col_of(&self, line: usize, byte: usize) -> usize`**
  the visual column of byte in a line (tabs to the next stop, wide characters 2)
- **`fn byte_at_col(&self, line: usize, col: usize) -> usize`**
  the byte of the cluster boundary nearest to column col
- **`fn can_undo(&self) -> bool`**
  there is a step to undo
- **`fn can_redo(&self) -> bool`**
  there is a step to redo
- **`fn undo_label(&self) -> Option<&str>`**
  the label of the step undo takes back
- **`fn redo_label(&self) -> Option<&str>`**
  the label of the step redo does again
- **`fn undo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  take the last step back -> false: nothing to undo
- **`fn redo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  do the last undone step again -> false: nothing to redo
- **`fn is_dirty(&self) -> bool`**
  the content differs from the state of the last mark_saved
- **`fn mark_saved(&mut self)`**
  the content is saved now
- **`fn clear_history(&mut self)`**
  forget the undo steps
- **`fn replace(&mut self, a: TextPos, b: TextPos, s: &str) -> TextPos`**
  replace a..b by s; the caret after it -> the end of s
- **`fn insert(&mut self, s: &str) -> TextPos`**
  replace the selection by s (a paste)
- **`fn delete(&mut self, a: TextPos, b: TextPos) -> bool`**
  remove a..b
- **`fn indentation(&self, line: usize) -> &str`**
  the leading blanks of a line
- **`fn indent_unit(&self) -> String`**
  one level of indentation (a tab or tab_width blanks)
- **`fn type_text(&mut self, s: &str, closers: &str) -> bool`**
  typed text replaces the selection; a closer of `closers` typed as the first character
  of a blank line takes one level of indentation away
- **`fn newline(&mut self, openers: &str) -> bool`**
  Enter: a line break with the line's indentation; after an opener of `openers` (the
  last non-blank character before the caret) one level more, and when its closer follows
  the caret, that goes to a line of its own
- **`fn tab(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Tab: the selected lines one level in (several lines selected), else the indentation
  up to the next tab stop at the caret (replacing the selection)
- **`fn back_tab(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Shift+Tab: the selected lines (or the caret's) one level out
- **`fn indent(&mut self, delta: i32) -> bool`**
  the selected lines (a selection ending at a line start leaves that line out) one level
  in (delta > 0) or out; the selection follows its text
- **`fn toggle_comment(&mut self, prefix: &str) -> bool`**
  line comments on (when not every selected non-blank line has one) or off
- **`fn move_lines(&mut self, delta: i32) -> bool`**
  Alt+Up / Alt+Down: the selected lines move one line up (delta &lt; 0) or down
- **`fn find_all(&self, q: &str, opts: u8) -> Vec<(TextPos, TextPos)>`**
  every match of q (FIND_CASE, FIND_WORD), at most FIND_MAX
- **`fn find_lines(&self, q: &str, opts: u8, first: usize, n: usize) -> Vec<(TextPos, TextPos)>`**
  the matches of q in lines first .. first + n
- **`fn find_next(&self, from: TextPos, q: &str, opts: u8, backwards: bool) -> Option<(TextPos, TextPos)>`**
  the next match after `from` (backwards: the last one before it), wrapping around
- **`fn sel_is_match(&self, q: &str, opts: u8) -> bool`**
  the selection is a match of q
- **`fn replace_next(&mut self, q: &str, rep: &str, opts: u8) -> bool`**
  replace the selection when it is a match, then select the next match -> replaced
- **`fn replace_all(&mut self, q: &str, rep: &str, opts: u8) -> usize`**
  replace every match (one undo step) -> how many
- **`fn set_diagnostics(&mut self, d: &[Diag])`**
  replace the diagnostics (Diag positions, clamped to the text); from now on they follow
  the edits until the next call (see the module header)
- **`fn clear_diagnostics(&mut self)`**
  no diagnostics
- **`fn diagnostics(&self) -> Vec<Diag>`**
  the diagnostics where they are now, by position
- **`fn diagnostic_count(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of diagnostics
- **`fn diagnostic(&self, i: usize) -> Option<Diag>`**
  diagnostic i (0 .. diagnostic_count(), by position) where it is now
- **`fn diagnostic_counts(&self) -> [usize; 3]`**
  the number of errors, warnings and infos (DIAG_\* order)
- **`fn diagnostics_at(&self, p: TextPos) -> Vec<Diag>`**
  the diagnostics at p (their part holds p, its end included; a point: its character),
  most severe first
- **`fn next_diagnostic(&self, p: TextPos, back: bool) -> Option<TextPos>`**
  the start of the first diagnostic after p (back: the last one before p), round the end
  of the text; None without diagnostics

#### `ui/highlight.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/highlight.rs`](../lib/ui/highlight.rs)

```text
highlight -- syntax highlighting for ui.code_editor: a small engine of token rules, the
built-in grammars (Rust, JSON, INI, TOML, a Markdown subset, JFS: the scripts of
lib/script) and the colours of the tokens

  Highlighter::rust() / json() / ini() / toml() / markdown() / jfs() / plain()
  Highlighter::for_name(s)            by name or file extension ("rs", "json", "ini", "cfg",
                                      "toml", "md", "jfs", a path); plain() for anything else
  Highlighter::new(&GRAMMAR)          an app's own grammar (a static Grammar of Rules)
  h.line(text, state, &mut tokens) -> state   the tokens of one line (SY_* kinds, byte
                                      ranges; the plain text between them is SY_TEXT) from
                                      the state the line before ended in; 0 = nothing open
  h.tokens(text) -> Vec<Vec<Token>>   every line of a text (tests)
  CodeTheme::light() / dark() / high_contrast(&HcColors), ui.code_theme()   the colours of
                                      the tokens and the editor (gutter, current line,
                                      selection, bracket match, find matches, diagnostics)

A grammar is a list of rules tried in order at every position: line comments, blocks (from
open to close, nested or not, optionally only at a line start: Markdown fences), strings
(escapes, multi-line or not), strings with code inside (Interp: the ${..} of JFS, whose
code the same rules highlight), Rust raw strings, word lists, numbers, punctuation and
functions of its own (Custom: JSON keys, Rust char literals / lifetimes / attributes, INI
sections and keys, Markdown headings, lists, emphasis and links).  Where no rule matches,
an identifier is read whole: before '(' a function (calls), before '!' a macro (macros),
capitalised a type (caps_types).  A construct still open at a line end is the line's end
state: rule index + 1, the nesting depth (bits 8..15) and a Rust raw string's '#' count
(bits 16..31); the editor keeps a state per line and highlights only the visible lines.
```

```rust
/// token kinds: plain text
SY_TEXT: u8 = 0
/// token kinds: keywords
SY_KEYWORD: u8 = 1
/// types (lists, capitalised names)
SY_TYPE: u8 = 2
/// functions, macros
SY_FUNC: u8 = 3
/// strings, character literals
SY_STRING: u8 = 4
/// numbers, dates
SY_NUMBER: u8 = 5
/// comments, Markdown quotations
SY_COMMENT: u8 = 6
/// true / false / null, enum constants
SY_CONST: u8 = 7
/// operators, brackets, separators
SY_PUNCT: u8 = 8
/// attributes, lifetimes, preprocessor lines
SY_META: u8 = 9
/// JSON / INI / TOML keys
SY_KEY: u8 = 10
/// Markdown headings, INI / TOML sections
SY_HEADING: u8 = 11
/// Markdown *emphasis*
SY_EMPH: u8 = 12
/// Markdown **strong**
SY_STRONG: u8 = 13
/// links, URLs
SY_LINK: u8 = 14
/// Markdown code spans and blocks
SY_CODE: u8 = 15
/// escape sequences in strings
SY_ESCAPE: u8 = 16
/// the number of kinds
SY_COUNT: usize = 17
```

- **`struct Token`**
  a highlighted part of a line: bytes start .. end
  - `start: usize`
  - `end: usize`
  - `kind: u8`

- **`enum Rule`**
  a rule of a grammar (see the module header)
  - `LineComment(&'static str)` -- from the text to the end of the line: a comment
  - `Block { open: &'static str, close: &'static str, kind: u8, nested: bool, bol: bool }` -- from open to close (nested: opens inside count; bol: open and close only at the start
    of a line, after blanks -- the whole line belongs to it); may span lines
  - `Str { open: &'static str, close: &'static str, escape: bool, multi: bool, kind: u8 }` -- a string from open to close; escape: a backslash takes the next character (SY_ESCAPE);
    multi: may span lines
  - `RawStr` -- Rust raw strings: r"..", r#".."#, br".." (may span lines)
  - `Interp { open: &'static str, close: &'static str, start: &'static str }` -- a string with code inside (interpolation), on one line: from open to close, a backslash
    takes the next character (\\u{..} its hex digits and brace; SY_ESCAPE); from `start`
    (ending with '{') to the '}' that closes it (braces inside count) the grammar's rules
    highlight code, the two delimiters SY_META
  - `Words(&'static [&'static str], u8)` -- identifiers of a list
  - `Number` -- number literals: 12, 0x1F, 0b101, 0o17, 1_000, 1.5e-3, suffixes (u8, f32)
  - `Custom(fn(&str, usize, bool) -> Option<(usize, u8)>)` -- a function of its own: (line, position, at the line start after blanks) -> (bytes, kind)
  - `Punct(&'static str)` -- single characters

- **`struct Grammar`**
  a language (see the module header)
  - `name: &'static str`
  - `exts: &'static [&'static str]` -- file extensions (lower case, without the dot)
  - `rules: &'static [Rule]`
  - `ident: &'static str` -- characters inside identifiers besides letters, digits and '_'
  - `calls: bool` -- an identifier before '(' is a function
  - `macros: bool` -- an identifier before '!' is a macro (Rust)
  - `caps_types: bool` -- capitalised identifiers are types
  - `comment: &'static str` -- the line comment of Ctrl+/ ("": none)
  - `openers: &'static str` -- Enter after one of these indents one level more
  - `closers: &'static str` -- one of these typed on a blank line goes one level out
  - `pairs: &'static str` -- the bracket pairs the editor matches: "()[]{}"

- **`struct Highlighter`**
  the highlighter of a grammar (see the module header)

**`impl Highlighter`**

- **`const fn new(g: &'static Grammar) -> Highlighter`**
  an app's own grammar
- **`const fn plain() -> Highlighter`**
  plain text: no tokens
- **`const fn rust() -> Highlighter`**
  Rust
- **`const fn json() -> Highlighter`**
  JSON (and JSONC comments)
- **`const fn ini() -> Highlighter`**
  INI files
- **`const fn toml() -> Highlighter`**
  TOML
- **`const fn markdown() -> Highlighter`**
  a Markdown subset
- **`const fn jfs() -> Highlighter`**
  the scripting language of lib/script (.jfs, JFNetworker's scripts)
- **`fn for_name(s: &str) -> Highlighter`**
  by name or extension, also of a path ("rs", "Rust", "x/y.toml"); plain() for others
- **`fn grammar(&self) -> &'static Grammar`**
  the grammar (comment prefix, openers, closers, bracket pairs)
- **`fn name(&self) -> &'static str`**
  the grammar's name ("Rust", "JSON" ...)
- **`fn line(&self, t: &str, state: u32, out: &mut Vec<Token>) -> u32`**
  the tokens of one line from the state of the line before -> the state at its end
- **`fn tokens(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<Vec<Token>>`**
  the tokens of every line of a text (tests)

- **`static RUST: Grammar`**
  Rust

- **`static JSON: Grammar`**
  JSON (comments of JSONC too)

- **`static INI: Grammar`**
  INI files (; and # comments at a line start, [sections], key = value, key: value)

- **`static TOML: Grammar`**
  TOML

- **`static MARKDOWN: Grammar`**
  a Markdown subset: headings, quotations, rules, lists, fenced code, code spans, emphasis,
  strong, links, escapes, HTML comments

- **`static JFS: Grammar`**
  the scripting language of lib/script (.jfs): calls before '(' are functions, the
  delimiters of ${..} in strings SY_META

- **`static PLAIN: Grammar`**
  plain text: no tokens

- **`struct CodeTheme`**
  the colours of a code editor (0xAARRGGBB); bold / italic: a bit per SY_\* kind
  - `bg: u32`
  - `fg: u32`
  - `gutter_bg: u32`
  - `gutter_fg: u32`
  - `gutter_cur: u32` -- the current line's number
  - `line_hl: u32` -- the current line's background
  - `sel: u32` -- the selection (focused / not focused)
  - `sel_inactive: u32`
  - `sel_text: u32` -- the selected text (0: the tokens keep their colours)
  - `bracket: u32` -- the frame around a matching bracket pair
  - `find: u32` -- the find matches and the current one
  - `find_cur: u32`
  - `find_frame: bool` -- find matches framed instead of filled (high contrast)
  - `caret: u32`
  - `tokens: [u32; SY_COUNT]`
  - `bold: u32`
  - `italic: u32`
  - `diag: [u32; 3]` -- the wavy underlines and gutter markers of errors, warnings and infos (DIAG_\* order)

**`impl CodeTheme`**

- **`fn light() -> CodeTheme`**
  on a light background (the colours of GitHub's light theme)
- **`fn dark() -> CodeTheme`**
  on a dark background (the colours of GitHub's dark theme)
- **`fn high_contrast(c: &plat::HcColors) -> CodeTheme`**
  the colours of a high-contrast scheme: few colours, keywords and headings bold;
  diagnostics in the text, link and highlight colours (the gutter markers' shapes tell
  them apart too)

**`impl crate::Ui`**

- **`fn code_theme(&self) -> CodeTheme`**
  the code editors' colours for the UI's theme: dark / light syntax colours on the UI's
  text box colours (accent selection, diagnostics in its critical / warning / info
  colours), or the high-contrast scheme's colours

#### `ui/code_edit.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/code_edit.rs`](../lib/ui/code_edit.rs)

```text
code_edit -- ui.code_editor: a code editor over a CodeDoc (code_doc.rs) with syntax
highlighting (highlight.rs)

  ui.code_editor(id, &mut doc, &hl, CE_*) -> EV_*   the editor, filling the place it gets
       (natural 560 x 320 DIP; next_size(-1, -1) fills): line numbers, the monospace font
       of mono_font_set (else the system's), tabs to tab_width, the current line, the
       bracket pair at the caret, a find / replace bar, scroll bars.  Only the visible lines
       are laid out and highlighted (the editor keeps each line's start state and follows
       the document's change journal), so a file of 100 000 lines scrolls as fast as a
       short one; of a long line only the part in view (code_long.rs keeps the columns and
       tokens of long lines and works them again near an edit only), so typing in a line of
       1 MB is as fast as in a short one.  EV_ACT: the text changed; EV_FOCUS while
       focused; EV_COMMIT: the focus left.  Ids id .. id + 15 (id + 1 / + 2 the scroll bars,
       + 3 .. 13 the find bar).
       CE_READONLY: select, copy and find only; CE_NO_GUTTER: no line numbers;
       CE_NO_FRAME: no box; CE_NO_FIND: no find bar; CE_NO_LINE: no current-line highlight;
       CE_MARKS: the gutter keeps its column of diagnostic markers while there are none
  ui.code_find(id, query, replace)   open the find bar (replace: with the replace row) with
       a query; the editor selects the first match from the caret on
  ui.code_status(id) -> CodeStatus   line and column of the caret (from 1), the matches
       and the current one, the lines tokenized in the last frame, the document's
       diagnostics per severity and the severity of the one at the caret
  ui.code_diag(id) -> Option<Diag>   the (most severe) diagnostic at the caret, its message
  ui.code_theme_set(Some(theme))     the colours of every code editor (None: code_theme())
  ui.code_font_size(pt)              the size of the code editors' font (default 10 pt)

Diagnostics (CodeDoc::set_diagnostics; they follow the edits, code_doc.rs) are wavy
underlines below their text in the colour of their severity (infos below warnings below
errors; a point or the end of a line: one cell) and a marker in the gutter's first column on
the line where one starts (the most severe: a filled circle with a cross, a triangle, an
"i" -- shapes, not only colours, also in high contrast).  The column is there while the
document has diagnostics (CE_MARKS: always, so the text does not move).  The pointer over an
underline or a marker shows the messages as a tooltip ("Fehler: ...", most severe first);
the ones at the caret are in code_status / code_diag and a K_TEXT record at the caret's line
for screen readers (after the editor's record: the app's post-modifiers stay the editor's).
Only the diagnostics of the visible lines are looked at (binary search by position), an
underline is one command however long it is.

Keys (besides those of ed_core.rs): Tab / Shift+Tab indent / unindent (several lines: the
block), Enter a line break with the indentation (one level more after an opener), a closer
typed on a blank line goes one level out, Backspace in leading blanks back to the previous
tab stop, Home toggles between the first non-blank and column 0, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X without a
selection the whole line, Ctrl+/ line comments, Alt+Up / Alt+Down move the lines, Ctrl+Up /
Ctrl+Down scroll, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+H replace, F3 / Shift+F3 (Enter / Shift+Enter in the
find box) the next / previous match, F8 / Shift+F8 the caret to the start of the next /
previous diagnostic (round the end; without diagnostics F8 stays the window's key for the
splitters), Esc closes the find bar (else drops the focus),
Ctrl+Tab (read-only: Tab) moves the focus on.  Mouse: click, drag, Shift+click, double
click a word, a click or drag in the gutter selects lines, the wheel (Shift: sideways).
Accessibility: a K_TEXTBOX record with the text (beyond 64 KB: the visible lines) and the
caret / anchor as byte offsets into it, ime_pos for IME and magnifiers, the edit state of
the text boxes while focused (ed_hold).
```

```rust
/// code_editor flags: select, copy and find only
CE_READONLY: u32 = 1
/// no line numbers
CE_NO_GUTTER: u32 = 2
/// no text box frame
CE_NO_FRAME: u32 = 4
/// no find bar
CE_NO_FIND: u32 = 8
/// no highlight of the current line
CE_NO_LINE: u32 = 16
/// the gutter keeps its column of diagnostic markers while the document has none
CE_MARKS: u32 = 32
```

- **`struct CodeStatus`**
  what code_status reports
  - `line: usize` -- the caret's line and column (from 1; columns with tabs expanded)
  - `col: usize`
  - `matches: usize` -- the find bar's matches (0: none or closed) and the current one (from 1; 0: none)
  - `current: usize`
  - `hl_lines: usize` -- the lines tokenized for highlighting states in the editor's last frame (the visible
    lines are tokenized again to draw them, not counted)
  - `lines: usize` -- the number of lines
  - `diags: [usize; 3]` -- the document's diagnostics: errors, warnings, infos (DIAG_\* order)
  - `diag: Option<u8>` -- the severity (DIAG_\*) of the most severe diagnostic at the caret (ui.code_diag: the
    diagnostic with its message)

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn code_theme_set(&mut self, theme: Option<CodeTheme>)`**
  the colours of every code editor (None: code_theme(), following the UI's theme)
- **`fn code_font_size(&mut self, pt: f32)`**
  the size of the code editors' font in points (0: 10 pt)
- **`fn code_find(&mut self, id: u32, query: &str, replace: bool)`**
  open the find bar of code editor id with a query (replace: with the replace row); the
  editor selects the first match from its caret on
- **`fn code_status(&self, id: u32) -> CodeStatus`**
  the caret, the find matches, the lines tokenized and the diagnostics in code editor
  id's last frame
- **`fn code_diag(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Diag>`**
  the most severe diagnostic at the caret of code editor id in its last frame (its
  message for a status bar)
- **`fn code_editor(&mut self, id: u32, doc: &mut CodeDoc, h: &Highlighter, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  ui_code_editor(id, doc, hl, CE_\*) -> EV_\* (see the module header)

### Lists, scrolling, tabs, expanders

Source: [`lib/ui/list.rs`](../lib/ui/list.rs)

```text
list -- scroll views, scroll bars, lists, tabs and expanders (WinUI 3 style)
                                                                 [src/ui/ui_list.s]

  scroll_begin(id, flags)                clipped viewport that takes its size like a box
       (next_size / parent) and lays its children out in a content area that may be
       larger; flags = SC_V (default) | SC_H | SC_NOBAR | SC_NOWHEEL | BOX_BG | BOX_CARD |
       PAD_n ...  Mouse wheel (48 DIP per notch, smooth), overlay scroll bars (2 DIP, 6 DIP
       while pointed at, draggable thumb, click on the track pages), Tab focus is scrolled
       into view.
  scroll_end()
  scroll_to(id, x, y)                    jump to a position in DIP (-1 keeps that axis)
  scroll_pos(id) -> (x, y)               current position in DIP
  scroll_extent(id) -> (w, h)            content size in DIP (last measure; 0 before) (U3)
  scrollbar(id, &mut pos, content, view, vertical) -> EV
       standalone scroll bar (natural thickness 12 DIP) for custom canvases; pos runs from
       0 to content - view in the caller's unit; EV_ACT when pos changed
  list_begin(id, &mut sel, count, item_h | LF_*) -> (first, end)
       virtualized list (own scroll view, fixed row height in DIP, 0 = 40); emit the rows
       first .. end-1; row i has the widget id `id + 1 + i`.  Up/Down/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn
       move the selection (sel, -1 = none) and scroll it into view; Enter: the selected
       row reports EV_DOUBLE (list_end too), Space: the first check box / switch of the
       selected row acts; the menu key: the selected row's right click.  The list is one Tab
       stop; the widgets inside custom rows are Tab stops in the selected row only.  Focus
       alone selects nothing: a focused list without a selection has the focus visual
       around it.
       LF_REORDER (U1): a row dragged more than 4 DIP is moved: an accent insertion line
       follows the pointer, the view scrolls near its edges, Esc cancels; on release
       list_end returns EV_DRAG with from | to << 16 (the app moves item `from` so that it
       ends at index `to`) and sel = to.  Widgets inside custom rows keep their clicks.
       The keyboard moves the selected row the same way: Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down one place,
       Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End to the top / bottom.
  list_item(i, label) -> EV              text row (EV_ACT clicked, EV_DOUBLE, EV_RCLICK)
  list_item_begin(i) -> EV               custom row: opens a BOX_H inside the row
  list_item_end()
  list_end(&mut sel) -> (EV, sel)        EV_ACT if sel changed this pass, EV_DOUBLE;
                                         EV_DRAG: a row was dropped (from | to << 16)
       (Rust: list_begin reads the selection into the list, list_end writes it back --
       the asm keeps a pointer to the app's variable in between; list_sel() reads it in
       the rows)
  tabs(id, &mut sel, names) -> EV        text tab header row, tab i has the id
                                         `id + 1 + i`; EV_ACT when sel changed; placed
                                         narrower than the tabs, the widest ones give
                                         way (labels cut with "…")
  expander_begin(id, header, &mut open) -> open   (emit the content when 1)
  expander_end()

Widget ids used internally: (id << 3 | k) | 0x80000000 for sub parts (k = 1..7),
(id + 1 + i) | 0xC0000000 for the content box of custom list rows.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn scroll_begin(&mut self, id: u32, flags: u32)`**
  ui_scroll_begin(id, flags)
- **`fn scroll_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_scroll_end
- **`fn scroll_to(&mut self, id: u32, x: i32, y: i32)`**
  ui_scroll_to(id, x, y): DIP, -1 keeps that axis; jumps without animation
- **`fn scroll_pos(&mut self, id: u32) -> (i32, i32)`**
  ui_scroll_pos(id) -> (x, y) DIP
- **`fn scroll_extent(&mut self, id: u32) -> (i32, i32)`**
  ui_scroll_extent(id) -> (w, h): measured content size of scroll view `id` (DIP; 0
  before its first pass).  With the view size (last_rect after scroll_end) the app can
  tell whether the content overflows.  (U3)
- **`fn scrollbar(&mut self, id: u32, pos: &mut i32, content: i32, view: i32, vertical: bool) -> u32`**
  ui_scrollbar(id, &mut pos, content, view, vertical) -> EV_\*
- **`fn list_begin(&mut self, id: u32, sel: &mut i32, count: i32, item_h: u32) -> (i32, i32)`**
  ui_list_begin(id, &mut sel, count, item_h | LF_\*) -> (first, end): the rows to emit
- **`fn list_item(&mut self, i: i32, label: &str) -> u32`**
  ui_list_item(i, label) -> EV_\*
- **`fn list_item_begin(&mut self, i: i32) -> u32`**
  ui_list_item_begin(i) -> EV_\*: row i with a BOX_H (gap 8 DIP) for custom content
- **`fn list_sel(&self) -> i32`**
  the innermost list's selection while its rows are emitted (the asm's rows see the
  app's variable change at once; here the list holds it until list_end), -1 outside a
  list
- **`fn list_item_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_list_item_end
- **`fn list_end(&mut self, sel: &mut i32) -> (u32, i32)`**
  ui_list_end(&mut sel) -> (EV_\* (EV_ACT if sel changed, EV_DOUBLE), sel); EV_DRAG: a
  row was dropped, the second value is from | to &lt;&lt; 16
- **`fn tabs_scrolling(&mut self, id: u32, sel: &mut i32, names: &[&str]) -> u32`**
  Tab strip with horizontal overflow arrows. Mouse scrolling and Left/Right,
  Home/End on the strip retain ordinary tab semantics; changed selections
  and resized viewports reveal the selected tab. Internal IDs follow the
  usual `(id * 8 + part) | 0x80000000` convention (parts 1, 2, 3 and 7).
- **`fn tabs(&mut self, id: u32, sel: &mut i32, names: &[&str]) -> u32`**
  ui_tabs(id, &mut sel, names) -> EV_\* (EV_ACT when sel changed)
- **`fn expander_begin(&mut self, id: u32, header: &str, open: &mut i32) -> i32`**
  ui_expander_begin(id, header, &mut open) -> open: a card-like header (48 DIP) with a
  chevron; when open the content follows in a padded card below it (BOX_V, PAD_16, gap
  8 DIP).  Always call expander_end.
- **`fn expander_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_expander_end

### Data views: grid, tree, badges, meters

Source: [`lib/ui/data.rs`](../lib/ui/data.rs)

```text
data -- data views: grid (table with columns), tree, badges, status dots, meters

  grid_begin(id, &mut st, cols, keys) -> (first, end)
       a virtualized table (fills its parent unless next_size says otherwise): a fixed
       header (click: sort by the column, again: descending;
       drag a column's right edge: its width, double click there: the default width) and
       the rows below it in a vertical scroll view (row height and header height from
       StyleData::grid_metrics).  keys: one stable key per row in display order (the app
       sorts and filters; the selection is kept by key, so it survives refreshes).
       Emit rows first .. end-1: grid_row(&mut st, i), then per column grid_cell(&st, c)
       and any widget (it is placed into the cell), or grid_text(&st, c, s).
       Mouse: click selects, Ctrl+click toggles, Shift+click selects a range, double click
       activates, right click selects the row and reports it.  Keys (grid focused): Up /
       Down / PgUp / PgDn / Home / End move the current row (Shift: extend), Ctrl+A all,
       Space toggles the current row, Enter activates.
  grid_row(&mut st, i) -> EV        row i (widget id id + 1 + i)
  grid_cell(&st, c)                 the next widget goes into column c of the current row
  grid_text(&st, c, s)              text in column c (ellipsis, the column's alignment)
  grid_end(&mut st) -> GridEv       ev: EV_ACT selection changed, EV_DOUBLE a row was
                                    activated, EV_RCLICK context menu requested; row: that
                                    row's index; sort_changed: re-sort the keys
  tree(id, &mut st, rows, row_h) -> TreeEv
       a virtualized tree from the app's visible rows (TreeRow: key, depth, children,
       check state, icon, label, detail); the chevron / Right / Left expand and collapse
       (st.expanded; TreeEv::expanded names a newly opened node for lazy loading), the
       check box / Space report TreeEv::check (the app applies it, e.g. with cascade),
       double click / Enter TreeEv::activated
  badge(kind, label)                status pill (BADGE_NEUTRAL .. BADGE_ACCENT; next_icon); in
                                    a narrower cell the label is cut with "…"
  status_dot(kind)                  a small status dot (10 DIP)
  meter(id, v, max, kind)           a capacity bar (next_size sets its size)

Ids: the header box (id << 3) | 0x80000000, the header cells ((id ^ 0xA5A5) << 3 | k) |
0x80000000 with k = 1 + column (sort), the grips ((id ^ 0x5A5A) << 3 | k) | 0x80000000; the
rows' scroll view id (its bars (id << 3 | 1 / 2) | 0x80000000); rows id + 1 + i; tree chevrons / check boxes
(id + 1 + i) | 0x40000000 / | 0x20000000.
```

- **`struct GridCol<'a>`**
  a grid column: title, width and minimum width in DIP, GC_\* flags
  - `title: &'a str`
  - `width: i32`
  - `min: i32`
  - `flags: u32`

**`impl<'a> GridCol<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(title: &'a str, width: i32) -> GridCol<'a>`**
  a column `width` DIP wide (at least 48)
- **`const fn flags(mut self, flags: u32) -> GridCol<'a>`**
  the same column with GC_\* flags
- **`const fn min(mut self, min: i32) -> GridCol<'a>`**
  the same column with a minimum width (DIP)

- **`struct GridState`**
  the app-owned state of a grid: selection (by key), current row, sort, column widths
  - `sel: BTreeSet<u64>` -- the selected rows' keys
  - `cur: Option<u64>` -- the current row (keyboard focus / last clicked)
  - `sort: Option<(usize, bool)>` -- the sort column and direction (true = descending); None = the app's order
  - `widths: Vec<i32>` -- column widths set by the user (DIP, 0 = the column's own)
  - `striped: bool` -- alternate row shading

**`impl GridState`**

- **`fn selected_in_order(&self) -> Vec<u64>`**
  the keys selected, in display order of the last pass
- **`fn select_only(&mut self, key: Option<u64>)`**
  select exactly this key (None: nothing) and make it current
- **`fn retain(&mut self, keys: &[u64])`**
  drop selected keys that are no longer shown (after a refresh)

- **`struct GridEv`**
  what happened in a grid during the pass
  - `ev: u32` -- EV_ACT selection changed, EV_DOUBLE a row was activated, EV_RCLICK context requested
  - `row: i32` -- the activated / context row (-1 = none)
  - `sort_changed: bool` -- the sort column or direction changed

- **`struct TreeRow<'a>`**
  one visible row of a tree (the app flattens its model through TreeState::expanded)
  - `key: u64`
  - `depth: u16`
  - `has_children: bool`
  - `check: Option<u8>` -- check box state 0 / 1 / 2 (indeterminate); None = no check box
  - `icon: u32`
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `detail: Option<&'a str>` -- secondary text after the label (size, date)

- **`struct TreeState`**
  the app-owned state of a tree: expanded nodes, current node
  - `expanded: BTreeSet<u64>`
  - `cur: Option<u64>`
  - `marks: BTreeMap<u64, u32>` -- app data per node (free use, e.g. a loading flag)

- **`struct TreeEv`**
  what happened in a tree during the pass
  - `expanded: Option<u64>` -- a node opened in this pass (load its children)
  - `collapsed: Option<u64>` -- a node closed in this pass
  - `check: Option<(u64, u8)>` -- a check box was toggled: (key, new state 0 / 1)
  - `activated: Option<u64>` -- double click / Enter on a node
  - `sel_changed: bool` -- the current node changed

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn grid_begin(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut GridState, cols: &[GridCol], keys: &[u64]) -> (i32, i32)`**
  ui_grid_begin(id, &mut st, cols, keys) -> (first, end): the rows to emit
- **`fn grid_row(&mut self, st: &mut GridState, i: i32) -> u32`**
  ui_grid_row(&mut st, i) -> EV_\* of row i (EV_ACT clicked)
- **`fn grid_cell(&mut self, st: &GridState, c: usize)`**
  ui_grid_cell(&st, c): the next widget is placed into column c of the current row
  (inset by the cell padding, full row height)
- **`fn grid_text(&mut self, st: &GridState, c: usize, s: &str)`**
  ui_grid_text(&st, c, s): body text in column c (cut with "…", the column's alignment)
- **`fn grid_text_ts(&mut self, st: &GridState, c: usize, ts: u32, s: &str)`**
  ui_grid_text_ts(&st, c, ts, s): text in column c with a text style (TS_\* | TX_\*)
- **`fn grid_end(&mut self, st: &mut GridState) -> GridEv`**
  ui_grid_end(&mut st) -> GridEv
- **`fn tree(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut TreeState, rows: &[TreeRow], row_h: i32) -> TreeEv`**
  ui_tree(id, &mut st, rows, row_h) -> TreeEv: the visible rows of a tree (row_h DIP,
  0 = the grid row height)
- **`fn badge(&mut self, kind: u32, label: &str)`**
  ui_badge(kind, label): a status pill (BADGE_\*; next_icon puts an icon before the text);
  placed narrower than the pill (a grid cell), the label is cut with "…"
- **`fn status_dot(&mut self, kind: u32)`**
  ui_status_dot(kind): a 10 DIP status dot (BADGE_\*)
- **`fn meter(&mut self, id: u32, v: i64, max: i64, kind: u32)`**
  ui_meter(id, v, max, kind): a capacity bar (natural 120 x 8 DIP; next_size)

### Shell parts: navigation, command bar, splitter, breadcrumb, wizard steps

Source: [`lib/ui/shell.rs`](../lib/ui/shell.rs)

```text
shell -- the parts of an application shell: navigation pane, command bar, splitter,
breadcrumb, segmented control, wizard step list

  nav_begin(id, &mut NavState)        vertical navigation pane (next_size sets its width;
                                      the style's surface), items scroll when they do not fit
  nav_toggle(id, label)               the pane's menu button: toggles NavState::compact
  nav_section(label)                  a group caption (compact: a divider)
  nav_item(id, icon, label, selected, badge) -> EV   EV_ACT when clicked; badge: a count
  nav_footer()                        the items after it stay at the bottom of the pane
  nav_end()
  command_bar(id, items) -> Option<id>   a row of subtle icon + label buttons; what does not
                                      fit goes into a "…" menu; CBI_END starts the group
                                      aligned to the end, CBI_SEP a separator; ST_ACCENT /
                                      ST_DISABLED / ST_CHECKED per item
  split_begin(id, pos, vertical)      two panes: the first `pos` DIP wide (vertical: high),
  split_next()                        a draggable grip, the second fills
  split_end(&mut pos) -> changed      the dragged position (DIP)
  breadcrumb(id, parts) -> Option<i>  path of links, the last part is the current page
  segmented(id, &mut sel, items) -> EV   a segmented control (EV_ACT when sel changed)
  wizard_steps(id, steps, current, states) -> Option<i>   vertical step list; a click on
                                      a done step (or one before the current) returns it

Ids: parts (id << 3 | k) | 0x80000000; items of segmented / wizard / breadcrumb id + 1 + i.
```

- **`struct NavState`**
  the app-owned state of a navigation pane
  - `compact: bool` -- icons only

- **`struct CmdItem<'a>`**
  an item of a command bar
  - `id: u32`
  - `icon: u32`
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `flags: u32` -- ST_ACCENT, ST_DISABLED, ST_CHECKED, CBI_SEP, CBI_END

**`impl<'a> CmdItem<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(id: u32, icon: u32, label: &'a str) -> CmdItem<'a>`**
- **`const fn flags(mut self, f: u32) -> CmdItem<'a>`**
  add flags (ST_ACCENT, CBI_SEP, ...; in any order with enabled())
- **`const fn enabled(mut self, on: bool) -> CmdItem<'a>`**
  disabled unless `on`

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn nav_begin(&mut self, id: u32, nav: &mut NavState)`**
  ui_nav_begin(id, &mut nav): open the pane (always call nav_end)
- **`fn nav_toggle(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, nav: &mut NavState) -> u32`**
  ui_nav_toggle(id, label): the menu button of the pane (toggles compact)
- **`fn nav_section(&mut self, label: &str)`**
  ui_nav_section(label): a group caption (a divider when the pane is compact)
- **`fn nav_item(&mut self, id: u32, icon: u32, label: &str, selected: bool, badge: Option<&str>) -> u32`**
  ui_nav_item(id, icon, label, selected, badge) -> EV_\* (EV_ACT clicked)
- **`fn nav_footer(&mut self)`**
  ui_nav_footer: end the scrolling item list; the items after it stay at the bottom
- **`fn nav_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_nav_end
- **`fn command_bar(&mut self, id: u32, items: &[CmdItem]) -> Option<u32>`**
  ui_command_bar(id, items) -> the id of the item clicked in this pass
- **`fn split_begin(&mut self, id: u32, pos: i32, vertical: bool)`**
  ui_split_begin(id, pos, vertical): two panes, the first `pos` DIP wide (vertical:
  high); emit the first pane, split_next, the second pane, split_end
- **`fn split_next(&mut self)`**
  ui_split_next: the grip, then the second pane
- **`fn split_end(&mut self, pos: &mut i32) -> bool`**
  ui_split_end(&mut pos) -> the grip moved (pos updated, DIP; the mouse or the keyboard:
  F8 focuses the grip, arrows move it)
- **`fn breadcrumb(&mut self, id: u32, parts: &[&str]) -> Option<usize>`**
  ui_breadcrumb(id, parts) -> the index of a clicked part (the last one is the current
  page and not a link)
- **`fn segmented(&mut self, id: u32, sel: &mut i32, items: &[&str]) -> u32`**
  ui_segmented(id, &mut sel, items) -> EV_\* (EV_ACT when sel changed)
- **`fn wizard_steps(&mut self, id: u32, steps: &[&str], current: usize, states: &[i32]) -> Option<usize>`**
  ui_wizard_steps(id, steps, current, states) -> a step to go back to (clicked);
  states: WS_\* per step (missing: done before the current, todo after it)
- **`fn page_header(&mut self, title: &str, subtitle: &str)`**
  ui_page_header(title, subtitle): a page title (TS_TITLE) with an optional secondary
  line under it
- **`fn key_value(&mut self, key: &str, value: &str, key_width: i32)`**
  ui_key_value(key, value, key_width): a "label: value" row (TS_BODY, the key in the
  secondary colour, key_width DIP)
- **`fn empty_state(&mut self, icon: u32, title: &str, text: &str)`**
  ui_empty_state(icon, title, text): a centred hint for an empty view (icon 0 = none);
  the text wraps at 360 DIP, or at the enclosing box's width when that is narrower

### Docking: panels at the sides, tab groups, floating tool windows

Source: [`lib/ui/dock.rs`](../lib/ui/dock.rs)

```text
dock -- a docking area: the app's panels at the sides of a document area (left, right,
bottom) in tab groups with splitters, dragged to other places with drop markers, floating in
tool windows and docked again, hidden, collapsed to a rail; the layout is the app's DockState

  dock_begin(id, &mut st, panels)   the area takes the next place (without next_size it fills
                                    the box); panels describe every panel each frame
                                    (DockPanel: id != 0, title, icon, DP_* flags, first place)
  dock_next(&mut st) -> Some(id)    the next place to fill: DOCK_CENTER (the document area)
                                    first, then the shown panel of every group, the floating
                                    windows last; emit its content (a vertical box that clips)
                                    and call it again until None
  dock_end(&mut st) -> changed      true when the user changed the layout (save it then)
  DockState                         the layout, kept by the app: save() -> text, load(text),
                                    reset, show / hide / toggle / focus / activate, float /
                                    dock_to, collapse / collapsed, size / set_size, groups /
                                    floats / hidden_panels, side / visible / front / shown

Places: a side holds tab groups (left / right: one above the other, bottom: side by side)
with splitters between them and towards the document area; a collapsed side is a rail of
icon buttons.  Left and right are the start and the end side: the layout is logical, so a
mirrored (RTL) window shows the left side at the right like everything else.
Dragging a tab (or the empty part of a tab strip: the whole group) shows drop markers at the
three edges of the area (a new group on that side) and on the group under the pointer (as a
tab, before, after it); a release over a tab strip inserts it there; anywhere else -- also
outside the window -- the panel floats in a tool window at the pointer (WF_TOOL, window ids
id + 1 .. id + DOCK_FLOAT_MAX).  Tabs of a floating window drag the same way onto the main
window's markers (the pointer stays with the floating window); its pin button or a double
click docks it where it came from, its close button hides its panels.  Esc cancels a drag.
Keyboard: the tab strip of a group is one focus stop (Left / Right / Home / End switch tabs,
the menu key or Shift+F10 open the group's menu with every move), Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp switch
tabs while the focus is anywhere in the group, DockState::focus(id) brings a panel forward
and gives its tab strip the focus (the app binds it to its commands).
Structural changes (clicks, drops, menu rows) are applied at dock_end, followed by another
pass; splitters change the sizes at once.  Widget ids are parts of the area id (pid).
```

```rust
/// the sides of a dock area (DockPanel::at, DockState::side); left / right are the start / end
/// side (a mirrored window shows them the other way round)
DOCK_LEFT: u8 = 0
DOCK_RIGHT: u8 = 1
DOCK_BOTTOM: u8 = 2
/// a floating tool window
DOCK_FLOAT: u8 = 3
/// dock_next: the document area in the middle
DOCK_CENTER: u32 = 0
/// DockPanel flags: no hide button or menu row (the app shows and hides it)
DP_NOCLOSE: u32 = 1
/// never floats (a drop outside the markers does nothing)
DP_NOFLOAT: u32 = 2
/// starts hidden (until DockState::show / focus); later the layout remembers it
DP_HIDDEN: u32 = 4
/// floating windows of one dock area at most (fixed: each is a window, WIN_MAX)
DOCK_FLOAT_MAX: usize = 6
/// drop marker kinds (StyleShell::dock_marker, sp.value): the part of the place it fills
DOCK_MK_LEFT: i32 = 0
DOCK_MK_RIGHT: i32 = 1
DOCK_MK_TOP: i32 = 2
DOCK_MK_BOTTOM: i32 = 3
DOCK_MK_CENTER: i32 = 4
```

- **`struct DockPanel<'a>`**
  a panel as the app describes it to dock_begin every frame
  - `id: u32` -- != 0 and stable (the saved layout refers to it)
  - `title: &'a str`
  - `icon: u32` -- IC_\* of its tab and of the rail of a collapsed side (0 = none)
  - `flags: u32` -- DP_\*
  - `side: u8` -- where it goes the first time: DOCK_LEFT / DOCK_RIGHT / DOCK_BOTTOM / DOCK_FLOAT
  - `group: u8` -- panels of one side with the same group number start as tabs of one group; the groups
    in the order of their numbers

**`impl<'a> DockPanel<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(id: u32, title: &'a str, icon: u32) -> DockPanel<'a>`**
  a panel that starts in group 0 of the left side
- **`const fn at(mut self, side: u8, group: u8) -> DockPanel<'a>`**
  its first place: side (DOCK_\*) and group number
- **`const fn flags(mut self, f: u32) -> DockPanel<'a>`**
  add DP_\* flags

- **`struct DockState`**
  the layout of a dock area: kept by the app and passed to dock_begin / dock_next /
  dock_end.  save() / load() turn it into a few lines of text: \\`dock 1\\`, then \\`side S SIZE
  COLLAPSED`, `group S TAG SIZE ACTIVE PANEL...`, `float SLOT X Y W H HOME HOMETAG ACTIVE
  PANEL...\\`, \\`hidden PANEL S TAG POS X Y W H HOME HOMETAG\\` (unknown lines are skipped).

**`impl DockState`**

- **`fn new() -> DockState`**
  the empty layout: every panel goes to its DockPanel place in the first frame
- **`fn reset(&mut self)`**
  forget the layout: every panel goes to its DockPanel place in the next frame
- **`fn show(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  show a hidden panel where it was, as the shown tab of its group
- **`fn hide(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  hide a panel (show brings it back to the same place)
- **`fn toggle(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  show a hidden panel, hide a visible one
- **`fn focus(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  show the panel as the shown tab (a collapsed side expands) and give its tab strip the
  keyboard focus in the next pass (a floating window comes to the front)
- **`fn activate(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  make the panel the shown tab of its group (a collapsed side expands)
- **`fn float(&mut self, id: u32, rect: Option<[i32; 4]>) -> bool`**
  float the panel in a tool window: rect = x, y (DIP from the main window's client
  origin), client width, height; None: cascaded from the top left -> false when every
  floating window of the area is in use
- **`fn dock_to(&mut self, id: u32, side: u8)`**
  dock the panel to a side, as a new group at its end
- **`fn collapse(&mut self, side: u8, on: bool)`**
  collapse a side to a rail of icon buttons, or expand it
- **`fn collapsed(&self, side: u8) -> bool`**
  the side is collapsed
- **`fn size(&self, side: u8) -> i32`**
  the width (left / right) or the height (bottom) of a side in DIP
- **`fn set_size(&mut self, side: u8, dip: i32)`**
  set the width / height of a side (DIP)
- **`fn groups(&self, side: u8) -> Vec<Vec<u32>>`**
  the tab groups of a side from start to end, each with its panels in tab order
- **`fn floats(&self) -> Vec<Vec<u32>>`**
  the panels of every floating window
- **`fn hidden_panels(&self) -> Vec<u32>`**
  the hidden panels
- **`fn side(&self, id: u32) -> Option<u8>`**
  where the panel is: DOCK_LEFT / DOCK_RIGHT / DOCK_BOTTOM / DOCK_FLOAT (None: hidden or
  unknown)
- **`fn visible(&self, id: u32) -> bool`**
  docked or floating (not hidden)
- **`fn front(&self, id: u32) -> bool`**
  the shown tab of its group (also on a collapsed side)
- **`fn shown(&self, id: u32) -> bool`**
  its content is on the screen: the front tab, on a side that is not collapsed (or
  floating)
- **`fn save(&self) -> String`**
  the layout as text (see DockState)
- **`fn load(text: &str) -> Option<DockState>`**
  a layout saved with save -> None when the text is no dock layout (version 1)

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn dock_begin(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut DockState, panels: &[DockPanel])`**
  dock_begin(id, &mut st, panels): open the dock area (always pair with dock_end; fill it
  with dock_next).  It takes the next place of the box (the whole rest when no size was
  set); panels: every panel the app has, each frame (titles and icons may change).
- **`fn dock_next(&mut self, st: &mut DockState) -> Option<u32>`**
  dock_next(&mut st) -> the next place to fill (None: done): DOCK_CENTER, then the id of
  a shown panel; its content goes into a vertical box (it clips) until the next call
- **`fn dock_end(&mut self, st: &mut DockState) -> bool`**
  dock_end(&mut st) -> the user changed the layout in this pass (store st.save() then)

### Charts

Source: [`lib/ui/chart.rs`](../lib/ui/chart.rs)

```text
chart -- small charts for dashboards: sparkline, bar chart (grouped or stacked), donut,
legend, and line charts of time series (line_chart over SeriesBuf rings).  Colours: 0 =
the style's chart palette (StyleData::chart_palette) by index.

  sparkline(id, values, color)          area + line, natural 120 x 32 DIP (next_size)
  bar_chart(id, labels, series, stacked) -> hovered column or -1
                                        value grid with labels, one column per label,
                                        natural 360 x 180 DIP; hovering a column shows a
                                        tooltip with its values.  Labels never overlap:
                                        where they do not fit side by side every k-th one
                                        is shown (the first and the last kept; a text
                                        record each), a low plot gets fewer value steps
  donut(id, slices, center, sub)        ring of slices with a centre text, natural 160 DIP
                                        (texts kept inside the hole)
  legend(items)                         colour dot + label per item, wrapping row (an
                                        item wider than the row: its label cut with "…")
  line_chart(id, &LineChart) -> Option<(series, x)>
       series of (x, value) points (LcSeries over a SeriesBuf: label, colour or palette
       index, line or area, LcUnit) over time -- LX_SECS seconds or LX_NANOS nanoseconds,
       ticks 0:05 / 1:00 / 1:30 (h:mm:ss from an hour on, decimals of the second below
       one) -- or plain numbers (LX_NUM).  Natural 480 x 200 DIP for the plot with its
       axes, the legend (legend(), the series' labels) below it; next_size sizes both.
       The y axis: "nice" ticks (1 / 2 / 2.5 / 5 x 10^k) labelled in the first series'
       unit; y_range fixed or automatic per end (NaN: from the visible values and the
       thresholds, out to the next tick).  The x range: x_range, else the data's --
       follow live with x_span (the newest x_span; LineChart::view() is what it shows).
       Grid lines at the ticks; markers (LcMarker: a line or a shaded range with a short
       label in a tag at the top: fault injections) and thresholds (LcThreshold: a dashed
       line with its label in a tag at its right end).  Tags never overlap: a marker's tag
       takes the first of up to three rows with room, else it is left out (the hover card
       still names the markers under the pointer).  Hovering the plot: a crosshair at the
       nearest point, a dot on every series and a card beside it at once (the style's
       tooltip surface) with the x and every series' value there; the return value is the
       series nearest to the pointer and that x.  Keys (the plot takes the focus: Tab, a
       click puts the cursor on the point under the pointer): Left / Right the previous /
       next point of the cursor's series, Up / Down another series, Home / End, Esc ends
       it; crosshair and card show the cursor, the record's label starts with its point.
       Up to two points per pixel column the points themselves are drawn, more as one
       band per series (per column the range of its values, SeriesBuf::columns), so
       100 000 points draw like 500.  No points at all: LineChart::empty in the middle
       ("Keine Daten" in the UI language).  High
       contrast: the scheme's highlight, text and link colours with a dash pattern per
       series (the legend shows line samples), no translucent fills.  The plot keeps its
       left-to-right order in mirrored windows (ltr_begin); the legend is mirrored.
       Records: K_CANVAS id, its label a summary (the name, then per series its last
       value, min. and max. in the view; value: the number of series); K_TEXT per axis
       label, tag and hover card row ("p95: 48 ms").  Flags LC_NO_LEGEND, LC_NO_GRID,
       LC_NO_HOVER.
  SeriesBuf::new(capacity)              the ring a series draws from: push(t, v) (times
                                        never decrease; a value that is not finite is a
                                        gap), clear, len / get / first / last / iter,
                                        lower_bound(t), nearest(t), min_max /
                                        min_max_in(t0, t1), columns(t0, t1, n) (per pixel
                                        column min / max / first / last), ver()
  LcUnit::Num(sfx) / Si(unit) / Secs    how values read: text(v, sep) ("48,2 ms", "1,25k
                                        req/s", "1,5 MB"), ticks(first, step, n, sep)
  lc_nice(lo, hi, steps), lc_time_step(min), lc_time_text(t, dec, hours, sep)
                                        the axis maths: tick steps, clock labels

Area, line and ring are vector paths filled at render time (cmd_custom); their drawing
object is kept per id and replaced only when the data or the size change, so an unchanged
chart does not redraw (dirty.rs hashes the object's identity and version).  A line chart
keeps its statistics, summary and plot per id, keyed by the series' versions and the
view; its crosshair, dots and card are ordinary commands over the plot.
```

- **`struct BarSeries<'a>`**
  one series of a bar chart
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `values: &'a [f32]`
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB, 0 = palette colour of the series index

- **`struct DonutSlice<'a>`**
  one slice of a donut
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `value: f32`
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB, 0 = palette colour of the slice index

- **`struct SeriesBuf`**
  a time series for line_chart: (t, value) points in a ring that keeps the newest
  `capacity` (a full buffer drops its oldest point on push).  Times never decrease (push
  refuses an earlier one, so every lookup is a binary search); a value that is not finite
  (NaN) is a gap where the line breaks.  ver() changes with every change: a chart redraws
  only then.

- **`struct SeriesCol`**
  one pixel column of a downsampled series (SeriesBuf::columns): the points with a finite
  value whose time falls into it
  - `col: u32` -- the column (0 .. n)
  - `n: u32` -- its points with a value
  - `min: f64`
  - `max: f64`
  - `first: f64` -- the values of its first and its last point
  - `last: f64`
  - `gap: bool` -- a gap came before it (after the previous point with a value inside t0 .. t1): the
    line breaks there; a gap inside a column starts a second entry for it

**`impl SeriesBuf`**

- **`fn new(capacity: usize) -> SeriesBuf`**
  an empty series that keeps the newest `capacity` points (at least one)
- **`fn push(&mut self, t: f64, v: f64) -> bool`**
  append a point (t: the time, or any x that never decreases; v NaN: a gap); false
  (nothing added) when t is not finite or earlier than the last point's
- **`fn clear(&mut self)`**
  remove every point
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of points
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
  no points
- **`fn capacity(&self) -> usize`**
  the most points it keeps
- **`fn ver(&self) -> u32`**
  changes with every push and clear (equal versions: equal points)
- **`fn get(&self, i: usize) -> Option<(f64, f64)>`**
  the i-th point, the oldest first
- **`fn first(&self) -> Option<(f64, f64)>`**
  the oldest point
- **`fn last(&self) -> Option<(f64, f64)>`**
  the newest point
- **`fn iter(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = (f64, f64)> + ExactSizeIterator + '_`**
  the points, the oldest first
- **`fn lower_bound(&self, t: f64) -> usize`**
  the index of the first point at t or later (len() when there is none)
- **`fn nearest(&self, t: f64) -> Option<usize>`**
  the index of the point with a finite value nearest to t (of two as near the earlier)
- **`fn min_max(&self) -> Option<(f64, f64)>`**
  the smallest and the largest finite value (None without one); looks at every point
- **`fn min_max_in(&self, t0: f64, t1: f64) -> Option<(f64, f64)>`**
  the smallest and the largest finite value of the points with t0 &lt;= t &lt;= t1
- **`fn columns(&self, t0: f64, t1: f64, n: usize) -> Vec<SeriesCol>`**
  the points with t0 &lt;= t &lt;= t1 in n columns of equal width (t1 belongs to the last):
  per column the range of its values, its first and its last value.  Columns without
  a point with a value are left out; the work is one pass over the points, the result
  at most n entries (plus one per gap)

- **`enum LcUnit<'a>`**
  how a line chart labels values (axis ticks, the hover card, the summary)
  - `Num(&'a str)` -- numbers, large ones with k / M / G / T (1,5k), then the suffix after a space
    ("req/s", "%"; "" none)
  - `Si(&'a str)` -- SI prefixes on a unit: Si("B") 950 B / 1,5 kB / 20 MB, Si("bit/s") 100 Mbit/s
  - `Secs` -- seconds shown as ns / µs / ms / s (latencies)

**`impl LcUnit<'_>`**

- **`fn text(&self, v: f64, sep: u32) -> String`**
  v as one value: three significant digits with the scale that fits ("48,2 ms",
  "1,25k req/s", "12 %", "1,5 MB"); sep = the decimal separator (ui.decimal_sep());
  "–" for a value that is not finite
- **`fn ticks(&self, first: f64, step: f64, n: u32, sep: u32) -> Vec<String>`**
  the labels of the axis ticks first + k \* step (k = 0 ..= n): one scale for all (the
  largest tick's; plain numbers get k / M only from 10 000 on), the decimals the step
  needs; a zero tick reads "0" with the unit ("0 ms", "0 req/s")

- **`fn lc_nice(lo: f64, hi: f64, steps: u32) -> (f64, f64, u32)`**
  "nice" ticks over lo ..= hi: (first, step, n) -- the step 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 x 10^k, first
  and first + n \* step the multiples of it at or around lo and hi, n &lt;= max(steps, 1) (at
  least 1; lo == hi spans |lo|, or 1)

- **`fn lc_time_step(min: f64) -> f64`**
  the step of a time axis (s): the smallest of 1 / 2 / 5 x 10^k below a second (down to a
  nanosecond), 1 2 5 10 15 30 s, 1 2 5 10 15 30 min, 1 2 3 6 12 h, then days (1 / 2 / 5 x
  10^k) that is at least `min`

- **`fn lc_time_text(t: f64, dec: u32, hours: bool, sep: u32) -> String`**
  a time t (s) as a clock: "0:05", "1:30", "12:00", with hours "1:00:00"; dec decimals of
  the second (up to 9) after sep (the decimal separator): "0:01,5"; negative with a minus

*line chart*

```rust
/// x axes of a line chart (LineChart::x)
LX_SECS: u8 = 0  // time in seconds: 0:05, 1:00, 1:30
LX_NANOS: u8 = 1  // time in nanoseconds (a simulation clock), labelled the same
LX_NUM: u8 = 2  // plain numbers
/// LineChart::flags
LC_NO_LEGEND: u32 = 1  // no legend below the plot
LC_NO_GRID: u32 = 2  // no grid lines
LC_NO_HOVER: u32 = 4  // no crosshair, card and keyboard cursor (no focus stop)
```

- **`struct LcSeries<'a>`**
  one series of a line chart: a label, its points, colour, line or area, unit
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `data: &'a SeriesBuf`
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB; 0 = the chart palette's colour `pal`, without one the series' index
  - `pal: Option<u8>`
  - `area: bool` -- a translucent fill under the line, down to zero (or to the edge of the plot)
  - `unit: LcUnit<'a>` -- how its values read (the y axis takes the first series')

**`impl<'a> LcSeries<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(label: &'a str, data: &'a SeriesBuf) -> LcSeries<'a>`**
  a line in the palette colour of its index, plain numbers
- **`const fn color(mut self, c: u32) -> LcSeries<'a>`**
  the same series in a colour (0xAARRGGBB)
- **`const fn pal(mut self, k: u8) -> LcSeries<'a>`**
  the same series in the chart palette's colour k (0 ..= 7)
- **`const fn area(mut self) -> LcSeries<'a>`**
  the same series as an area
- **`const fn unit(mut self, u: LcUnit<'a>) -> LcSeries<'a>`**
  the same series with a unit

- **`struct LcMarker<'a>`**
  a marker on the x axis: a line at t0, or the range t0 .. t1 shaded (fault injections)
  - `t0: f64`
  - `t1: f64` -- &lt;= t0: a line
  - `label: &'a str` -- a short label in a tag at the top of the plot ("" none)
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB, 0 = T_TEXT2

**`impl<'a> LcMarker<'a>`**

- **`const fn line(t: f64, label: &'a str) -> LcMarker<'a>`**
  a line at t
- **`const fn range(t0: f64, t1: f64, label: &'a str) -> LcMarker<'a>`**
  the range t0 .. t1
- **`const fn color(mut self, c: u32) -> LcMarker<'a>`**
  the same marker in a colour

- **`struct LcThreshold<'a>`**
  a threshold: a dashed horizontal line at a value with a label at its right end
  - `value: f64`
  - `label: &'a str`
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB, 0 = T_TEXT2

**`impl<'a> LcThreshold<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(value: f64, label: &'a str) -> LcThreshold<'a>`**
  a threshold at value with its label, in T_TEXT2
- **`const fn color(mut self, c: u32) -> LcThreshold<'a>`**
  the same threshold in a colour

- **`struct LineChart<'a>`**
  what ui.line_chart shows: the series and how (see the module header of chart.rs); build
  it with LineChart::new(&series) and the setters, or change the fields
  - `series: &'a [LcSeries<'a>]`
  - `x: u8` -- the x axis: LX_SECS (default), LX_NANOS or LX_NUM
  - `x_range: (f64, f64)` -- the visible x range (the points' units); empty (the default) = the data's
  - `x_span: f64` -- follow live: without x_range the newest x_span of the data (0 = all of it)
  - `y_range: (f64, f64)` -- the y range; a NaN end (the default) is automatic: the visible values and the
    thresholds, out to the next tick.  (0.0, f64::NAN): from zero (metrics)
  - `markers: &'a [LcMarker<'a>]`
  - `thresholds: &'a [LcThreshold<'a>]`
  - `flags: u32` -- LC_\*
  - `name: &'a str` -- the chart's name: the start of its summary (screen readers)
  - `empty: &'a str` -- the text without points ("" = "Keine Daten" in the UI language)

**`impl<'a> LineChart<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(series: &'a [LcSeries<'a>]) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  the series over time in seconds, both ranges automatic
- **`const fn x_axis(mut self, x: u8) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  the x axis: LX_SECS, LX_NANOS or LX_NUM
- **`const fn x_range(mut self, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  a fixed x range (a paused view)
- **`const fn follow(mut self, span: f64) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  follow live: the newest `span` of the data
- **`const fn y_range(mut self, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  the y range (a NaN end: automatic)
- **`const fn markers(mut self, m: &'a [LcMarker<'a>]) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  markers on the x axis (lines and shaded ranges with tags)
- **`const fn thresholds(mut self, t: &'a [LcThreshold<'a>]) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  thresholds (dashed lines with tags)
- **`const fn flags(mut self, f: u32) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  LC_\* flags
- **`const fn name(mut self, n: &'a str) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  the name its summary starts with
- **`const fn empty(mut self, s: &'a str) -> LineChart<'a>`**
  the text of the empty chart
- **`fn view(&self) -> (f64, f64)`**
  the x range the chart shows (the points' units): x_range when it is set, else the
  data's -- with x_span the newest x_span of it (from the first point on while the
  data is shorter: it grows from the left); without points 0 .. x_span (or one second)

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn sparkline(&mut self, id: u32, values: &[f32], color: u32)`**
  ui_sparkline(id, values, color): area + line over the values (min .. max scaled)
- **`fn bar_chart(&mut self, id: u32, labels: &[&str], series: &[BarSeries], stacked: bool) -> i32`**
  ui_bar_chart(id, labels, series, stacked) -> the hovered column (-1 = none)
- **`fn donut(&mut self, id: u32, slices: &[DonutSlice], center: &str, sub: &str)`**
  ui_donut(id, slices, center, sub): ring of slices (fractions of their sum) with a
  centre text (TS_SUBTITLE; TS_BODY_STRONG where that is wider than the hole) and a
  caption below it (left out where the hole is too low for both)
- **`fn legend(&mut self, items: &[(&str, u32)])`**
  ui_legend(items): a colour dot and a label per item (colour 0 = palette by index),
  laid out in a wrapping row; an item wider than the row has its label cut with "…"
- **`fn line_chart(&mut self, id: u32, c: &LineChart) -> Option<(usize, f64)>`**
  ui_line_chart(id, chart) -> the hovered series and the x it snapped to: series over
  time (or plain numbers) with axes, grid, legend, markers, thresholds and a hover card
  (see the module header of chart.rs)

### Toasts, spinners, progress

Source: [`lib/ui/notify.rs`](../lib/ui/notify.rs)

```text
notify -- transient feedback: toasts, spinner, indeterminate progress

  toast(kind, title, msg, ms)         queue a notification card (IB_INFO .. IB_ERROR; ms 0
                                      = 5 s, u32::MAX = until closed); returns its id
  toast_host()                        draw the queued toasts (bottom right, newest at the
                                      bottom, above dialogs); call it once per frame after
                                      the content.  Hovering keeps a toast; its close button
                                      removes it; expiry wakes the loop (timer UIT_TOAST).
  toast_dismiss(id) / toast_clear()
  toasts() -> [(id, kind, title, msg)]   the queued toasts (a notification history)
  spinner(id, size_dip)               a turning ring while something loads
  progress_indeterminate(id)          a bar with a running segment (natural 200 x 4 DIP)
The animations keep the window repainting while they are shown.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn toast(&mut self, kind: u32, title: &str, msg: &str, ms: u32) -> u32`**
  ui_toast(kind, title, msg, ms) -> toast id
- **`fn toast_dismiss(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  ui_toast_dismiss(id)
- **`fn toast_clear(&mut self)`**
  ui_toast_clear
- **`fn toasts(&self) -> Vec<(u32, u32, String, String)>`**
  the queued toasts: (id, kind, title, message)
- **`fn toast_host(&mut self)`**
  ui_toast_host: draw the toasts (once per frame, after the content)
- **`fn spinner(&mut self, id: u32, size: i32)`**
  ui_spinner(id, size_dip): a turning ring
- **`fn progress_indeterminate(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  ui_progress_indeterminate(id): a bar with a running segment

datepick -- date and time input

  time_box(id, &mut hour, &mut minute) -> EV    two number boxes "HH : MM" (EV_ACT changed)
  weekday_toggles(id, &mut mask) -> EV          seven toggle buttons, bit 0 = Monday ..
                                                bit 6 = Sunday (EV_ACT changed); they wrap
                                                where the row is narrower (BOX_WRAP)

                                                i18n::fmt_date) that opens a month calendar

Ids: parts (id << 3 | k) | 0x80000000; calendar days ((id ^ 0x3C3C) << 6 | cell) | 0x80000000.
