TB_HYPHENATE: u32 = 0x0080_0000  // with TB_MULTI | TB_WRAP: hyphenate words that do not fit (hyph.rs)
TB_PASSWORD: u32 = 0x0100_0000  // a dot per character; no copy / cut
TB_READONLY: u32 = 0x0200_0000  // selectable and copyable, not editable
TB_DIGITS: u32 = 0x0400_0000  // accept only 0-9
TB_MULTI: u32 = 0x0800_0000  // multi-line
TB_SIGNED: u32 = 0x1000_0000  // with TB_DIGITS: also '-'
TB_DECIMAL: u32 = 0x2000_0000  // with TB_DIGITS: also ',' and '.'
TB_WRAP: u32 = 0x4000_0000  // with TB_MULTI: wrap long lines at the box width
TB_SPELL: u32 = 0x8000_0000  // spell checking: misspelled words underlined, suggestions (edit_spell.rs)
UIT_CARET: u32 = 0x7FFE_0001  // timer id of the caret blink
```

### Other modules

#### `ui/a11y.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/a11y.rs`](../lib/ui/a11y.rs)

```text
a11y -- the semantic records as the platform's accessibility tree (plat::a11y): after the
passes of a frame the records of every shown window become a snapshot that screen readers
read through AT-SPI2 (Linux), UI Automation (Windows), the browser's ARIA shadow tree or
Android's virtual views; their actions come back as requests that the next passes carry
out through the widgets' own behaviour.

  a11y_tree() -> plat::a11y::Snapshot   the tree as assistive technology gets it
Runtime (runtime.rs): a11y_frame after the passes (publishes while plat::a11y::active();
starts the bridge with the first window frame and hands it i18n::tr for the names of the
roles: plat::a11y::set_translator), a11y_poll on E_WAKE (takes the requests).
Widgets: behave asks a11y_click(id) (a pending click, toggle, select or open acts like
Space on the focused widget: EV_ACT); the sliders ask a11y_value(id), the text boxes
a11y_text(id) for a new value (both public for widgets of an app's own).  A click no widget took in its passes becomes a pointer
click in the middle of the record.

The tree: every record of a window becomes a node in the record order -- roles from the
kinds (K_*), states from SS_* (a check box with value 2 is mixed), a heading's level from its
value (K_HEADING: Node::value, clamped to 1 ..= 9).  Left out: title bars, empty texts,
records without area, boxes without a label (a box with tab records inside is the tab
strip).  Containers are lists, dialogs, titled boxes and tab strips: a node's parent is the
smallest one on its layer whose rectangle holds the node's centre.  Menu bar entries next to
each other get a menu bar; the rows of a popup (menus, drop-downs) a menu or list that hangs
below the open record that opened it.  Names: the label; text boxes, drop-downs (their label
is the text / the choice), sliders, progress bars and lists without one take the text or
heading record right before them (to the left, or above and aligned).  The focus of a list
or tab strip is passed on to its selected row / tab.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn a11y_tree(&self) -> Snapshot`**
  The accessibility tree of the last pass as assistive technology gets it (screen
  readers through AT-SPI2 / UI Automation): every shown window with its nodes (roles,
  names, states, values, rectangles), built from the semantic records (see sem()).
- **`fn a11y_value(&mut self, id: u32) -> Option<i32>`**
  A value a screen reader set for slider-like widget `id` (its record's value scale),
  taken once: the built-in sliders apply it themselves; a widget of its own applies it
  like keyboard input (clamped) in the pass it is built.
- **`fn a11y_text(&mut self, id: u32) -> Option<String>`**
  A text a screen reader set for text widget `id`, taken once (the built-in text boxes
  apply it themselves).

#### `ui/agent.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/agent.rs`](../lib/ui/agent.rs)

```text
Universal application automation through the existing input, command and render paths.
Domain semantics remain in App::actions/action; no screen-coordinate inference is used.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn agent_enabled(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether external control was explicitly activated. No endpoint opens by reading this.
- **`fn agent_connected(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether the active control session has received a client request.
- **`fn set_agent_enabled(&mut self, enabled: bool)`**
  Enable or revoke external control. Revocation also discards screenshot resources.

**`impl Runtime`**

- **`fn set_agent_enabled(&mut self, enabled: bool)`**
  Explicitly opt into the same control dispatcher used by native JSON/MCP sessions.
- **`fn control(&mut self, session: &mut agent_core::RpcSession, line: &[u8]) -> Option<String>`**
  Handle one control request without IO. The caller owns one session per connection.

#### `ui/assoc.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/assoc.rs`](../lib/ui/assoc.rs)

```text
assoc -- the app's file types and URL schemes at start-up (plat::assoc): the switches every
app gets through ui::main!

  --register            register this program for PACKAGE filetypes= / schemes= (Windows:
                        HKCU\Software\Classes; Linux: a .desktop file, the own MIME types,
                        mimeapps.list); defaults of other programs stay and are listed
  --register-replace    the same, and those defaults go to this app too (the user's own pick
                        in Windows' dialog always stays)
  --unregister          remove exactly what the registration added, put back what it replaced
They print what they did (a Windows GUI program: on the console it was started from) and end
the program: exit code 0 done, 1 failed, 2 not possible here or nothing declared.

  desk_boot(package) -> Option<exit code>   (main!) keep the built-in PACKAGE text
                        (plat::assoc::package_set), run a switch; headless runs (--shot,
                        --script, the agent protocols) leave the system's list of recent files
                        alone (plat::recent::recent_os(false); jfgui_RECENT still redirects it).
                        Without a switch, Windows: the app id as the explicit AppUserModelID
                        once the setup installed the program or --register registered it
                        (plat::assoc::app_id_boot), before the first window
  assoc_switch(pkg, switch) -> Option<(exit code, text)>   one switch for pkg (None: no switch)
```

- **`fn desk_boot(package: Option<&str>) -> Option<i32>`**
  (main!) PACKAGE, then the switches -> Some(exit code) when one of them ran

- **`fn assoc_switch(pkg: &Package, switch: &str) -> Option<(i32, String)>`**
  run --register / --register-replace / --unregister for pkg -> (exit code, what it says)

#### `ui/diagram.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/diagram.rs`](../lib/ui/diagram.rs)

```text
diagram -- a node / edge canvas: zoom and pan, grid and snapping, a spatial index, hit
testing, selection (click, marquee, keyboard), moving, connecting, waypoints, a minimap and
one semantic record per visible node.  The app owns the model and paints it; the widget
keeps the view, the selection and the gestures in DiagramState and reports what the user
did as DEv events.

  ui.diagram(id, &mut st, &m, tool, paint, ver) -> Vec<DEv>
                                  the canvas in the next layout slot (size it with
                                  next_size); tool DG_SELECT / DG_PAN / DG_CONNECT /
                                  DG_PLACE; paint draws the content at render time
                                  (DgPaint); ver stands for everything it shows besides the
                                  geometry (labels, states, colours)
  ui.diagram_minimap(id, &mut st, &m) -> bool    an overview in the bottom right corner of
                                  the canvas; pressing / dragging there moves the view
  ui.diagram_sems(id, &mut st, &m, &label)   one K_LISTITEM record per visible node
                                  (scripts: click listitem:"R1"; screen readers), no hit box
  ui.diagram_edge_sems(id, &mut st, &m, &label)   the same for the visible edges (a box
                                  around the middle of the route); st.tab_edges lets Tab
                                  walk them after the nodes, st.name names the canvas
  Viewport::{scale, to_screen, to_world, world_rect, rect_to_screen, zoom_at, step, fit}
  dg_paint_grid(g, vp, step, minor, major)   grid lines inside the clip (render time)
  dg_edge_points(m, i, &mut out)  the route of edge i (world polyline) without a state
  dg_stroke_edge(g, vp, pts, width, argb, cap0, cap1, dash)   stroke a route (gfx::dash
                                  caps LCAP_* and patterns DASH_*), culled by the clip
  dg_point_at(pts, f) -> point    the point at fraction f of a route's length (packets)
  dg_hairline(g, vp, pts, argb)   a route as 1 px anti-aliased lines: far cheaper than
                                  dg_stroke_edge for many thin edges (DgFrame::moving)
  DgFrame::find(margin, edges)    the nodes or edges near the clip (the spatial buckets)

Model (DModel, borrowed every frame): nodes with a world rectangle and a range of ports,
ports at a position relative to their node's top left corner, edges from key a to key b
(a port, or a node: then the route starts on its border) with a route DR_STRAIGHT /
DR_BEZIER / DR_ORTHO through a range of waypoints.  Keys are non-zero and unique over
nodes, ports and edges; later nodes lie on top.  ver changes whenever the geometry
changes: the key maps, the routes and the spatial buckets (256 world units) are rebuilt
then.  World units are DIP at zoom 1.

Input: the hit test prefers the handles of selected edges (waypoints, then the middles of
their stretches), then the ports of the node under the pointer, the topmost node, the
nearest edge (max(5 DIP, half the edge width + 3 DIP)), the background.  A press + drag
(4 DIP) on a selected node moves the selection (snapped to the grid, Alt: free), from a
port connects, on a handle moves or inserts a waypoint, on the background draws a marquee
(Shift adds, Ctrl toggles); middle drag, Space + drag and DG_PAN pan; the wheel scrolls
(Shift: sideways), Ctrl + wheel zooms at the pointer.  Keys while the canvas has the focus:
arrows nudge the selection (grid steps, Shift x10, Alt 1) or pan, Del, Ctrl+A, Esc cancels
a gesture (else clears the selection), Tab / Shift+Tab walk the nodes (with tab_edges then
the edges, a focused edge drawn with the focus ring along its route; the focus leaves after
the last), Enter activates, Ctrl + plus / minus zoom, Ctrl+0 fits, Shift+F10 / the menu key
ask for the context menu.  DiagramState::test_keys stands in for held keys in scripts.
Drawing: the paint runs as one custom command whose version covers ver, the model version,
the view, the theme and the gesture flag; selection, hover, ports, handles, marquee and rubber
band are recorded commands on top, so hovering redraws only their cells.  The paint draws the
whole canvas into a backing store (an XRGB surface of the DiagramState) once per version;
every dirty rectangle copies its part out of it.  Skip what lies outside DgFrame::clip
(DgFrame::find asks the spatial buckets).  While a gesture moves the view or nodes (a pan,
wheel turns until MOVING_MS after the last one, a drag of nodes or a waypoint)
DgFrame::moving asks for less detail; a full paint follows the gesture.  Content that moves
every frame (packets) is best drawn after diagram() with ui.draw_* inside
ui.clip_push(st.vp.rect).
```

```rust
/// tools of ui.diagram
DG_SELECT: u32 = 0  // select, move, connect from ports, waypoints
DG_PAN: u32 = 1  // a left drag pans
DG_CONNECT: u32 = 2  // a drag (or two clicks) from a node / port to another connects
DG_PLACE: u32 = 3  // a click reports DEv::Click (snapped) to place something
/// edge routes (DEdge::route)
DR_STRAIGHT: u8 = 0
DR_BEZIER: u8 = 1
DR_ORTHO: u8 = 2  // horizontal and vertical stretches (L / Z shapes)
/// node flags (DNode::flags)
DN_LOCKED: u32 = 1  // never moved by the widget
DN_NOSELECT: u32 = 2  // decoration: never hit nor selected
/// port flags (DPort::flags)
DPT_HIDDEN: u32 = 1  // neither shown nor hit
DPT_USED: u32 = 2  // shown filled (connected)
```

- **`struct Viewport`**
  what part of the world the canvas shows: zoom (DIP per world unit, 1 = 100 %), the world
  point at the centre of rect; rect (absolute px) and dpi are kept by ui.diagram
  - `zoom: f32`
  - `cx: f64`
  - `cy: f64`
  - `rect: [i32; 4]`
  - `dpi: i32`

**`impl Viewport`**

- **`const ZOOM_MIN: f32 = 0.1`**
- **`const ZOOM_MAX: f32 = 8.0`**
- **`fn scale(&self) -> f64`**
  px per world unit
- **`fn to_screen(&self, p: [f32; 2]) -> [f32; 2]`**
  a world point in absolute px
- **`fn to_world(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> [f32; 2]`**
  an absolute px position in world units
- **`fn world_rect(&self) -> [f32; 4]`**
  the world rectangle x0, y0, x1, y1 the canvas shows
- **`fn rect_to_screen(&self, r: [f32; 4]) -> [f32; 4]`**
  a world rectangle x, y, w, h in px (x, y, w, h, fractional)
- **`fn zoom_at(&mut self, zoom: f32, sx: f32, sy: f32)`**
  zoom (clamped) keeping the world point under the absolute px (sx, sy) in place
- **`fn step(&mut self, dir: i32, sx: f32, sy: f32)`**
  the next zoom step above (dir > 0) or below around the absolute px (sx, sy)
- **`fn fit(&mut self, b: [f32; 4], margin: i32)`**
  show the world rectangle b (x0, y0, x1, y1) with `margin` DIP around it, at most 100 %

- **`struct DNode`**
  a node: world rectangle x, y, w, h, its ports (a range of DModel::ports), DN_\* flags
  - `key: u64`
  - `rect: [f32; 4]`
  - `ports: Range<u32>`
  - `flags: u32`

- **`struct DPort`**
  a port: its position relative to the node's top left corner, DPT_\* flags
  - `key: u64`
  - `at: [f32; 2]`
  - `flags: u32`

- **`struct DEdge`**
  an edge from key a to key b (ports or nodes) along route DR_\* through a range of
  DModel::wps
  - `key: u64`
  - `a: u64`
  - `b: u64`
  - `route: u8`
  - `wps: Range<u32>`

- **`struct DModel<'a>`**
  the app's diagram, borrowed for one call; ver changes with every geometry change
  - `nodes: &'a [DNode]`
  - `ports: &'a [DPort]`
  - `edges: &'a [DEdge]`
  - `wps: &'a [[f32; 2]]`
  - `ver: u32`

- **`enum DHit`**
  what a point of the canvas shows
  - `None`
  - `Node(u64)`
  - `Port(u64)`
  - `Edge { key: u64, seg: u32, t: f32 }` -- an edge: seg = the stretch between its defining points seg and seg + 1 (0 = the
    start, then the waypoints), t = 0..1 along it
  - `Waypoint(u64, u32)` -- the handle of waypoint idx of a selected edge
  - `Mid(u64, u32)` -- the handle in the middle of stretch idx of a selected edge (a drag inserts waypoint idx)

**`impl DHit`**

- **`fn key(&self) -> u64`**
  the node, port or edge key (0 = the background)

- **`enum DEv`**
  what the user did (ui.diagram's result, in order)
  - `Select` -- st.sel changed
  - `Move { keys: Vec<u64>, d: [f32; 2], total: [f32; 2], done: bool }` -- move nodes `keys` by d (world units); the d of one gesture add up to total; done = the
    gesture ended (released, a key nudge; Esc sends d = minus everything so far)
  - `Connect { from: u64, to: u64, quick: bool }` -- connect from -> to (port or node keys); quick = dragged out of a port with DG_SELECT
  - `ConnectDrag { from: u64, at: [f32; 2], over: u64 }` -- a connection is being drawn: the pointer at `at`, over port / node `over` (0 = none)
  - `ConnectCancel` -- the connection ended without a target (released elsewhere, Esc)
  - `Waypoint { edge: u64, idx: u32, at: [f32; 2], insert: bool, done: bool }` -- waypoint idx of edge goes to at; insert = add it at idx first (the first event of a
    drag from a middle handle); done = released
  - `WaypointDelete { edge: u64, idx: u32 }` -- remove waypoint idx of edge (double click on its handle, Esc after an insert)
  - `Activate(DHit)` -- double click on a node / port / edge, Enter on the focused node
  - `Context(DHit, [i32; 2])` -- right click, Shift+F10 or the menu key: at = window px (logical, for popups)
  - `Delete` -- Del with a selection: delete st.sel
  - `Click { at: [f32; 2] }` -- a click on the background, or anywhere with DG_PLACE (snapped then); world units
  - `ViewChanged` -- zoom or centre changed

- **`struct DgRoute`**
  an edge's route in world units: the polyline, the indices of its defining points (a, the
  waypoints, b) in it, its bounding box x0, y0, x1, y1 (empty pts: an end is unknown)
  - `key: u64`
  - `pts: Vec<[f32; 2]>`
  - `marks: Vec<u32>`
  - `bb: [f32; 4]`

- **`struct DgGeo`**
  the routes of every edge in model order and the spatial buckets of nodes and edges, built
  once per model version (DgFrame::find asks the buckets)
  - `routes: Vec<DgRoute>`

- **`struct DgFrame<'a>`**
  what a DgPaint gets at render time
  - `vp: Viewport`
  - `clip: [f32; 4]` -- the world rectangle x0, y0, x1, y1 that needs pixels now: skip what lies outside
  - `geo: &'a DgGeo`
  - `theme: &'a [u32]` -- the theme's colours (color(T_\*)), the canvas background (opaque)
  - `bg: u32`
  - `fonts: [(u32, i32); 7]` -- font and size (24.8 px at zoom 1) of every TS_\* text style
  - `dark: bool`
  - `moving: bool` -- a gesture moves the view or nodes (a pan, wheel turns, a drag of nodes or a waypoint):
    leave out what costs and nobody reads in passing (small labels; plain shapes,
    dg_hairline); the canvas is painted in full after it

**`impl DgFrame<'_>`**

- **`fn color(&self, tok: u32) -> u32`**
  0xAARRGGBB of a theme token
- **`fn visible(&self, r: [f32; 4]) -> bool`**
  the world rectangle x, y, w, h (with 2 px for anti-aliasing) touches the clip
- **`fn route_visible(&self, rt: &DgRoute, width: f32) -> bool`**
  a route stroked `width` world units wide (dg_stroke_edge, arrow heads included)
  touches the clip
- **`fn find(&self, margin: f32, edges: bool) -> Vec<u32>`**
  the nodes (edges = false: DModel::nodes) or the edges whose spatial buckets touch the
  clip grown by `margin` px: ascending indices, a superset of what can need paint (cheaper
  than looking at all of them)
- **`fn font(&self, ts: u32) -> (u32, i32)`**
  font and size (24.8 px) of text style ts at the current zoom

- **`trait DgPaint`**
  the app's painting of a diagram (render time): nodes, edges (DgFrame::geo), labels; it
  runs once per dirty rectangle, so skip what DgFrame::visible / route_visible reject
  - `fn paint(&self, g: &mut Gfx, f: &DgFrame)`

- **`struct DiagramState`**
  the widget's state, kept by the app: the view, the selection (node and edge keys), the
  focused node, grid and snapping, the hover, the gesture in progress and the index
  - `vp: Viewport`
  - `sel: BTreeSet<u64>`
  - `focus: u64` -- the node with the keyboard focus (0 = none): Tab walks, Enter activates it
  - `grid: f32` -- grid step in world units (0 = no grid)
  - `snap: bool` -- moves, waypoints and DG_PLACE clicks snap to the grid (Alt held: free)
  - `hover: DHit` -- what the pointer is over (after the last diagram call)
  - `edge_width: f32` -- the stroke width of the edges in world units (hit testing, the highlight)
  - `test_keys: u32` -- scripts cannot hold keys: 1 = as if Space were held, 2 = Ctrl
  - `tab_edges: bool` -- Tab / Shift+Tab also walk the edges (after the nodes, in model order): the focused
    edge is selected, Enter activates it, the menu key asks for its context menu
  - `name: String` -- the canvas' name for screen readers (its K_CANVAS record; empty: none)

**`impl DiagramState`**

- **`fn new() -> DiagramState`**
  grid 16, snapping on, edges 2 units wide; the first diagram call fits the content
- **`fn request_fit(&mut self)`**
  fit the whole content into the view with the next diagram call
- **`fn busy(&self) -> bool`**
  a gesture (drag, marquee, connection, pan) is in progress
- **`fn route(&self, key: u64) -> Option<&DgRoute>`**
  the route of edge `key` (as of the last diagram call)
- **`fn geo(&self) -> &Rc<DgGeo>`**
  every route (model order), shared with the paint
- **`fn bounds(&self) -> Option<[f32; 4]>`**
  the bounding box x0, y0, x1, y1 of nodes and routes (None: empty)
- **`fn visible(&self) -> &[u32]`**
  the indices of the nodes the canvas showed in the last diagram call

**`impl DgGeo`**

- **`fn find(&self, r: [f32; 4], edges: bool, out: &mut Vec<u32>)`**
  the indices of the nodes (edges = false) or edges whose buckets touch r (world x0, y0,
  x1, y1), ascending: a superset of what overlaps it (all when r spans too many buckets)

- **`fn dg_length(pts: &[[f32; 2]]) -> f32`**
  the length of a polyline

- **`fn dg_point_at(pts: &[[f32; 2]], f: f32) -> [f32; 2]`**
  the point at fraction f (0..1) of a polyline's length (a packet travelling along an edge)

- **`fn dg_edge_points(m: &DModel, i: usize, out: &mut Vec<[f32; 2]>)`**
  the route of edge i of m (world polyline) into out, without a DiagramState (ports and
  nodes are looked up linearly; DiagramState::route has them indexed)

- **`fn dg_paint_grid(g: &mut Gfx, vp: &Viewport, step: f32, minor: u32, major: u32)`**
  grid lines every `step` world units (every fifth in `major`) inside the clip and the
  canvas; steps closer than 8 px are widened five times

- **`fn dg_stroke_edge(g: &mut Gfx, vp: &Viewport, pts: &[[f32; 2]], width: f32, argb: u32, cap0: u32, cap1: u32, dash: u32)`**
  stroke a route (world points) `width` world units wide (at least 1 px) in argb, with
  gfx::dash caps (LCAP_\*: arrows at an end) and pattern DASH_\*; nothing when it misses the
  clip

- **`fn dg_hairline(g: &mut Gfx, vp: &Viewport, pts: &[[f32; 2]], argb: u32)`**
  a route (world points) as 1 px anti-aliased lines in argb (Xiaolin Wu): a fraction of
  dg_stroke_edge's cost for many thin edges (the level of detail of DgFrame::moving); nothing
  outside the clip

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn diagram(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut DiagramState, m: &DModel, tool: u32, paint: Option<Rc<dyn DgPaint>>, ver: u32) -> Vec<DEv>`**
  ui_diagram(id, st, m, tool, paint, ver) -> what the user did: the node / edge canvas
  in the next layout slot (see the file header)
- **`fn diagram_minimap(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut DiagramState, m: &DModel) -> bool`**
  ui_diagram_minimap(id, st, m) -> the view moved: an overview of the nodes and the
  shown part in the bottom right corner of the last diagram (nothing when the canvas is
  small); pressing or dragging there centres the view on that point
- **`fn diagram_sems(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut DiagramState, m: &DModel, label: &dyn Fn(u64) -> String)`**
  ui_diagram_sems(id, st, m, label): one K_LISTITEM record per node the last diagram
  call showed (label(key), value = the node's index, selected / focused / hover states),
  cut to the canvas; a screen reader's click on one selects it
- **`fn diagram_edge_sems(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut DiagramState, m: &DModel, label: &dyn Fn(u64) -> String)`**
  ui_diagram_edge_sems(id, st, m, label): one K_LISTITEM record per edge the last diagram
  call showed (label(key); value = the edge's index; selected / focused / hover states),
  a small box around the middle of its route cut to the canvas, after the nodes' records;
  a screen reader's click on one selects the edge (and focuses it with tab_edges)

#### `ui/md_doc.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/md_doc.rs`](../lib/ui/md_doc.rs)

```text
md_doc -- the document of the Markdown / HTML viewer (md_view.rs): blocks of formatted text,
read from Markdown (CommonMark with GitHub's tables, task lists, strikethrough and bare
links) or from HTML (the reader of the rich-text editor, rich_html.rs)

  MdDoc::markdown(s) / MdDoc::html(s)  parse; never panics, takes linear time: nesting, input
                                       size and the inline parser's work are capped
  doc.blocks() -> &[MdBlock]           the blocks in reading order (see MdBlock)
  doc.links() / images() / tables()    link targets (MdSpan::link - 1), images (MdSpan::image
                                       - 1: src, alt, title, size), table column alignments
  doc.plain() / doc.to_html()          everything as text (list markers, cells by tabs) / HTML
  doc.plain_range(a, b) / html_range(a, b)   a part: TextPos { line: block, byte }
  doc.link_spots()                     every link in reading order (block, bytes, link)
  doc.forms() / fields() / field_spots()   the forms of HTML, their fields (MdSpan::field - 1;
                                       hidden ones have no character; their first values:
                                       md_view keeps the current ones) and where the visible
                                       ones stand in reading order; field.caption(): a
                                       button's caption
  doc.truncated()                      a limit cut the input
  HTML documents keep their element tree (md_dom.rs: queries, changes of text, attributes,
  classes and structure; MdNode handles that stay the same across changes); the blocks,
  fields and forms name their elements (MdBlock::node, MdField::node, MdForm::node).
  doc.update() -> the blocks were derived again after changes: in place when every change
                                       lies inside block elements that show one paragraph of
                                       text by themselves (no links, images, fields, blocks in
                                       it: O(that paragraph)), else all of them (linear, no
                                       layout); md_view.rs keeps its place, selection, focus,
                                       the fields' values and the layouts that still hold
  doc.field_of(n) -> the field of element n

The model: a block is a paragraph, a heading (level 1..6), a code block (its text, the
language of the fence), a rule or a table row (cells: byte ranges of the text, '\t' between
them).  Its place: `quote` (block quotes around it), `list` (lists around it), `marker` /
`number` / `task` (it starts a list item), `space` (the gap before it: 0 none, 1 a tight
list's, 2 a paragraph's).  Its text holds the visible characters (an image is one U+FFFC,
a hard break '\n'); spans give ranges their style (MS_*), link, image and colours.

Markdown: ATX and setext headings, paragraphs with lazy continuation lines, block quotes,
bullet (- + *) and ordered (1. 1)) lists with start numbers, tight / loose spacing and task
items ([ ] / [x]), fenced (``` ~~~ with an info string) and indented code, thematic breaks,
GFM tables (alignment row, escaped pipes), HTML blocks (through the HTML reader), link
reference definitions; inline: backslash escapes, entities, code spans, emphasis and strong
emphasis (the delimiter algorithm with the rule of three), ~~strikethrough~~, links and
images (inline, full / collapsed / shortcut references, titles), autolinks (<...>, bare
http:// https:// www.), hard breaks (two spaces, backslash) and soft breaks, a little inline
HTML (br, b / strong, i / em, s / del, u / ins, code / kbd, a href, img).  Other tags are
dropped, their text stays.  Tabs expand to 4 columns.

Forms (HTML, also in Markdown's HTML blocks): <form action method> (forms do not nest),
<input> of type text (and the other text types: email, search, url, tel, number ...),
password, checkbox, radio, hidden, submit, image (a submit button), reset and button,
<textarea> (its text read raw, one leading line end dropped), <select> with <option value
selected> (one choice), <button type> (its text the caption), <label> (around a field or
for= its id: the field's name; aria-label wins, title is the last resort) and form= (a field
outside its form).  A field is one U+FFFC in the text with a span of its own (MdSpan::field);
a disabled check box at the start of a list item is that item's task box (as Markdown's
"[x]" is written out by html_range).
```

```rust
/// MdBlock::kind: a paragraph
MB_PARA: u8 = 0
/// a heading (MdBlock::level 1 ..= 6)
MB_HEADING: u8 = 1
/// a code block (MdBlock::lang: the fence's language)
MB_CODE: u8 = 2
/// a thematic break (no text)
MB_RULE: u8 = 3
/// a table row (MdBlock::cells, table, head)
MB_ROW: u8 = 4
/// MdSpan::style: strong
MS_BOLD: u16 = 1
/// emphasis
MS_ITALIC: u16 = 2
/// struck through
MS_STRIKE: u16 = 4
/// code (monospace)
MS_CODE: u16 = 8
/// underlined (HTML)
MS_UNDER: u16 = 16
/// MdBlock::marker: no list item starts here
MK_NONE: u8 = 0
/// a bullet item
MK_BULLET: u8 = 1
/// a numbered item (MdBlock::number, delim)
MK_NUMBER: u8 = 2
/// MdTable::aligns: not given
MA_NONE: u8 = 0
/// left (start)
MA_LEFT: u8 = 1
/// centred
MA_CENTER: u8 = 2
/// right (end)
MA_RIGHT: u8 = 3
/// MdField::kind: a one-line text field (<input> of type text, email, search, url, tel,
/// number and every type not named below)
MF_TEXT: u8 = 0
/// a password field (its text never leaves the view but in the form's data)
MF_PASSWORD: u8 = 1
/// a check box
MF_CHECKBOX: u8 = 2
/// a radio button: one of the radios of its form with its name
MF_RADIO: u8 = 3
/// a hidden field (no character in the text)
MF_HIDDEN: u8 = 4
/// a text area (<textarea>: several lines)
MF_TEXTAREA: u8 = 5
/// a drop-down list (<select>)
MF_SELECT: u8 = 6
/// a submit button (<button>, <input type=submit> / image)
MF_SUBMIT: u8 = 7
/// a reset button: the form's fields get their first values back
MF_RESET: u8 = 8
/// a button without an action of its own (<button type=button>, <input type=button>)
MF_BUTTON: u8 = 9
```

- **`struct MdSpan`**
  a range of a block's text with its style
  - `a: u32` -- bytes a .. b of the block's text
  - `b: u32`
  - `style: u16` -- MS_\*
  - `link: u32` -- a link: index + 1 into MdDoc::links (0: none)
  - `image: u32` -- an image (the text is U+FFFC): index + 1 into MdDoc::images (0: none)
  - `color: u32` -- HTML colours 0xAARRGGBB (0: the theme's)
  - `bg: u32`
  - `field: u32` -- a form field (the text is U+FFFC): index + 1 into MdDoc::fields (0: none)

- **`struct MdBlock`**
  a block of the document (see the module header)
  - `kind: u8` -- MB_\*
  - `level: u8` -- headings: 1 ..= 6
  - `text: String` -- the visible text (U+FFFC an image, '\\n' a hard break or a code line's end, '\\t' between
    cells)
  - `spans: Vec<MdSpan>` -- styled ranges, ascending, not overlapping (the text between them is plain)
  - `quote: u8` -- block quotes around it
  - `list: u8` -- lists around it (0: none)
  - `path: u32` -- the containers from the outside in: bit i set = the i-th is a block quote, clear = a
    list
  - `marker: u8` -- MK_\*: a list item starts with this block
  - `number: u32` -- MK_NUMBER: the item's number and its delimiter ('.' or ')')
  - `delim: u8`
  - `task: u8` -- a task item: 0 none, 1 open, 2 done
  - `space: u8` -- the gap before it: 0 none, 1 a tight list's, 2 a paragraph's
  - `lang: String` -- code blocks: the language of the fence ("" none)
  - `cells: Vec<(u32, u32)>` -- table rows: the cells' byte ranges
  - `table: u32` -- table rows: index into MdDoc::tables, a header row
  - `head: bool`
  - `align: u8` -- paragraphs: 0 start, 1 centre, 2 end (HTML)
  - `node: MdNode` -- HTML: the element whose content it shows (the innermost block element: p, li, h1, the
    row of a cell ...; MdNode::NONE: none, Markdown)

- **`struct MdImage`**
  an image of the document
  - `src: String`
  - `alt: String`
  - `title: String`
  - `w: u32` -- size given by HTML attributes (px, 0: the picture's)
  - `h: u32`

- **`struct MdTable`**
  a table: its columns' alignment (MA_\*)
  - `aligns: Vec<u8>`

- **`struct MdLinkSpot`**
  a link in reading order: block, bytes a .. b of its text, the link (index + 1)
  - `block: usize`
  - `a: u32`
  - `b: u32`
  - `link: u32`

- **`struct MdForm`**
  a form of HTML
  - `action: String` -- where its data goes (as written: the app resolves it) and how ("get" / "post": lower
    case, "get" when not given)
  - `method: String`
  - `id: String`
  - `name: String`
  - `node: MdNode` -- its &lt;form> element (an HTML document)

- **`struct MdOption`**
  a choice of a drop-down list: the value sent, the text shown
  - `value: String`
  - `label: String`

- **`struct MdField`**
  a field of a form (its first value: the view keeps the current one, MdViewState)
  - `kind: u8` -- MF_\*
  - `form: u32` -- its form: index + 1 into MdDoc::forms (0: none -- it sends nothing)
  - `name: String`
  - `id: String`
  - `value: String` -- text fields: the text; check boxes, radios, buttons: the value sent ("on" for check
    boxes and radios without one)
  - `label: String` -- the name screen readers say (aria-label, the &lt;label>, title); buttons: the caption
  - `placeholder: String`
  - `checked: bool` -- check boxes and radios: checked at first
  - `options: Vec<MdOption>` -- drop-down lists: the choices, the one chosen at first (-1: none)
  - `selected: i32`
  - `size: u32` -- text fields: the width in characters (size; text areas: cols; 0: the default), text
    areas: the lines (rows)
  - `rows: u32`
  - `maxlength: u32` -- at most this many characters (0: no limit)
  - `disabled: bool`
  - `readonly: bool`
  - `node: MdNode` -- its element (&lt;input>, &lt;select> ... of an HTML document; the view keeps its value while
    the element stays)

**`impl MdField`**

- **`fn caption(&self) -> &str`**
  a button's caption: its own, else "Senden" / "Zurücksetzen" (submit / reset, in the UI
  language); "" for the other kinds

- **`struct MdFieldSpot`**
  a visible field in reading order: block, byte of its U+FFFC, the field (index + 1)
  - `block: usize`
  - `a: u32`
  - `field: u32`

- **`struct MdDoc`**
  the document (see the module header)

**`impl MdDoc`**

- **`fn markdown(s: &str) -> MdDoc`**
  a document from Markdown (see the module header)
- **`fn html(s: &str) -> MdDoc`**
  a document from HTML: what the rich-text editor reads (paragraphs, headings h1 .. h6,
  lists, block quotes, formats, links, colours) and rules, images, preformatted blocks
  (&lt;pre>&lt;code class="language-x">), tables and forms (see the module header)
- **`fn update(&mut self) -> bool`**
  derive the blocks (fields, forms, links ...) again after changes of the element tree
  (md_dom.rs; the view does it every frame) -> there were changes.  In place when every
  change lies inside block elements that show one paragraph of plain formatted text by
  themselves (O(those paragraphs)), else all of them (linear in the document).
- **`fn field_of(&self, n: MdNode) -> Option<usize>`**
  the field whose element is n (an index of fields())
- **`fn blocks(&self) -> &[MdBlock]`**
  the blocks in reading order
- **`fn links(&self) -> &[String]`**
  the link targets (MdSpan::link - 1)
- **`fn link(&self, link: u32) -> &str`**
  the target of MdSpan::link (index + 1); "" for 0
- **`fn images(&self) -> &[MdImage]`**
  the images (MdSpan::image - 1)
- **`fn tables(&self) -> &[MdTable]`**
  the tables (MdBlock::table)
- **`fn link_spots(&self) -> &[MdLinkSpot]`**
  every link in reading order (adjacent spans of one link joined)
- **`fn forms(&self) -> &[MdForm]`**
  the forms (MdField::form - 1)
- **`fn fields(&self) -> &[MdField]`**
  the fields of the forms in document order (MdSpan::field - 1)
- **`fn field_spots(&self) -> &[MdFieldSpot]`**
  every visible field in reading order
- **`fn truncated(&self) -> bool`**
  a limit cut the input (size, blocks)
- **`fn end(&self) -> TextPos`**
  the place after the last character
- **`fn plain(&self) -> String`**
  the whole document as text
- **`fn to_html(&self) -> String`**
  the whole document as HTML
- **`fn plain_range(&self, a: TextPos, b: TextPos) -> String`**
  the text of a .. b: blocks on lines of their own (a blank line before paragraphs),
  list markers ("- ", "1. ", "[x] "), cells by tabs, images as their alt texts, buttons
  as their captions (the other fields: nothing)
- **`fn html_range(&self, a: TextPos, b: TextPos) -> String`**
  the HTML of a .. b: h1 .. h6, p, ul / ol / li (task items with a disabled check box),
  blockquote, pre / code (class language-x), hr, table / tr / th / td (align), strong,
  em, del, u, code, a href, img src alt, colours as span styles; of forms only the
  buttons' captions (as text)

#### `ui/md_dom.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/md_dom.rs`](../lib/ui/md_dom.rs)

```text
md_dom -- the elements of an HTML document of the viewer (MdDoc::html, md_doc.rs): a tree whose
nodes keep their identity across changes, queries by simple selectors (also the selectors of
the style sheets, rich_html.rs), changes of text, attributes, classes and structure; the
blocks follow at MdDoc::update (md_view.rs does it every frame)

  doc.root() -> MdNode                 the document: its children are the HTML's top level
  doc.by_id(id) -> Option<MdNode>      the first element in the document with this id (an
                                       index: O(log n))
  doc.select(sel) / select_first(sel)  the elements of the document a selector list matches,
                                       in document order
  doc.select_in(n, sel) / matches(n, sel)   among n's descendants / n itself
  doc.parent(n) / children(n) / next_sibling(n) / prev_sibling(n)
  doc.tag(n) ("" for a text) / is_text(n) / alive(n) / attached(n) (in the document)
  doc.attr(n, name) / attrs(n) / has_class(n, c) / text_of(n) (all its text, textContent) /
  inner_html(n)
  changes (true / a node: done; false / MdNode::NONE: a node that is gone, a Markdown
  document, a name that is none, the cap of nodes):
  doc.set_text(n, s) (an element's children become one text; they are freed) /
  set_attr(n, name, value) / remove_attr(n, name) / add_class(n, c) / remove_class(n, c) /
  toggle_class(n, c) -> on / create_element(tag) / create_text(s) (not in the document yet) /
  insert(parent, before, n) (before: None = at the end; a node in the document moves) /
  remove(n) (out of the document, kept: it may go in again) / free(n) (gone: its handles and
  those of its descendants refer to nothing) / set_inner_html(n, html)
  MdNode::raw() / MdNode::from_raw(v): a handle as a number (the objects of a script host)

The tree: HTML read the way browsers do, simplified -- void elements (br, img, input ...),
raw text (script, style, textarea, title, template, noscript, svg), a <p> closed by a block,
<li> by <li>, <dd> / <dt>, <td> / <th>, <tr>, <option> by their like, <head> by the first
element of the body; an end tag closes the elements above its own, but not across a table
cell or a button, and an inline element's end tag does not close a block (it is dropped); a
stray </p> is an empty paragraph; comments go.  Depth (DEPTH_MAX open elements: deeper ones
stay empty, their content follows them) and nodes (NODES_MAX: the rest is cut, truncated)
are capped, so parsing stays linear.

Selectors: a list (a, b) of compounds -- a tag or *, #id, .class, [attr], [attr=v] (also ~=
|= ^= $= *=, values in quotes or not) -- joined by descendant (blank) and child (>)
combinators; tags and attribute names ignore case, ids, classes and values do not.  Anything
else (pseudo-classes, sibling combinators, escapes) makes the selector match nothing.  A
match costs O(depth x compounds) per element (each run of child combinators is matched at
the nearest ancestor that takes it), a query at most a budget proportional to the tree.
```

- **`struct MdNode`**
  a node of an HTML document's element tree (an element or a text): the same across changes
  of the document; a freed node's handle refers to nothing (MdDoc::alive)

**`impl MdNode`**

- **`const NONE: MdNode = MdNode { i: 0, g: 0 }`**
  no node
- **`fn is_none(self) -> bool`**
  it is MdNode::NONE
- **`fn raw(self) -> u64`**
  the handle as a number (0: none), e.g. for a script host's objects
- **`fn from_raw(v: u64) -> MdNode`**
  the handle of raw()

**`impl MdDoc`**

- **`fn root(&self) -> MdNode`**
  the document's root (MdNode::NONE for a document from Markdown): its children are the
  top level of the HTML
- **`fn by_id(&self, id: &str) -> Option<MdNode>`**
  the first element in the document with this id
- **`fn select(&self, sel: &str) -> Vec<MdNode>`**
  the elements of the document a selector list matches, in document order (see md_dom.rs;
  a selector it does not support matches nothing)
- **`fn select_first(&self, sel: &str) -> Option<MdNode>`**
  the first element select(sel) would give
- **`fn select_in(&self, n: MdNode, sel: &str) -> Vec<MdNode>`**
  the elements below n a selector list matches, in document order
- **`fn matches(&self, n: MdNode, sel: &str) -> bool`**
  element n matches a selector list
- **`fn parent(&self, n: MdNode) -> Option<MdNode>`**
  n's parent (None: the root, a node out of the document, a node that is gone)
- **`fn children(&self, n: MdNode) -> Vec<MdNode>`**
  n's children (elements and texts) in order
- **`fn next_sibling(&self, n: MdNode) -> Option<MdNode>`**
  the node after n under the same parent
- **`fn prev_sibling(&self, n: MdNode) -> Option<MdNode>`**
  the node before n under the same parent
- **`fn tag(&self, n: MdNode) -> &str`**
  an element's tag in lower case ("" for a text, "#document" for the root)
- **`fn is_text(&self, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  n is a text
- **`fn alive(&self, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  n exists (it was not freed)
- **`fn attached(&self, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  n is in the document
- **`fn attr(&self, n: MdNode, name: &str) -> Option<&str>`**
  an attribute of element n (names in lower case)
- **`fn attrs(&self, n: MdNode) -> &[(String, String)]`**
  the attributes of element n in order (names in lower case, values decoded)
- **`fn has_class(&self, n: MdNode, c: &str) -> bool`**
  element n has class c
- **`fn text_of(&self, n: MdNode) -> String`**
  all the text of n (a text: its own; an element: that of its descendants, as textContent)
- **`fn inner_html(&self, n: MdNode) -> String`**
  the HTML of n's children
- **`fn changed(&self) -> bool`**
  the tree changed since the blocks were derived (update() derives them)
- **`fn set_text(&mut self, n: MdNode, s: &str) -> bool`**
  set n's text: a text's own; an element's children (freed) become one text
- **`fn set_attr(&mut self, n: MdNode, name: &str, value: &str) -> bool`**
  set an attribute of element n (the name in lower case; "id" updates the index)
- **`fn remove_attr(&mut self, n: MdNode, name: &str) -> bool`**
  remove an attribute of element n -> it had one
- **`fn add_class(&mut self, n: MdNode, c: &str) -> bool`**
  add class c to element n
- **`fn remove_class(&mut self, n: MdNode, c: &str) -> bool`**
  remove class c from element n -> it had it
- **`fn toggle_class(&mut self, n: MdNode, c: &str) -> bool`**
  class c on element n off when it has it, else on -> on
- **`fn create_element(&mut self, tag: &str) -> MdNode`**
  a new element (not in the document: insert puts it there) -> MdNode::NONE: a Markdown
  document, a tag that is none, the cap of nodes
- **`fn create_text(&mut self, s: &str) -> MdNode`**
  a new text (not in the document)
- **`fn insert(&mut self, parent: MdNode, before: Option<MdNode>, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  put n under element `parent` before its child `before` (None: at the end); a node with a
  parent moves -> false: a node that is gone, the root, n above parent, before no child of
  parent
- **`fn remove(&mut self, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  take n out of the document (it stays: insert may put it back; free drops it)
- **`fn free(&mut self, n: MdNode) -> bool`**
  drop n and its descendants (out of the document first): their handles refer to nothing
- **`fn set_inner_html(&mut self, n: MdNode, html: &str) -> bool`**
  element n's children (freed) become the nodes of an HTML text (raw text elements: the
  text)

#### `ui/md_view.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/md_view.rs`](../lib/ui/md_view.rs)

```text
md_view -- ui.markdown_view / ui.html_view: a read-only document view over an MdDoc
(md_doc.rs) for help pages, README-like content, release notes and chat output

  ui.markdown_view(id, &mut MdViewState, text, MV_*) -> MdEv   Markdown; parsed again only
       when the text changes (the state keeps a hash of it)
  ui.html_view(id, &mut MdViewState, html, MV_*) -> MdEv        HTML (the rich-text reader)
  ui.doc_view(id, &mut MdViewState, MV_*) -> MdEv                the document set before
       (st.set_markdown / set_html / set_doc)
  MdEv { ev, link, hover, field, submit }   ev: EV_FOCUS, EV_HOVER, EV_ACT (a link was
       activated); link: the activated link's target (a click on it, Enter on the focused
       one); hover: the target of the link under the pointer; field: a form field the user
       changed (typed, toggled, chose) or a button without a submit / reset action he pressed;
       submit: a form was sent (MdSubmit: the form, its action and method, the name / value
       pairs, the button).  The view fills the place it gets (natural 480 x 320 DIP;
       next_size(-1, -1) fills).
  MdViewState::new() / base (where relative image paths start, e.g. "app://help/") / label
       (the name for screen readers; "" = "Dokument") / doc() / selection() /
       set_selection(sel) / select_all() / selected_text() / selected_html() /
       scroll_to_block(i) / scroll_to_end() (the end, also while the document grows: chat
       output; scrolling to the end of a long document does the same until the user scrolls
       away) / first_visible() -> (block, px above the view) / focused_link()
  Changes of the document (HTML: its elements, md_dom.rs -- page scripts): st.doc_mut() ->
       &mut MdDoc; the view takes the changes every frame (st.update(): now): the blocks
       derived again (MdDoc::update), the layouts and heights of the blocks that stay kept,
       the view on the block it showed, the selection and the focused link with their blocks,
       the fields' values by their elements (what the user or the app gave a field stays;
       the others follow the document's values), a focused field's widget moved with it
  Images from the app: st.images = MI_LOCAL (default: VFS names and paths, other addresses
       show their alt text), MI_ASK (as MI_LOCAL; http:, https: and data: addresses are asked
       from the app) or MI_APP (every image is asked: nothing is read by the view -- pages
       from the network).  st.image_requests() -> the addresses the view waits for (each
       once; relative ones after base, the rest as written); st.set_image(addr, Some(bytes) |
       None) answers (decoded at once by the image decoders: SVG or img_core; None or bytes
       it cannot decode: the alt text) -- in a frame before the view, or the app asks for one
       (invalidate) when the bytes come outside.  Until then a frame with the alt text stands
       in (at the width / height the HTML gives, else the frame's size); the image's block is
       laid out again when its bytes come, the view stays where it is.
  Forms (HTML: md_doc.rs "Forms"): the fields are the library's widgets in the text flow --
       text boxes (password fields: dots, nothing to copy or read out), text areas, check
       boxes, radios, drop-down lists, buttons -- with the style's look, high contrast, text
       scale and mirroring.  Their values live in the state: field_text(i) / field_checked(i)
       / field_selected(i), set_field_text / set_field_checked / set_field_selected,
       form_data(form, button) (the pairs a browser sends), reset_form(form),
       focused_field(); a new document starts with its first values (a changed one keeps
       them, above).  Keys: Tab / Shift+Tab
       go through links and fields in reading order (a group of radios is one stop: the
       checked one; Up / Down and Left / Right -- as the radios lie in their paragraph --
       choose inside it), Space toggles, Enter in a text field, check
       box or radio sends its form (with its first submit button, none when that is
       disabled), Enter / Space on a button presses it, Esc in a text field returns to the
       view, PgUp / PgDn that a field does not take scroll the view.  The fields follow the
       window's mirroring (as every widget), not the direction of their paragraph.  A
       document without fields reads as before.
  Flags: MV_NO_FRAME (no card, a smaller padding), MV_OPEN_LINKS (an activated link is also
       opened with open_url: its scheme rules and the app's policy apply; never without the
       user's click or Enter), MV_RTL / MV_LTR (the document's direction; default: that of
       its first strong character, else the window's)

Layout: the blocks in a column; block quotes indent with a bar, lists with their markers in
front (bullets by depth: disc, ring, square; numbers; task boxes), headings 2 / 1.5 / 1.25 /
1 / 0.875 / 0.85 times the body text in bold (h1 and h2 underlined), code blocks in the
monospace font on a tinted box with the code editor's highlighting (Highlighter::for_name of
the fence's language, ui.code_theme colours), tables with column widths from their cells
(wrapped to fit the column), images at their size (DIP; wider than the column: scaled down;
SVGs through img_svg, sharp at every size), rules.  Text wraps at text::segment's line
breaks (clusters inside a word too long).  A paragraph's direction comes from its first
strong character: Hebrew and Arabic run right to left (their runs shaped and reordered by
text_shape); indents and markers follow the document's direction.  Only the blocks in view
are laid out (cached per width, dpi, text scale and fonts) and drawn; scrolling is anchored at
the first visible block (vlist.rs Rows), so blocks laid out for the first time never move
what is shown.
Mouse: a drag selects (the view scrolls at its edges), Shift+click extends, a double click
selects a word; a click on a link activates it.  Keys (focused): Up / Down scroll by a line,
PgUp / PgDn and Space / Shift+Space by a view, Home / End to the ends, Tab / Shift+Tab
through the links and fields (the focused link is framed, a field gets the focus; scrolled
into view; past the last one the focus moves on), Enter activates the focused link, Esc
drops it, Ctrl+A selects all,
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+Insert copy the selection as text (list markers, cells by tabs) and HTML.
Images: names of the VFS ("app://", "data://" ...) and paths (relative ones after base) are
read on first view and kept in the state; http(s) addresses are never fetched by the view
(MI_LOCAL: the alt text shows in a frame instead; MI_ASK / MI_APP: the app fetches them).
Records: K_BOX id (label: the label, value: the scroll position in DIP); per visible block
K_HEADING (value: the level), K_TEXT (paragraphs, code, table cells), K_LISTITEM (the first
block of a list item, value: its number), K_CHECKBOX (a task's box, checked), K_LINK per
link, K_IMAGE (label: the alt text) per image; per visible field the widget's record
(K_TEXTBOX, K_CHECKBOX, K_RADIO, K_COMBO, K_BUTTON: label the field's name -- its <label>,
aria-label, title, placeholder -- or a button's caption; text boxes and lists take it from a
K_TEXT record without area along their top edge).  Ids: id (focus, keys), part_id(id, 1)
the scroll bar, md_field_id(id, i) the fields.
```

```rust
/// markdown_view flags: no card around the document
MV_NO_FRAME: u32 = 1
/// an activated link is also opened (open_url)
MV_OPEN_LINKS: u32 = 2
/// the document runs right to left (indents and markers on the right)
MV_RTL: u32 = 4
/// the document runs left to right (also in a mirrored window)
MV_LTR: u32 = 8
/// MdViewState::images: VFS names and paths are read, other addresses show their alt text
MI_LOCAL: u8 = 0
/// as MI_LOCAL, but http:, https: and data: addresses are asked from the app
MI_ASK: u8 = 1
/// every image is asked from the app (the view reads no file)
MI_APP: u8 = 2
```

- **`struct MdEv`**
  what a document view reports (see the module header)
  - `ev: u32` -- EV_FOCUS, EV_HOVER, EV_ACT (a link was activated)
  - `link: Option<String>` -- the target of the link activated this frame
  - `hover: Option<String>` -- the target of the link under the pointer
  - `field: Option<usize>` -- a field the user changed this frame, or a button (MF_BUTTON) he pressed (index of
    doc().fields())
  - `submit: Option<MdSubmit>` -- a form sent this frame (Enter in a field, a submit button)

- **`struct MdSubmit`**
  a form being sent: what a browser would send (MdViewState::form_data)
  - `form: usize` -- the form (index of doc().forms()), its action (as written) and method ("get" / "post")
  - `action: String`
  - `method: String`
  - `fields: Vec<(String, String)>` -- the name / value pairs in document order
  - `button: Option<usize>` -- the submit button that sent it (None: Enter in a form without one)

- **`fn md_field_id(id: u32, i: usize) -> u32`**
  the widget id of field i of the view `id` (the drop-down lists' rows take ids of their own)

- **`struct MdViewState`**
  the state of a document view (see the module header)
  - `base: String` -- where relative image paths start ("app://help/"; "" = as given)
  - `label: String` -- the name for screen readers ("" = "Dokument")
  - `images: u8` -- where the images come from: MI_LOCAL (default), MI_ASK, MI_APP (see the module header)

**`impl MdViewState`**

- **`fn new() -> MdViewState`**
  an empty document
- **`fn doc(&self) -> &MdDoc`**
  the document shown
- **`fn doc_mut(&mut self) -> &mut MdDoc`**
  the document to change (an HTML document's elements, md_dom.rs): the view takes the
  changes at its next frame (or update()) and keeps its place, selection, focus and the
  values the user gave the fields that stay
- **`fn update(&mut self) -> bool`**
  take the document's changes now (MdDoc::update; the view does it every frame) -> there
  were changes
- **`fn set_markdown(&mut self, s: &str)`**
  show Markdown (parsed now unless it is the text shown already)
- **`fn set_html(&mut self, s: &str)`**
  show HTML (parsed now unless it is the text shown already)
- **`fn set_doc(&mut self, doc: MdDoc)`**
  show a document
- **`fn selection(&self) -> TextSel`**
  the selection (TextPos: block, byte of its text)
- **`fn set_selection(&mut self, sel: TextSel)`**
  select a range (clamped to the document)
- **`fn select_all(&mut self)`**
  select the whole document
- **`fn selected_text(&self) -> String`**
  the selection as text (list markers, cells by tabs, images as their alt texts)
- **`fn selected_html(&self) -> String`**
  the selection as HTML
- **`fn scroll_to_block(&mut self, i: usize)`**
  show block i at the top
- **`fn scroll_to_end(&mut self)`**
  show the end, also while the document grows (until the user scrolls away)
- **`fn first_visible(&self) -> (usize, i32)`**
  the first visible block and how many px of it are above the view
- **`fn focused_link(&self) -> Option<usize>`**
  the link focused with Tab (an index of doc().link_spots())
- **`fn image_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<String>`**
  the image addresses the view waits for since the last call (MI_ASK / MI_APP; each one
  once): the app fetches them and answers with set_image
- **`fn set_image(&mut self, addr: &str, data: Option<&[u8]>) -> bool`**
  the bytes of an image address (None: it could not be had): decoded now, shown from the
  next frame on (the alt text when they are no picture) -> an image of the document waited
  for it.  An address not asked yet is kept for the images that need it later.
- **`fn field_text(&self, i: usize) -> &str`**
  field i's text (text fields, text areas, hidden fields; "" for the other kinds)
- **`fn field_checked(&self, i: usize) -> bool`**
  field i is checked (check boxes, radios)
- **`fn field_selected(&self, i: usize) -> i32`**
  the option chosen in field i (drop-down lists; -1: none)
- **`fn set_field_text(&mut self, i: usize, s: &str)`**
  set field i's text (text fields, text areas, hidden fields; changes of the document keep
  it, as the user's input)
- **`fn set_field_checked(&mut self, i: usize, on: bool)`**
  check field i or not (a radio: the others of its group go off)
- **`fn set_field_selected(&mut self, i: usize, k: i32)`**
  choose option k of field i (a drop-down list; -1: none)
- **`fn form_data(&self, form: usize, button: Option<usize>) -> Vec<(String, String)>`**
  the name / value pairs form `form` sends with the submit button `button` (as browsers
  build them: fields with a name that are not disabled; check boxes and radios when
  checked; a list's chosen value; of the buttons only `button`)
- **`fn reset_form(&mut self, form: usize)`**
  the fields of form `form` get their first values back
- **`fn focused_field(&self) -> Option<usize>`**
  the field with the keyboard focus (an index of doc().fields())

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn markdown_view(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut MdViewState, text: &str, flags: u32) -> MdEv`**

- **`fn doc_view(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut MdViewState, flags: u32) -> MdEv`**

#### `ui/vlist.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/vlist.rs`](../lib/ui/vlist.rs)

```text
vlist -- lists whose rows have different heights, virtualized: only the rows in view are
built, laid out and drawn, for any number of rows

  ui.vlist_begin(id, &mut VListState, count) -> (first, end)   the rows to emit, first ..
       end - 1 (the view takes its place like a box: natural 320 x 240 DIP, next_size(-1, -1)
       fills)
  ui.vlist_item_begin(i) -> EV       row i: the style's list row (hover, selection, focus)
       and a BOX_V of the list's width at the row's place; the box's natural height is the
       row's height (measured every pass it is built, unless st.set_height gave one).
       EV_ACT clicked, EV_DOUBLE, EV_RCLICK
  ui.vlist_item_end()
  ui.vlist_end(&mut VListState) -> EV   EV_ACT the selection changed (a click, the keys),
       EV_DOUBLE Enter or a double click, EV_FOCUS, EV_HOVER
  ui.vlist_sel() -> i32               the selection while the rows are emitted
  VListState::new() / sel (-1: none) / estimate (DIP of a row not measured yet; 0: 40, then
       the mean of the measured rows) / set_height(i, dip) (0: measure again) /
       invalidate(i) / invalidate_all() / insert(at, n) / remove(at, n) (rows above the view:
       it keeps showing the same rows) / reveal(i) / scroll_to(i) / first_visible() ->
       (row, px of it above the view) / row_height(i) (px, measured or estimated) /
       row_known(i) / set_count(n) (vlist_begin does it) / scroll_pos() / set_scroll_pos(px)
       / total_height() (px; rows not measured count with the estimate)

Scrolling is anchored at the first visible row (its index and how far it is scrolled out):
rows above it may change their height, come or go without moving what is shown.  The
heights sit in Fenwick trees (the heights known and how many are known; the others count
with the estimate), so a position and the row at a position cost O(log n); the scroll bar
shows the anchor's position in the total.  Keys (focused): Up / Down, PgUp / PgDn (a view of
rows), Home / End move the selection and scroll it into view (exactly, once the rows on the
way are measured), Enter: EV_DOUBLE.  The wheel scrolls (smoothly unless animations are
off), the scroll bar drags.  A change of dpi, width or text scale measures every row again.
Ids: id the view (focus; K_LIST: value sel, max count), id + 1 + i the rows (K_LISTITEM,
value i), (id + 1 + i) | 0xC000_0000 their content boxes, part_id(id, 1) the scroll bar.

Rows (crate): the height cache and anchor on their own -- the Markdown viewer (md_view.rs)
scrolls its blocks with it.
```

- **`struct VListState`**
  the state of a list with rows of different heights (see the module header)
  - `sel: i32` -- the selected row, -1 none
  - `estimate: i32` -- the height of a row that was not measured yet (DIP; 0: 40 at first, then the mean of
    the measured rows)

**`impl VListState`**

- **`fn new() -> VListState`**
  no rows yet, nothing selected
- **`fn set_height(&mut self, i: usize, dip: i32)`**
  row i is `dip` high (the app knows it: its box is not measured); 0 measures it again
- **`fn invalidate(&mut self, i: usize)`**
  row i is measured again the next time it is built
- **`fn invalidate_all(&mut self)`**
  every row is measured again
- **`fn insert(&mut self, at: usize, n: usize)`**
  n rows were inserted before row `at`: the view keeps showing the rows it showed (also
  the selection stays on its row)
- **`fn remove(&mut self, at: usize, n: usize)`**
  rows at .. at + n were removed (the selection on one of them: none)
- **`fn reveal(&mut self, i: usize)`**
  scroll row i fully into view (the next pass)
- **`fn scroll_to(&mut self, i: usize)`**
  show row i at the top of the view
- **`fn first_visible(&self) -> (usize, i32)`**
  the first visible row and how many px of it are scrolled out above the view
- **`fn row_height(&self, i: usize) -> i32`**
  row i's height in px (measured or given; else the estimate)
- **`fn row_known(&self, i: usize) -> bool`**
  row i's height is measured or given
- **`fn set_count(&mut self, n: usize)`**
  the number of rows (vlist_begin sets it from its count; rows come and go at the end)
- **`fn scroll_pos(&self) -> i64`**
  the scroll position: px from the first row's top to the view's top (rows not measured
  count with the estimate)
- **`fn set_scroll_pos(&mut self, px: i64)`**
  scroll to a position (px; the next pass keeps the view inside the rows)
- **`fn total_height(&self) -> i64`**
  the height of all rows (px; rows not measured count with the estimate)

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn vlist_begin(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut VListState, count: usize) -> (usize, usize)`**
  ui_vlist_begin(id, &mut st, count) -> (first, end): the rows to emit (see the module
  header)
- **`fn vlist_item_begin(&mut self, i: usize) -> u32`**
  ui_vlist_item_begin(i) -> EV_\*: row i (see the module header)
- **`fn vlist_item_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_vlist_item_end: the row's height is measured
- **`fn vlist_sel(&self) -> i32`**
  the selection of the innermost vlist while its rows are emitted (-1 outside one)
- **`fn vlist_end(&mut self, st: &mut VListState) -> u32`**
  ui_vlist_end(&mut st) -> EV_\* (see the module header)

#### `ui/code_long.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/code_long.rs`](../lib/ui/code_long.rs)

```text
code_long -- what ui.code_editor (code_edit.rs) keeps of the long lines it shows: checkpoints
of their columns and their tokens, so that a pass looks at the part of a line in view and an
edit works again only near it

  Longs::col / byte / floor     columns (code_doc.rs: col_from, byte_from, cell_floor) from
                                the checkpoint before the place
  Longs::tokens                 the tokens of a long line (highlight.rs) and its end state

A line of COL_LONG bytes or more gets checkpoints (byte, column) at cluster boundaries about
every COL_STEP bytes and keeps its tokens with places outside every construct about every
TOK_STEP bytes.  The entries follow the document's change journal (lines that moved keep
theirs); a line changed in place keeps its text of before, and the next look at it compares:
the columns are walked again from the checkpoint before the change to where they meet the
old ones again (moved along after that, a tab evens out a shift of the columns), the tokens
are scanned again from a place TOK_REACH bytes before the change (rules look ahead) to the
first place after it where the scan is where the old scan was.  A construct that looks
further ahead than TOK_REACH (Markdown emphasis waiting for its closer) is seen again when the
whole line is scanned: a change of its start state, another grammar.
```

- **`fn code_long_check(text: &str, h: &Highlighter, tw: u8, edits: &[(usize, usize, &str)]) -> Vec<String>`**
  (tests) line `text` changed by `edits` one after the other (bytes a..b of the line then
  replaced by s): the column checkpoints and the tokens a code editor keeps of a long line,
  brought along through each change, against a fresh look at the line -> what differs (empty:
  nothing)

#### `ui/text_surface.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/text_surface.rs`](../lib/ui/text_surface.rs)

```text
Input/selection overlay for externally laid out rich text. New opt-in UI API.
The caller paints content; the existing textbox engine handles Unicode, clipboard and IME.
```

- **`struct TextSurfaceLine`**
  One visual line of a text editing surface, in absolute physical window coordinates.
  - `start: usize` -- UTF-8 byte range, excluding an explicit newline. Soft wraps share their boundary.
  - `end: usize`
  - `rect: [i32; 4]` -- Hit/selection rectangle [x, y, width, height]. It may cover a different page per line.
  - `carets: Vec<(usize, i32)>` -- UTF-8 byte caret stops and their absolute x coordinates, in logical order.

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn textbox_surface( &mut self, id: u32, text: &mut String, cap_flags: u32, lines: &[TextSurfaceLine], ) -> u32`**
  Edit one UTF-8 buffer over caller-rendered rich text, without repainting its content.
  Layout may span differently sized/aligned lines and pages; each UTF-8 scalar boundary
  needs a caret stop. Text changes report EV_ACT and request a fresh layout on the next
  pass. Invalid ranges reject the call without consuming input. The caller owns scroll
  positioning and document history. Ordinary textboxes are unaffected.
- **`fn textbox_surface_change(&self) -> Option<(usize, usize, String)>`**
  Replacement in the original buffer from the most recent surface call. The range
  respects the actual insertion location even when surrounding characters repeat.

#### `ui/fontpick.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/fontpick.rs`](../lib/ui/fontpick.rs)

```text
fontpick -- the system's fonts in the UI: the font database and its rules, loading a
choice, text in such a font, a font picker and a font dialog

  FontSel { family, weight, italic, size, axes }   a choice: a family (also a generic one:
                                   "sans-serif", "serif", "monospace" ...), 100..900, italic,
                                   the size in points, axis values of a variable family
                                   (FontSel::new: none; axis / set_axis)
  ui.fonts() -> &FontDb            the installed fonts, scanned on first use (cache
                                   cache://fontdb.fdb; jfgui_FONTDIRS: these folders, no cache)
  ui.font_conf() -> &FontConf      generic families, substitutes, the languages' fonts
                                   (text::fontconf: a light fontconfig)
  ui.font_load(&sel) -> Option<u32>   resolve (FontDb::resolve in the UI language) and load
                                   into ui.text: a font id for set_font / cmd_text; each
                                   family / weight / italic once.  A variable face: its
                                   instance (FontDb::load_var): weight -> wght, italic -> ital
                                   / slnt, the size -> opsz, the axes named win; the instances
                                   of the VAR_KEEP most recent such choices and the app
                                   theme's faces stay loaded (older ones are unloaded, their
                                   ids may be reused)
  ui.font_resolved(&sel) -> String the installed family font_load takes ("" none)
  ui.font_register(family, weight, italic, font)   a font of the app's own (load_mem) under
                                   a family name for font_load; font_registered() lists them
  ui.text_in_font(font, size_pt, s)   one line of text in a font id at a size in points
  ui.font_picker(id, &mut sel) -> EV  a drop-down button with the family (a search box and
                                   the families open below it: typing filters and takes
                                   the first match, Up / Down / a click choose) and a size
                                   box in points; EV_ACT when sel changed
  ui.font_dialog(id, &open, &mut sel) -> EV   a modal dialog window "Schriftart": search,
                                   families, the family's styles, sizes, a preview in the
                                   font, OK / Abbrechen; works on a copy of sel and writes it
                                   back on OK (EV_ACT); closing clears open.  A variable
                                   family lists its named instances as styles and gets a
                                   slider and a number box per axis (fvar's range and name;
                                   hidden axes not), opsz with "Automatisch" (follows the size)
  font_language() -> String        the language the fonts follow: the user's tag of the UI
                                   language (ja-JP, zh-Hant-TW), else its code

The runtime hands font_language() to the system fallback (text::fallback, again when the
UI language changes), so missing Han characters take the forms of the language.  Ids:
the scope of the widget's id, then "family", "search", "list", "styles", "size",
"sizes", the axes' "axis" scope with per axis id_n(k) (slider), id_n(k + 100) (number
box), "opsz_auto" (ids.rs).
```

  - `axes: Vec<([u8; 4], f32)>` -- axis values of a variable family in user units by tag (`(*b"wdth", 87.5)`); the axes
    not named follow weight (wght), italic (ital, slnt) and size (opsz), else their
    defaults; families that are not variable ignore them

**`impl FontSel`**

#### `ui/grid.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/grid.rs`](../lib/ui/grid.rs)

```text
grid -- a grid box: rows and columns with spans and alignment (a box with its own placing
mode; data.rs's grid_begin is the data table)

  gridbox_begin(id, cols, flags, gap)   open a grid: one entry per column in DIP, > 0
                                        fixed, 0 its widest child, < 0 a share of the width
                                        left (fill weight); rows grow with their tallest
                                        child.  flags: the box decorations and padding of
                                        box_begin (BOX_CARD, BOX_CLIP, pad(n), ...) and the
                                        alignment of the children: GRID_H_START | _CENTER |
                                        _END (default: stretched across the cell),
                                        GRID_V_START | _END | _STRETCH (default: centred);
                                        gap: DIP between cells
  gridbox_rows(rows)                    (after gridbox_begin) row sizes like cols; rows
                                        without an entry are 0 (their tallest child); < 0
                                        share the height left when the grid has a fixed one
  gridbox_end()
  next_span(cols, rows)                 the next child covers that many cells
  next_cell(col, row)                   the next child starts there (later cells follow it)
  next_align(h, v)                      the next child's alignment: AL_START, AL_CENTER,
                                        AL_END, AL_STRETCH (AL_DEFAULT: the grid's)

Children fill the cells row by row, skipping cells a row span still covers.  next_size
still applies: a fixed size is aligned in the cell, a natural one too, a fill size (< 0)
stretches.  Natural column widths and row heights come from the previous pass, as box
sizes do; a change asks for another pass.  A spanned child widens the last of its natural
columns (rows) when it does not fit.  A TX_WRAP text (and a BOX_WRAP box) wraps at the
width its cell gives it (avail_width), so its row grows with its lines.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn gridbox_begin(&mut self, id: u32, cols: &[i32], flags: u32, gap: i32)`**
  gridbox_begin(id, cols, flags, gap): open a grid (see the module comment)
- **`fn gridbox_rows(&mut self, rows: &[i32])`**
  gridbox_rows(rows): row sizes of the open grid (DIP; > 0 fixed, 0 natural, &lt; 0 fill)
- **`fn next_span(&mut self, cols: u32, rows: u32)`**
  next_span(cols, rows): the next grid child covers that many cells
- **`fn next_cell(&mut self, col: u32, row: u32)`**
  next_cell(col, row): the next grid child starts in that cell
- **`fn next_align(&mut self, h: u32, v: u32)`**
  next_align(h, v): the next grid child's alignment (AL_\*; AL_DEFAULT: the grid's)
- **`fn gridbox_end(&mut self)`**
  gridbox_end: store the measured sizes (another pass when they changed), close the box

#### `ui/hexview.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/hexview.rs`](../lib/ui/hexview.rs)

```text
hexview -- bytes as hex and ASCII side by side, with marked ranges (a packet inspector)

  hex_view(id, &mut st, data, marks) -> HexEv
       rows "0010  45 00 00 54 ...  |E..T....|" in the system's monospace font (else the
       UI font, a character per cell), virtualized in a vertical scroll view that fills
       its parent unless next_size says otherwise; st.cols bytes per row (0: 16 when they
       fit, else 8), offsets with 4 hex digits (8 beyond 64 KiB).  marks are translucent
       fills behind their bytes in both columns (colour 0 = the chart palette colour of
       the mark's index; an opaque colour gets a highlight's alpha), smaller ranges over
       larger ones.  The selection (st.sel: start, length), the byte under the pointer and,
       while the view has the focus, the caret show in the hex and the ASCII column
       together; zero bytes and the dots of other bytes are dimmed.
       Mouse: a click selects a byte (HexEv::clicked_key: the key of the smallest mark
       holding it), a drag a range (the view scrolls at its edges), Shift+click extends
       it, a double click selects the mark's range, a click on an offset its row; the byte
       under the pointer is HexEv::hover, its offset a tooltip.  Keys (focused): arrows,
       PgUp / PgDn, Home / End (of the row; with Ctrl of the data) move the caret (Shift
       extends; a move reports the caret's mark like a click), Ctrl+A selects all, Ctrl+C
       copies the selection as hex in one line ("45 00 00 54").  When the app changes
       st.sel the view scrolls to it.
       HexEv::ev: EV_ACT the user changed the selection, EV_DOUBLE, EV_RCLICK (the byte is
       selected first: open a context menu), EV_HOVER, EV_FOCUS.

Ids: id (the scroll view; focus; its bar part(id, 1)), part(id, 3) the rows.  Records:
K_LIST id (value: the caret, max: the number of bytes), K_BOX part(id, 3) (value: the byte
under the pointer or -1), per visible row K_TEXT with its offset ("0010", value: the
offset), its hex bytes ("45 00 00 54 ...") and its characters ("E..T...."); the hover
tooltip is a K_TEXT too.  The rows keep their left-to-right order in mirrored windows
(ltr_begin).
```

- **`struct HexMark`**
  a marked byte range of a hex view (a protocol field)
  - `start: u32`
  - `len: u32`
  - `color: u32` -- 0xAARRGGBB (an opaque colour is drawn translucent); 0 = the chart palette colour of
    the mark's index
  - `key: u64` -- the app's key of the range (HexEv::clicked_key)

- **`struct HexState`**
  the app-owned state of a hex view: selection, bytes per row, caret
  - `sel: Option<(u32, u32)>` -- the selected bytes: (start, length >= 1); when the app changes it, the view scrolls to it
  - `cols: u8` -- bytes per row; 0 = 16 when they fit, else 8

**`impl HexState`**

- **`fn caret(&self) -> u32`**
  the keyboard caret (a byte offset)
- **`fn reveal(&mut self, off: u32)`**
  scroll byte `off` into view

- **`struct HexEv`**
  what happened in a hex view during the pass
  - `hover: Option<u32>` -- the byte under the pointer
  - `clicked_key: Option<u64>` -- a byte was clicked or the caret moved onto it: the key of the smallest mark holding it
  - `ev: u32` -- EV_ACT the selection changed, EV_DOUBLE, EV_RCLICK, EV_HOVER, EV_FOCUS

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn hex_view(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut HexState, data: &[u8], marks: &[HexMark]) -> HexEv`**
  ui_hex_view(id, &mut st, data, marks) -> HexEv: bytes as hex and ASCII rows with
  marked ranges, a selection and a caret (see the module header of hexview.rs)

```text
imgview -- SVG pictures and the image viewer (ROADMAP §6)

       DIP (0 and 0: the intrinsic size, one 0: from the aspect ratio); currentColor is the
