```text
       page, Home / End to the top / bottom; + / - (with or without Ctrl) zoom in steps,
       Ctrl+0 fits, Ctrl+1 shows 100 %.  Scroll bars at the right and bottom edges when the
       image is larger than the view (IV_NO_BARS: none).
       Drawing: bitmaps through mip levels (2 x 2 box) and bilinear sampling below 400 %,
       nearest neighbour above (IV_SMOOTH: bilinear at every zoom), a pixel grid from 800 %
       (IV_NO_GRID: none); SVGs are drawn again at the zoom (only the visible part,
       currentColor black, IV_TEXT_COLOR: the text colour).  Transparent parts over a
       checkerboard (IV_NO_CHECKER: the view's background); the theme decides its colours
       (light, dark, high contrast: plain background).
  ImageViewState { zoom, cx, cy, fit, label }: zoom 1.0 = 100 % (a bitmap pixel on one
       screen pixel, an SVG at its intrinsic size in DIP); (cx, cy) the image point at the
       view's centre; fit: the zoom follows the view.  st.set_fit() / set_actual() /
       zoom_to(rect) / zoom_by(factor) / zoom_pct().  A new image (another Rc) fits.
  SvgText { text, fonts }: img_svg::TextHook on ui's text engine; SvgFonts picks the faces:
       families registered with ui.font_register, "monospace" = ui.mono_font_set's font,
       everything else the style's fonts (regular / semibold / bold; italic slanted).

Ids: id (the view: focus, K_IMAGE with st.label, the SVG's title or "Bild"; value = zoom %),
part(id, 1) / part(id, 2) the vertical / horizontal scroll bar.
```

```rust
/// image_view flags
IV_WHEEL_SCROLL: u32 = 1  // the wheel scrolls, Ctrl + wheel zooms
IV_NO_GRID: u32 = 2  // no pixel grid at high zoom
IV_SMOOTH: u32 = 4  // bilinear at every zoom (no visible pixels)
IV_NO_BARS: u32 = 8  // no scroll bars
IV_NO_CHECKER: u32 = 16  // transparency over the view background
IV_TEXT_COLOR: u32 = 32  // an SVG's currentColor is the text colour (else black)
```

- **`struct SvgFonts`**
  the faces SvgText may use (taken from the Ui at frame time)
  - `faces: Vec<(String, u32, bool, u32)>` -- (family lower case, weight, italic, font id) of ui.font_register
  - `mono: Option<u32>` -- "monospace"

- **`struct SvgText<'a>`**
  an img_svg::TextHook on a text engine
  - `text: &'a mut Text`
  - `fonts: &'a SvgFonts`

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn svg_fonts(&mut self) -> Rc<SvgFonts>`**
  the faces for SVG text (registered families, the monospace font); shared until the
  registered fonts change
- **`fn svg(&mut self, id: u32, doc: &Rc<Svg>, w: i32, h: i32) -> u32`**
  ui_svg(id, doc, w, h) -> EV: an SVG at w x h DIP (see the module header of imgview.rs)

- **`enum ViewImage<'a>`**
  what ui.image_view shows
  - `Bitmap(&'a Rc<Surface>, u32)` -- a bitmap (FMT_PARGB, FMT_ARGB or FMT_XRGB) and its version (bump it when the
    pixels change)
  - `Svg(&'a Rc<Svg>)`

- **`struct ImageViewState`**
  the app-owned state of an image view (see the module header of imgview.rs)
  - `zoom: f64` -- 1.0 = 100 %
  - `cx: f64` -- the image point (image px) at the centre of the view
  - `cy: f64`
  - `fit: bool` -- the zoom follows the view: the whole image, centred
  - `label: String` -- the accessible name (empty: the SVG's title, else "Bild")

**`impl ImageViewState`**

- **`fn zoom_pct(&self) -> i32`**
  the zoom in percent (rounded)
- **`fn set_fit(&mut self)`**
  fit mode: the whole image in the view
- **`fn set_actual(&mut self)`**
  100 %, the centre kept
- **`fn zoom_by(&mut self, f: f64)`**
  multiply the zoom (about the view's centre)
- **`fn zoom_to(&mut self, r: [f64; 4])`**
  show the image rectangle x, y, w, h (image px) as large as the view allows

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn image_view(&mut self, id: u32, st: &mut ImageViewState, img: ViewImage, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  ui_image_view(id, st, img, flags) -> EV: the image viewer (see the module header of
  imgview.rs)

#### `ui/history.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/history.rs`](../lib/ui/history.rs)

```text
history -- undo / redo for an app's own state

  History::new(limit)                  empty; at most `limit` steps are kept (the oldest go)
  h.apply(&mut state, edit)            run an Edit and record it (the redo steps go)
  h.undo(&mut state) / h.redo(&mut state) -> bool
  h.can_undo() / can_redo()            undo_label() / redo_label() -> the step's label;
                                       undo_value() / redo_value() -> the step as data
  h.group_begin(label) / group_end()   the edits between them are one step
  h.mark_saved() / dirty()             whether the state differs from the saved one
  h.mark_unsaved()                     the state counts as unsaved (a recovered copy)
  h.clear()
  Snapshot::new(label, before, after)  an Edit for small states: the whole value (Clone)
  ui.undo_keys() -> Option<bool>       Ctrl+Z (Some(true)) / Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z
                                       (Some(false)) when no text field has the keyboard;
                                       the key is consumed

An Edit changes the state forward (apply) and back (revert); merge lets a step absorb the
next one of the same kind (typing in one field, dragging a slider) so one undo takes it
all back.  Text fields keep their own undo; the edits here are the app's.
```

- **`trait Edit<S>`**
  one undoable change of a state S
  - `fn apply(&mut self, s: &mut S)`
    do it (again)
  - `fn revert(&mut self, s: &mut S)`
    take it back
  - `fn label(&self) -> &str`
    shown in "Rückgängig: …"
  - `fn merge(&mut self, _next: &mut dyn Edit<S>) -> bool`
    absorb the following edit into this one (true: it is part of this step now)
  - `fn value(&self) -> Option<&dyn core::any::Any>`
    (merge) the edit as Any-like data: the merge partner's own value

- **`struct Snapshot<T: Clone + 'static>`**
  an Edit of a whole small value (Clone): before and after

**`impl<T: Clone + 'static> Snapshot<T>`**

- **`fn new(label: &str, before: T, after: T) -> Self`**
- **`fn merging(mut self, key: u32) -> Self`**
  edits with the same key merge into one step

- **`struct History<S>`**
  the undo and redo steps of a state S

**`impl<S: 'static> History<S>`**

- **`fn new(limit: usize) -> Self`**
- **`fn apply(&mut self, s: &mut S, mut edit: Box<dyn Edit<S>>)`**
  run the edit and record it as the newest step (redo steps are gone)
- **`fn record(&mut self, mut edit: Box<dyn Edit<S>>)`**
  record an edit that was already applied
- **`fn undo(&mut self, s: &mut S) -> bool`**
  take the newest step back -> false when there is none
- **`fn redo(&mut self, s: &mut S) -> bool`**
  do the last undone step again -> false when there is none
- **`fn can_undo(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn can_redo(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn undo_label(&self) -> Option<&str>`**
  the label of the step undo would take back
- **`fn redo_label(&self) -> Option<&str>`**
  the label of the step redo would do again
- **`fn undo_value(&self) -> Option<&dyn core::any::Any>`**
  the step undo would take back as data (Edit::value; None for a group): the app can
  see what kind of edit it is before it runs
- **`fn redo_value(&self) -> Option<&dyn core::any::Any>`**
  the step redo would do again as data (Edit::value)
- **`fn group_begin(&mut self, label: &str)`**
  the following edits are one step (nested groups join the outer one)
- **`fn group_end(&mut self)`**
  close the group of group_begin (an empty group records nothing)
- **`fn mark_saved(&mut self)`**
  the state is saved now (dirty() false until the next change)
- **`fn mark_unsaved(&mut self)`**
  the state counts as unsaved until the next mark_saved (a copy recovered after a crash)
- **`fn dirty(&self) -> bool`**
  the state differs from the saved one
- **`fn clear(&mut self)`**
  forget every step (the current state counts as saved when it was)
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of undo steps
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn undo_keys(&mut self) -> Option<bool>`**
  undo_keys() -> Some(true) for Ctrl+Z, Some(false) for Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z, when no
  text field has the keyboard (they keep their own undo); the key is consumed

#### `ui/hyph.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/hyph.rs`](../lib/ui/hyph.rs)

```text
hyph -- hyphenation of wrapped texts and text boxes (spell::Hyphenator, text::segment)

  TX_HYPHENATE (text style, with TX_WRAP), TB_HYPHENATE (textbox, with TB_MULTI | TB_WRAP)
       a word that does not fit at the end of a line is broken at its last hyphenation
       point that fits, and a hyphen is drawn there.  Soft hyphens (U+00AD) in the text
       work in every wrapped text, with or without the flag: invisible inside a line, a
       hyphen where the line breaks after one
  hyph_language(tag)          the language: a BCP 47 tag; "" (default) = font_language(),
                              the user's tag of the UI language
  next_hyph_language(tag)     the language of the next wrapped text (TX_WRAP) or multi-line
                              box only (it counts when that one hyphenates)
  hyph_sources(SRC_*)         where dictionaries come from (spell crate; 0 = the default:
                              everything in window mode, only app:// in headless runs, so
                              scripts never depend on the machine)
  hyph_set(tag, hyphenator)   the app's own patterns for a language (before any source)
  hyphenator(tag) -> Option<Arc<Hyphenator>>   the patterns for a tag ("": the current
                              language), found (spell::find_hyphen: hyph_xx_YY.dic of
                              LibreOffice, /usr/share/hyphen, config://hyphen,
                              app://hyphen) and read on first use, then kept

A dictionary is read on the UI thread the first time a language is needed (de_DE, 1 MB:
some 40 ms); a language without one keeps texts unhyphenated (soft hyphens still work).
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn hyph_language(&mut self, tag: &str)`**
  the hyphenation language: a BCP 47 tag ("de-DE"); "" = the UI language's
- **`fn next_hyph_language(&mut self, tag: &str)`**
  the language of the next wrapped text or multi-line box only (it counts when that one
  hyphenates: TX_HYPHENATE, TB_HYPHENATE)
- **`fn hyph_sources(&mut self, sources: u32)`**
  where hyphenation dictionaries come from (spell::SRC_\*; 0 = the default)
- **`fn hyph_set(&mut self, tag: &str, h: Hyphenator)`**
  the app's own hyphenation patterns for a language tag ("de", "en-US")
- **`fn hyphenator(&mut self, tag: &str) -> Option<Arc<Hyphenator>>`**
  the hyphenation patterns for a tag ("": the current language), None when there are none

#### `ui/i18n_locale.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/i18n_locale.rs`](../lib/ui/i18n_locale.rs)

```text
i18n_locale -- regional formats (a compact subset of CLDR) and plural categories

  Locale::get(tag) -> Locale          the best match of a BCP 47 tag: the tag itself, the
                                      language with the region, the language's default
                                      ("de" -> de-DE, "en" -> en-US), else "en-001"
  locale() / set_locale(tag) / locale_tag()   the user's format: ui boots it from
                                      jfgui_LANG, the system (window mode) or "de-DE"
                                      (headless runs, so shots match on every machine)
  loc.fmt_int(n)                      "1.234.567" (de), "1,234,567" (en), "12,34,567" (hi)
  loc.fmt_num(v, decimals)            fixed decimals, rounded; grouped
  loc.fmt_percent(fraction, decimals) 0.25 -> "25 %" (de), "25%" (en), "%25" (tr)
  loc.fmt_currency(v, "USD") / fmt_money(v)   "1.234,56 $" (de), "$1,234.56" (en-US);
                                      fmt_money in the locale's own currency
  loc.fmt_size(bytes)                 "1,5 MB" (1024 based; French "Mo")
  loc.fmt_date(&civil, DATE_SHORT | DATE_LONG) / fmt_time(&civil) / fmt_date_time(&civil)
                                      "17.10.2026" / "17. Oktober 2026" / "19:58";
                                      en-US "10/17/2026" / "October 17, 2026" / "7:58 PM"
  loc.first_weekday() (0 = Monday .. 6 = Sunday), rtl(), decimal(), group(), currency(), tag()
  fmt_int / fmt_num / fmt_percent / fmt_currency / fmt_money / fmt_size / fmt_date /
  fmt_time / fmt_date_time            the same with locale()
  plural(lang, i, v, f) / plural_int(lang, n) -> Plural   CLDR cardinal categories (i the
                                      integer digits, v the number of visible fraction
                                      digits, f those digits as an integer)

Numbers use ASCII digits everywhere (also Arabic and Hindi); spaces inside numbers and
before units are no-break spaces (U+00A0, French U+202F).  Long dates use the format
(genitive) month names of the locale's language.
```

```rust
/// fmt_date: "17.10.2026" / "10/17/2026"
DATE_SHORT: u32 = 0
/// fmt_date: "17. Oktober 2026" / "October 17, 2026"
DATE_LONG: u32 = 1
```

- **`struct Locale`**
  the formats of one region (copy it freely)

**`impl Locale`**

- **`fn get(tag: &str) -> Locale`**
  the best match of a BCP 47 tag or a POSIX locale name (see the module comment)
- **`fn tag(&self) -> &'static str`**
  the tag of the matched data ("de-DE", "en-001")
- **`fn decimal(&self) -> char`**
  the decimal sign
- **`fn group(&self) -> char`**
  the thousands separator
- **`fn first_weekday(&self) -> u32`**
  the first day of the week: 0 = Monday .. 6 = Sunday
- **`fn rtl(&self) -> bool`**
  right-to-left script (Arabic, Hebrew)
- **`fn currency(&self) -> &'static str`**
  the ISO 4217 code of the region's currency
- **`fn month_name(&self, m: u32) -> &'static str`**
  the long (format) name of month m (1..12) in the locale's language
- **`fn fmt_int(&self, n: i64) -> String`**
  an integer with group separators
- **`fn fmt_num(&self, v: f64, decimals: u32) -> String`**
  a number with exactly `decimals` fraction digits (rounded) and group separators
- **`fn fmt_percent(&self, fraction: f64, decimals: u32) -> String`**
  a fraction as percent: 0.25 -> "25 %" (de) / "25%" (en)
- **`fn fmt_currency(&self, v: f64, code: &str) -> String`**
  an amount of the ISO 4217 currency `code` ("EUR", "USD"; unknown codes are shown as is)
- **`fn fmt_money(&self, v: f64) -> String`**
  an amount in the region's own currency
- **`fn fmt_size(&self, bytes: u64) -> String`**
  a byte count: "512 B", "1,5 KB", "23 MB" (1024 based, one decimal below 10)
- **`fn fmt_date(&self, c: &Civil, style: u32) -> String`**
  a date: DATE_SHORT "17.10.2026" / DATE_LONG "17. Oktober 2026"
- **`fn fmt_time(&self, c: &Civil) -> String`**
  a time of day: "19:58" / "7:58 PM"
- **`fn fmt_date_time(&self, c: &Civil) -> String`**
  the short date and the time: "17.10.2026, 19:58" / "10/17/2026, 7:58 PM"

- **`fn locale() -> Locale`**
  the user's regional format (default "de-DE")

- **`fn locale_tag() -> String`**
  the tag the format was asked for ("de-LU" may use the data of "de-DE")

- **`fn set_locale(tag: &str)`**
  set the user's regional format (a BCP 47 tag or a POSIX locale name)

- **`fn fmt_int(n: i64) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_int in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_num(v: f64, decimals: u32) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_num in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_percent(fraction: f64, decimals: u32) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_percent in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_currency(v: f64, code: &str) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_currency in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_money(v: f64) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_money in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_size(bytes: u64) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_size in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_date(c: &Civil, style: u32) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_date in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_time(c: &Civil) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_time in the user's format

- **`fn fmt_date_time(c: &Civil) -> String`**
  Locale::fmt_date_time in the user's format

- **`enum Plural`**
  a CLDR plural category
  - `Zero`
  - `One`
  - `Two`
  - `Few`
  - `Many`
  - `Other`

**`impl Plural`**

- **`fn name(self) -> &'static str`**
  the CLDR keyword: "zero", "one", "two", "few", "many", "other"

- **`fn plural_int(lang: &str, n: i64) -> Plural`**
  the plural category of an integer in a language ("de", "ru-RU", ...)

- **`fn plural(lang: &str, i: u64, v: u32, f: u64) -> Plural`**
  the plural category of a number: i = its integer digits, v = the number of visible fraction
  digits, f = those digits as an integer ("1,50": i 1, v 2, f 50)

#### `ui/i18n_msg.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/i18n_msg.rs`](../lib/ui/i18n_msg.rs)

```text
i18n_msg -- messages with named, numbered and plural placeholders (a subset of ICU
MessageFormat), so translations may reorder and inflect

  msg(text, &[("n", 3.into()), ("dir", "Bilder".into())]) -> String

  {name} {0} {}            an argument by name, by position, or the next one in order;
                           numbers as they are, with the locale's decimal sign ("1234,5")
  {n, number}              grouped ("1.234,5"); styles: integer (rounded), percent (a
                           fraction: 0.25 -> "25 %"), currency/EUR, size (bytes: "1,5 MB")
  {d, date} {d, date, long} {d, time} {d, datetime}   an Arg::Date (datetime::Civil)
  {n, plural, =0 {keine Dateien} one {# Datei} other {# Dateien}}
                           the CLDR category of the UI language (language_code()); =N
                           matches before the categories; # is the number (grouped);
                           "offset:1" before the options subtracts 1 for # and the category
  {g, select, female {sie} male {er} other {es}}
  '{' '}' '#' quote,  '' is an apostrophe; a lone apostrophe stays ("geht's")

The numbers follow the user's format (locale()).  A missing argument prints as {name};
broken syntax prints the rest of the text as it is.
```

  - `Int(i64)`

#### `ui/i18n_collate.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/i18n_collate.rs`](../lib/ui/i18n_collate.rs)

```text
i18n_collate -- sorting by language (collation) and Unicode case mapping

  collate(a, b) -> Ordering           two texts in the order of the user's language
                                      (locale_tag(): the format locale, as Windows'
                                      CompareStringEx): base letters first, then accents,
                                      then case: "a" < "A" < "á" < "ä" < "b"
  collator() / Collator::new(tag)     a collator with options: .strength(COLL_PRIMARY ..
                                      COLL_IDENTICAL), .numeric(true) ("Datei 2" before
                                      "Datei 10"), .phonebook(true) (German phone book:
                                      ä = ae); .compare(a, b), .key(s) (a sort key: keys
                                      compare like their texts), .sort(items, text).  The
                                      tag may carry "-u-co-phonebk", "-u-kn", "-u-ks-level1"
  Locale::collate(a, b) / collator()  the same for a fixed region
  to_upper(s) / to_lower(s) / fold(s) case mapping of all of Unicode in the user's language:
                                      ß -> SS, "ΟΔΟΣ" -> "οδος" (final sigma), Turkish and
                                      Azeri i / İ and ı / I; fold() for comparisons (ß and
                                      ẞ -> ss, ς -> σ)
  to_upper_in(lang, s) / to_lower_in / fold_in   the same for a language
  eq_ignore_case(a, b)                equal except for case (also composed against
                                      decomposed accents: "É" = "e\u{301}")

The collation is a compact form of the Unicode Collation Algorithm, not the CLDR data:
every character becomes collation elements (primary: the letter, secondary: its accents,
tertiary: case and variants such as ß or ſ); the canonical decompositions come from the
generated table i18n_unicode.rs (tools/gen_unicode.py).  Order of the primaries: spaces,
punctuation and symbols (by code point), digits (by value), Latin letters a .. z, then the
letters of the other scripts by code point (Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, ..., kana as
hiragana, CJK).  Language rules where they are usual: German (ä like a; phone book ä = ae),
Swedish / Finnish (å ä ö after z), Danish / Norwegian (æ ø å after z, aa = å), Spanish
(ñ after n), Czech / Slovak (č ř š ž, ch after h), Polish (ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż), Turkish
(ç ğ ı ö ş ü, I is the capital of ı).  Everywhere: ß = ss, æ = ae, œ = oe, ø ł đ like o l d
with a secondary difference, ð þ ŋ ı letters of their own, Cyrillic і ї й ґ є ў ђ ј љ њ ћ
џ in their alphabetical places, Hebrew final forms as variants.

core and alloc bring the default case mappings of all of Unicode (char::to_uppercase,
str::to_lowercase with the final sigma); this module adds the language rules (Turkish,
Azeri) and case folding.  Not done: Lithuanian dot rules, Greek upper case without accents.
```

```rust
/// collation strength: base letters only ("a" = "A" = "ä")
COLL_PRIMARY: u32 = 1
/// collation strength: base letters and accents ("a" = "A" < "ä"): sorting without case
COLL_SECONDARY: u32 = 2
/// collation strength: base letters, accents and case ("a" < "A" < "ä"; the default)
COLL_TERTIARY: u32 = 3
/// collation strength: as COLL_TERTIARY, then the code points (only equal texts compare equal)
COLL_IDENTICAL: u32 = 4
```

- **`struct Collator`**
  compares texts in the order of a language (see the module comment); copy it freely

**`impl Collator`**

- **`fn new(tag: &str) -> Collator`**
  the collator of a language (a BCP 47 tag or a POSIX name; unknown languages sort by the
  common rules); "-u-co-phonebk", "-u-kn" and "-u-ks-level1 / 2 / 3 / identic" set the
  options as in ICU, also "de-DE_phoneb" (Windows) and "@collation=phonebook" (POSIX)
- **`fn strength(mut self, s: u32) -> Collator`**
  the same collator with another strength (COLL_PRIMARY .. COLL_IDENTICAL)
- **`fn numeric(mut self, on: bool) -> Collator`**
  numbers by their value: "Datei 2" before "Datei 10", "007" = "7" up to the tertiary level
- **`fn phonebook(mut self, on: bool) -> Collator`**
  German phone book order (ä = ae, ö = oe, ü = ue); no effect in other languages
- **`fn compare(&self, a: &str, b: &str) -> Ordering`**
  compare two texts
- **`fn key(&self, s: &str) -> Vec<u32>`**
  the sort key of a text: keys compare as their texts do (sort_by_cached_key, indexes)
- **`fn sort<T>(&self, items: &mut [T], text: impl Fn(&T) -> &str)`**
  sort items by a text of each (stable; each key is computed once)

- **`fn collator() -> Collator`**
  the user's collator (the language of locale_tag(), tertiary strength)

- **`fn collate(a: &str, b: &str) -> Ordering`**
  compare two texts in the order of the user's language (see the module comment)

**`impl Locale`**

- **`fn collate(&self, a: &str, b: &str) -> Ordering`**
  compare two texts in the order of the region's language
- **`fn collator(&self) -> Collator`**
  the collator of the region's language

- **`fn to_upper(s: &str) -> String`**
  upper case in the user's language: "straße" -> "STRASSE", Turkish "i" -> "İ"

- **`fn to_lower(s: &str) -> String`**
  lower case in the user's language: "ΟΔΟΣ" -> "οδος", Turkish "I" -> "ı"

- **`fn fold(s: &str) -> String`**
  case folding in the user's language (for comparisons, not for display): "Straße" ->
  "strasse", "ΣΟΦΟΣ" and "σοφος" -> "σοφοσ"

- **`fn eq_ignore_case(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool`**
  equal except for case in the user's language ("STRASSE" = "Straße"); composed and
  decomposed accents are equal too

- **`fn to_upper_in(lang: &str, s: &str) -> String`**
  upper case in a language (BCP 47 tag)

- **`fn to_lower_in(lang: &str, s: &str) -> String`**
  lower case in a language (BCP 47 tag)

- **`fn fold_in(lang: &str, s: &str) -> String`**

  Turkish and Azeri with their I / ı and İ / i

#### `ui/ids.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/ids.rs`](../lib/ui/ids.rs)

```text
ids -- widget ids from names: hashing and a stack of scopes

  wid(name) -> u32             const: the id of a name outside every scope, for constants
                               (const SAVE: u32 = ui::wid("save") == ui.id("save") there)
  wid_path(&[names]) -> u32    const: the last name inside the scopes of the ones before
                               (wid_path(&["layers", "add"]) == ui.id("add") after
                               ui.id_push_str("layers"))
  ui.id(name) -> u32           a name in the current scope (takes &self: ui.button(ui.id("save"), ..))
  ui.id_n(n) -> u32            a number in the current scope (the rows of a loop)
  ui.id_push(n) / ui.id_push_str(name) / ui.id_pop()   open / close a scope: a number (an
                               index, a document's id) or a name
  ui.id_scope(n, |ui| ...)     id_push, the closure, id_pop
The names of hashed ids are kept for the frame in scripts, with jfgui_DEBUG=1 and while the
inspector is open (it shows them: inspect.rs).

A hashed id is FNV-1a over the bytes (a number: its four bytes, little endian) and a tag
byte (1 name, 2 number), seeded with the scope, then mixed (murmur3's finaliser) into
ID_HASH_BASE .. 0x0FFE_FFFF.  Constants written by hand stay below ID_HASH_BASE and never
meet hashed ids; bits 28..31 stay the library's (part_id); the 64 Ki ids above the range
leave room for widgets that also take id + 1 + i.  Two names of one pass collide with a
chance of about 1 : 134 million per pair; scripts and jfgui_DEBUG=1 warn about two names
with one id and about an id two widgets share (naming the hashed names involved).  The
stack starts empty in every pass; a scope still open at the end of App::frame is closed
(a UIWARN the first time).
```

```rust
/// the first hashed id; ids written by hand stay below it
ID_HASH_BASE: u32 = 0x0800_0000
```

- **`const fn wid(name: &str) -> u32`**
  the id of a name outside every scope (the same as ui.id(name) there)

- **`const fn wid_path(names: &[&str]) -> u32`**
  the id of the last name inside the scopes of the names before it (id_push_str each);
  no names: wid("")

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn id(&self, name: &str) -> u32`**
  the id of a name in the current scope
- **`fn id_n(&self, n: u32) -> u32`**
  the id of a number in the current scope (the rows of a loop)
- **`fn id_push(&mut self, n: u32)`**
  open a scope named by a number (an index, a document's id); always pair with id_pop
- **`fn id_push_str(&mut self, name: &str)`**
  open a scope named by a name; always pair with id_pop
- **`fn id_pop(&mut self)`**
  close the scope of the last id_push / id_push_str
- **`fn id_scope<R>(&mut self, n: u32, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui) -> R) -> R`**
  id_push(n), f(ui), id_pop()

#### `ui/inspect.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/inspect.rs`](../lib/ui/inspect.rs)

```text
inspect -- the live inspector: an overlay in the app's windows and the tool window
"Inspektor" (ROADMAP §12)

App-facing:
  inspect_enable(on)         arm the inspector: its hot keys open and close it (off: closed,
                             the keys reach the app again)
  inspect_show(on)           open / close it (opening arms it)
  inspect_open() -> bool     it is open
  inspect_keys(&[chord])     its hot keys, VK | MOD_* << 16 (default Ctrl+Shift+I and F12)
Command line: --inspect arms and opens it; jfgui_INSPECT=1 arms it, jfgui_INSPECT=open opens
it too.

Closed (the default) it costs nothing: the runtime's hooks test one flag and nothing is
recorded or drawn.  Open:
  * the overlay in every window of the app: the widget under the pointer outlined, with a tag
    (kind, id in hex and its hashed name when known, label, size in DIP, state); the selected
    widget; optionally the layout boxes, the Tab order and the repainted rectangles of the
    last frames (flashing).  The overlay is drawn into the framebuffer after the app's
    commands, outside their lists: the app's dirty regions stay its own (ins_render_begin
    adds the overlay's old and new rectangles, which are redrawn from the app's commands)
  * the tool window "Inspektor" (WF_TOOL: it never takes the keyboard by itself; Esc, its
    close button and drops on it never reach the app): the widget tree of the current pass
    (the semantic records of the app's windows inside their layout boxes; collapsible,
    selectable; selecting highlights in the app), the properties of the selected widget, a
    script selector to copy (Ctrl+C or "Kopieren"), frame statistics, the theme's colour
    tokens; "Auswählen" picks a widget with a click into the app (the click does not reach
    it; Esc ends the pick)
The inspector's own window is left out of the tree, the overlay and the pick.
Development builds edit in it (inspect_edit.rs): the tab "Farben" is editable, the tab
"Darstellung" and the widget operations below the properties are added.

Script commands (auto.rs `inspect ...`, sc_inspect):
  inspect on|off|toggle      open / close (on arms it)     inspect arm|disarm   hot keys
  inspect pick               the pick mode ("Auswählen")   inspect select S|none
  inspect option outlines|order|dirty on|off               inspect tab widgets|frame|colors|look
  inspect copy               copy the selector ("Kopieren")
  inspect snap               remember the main window's frame (for `inspect expect same`)
  inspect expect open|closed|idle|same|excluded            inspect expect pick|flash on|off
  inspect expect selected S|none   inspect expect hover S|none
  inspect expect selector "s"      inspect expect copied "s"
idle: the inspector did no work since it closed (or since the last idle check); same: the main
window renders byte for byte as at `inspect snap`; excluded: the tree holds no record of the
inspector's own window.  Editing (development builds): inspect set|reset|undo|redo|save|list|
do ..., inspect expect changes|list|value|undo|redo|message (inspect_edit.rs).
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn inspect_enable(&mut self, on: bool)`**
  arm the inspector (`--inspect`, `jfgui_INSPECT=1`): its hot keys (Ctrl+Shift+I and F12,
  inspect_keys) open and close it; false closes it, the keys reach the app again
- **`fn inspect_show(&mut self, on: bool)`**
  open / close the inspector: its overlay in the app's windows and its tool window
  "Inspektor" (opening arms it); closed it costs nothing
- **`fn inspect_open(&self) -> bool`**
  the inspector is open
- **`fn inspect_keys(&mut self, keys: &[u32])`**
  the inspector's hot keys: VK | MOD_\* &lt;&lt; 16 each (MOD_SHIFT / MOD_CTRL / MOD_ALT);
  default Ctrl+Shift+I and F12, none: only the API and `--inspect` open it

#### `ui/perm.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/perm.rs`](../lib/ui/perm.rs)

```text
perm -- what build_rs.py builds into an app, set up before it starts, and the app's
permissions on the UI side (plat::policy, docs/PERMISSIONS.md, docs/VFS.md)

  boot(app, manifest, assets)   (main!) the app's name for its folders (plat::vfs::
                          set_app_id), its asset bundle as app:// (JFA1, apps/NAME/assets),
                          then its manifest (apps/NAME/PERMISSIONS, a BINS program's own
                          PERMISSIONS.<bin>); Err(exit code) for a bundle or manifest it
                          refuses.  Before the manifest: the user's languages and format
                          (i18n::boot: jfgui_LANG, else the system in window mode, German in
                          headless runs).  The paths on the command line come from the user:
                          with fs.user they may be read and written (folders with everything
                          below).  The steps are plat::boot's, which console programs
                          (rt::main!) run without the UI.  Script runs (--script) keep the
                          answers to permission questions in memory (jfgui_PERM_STORE or
                          `perm store` for a file).
  grant_user(path)        the same for a path of the file dialog or a drop
  trusted(f)              f on this thread without file checks: the library's own file
                          dialog lists folders, scripts read and write their files
  ask_here(on)            (runtime) the UI thread asks the questions of ask lines and agent
                          actions (window runs; scripts after `perm answer dialog`)
  answer(id, a) / set_answer(a) / set_wait(ms) / set_store(path)   (scripts: perm ...)
  Ui::perm_dialog()       (run_passes, after App::frame) the first open question as a content
                          dialog: what, the path / host / program / action, the plugin, the
                          manifest's reason (through the app's catalogue), the ask line, and
                          "Einmal erlauben" (until the program ends), "Immer erlauben"
                          (stored), "Ablehnen" (until the program ends), "Nie erlauben"
                          (stored); Esc = Ablehnen.  The answer reaches the app as
                          UIC_PERMISSION (arg 1 allowed, 0 refused): an access the UI thread
                          made while the question was open was refused, it may try again.
  Ui::permissions_page(id) -> bool   the ready-made settings section: every ask line and
                          answered agent action with what it allows, the rule, the reason
                          and the answer; "Zurücksetzen: <rule>" revokes one (asked again
                          on the next access), "Alle zurücksetzen" all; true when an answer
                          was revoked.  Ids: the scope of `id`, then the rule ("reset").

The key of plat::policy stays here: apps cannot widen their own permissions or answer
their own questions.
```

  (main!) set up the app: its name, its assets (app://), its permissions

**`impl Ui`**

#### `ui/recent.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/recent.rs`](../lib/ui/recent.rs)

```text
recent -- the app's list of recent files ("Zuletzt geöffnet") and the system's (plat::recent)

  recent_add(path)         a file the user opened or saved: first in the app's list (no
                           duplicates, at most RECENT_KEEP) and in the system's list
                           (plat::recent_add: Windows' recent files and jump list,
                           recently-used.xbel; needs the file readable under the app's
                           permissions)
  recent_files() -> [path] the app's list, newest first (a file may be gone meanwhile: the
                           app tells the user and calls recent_remove)
  recent_open(path) -> RecentOpen   a file of the list about to be opened (call it from the
                           user's click or key): Ready (read it now), Asking (the browser asks
                           for the permission again: App::command(UIC_RECENT, 1 readable /
                           0 refused or gone) follows, recent_reopened() names the file) or
                           Missing
  recent_reopened() -> Option<path>   the file UIC_RECENT answered for (once)
  recent_remove(path)      out of both lists
  recent_clear()           both lists emptied (the system's: this app's entries)

The app's list is config://recent.list (one path per line, newest first), read on first use
and kept in memory.  OS paths are kept absolute ("C:/x/a.png", "/home/u/a.png"; a folder
mount's file as its OS path), so another spelling of the same file is no new entry, and as
plat::persistent_name gives them (a Flatpak's file from the documents portal as its lasting
document: one of the portal's file dialog opens again after a restart without a new
dialog).  Headless runs (--shot, --script, agents) never touch the file and leave the
system's list alone (the list lives in memory there; jfgui_RECENT redirects the system's
list, plat/recent.rs).

The browser: the list is persisted in the origin's storage with every change (an emptied
list as an empty file: the storage keeps no deletions), so a reload starts with it.  A file
of the user's own (/handles/ID/NAME, Chromium's pickers) is read in at the start while the
browser still grants it; else recent_open asks through plat::web::reopen (the browser wants
the user's gesture).  Firefox and Safari have no such handles: the list stays, its files open
when the app kept them in the storage itself (plat::web::persist).
Android: the list is a file of the app's internal storage; the picker's grants are lasting
(takePersistableUriPermission), and a single document's grant is given up when its entry
leaves the list (pushed out, removed, cleared: Android keeps at most 128 / 512 of them); a
folder's grant stays, the app may use the folder for more.
```

```rust
/// how many files the app's list keeps
RECENT_KEEP: usize = 20
```

- **`enum RecentOpen`**
  what recent_open found for a file of the list
  - `Ready` -- the file can be read now
  - `Asking` -- the browser asks the user for the permission again (a file of the user's own after a
    reload): App::command(UIC_RECENT, 1 readable now / 0 refused or gone) follows
  - `Missing` -- gone or out of reach: the app tells the user and may call recent_remove

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn recent_add(&mut self, path: &str)`**
  a file the user opened or saved: first in the app's recent files and in the system's
- **`fn recent_open(&mut self, path: &str) -> RecentOpen`**
  a file of the recent list about to be opened (from the user's click or key): Ready,
  Asking (the browser asks for the permission; UIC_RECENT follows) or Missing
- **`fn recent_reopened(&mut self) -> Option<String>`**
  the file UIC_RECENT answered for, once
- **`fn recent_files(&self) -> Vec<String>`**
  the app's recent files, newest first
- **`fn recent_remove(&mut self, path: &str)`**
  a file out of the app's and the system's recent files
- **`fn recent_clear(&mut self)`**
  the app's recent files and its entries in the system's list forgotten

#### `ui/ribbon.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/ribbon.rs`](../lib/ui/ribbon.rs)

```text
Ribbon groups and typography tiles. Additive native UI component by office_ribbon;
no legacy counterpart. Uses normal focus, semantics, popups and style tokens.
```

- **`struct RibbonSample`**
  Explicit typography for a document sample, independent of the application's theme.
  Sizes and baseline displacement are 24.8 DIP; positive displacement moves downwards.
  - `font: u32`
  - `size: i32`
  - `color: u32`
  - `highlight: Option<u32>`
  - `baseline_shift: i32`
  - `underline: bool`
  - `strike: bool`

- **`struct RibbonMetrics`**
  Style-owned ribbon geometry in DIP. A scrolling ribbon keeps every group's
  original arrangement; a collapsing ribbon can use the compact/flyout layouts.
  - `content_height: i32`
  - `caption_height: i32`
  - `group_gap: i32`
  - `content_gap: i32`
  - `inset_x: i32` -- Zero uses the style's existing uniform `ribbon_padding`.
  - `inset_y: i32`
  - `collapse_groups: bool`

- **`struct RibbonGroup<'a>`**
  One ribbon group. Reserve `id..=id + 3` for its box, overflow and popup.
  - `id: u32` -- Stable base ID, unique across the window.
  - `label: &'a str` -- Visible group caption and accessible overflow name.
  - `width: i32` -- Preferred group width in DIP.
  - `compact_width: i32` -- Smallest width that still displays all controls, in DIP.

**`impl<'a> RibbonGroup<'a>`**

- **`const fn new(id: u32, label: &'a str, width: i32, compact_width: i32) -> Self`**
  Construct a group with a preferred and compact content width.

- **`enum RibbonGroupMode`**
  Presentation of an open ribbon group; pass it to `ribbon_group_end`.
  - `Inline(i32)` -- Preferred or compact inline width in DIP.
  - `Flyout(i32)` -- Group shown in a popup at its preferred width in DIP.

**`impl RibbonGroupMode`**

- **`fn width(self) -> i32`**
  Actual width available to the controls, in DIP.

- **`struct RibbonLayout`**
  Per-frame ribbon layout: shrink groups before moving them into labeled flyouts.

**`impl RibbonLayout`**

- **`fn new(available_width: i32, groups: &[RibbonGroup<'_>]) -> Self`**
  Compute group presentation for an available inner width in DIP.
  Groups collapse from right to left; extremely narrow windows can scroll.
- **`fn with_metrics( available_width: i32, groups: &[RibbonGroup<'_>], metrics: RibbonMetrics, ) -> Self`**
  Compute a layout using the active style's sizing and overflow policy.
- **`fn is_collapsed(&self, index: usize) -> bool`**
  Whether a group is reachable through its labeled overflow button.
- **`fn group_width(&self, index: usize) -> Option<i32>`**
  Width occupied by a group in the ribbon, in DIP.

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn ribbon_begin(&mut self, id: u32, groups: &[RibbonGroup<'_>]) -> RibbonLayout`**
  Start a style-sized ribbon (110 DIP by default). Pair with `ribbon_end`.
  All groups remain keyboard reachable; a scroll strip is the final fallback.
- **`fn ribbon_group_begin( &mut self, layout: &RibbonLayout, index: usize, group: &RibbonGroup<'_>, ) -> Option<RibbonGroupMode>`**
  Begin a group's controls when visible, or render its overflow button.
  Only call `ribbon_group_end` when this returns `Some`.
- **`fn ribbon_group_end(&mut self, mode: RibbonGroupMode, label: &str)`**
  Finish controls and draw the inline group caption; closes overflow when appropriate.
  Flyouts already have their named opener, so no trailing caption is painted
  over a nested action menu emitted while building their controls.
- **`fn ribbon_group_end_launcher( &mut self, mode: RibbonGroupMode, label: &str, id: u32, action_label: &str, flags: u32, ) -> u32`**
  Finish a group with a separately focusable dialog-launch button in its caption.
  `id` is an additional unique widget ID; `action_label` is its full semantic name.
  Activation is returned to the app, which opens its existing dialog. Disabled
  launchers retain their label and cannot be invoked through keyboard or agents.
- **`fn ribbon_end(&mut self)`**
  Finish the ribbon begun with `ribbon_begin`.
- **`fn ribbon_button_width(&mut self, label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32) -> i32`**
  Natural action width in DIP, including the style's icon, label and menu
  spacing. Measuring neither consumes next_\* hints nor creates a widget.
  Use it when composing translated ribbon columns before ribbon_begin.
- **`fn ribbon_button(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  Compact ribbon action with clipped drawing, native focus and a full tooltip.
  `ST_ICON_ONLY`, `ST_LARGE`, `ST_CHECKED` and `ST_DISABLED` are supported.
- **`fn ribbon_large_button(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  Large ribbon action: the style draws its icon above a visible caption.
  It is one normal focusable, inspectable button. Use `next_size` to override
  its natural style size; checked/disabled flags keep their ordinary meaning.
- **`fn ribbon_menu_button(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32) -> u32`**
  Ribbon-styled menu opener. `id` is also the popup identifier. Its natural
  dimensions, icon, menu indicator and enabled state come from the style.
- **`fn ribbon_stacked_split_button( &mut self, id: u32, menu_id: u32, label: &str, menu_label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32, ) -> u32`**
  Large split action with an icon hit area above its menu caption. Both
  parts remain independently focusable and discoverable through semantics.
  Pair the `menu_id` with a normal flyout. Alt+Down/F4 opens the caption menu.
- **`fn ribbon_split_button( &mut self, id: u32, menu_id: u32, label: &str, menu_label: &str, icon: u32, flags: u32, ) -> u32`**
  A large primary action beside an independently focusable dropdown.
  `id` identifies the primary action; `menu_id` identifies both the dropdown
  button and its popup. Both IDs must be unique. `menu_label` is a full semantic
  name, not an unlabeled chevron. Pair with `flyout_begin(menu_id, ..)` and
  `flyout_end` immediately afterwards to provide actual secondary actions.
  Returns primary EV_\* flags plus EV_OPEN while the dropdown popup is open.
  Tab reaches both parts; Enter/Space activate the focused part. Alt+Down or
  unbound F4 on the main part forwards to the existing dropdown keyboard path.
- **`fn ribbon_gallery_begin(&mut self, id: u32)`**
  Begin an inset horizontal gallery on an input-colored surface. The caller
  supplies its size and tiles; finish with `box_end`. The whole frame is painted
  before applying the three-DIP tile inset, including in dark themes.
- **`fn ribbon_tile( &mut self, id: u32, label: &str, preview: &str, typography: u32, selected: bool, ) -> u32`**
  Typography preview tile for a style gallery; selection is exposed semantically.
  `typography` is a `TS_*` style; use `next_size` to set a compact gallery width.
- **`fn ribbon_font_tile(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, preview: &str, typography: u32, selected: bool, face: Option<(u32, i32, u32)>) -> u32`**
  A gallery tile with an optional document font, 24.8-DIP size and ARGB ink.
  The surrounding control follows the application theme; the sample stays document-colored.
- **`fn ribbon_sample_tile(&mut self, id: u32, label: &str, preview: &str, typography: u32, selected: bool, sample: Option<RibbonSample>) -> u32`**
  Style-gallery tile with explicit highlight, baseline and text decorations.

#### `ui/settings_page.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/settings_page.rs`](../lib/ui/settings_page.rs)

```text
settings_page -- the settings page of a typed schema (base::settings)

  settings_page(id, &mut settings) -> true when a value changed in this pass

The keys of the schema without KF_HIDDEN, grouped by section: the sections of
Schema::sections first (with their titles), then the others in the order of their first
key (titled by their name; keys without a section: "Allgemein").  Each section is a title
and a card; each key a row: its label on the left, the control on the right -- bool a
switch, int a number box (min..max, step), num a number box with its decimals, text a text
box (at most max bytes), choice a combo box, colour a swatch and a button with the hex code
that opens a picker -- and a reset button (disabled at the default); its help text and
(KF_RESTART) a note below.  The label is the text right before the control, so screen
readers name text boxes, number boxes and combo boxes by it (their own text is their
value); the switch and the colour button carry it as their label (scripts: click "Dunkles
Design").  The reset buttons are "Zurücksetzen: <label>".  Labels, help texts, section
titles and choice labels go through i18n::t (the app's catalogue).  Ids: the scope of `id`,
then the key's name ("value", "reset", "swatch", "pick" inside it; ids.rs).
```

#### `ui/slider.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/slider.rs`](../lib/ui/slider.rs)

**`impl Range`**

- **`fn position(&self, value: i32, travel: i32) -> i32`**
  Map a value to the slider's usable pixel travel. RG_LOG applies to positive,
  increasing bounds; all other bounds use linear mapping. Degenerate ranges
  or travel return zero. Values outside the range are clamped.
- **`fn value_at(&self, position: i32, travel: i32) -> i32`**
  Map pixel travel to the nearest integer value, before step snapping. The
  logarithmic inverse uses bounded binary search (at most 31 iterations).
  Keyboard steps and semantic values always remain in the original units.

#### `ui/sound.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/sound.rs`](../lib/ui/sound.rs)

```text
sound -- the system's sounds from the UI (plat::audio::sound)

  beep(SOUND_*) -> bool    the system's sound for an event (plat::audio::SOUND_INFO,
                           SOUND_WARNING, SOUND_ERROR, SOUND_QUESTION, SOUND_NOTIFY,
                           SOUND_DEFAULT) unless sounds are off -> false: nothing played
  dialog_sound(SOUND_*)    right after dialog_begin returned true: the sound once, when the
                           dialog has just opened, where the platform's message dialogs play
                           one (plat::audio::dialog_sounds: Windows like MessageBox, Linux
                           desktops while event sounds are on; not Android, not the browser)
  set_sounds(on), sounds() the app's own switch (default on; an app setting "Klänge");
                           jfgui_SOUNDS=0 turns them off for the process

An app whose PERMISSIONS lack `audio.output` plays nothing: beep is refused like any other
access (an ask line asks, "PERMDENY audio.output" once, plat::policy::denials), dialog_sound
stays silent without a question or a record (plat::policy::audio_granted).

Headless runs (scripts, --shot) play nothing: plat::audio's dry run prints "sound: NAME", and
the script command `expect sound KIND|none` checks the last sound requested (auto.rs).
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn beep(&mut self, kind: u32) -> bool`**
  the system's sound for kind (plat::audio::SOUND_\*) -> false: off, unknown, not
  permitted (`audio.output`) or not played
- **`fn dialog_sound(&mut self, kind: u32) -> bool`**
  inside an open content dialog: its sound, once when it has just opened, where message
  dialogs play one on this platform and the app may play sound -> whether a sound was
  asked for
- **`fn set_sounds(&mut self, on: bool)`**
  the app's switch for its sounds (beep, dialog_sound); on by default
- **`fn sounds(&self) -> bool`**
  sounds are on: the app's switch and jfgui_SOUNDS (0: off)

#### `ui/rtl.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/rtl.rs`](../lib/ui/rtl.rs)

```text
rtl -- right-to-left layout: every window mirrored as a whole (as Windows' WS_EX_LAYOUTRTL)

  rtl() -> bool                    the windows are mirrored now
  set_rtl(Some(on) | None)         force it, or None: from the UI language (Arabic, Hebrew,
                                   Persian, Urdu, ...: i18n::rtl_language); command line
                                   --rtl / --ltr
  ltr_begin(x, w) / ltr_end()      a region of the window whose content keeps its reading
                                   order (text fields, canvases, colour pads): it moves to its
                                   mirrored place as a whole
  ltr_x(x) -> x                    a logical x (the pointer: wp.ctx.mx) inside the outermost
                                   open region, so the region's own maths stays LTR

Layout and hit testing stay in logical (LTR) coordinates: a box's first child is its
logical start.  Before a window is rendered, every recorded command is mirrored across
it (cmd_mirror): boxes, clips, lines and shapes flip; text, images and custom drawings
move but keep their direction; directional icons (chevrons, back / forward, undo / redo,
indent) are swapped for their mirror images.  Input comes back the same way: the pointer x
is mirrored, a horizontal wheel turns round, plain Left / Right swap (text fields swap
them back).  What leaves the UI is physical: sems (scripts, the agent), popup rects of OS
popup windows, the platform's hit tests, resize edges and the IME caret.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn rtl(&self) -> bool`**
  the windows are mirrored now (right-to-left layout)
- **`fn set_rtl(&mut self, on: Option<bool>)`**
  mirror the windows (Some(true)), never (Some(false)) or as the UI language reads (None)
- **`fn ltr_begin(&mut self, x: i32, w: i32)`**
  ltr_begin(x, w): the following commands of this layer keep their LTR order inside the
  columns x .. x + w (px); pairs with ltr_end
- **`fn ltr_end(&mut self)`**
  close the region of ltr_begin
- **`fn ltr_x(&self, x: i32) -> i32`**
  a logical x (the pointer) as the open ltr_begin region sees it: its content is not
  mirrored, so the pointer is mirrored back across the region
- **`fn rtl_map(&self, x: i32, ix: i32, iw: i32) -> i32`**
  rtl_map(x, ix, iw): a logical x as a region ix .. ix + iw that keeps its LTR content
  sees it (the same before its ltr_begin)

Source: [`lib/ui/screen.rs`](../lib/ui/screen.rs)

```text
screen -- the monitors, global shortcuts, a colour from anywhere on the screen and pictures of
the screen for the app (plat::screen, plat::hotkey)

  monitors() -> Vec<Monitor>       every monitor, the primary one first (rect / work area in
                                   desktop units, dpi, refresh, name); a change comes as
                                   App::command(UIC_SETTINGS, plat::SET_MONITORS)

                                   ("Ctrl+Alt+K"; plat::Chord::parse names the keys): when it
                                   is pressed anywhere, App::command(UIC_HOTKEY, id); when the
                                   desktop drops it later (the portal's dialog),
                                   App::command(UIC_HOTKEY_LOST, id) and hotkey_error(id)
                                   tells why.  Needs `input.global` in the manifest.
  hotkey_unregister(id) -> bool    hotkeys_available() -> bool
  pick_color() -> bool             the user clicks a pixel anywhere on the screen (Esc
                                   cancels); then App::command(UIC_PICK, 1 picked / 0 not) and
                                   picked_color() -> Some(0xRRGGBB); false: not possible here
  pick_available() -> bool         a colour picker with CP_PIPETTE shows its pipette then
  screenshot(rect) -> bool         a picture of the whole desktop (None) or a rectangle; then

  screen_error() -> Option<ScreenError>   why the last pick / picture failed

Headless runs (scripts, --shot) touch nothing real: shortcuts are only recorded (the script
command `system hotkey ID` presses one), a pick waits for `system pick RRGGBB|cancel`, the
monitors are the window (or the script's `screen` rectangle) at the run's dpi, pictures are
Unavailable.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn monitors(&mut self) -> Vec<Monitor>`**
  every monitor, the primary one first
- **`fn hotkeys_available(&mut self) -> bool`**
  whether global shortcuts work here
- **`fn hotkey_register(&mut self, id: u32, chord: &str, description: &str) -> Result<(), HotkeyError>`**
  register chord ("Ctrl+Alt+K") as the global shortcut id; description tells the user
  what it does (the desktop's dialog shows it)
- **`fn hotkey_unregister(&mut self, id: u32) -> bool`**
  remove the global shortcut id -> false when it was not registered
- **`fn hotkey_error(&self, id: u32) -> Option<HotkeyError>`**
  why the desktop dropped the shortcut id (after UIC_HOTKEY_LOST)
- **`fn pick_available(&self) -> bool`**
  whether the user can pick a colour anywhere on the screen here (headless: yes, the
  script answers)
- **`fn pick_color(&mut self) -> bool`**
  the user picks a pixel anywhere on the screen; UIC_PICK reports the end -> false when
  that is not possible here (or a pick runs)
- **`fn picked_color(&mut self) -> Option<u32>`**
  the colour of the last pick (0xRRGGBB), once
- **`fn screenshot(&mut self, rect: Option<[i32; 4]>) -> bool`**
  a picture of the whole desktop (None) or of a rectangle (desktop units); UIC_SCREENSHOT
  reports it -> false when that is not possible here
- **`fn screenshot_take(&mut self) -> Option<Surface>`**
  the picture of the last screenshot, once
- **`fn screen_error(&self) -> Option<ScreenError>`**
  why the last pick or picture failed (None: it worked or was not asked for)

#### `ui/scrollcopy.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/scrollcopy.rs`](../lib/ui/scrollcopy.rs)

```text
scrollcopy -- scroll copies: when only a scroll view's content moved, the pixels that stay
valid are moved inside the framebuffer; the band that came into view and whatever really
changed are drawn again

  scroll_copy_begin(id, ox, oy)   the commands recorded until scroll_copy_end are the content
                                  of scroll view `id` and move with it; (ox, oy) = window px
                                  of the content's origin (its place minus the scroll offset).
                                  Call right after the view's clip.  Scroll views, lists, data
                                  views, vlist, document, code and multi-line text views do.
  scroll_copy_end()
  (dirty.rs) Pass: the content grids of a frame while dirty_compute hashes the commands;
  sc_plan: the window cells a copy can make valid; sc_want: copy or draw; sc_copy: the copy
  scopy_present(n) (render_live): the moved cells join the presented rectangles
  scopy_done() (render_live, after drawing): the frame's cost for sc_want

A view whose origin moved (its clip staying) in the last RECENT frames gets a grid of 32 x 32 px cells aligned
at its content's origin, over its clip.  A cell's hash mixes, in drawing order, every content
command touching it (hash and box relative to the origin, so a moved command keeps them) and
every other command over the view that is flat there (a fill covering the cell's visible
part: window background, cards; an opaque one forgets what was below).  Anything else over
the cell (text or shapes of other layers, scroll bars, popups, the uneven edge of a fill) and
content whose pixels may change when it moves (the rasterizer works in absolute f32
coordinates: rounded corners, circles, lines; custom drawings, icons painted by the style or
an icon hook, very large or left-cut text) marks the cell bad.  When the origin moved by
(dx, dy) since the last frame and the view's clip stayed, a cell with its old hash that is
bad in neither frame shows the same pixels moved by (dx, dy): the dirty window cells covered
by such cells may be copied instead of drawn -- byte-identical to a full redraw
(--verify-dirty checks it).

A copy reads and writes a cell's pixels: filling a flat cell again is cheaper, drawing text
or icons is not, and every rectangle left to draw replays the commands.  So only cells with
detail are copied, small gaps between drawn cells are drawn too, a copy must take over a
quarter of what would be drawn, and per view the measured cost of frames that copied and of
frames that drew decides (the other way is tried again every EXPLORE frames; the first
frames try both); a view that moved IDLE_MAX frames in a row with grids but without copying
gets none for SKIP frames.  Frames checked by --verify-dirty always copy when they can (and
never skip).  No copy: a horizontal move in a mirrored window, the inspector, pending canvas
damage, a full redraw.  `expect scrollcopy` (auto.rs) counts the frames that copied,
jfgui_DEBUG=1 prints them.
```

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn scroll_copy_begin(&mut self, id: u32, ox: i64, oy: i64)`**
  ui_scroll_copy_begin(id, ox, oy): the commands recorded until scroll_copy_end are the
  content of scroll view `id`; (ox, oy) = the window px of the content's origin (its
  position minus the scroll offset).  Call right after the view's clip.  When only the
  origin moved between two frames, pixels still shown may be moved in the framebuffer
  instead of drawn again (content that does not move with the origin is simply drawn).
- **`fn scroll_copy_end(&mut self)`**
  ui_scroll_copy_end: the end of the content of scroll_copy_begin

#### `ui/symbol.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/symbol.rs`](../lib/ui/symbol.rs)

```text
symbol -- multi-colour vector symbols (device pictures for diagrams and palettes): vicon's
layers with palette roles and stroke widths, parsed once, drawn as vectors or rasterised
once per size and palette and blitted

  Symbol::parse(art, vb) -> Symbol     art: SVG path layers separated by '|' on a vb[0] x
                                       vb[1] grid (tools/vsym.py writes them from SVG files)
  sym.paint(g, x, y, scale, &pal)      every layer, the grid's (0, 0) at x, y (the draw
                                       context's coordinates, like Dc::fill), scale = px
                                       per grid unit
  sym.raster(g, w, &pal) -> Surface    the symbol w px wide in a PARGB surface
  sym.height(w) -> px                  the height of the symbol drawn w px wide
  SymPalette { c: [u32; 10] }          the colours of the roles SYM_INK .. SYM_HI
  SymPalette::from_theme(ui, tint)     light, dark or high contrast from the theme's tokens;
                                       tint = the category colour 0xRRGGBB (its light value)
  SymPalette::light / dark(text, bg, tint), contrast(ui)   the three schemes
  pal.powered_off()                    LEDs and screens dark (a device without power)
  SymbolCache::new()                   rasters of up to 256 (symbol, width, palette)
  cache.draw(g, id, &sym, x, y, w, &pal, opacity)   the symbol w px wide at x, y: the
                                       cached raster blitted, wider than 256 px the
                                       vectors; opacity 0..255 (power off: 115 = 45 %)
  cache.get(g, id, &sym, w, &pal) -> Option<Rc<Surface>>   the raster itself

Layer prefixes (vicon.rs's syntax extended, so its art stays valid): F filled (non-zero
rule), E filled (even-odd), neither = stroked with round caps and joins; #n palette role
0..9 (default 0, an 'A' layer 4); S<w> stroke width in grid units (default 1.5; at least
0.8 px when drawn).  Layers paint in order.  Roles: 0 ink (outlines), 1 body, 2 body shade,
3 screen, 4 category tint, 5 ports and dark parts, 6 ok, 7 warn, 8 crit (status LEDs),
9 highlight.  Light and dark themes swap the palette only.

The cache key is (id, width, palette hash) with the palette compared too; `id` is the
caller's number for the symbol.  Rasters are drawn at whole pixels, so x, y of draw are
integers; paint takes fractional positions (a zoomed diagram).
```

```rust
SYM_INK: u8 = 0  // outlines
SYM_BODY: u8 = 1  // the device's body
SYM_SHADE: u8 = 2  // a body part in shadow (sides, bezels, recesses)
SYM_SCREEN: u8 = 3  // displays
SYM_TINT: u8 = 4  // the category colour (one band per symbol)
SYM_PORT: u8 = 5  // ports, grilles, dark parts
SYM_OK: u8 = 6  // status LEDs
SYM_WARN: u8 = 7
SYM_CRIT: u8 = 8
SYM_HI: u8 = 9  // highlight (light details)
SYM_ROLES: usize = 10
/// the widest symbol SymbolCache rasterises (px); wider ones are drawn as vectors
SYM_CACHE_MAX_W: i32 = 256
```

- **`struct Symbol`**
  a parsed multi-colour symbol (see the module comment)
  - `vb: [f32; 2]` -- the grid: width and height in grid units

**`impl Symbol`**

- **`fn parse(art: &str, vb: [f32; 2]) -> Symbol`**
  parse the layers once; layers whose path data does not parse are left out
- **`fn layers(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of layers that parsed
- **`fn height(&self, w: i32) -> i32`**
  the height in px of the symbol drawn w px wide
- **`fn paint(&self, g: &mut Gfx, x: f32, y: f32, scale: f32, pal: &SymPalette)`**
  draw every layer with the grid's (0, 0) at x, y (draw context coordinates) and
  `scale` px per grid unit; the draw colour is kept
- **`fn raster(&self, g: &mut Gfx, w: i32, pal: &SymPalette) -> Surface`**
  the symbol w px wide in a new PARGB surface (height(w) px high)

- **`struct SymPalette`**
  the colours of a symbol's roles (straight 0xAARRGGBB, index = SYM_\* role)
  - `c: [u32; SYM_ROLES]`

**`impl SymPalette`**

- **`fn from_theme(ui: &Ui, tint: u32) -> SymPalette`**
  the palette of the current theme: high contrast, dark or light; tint = the category
  colour 0xRRGGBB as it looks in the light theme
- **`fn light(text: u32, bg: u32, tint: u32) -> SymPalette`**
  the light scheme from the text and window colours (opaque): slate outlines, near-white
  bodies, pale steel screens
- **`fn dark(text: u32, bg: u32, tint: u32) -> SymPalette`**
  the dark scheme: light grey outlines, bodies a step above the window, dark screens,
  the tint lighter and greyer
- **`fn contrast(ui: &Ui) -> SymPalette`**
  high contrast: outlines and ports in the text colour, every fill in the window colour,
  the tint band in the highlight (accent) colour, LEDs in the status colours
- **`fn powered_off(&self) -> SymPalette`**
  a device without power: status LEDs dark, screens off
- **`fn hash(&self) -> u32`**
  FNV-1a of the colours (the cache key)

- **`struct SymbolCache`**
  rasters of symbols per (id, width, palette), the least recently used one dropped
  beyond 256

**`impl SymbolCache`**

- **`fn new() -> SymbolCache`**
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of rasters kept
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn clear(&mut self)`**
  drop every raster
- **`fn get(&mut self, g: &mut Gfx, id: u32, sym: &Symbol, w: i32, pal: &SymPalette) -> Option<Rc<Surface>>`**
  the raster of symbol `id` w px wide in this palette, made on the first call; None for
  widths outside 1..=SYM_CACHE_MAX_W
- **`fn draw(&mut self, g: &mut Gfx, id: u32, sym: &Symbol, x: i32, y: i32, w: i32, pal: &SymPalette, opacity: u32)`**
  draw symbol `id` w px wide with its top-left corner at x, y (draw context
  coordinates) at opacity 0..255: the cached raster, wider than SYM_CACHE_MAX_W the
  vectors (through a raster when translucent)

#### `ui/term.rs`

Source: [`lib/ui/term.rs`](../lib/ui/term.rs)

```text
term -- a terminal / console widget: a scrollback ring with an ANSI subset, the input line on
textbox_surface (IME, clipboard, selection), history, completion, IOS-style `?` help, a
--More-- pager, busy mode with type-ahead, raw keys, mouse selection and search

  TermState::new(scrollback) -> st     a console (the app keeps one per console); scrollback
                                       = lines kept (at least 100)
  st.write(&[u8]) / st.write_str(s)    output: UTF-8 with an ANSI subset -- SGR 0 1 2 4 7 22
                                       24 27, colours 30-37 / 90-97 / 39, backgrounds 40-47 /
                                       100-107 / 49 (38;5 / 48;5 / 38;2 mapped to the 16);
                                       \r \n \t BS, BEL (the console flashes), ESC[K (0 1 2),
                                       ESC[2J (the screen scrolls clear), ESC[3J (the
                                       scrollback too), ESC[H, ESC[nC / nD / nG; OSC skipped
  st.clear()                           drop the scrollback and the current line
  st.set_prompt(s)                     the prompt before the input (SGR allowed)
  st.set_mode(TM_*)                    TM_LINE the input line; TM_BUSY a command runs: no
                                       input line, typed lines wait (type-ahead) and come
                                       back one Submit at a time in TM_LINE; TM_RAW every key
                                       goes to the app (TermEv::Raw); TM_SECRET a line typed
                                       without echo or history (passwords)
  st.input_set(s, caret)               replace the input line (caret: a byte index)
  st.complete_reply(line, list)        the answer to TermEv::Complete: the new line, and
                                       candidates listed in columns below the old one
  st.pager(on)                         on: the following output pages -- a screen minus one
                                       line (st.page_len lines when set, as "terminal
                                       length"), then pager_text (" --More-- "): Space a page,
                                       Enter a line, q / Esc / Ctrl+C TermEv::PagerQuit (later
                                       output is dropped until pager(false)); off: the app
                                       wrote everything (a held rest still pages)
  st.grid() -> (cols, rows)            the character grid of the last layout
  st.text() -> String                  scrollback and the current line as plain text
  ui.terminal(id, &mut st, TF_*) -> Vec<TermEv>   the console, filling the place it gets
                                       (natural 480 x 240 DIP; next_size(-1, -1) fills);
                                       ids id .. id + 7 (id + 1: the input line)
  ui.mono_font_set(font)               the monospace font of every console (an id from
                                       ui.text.load_mem; apps embed DejaVu Sans Mono)
  ui.mono_font(size_pt) -> (font, cell_w)   that font, else font_load("monospace"), else
                                       FONT_REG drawn cell by cell; the size is adjusted so
                                       that a cell is a whole number of pixels

Keys while focused: Enter submits (the line is echoed after the prompt and kept in the
history), Tab TermEv::Complete, Up / Down the history, Home / End; TF_QHELP: a typed `?` is
not inserted but gives TermEv::Help (the line up to the caret); Ctrl+C copies a selection,
else TermEv::Interrupt (echoes ^C); TF_CTRL_SHIFT6: Ctrl+Shift+6 interrupts too; Ctrl+D on an
empty line TermEv::Eof, Ctrl+Z on an empty line and Ctrl+L TermEv::Chord; Ctrl+U clears the
line before the caret; Ctrl+Shift+C copies; Ctrl+V / Ctrl+Shift+V paste (every pasted line
is one Submit); PgUp / PgDn (also with Shift), Ctrl+Up / Down, Ctrl+Home / End scroll;
Ctrl+F the search bar (F3 / Enter: the next older match, Shift+F3 / Shift+Enter: newer, Esc
closes it).  While busy or paging the console holds the keyboard as a text box would: plain
keys are no accelerators, the undo keys stay with it (the app's undo does not run).  Mouse:
a drag selects in the scrollback, a double click a word, the wheel scrolls; scrolled up,
new output shows a "Neue Ausgabe" button that jumps down.  Every
visible line is a K_TEXT record (`expect text:"..." exists`), the input line the K_TEXTBOX
id + 1.  Colours: a 16-colour palette from the theme tokens (light / dark).  Every character
takes one cell (wide CJK characters overlap the next); right-to-left the rows stay LTR.

The visible rows are drawn by two cached Draw objects (scrollback, current line + input),
replaced only when what they show changes, so typing redraws only the input rows.
```

```rust
/// TermState::mode: the input line
TM_LINE: u8 = 0
/// TermState::mode: a command runs -- no input line, typed text waits (type-ahead)
TM_BUSY: u8 = 1
/// TermState::mode: every key and character goes to the app (TermEv::Raw)
TM_RAW: u8 = 2
/// TermState::mode: a line typed without echo or history (passwords)
TM_SECRET: u8 = 3
TF_QHELP: u32 = 1  // a typed `?` asks for help (TermEv::Help, IOS)
TF_CTRL_SHIFT6: u32 = 2  // Ctrl+Shift+6 interrupts too (IOS)
TF_NO_INPUT: u32 = 4  // output only: no input line
TF_NO_FRAME: u32 = 8  // no border, a small padding
TK_KEY: u32 = 0x8000_0000  // TermEv::Raw: a key (VK | MOD_* << 16), not a character
```

- **`enum TermEv`**
  what ui.terminal reports
  - `Submit(String)` -- Enter: the line (already echoed after the prompt and kept in the history)
  - `Complete { line: String, caret: usize }` -- Tab: the input line and the caret (byte index); answer with complete_reply
  - `Help(String)` -- TF_QHELP: `?` was typed; the line up to the caret (echoed with the `?`)
  - `Interrupt` -- Ctrl+C without a selection (TF_CTRL_SHIFT6: also Ctrl+Shift+6)
  - `Eof` -- Ctrl+D on an empty line
  - `Chord(u32)` -- Ctrl+Z on an empty line, Ctrl+L: VK | MOD_\* &lt;&lt; 16
  - `PagerQuit` -- the pager was quit (q, Esc, Ctrl+C)
  - `Resize(u16, u16)` -- the character grid changed (also at the first layout): columns, rows
  - `Raw(Vec<u32>)` -- TM_RAW: characters, and keys as TK_KEY | VK | MOD_\* &lt;&lt; 16; Enter 13, Tab 9,
    Backspace 127, Esc 27, Ctrl+letter 1..26

- **`struct TermState`**
  the state of one console (see the module header); the app keeps it between frames
  - `prompt: String` -- the text before the input (SGR allowed)
  - `mode: u8` -- TM_LINE, TM_BUSY, TM_RAW, TM_SECRET
  - `flags: u32` -- TF_\* added to the flags of ui.terminal
  - `font: Option<u32>` -- a font id for this console (None: ui.mono_font)
  - `size_pt: f32` -- the text size in points (default 10)
  - `pager_text: String` -- the pager's line (default " --More-- ")
  - `page_len: u16` -- lines of output per page of the pager (0, the default: the screen minus one line)

**`impl TermState`**

- **`fn new(scrollback: usize) -> TermState`**
  a console keeping `scrollback` lines (at least 100)
- **`fn write(&mut self, s: &[u8])`**
  output: UTF-8 with the ANSI subset of the module header (paged while the pager is on)
- **`fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str)`**
  write(s.as_bytes())
- **`fn clear(&mut self)`**
  drop the scrollback and the current line (the history stays)
- **`fn set_prompt(&mut self, s: &str)`**
  the prompt before the input (SGR allowed)
- **`fn set_mode(&mut self, mode: u8)`**
  TM_LINE, TM_BUSY, TM_RAW or TM_SECRET
- **`fn input_set(&mut self, s: &str, caret: usize)`**
  replace the input line; caret: a byte index (clamped to a character start)
- **`fn input(&self) -> &str`**
  the input line as typed so far
- **`fn history(&self) -> &[String]`**
  the lines submitted so far (oldest first)
- **`fn complete_reply<S: AsRef<str>>(&mut self, line: &str, list: &[S])`**
  the answer to TermEv::Complete: the new input line (caret at its end); a non-empty
  list is shown in columns below the line as typed
- **`fn pager(&mut self, on: bool)`**
  on: the following output pages (see the module header); off: the app wrote all of it
- **`fn pager_waiting(&self) -> bool`**
  the pager holds output and waits for a key
- **`fn grid(&self) -> (u16, u16)`**
  the character grid of the last layout (columns, rows; 0 before the first)
- **`fn text(&self) -> String`**
  the scrollback and the current line as plain text (lines joined with '\\n')
- **`fn line_count(&self) -> usize`**
  lines kept in the scrollback

**`impl Ui`**

- **`fn mono_font_set(&mut self, font: u32)`**
