### `text/lcd.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/lcd.rs`](../lib/text/lcd.rs)

```text
lcd -- subpixel (LCD, ClearType-like) glyph smoothing

  set_subpixel(SUBPIXEL_*) / subpixel()   the order of the display's subpixels; NONE (the
       default) keeps greyscale masks.  RGB / BGR: three columns per pixel, VRGB / VBGR:
       three rows (rotated panels)

A glyph is rasterized at three times the resolution across the subpixels (x for RGB / BGR,
y for VRGB / VBGR), FreeType's default 5-tap FIR filter (08 4D 56 4D 08, sum 256) spreads
every subpixel's coverage over its neighbours (fewer colour fringes, the energy of each
pixel kept), and each colour channel is blended with its own coverage.  The cache entry
holds 3 bytes per pixel in the physical order of the subpixels (left to right, or top to
bottom), so RGB and BGR share it; the mask is one pixel wider (taller) on each side than
the greyscale one.

Blending is gamma-correct-ish: target and text colour go to linear light (gamma 1.6, a
256-entry table), each channel is mixed there and comes back through a 2 x 4096-entry
table.  Linear light makes dark text thinner and light text bolder, so the coverage is
adjusted first by the text colour's luminance (DirectWrite's "enhanced contrast",
c' = c (1 + k) / (1 + k c), k = LCD_DARK for black text down to -LCD_LIGHT for white):
black, white and grey text keep the weight of greyscale text within a few per cent
(fonttest --selftest measures it).

Used only where it is safe: an opaque target (FMT_XRGB, the window framebuffer) and a
glyph from the cache.  A8 and PARGB targets (layers, images, anything composited later),
colour glyphs (COLR layers, CBDT bitmaps), the icon font, glyphs too large for the cache
(filled as paths) and black-and-white masks (set_antialias(false)) stay greyscale.  The
text colour's alpha and the global opacity scale the coverage (the target stays opaque).
Mirrored (RTL) windows mirror the command lists, not the pixels: text keeps the physical
subpixel order.
```

```rust
/// set_subpixel: greyscale smoothing (no subpixels)
SUBPIXEL_NONE: u8 = 0
/// set_subpixel: red, green, blue from left to right
SUBPIXEL_RGB: u8 = 1
/// set_subpixel: blue, green, red from left to right
SUBPIXEL_BGR: u8 = 2
/// set_subpixel: red, green, blue from top to bottom
SUBPIXEL_VRGB: u8 = 3
/// set_subpixel: blue, green, red from top to bottom
SUBPIXEL_VBGR: u8 = 4
```

**`impl Text`**

- **`fn set_subpixel(&mut self, order: u8)`**
  the subpixel order of the display (SUBPIXEL_\*): RGB / BGR / VRGB / VBGR draw glyphs on
  opaque (FMT_XRGB) targets with subpixel smoothing, NONE (the default) in greyscale;
  see lcd.rs for where it applies
- **`fn subpixel(&self) -> u8`**
  the subpixel order in use (SUBPIXEL_\*)
- **`fn lcd_tables_exact(&mut self) -> bool`**
  (tests) every byte survives the trip through linear light unchanged

### `text/outline.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/outline.rs`](../lib/text/outline.rs)

```text
outline -- glyph outline buffer, path emitter and the operations of synthetic styles
                                                                      [src/text/outline.s]

  Outline::reset / point / reserve / close / contour / npts / bbox
  emit(path, gp, zones)       append the buffer to the path with the gp transform (TrueType
                              contours exactly like glyph_path; cubic contours flattened like
                              path_cubic); zones = FS_SHARP grid fitting (fit_zones)
  embolden(strength)          FreeType FT_Outline_EmboldenXY(strength, strength)
  shear(k), transform(from, a, b, c, d), translate(from, dx, dy)
  owner_set / owner_is        "prepared" tracking: a box query leaves the untransformed
                              outline of (font context, glyph) in the buffer

Points f32 x, y (font units, y up) + u8 tags; contour ends u32 (last point index).
TrueType contours (OLT_ON / OLT_OFF) follow the implied-midpoint rules; cubic contours
(CFF) start with an on-curve point, two OLT_CUBIC points between on-curve points.
```

```rust
OLT_OFF: u8 = 0  // quadratic control point
OLT_ON: u8 = 1  // on-curve point
OLT_CUBIC: u8 = 2  // cubic control point
OL_MAX_PTS: usize = 1 << 20
OL_MAX_CONT: usize = 1 << 18
F_TAN12: f32 = 0.21255656
F_INV30: f32 = 0.033333335
```

- **`struct Zones`**
  FS_SHARP zones: {z (font units), p (px)} ascending
  - `n: usize`
  - `z: [(f32, f32); ZONE_MAX]`

**`impl Zones`**

- **`fn fit(desc: i32, xh: i32, caph: i32, asc: i32, sy: f32) -> Zones`**
  descender, 0, x-height, cap height, ascender snapped with sy  [ol_fit_zones]

- **`struct Outline`**
  - `pts: Vec<(f32, f32)>`
  - `tags: Vec<u8>`
  - `ends: Vec<u32>`
  - `err: bool`

**`impl Outline`**

- **`fn reset(&mut self)`**
  empty the buffer (owner cleared)  [ol_reset]
- **`fn npts(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn point(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32, tag: u8) -> bool`**
  append a point (font units, OLT_\*)  [ol_point]
- **`fn reserve(&mut self, n: usize) -> Option<usize>`**
  append n points (0, 0, OLT_OFF) to be filled in; the index of the first  [ol_reserve]
- **`fn close(&mut self)`**
  end the current contour  [ol_close]
- **`fn contour(&mut self, last: u32) -> bool`**
  end a contour at point index last (last &lt; cstart: empty, ignored)  [ol_contour]
- **`fn owner_set(&mut self, serial: u64, glyph: u32)`**
- **`fn owner_is(&self, serial: u64, glyph: u32) -> bool`**
- **`fn bbox(&self) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  control box {xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax} (floor / ceil, clamped to +-1e6)  [ol_box]
- **`fn shear(&mut self, k: f32)`**
  x += y \* k  [ol_shear]
- **`fn transform(&mut self, from: usize, a: f32, b: f32, c: f32, d: f32)`**
  points from..n: (x, y) -> (a x + c y, b x + d y)  [ol_transform]
- **`fn translate(&mut self, from: usize, dx: f32, dy: f32)`**
  points from..n += (dx, dy)  [ol_translate]
- **`fn embolden(&mut self, strength: f32)`**
  FreeType FT_Outline_EmboldenXY(strength, strength): every edge moves outwards by
  strength / 2, the glyph grows up / right by strength  [ol_embolden]
- **`fn emit(&self, path: &mut Path, gp: &Gp, zones: Option<&Zones>)`**
  append every contour to the path (gp transform, composite offset dx / dy honoured;
  zones: FS_SHARP vertical fitting)  [ol_emit]

- **`fn cubic(path: &mut Path, p: [f32; 8])`**
  flatten the cubic {p0, c1, c2, p3} (device px; p0 is the current point) into the path,
  the subdivision of path_cubic (tolerance 0.2 px)  [ol_cubic]

### `text/record.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/record.rs`](../lib/text/record.rs)

```text
record -- glyphs placed now and blended later from the glyph cache, by any thread (the row
bands of ui's render_par.rs)

  GlyphRec::default() / rec.begin(&text)   an empty record, bound to the cache as it is now
  text.record_n(&mut rec, dc, sf, x, y, s, len) -> placed   draw_n's glyphs appended to rec
       instead of blended (dc and sf as draw_n would get them; dc's colour is recorded with
       every glyph): layout, shaping, fallback fonts and rasterizing the masks into the cache
       happen now.  false: a glyph cannot come from the cache (too large: a filled path; a
       colour bitmap above the cache's limit) -- that text must be drawn with draw_n
  text.record_icon(&mut rec, dc, sf, cp, x, y, size_fx) -> placed   the same for icon_draw
  rec.len()                          glyphs so far (a text's range: len before .. after)
  rec.valid(&text)                   the cache was not flushed since begin (the keys hold)
  text.glyphs() -> GlyphView         the cache read-only, Send + Sync
  view.draw(&rec, from, to, dc, sf)  blend glyphs from .. to in their colours inside dc's
                                     clip (dc.row0 honoured): the bytes draw_n gives there

A glyph is its cache key, pen x and baseline (absolute target pixels), its box (cheap
culling against the clip), the colour and how it is blended (mask, colour bitmap, subpixel
mask with a copy of the colour's coverage adjustment).  Masks depend only on the key, so
blending them later, clipped, gives the pixels of drawing them now.
```

- **`struct GlyphRec`**
  glyphs placed by record_n / record_icon, blended later by GlyphView::draw

**`impl GlyphRec`**

- **`fn begin(&mut self, t: &Text)`**
  empty, bound to the glyph cache as it is now
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
  glyphs recorded so far
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn valid(&self, t: &Text) -> bool`**
  the glyph cache was not flushed since begin: every recorded key is still there

**`impl Text`**

- **`fn record_n(&mut self, rec: &mut GlyphRec, dc: &mut Dc, sf: &mut Surface, x: i32, y: i32, s: &[u8], len: usize) -> bool`**
  draw_n's glyphs appended to rec instead of blended (record.rs); false: one of them
  cannot be blended from the cache, draw that text with draw_n
- **`fn record_icon(&mut self, rec: &mut GlyphRec, dc: &mut Dc, sf: &mut Surface, cp: u32, x: i32, y: i32, size_fx: i32) -> bool`**
  icon_draw's glyph appended to rec (record_n)
- **`fn glyphs(&self) -> GlyphView<'_>`**
  the glyph cache read-only, for blending recorded glyphs on other threads

- **`struct GlyphView<'a>`**
  the glyph cache read-only (Text::glyphs): blends recorded glyphs, from any thread

**`impl GlyphView<'_>`**

- **`fn draw(&self, rec: &GlyphRec, from: usize, to: usize, dc: &mut Dc, sf: &mut Surface)`**
  blend the glyphs from .. to of rec in their colours inside dc's clip (rec.valid must
  hold: a missing mask is skipped)

Source: [`lib/text/rendering.rs`](../lib/text/rendering.rs)

```text
Per-face raster policy. Layout advances, document fonts and legacy renderers
keep their original contracts; styles opt in only for their own UI faces.
```

- **`enum FontRaster`**
  Glyph rasterization independent of font metrics and text editing coordinates.
  - `Legacy` -- Original x-height fitting and downward quarter-pixel positioning.
  - `Natural` -- Preserve the outline scale and round to the nearest quarter pixel.

**`impl Text`**

- **`fn font_raster(&self, font: u32) -> FontRaster`**
  Raster policy of a registered face. Unknown ids follow the fallback face.
- **`fn set_font_raster(&mut self, font: u32, raster: FontRaster) -> bool`**
  Change only this face's rasterization; invalidate cached masks on change.
  Returns false for an unregistered id. Measuring and caret advances are unchanged.

### `text/registry.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/registry.rs`](../lib/text/registry.rs)

```text
registry -- the font registry: embedded SGF1 fonts, runtime fonts (ttf.rs) and the derived
fonts of font_style (synthetic bold / italic / sharp)       [src/text/font.s, outline.s]

  register(data) -> id / -1            add an SGF1 font
  load_mem(data, face) / load_file(path, face) -> id / ERR_*   runtime fonts (ttf.rs)
  style(font, flags) -> id / ERR_*     derived font with FS_SYN_BOLD (outline dilated by
       upem/30, advance + upem/30), FS_SYN_ITALIC (x += y * tan 12 deg) and/or FS_SHARP
       (vertical grid fitting); flags 0 = font itself; the same (font, flags) pair always
       gives the same id
  unload(id) -> 0 / -1                 a runtime font and every font derived from it; the
       glyph cache is flushed; the id may be reused later
  count(), valid(id), hdr(font) (font_data), glyph(font, cp), has, adv, kern, kern_table,
  upem, metrics, metric, is_color, name, layers, glyph_box, glyph_path
Variable fonts (var.rs):
  var_axes(font) / var_instances(font)   fvar's axes and named instances (empty: not variable)
  var_values(font) -> user values per axis (an instance's, else the defaults)
  vary(font, &[(tag, value)]) -> id / ERR_*   an instance (VarFont: the base font at
       normalized coordinates; own id, serial and metrics, so glyph cache entries, outline
       buffer and shaping engines never mix instances); axes not named keep font's values;
       all-default coordinates give the variable font itself; the same coordinates the same
       id; synthetic styles of font carry over; unload(base) unloads its instances
  vary_named(font, i) -> id / ERR_*    named instance i

Font ids 0..3 are the embedded fonts (never reused).  An unknown or unloaded id behaves
like font 0.
```

```rust
FONT_EMBEDDED: u32 = 4  // ids below this are the embedded fonts (never unloaded)
FONT_MAX_IDS: u32 = 4096  // registry capacity
```

- **`struct SynFont`**
  a font derived by font_style (TFK_SYN context)
  - `hdr: Hdr`
  - `fm: Metrics`
  - `base: u32`
  - `syn: u32`
  - `strength: f32` -- embolden strength in font units
  - `serial: u64`

**`impl Text`**

- **`fn register(&mut self, data: &'static [u8]) -> i32`**
  font_register(data) -> id / -1
- **`fn set_embedded(&mut self, fonts: [&'static [u8]; 4], names: [[&'static str; 5]; 4])`**
  replace the embedded fonts 0..3 (SGF1 or TrueType / OpenType; a style switched at run
  time): the ids keep their meaning, fonts derived from them (style) take the new
  metrics, cached glyphs are dropped; each face starts with the legacy raster policy
- **`fn face_count(data: &[u8]) -> i32`**
  font_face_count(data) -> faces (1 for a plain sfnt, n for a TTC / OTC) / ERR_\*
- **`fn load_mem(&mut self, data: &[u8], face: u32) -> i32`**
  font_load_mem(data, face) -> id / ERR_\* (the data is copied)
- **`fn load_file(&mut self, path: &str, face: u32) -> i32`**
  font_load_file(path, face) -> id / ERR_\* (ERR_IO when it cannot be read)
- **`fn unload(&mut self, id: u32) -> i32`**
  font_unload(id) -> 0 / -1
- **`fn count(&self) -> u32`**
  font_count() -> ids in use are below this value
- **`fn valid(&self, id: u32) -> bool`**
  font_valid(id): the id names a registered font
- **`fn hdr(&self, font: u32) -> Hdr`**
  font_data: the SGF1-compatible header (an unknown id gives font 0)
- **`fn upem(&self, font: u32) -> i32`**
- **`fn glyph(&self, font: u32, cp: u32) -> u32`**
  font_glyph(font, cp) -> glyph (SGF1: fallback glyph, runtime: 0 = .notdef)
- **`fn has(&self, font: u32, cp: u32) -> bool`**
  font_has(font, cp)
- **`fn adv(&self, font: u32, g: u32) -> i32`**
  font_adv(font, glyph): advance in font units (synthetic bold included)
- **`fn kern(&self, font: u32, g1: u32, g2: u32) -> i32`**
  font_kern(font, g1, g2): kerning in font units (signed)
- **`fn kern_table(&self, font: u32, g1: u32, g2: u32) -> i32`**
  font_kern_table: the 'kern' table only (runtime fonts; others: font_kern)
- **`fn is_color(&self, font: u32) -> bool`**
  font_is_color: COLR layers or CBDT bitmaps
- **`fn layers(&self, font: u32, g: u32, cap: usize, out: &mut Vec<(u32, u32)>)`**
  font_layers(font, glyph, cap) into out: {glyph | LAYER_FG, argb}; empty = draw it
  normally
- **`fn name(&self, font: u32, which: u32) -> &[u8]`**
  font_name(font, FN_\*) -> UTF-8 ("" when unknown)
- **`fn metrics(&self, font: u32) -> Option<Metrics>`**
  font_metrics(font) -> FONTMETRICS (None when no font exists)
- **`fn metric(&self, font: u32, field: u32) -> i32`**
  font_metric(font, FM_\*) -> one FONTMETRICS field
- **`fn glyph_box(&mut self, font: u32, g: u32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  glyph_box(font, glyph) -> {xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax} (font units, control box); None =
  empty.  Runtime fonts leave the glyph's outline in the outline buffer.
- **`fn glyph_path(&mut self, font: u32, g: u32)`**
  glyph_path(font, glyph): append the outline to the path, transformed by gp (origin
  x / y in float pixels, sx / sy float pixels per unit)
- **`fn var_axes(&self, font: u32) -> Vec<VarAxis>`**
  the variation axes of a font (fvar; empty: not a variable font); instances and the
  fonts derived from them report their variable font's
- **`fn var_instances(&self, font: u32) -> Vec<VarInstance>`**
  the named instances of a variable font (fvar; empty: none or not variable)
- **`fn var_values(&self, font: u32) -> Vec<f32>`**
  the axis values of a font in user units, one per axis of var_axes (an instance's own,
  else the defaults)
- **`fn var_coords(&self, font: u32) -> Vec<i16>`**
  the normalized coordinates of an instance: F2Dot14 bits per axis with avar applied
  (what HarfBuzz's hb_font_get_var_coords_normalized reports); empty for a variable font
  itself (its default instance) and for fonts that are not variable
- **`fn vary(&mut self, font: u32, values: &[([u8; 4], f32)]) -> i32`**
  an instance of a variable font with axis values in user units (tag, value): axes not
  named keep font's values (an instance's, else the defaults); values are clamped to their
  axis, unknown tags ignored -> font id / ERR_\*.  All-default coordinates give the variable
  font itself, the same coordinates the same id; synthetic styles of font (style) carry
  over; a font that is not variable gives itself.  Each instance has its own glyph cache
  entries and metrics (MVAR); unloading the variable font unloads its instances.
- **`fn vary_named(&mut self, font: u32, i: usize) -> i32`**
  named instance i of a variable font (var_instances) -> id / ERR_\* (ERR_FAIL: no such
  instance)
- **`fn style(&mut self, font: u32, flags: u32) -> i32`**
  font_style(font, FS_\*) -> id / ERR_\*

### `text/segment.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/segment.rs`](../lib/text/segment.rs)

```text
segment -- Unicode text segmentation: grapheme clusters and words (UAX #29), line break
opportunities (UAX #14), Unicode 15.0 (segment_data.rs, tools/gen_segment.py)

  grapheme_next(s, i) -> index     the end of the grapheme cluster that starts at or holds i
  grapheme_prev(s, i) -> index     the start of the cluster before i (0 at the start)
  cluster_end(s, i) -> index       the end of the cluster that starts at boundary i (walks
                                   over a text cluster by cluster)
  is_grapheme_boundary(s, i)
  graphemes(s) -> Vec<usize>       every cluster boundary, 0 and s.len() included
  pictographic_cluster(s, a, b)    the cluster a..b is an emoji sequence (Backspace deletes it
                                   whole; other clusters lose their last code point)
  word_bounds(s) -> Vec<usize>     every word boundary, 0 and s.len() included
  word_at(s, i) -> (start, end)    the word segment that holds i (at s.len(): the last one)
  word_kind(s, a, b) -> WK_*       WK_WORD (a letter or number in it), WK_SPACE (only white
                                   space), WK_PUNCT
  word_next(s, i) / word_prev(s, i)   Ctrl+Right / Ctrl+Left: the start of the next word
                                   after i (spaces skipped) / of the word before i
  line_breaks(s) -> Vec<(usize, bool)>   break opportunities (index where a line may start,
                                   mandatory), s.len() last (mandatory)
  wrap_end(s, pos, pe, fits) -> end   where a line from pos ends inside pos..pe: the last
                                   opportunity whose text (without trailing spaces) fits,
                                   else graphemes while they fit (at least one); a mandatory
                                   break inside ends it
  wrap_end_hyph(s, pos, pe, fits, hyph) -> (end, hyphen)   the same with hyphenation: a line
                                   may end after a soft hyphen (U+00AD) or, with a hook
                                   (hyph(word, &mut offsets): where a word may break, e.g.
                                   spell::Hyphenator::hyphenate), inside the word that does
                                   not fit; hyphen: draw a hyphen after the line.
                                   fits(a, b, hyphen): a..b (and a hyphen) fits
  char_props(c) -> u32             the packed properties (tests, other tables)

Indices are byte offsets into UTF-8 text; an index inside a character is moved to that
character's start.  Rules: UAX #29 GB3..GB13 and WB3..WB16 of Unicode 15.0 (no GB9c: that came
with 15.1); UAX #14 LB2..LB31 with the pair rules of LB25 (numbers), LB30 for East Asian
parentheses and LB30b for emoji modifiers.  Grapheme and word scans around i start at the
nearest place before i where no rule joins or looks across (usually right there; at the
latest the paragraph start, the last '\n' before i) and words end at the next such place,
so the cost does not grow with the length of a line.
```

```rust
/// word_kind: a word (a letter or number in it)
WK_WORD: u32 = 0
/// word_kind: white space only
WK_SPACE: u32 = 1
/// word_kind: anything else (punctuation, symbols)
WK_PUNCT: u32 = 2
```

- **`fn char_props(c: char) -> u32`**
  the packed properties of a character (see segment_data.rs)

- **`fn grapheme_next(s: &str, i: usize) -> usize`**
  the end of the grapheme cluster that starts at or holds i (s.len() at the end)

- **`fn cluster_end(s: &str, i: usize) -> usize`**
  the end of the grapheme cluster that starts at i, a cluster boundary (grapheme_next without
  looking back: walks from boundary to boundary)

- **`fn grapheme_prev(s: &str, i: usize) -> usize`**
  the start of the grapheme cluster before i (0 at the start)

- **`fn is_grapheme_boundary(s: &str, i: usize) -> bool`**
  i is a cluster boundary

- **`fn graphemes(s: &str) -> Vec<usize>`**
  every cluster boundary of s (0 and s.len() included)

- **`fn pictographic_cluster(s: &str, a: usize, b: usize) -> bool`**
  the cluster a..b is an emoji sequence (pictographs, flags, keycaps, ZWJ sequences)

- **`fn word_bounds(s: &str) -> Vec<usize>`**
  every word boundary of s (0 and s.len() included)

- **`fn word_kind(s: &str, a: usize, b: usize) -> u32`**
  the kind of the segment a..b (WK_WORD, WK_SPACE, WK_PUNCT)

- **`fn word_at(s: &str, i: usize) -> (usize, usize)`**
  the word segment that holds i (at the end of the text: the last one)

- **`fn word_next(s: &str, i: usize) -> usize`**
  Ctrl+Right: the start of the next word after i (the rest of this word and the spaces after
  it skipped)

- **`fn word_prev(s: &str, i: usize) -> usize`**
  Ctrl+Left: the start of the word before i (spaces before i skipped)

- **`fn line_breaks(s: &str) -> Vec<(usize, bool)>`**
  the break opportunities of s: (index where a line may start, mandatory); the end of the
  text is the last entry (mandatory)

- **`fn wrap_end(s: &str, pos: usize, pe: usize, fits: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize) -> bool) -> usize`**
  where a line starting at pos ends inside pos..pe (pos &lt; end &lt;= pe; pe when pos == pe): the
  whole rest when it fits, else the last break opportunity whose text before it (without
  trailing spaces) fits, else grapheme clusters while they fit (at least one); a mandatory
  break inside ends the line there.  fits(a, b): the text a..b fits.

- **`fn wrap_end_hyph( s: &str, pos: usize, pe: usize, fits: &mut dyn FnMut(usize, usize, bool) -> bool, mut hyph: Option<&mut dyn FnMut(&str, &mut Vec<usize>)>, ) -> (usize, bool)`**
  wrap_end with hyphenation: where a line starting at pos ends inside pos..pe, and whether
  it ends with a hyphen (to be drawn after its text).  As wrap_end, and: an opportunity
  after a soft hyphen (U+00AD) counts with the hyphen's width; when the next word does not
  fit, hyph(word, &mut offsets) gives the places where that whole word (UAX #29) may break
  (byte offsets inside it, ascending) and the line ends at the last one that fits with a
  hyphen -- also inside a single word too long for a line, before graphemes are cut.  Words
  with a digit or a soft hyphen of their own are never hyphenated.  fits(a, b, hyphen):
  the text a..b fits (with a hyphen after it).

- **`fn unicode_version() -> &'static str`**
  the Unicode version of the tables

### `text/ttf.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/ttf.rs`](../lib/text/ttf.rs)

```text
ttf -- sfnt loader for runtime fonts: TrueType (glyf), OpenType (CFF outlines via cff.rs),
collections (TTC / OTC), colour tables (colr.rs)                      [src/text/ttf.s]

  face_count(data) -> faces (1 for a plain sfnt, n for a TTC / OTC) / ERR_*
  TtFont::open(data, face, ol, serial) -> the font context / ERR_*
  glyph(cp), has(cp), adv(g), kern(g1, g2), kern_table(g1, g2), name(which)
  bbox(g, ol), path(g, ol, path, gp)       the outline through the outline buffer
  sfnt_name(table, id) -> UTF-8            best record: Windows Unicode German (0x0407),
       German variants, English (0x0409), other Windows languages, Unicode platform,
       Mac Roman English

Errors: ERR_TRUNC (too short / truncated directory), ERR_HDR (not an sfnt, bad head /
maxp), ERR_UNSUPPORTED (no usable outlines: e.g. CFF2 only), ERR_FAIL (face index out of
range), ERR_LIMIT (file >= 2 GB).

Tables: head, hhea, hmtx, maxp, loca, glyf (simple + composite: offsets, scale, x/y scale,
2x2, point matching, SCALED_COMPONENT_OFFSET; nesting <= 16, <= 4096 components per
glyph), cmap (formats 0, 4, 6, 12, 13; (3,10) > (0,x) fmt 12 > (3,1) > (0,x) > (3,0)
symbol > (1,0) Mac Roman), OS/2, post, name, kern (version 0 and Apple version 1, format
0), GPOS pair adjustment (lookup type 2 formats 1 and 2, extension type 9; x advance of
the first glyph; 'kern' feature of the DFLT and latn default language systems).  Every
offset is checked against its table and the file; malformed glyphs come out empty.  Like
GDI / FreeType: glyf outlines are shifted by hmtx lsb - xMin; symbol fonts ((3,0) cmap)
also map U+0000..U+00FF and the Windows-1252 characters to U+F000 + code page byte; a CFF
FontMatrix that is not exactly 1/unitsPerEm scales the outline.

Variable fonts (var.rs): fvar / avar / gvar / HVAR / MVAR / GDEF's store are read at open
(var); the plain calls give the default instance, the *_var calls an instance at
normalized coordinates (registry.rs: VarFont):
  prep_var(g, coords, serial, ol)    the outline with gvar deltas (simple glyphs: points with
       IUP; composites: the component offsets), shifted by its varied phantom point pp1
  adv_var(g, coords)                 hmtx + HVAR; without HVAR: hmtx + the phantom points'
       deltas (adv_table: every glyph at once)
  kern_var(g1, g2, coords)           GPOS pair values + their VariationIndex deltas (GDEF)
  metrics_var(coords, wght, ol)      FONTMETRICS + header with MVAR deltas (hasc / hdsc /
       hlgp on hhea and OS/2, hcla, hcld, xhgt, cpht, undo, unds, stro, strs)
CFF2 outlines are not supported (no usable outlines: ERR_UNSUPPORTED).
```

```rust
ERR_FAIL: i32 = -1
ERR_TRUNC: i32 = -1
ERR_HDR: i32 = -2
ERR_NOMEM: i32 = -8
ERR_UNSUPPORTED: i32 = -9
ERR_IO: i32 = -13
ERR_LIMIT: i32 = -15
FILE_MAX: u64 = 0x7FFF_FFF0
NAME_CAP: usize = 256
// table indices (TT_*)
TT_HEAD: usize = 0
TT_HHEA: usize = 1
TT_HMTX: usize = 2
TT_MAXP: usize = 3
TT_LOCA: usize = 4
TT_GLYF: usize = 5
TT_CMAP: usize = 6
TT_OS2: usize = 7
TT_POST: usize = 8
TT_NAME: usize = 9
TT_KERN: usize = 10
TT_GPOS: usize = 11
TT_CFF: usize = 12
TT_COLR: usize = 13
TT_CPAL: usize = 14
TT_CBDT: usize = 15
TT_CBLC: usize = 16
TT_FVAR: usize = 17
TT_AVAR: usize = 20
TT_GVAR: usize = 21
TT_HVAR: usize = 22
```

### `text/var.rs`

Source: [`lib/text/var.rs`](../lib/text/var.rs)

```text
var -- OpenType font variations: fvar (axes, named instances), avar (segment maps), gvar
(TrueType point deltas), HVAR (advance deltas), MVAR (font-wide metrics) and the item
variation store HVAR, MVAR and GDEF share

  VarAxis { tag, min, def, max, hidden, name }, VarInstance { name, coords }   what fvar
       says, in user units; names from the name table (an axis without one: its tag)
  Var::parse(tables) -> Option<Var>  a font's fvar, avar, gvar, HVAR, MVAR, GDEF store
  normalize(user) -> coords          F2Dot14 per axis: clamped to the axis, -1 .. 0 .. 1
       around the default in 16.16, avar in 16.16, then 2.14 (rounded like HarfBuzz and
       FreeType: floor(x + 0.5))
  gvar_deltas(gvar, glyph, coords, orig, ends, out, budget)   the deltas of a glyph's points
       and of its 4 phantom points, added to out: embedded and shared peak tuples,
       intermediate regions, shared and private packed point numbers, packed deltas (zero
       runs, bytes, words, longs), IUP for the outline points a tuple leaves out
  hvar_delta(hvar, glyph, coords)    the advance delta (HVAR, with or without its mapping)
  mvar_delta(mvar, tag, coords)      a font-wide metric's delta (MVAR)
  gdef_delta(gdef, outer, inner, coords)   a GPOS VariationIndex delta (GDEF's store)

Every offset is checked against its table (gvar data against the glyph's own range).
Broken gvar data of a glyph: false (the glyph comes out empty, like broken glyf data);
broken HVAR / MVAR / store data: no delta.  Bounded work: a glyph whose tuples x points
exceed VAR_BUDGET counts as broken; a store row whose regions x axes exceed IVS_WORK has
no delta.  Not supported: avar version 2 beyond its segment maps, CFF2 outlines (such
fonts do not load), VVAR (no vertical layout).
```

```rust
/// axes and named instances read at most
AXES_MAX: usize = 64
INSTANCES_MAX: usize = 1024
```

## spell

*spell checking: Hunspell dictionaries, the system's checker, a personal word list* -- crate root [`lib/spell/lib.rs`](../lib/spell/lib.rs)

```text
spell -- spell checking: Hunspell dictionaries read by the library itself, the system's
checker (Windows ISpellChecker), a personal word list

  Dictionary::from_bytes(aff, dic) / load(aff_path, dic_path)   a Hunspell dictionary
       (.aff + .dic, any SET encoding of aff.rs); add_dic(bytes) a further word list;
       check(word), suggest(word), add_word(word); wordchars(), language(), words(),
       unsupported() (the .aff keywords it ignored)
  find(lang, SRC_*) -> Source        where the checker for a language tag lives
  languages(SRC_*) -> tags           the languages there are checkers for
  Speller::open(lang, SRC_*) / from_source(&source) / with_dictionary(dict, lang)
       the checker the UI uses: check(word), check_token(text, &token), cached(word),
       suggest(word), add(word) / remove(word) (the personal word list, kept in a file:
       set_personal_file), ignore(word) (this session), misspelled(text) -> byte ranges,
       language(), backend(), revision() (changes when the word lists change);
       suggester() -> Suggester: suggest(word, max) on another thread (Hunspell only)
  tokens(text, wordchars) -> Token   the words of a text worth checking (token.rs)
  personal_path(lang)                "config://spell/<language>.dic"
  Hyphenator::from_dic(bytes) / from_tex(text) / load(path), hyphenate(word)   hyphenation
       (Liang's patterns: libhyphen's hyph_xx_YY.dic, TeX's \patterns; hyphen.rs);
       find_hyphen(lang, SRC_*) / hyphen_languages(SRC_*): the dictionaries of the sources

Sources (SRC_*), tried in this order for every language:
  SRC_SYSTEM  Windows: ISpellChecker (plat::spell) for the language, then the Hunspell
              folders of DICPATH; Linux: DICPATH, $XDG_DATA_HOME/hunspell
              (~/.local/share/hunspell), and hunspell, myspell, myspell/dicts below every
              XDG_DATA_DIRS folder (/usr/local/share, /usr/share); Web / Android: none
  SRC_USER    config://hunspell -- dictionaries the user put there
  SRC_APP     app://hunspell -- dictionaries the app ships (apps/NAME/assets/hunspell)
A dictionary file NAME.aff (with NAME.dic beside it) serves a tag when NAME, read without
case and with '-' as '_', is the tag ("de_DE"), a variant of it ("de_DE_frami"), the bare
language ("de"), or the language in another region ("de_AT"; the main region first:
"de_DE", "en_US").  Headless runs and tests use SRC_APP only, so their results never
depend on the machine.

What the Hunspell reader supports and ignores: aff.rs (format), check.rs (affix and compound
rules), suggest.rs (suggestions).  The checks follow Hunspell 1.7 (compared on de_DE_frami,
en_US, en_GB: docs/ROADMAP.md 4), with one difference on purpose: an UPPER word with a break
point ("CD-ROM", "E-MAIL-ADRESSE") is correct when its pieces are (Hunspell splits the Title
case form it made and rejects "Cd-rom").  Not supported: COMPOUNDSYLLABLE, COMPOUNDROOT,
COMPOUNDMORESUFFIXES, COMPLEXPREFIXES (two prefixes), a prefix together with two suffixes,
morphology (AM, the fields of the .dic), PHONE suggestions, OCONV, the replacements of
CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN (simplified compounds), the Turkish / Azeri casing of LANG; no clock
limits (Hunspell's results depend on the machine's speed, these never do).

Personal word list: one word per line (a first line with a number is skipped), UTF-8.  A
word added in lower case is also accepted Capitalised and in UPPER case; "Paris" only so.
Words ignored for the session work the same way and are never written.  The system's
checker never learns them (Windows' own word list stays untouched).
```

### `spell/hyphen.rs`

Source: [`lib/spell/hyphen.rs`](../lib/spell/hyphen.rs)

```text
hyphen -- hyphenation: Liang's algorithm on TeX patterns and on the dictionaries of
libhyphen (LibreOffice / OpenOffice "hyph_xx_YY.dic")

  Hyphenator::from_dic(bytes) -> Option   a libhyphen dictionary: the character set on the
       first line (UTF-8, ISO8859-1 .. -16, KOI8-R / -U, microsoft-cp1251 ...: aff.rs),
       LEFTHYPHENMIN / RIGHTHYPHENMIN / COMPOUNDLEFTHYPHENMIN / COMPOUNDRIGHTHYPHENMIN n,
       NOHYPHEN a,b,... (no break next to these), NEXTLEVEL (the patterns before it find
       the parts of a compound word, the ones after it hyphenate each part), one pattern per
       line, '%' / '#' comments
  Hyphenator::from_tex(text) -> Option    the \patterns{...} and \hyphenation{...} blocks of
       a TeX pattern file (hyph-utf8's hyph-*.tex; UTF-8, '%' comments)
  load(path) -> Option                    a .dic file, or .tex (by its \patterns)
  add_patterns(text)                      more patterns, whitespace-separated ("hy3ph")
  add_exceptions(text)                    words with every break shown ("ta-ble"): exact
                                          results for these words
  set_min(left, right)                    characters a break leaves at least on the left /
                                          right of the word (default and minimum: the
                                          dictionary's values, else 2 and 2)
  hyphenate(word) -> Vec<usize>           where word may break (byte offsets of the first
                                          character after each break, ascending)
  hyphenated(word, sep) -> String         word with sep at every break (tests, tools)
  find_hyphen(lang, SRC_*) -> Option<(path, tag)>, hyphen_languages(SRC_*)
                                          the dictionaries of a source (see below)

Liang: every pattern is letters with a digit (0..9) between them; for each place between
two letters of ".word." the largest digit of the matching patterns wins and odd allows a
break.  The word is lower-cased first (character by character) and digits in it count
as word boundaries ('.').  TeX patterns: every matching pattern counts.  .dic files are
made for libhyphen and read as it reads them: its automaton applies at each character only
the pattern that is its state there (the longest suffix of the text read so far that begins
some pattern; de_DE's first level is a list of words that relies on it), and it works in two
levels: the first level's odd places split a word into parts, every part goes through the
first level again (it may show parts the whole word hid), a part without parts is hyphenated
by the second level with COMPOUNDLEFT / RIGHTHYPHENMIN at its inner ends; never a break
after the last character.  A dictionary without NEXTLEVEL gets libhyphen's default first
level (parts at '-', '\'', U+2013, U+2019, which NOHYPHEN keeps from breaking themselves).
Then no break leaves fewer than LEFTHYPHENMIN / RIGHTHYPHENMIN characters at the ends, and
NOHYPHEN removes the breaks next to its strings.  The results equal libhyphen 2.8's on the 21
dictionaries of the freedesktop SDK (spelltest --hyphenate; 214,000 words, 0 differences).
Not supported: libhyphen's non-standard hyphenation ("c1k/k=k,1,1": Zucker -> Zuk-ker,
mainly hu_HU) -- such a pattern keeps the places around its replaced letters from breaking
(odd digits there count one more), so no break ever needs a changed spelling.

Sources (spell::SRC_*), like the Hunspell dictionaries (speller.rs): SRC_SYSTEM: DICPATH,
on Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/hyphen and hyphen, hunspell, myspell, myspell/dicts below every
XDG_DATA_DIRS folder (/usr/share/hyphen: Debian's hyphen-* packages), on Windows also the
dictionary extensions of LibreOffice (%ProgramFiles%\LibreOffice\share\extensions\dict-*);
SRC_USER: config://hyphen; SRC_APP: app://hyphen.  A file hyph_<tag>.dic serves a language
tag like a Hunspell file NAME.aff: the tag ("de_DE"), the bare language, another region.
```

- **`struct Hyphenator`**
  hyphenation patterns of one language (see the module header)

**`impl Hyphenator`**

- **`fn new() -> Hyphenator`**
  no patterns (no breaks) and libhyphen's default first level
- **`fn from_dic(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Hyphenator>`**
  a libhyphen dictionary (hyph_xx_YY.dic); None when it has no pattern
- **`fn from_tex(text: &str) -> Option<Hyphenator>`**
  the \\patterns{...} and \\hyphenation{...} of a TeX file; None when it has no pattern
- **`fn load(path: &str) -> Option<Hyphenator>`**
  a .dic file (or a TeX file: .tex)
- **`fn add_patterns(&mut self, text: &str)`**
  more patterns (whitespace-separated, "hy3ph"), added to the hyphenating level
- **`fn add_exceptions(&mut self, text: &str)`**
  exceptions: words with every break as '-' ("ta-ble", "project"); they replace the
  patterns for exactly these words (any case)
- **`fn set_min(&mut self, left: usize, right: usize)`**
  characters a break leaves at least at the start / end of a word (the dictionary's
  LEFTHYPHENMIN / RIGHTHYPHENMIN stay the minimum)
- **`fn min(&self) -> (usize, usize)`**
  (LEFTHYPHENMIN, RIGHTHYPHENMIN) in effect
- **`fn patterns(&self) -> (usize, usize)`**
  the patterns of both levels (tests, tools)
- **`fn hyphenate(&self, word: &str) -> Vec<usize>`**
  where word may break: the byte offset of the first character after each break
- **`fn hyphenated(&self, word: &str, sep: &str) -> String`**
  word with sep at every break ("hy-phen-ation")

- **`fn find_hyphen(lang: &str, sources: u32) -> Option<(String, String)>`**
  the hyphenation dictionary for a language tag: (path, the tag it serves); sources in the
  order SRC_SYSTEM, SRC_USER, SRC_APP (as spell::find)

- **`fn hyphen_languages(sources: u32) -> Vec<String>`**
  the language tags there are hyphenation dictionaries for (sorted, each once)

**`impl Speller`**

- **`fn with_dictionary(mut dict: Dictionary, lang: &str) -> Speller`**
  a checker for a Hunspell dictionary
- **`fn from_source(s: &Source) -> Option<Speller>`**
  the checker of a source (Hunspell files are read now)
- **`fn open(lang: &str, sources: u32) -> Option<Speller>`**
  the checker for a language tag (find + from_source)
- **`fn language(&self) -> &str`**
  the language tag ("de-DE")
- **`fn backend(&self) -> &'static str`**
  "hunspell" or "system"
- **`fn dictionary(&self) -> Option<&Dictionary>`**
  the Hunspell dictionary (None for the system's checker)
- **`fn wordchars(&self) -> &[char]`**
  WORDCHARS of the dictionary (for tokens())
- **`fn revision(&self) -> u32`**
  changes whenever the personal or the ignored words change (caches of results depend on it)
- **`fn cached(&self, word: &str) -> Option<bool>`**
  the cached result for a word (None: not checked yet)
- **`fn check(&mut self, word: &str) -> bool`**
  the word is correct (personal and ignored words, then the checker; cached)
- **`fn check_token(&mut self, text: &str, t: &Token) -> bool`**
  a token of `text` is correct: the word, or the word with the dot that follows it
  (an abbreviation)
- **`fn token_errors(&mut self, text: &str, t: &Token) -> Vec<(usize, usize)>`**
  the misspelled byte ranges of one token: none when it is correct.  A hyphenated word
  marks only its wrong parts: from each part on the longest run of parts that is a word
  counts as right ("E-Mail" of "E-Mail-Adr"), wrong parts next to each other are one
  range ("E-Mial"); "Hasu-Tür" marks "Hasu"; right parts make a right word (a personal
  word inside)
- **`fn misspelled(&mut self, text: &str) -> Vec<(usize, usize)>`**
  the byte ranges of the misspelled words of a text
- **`fn suggest(&mut self, word: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String>`**
  corrections, best first (at most max)
- **`fn suggester(&self) -> Option<Suggester>`**
  suggest() for another thread: the Hunspell dictionary and the personal list as they are
  now (None for the system's checker, which stays on its thread)
- **`fn add(&mut self, word: &str) -> bool`**
  add a word to the personal list (written to the file of set_personal_file) -> the file
  was written (or there is none)
- **`fn remove(&mut self, word: &str) -> bool`**
  take a word off the personal list -> the file was written (or there is none)
- **`fn ignore(&mut self, word: &str)`**
  accept the word for this session (not written anywhere)
- **`fn personal(&self) -> Vec<String>`**
  the personal list
- **`fn ignored(&self) -> Vec<String>`**
  the words ignored this session
- **`fn set_personal_file(&mut self, path: Option<&str>)`**
  keep the personal list in a file (read now; None: in memory only)

  a Speller's suggestions for a worker thread (Speller::suggester): the same results as
  Speller::suggest at the time it was made

**`impl Suggester`**

- **`fn suggest(&self, word: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String>`**
  corrections, best first (at most max)

### `spell/token.rs`

Source: [`lib/spell/token.rs`](../lib/spell/token.rs)

```text
token -- the words of a text that are worth checking

A word is a run of letters (alphabetic characters and combining marks, plus the
dictionary's WORDCHARS); apostrophes and hyphens join letters ("don't", "E-Mail"), dots only
when WORDCHARS has them ("z.B").  Skipped: words with a digit ("3D", "MP3", "1st"), and every
blank-separated chunk that looks like a URL, an e-mail address or a path (contains "://",
'@' or '\\', starts with "www.", '/' or "~/", or a drive "C:").  A token records whether a
'.' follows it, so an abbreviation ("usw.") can be checked with its dot.
```

- **`struct Token`**
  a word of a text: its byte range, and whether a '.' follows it
  - `start: usize`
  - `end: usize`
  - `dot: bool`

- **`fn tokens(text: &str, wordchars: &[char]) -> Vec<Token>`**
  the words of `text` to check (see the module header); `wordchars`: the dictionary's
  WORDCHARS

## img_core

*image I/O dispatch, records, metadata, colour, resampling, image operations* -- crate root [`lib/img_core/lib.rs`](../lib/img_core/lib.rs)

```text
img_core -- the shared part of the image codecs: records of img.inc (decode options,
metadata, encode options, codec descriptor, format table), error codes, and the modules
every codec builds on                                              [ASMLIB/inc/img.inc]

  ImgDec        decode options (IMGDEC): flags IMGD_*, frame, hint, pixel budget, cancel
  ImgMeta       decoded metadata (IMGMETA); to_bytes() = the 128-byte record of the
                assembly with the blob pointers zeroed (codectest op 261 compares it),
                incl. IM_CHRM (PNG cHRM) and the DDS fields IM_DXGI / IM_TEXFL / IM_TEXN
  ImgOpt        encode options (IMGOPT); from_bytes() reads the 64-byte record
  Codec         a codec descriptor (IMGCODEC): probe / decode / encode, caps, iom; and
                for the core formats the functions the assembly calls directly: scan
                (png_meta / jpeg_meta / ...), decode_fl (png_decode_fl / ...: the classic
                decoders of img_decode and BMP's embedded PNG / JPEG), save (png_encode /
                jpeg_encode / ...: the classic encoders of img_save); Codec::EMPTY for
                struct update syntax
  FmtInfo       a format table entry (IMGFMT)

Modules (owners during the R6 wave, see rewrite/AGENTS.md):
  checksum, inflate, deflate, gzip, meta (imgmeta.s), exif, icc, io (imgio.s, imgreg.s,
  imgcore.s glue), bits (the bit readers of img_int.inc)  -- R6-core
  yuv                                                     -- R6-jpeg
  quantize                                                -- R6-bgt (bmp / gif / tga)
  resample, xform, mip, ops (imgops.s)                    -- R6-xf
  icc_xform (+ icc_eval, icc_bi: icc_xform.s, icc.inc)    -- R6-icc

Decoded images are gfx::Surface values (FMT_PARGB, or FMT_ARGB with IMGD_STRAIGHT).
```

### `img_core` crate root

Re-exports: `gfx::Surface`

- **`type ParallelFor = fn(usize, &(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync))`**
  runs f(i) for every i in 0..n, possibly on several threads (thr_parallel_for)

- **`fn set_parallel(f: ParallelFor)`**
  the loop the codecs' parallel parts run on (the asm's thr_parallel_for: ICC LUT grids, YUV
  bands); the apps pass a wrapper of plat::parallel_for -- img_core does not depend on plat.
  Without it everything runs on the calling thread (the same bytes)

- **`fn parallel() -> Option<ParallelFor>`**
  the loop set by set_parallel

- **`struct ImgDec<'a>`**
  decode options (IMGDEC); Default = premultiplied output, orientation applied, frame 0,
  no hint, IMG_MAXPX_DEF pixels, no metadata blobs, no cancel flag
  - `flags: u32` -- IMGD_\*
  - `frame: u32` -- frame / page / mip level
  - `hint: u32` -- IMGF_\* expected from the file name (0 = none)
  - `maxpx: u64` -- max w \* h (0 = IMG_MAXPX_DEF) -> ERR_LIMIT
  - `maxmem: u64` -- memory budget for codec scratch (0 = no limit)
  - `cancel: Option<&'a AtomicU32>`

**`impl ImgDec<'_>`**

  the pixel budget (maxpx, or the default)
- **`fn cancelled(&self) -> bool`**
  the cancel flag is set

- **`struct ImgMeta`**
  decoded metadata (IMGMETA)
  - `fmt: u32` -- IMGF_\*
  - `w: u32` -- stored width (before orientation)
  - `h: u32` -- stored height
  - `bits: u8` -- bits per sample of the source (1..16, 32 = float)
  - `model: u8` -- IMM_\*
  - `orient: u8` -- EXIF orientation 1..8
  - `channels: u8` -- samples per pixel incl. alpha (0 = unknown)
  - `flags: u32` -- IMF_\*
  - `frames: u32` -- frames / pages / mip levels
  - `dpix: u32` -- dots per inch 16.16 (0 = unknown)
  - `dpiy: u32`
  - `cicp: u32` -- primaries | transfer &lt;&lt; 8 | matrix &lt;&lt; 16 | full range &lt;&lt; 24
  - `gamma: u32` -- file gamma \* 100000 (PNG gAMA)
  - `icc: Vec<u8>` -- IMGD_ICC
  - `exif: Vec<u8>` -- IMGD_EXIF: TIFF structure without "Exif\\0\\0"
  - `xmp: Vec<u8>` -- IMGD_XMP
  - `delay: u32` -- ms (animations)
  - `loops: u32` -- animation loop count (0 = forever)
  - `quality: u32` -- estimated encoder quality 1..100
  - `resunit: u32` -- IMR_\*
  - `chrm: [u16; 8]` -- IM_CHRM: PNG cHRM white x, y, red x, y, green x, y, blue x, y / 50000
  - `dxgi: u16` -- IM_DXGI: DXGI_FORMAT of DDS pixel data
  - `texfl: u8` -- IM_TEXFL: TXF_\*
  - `texn: u32` -- IM_TEXN: DDS array size / cubes / depth

**`impl ImgMeta`**

- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 128]`**
  the 128-byte IMGMETA record of the assembly (blob pointers 0, lengths kept)

- **`struct ImgOpt<'a>`**
  encode options (IMGOPT); Default = the format's defaults
  - `fmt: u32` -- IMGF_\* (save: 0 = from the file extension)
  - `quality: u32` -- 1..100 (0 = format default)
  - `flags: u32` -- IOF_\*
  - `bitdepth: u32` -- bits per pixel 0 auto / 32 / 24 / 8
  - `samplebits: u32` -- bits per sample 8 / 10 / 12 (0 = 8)
  - `dither: u32` -- dithering level + 1 (0 = default 7, 1 = off .. 9 = level 8)
  - `athresh: u32` -- transparency threshold + 1 (0 = default 128)
  - `chroma: u32` -- 444 / 422 / 420 / 400 (0 = format default)
  - `effort: u32` -- 1..9 (0 = default); PNG: deflate level
  - `ddsfmt: u32` -- DDSF_\*
  - `mipfilter: u32` -- MIPF_\*
  - `tiffcomp: u32` -- TIFC_\*
  - `meta: Option<&'a ImgMeta>` -- metadata to embed
  - `cancel: Option<&'a AtomicU32>`

**`impl<'a> ImgOpt<'a>`**

- **`fn from_bytes(b: &[u8]) -> ImgOpt<'a>`**
  the scalar fields of a 64-byte IMGOPT record (IO_META / IO_CANCEL ignored)
- **`fn cancelled(&self) -> bool`**

- **`type ProbeFn = fn(&[u8], &mut ImgMeta) -> bool`**
  probe(data, meta) -> recognised (header + metadata scan, no pixels)

- **`type DecodeFn = fn(&[u8], &mut Surface, &ImgDec, &mut ImgMeta) -> i32`**
  decode(data, out, dec, meta) -> 0 / ERR_\*  (meta: the caller's ImgMeta, already
  cleared with fmt set; dec.flags tell which blobs to copy)

- **`type EncodeFn = fn(&Surface, &ImgOpt, &mut Vec<u8>) -> i32`**
  encode(surface, opt, out) -> 0 / ERR_\*  (FMT_XRGB / PARGB / ARGB / A8 input)

- **`type ScanFn = fn(&[u8], &mut ImgMeta, u32) -> i32`**
  scan(data, meta, flags) -> 0 / ERR_\*: the header / metadata scanner of a core format
  (png_meta, jpeg_meta, bmp_meta, gif_meta; flags = IMGD_\* of the blobs to copy)

- **`type DecodeFlFn = fn(&[u8], &mut Surface, u32) -> i32`**
  decode_fl(data, out, jdf) -> 0 / ERR_\*: the classic decoder (png_decode_fl, ...);
  jdf = JDF_STRAIGHT (FMT_ARGB) | JDF_NO_ORIENT, else FMT_PARGB

- **`type SaveFn = fn(&Surface, u32) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  save(surface, quality) -> file bytes or None (out of memory, unsupported surface): the
  classic encoder of img_save (png_encode, jpeg_encode(quality), bmp_encode, gif_encode)

- **`struct Codec`**
  a codec descriptor (IMGCODEC); every codec crate exports one `pub static CODEC: Codec`
  (`Codec { probe: Some(..), decode: Some(..), ..Codec::EMPTY }`)
  - `probe: Option<ProbeFn>`
  - `decode: Option<DecodeFn>`
  - `encode: Option<EncodeFn>`
  - `caps: u32` -- IFC_DECODE / IFC_ENCODE really implemented
  - `iom: u32` -- IOM_\* the encoder honours
  - `scan: Option<ScanFn>` -- core formats: metadata scanner
  - `decode_fl: Option<DecodeFlFn>` -- core formats: classic decoder (img_decode)
  - `save: Option<SaveFn>` -- core formats: classic encoder (img_save)

**`impl Codec`**

- **`const EMPTY: Codec = Codec { probe: None, decode: None, encode: None, caps: 0, ...`**

### `img_core/bits.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/bits.rs`](../lib/img_core/bits.rs)

```text
bits -- the bit readers of the codecs (MSB-first and LSB-first)  [ASMLIB/inc/img_int.inc]

  BrM (MSB first: JPEG entropy data without stuffing, HEVC, AV1 headers, JXR)
  BrL (LSB first: deflate, VP8L, JPEG XL)
  r = BrX::new(data, pos); r.refill(); r.get(n) / r.peek(n) / r.skip(n); r.overrun()

The state of the assembly macros: a 64-bit buffer, a bit count and a byte position that
keeps counting past the end of the data (zero bytes are shifted in there, nothing is
read).  After refill() at least 56 bits are available.  overrun() is BRx_OVERRUN: more
zero padding bytes consumed than bits are left.  Values of n: 1..56 (get / peek / skip).
```

- **`struct BrM<'a>`**
  MSB-first reader (BRM_\*)
  - `data: &'a [u8]`
  - `buf: u64`
  - `cnt: u32`
  - `pos: usize` -- may pass data.len()

**`impl<'a> BrM<'a>`**

- **`fn new(data: &'a [u8], pos: usize) -> Self`**
  BRM_INIT with the byte position pos
- **`fn refill(&mut self)`**
  BRM_REFILL: at least 56 bits in the buffer
- **`fn peek(&self, n: u32) -> u64`**
  BRM_PEEK: the next n bits
- **`fn skip(&mut self, n: u32)`**
  BRM_SKIP
- **`fn get(&mut self, n: u32) -> u64`**
  BRM_GET / BRM_GETV
- **`fn overrun(&self) -> bool`**
  BRM_OVERRUN: true when more padding bytes were consumed than bits are left

- **`struct BrL<'a>`**
  LSB-first reader (BRL_\*)
  - `data: &'a [u8]`
  - `buf: u64`
  - `cnt: u32`
  - `pos: usize` -- may pass data.len()

**`impl<'a> BrL<'a>`**

- **`fn new(data: &'a [u8], pos: usize) -> Self`**
  BRL_INIT with the byte position pos
- **`fn refill(&mut self)`**
  BRL_REFILL: at least 56 bits in the buffer
- **`fn peek(&self, n: u32) -> u64`**
  BRL_PEEK: the next n bits
- **`fn skip(&mut self, n: u32)`**
  BRL_SKIP
- **`fn get(&mut self, n: u32) -> u64`**
  BRL_GET / BRL_GETV
- **`fn overrun(&self) -> bool`**
  BRL_OVERRUN

### `img_core/checksum.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/checksum.rs`](../lib/img_core/checksum.rs)

```text
checksum -- CRC-32 (zlib / PNG polynomial) and Adler-32  [src/img/checksum.s]

  crc32(crc, data) -> u32        start with crc = 0 (like zlib's crc32())
  adler32(adler, data) -> u32    start with adler = 1

CRC: table driven (slice-by-8 here, slice-by-4 in the assembly: the same values).
Adler-32: blocks of at most 5552 bytes summed exactly in 64 bit, both sums reduced mod
65521 after every block (as the assembly's SSE2 loop); a call with no data returns the
start value unchanged.
```

- **`fn crc32(crc: u32, data: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  CRC-32 (zlib / PNG) of data, continuing crc (start with 0)  [crc32]

- **`fn adler32(adler: u32, data: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  Adler-32 (zlib) of data, continuing adler (start with 1)  [adler32]

### `img_core/deflate.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/deflate.rs`](../lib/img_core/deflate.rs)

```text
deflate -- DEFLATE (RFC 1951) / zlib (RFC 1950) compression  [src/img/deflate.s]

  zlib_deflate(src, level) -> Vec          zlib stream (level 0..9, < 0 = 6, > 9 = 9)
  deflate_raw(src, level) -> Vec           raw RFC 1951 data
  deflate_raw_ex(st, src, level, head, tail) -> Vec   head free bytes before the data
                                           (gzip writes its header there), tail reserved
                                           after it (not part of the Vec)
  DeflateState::new() -> Box               a reusable compressor state (~330 KB; one
                                           thread at a time); the same bytes as fresh calls
  zlib_deflate_st(st, src, level) / deflate_raw_st(st, src, level) -> Vec
  zlib_deflate_to(st, src, level, dst) / deflate_raw_to(...) -> Ok(bytes) /
                                           Err(ERR_OVERFLOW): into dst (no allocation with
                                           a state); overflow when the stream + 8 bytes do
                                           not fit (dst contents undefined then)
  deflate_bound(len) -> len + len / 512 + 128   a cap with which *_to never overflow

The algorithm and every table of the assembly: 3-byte multiplicative hash, head / prev
chains over "global" positions (input offset + base; every input starts GEN_GAP after
the previous one, so a reused state matches a fresh one), zlib's levels (greedy 1..3, lazy
4..9, chain depth / nice / lazy limits), TOO_FAR, 16K-symbol blocks written as the
cheapest of stored / fixed / dynamic by exact bit count, two-queue Huffman lengths with
miniz's Kraft repair, RLE-coded code lengths.  Inputs of 4 GiB - 64 KiB and more are
stored.  The output limit: a block that would end past cap - 8 stops the compressor
(ERR_OVERFLOW).  Speed (perf-inflate): the LZ77 loops keep their state in locals and
load the next position's hash head before the current chain walk (the walk is a chain of
dependent loads; the early load overlaps it) -- the same candidates in the same order.
```

- **`struct DeflateState`**
  a compressor state (DS_\*); reusable, one thread at a time

**`impl DeflateState`**

- **`fn new() -> Box<DeflateState>`**
  a zeroed state  [deflate_state_new]

- **`fn deflate_bound(len: usize) -> usize`**
  output capacity with which the \*\_to functions never report ERR_OVERFLOW  [deflate_bound]

- **`fn zlib_deflate_to(st: Option<&mut DeflateState>, src: &[u8], level: i32, dst: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, i32>`**
  zlib stream into dst  [zlib_deflate_to]

- **`fn deflate_raw_to(st: Option<&mut DeflateState>, src: &[u8], level: i32, dst: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, i32>`**
  raw deflate data into dst  [deflate_raw_to]

- **`fn zlib_deflate(src: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8>`**
  zlib stream  [zlib_deflate]

- **`fn zlib_deflate_st(st: Option<&mut DeflateState>, src: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8>`**
  zlib stream with a reusable state (None = a temporary one)  [zlib_deflate_st]

- **`fn deflate_raw(src: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8>`**
  raw deflate data  [deflate_raw]

- **`fn deflate_raw_st(st: Option<&mut DeflateState>, src: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8>`**
  raw deflate data with a reusable state  [deflate_raw_st without head / tail]

- **`fn deflate_raw_ex(st: Option<&mut DeflateState>, src: &[u8], level: i32, head: usize, tail: usize) -> Vec<u8>`**
  raw deflate data after `head` zero bytes (head, tail: 0..65536, larger values clamped);
  the Vec holds head + the compressed bytes, with room for `tail` more  [deflate_raw_st]

### `img_core/exif.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/exif.rs`](../lib/img_core/exif.rs)

```text
exif -- TIFF IFD reader (EXIF blocks; shared with the TIFF codec) and EXIF helpers
                                                                         [src/img/exif.s]

  Tifr::open(data) -> Ok(reader) / Err(ERR_TRUNC / ERR_HDR)
  tr.visit(off) -> 0 / ERR_LIMIT        record an IFD (a cycle or TIFR_MAXIFD IFDs: limit)
  tr.count(off) -> entries (clamped to what fits) / ERR_TRUNC
  tr.ifd(off) -> entries / ERR_*        visit + count
  tr.entry(off, i) -> Ok(TEnt) / Err(ERR_HDR unknown type / ERR_TRUNC)
  tr.find(off, tag) -> Some(TEnt)       first entry with the tag (bad entries skipped)
  tr.get(te, i) -> u64                  integer value i (signed types sign-extended,
                                        RATIONAL: numerator, FLOAT / DOUBLE: raw bits)
  tr.rational(te, i) -> (num, den)      RATIONAL / SRATIONAL value i (others: value / 1)
  tr.next(off) -> offset of the next IFD (0 = none)
  exif_read(blob) -> (0 / ERR_*, ExifInfo)   orientation, resolution, colour space
  exif_orientation(blob) -> 1..8
  exif_set_orientation(blob, o) -> bool      patch the IFD0 Orientation SHORT in place
  exif_copy_orient1(blob) -> Vec             copy with orientation 1

The reader works on a TIFF structure in memory: "II*\0" / "MM\0*" (classic, 4-byte
offsets, 12-byte entries) or BigTIFF "II+\0" / "MM\0+" (8-byte offsets, 20-byte
entries); every read is bounds-checked, value spans must lie inside the data.
```

```rust
TIFR_MAXIFD: usize = 1024  // IFDs per reader (chain + sub-IFDs), cycles detected
TIFR_MAXDEPTH: u32 = 3  // sub-IFD nesting callers must respect
```

- **`struct TEnt`**
  one decoded IFD entry (TENT)
  - `tag: u32`
  - `typ: u32` -- TIFF field type 1..18
  - `count: u64` -- number of values
  - `voff: u64` -- offset of the values in the TIFF structure
  - `bytes: u64` -- count \* type size (inside the data)

- **`struct Tifr<'a>`**
  a TIFF IFD reader (TIFR)
  - `data: &'a [u8]`
  - `be: bool` -- "MM"
  - `big: bool` -- BigTIFF
  - `ifd0: u64` -- offset of the first IFD

**`impl<'a> Tifr<'a>`**

- **`fn open(data: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Tifr<'a>, i32>`**
  start reading the TIFF structure: byte order, classic / BigTIFF, first IFD offset
  [tifr_open]
- **`fn visit(&mut self, off: u64) -> i32`**
  record that the IFD at off is being read: ERR_LIMIT when it was read before or
  TIFR_MAXIFD IFDs were read  [tifr_visit]
- **`fn count(&self, off: u64) -> i64`**
  entries of the IFD at off, clamped to the entries that fit, or ERR_TRUNC
  [tifr_count]

- **`fn entry(&self, off: u64, i: u64) -> Result<TEnt, i32>`**

- **`fn find(&self, off: u64, tag: u32) -> Option<TEnt>`**

  RATIONAL: numerator, FLOAT / DOUBLE: raw bits; 0 when i >= count  [tifr_get]
- **`fn rational(&self, te: &TEnt, i: u64) -> (u64, u64)`**

  give value / 1; i >= count: 0 / 0  [tifr_rational]

  - `orioff: u32` -- offset of the orientation SHORT in the blob (0 = none)

```text
gzip -- gzip (RFC 1952) members on top of inflate_raw / deflate_raw  [src/img/gzip.s]

  gzip_decode(src, dst) -> Ok((bytes, consumed)) / Err(ERR_*)   ONE member; consumed =
                                   the member length incl. the trailer
  gzip_decode_st(st, src, dst)     the same with an inflate state (None = temporary)
  gzip_encode(src, level) -> Vec   one member: 1F 8B 08, FLG 0, MTIME 0, XFL (2 for level 9,
                                   4 for level 1, else 0), OS 255, deflate, CRC32, ISIZE
  gzip_encode_st(st, src, level) -> Vec
  gzip_encode_to(st, src, level, dst) -> Ok(bytes) / Err(ERR_OVERFLOW)   into dst
                                   (deflate_bound(len) always suffices)
  gzip_isize(src) -> Ok(ISIZE) / Err(ERR_TRUNC)   the last 4 bytes of a single member

Decoding: ID1 ID2, CM 8, FLG (reserved bits 5..7 must be 0), MTIME, XFL, OS, then FEXTRA,
FNAME, FCOMMENT, FHCRC (low 16 bits of the CRC-32 of the header bytes), the deflate data,
CRC32 and ISIZE.  Errors: ERR_TRUNC, ERR_HDR, ERR_CHECKSUM and the inflate errors.
```

### `img_core/icc.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/icc.rs`](../lib/img_core/icc.rs)

```text
icc -- ICC profile container helpers (no colour conversion: that is icc_xform)
                                                                          [src/img/icc.s]

  icc_check(data) -> profile size / ERR_TRUNC / ERR_HDR / ERR_UNSUPPORTED
  icc_jpeg_collect(data) -> (1 found / 0 none / ERR_CHUNK, profile)
  icc_jpeg_segments(icc) -> Ok(APP2 segments) / Err(ERR_LIMIT)

icc_check validates the 128-byte header and the tag table: declared size >= 132 and
<= len, 'acsp' at byte 36, major version 2..5, the tag count fits, every tag's data lies
inside the declared size.  JPEG embeds a profile in APP2 segments "ICC_PROFILE\0" + seq
(1-based) + count + data; icc_jpeg_collect walks the segments before the first SOS and
reassembles them in sequence order, rejecting (ERR_CHUNK) like libjpeg's
read_icc_profile: a count of 0, counts that differ, a sequence number of 0 or > count, a
duplicate, a missing one and an empty result.  icc_jpeg_segments produces the complete
APP2 segments (FF E2, length, header, <= 65519 data bytes each); more than 255 segments
-> ERR_LIMIT.
```

- **`fn icc_check(data: &[u8]) -> i64`**
  the declared profile size or ERR_TRUNC (shorter than the header / the declared size),
  ERR_HDR (bad signature, size, tag table), ERR_UNSUPPORTED (major version not 2..5)
  [icc_check]

- **`fn icc_jpeg_collect(data: &[u8]) -> (i32, Vec<u8>)`**
  reassemble the APP2 ICC_PROFILE segments of a JPEG file -> (1 profile / 0 no
  ICC_PROFILE segment / ERR_CHUNK inconsistent segments, profile bytes)  [icc_jpeg_collect]

- **`fn icc_jpeg_segments(icc: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, i32>`**
  the complete APP2 marker segments that embed an ICC profile in a JPEG (written after
  APP0 / APP1); empty for an empty profile  [icc_jpeg_segments]

### `img_core/icc_xform.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/icc_xform.rs`](../lib/img_core/icc_xform.rs)

```text
icc_xform -- ICC colour transforms                  [src/img/icc_xform.s, inc/icc.inc]

  IccXform::build(src, dst, intent, flags) -> IccXform | ERR_*
       src / dst = profile bytes (None = the built-in sRGB); intent ICC_* , flags
       ICF_BPC / ICF_NOIDENT / ICF_LUT.  ERR_TRUNC / ERR_HDR (broken profile, bad tag),
       ERR_UNSUPPORTED (CMYK / Lab / other device spaces, links, abstract, named colour,
       unknown tag types, gray LUT profiles, singular colorants, intent > 3), ERR_LIMIT
       (curv > 2^20 entries)  [icc_xform_build]
  xf.row(src, dst)        straight BGRA pixels (8 bit), alpha unchanged; any thread, no
                          allocation  [icc_xform_row]
  xf.row_in_place(px)     the same with src == dst
  xf.kind() -> ICX_*      [icc_xform_kind]
  icc_builtin(id) -> profile bytes (static) | None   ICC_BI_*  [icc_builtin]
  icc_describe(icc, buf) -> bytes   UTF-8 'desc' text, NUL-terminated  [icc_describe]
  set_parallel(f)         the loop that builds LUT grids (plat::parallel_for in the apps;
                          without one the grid planes are built one after the other)

Profiles: RGB and gray, v2 and v4, classes mntr / scnr / prtr / spac.  Matrix/TRC
(rXYZ gXYZ bXYZ + rTRC gTRC bTRC, gray kTRC; curv identity / gamma / table, para 0..4)
and LUT tags (A2B0..2 / B2A0..2 as lut8 / lut16 / mAB / mBA; PCS XYZ or Lab).  Tag choice
like LittleCMS: the intent's LUT tag (absolute: *1), else *0, else the matrix/TRC.
Media white for the absolute intent: wtpt (D50 for v2 display profiles, like lcms).

Paths (ICX_*): identical profiles -> copy; matrix/TRC on both sides -> ICX_MATRIX: per
channel f32 linearisation tables (256), one 3x3 f32 matrix (dst^-1 * adapt * src), linear
values clamped to 0..1, index round(sqrt(v) * 4096) into u8 inverse tables (4097 entries,
built by inverting 8193 forward samples of the destination TRC) -- a simd::Kernel, 4 (SSE2)
or 8 (AVX2) pixels per step, every lane computes what the assembly's SSE lane computes;
a result that maps every channel value to itself becomes ICX_IDENTITY.  Otherwise
ICX_LUT: the whole float64 pipeline (src -> PCS XYZ -> intent / BPC -> dst) sampled on a
33^3 grid whose node positions are (k/32)^2 per axis (dense near black), f32 per channel,
tetrahedral interpolation in f32 (grid planes on the worker pool, see set_parallel).  For
matrix/TRC (gray) destinations the grid holds the destination's LINEAR values, unclamped,
and every pixel ends like the matrix path (clamp, sqrt index, inverse TRC table); for B2A
destinations device values.  The tetrahedron is chosen without branches (a table over the
three comparisons of the assembly's decision tree, the weights as max / median / min of
the fractions): the same vertices and weights, no mispredictions on random pixels.

The handle of the assembly becomes a value (dropping it frees it); the parsing and the
float64 maths are in icc_eval, the built-in profiles and the description in icc_bi.
Deviation: out of memory aborts (Vec) instead of ERR_NOMEM.
```

*icc.inc*

```rust
ICC_PERCEPTUAL: u32 = 0  // rendering intents (ICC numbering)
ICC_RELATIVE: u32 = 1  // relative colorimetric
ICC_SATURATION: u32 = 2
ICC_ABSOLUTE: u32 = 3  // absolute colorimetric
ICF_BPC: u32 = 1  // black point compensation (not with ICC_ABSOLUTE)
ICF_NOIDENT: u32 = 2  // never take the identity shortcut (tests)
ICF_LUT: u32 = 4  // always use the 3D LUT path (tests)
ICX_IDENTITY: u32 = 0  // rows are copied
ICX_MATRIX: u32 = 1  // linearisation tables + 3x3 matrix + inverse tables
ICX_LUT: u32 = 2  // 33^3 3D LUT, tetrahedral interpolation
ICC_BI_SRGB: u32 = 0  // sRGB IEC61966-2.1 compatible
ICC_BI_A98: u32 = 1  // A98 RGB compatible (CSS Color 4 a98-rgb: D65, gamma 563/256)
ICC_BI_P3: u32 = 2  // Display P3
ICC_BI_ROMM: u32 = 3  // ROMM RGB (ISO 22028-2, D50, gamma 1.8)
ICC_BI_GRAY22: u32 = 4  // gray, gamma 2.2, D50
ICC_BI_COUNT: u32 = 5
ICC_MON_PRIMARY: i32 = -1  // plat::monitor_icc: the primary monitor
```

- **`struct IccXform`**
  a colour transform between two profiles

- **`fn set_parallel(f: ParallelFor)`**
  the loop the LUT grids are built with = img_core::set_parallel (kept for its callers)

**`impl IccXform`**

- **`fn build(src: Option<&[u8]>, dst: Option<&[u8]>, intent: u32, flags: u32) -> Result<IccXform, i32>`**
  a transform from profile src to profile dst (None = the built-in sRGB)
  [icc_xform_build]
- **`fn kind(&self) -> u32`**
  ICX_IDENTITY / ICX_MATRIX / ICX_LUT  [icc_xform_kind]
- **`fn row(&self, src: &[u8], dst: &mut [u8])`**
  dst.len() / 4 straight BGRA pixels from src (at least as long) to dst, alpha

- **`fn row_in_place(&self, px: &mut [u8])`**

### `img_core/inflate.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/inflate.rs`](../lib/img_core/inflate.rs)

```text
inflate -- DEFLATE (RFC 1951) and zlib (RFC 1950) decompression  [src/img/inflate.s]

  zlib_inflate(src, dst) -> Ok(bytes written) / Err(ERR_*)
  inflate_raw(src, dst) -> Ok(bytes) / Err(ERR_*)
  inflate_raw_ex(src, dst) -> Ok((bytes, consumed)) / Err(ERR_*)   consumed = input bytes
                                    of the deflate data (up to the end of the final block)
  InflateState::new() -> Box      reusable decoder state (one thread at a time; an error
                                    never affects later calls)
  zlib_inflate_st(st, src, dst) / inflate_raw_st(st, src, dst)   the same with a state
                                    (None = a temporary one, like the classic calls)
  rev16(x)                        16-bit bit reversal (shared with deflate)
  LBASE / LEXT / DBASE / DEXT / CLORDER   the code tables (shared with deflate)

The output buffer has a fixed capacity: every write is bounds-checked (ERR_OVERFLOW),
every back reference is checked against the bytes produced so far (ERR_DIST), reading
past the end of the input gives ERR_TRUNC.  zlib header errors: ERR_HDR; a wrong
Adler-32: ERR_CHECKSUM.

The bit buffer behaves exactly as the assembly's (the error codes of corrupt input depend
on it): refilled 8 bytes at a time while 8 input bytes remain (the count becomes
56 + count % 8), byte by byte near the end with zero bytes counted as padding (more than
PAD_MAX of them = ERR_TRUNC); Huffman tables as stb_image (10-bit fast table, canonical
slow path); a code table's sorted-index arrays keep entries of an earlier build (the
slow path checks the length, as the assembly).

Speed (perf-inflate): the symbol loop runs in codes_fast while 8 input bytes remain at
every refill and a whole match fits the output: no slow refill, no overflow checks, no
call on the literal path (the state stays in registers), u32 fast tables (lx / dx) with
the length / distance base and extra-bit count folded in (one load and two shifts per
code), wide match moves.  It hands over to the careful loop before the symbol where a
condition fails; both follow the assembly's loop step by step.
```

### `img_core/io.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/io.rs`](../lib/img_core/io.rs)

```text
io -- image files: format detection, codec dispatch, load and save; the format table and
the glue of the core codecs                    [src/img/imgio.s, imgreg.s, imgcore.s glue]

Classic API (FMT_PARGB, PNG / JPEG / BMP / GIF only, through the codecs' decode_fl / save):
  decode(data) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)     PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP by magic bytes (and SVG
                                               once img_svg::register entered IMGF_SVG)
  load(path) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)
  save(path, sf) / save_ex(path, sf, quality) -> 0 / ERR_*   by extension (.png .jpg .jpeg
                                               .jfif .jpe .bmp .dib .gif, any case)
  format(path) -> IMGF_* of those extensions (0 = unknown)
Extended API:
  detect(data, hint) -> IMGF_* / 0             magic bytes (TGA: hint or its probe)
  probe(data, meta) -> IMGF_* / 0              detect + header scan into meta
  decode_ex(data, dec, meta) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)
  load_ex(path, dec, meta) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)
  encode(sf, opt) -> Ok(file bytes) / Err(ERR_*)
  save_opt(path, sf, opt) -> 0 / ERR_*         atomic write (the file hook)
  opt_init(fmt) -> ImgOpt                      paint.net's defaults
  format_info(fmt) -> Option<FmtInfo>          format_from_path(path) -> IMGF_* / 0
  filter_list(need, cap) -> the ui_filedlg list "png=PNG\0jpg;...=JPEG\0...\0" (empty when
                                               it does not fit into cap bytes)
  register(fmt, codec) -> 0 / ERR_UNSUPPORTED  register_dyn(name, exts, mime, props, codec)
  register_slot(IMGF_SVG, name, exts, mime, props, codec)   (svg) a built-in format without
                                               a static entry (img_svg::register)
  set_file_io(FileIo)                          the file functions of load / save (img_core
                                               does not depend on plat: the app sets them)
Glue for the core codecs (imgcore.s):
  core_decode(data, sf, dec, meta, scan, decode_fl) -> 0 / ERR_*   scanner, frame / size
                                               checks, then the classic decoder
  core_probe(data, meta, scan) -> bool
  dpi_ppm(dpi) / ppm_dpi(ppm)                  16.16 dpi <-> pixels per metre

The format table has a static entry per built-in format (name, extensions, MIME,
properties); a codec crate's `CODEC` gets into it through register (img_all::
use_core_codecs / use_all_codecs).  Runtime formats (plugins) use the slots IMG_DYN0 ..
IMGF_COUNT - 1.

decode_ex: the codec gets a normalised copy of dec (maxpx filled in; ICC / EXIF / XMP
dropped when the caller passed no ImgMeta); the ImgMeta is cleared first and gets fmt,
orient 1, frames 1.  After a successful decode the orientation is applied (unless
IMGD_NO_ORIENT or the codec did it: IMF_ORIENT_APPLIED) and the pixels are converted to
FMT_ARGB (IMGD_STRAIGHT) or FMT_PARGB.  On an error the blobs are dropped (the other
metadata fields stay).
```

*detection*

```rust
PNG_SIG: [u8; 8] = [0x89, b'P', b'N', b'G', 0x0D, 0x0A, 0x1A, 0x0A]
```

- **`fn detect(data: &[u8], hint: u32) -> u32`**
  the format of data by its magic bytes (order: PNG, JPEG, GIF, DDS, WebP, TIFF / BigTIFF,
  JPEG XR, ISOBMFF (AVIF / HEIC), JPEG XL container, PDN, gzip (legacy PDN), JPEG XL
  codestream, BMP, runtime formats, TGA by hint or its registered probe) -> IMGF_\* / 0
  [img_detect]

- **`fn probe(data: &[u8], meta: Option<&mut ImgMeta>) -> u32`**
  detect without a hint; with a meta: it is cleared (fmt, orient 1, frames 1 set) and the
  registered codec's probe reads the header into it (w = 0 when the header could not be
  read; no blobs)  [img_probe]

- **`fn decode_ex(data: &[u8], dec: Option<&ImgDec>, meta: Option<&mut ImgMeta>) -> Result<Surface, i32>`**
  decode any registered format into a new surface: FMT_ARGB with IMGD_STRAIGHT, else
  FMT_PARGB (see the module header)  [img_decode_ex]

- **`fn load_ex(path: &str, dec: Option<&ImgDec>, meta: Option<&mut ImgMeta>) -> Result<Surface, i32>`**
  read a file and decode_ex it; a zero dec.hint comes from the file extension; ERR_IO
  when unreadable  [img_load_ex]

- **`fn encode(sf: &Surface, opt: Option<&ImgOpt>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, i32>`**
  encode sf (FMT_XRGB, PARGB, ARGB or A8) as opt.fmt  [img_encode]
  Errors: ERR_UNSUPPORTED (format unknown / not registered / no encoder, or another
  surface format), ERR_DIMS (empty surface), ERR_CANCEL and the codec errors.

- **`fn save_opt(path: &str, sf: &Surface, opt: Option<&ImgOpt>) -> i32`**
  encode and write the file atomically; fmt 0 takes the format from the extension;
  ERR_IO when writing fails  [img_save_opt]

- **`fn core_decode(data: &[u8], sf: &mut Surface, dec: &ImgDec, meta: &mut ImgMeta, scan: ScanFn, decode_fl: DecodeFlFn) -> i32`**
  run the metadata scanner; with IMGD_PROBE return its result; else refuse frame > 0,
  check the header size (ERR_LIMIT) and call the classic decoder with JDF_STRAIGHT
  (IMGD_STRAIGHT) | JDF_NO_ORIENT (IMGD_NO_ORIENT)  [core_decode]

- **`fn core_probe(data: &[u8], meta: &mut ImgMeta, scan: ScanFn) -> bool`**
  the scanner without blobs: recognised (meta filled)  [core_probe]

- **`fn dpi_ppm(dpi: u32) -> u32`**
  pixels per metre from a 16.16 dpi value (rounded, at most 0x7FFFFFFF)  [dpi_ppm]

- **`fn ppm_dpi(ppm: u32) -> u32`**
  16.16 dpi from pixels per metre (0 -> 0)  [ppm_dpi]

### `img_core/meta.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_core/meta.rs`](../lib/img_core/meta.rs)

```text
meta -- shared helpers of the codecs: metadata blobs, size limits, straight <->
premultiplied conversion, orientation, sample depth conversion, JPEG segment walking
                                                                     [src/img/imgmeta.s]

  meta_blob(meta, Blob, src)            copy src into the ICC / EXIF / XMP blob (len 0: nothing)
  meta_free(meta)                       drop the blobs (the other fields stay)
  dims_check(w, h, dec) -> 0 / ERR_DIMS / ERR_LIMIT    w, h 1..IMG_MAXDIM, w * h <= maxpx
  mem_check(bytes, dec) -> 0 / ERR_LIMIT               against dec.maxmem (0 = no limit)
  surf_alloc(w, h, fmt, dec) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)   dims_check + a zeroed surface
  premultiply(sf) / unpremultiply(sf)   FMT_ARGB <-> FMT_PARGB in place (others untouched)
  convert(sf, fmt) -> 0 / ERR_UNSUPPORTED   in place to FMT_PARGB / FMT_ARGB from XRGB,
                                        PARGB, ARGB
  surf_convert(src, fmt) -> Ok(surface) / Err(ERR_*)   a new surface from any get_row source
  get_row(sf, y, dst, fmt)              row y as w straight (FMT_ARGB) / premultiplied
                                        (FMT_PARGB) BGRA pixels from XRGB (alpha 255),
                                        PARGB, ARGB, A8 (grey); other formats: transparent
  orient(sf, o) -> 0                    apply an EXIF orientation 2..8 (5..8 swap w and h)
  u16_to_u8(v)                          round(v / 257)
  row_u16_to_u8(dst, src, be)           16-bit samples (bytes, LE / BE) -> bytes
  half_to_f32(h)                        IEEE half -> single precision bits
  row_half_to_u8(dst, src) / row_f32_to_u8(dst, src)   round(clamp(v, 0, 1) * 255), NaN -> 0
  row_f32_to_srgb8(dst, src)            linear floats -> sRGB bytes (4096-entry table)
  jpg_seg_next(data, js) -> marker      JPEG marker segment iterator (JSeg)
  srgb_lin(v) / SRGB_LIN_BITS           sRGB byte -> linear light (f32)
  all_opaque(sf) -> bool                every alpha of a 32-bit surface is 255  [png.s]
  unpremul(p)                           premultiplied -> straight, one pixel  [png.s]

Straight -> premultiplied: round(c * a / 255); premultiplied -> straight: min(255,
(c * ceil(255 * 2^24 / a) + 2^23) >> 24), a = 0 gives 0 (gfx::straight's kernels have
exactly these rules).
```

  IEEE halves -> bytes round(clamp(v, 0, 1) \* 255), NaN -> 0  [img_row_half_to_u8]

  linear-light floats -> sRGB-encoded bytes (clamp 0..1, NaN -> 0, 4096-entry table)
  [img_row_f32_to_srgb8]

  sRGB decode (IEC 61966-2-1) of v / 255  [g_img_srgb_lin]

- **`struct JSeg`**
  a JPEG segment walker (JSEG): pos = next read offset (start: 2, after SOI); ptr / len =
  the payload of the current segment (offset into the data)
  - `pos: usize`
  - `ptr: usize`
  - `len: usize`

**`impl JSeg`**

- **`fn new() -> JSeg`**

- **`fn jpg_seg_next(data: &[u8], js: &mut JSeg) -> u32`**
  the next JPEG marker segment from js.pos: skips bytes that are not 0xFF, fill bytes,
  standalone markers (TEM, RSTn); returns the marker (0xC0..0xFE) with js.ptr / js.len =
  the payload (after the 2 length bytes) and js.pos behind it; 0xD9 (EOI) and 0xD8 (SOI)
  come with len 0; 0 = end of data, a truncated segment or a length &lt; 2  [jpg_seg_next]
