### `img_svg/doc.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_svg/doc.rs`](../lib/img_svg/doc.rs)

```text
doc -- the parsed document: elements with their kind, attributes, cascaded properties,
pre-built path data, the id map, the intrinsic size and the embedded raster images

The cascade runs once at parse time: presentation attributes, then the matching rules of
every <style> sheet (by specificity, then order), then the style attribute; later
declarations win.  Inheritance and "inherit" are resolved while rendering (render.rs),
because `use` makes an element inherit from the referencing element.
```

- **`struct Svg`**
  a parsed SVG document (immutable; render it as often as needed)

**`impl Svg`**

- **`fn parse(data: &[u8]) -> Result<Svg, i32>`**
  parse an SVG document (UTF-8 XML; gzip data (.svgz) is inflated first):
  Err(ERR_HDR) when it is no SVG, ERR_LIMIT beyond the size limits
- **`fn size(&self) -> (f64, f64)`**
  the intrinsic size in px (CSS px = DIP): width / height of the root, else its viewBox,
  else 300 x 150
- **`fn view_box(&self) -> Option<[f64; 4]>`**
  the root's viewBox (x, y, w, h), if it has one
- **`fn title(&self) -> &str`**
  the text of the root's &lt;title> (blanks collapsed; empty without one)
- **`fn truncated(&self) -> bool`**
  the file ended early or a limit dropped elements (what was read is drawn)
- **`fn element_count(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of elements

### `img_svg/render.rs`

Source: [`lib/img_svg/render.rs`](../lib/img_svg/render.rs)

```text
render -- draw a parsed document through gfx: styles with inheritance, the element walk
(svg, g, a, switch, use + symbol, shapes, text, image), paints (colours, gradients),
group opacity in layers, clip paths as 8-bit masks

Coordinates: every element is drawn with the matrix user space -> device pixels; paths are
flattened in device space (gfx::pathdata, 0.05 px), strokes are outlined there by
gfx::dash (width = stroke-width x sqrt(|det|) of the matrix: non-uniform scaling draws an
even width), filled by gfx::raster with the fill rule.  Opacity of an element that paints
one thing (only fill or only stroke) multiplies that paint; groups and elements that paint
both are drawn into a layer (the bounds of the content, inside the clip) and composited.
Text needs a TextHook (the app's font engine): one line per text chunk, tspans with their
own style and x / y / dx / dy (first values), text-anchor; without a hook text is skipped.
Limits: MAX_DRAWS element visits per render, MAX_NEST nesting (groups, use), MAX_LAYERS
layers alive at once (deeper opacity is applied to the paints), use cycles are cut.
```

- **`trait TextHook`**
  the font engine for &lt;text> (an app's; ui::SvgText wraps the UI's): glyph outlines and
  advances of one line
  - `fn outline(&mut self, path: &mut Path, s: &str, font: &FontSpec, px: f32, x: f32, y: f32) -> f32`
    append the outline of `s` to `path` (flattened closed contours in path pixels): the
    baseline starts at (x, y), `px` pixels per em; returns the advance in pixels
  - `fn advance(&mut self, s: &str, font: &FontSpec, px: f32) -> f32`
    the advance of `s` in pixels at `px` pixels per em

- **`struct FontSpec<'a>`**
  what a text run asks of the font engine
  - `family: &'a str` -- the font-family list as written ("Arial, sans-serif")
  - `weight: u16` -- 100 .. 900 (400 normal, 700 bold)
  - `italic: bool`

- **`struct Opts<'a>`**
  render options
  - `color: u32` -- the colour of currentColor at the root (0xAARRGGBB)
  - `text: Option<&'a mut dyn TextHook>` -- the font engine for text (None: text is not drawn)

**`impl Svg`**

- **`fn render(&self, sf: &mut Surface, m: &Matrix, clip: Option<[i32; 4]>, opts: &mut Opts)`**
  draw the document: its viewport (the intrinsic size, viewBox mapped by
  preserveAspectRatio) through m (intrinsic px -> surface px); clip: the surface
  rectangle x0, y0, x1, y1 (exclusive) that may change (None: all of it).  Content
  outside the viewport is clipped (to its box under m).  The surface: FMT_PARGB, or the
  window's FMT_XRGB (blended the same way)
- **`fn render_rect(&self, sf: &mut Surface, x: f64, y: f64, w: f64, h: f64, clip: Option<[i32; 4]>, opts: &mut Opts)`**
  draw the document into the rectangle x, y, w, h of the surface as its viewport (the
  viewBox mapped into it by preserveAspectRatio: sharp at any size)
- **`fn rasterize(&self, w: i32, h: i32, opts: &mut Opts) -> Result<Surface, i32>`**
  a new FMT_PARGB surface w x h with the document drawn into it (render_rect);
  Err(ERR_DIMS) for sides outside 1 .. 65535, Err(ERR_LIMIT) beyond IMG_MAXPX_DEF pixels

## fx

*effects and adjustments* -- crate root [`lib/fx/lib.rs`](../lib/fx/lib.rs)

```text
fx -- the effect and adjustment kernels: the FXDESC registry, prepare / render on ROIs from
worker threads, deterministic per pixel                       [src/fx/*.s, inc/fx.inc]

The contract (fx.inc).  An application (PaintCraft, efftest) runs an effect by
  1. copying the source layer (FMT_ARGB, straight alpha) -> FxArgs::src,
  2. calling desc.prepare once when it has one (global statistics, LUTs, noise tables):
     Ok(Some(aux)) / Ok(None) / Err(ERR_*) -- ERR_CANCEL when the job was cancelled,
  3. calling desc.render for many rectangles (ROIs) -- from several worker threads at once
     -- until the ROIs cover the area to change; every call gets the aux of step 2,
  4. blending the destination back through the selection mask itself
     (gfx::straight::lerp_mask_row).
Rules: render writes the destination only inside its ROI (Dst holds exactly those pixels)
and may read the whole source; the result of a pixel depends only on (source, params, aux)
-- never on the ROI split or the thread count (bit-identical); render polls the job's
cancel flag once per row (FxArgs::cancelled) and returns ERR_CANCEL at once.  Pixels are
straight ARGB (0xAARRGGBB = bytes B, G, R, A).  Random effects use hash32(x, y, seed,
stream), never a sequential generator.  FXF_BANDS: render wants full-width row bands (the
runner splits by rows only); FXF_WHOLE: one call over the whole image.

API (the asm records as Rust types):
  FxDesc   FXDESC: id (FX_*), flags (FXF_*), name (ASCII key), prepare / render (fn
           pointers; FXD_FREE is the Drop of the aux), props (FXPROP records), category
           (FXC_*), user (free for the registering code, e.g. a plugin index)
  FxProp   FXPROP: typ (FP_*), dec, slot, flags (FPF_*), name, min, max, def (FP_COLOR:
           the f64 bits are the ARGB colour -- color()), def_y (FP_PAN: the y default),
           choices (FP_CHOICE keys)
  Params   the parameter block: FX_NSLOTS u64 slots (i64 for FP_INT / BOOL / CHOICE / SEED,
           f64 bits for FP_DEC / ANGLE / PAN, ARGB in the low half for FP_COLOR, raw bytes
           for FP_BLOB); defaults(desc, &mut params) fills it
  FxArgs   FXARGS without the destination: src, ROI x0 y0 x1 y1, params, aux, job (a
           Cancel flag: the worker pool's JobCtl, an AtomicBool / AtomicU32), sel (the
           selection TMask: statistics may be limited to it)
  Dst      the destination pixels of one render call: one &mut [u8] per ROI row with the
           pixels x0..x1 -- of_surface (one call owns the whole rectangle), tiles (disjoint
           rectangles of one surface for parallel calls; the row slices of all of them live
           in one caller-owned Vec), strided (rows of a tile buffer), or new (a row list)
  Aux      Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>: the result of prepare, read by render (aux::<T>())
  registry use_all() registers the built-in groups (menu order), register(group) adds a
           group (&'static [FxDesc], e.g. plugin effects), count(), get(i), find(name),
           find_id(id), defaults(desc, params)
  hash32(x, y, seed, stream)   deterministic per-pixel random bits (fx_common.s)
  rows(a, dst, f)              fx_rows: f(dst_row, src_row, x0, y) for every ROI row

Modules: lut (fx_lut.s), hist (fx_hist.s), adj (fx_adj.s), color (fx_color.s), stylize
(fx_stylize.s), conv (fx_conv.s), lochist (fx_lochist.s), blur (fx_blur.s), artistic
(fx_artistic.s), noise (fx_noise.s), photo (fx_photo.s), object (fx_object.s), warp
(fx_warp.s), perlin (fx_perlin.s), distort (fx_distort.s), render (fx_render.s).
```

### `fx` crate root

Re-exports: `gfx::tmask::TMask`

Re-exports: `gfx::Surface`

Re-exports: `plat::JobCtl`

*constants (fx.inc)*

```rust
FX_NSLOTS: usize = 32  // parameter slots per effect
FXF_ADJ: u32 = 1  // adjustment (Korrekturen) rather than effect
FXF_PREPARE: u32 = 2  // has a prepare step (statistics over the source / selection)
FXF_SEED: u32 = 4  // uses a random seed (has an FP_SEED property)
FXF_BANDS: u32 = 8  // render wants full-width row bands
FXF_WHOLE: u32 = 16  // render must get the whole image in one call
```

- **`type Aux = Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>`**
  the result of prepare (read-only in render; FXD_FREE = its Drop)

- **`type PrepareFn = fn(&FxArgs) -> Result<Option<Aux>, i32>`**
  FXD_PREPARE: Ok(Some(aux)) / Ok(None) / Err(ERR_\*)

- **`type RenderFn = fn(&FxArgs, &mut Dst) -> i32`**
  FXD_RENDER: 0 / ERR_CANCEL / ERR_\*

- **`struct FxDesc`**
  an effect (FXDESC)
  - `id: u32`
  - `flags: u32`
  - `name: &'static str`
  - `prepare: Option<PrepareFn>`
  - `render: RenderFn`
  - `props: &'static [FxProp]`
  - `category: u32`
  - `user: usize` -- free for the code that registers the group (0 for the built-in effects)

- **`struct FxProp`**
  a property (FXPROP); slot i of the parameter block belongs to property i, except FP_PAN
  (2 slots) and FP_BLOB (max slots)
  - `typ: u8`
  - `dec: u8`
  - `slot: u8`
  - `flags: u8`
  - `name: &'static str`
  - `min: f64`
  - `max: f64`
  - `def: f64` -- the default (FP_COLOR: the bits of this f64 are the ARGB colour)
  - `def_y: f64` -- FP_PAN: the y default (FXP_CHOICES of the asm record)
  - `choices: &'static [&'static str]`

**`impl FxProp`**

- **`const fn new(typ: u8, dec: u8, slot: u8, flags: u8, name: &'static str, min: f64, max: f64, def: f64) -> FxProp`**
  an FP_INT / DEC / BOOL / ANGLE / SEED / BLOB property (FXPROP)
- **`const fn choice(slot: u8, name: &'static str, max: f64, def: f64, choices: &'static [&'static str]) -> FxProp`**
  an FP_CHOICE property
- **`const fn color(slot: u8, name: &'static str, argb: u32) -> FxProp`**
  an FP_COLOR property (FXPROPC: the default's bits are the colour)
- **`const fn pan(slot: u8, name: &'static str, dec: u8, min: f64, max: f64, x: f64, y: f64) -> FxProp`**
  an FP_PAN property (default x, y)
- **`fn def_color(&self) -> u32`**
  the default colour of an FP_COLOR property

- **`struct Params(pub [u64; FX_NSLOTS])`**
  the parameter block (FX_NSLOTS 8-byte slots)

**`impl Params`**

- **`fn i(&self, slot: usize) -> i64`**
  slot as i64
- **`fn f(&self, slot: usize) -> f64`**
  slot as f64
- **`fn int(&self, slot: usize, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32`**
  the i64 slot clamped to lo..=hi  [prm_int]
- **`fn dbl(&self, slot: usize, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> f64`**
  the f64 slot clamped to lo..=hi, NaN -> lo  [prm_f64]
- **`fn byte(&self, slot: usize, i: usize) -> u8`**
  byte i of the block counted from slot `slot` (FP_BLOB)
- **`fn set_i(&mut self, slot: usize, v: i64)`**
- **`fn set_f(&mut self, slot: usize, v: f64)`**
- **`fn set_byte(&mut self, slot: usize, i: usize, v: u8)`**

- **`trait Cancel`**
  a cancel flag render / prepare poll (JOB_CANCEL of FXA_JOB): the pool's JobCtl, or any
  flag of the caller's
  - `fn cancelled(&self) -> bool`

- **`struct FxArgs<'a>`**
  the arguments of prepare / render (FXARGS without the destination)
  - `src: &'a Surface`
  - `x0: i32`
  - `y0: i32`
  - `x1: i32`
  - `y1: i32`
  - `params: &'a Params`
  - `aux: Option<&'a (dyn Any + Send + Sync)>`
  - `job: Option<&'a (dyn Cancel + Sync)>`
  - `sel: Option<&'a TMask>`

**`impl<'a> FxArgs<'a>`**

- **`fn new(src: &'a Surface, roi: [i32; 4], params: &'a Params) -> FxArgs<'a>`**
  arguments for the ROI (x0, y0) - (x1, y1) without aux, job and selection
- **`fn cancelled(&self) -> bool`**
  the job's cancel flag is set (JOB_CANCEL)
- **`fn aux<T: 'static>(&self) -> Option<&'a T>`**
  the aux of prepare as T
- **`fn src_row(&self, y: i32) -> &'a [u8]`**
  source row y (w \* 4 bytes)

- **`fn row(sf: &Surface, y: i32) -> &[u8]`**
  row y of a surface (w \* 4 bytes)

- **`fn px(b: &[u8], i: usize) -> u32`**
  pixel i of a row

- **`fn put(b: &mut [u8], i: usize, v: u32)`**
  set pixel i of a row

- **`struct Dst<'a>`**
  the destination pixels of one render call: row k holds the pixels x0..x1 of row y0 + k
  - `x0: i32`
  - `y0: i32`
  - `x1: i32`
  - `y1: i32`

**`impl<'a> Dst<'a>`**

- **`fn new(roi: [i32; 4], rows: Vec<&'a mut [u8]>) -> Dst<'a>`**
  a destination from row slices (each (x1 - x0) \* 4 bytes, y1 - y0 of them)
- **`fn strided(roi: [i32; 4], buf: &'a mut [u8], stride: usize) -> Dst<'a>`**
  a destination in one buffer: row y0 + k at k \* stride (e.g. a tile buffer with stride
  (x1 - x0) \* 4)
- **`fn of_surface(sf: &'a mut Surface, roi: [i32; 4]) -> Dst<'a>`**
  the rectangle of a surface (clamped to it) as one destination
- **`fn row(&mut self, y: i32) -> &mut [u8]`**
  the pixels x0..x1 of row y (y0 &lt;= y &lt; y1)

- **`fn tiles<'a>(sf: &'a mut Surface, rects: &[[i32; 4]], store: &'a mut Vec<&'a mut [u8]>) -> Vec<Dst<'a>>`**
  disjoint rectangles of a surface as destinations (clamped to the surface; empty ones are
  empty destinations); panics when two rectangles overlap.  `store` holds the row slices of
  all destinations (one allocation, cleared first; pass a new or reused empty Vec):
  ```text
  let mut store = Vec::new();
  let dsts = fx::tiles(&mut surface, &rects, &mut store);
  ```

- **`fn rows(a: &FxArgs, dst: &mut Dst, mut f: impl FnMut(&mut [u8], &[u8], i32, i32)) -> i32`**
  fx_rows: f(dst_row, src_row, x0, y) for every row of the ROI (rows = the pixels x0..x1);
  polls the cancel flag before every row  -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL

- **`fn register(group: &'static [FxDesc]) -> i32`**
  add a group of effects; a group already registered is ignored -> 0 | ERR_LIMIT

- **`fn use_all()`**
  register every built-in group in menu order (adjustments first)  [fx_use_all]

- **`fn count() -> usize`**
  the number of registered effects

- **`fn get(i: usize) -> Option<&'static FxDesc>`**
  the i-th registered effect (group order, then table order)

- **`fn find(name: &str) -> Option<&'static FxDesc>`**
  the effect with this ASCII key

- **`fn find_id(id: u32) -> Option<&'static FxDesc>`**
  the effect with this FX_\* id

- **`fn defaults(desc: &FxDesc, p: &mut Params)`**
  every property's default into its slot(s); slots without a property are 0

- **`fn hash32(x: u32, y: u32, seed: u32, stream: u32) -> u32`**
  deterministic per-pixel random bits: a murmur3-style finaliser over the inputs  [fx_hash32]

### `fx/adj.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/adj.rs`](../lib/fx/adj.rs)

```text
adj -- the 13 adjustments (Korrekturen) of paint.net 5.1 as pure kernels    [src/fx/fx_adj.s]

  FXTAB            the group table (menu order of paint.net)

Pixels are straight ARGB; every adjustment keeps alpha (except Invert Alpha) and changes the
colour of transparent pixels like any other.  Intensity I = (7471 B + 38470 G + 19595 R) >> 16.

  auto_level          prepare: histogram (alpha > 0, selection > 0) -> paint.net
                      HistogramRgb.MakeLevelsAuto -> Level lut
  black_white         B = G = R = I
  brightness_contrast paint.net 3.x BrightnessAndContrastAdjustment (integer tables)
  curves              natural cubic spline luts (Luminosity: c + curve[I] - I, or R/G/B)
  exposure            linear light: out = enc(dec(c) * 2^ev) per channel lut
  highlights_shadows  blurred alpha-weighted intensity grid (prepare) -> gain
                      2^(2 s (1-m)^2 - 2 h m^2) on linear light
  hue_saturation      paint.net HueSaturationLightness (f32 lanes as the asm's SSE code)
  invert_alpha        A = 255 - A
  invert_colors       B, G, R = 255 - c
  levels              paint.net UnaryPixelOps.Level (lut::levels_lut) with a channel mask
  posterize           paint.net PosterizePixel levels per channel
  sepia               Desaturate, then Level with gamma B 1.2, G 1.0, R 0.8 (constant tables)
  temperature_tint    luminance-normalised linear-light channel gains
```

- **`static FXTAB: [FxDesc; 13]`**
  the group table (menu order of paint.net)  [fxtab_adj]

### `fx/artistic.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/artistic.rs`](../lib/fx/artistic.rs)

```text
artistic -- effect group "artistic" (Künstlerisch): ink_sketch, oil_painting, pencil_sketch
                                                                       [src/fx/fx_artistic.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

  oil_painting   brush size b (1..8), coarseness L (3..255): paint.net 3's oil painting: the
                 (2b+1)^2 square window bucketed by intensity FastScale(I, L); the fullest
                 bucket (lowest index on ties) gives the pixel: alpha = sum A / n, colour =
                 sum (c A) / sum A
  pencil_sketch  tip t (1..20), colour range c: D = desaturate(invert(BrightnessContrast(
                 GaussianBlur(src, t), c, -c))); dst = ColorDodge(desaturate(src), D)
  ink_sketch     outline k (0..99), colouring c: Glow (radius 6, b = c = -(c - 50) * 2)
                 screened over the source, then a 5x5 edge kernel (centre 24, others -1) on
                 the premultiplied source darkens it: d = min(255, I (k + 5) >> 6)
```

- **`static FXTAB: [FxDesc; 3]`**
  the group table  [fxtab_artistic]

### `fx/blur.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/blur.rs`](../lib/fx/blur.rs)

```text
blur -- effect group "blur" (Weichzeichnen)                              [src/fx/fx_blur.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

Effects: bokeh_blur, fragment_blur, gaussian_blur, median, motion_blur, radial_blur,
sketch_blur, square_blur, surface_blur, unfocus, zoom_blur
  gaussian_blur  radius r (0..200): Gaussian with 12 sigma^2 = 2 r (r + 2), premultiplied,
                 edges clamped (conv::sep_run)
  square_blur    mean of the (2r+1)^2 square (box, running sums)
  unfocus        mean over the paint.net disc (conv::disc_run)
  median         per channel percentile of the disc (lochist; colour histograms skip alpha 0)
  motion_blur    N = (1 + d) * 3 / 2 bilinear samples (1/16 px) along the direction, mean of
                 the valid ones (interior pixels: collapsed taps, the same integer sum)
  zoom_blur      paint.net 3's zoom blur in 64-bit fixed point, ColorBgra.Blend
  radial_blur    paint.net 3's radial blur (64-bit), ColorBgra.Blend
  fragment_blur  paint.net 3's FragmentEffect
  surface_blur   histogram bilateral filter over the disc
  bokeh_blur     disc mean in linear light with boosted highlights (f32 sums)
  sketch_blur    three layers of stroke cells, 2R + 1 bilinear samples along each cell's
                 direction
```

### `fx/color.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/color.rs`](../lib/fx/color.rs)

```text
color -- Farbe: Quantize                                                 [src/fx/fx_color.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

quantize: colors 2..256, algorithm octree | median_cut, dithering 0..8, alpha keep | binary.
prepare (single thread, polls the cancel flag per row) does everything over the ROI and keeps
the result image in aux; render copies rows (so tiles / threads cannot change the result).
  considered pixels (palette statistics): inside the ROI, selection coverage > 0, alpha > 0
    (keep) / alpha >= 128 (binary); row-major order
  palette: <= K distinct colours -> exactly those (first appearance); else
    octree  Gervautz-Purgathofer: 8 levels, child = bit (7-L) of R, G, B; after every pixel,
            while leaves > K the most recently created internal node of the deepest level
            with internal nodes absorbs its children; palette = leaves depth first
    median_cut  Heckbert on a 32^3 histogram: split the box with the most pixels (ties:
            first) along its longest cell extent after the first slice s with 2 * count(lo..s)
            >= count, boxes shrunk to their occupied cells; colour = round(sum / count)
  mapping: nearest palette colour (squared RGB distance, ties -> lowest index, through lazily
    built candidate lists per 16^3 cell), Floyd-Steinberg (7 / 3 / 5 / 1 in 16ths) when
    dithering L > 0: v = clamp(c + ((E L + 64) >> 7)); only "opaque" pixels take and pass
    on error
  alpha: keep -> unchanged; binary -> 255 when alpha >= 128, else 0
```

- **`static FXTAB: [FxDesc; 1]`**
  the group table  [fxtab_color]

### `fx/conv.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/conv.rs`](../lib/fx/conv.rs)

```text
conv -- shared convolution helpers of the fx kernels                     [src/fx/fx_conv.s]

  exp(x) / ln(x) / pow(x, y)       f64 e^x (Cody-Waite + degree 12 Taylor), ln (2 atanh), x^y
  roi(a) -> Option<[i32; 4]>       the ROI clamped to the image (fxc_roi), None when empty
  copy_roi(a, dst) -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL      destination ROI = source ROI
  pint(a, slot, lo, hi) / pdbl(a, slot)   clamped i64 / f64 parameters (pdbl: NaN / inf -> 0,
                                   clamped to +-1e6)
  load_row(w16, src, y, x0, x1, mode)     working pixels (4 x i16 premultiplied, full 16320)
                                   of (x0 .. x1-1, y); outside: edge pixels or 0 (FXL_ZERO);
                                   FXL_GAMMA: linear light
  var12(r), Kern::gauss(var12), Kern::boxk(h)   separable kernels (exact FIR for sigma <= 6,
                                   else a cascade of 3 boxes)
  sep_run(sep, io) -> 0 | ERR_*    separable convolution of a ROI in strips: H pass of the
                                   rows (clamped / loaded), V pass, io.emit per row
  disc_run(disc, io) -> 0 | ERR_*  sums over the paint.net disc of every ROI pixel (prefix
                                   sums per row, i32 or f32 accumulation)
  disc_edges(r) -> (E, area)       half widths of the disc rows
  bac_init(b, c) -> (tab, mode), bac_row, desat_row   paint.net 3 Brightness / Contrast
  blurbac(a, dst, r, b, c, f)      Gaussian blur then Brightness / Contrast of the ROI;
                                   f(dst, y, x0, row) finishes each output row

Exactness: every sum is an integer (running box sums, FIR dot products), so the result of
a pixel never depends on the ROI split; box means are rounded through f32
(rint(f32(S) * f32(1 / w))), FIR sums as (S + 8192) >> 14 saturated to i16.
```

```rust
FXL_GAMMA: u32 = 1  // linear light (RS_GAMMA)
FXL_ZERO: u32 = 2  // outside the image = transparent (default: clamp to the edge)
KT_COPY: u32 = 0
KT_FIR: u32 = 1
KT_BOX: u32 = 2
KN_MAXTAPS: usize = 255
KN_MAXBOX: usize = 8
DSF_F32: u32 = 1  // disc: accumulate the per-row sums in f32
```

- **`fn exp(x: f64) -> f64`**
  e^x: k = rint(x / ln 2), r = x - k ln2 (Cody-Waite), degree 12 Taylor  [fxc_exp]

- **`fn ln(x: f64) -> f64`**
  ln x: x = m 2^e, ln m = 2 atanh((m - 1) / (m + 1)); x &lt;= 0 or denormal -> -745  [fxc_ln]

- **`fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64`**
  x^y = exp(y ln x) for x > 0, else 0  [fxc_pow]

- **`fn roi(a: &FxArgs) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  the ROI clamped to the image (x0, y0 >= 0, x1 &lt;= w, y1 &lt;= h); None when empty  [fxc_roi]

- **`fn copy_roi(a: &FxArgs, dst: &mut Dst) -> i32`**
  destination ROI = source ROI  [fxc_copy_roi]

- **`fn dst_px<'d>(dst: &'d mut Dst, y: i32, x0: i32, n: i32) -> &'d mut [u8]`**
  the destination pixels x0 .. x0 + n of row y

- **`fn pint(a: &FxArgs, slot: usize, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> i32`**
  i64 parameter slot clamped to [lo, hi]  [fxc_pint]

- **`fn pdbl(a: &FxArgs, slot: usize) -> f64`**
  f64 parameter slot; NaN / infinite -> 0, clamped to -1e6 .. 1e6  [fxc_pdbl]

- **`fn load_row(dst: &mut [i16], src: &Surface, y: i32, x0: i32, x1: i32, mode: u32)`**
  w16 = working pixels of (x0 .. x1-1, y); outside columns / rows: the edge pixel (clamp)
  or 0 (mode & FXL_ZERO); mode & FXL_GAMMA: linear light  [fxc_load_row]

- **`fn var12(r: i32) -> i32`**
  paint.net-like blur radius -> 12 sigma^2 = 2 r (r + 2) (r &lt;= 0 -> 0)  [fxc_var12]

- **`struct Kern`**
  a separable 1-D kernel (KERN)
  - `typ: u32`
  - `halo: i32`
  - `n: i32` -- FIR taps (odd) / number of boxes
  - `w: [i16; 256]` -- FIR weights (+ a 0 pad tap)
  - `h: [i32; KN_MAXBOX]` -- box half widths

**`impl Kern`**

- **`fn copy() -> Kern`**
  the identity
- **`fn boxk(h: i32) -> Kern`**
  one box of width 2h + 1 (h &lt;= 0: identity)  [fxc_kern_box]
- **`fn gauss(var12: i32) -> Kern`**
  Gaussian with 12 sigma^2 = var12 (&lt;= 0: identity)  [fxc_kern_gauss]
  ```text
  FIR (var12 <= 432): h = ceil(sqrt(0.75 var12)) (1..18), g_i = exp(-6 i^2 / var12),
  sum = g_0 + 2 g_1 + ..., q_i = trunc(g_i (16384 / sum) + 0.5), the centre absorbs
  16384 - (q_0 + 2 sum q_i).  Boxes: wl = largest odd w with 3 w^2 <= var12 + 3,
  m = (2 num + den) / (2 den) (num = 3 wl^2 + 12 wl + 9 - var12, den = 4 wl + 4,
  m <= 3): m boxes of width wl, then 3 - m of wl + 2.
  ```

- **`struct Sep<'a>`**
  a separable run (SEP): source, job, kernels, the output ROI, loader mode
  - `src: &'a Surface`
  - `job: Option<&'a (dyn Cancel + Sync)>`
  - `kh: &'a Kern`
  - `kv: Option<&'a Kern>`
  - `x0: i32`
  - `y0: i32`
  - `x1: i32`
  - `y1: i32`
  - `mode: u32`
  - `custom_load: bool` -- io.load replaces fxc_load_row (rows are then not clamped to the image)

**`impl<'a> Sep<'a>`**

- **`fn new(a: &FxArgs<'a>, k: &'a Kern) -> Option<Sep<'a>>`**
  the standard run of an effect: source / job / ROI of a (None when the ROI is empty)
  [fxc_sep_init]

- **`trait SepIo`**
  the row source and sink of sep_run (SP_LOAD / SP_EMIT)
  - `fn load(&mut self, _sep: &Sep, _w16: &mut [i16], _y: i32, _x0: i32, _x1: i32)`
    a custom loader (when Sep::custom_load): w16 of (x0 .. x1-1, y)
  - `fn emit(&mut self, sep: &Sep, y: i32, row: &[i16])`
    output row y (columns sep.x0 .. sep.x1-1) as working pixels

- **`struct EmitArgb<'d, 'e>(pub &'d mut Dst<'e>)`**
  the standard emitter: working row -> straight ARGB in the destination  [fxc_emit_argb]

- **`fn sep_run(sep: &Sep, io: &mut impl SepIo) -> i32`**
  separable convolution of a ROI -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL  [fxc_sep_run]
  Strips of S rows: H pass for the rows sy0 - HY .. sy1 + HY (clamped rows computed once),
  then the V pass over a row table, then io.emit per row.

- **`fn disc_edges(r: i32) -> (Vec<i32>, i32)`**
  half widths of the disc rows E[0..r] (paint.net LocalHistogramEffect: largest u with
  u^2 + v^2 &lt;= ((2r+1)^2 + 2) / 4) and the area  [fxc_disc_edges]

- **`struct Disc<'a>`**
  a disc run (DSC)
  - `src: &'a Surface`
  - `job: Option<&'a (dyn Cancel + Sync)>`
  - `r: i32`
  - `flags: u32`
  - `x0: i32`
  - `y0: i32`
  - `x1: i32`
  - `y1: i32`
  - `mode: u32`
  - `area: i32` -- pixels in the disc (set by disc_run)
  - `custom_prep: bool` -- io.prep replaces the default row preparation

**`impl<'a> Disc<'a>`**

- **`fn new(a: &FxArgs<'a>, r: i32) -> Option<Disc<'a>>`**
  the standard run of an effect (None when the ROI is empty)  [fxc_disc_init]

- **`enum DiscRow<'r>`**
  the summed row of a disc run: i32 x 4 per pixel, or f32 x 4 with DSF_F32
  - `I(&'r mut [i32])`
  - `F(&'r mut [f32])`

- **`trait DiscIo`**
  the row source and sink of disc_run (DS_PREP / DS_EMIT)
  - `fn prep(&mut self, _d: &Disc, _v: &mut [i32], _y: i32, _x0: i32, _x1: i32)`
    custom preparation (Disc::custom_prep): i32 x 4 values of (x0 .. x1-1, y)
  - `fn emit(&mut self, d: &Disc, y: i32, row: DiscRow)`

- **`struct DiscArgb<'d, 'e>(pub &'d mut Dst<'e>)`**
  the standard emitter (i32 sums): W16 = rint(f32(sum) \* f32(1 / area)), then straight ARGB
  [fxc_disc_emit_argb]

- **`fn disc_run(d: &mut Disc, io: &mut impl DiscIo) -> i32`**
  disc sums of a ROI -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL  [fxc_disc_run]
  Per source row a prefix sum P (i32, wrapping) makes each disc row one difference
  P[x + e + 1] - P[x - e]; rows are clamped to the image; the rows are summed in i32 or (DSF_F32)
  in f32 in the order v = -r .. r.

- **`fn bac_init(b: i32, c: i32) -> ([i32; 256], u32)`**
  paint.net 3 BrightnessAndContrast as used inside Glow / Soften Portrait / Pencil / Ink:
  (tab, mode) -- mode 0 (div = 100) / 1: shift tables, mode 2 (contrast 100): threshold
  [fxc_bac_init]

- **`fn bac_row_inplace(row: &mut [u8], tab: &[i32; 256], mode: u32)`**
  apply bac_init's table to a straight ARGB row (dst may be src: pass the same slice twice
  through bac_row_inplace)  [fxc_bac_row]

- **`fn desat_row(dst: &mut [u8], src: &[u8])`**
  B = G = R = intensity, alpha kept  [fxc_desat_row]

- **`fn desat_inplace(row: &mut [u8])`**
  desat_row in place

- **`fn blurbac(a: &FxArgs, dst: &mut Dst, r: i32, b: i32, c: i32, mut f: impl FnMut(&mut Dst, i32, i32, &mut [u8])) -> i32`**
  the paint.net 3 chain "Gaussian blur (radius r) of the source, then Brightness /
  Contrast" for the ROI; f(dst, y, x0, row) receives the straight ARGB result of each row
  (columns x0 ..) and writes the destination itself -> 0 | ERR_\*  [fxc_blurbac]

- **`fn w16_of(p: u32) -> [i16; 4]`**
  working values of one straight pixel  (rs_to_work, no gamma)

### `fx/distort.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/distort.rs`](../lib/fx/distort.rs)

```text
distort -- effect group "distort" (Verzerren): Bulge, Crystalize, Dents, Frosted Glass,
Morphology, Pixelate, Polar Inversion, Tile Reflection, Twist           [src/fx/fx_distort.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

The warp effects are small mapping functions for the warp framework (warp.rs); Pixelate and
Morphology have their own loops.  Every pixel depends only on (source, parameters, aux).
  bulge          a = amount / 100, R = default radius: |p| < R: p (1 - a (1 - |p| / R)^2)
  twist          R = size * default radius, k = sign(amount) amount^2 / 100: p rotated by
                 k (1 - |p| / R)^3
  polar_inversion  p lerp(1, R^2 / |p|^2, amount)
  tile_reflection  (s, t) = p rotated by -angle, s += k tan(s pi / size) (t likewise), back
  dents          p + d (-sin a, cos a), a = theta * 4 octaves of perlin noise
  frosted_glass  samples moved by r ((1 - s) w + s n): w random point of the unit disc, n two
                 perlin fields
  crystalize     Voronoi cells of a jittered grid: the colour of the source pixel under the
                 nearest site
  pixelate       blocks filled with their premultiplied average (exact integers)
  morphology     max (dilate) / min (erode) / open / close of the premultiplied channels over
                 a circle / square / diamond (exact window maxima by doubling)
```

- **`static FXTAB: [FxDesc; 9]`**
  the group table  [fxtab_distort]

### `fx/lochist.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/lochist.rs`](../lib/fx/lochist.rs)

```text
lochist -- sliding local histograms for median / percentile / oil / surface style effects
                                                                        [src/fx/fx_lochist.s]

  lh_run(a, dst, r, shape, alpha0, f)    for every ROI pixel (x, y): the histograms (Hist) of
                                   the window around it (LHS_DISC = paint.net disc of radius
                                   r, LHS_SQUARE = (2r+1)^2), then dst(x, y) = f(hist)
  lh_run_oil(a, dst, r, shape, levels, f)  the same with pixels bucketed by intensity (Oil)
  lh_percentile(hist, ch, target)  smallest v with count(<= v) >= max(target, 1) (255 when
                                   fewer pixels)
  lh_rank(hist, ch, v)             pixels with value < v
  lh_edges(r, shape) -> (E, area)  half widths of the window rows

Window: pixels outside the image are not counted.  alpha0 (LHF_ALPHA0) keeps pixels with
alpha 0 out of the colour histograms (ncol counts the rest; the alpha histogram sees every
pixel, nall).  Oil: bucket = FastScale(I, levels), alpha-0 pixels count as transparent black.
Traversal: the histogram of the first ROI column slides down one row per ROI row, is
copied, then slides right along the row; every result depends on the window content only.
```

```rust
LHS_DISC: u32 = 0
LHS_SQUARE: u32 = 1
```

  - `nall: u32`
  - `ncol: u32`
  - `src: u32`

  the intensity buckets of a window (OIL): pixels per bucket, per bucket sum B\*A, G\*A, R\*A, A
  - `cnt: [u32; 256]`
  - `sum: [[u32; 4]; 256]`
  - `n: u32`
  - `src: u32`

### `fx/lut.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/lut.rs`](../lib/fx/lut.rs)

```text
lut -- shared helpers of the effect kernels: per-channel tables, intensity, sRGB, Levels
and spline tables, the x87 maths                                          [src/fx/fx_lut.s]

  lut_row(dst, src, lut)        per channel table lookup; lut = 4 x 256 bytes B, G, R, A
  lut_ident(lut)                four identity tables
  luma(argb) -> u32             paint.net intensity (7471 B + 38470 G + 19595 R) >> 16
  luma_row(dst8, src)           the intensity of every pixel as a byte
  pow / exp2 / log2 / cos / sin x87 maths (rt::x87; fx_pow, fx_exp2, fx_log2, fx_cos, fx_sin)
  srgb_dec(c) / srgb_enc(l)     sRGB 0..1 <-> linear 0..1 (IEC 61966-2-1, f64)
  lin_table(out)                f32[256]: srgb_dec(i / 255)
  srgb_table(out, n)            u8[n]: round(255 srgb_enc(i / (n - 1))), n >= 2
  levels_lut(lut, lvl)          paint.net UnaryPixelOps.Level as a 1024-byte lut
  spline_lut(lut, pts)          u8[256] from control points {x, y}: natural cubic spline
                                (the values of paint.net's Curves), ClampToByte

Levels, channel i (B, G, R) and input j: v = f32(j) - in_lo; v < 0 -> out_lo; j >= in_hi
-> out_hi; else trunc(clamp(out_lo + (out_hi - out_lo) pow(f64(f32(v / f32(in_hi -
in_lo))), f64(gamma)), 0, 255)).  A channel with in_hi <= in_lo is the identity; gamma is
clamped to 0.1 .. 10 (NaN -> 1).
```

Re-exports: `rt::x87::{cos, exp2, log2, pow, sin}`

```rust
FX_SPLINE_MAX: usize = 64
```

- **`fn lut_row(dst: &mut [u8], src: &[u8], lut: &[u8; 1024])`**
  dst[i] = {lut[B], lut[256 + G], lut[512 + R], lut[768 + A]}  [fx_lut_row]

- **`fn lut_ident(lut: &mut [u8])`**
  four identity tables  [fx_lut_ident]

- **`fn luma(c: u32) -> u32`**
  (7471 B + 38470 G + 19595 R) >> 16  [fx_luma]

- **`fn luma_row(dst: &mut [u8], src: &[u8])`**
  the intensity of every pixel  [fx_luma_row]

- **`fn srgb_dec(c: f64) -> f64`**
  c &lt;= 0.04045 ? c / 12.92 : ((c + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4  [fx_srgb_dec]

- **`fn srgb_enc(l: f64) -> f64`**
  l &lt;= 0.0031308 ? 12.92 l : 1.055 l^(1/2.4) - 0.055, clamped to 0..1  [fx_srgb_enc]

- **`fn lin_table(out: &mut [f32])`**
  f32[256] linear values of the sRGB bytes  [fx_lin_table]

- **`fn srgb_table(out: &mut [u8], n: usize)`**
  u8[n]: trunc(255 srgb_enc(i / (n - 1)) + 0.5)  [fx_srgb_table]

- **`struct Lvl`**
  the LVL record of levels_lut (channel order B, G, R)
  - `inlo: [u8; 4]`
  - `inhi: [u8; 4]`
  - `outlo: [u8; 4]`
  - `outhi: [u8; 4]`
  - `gamma: [f32; 3]`

- **`fn levels_lut(lut: &mut [u8; 1024], lvl: &Lvl)`**
  paint.net UnaryPixelOps.Level as a 1024-byte lut (alpha identity)  [fx_levels_lut]

- **`fn spline_lut(lut: &mut [u8], pts: &[u8], n: usize)`**
  u8[256] from up to FX_SPLINE_MAX control points {x, y} (pts = 2 n bytes, any order, a
  repeated x: the last wins); n = 0: identity, n = 1: constant  [fx_spline_lut]

```text
noise -- effect group "noise" (Rauschen): add_noise, reduce_noise         [src/fx/fx_noise.s]

  add_noise     intensity (0..100), colour saturation (0..400), coverage (0..100), seed:
                paint.net 3's Add Noise with per-pixel hashes h_k = hash32(x, y, seed, k):
                changed when h_0 mod 100 < coverage; n_k = ((sum of the 4 bytes of h_k) -
                510) * 1774 >> 8 for R (1), G (2), B (3); i = (4899 r + 9618 g + 1867 b) >> 14,

                channel' = clamp(channel + ((c dev + 32768) >> 16)); alpha kept
  reduce_noise  radius (0..200), strength (0..1): per channel the median m of the disc,
                f = strength (1 - 0.75 I), v' = trunc(clamp(v + f (m - v), 0, 255))
```

### `fx/perlin.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/perlin.rs`](../lib/fx/perlin.rs)

```text
perlin -- deterministic 2-D gradient noise for the fx kernels (Clouds, Turbulence, Dents,
Frosted Glass)                                                            [src/fx/fx_perlin.s]

  perlin(x, y, seed, stream) -> f64        gradient noise, about -1 .. 1
  perlin_row(rec, acc)                     acc[j] += amp * noise(x_j, y) along a row

Improved Perlin noise (quintic fade 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3) on the integer lattice; the gradient
of lattice point (ix, iy) is G[h & 15], h = hash32(ix, iy, seed, stream), G_k = sqrt(2)
(cos, sin)(2 pi (k + 0.5) / 16).  g00 = G00.x fx + G00.y fy, g10 = G10.x (fx - 1) + G10.y fy,
g01 = G01.x fx + G01.y (fy - 1), g11 = G11.x (fx - 1) + G11.y (fy - 1); a = g00 + u (g10 -
g00), b = g01 + u (g11 - g01), noise = a + v (b - a), u / v = fade(fx / fy) computed as
((((f 6) - 15) f + 10) f) f f.  Coordinates are clamped to +-2^30; fixed operation order:
perlin and perlin_row give bit-identical values.
```

- **`fn perlin(x: f64, y: f64, seed: u32, stream: u32) -> f64`**
  gradient noise at (x, y)  [fxn_perlin]

- **`struct PerlinRow`**
  a row of noise samples (PERLIN_ROW): x_j = (x0 + j step) \* inv + ofsx
  - `n: usize`
  - `x0: i32`
  - `step: i32`
  - `abs: bool`
  - `seed: u32`
  - `stream: u32`
  - `inv: f64`
  - `ofsx: f64`
  - `y: f64`
  - `amp: f64`

- **`fn perlin_row(r: &PerlinRow, acc: &mut [f64])`**
  acc[j] += amp \* noise(x_j, y) (|noise| when abs); the lattice gradients are reused while
  consecutive x_j stay in one cell  [fxn_perlin_row]

### `fx/render.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/render.rs`](../lib/fx/render.rs)

```text
render -- effect group "render" (Rendern): Clouds, Julia Fractal, Mandelbrot Fractal,
Turbulence                                                                [src/fx/fx_render.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

All four are per-pixel functions of (x, y, image size, parameters).
  clouds      paint.net 3.x algorithm, own lattice noise: dx = 2x - w, dy = 2y - h; octaves
              i = 0, 1, ... while i < 12, amp > 0.03 and div > 0 (amp = power^i, div = scale
              >> i): val += perlin(dx / div + ox_i, dy / div + oy_i, seed, i) amp;
              t = clamp((val + 1) / 2, 0, 1)
  turbulence  octaves i < detail while div > 0, amp = roughness^i; val = sum |perlin| amp;
              t = clamp(2 val / sum amp, 0, 1)
              Colour = round(c1 + (c2 - c1) t) per channel (f32), blended over the source
              with the blend mode (gfx::blendmode)
  julia_fractal / mandelbrot_fractal  paint.net 3.x algorithms, count samples per pixel,
              escape iteration per sample (the asm runs 6 / 12 packed lanes; every sample
              does the same IEEE operations), colour schemes classic / grayscale / palette /
              rainbow, channel sums divided by count (truncating)
```

### `fx/stylize.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/stylize.rs`](../lib/fx/stylize.rs)

```text
stylize -- Stilisieren: Edge Detect, Emboss, Outline, Relief           [src/fx/fx_stylize.s]

  FXTAB            the group table

Edge Detect, Emboss and Relief are paint.net 3.x ColorDifferenceEffect kernels: a 3 x 3
weight matrix rotated by the angle (r = angle * 2 * pi / 360, dr = pi / 4):
      cos(r + dr)  cos(r + 2dr)  cos(r + 3dr)
      cos(r)       CENTER        cos(r + 4dr)
      cos(r - dr)  cos(r - 2dr)  cos(r - 3dr)
Weights are quantised to wq = floor(w * 16384 + 0.5) (integer sums, bit-exact, tile
independent); taps outside the image count as 0.  Per channel v = trunc(sum wq * c / 16384)
(towards zero) + OFFSET, clamped to 0..255; alpha = the centre pixel's alpha.
  edge_detect  CENTER 0, OFFSET 128, channels B, G, R        (angle default 45)
  relief       CENTER 1, OFFSET 0, channels B, G, R          (angle default 45)
  emboss       CENTER 0, OFFSET 128, on the intensity, output B = G = R = v (angle default 0)
  outline      paint.net 3.x OutlineEffect (hist::lochist): per channel over the circle of
               radius `thickness`: skip empty bins, count up to area (100 - intensity) / 200
               -> c1, on up to area (100 + intensity) / 200 -> c2, c = 255 - (c2 - c1);
               alpha = a2 (the alpha scan skips on the BLUE histogram like paint.net)
```

- **`static FXTAB: [FxDesc; 4]`**
  the group table  [fxtab_stylize]

### `fx/warp.rs`

Source: [`lib/fx/warp.rs`](../lib/fx/warp.rs)

```text
warp -- warp framework of the distort effects: inverse mapping per destination pixel, n x n
supersampling, bilinear sampling in premultiplied space, edge behaviour; the f64 maths the
fx kernels share                                                          [src/fx/fx_warp.s]

  prepare(a) -> aux                bounds for centre / radius (the selection's bounding box)
  Warp::new(a)                     the WARP record of a render call (fxw_init)
  wr.center(x, y)                  centre from an FP_PAN pair (fxw_center)
  wr.run(a, dst, map) -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL      render the ROI through map (fxw_run)
  sincos(x) -> (sin, cos)          f64, |x| <= 1e9 (fdlibm kernels)        [fxm_sincos]
  log(x)                           f64 ln, x clamped to [DBL_MIN, DBL_MAX]   [fxm_log]

Coordinates: pixel (x, y) is the POINT (x, y) (pixel centres at integers); the image covers
[-0.5, w - 0.5) x [-0.5, h - 0.5).  For every destination pixel of the ROI run takes n x n
sample points p = (x - cx + ox_i, y - cy + oy_i) relative to the centre (paint.net's rotated
grid: oy_i = (i + 1) / (n*n + 1) - 0.5, ox_i = frac(n (i + 1) / (n*n + 1)) - 0.5; n = 1:
one sample at the centre) and calls map(wr, cur, pt) -> identity?  pt = the point relative to
the centre on entry, the SOURCE point on return (identity: the sample is the pixel's own
source pixel, exactly).  A source point is sampled bilinearly from the 2 x 2 pixels around it
with f32 weights, alpha-weighted (each tap contributes w (c a, a)); taps outside the image
follow the edge mode (CLAMP / WRAP / REFLECT per tap; PRIMARY / SECONDARY / TRANSPARENT /
ORIGINAL replace a sample outside the image area by that colour).  The pixel = sum of its
samples: a = round(S_a / (n n)), c = round(S_c / S_a); a = 0 -> 0.  Pixels farther than
rin + 0.75 from the centre (rin > 0) are copied unchanged.
```

```rust
FXW_CLAMP: i32 = 0  // clamp taps to the image
FXW_WRAP: i32 = 1  // tile the image
FXW_REFLECT: i32 = 2  // mirror (period 2n, edge pixels repeated)
FXW_PRIMARY: i32 = 3  // samples outside the image = col1
FXW_SECONDARY: i32 = 4  // samples outside the image = col2
FXW_TRANSPARENT: i32 = 5  // samples outside the image = transparent
FXW_ORIGINAL: i32 = 6  // samples outside the image = the destination's own pixel
FXW_NEDGE: i32 = 7
```

- **`struct Bounds(pub [i32; 4])`**
  the aux of prepare: the bounds x0, y0, x1, y1

- **`fn prepare(a: &FxArgs) -> Result<Option<Aux>, i32>`**
  the bounding box of the selection (clipped to the image) or the whole image  [fxw_prepare]

- **`struct Warp<'a>`**
  the WARP record of one render call
  - `src: &'a Surface`
  - `w: i32`
  - `h: i32`
  - `x0: i32`
  - `y0: i32`
  - `x1: i32`
  - `y1: i32`
  - `job: Option<&'a (dyn Cancel + Sync)>`
  - `q: i32` -- quality 1..5: n x n samples per pixel
  - `edge: i32`
  - `col1: u32`
  - `col2: u32`
  - `cx: f64`
  - `cy: f64`
  - `rin: f64` -- radius of influence (0 = map every pixel)
  - `rdef: f64` -- default radius = min(bounds w, h) / 2
  - `bx0: i32`
  - `by0: i32`
  - `bx1: i32`
  - `by1: i32`
  - `p: [f64; 16]` -- effect parameters (WR_P)
  - `seed: u32`

- **`struct Cur`**
  the pixel and sample a map function is called for (WR_CURX / CURY / CURS)
  - `x: i32`
  - `y: i32`
  - `s: i32`

**`impl<'a> Warp<'a>`**

- **`fn new(a: &FxArgs<'a>) -> Warp<'a>`**
  the record from the arguments: ROI clipped to the image, bounds (aux of prepare or the
  image), rdef, centre of the bounds, q = 1, edge CLAMP, rin = 0  [fxw_init]
- **`fn center(&mut self, x: f64, y: f64)`**
  centre from an FP_PAN value (-1 = left / top edge of the bounds, 1 = right / bottom;
  clamped to -2 .. 2): cx = bx0 - 0.5 + bw (1 + x) / 2  [fxw_center]
- **`fn run(&mut self, dst: &mut Dst, mut map: impl FnMut(&Warp, Cur, &mut [f64; 2]) -> bool) -> i32`**
  render the ROI through map -> 0 | ERR_CANCEL  [fxw_run]

- **`fn sincos(x: f64) -> (f64, f64)`**
  (sin x, cos x): k = rint(x 2/pi), Cody-Waite reduction, fdlibm kernels; x clamped to
  +-1e9 (NaN -> 0)  [fxm_sincos]

- **`fn log(x: f64) -> f64`**
  ln x (fdlibm e_log.c); x clamped to [DBL_MIN, DBL_MAX] (NaN, 0, negatives -> ln DBL_MIN)
  [fxm_log]

## plat

*the platform layer: process, files, threads, windows (Windows and Linux)* -- crate root [`lib/plat/lib.rs`](../lib/plat/lib.rs)

```text
plat -- the platform layer: one module per OS with the same functions  [src/plat]

  process: entry point (calls the app's jfgui_main), args(), arg_value(name), exit(code),
           write_stdout / write_stderr, time_us(), sleep_ms(ms), date()
  environment: env(name) (= getenv), setenv(name, Some / None), config_dir(), temp_dir(), cwd()
  folders: user_dir(DIR_DOCUMENTS ..) (desktop, documents, downloads, pictures, music,
           videos: Known Folders / XDG user dirs), log_dir()                  (dirs.rs)
  files:   read_file(path), write_file(path, data) (native: exclusive sibling + rename),
           File::open(path, FO_*) / open_temp(dir) -> read_at / write_at / size / sync,
           file_exists(path) (0 / 1 file / 2 dir), mkdir (with parents), delete, rename,
           trash (into the recycle bin / freedesktop trash; trash.rs),
           file_exists_checked(path) (Some(0) missing, None error), FileLock::acquire(path),
           AtomicFile::create(path) -> write_at / commit (write_file in pieces),
           dir_list(path, f(name, is_dir, size_lo)) -- checked against the app's
           permissions first (guarded.rs); a refused path behaves like a missing one
  policy:  the app's permissions (apps/NAME/PERMISSIONS): install, the fs / process /
           url / plugin / print checks, grants for the user's files      (policy.rs)
  boot:    the app's name, app:// and its manifest at start-up (rt::main! through
           rt::boot; ui::main! calls the parts itself)                    (boot.rs)
  vfs:     "scheme://path" names in every file function: app:// (the bundled assets),
           config:// data:// cache:// logs:// (the app's folders), documents:// and the
           other user folders, mem://, mounted providers
           (MemFs, DirFs, Overlay, Sub, Bundle); data_dir(), cache_dir()   (vfs.rs);
           display_name(path); Android content:// (ContentFs, DocHost)     (content.rs);
           persistent_name(path): a chosen file's name that lasts across restarts (Flatpak's
           documents portal: linux_docs.rs)
  secret:  secret_set / secret_get / secret_delete / secret_available: passwords, tokens and
           keys in the system's store (Credential Manager + DPAPI, Secret Service; needs
           `secrets` in the manifest)                                        (secret.rs)
  instance: claim(app) -> Primary / Forwarded / Alone, take() -> requests of later starts
           (the app's single instance; pipe / abstract socket per user)  (instance.rs)
  spell:   sys_spell_find / sys_spell_languages, SysSpeller (check, suggest): the system's
           spell checker (Windows ISpellChecker; elsewhere none)          (spell.rs)
  tray:    tray_set / tray_remove (the symbol in the notification area, its menu), notify /
           notify_close (system notifications), tray_take() -> events   (tray.rs)
  power:   inhibit(reason, INHIBIT_SUSPEND | INHIBIT_IDLE) -> Option<Inhibit> (no standby /
           screen saver while the guard lives), inhibited()              (power.rs)
  autostart: autostart_set(on, args) / autostart_get() / autostart_entry() (Run key, XDG
           autostart, Background portal, MSIX StartupTask; needs `autostart` in the manifest)
           (autostart.rs)
  pkg:     packaged() (MSIX, Flatpak, AppImage, Snap or a plain program), msix_updates (App
           Installer), FlatpakMonitor / flatpak_spawn_latest (the Flatpak portal),
           restart_appimage                                                   (pkg.rs)
  taskbar: taskbar_progress / taskbar_badge / taskbar_tasks (the taskbar button: progress,
           overlay / count, jump list; ITaskbarList3, Unity LauncherEntry), app_user_model_id
           / set_app_user_model_id (Windows: the app's explicit id)        (taskbar.rs)
  assoc:   assoc_register / assoc_conflicts / assoc_unregister: the app's PACKAGE file types
           and URL schemes for this program without a setup (HKCU\Software\Classes; .desktop,
           shared-mime-info, mimeapps.list), file_uri_path                    (assoc.rs)
  recent:  recent_add / recent_list / recent_remove / recent_clear: the system's recent files
           (SHAddToRecentDocs and the jump list; recently-used.xbel)          (recent.rs)
  audio:   Stream (open / open_fill, write, start / pause / stop, volume, latency, the default
           device followed), play / play_file (WAV, Ogg Vorbis), sound(SOUND_*): the system's
           sounds (WASAPI, PulseAudio protocol, WebAudio, AAudio)               (audio.rs)
  screen:  monitors() (rect, work area, dpi, refresh, primary; SET_MONITORS), pick_start (a
           pixel's colour anywhere), capture_start (pictures of the screen)  (screen.rs)
  hotkey:  hotkey_register / hotkey_unregister / hotkey_take: global shortcuts (RegisterHotKey,
           XGrabKey, the GlobalShortcuts portal)                             (hotkey.rs)
  threads: thread_spawn(stack, f) -> Thread (join), thread_yield(), Sem (post / wait),
           wake() (any thread: E_WAKE on the UI thread), wait_events(deadline, on_event)
           (headless), cpu_count(), mem_total()
  pool:    thr_init / thr_count / thr_shutdown / thr_self, parallel_for, Job   (pool.rs)
  task:    async execution: Executor (ui() in the event loop, new() / block_on), Task,
           spawn_blocking (a pool for blocking work), sleep, CancelToken, Progress, join /
           select                                                            (task.rs)
  aio:     files without blocking: read_file / write_file / copy_file with progress and
           cancellation, Reader / Writer chunk by chunk (AtomicFile underneath)  (aio.rs)
  sync:    Mutex, Condvar, RwLock, channel (futex / WaitOnAddress)          (sync.rs)
  rand:    fill_random, random_bytes, random_u64 (the OS CSPRNG)             (rand.rs)
  net:     TcpListener, TcpStream, UdpSocket, SocketAddr, resolve            (net.rs)
  fs:      stat / lstat / read_dir / links / set_times / free_space /
           write_file_private / local_zone_id                                (fs.rs)
  cpu:     cpu_features() (CPU_*), cpu_brand()                                 (cpu.rs)
  crash:   crash_hook(Some(f)): f(&CrashInfo) before exit code 3 -- hardware faults (VEH /
           signals, the stderr line of ASMLIB) and panics; crash_test() crashes on purpose
  windows: the window-indexed API of the assembly (win_create / win_show / win_present /
           wait ..., popups, clipboard, drops, pen, cursors; consts.rs, evq.rs, pwin0.rs)
  dnd:     drag and drop between programs: DragData (files, text, URLs, HTML, image),
           the drop target hook, the pending drop, drag_start (dragging out)    (dnd.rs)
  (plat-shared) print(job) + page layout / PDF writer (print.rs; win_print.rs,
           linux_print.rs), plugin libraries lib_open / lib_sym / lib_close / lib_seg and
           the crash guard guard_call / guard_run / guard_tag (plib.rs; win_lib.rs,
           linux_elfload.rs, linux_guard.rs), monitor_icc / monitor_key (icc.rs), the
           portal's file dialog / OpenURI / Print (linux_portal.rs)
  (jxl-module) the loadable JPEG XL writer module: jxlenc_set_path / jxlenc_ready /
           jxlenc_encode (modhost.rs; the records in modabi.rs)

The layer knows events, pixel rows, files and threads only -- no UI, no gfx.  One of the
four crates that may contain `unsafe` (rt, simd, plat, plugin); nothing unsafe leaves it.
```

- **`fn persistent_name(name: &str) -> String`**
  The name under which a file the user chose stays reachable after a restart, for a list of
  recent files or a session (ui.recent_add keeps this one).  A document of Flatpak's
  documents portal (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/doc/ID/NAME`) is asked for its lasting form
  (`Documents.Add`, persistent; linux_docs.rs): `<mount>/<ID>/<NAME>` of the portal's answer.
  Where the portal reaches the real file that is a lasting document of it; for a document
  of its own mount the portal answers that document's own ID, so inside the sandbox the name
  stays as the dialog gave it (the portal's file dialog makes lasting documents, "Open with"
  session ones).  Every other name comes back unchanged: Android keeps the grant of a
  `content://` document and the browser the handle of a `/handles/` file when the user
  chooses it, and OS paths need nothing.  The name must be readable under the app's
  permissions.

### `plat/process.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/process.rs`](../lib/plat/process.rs)

```text
Native child processes for tools and application helpers; no assembly counterpart.
run_elevated / elevated: a program with administrator or root rights (a service install).
```

- **`struct Command<'a>`**
  Shell-free child invocation. Environment entries override inherited values.
  - `program: &'a str` -- Executable path, or a program found in PATH.
  - `args: &'a [&'a str]` -- Arguments excluding argv[0]; empty arguments are preserved.
  - `cwd: Option<&'a str>` -- Child working directory, or None to inherit.
  - `env: &'a [(&'a str, Option<&'a str>)]` -- Environment overrides; None removes a variable.

- **`fn run_elevated(program: &str, args: &[&str]) -> Result<i32, String>`**
  Run a program with administrator / root rights and wait for it -> its exit code.  Windows:
  the UAC prompt (ShellExecuteEx "runas", hidden window, no pipes); Linux: directly when this
  process is root, otherwise through pkexec (the desktop's password prompt).  Err when the
  user refused or no way exists (the text says what to do).

- **`fn elevated() -> bool`**
  Whether this process runs with administrator (Windows) / root (Linux) rights.

- **`fn exec(program: &str, args: &[&str], env: &[(&str, Option<&str>)]) -> u32`**
  Replace this process by a program, keeping its PID, its terminal and its standard handles
  (Linux: execve; argv[0] = program, a name without '/' is looked up in PATH, the environment
  of this process with the overrides of env as in Command, SIGPIPE back to its default).
  Returns only on failure: the error number (refused by the manifest: EACCES).  Windows has
  no such call: 50 (ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED).  The AppImage runtime (apps/appimagert) starts the
  AppRun of the image with it.

**`impl Command<'_>`**

- **`fn spawn(&self) -> Result<Child, u32>`**
  Start a hidden process with pipes. Dropping its handle terminates its tree.

### `plat/sync.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/sync.rs`](../lib/plat/sync.rs)

```text
sync -- blocking primitives for worker threads (servers, background jobs)

  Mutex<T> (lock / try_lock -> MutexGuard)     Condvar (wait / wait_timeout / notify_*)
  RwLock<T> (read / write; writers first)      channel(cap) -> (Sender<T>, Receiver<T>)

One primitive per OS: wait on a 32-bit word while it holds a value, wake one / all waiters
(Windows WaitOnAddress, Linux private futexes).  Mutex and Condvar are the futex algorithms
of Rust's std; RwLock and the channel are built on them.  A lock is not poisoned by a panic
(panics abort the process here).
Not here: rt::SpinLock (rt keeps spin locks for the allocator and for modules, where plat is
replaced).
```

- **`struct Mutex<T: ?Sized>`**
  a mutual-exclusion lock around a value

**`impl<T> Mutex<T>`**

- **`const fn new(v: T) -> Mutex<T>`**

**`impl<T: ?Sized> Mutex<T>`**

  the value without locking (the borrow proves exclusivity)

- **`struct MutexGuard<'a, T: ?Sized>`**
  the locked value; unlocks when dropped

**`impl Condvar`**

- **`fn wait_while<'a, T: ?Sized>(&self, mut g: MutexGuard<'a, T>, mut cond: impl FnMut(&mut T) -> bool) -> MutexGuard<'a, T>`**

### `plat/net.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/net.rs`](../lib/plat/net.rs)

```text
net -- TCP, UDP and Unix domain sockets (IPv4 and IPv6) with timeouts

  IpAddr / SocketAddr: parse ("10.0.0.5:9443", "[::1]:80"), Display, loopback / unspecified
  TcpListener::bind(&addr) / accept() / accept_timeout(ms) / local_addr()
  TcpStream::connect(&addr, timeout_ms) / read / write / write_all / read_exact,
            set_read_timeout / set_write_timeout (ms, None = block), set_nodelay,
            shutdown_write, peer_addr / local_addr, wait_readable(ms)
  UdpSocket::bind / send_to / recv_from(buf, timeout_ms)
  UnixListener::bind(path) / accept() / accept_timeout(ms); connect_unix(path, timeout_ms)
            -> UnixStream (the stream calls of TcpStream; addresses and nodelay do not apply)
            Linux, and Windows 10 1803 and later (AF_UNIX)
  resolve(host, port): numeric addresses, "localhost"; Windows also the system resolver
            (GetAddrInfoW).  Linux names go through netio::dns (no libc here).
  NetError: the kinds callers act on, with the OS code

The app's permissions (policy.rs, net.connect / net.listen) are checked before connect,
bind, send_to and a name lookup; Unix sockets follow the file rules (fs.write on the path).
A refusal is NetErrorKind::Denied.

Timeouts are readiness waits (WSAPoll / poll) before each call, never SO_RCVTIMEO: after a
timed-out blocking receive Windows leaves the connection in an undefined state.  Sockets are
not inherited by child processes; sends never raise SIGPIPE.  Every method takes &self, so
one thread may read while another writes (Arc<TcpStream>).
```

- **`enum IpAddr`**
  - `V4([u8; 4])`
  - `V6([u8; 16])`

### `plat/fs.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/fs.rs`](../lib/plat/fs.rs)

```text
fs -- file system access for backup and restore

  stat(path) / lstat(path) -> Option<Meta>     kind, size, times (ns), mode / attributes,
                                                owner, device and file id, link count
  read_dir(path) -> Option<Vec<DirEntry>>      names and kinds ("." / ".." left out)
  read_link / symlink(target, link, dir) / hard_link(existing, new)
  set_times(path, atime_ns, mtime_ns)          on the link itself, never its target
  set_mode(path, mode) (Linux) / set_attrs(path, attrs) (Windows) / set_owner (Linux)
  free_space(path) -> Option<(free, total)>    sync_dir(dir) (Linux: fsync of the directory)
  write_file_private(path, data)               owner-only file (0600 / protected DACL),
                                               fsync, atomic rename, directory sync
  mkdir_private(path)                          owner-only directory (with parents)
  local_zone_id() -> "Europe/Berlin" | "win:W. Europe Standard Time"
  long_path(path) (Windows): the \\?\ form every call here uses

Windows: reparse points count as links only for symbolic links and junctions; other tags
(deduplication, cloud placeholders) are ordinary files whose data is read.  Files are
opened with backup semantics (directories, and backup privileges when the process holds
them).

vfs names ("scheme://path", vfs.rs) work too: a folder mount's name is its OS path (and
checked as one); mem://, bundles, ZIP archives and other mounts answer from the provider
(stat: kind, size, times; read_dir; set_times; write_file_private / mkdir_private as
write / mkdir).  They have no links (read_link None, symlink / hard_link false), owners,
modes or free space.
```

- **`enum FileKind`**
  what a directory entry is
  - `File`
  - `Dir`
  - `Symlink` -- a symbolic link (Windows: also a junction)
  - `Other` -- devices, pipes, sockets

- **`struct Meta`**
  the metadata of a file
  - `kind: Option<FileKind>`
  - `size: u64`
  - `mtime_ns: i64` -- nanoseconds since 1970
  - `atime_ns: i64`
  - `ctime_ns: i64` -- Linux: status change; Windows: creation
  - `mode: u32` -- Linux: st_mode (type and permission bits); Windows: 0
  - `uid: u32`
  - `gid: u32`
  - `attrs: u32` -- Windows: FILE_ATTRIBUTE_\*; Linux: 0
  - `dev: u64` -- device (Windows: volume serial number) and file id (inode / file index)
  - `ino: u64`
  - `nlink: u32`

**`impl Meta`**

- **`fn is_dir(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn is_file(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn is_symlink(&self) -> bool`**

- **`struct DirEntry`**
  - `name: String`
  - `kind: FileKind`

- **`fn join(dir: &str, name: &str) -> String`**
  "a/b" + "c" with the platform separator

- **`fn parent(path: &str) -> &str`**
  the parent directory of a path ("" for a bare name)

- **`fn stat(path: &str) -> Option<Meta>`**
  the metadata of path, links followed; a vfs name: its folder mount's file, else the
  provider's kind, size and times (mtime also as ctime; Linux modes 0644 / 0755)

- **`fn lstat(path: &str) -> Option<Meta>`**
  the metadata of path itself (a link is not followed); mounts without OS files have no links

- **`fn read_dir(path: &str) -> Option<Vec<DirEntry>>`**
  the entries of a folder ("." / ".." left out)

- **`fn read_link(path: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  the target of a symbolic link (Windows: also a junction)

- **`fn symlink(target: &str, link: &str, dir: bool) -> bool`**
  a symbolic link at link to target (dir: a folder's link on Windows); a vfs name as target
  stands for its OS path.  Only on OS paths and folder mounts.

- **`fn hard_link(existing: &str, new: &str) -> bool`**
  a second name new for the file existing (both OS paths or folder mounts)

- **`fn set_times(path: &str, atime_ns: i64, mtime_ns: i64) -> bool`**
  access and modification times (ns since 1970), on a link itself, never its target; a
  mount: its provider's times (MemFs keeps them; bundles and ZIP archives are read-only)

- **`fn set_mode(path: &str, mode: u32) -> bool`**
  permission bits (07777; Windows: nothing to do); a mount without OS files has none

- **`fn set_attrs(path: &str, attrs: u32) -> bool`**
  FILE_ATTRIBUTE_\* (read-only, hidden, system, archive ...; Linux: nothing to do)

- **`fn set_owner(path: &str, uid: u32, gid: u32) -> bool`**
  owner and group (Linux; Windows: nothing to do)

- **`fn free_space(path: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64)>`**
  (free, total) bytes of the volume of path; None for mounts without OS files

- **`fn sync_dir(dir: &str) -> bool`**
  make a folder's changes durable (Linux: fsync of the directory); a mount without OS files:
  whether the folder exists

- **`fn write_file_private(path: &str, data: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  an owner-only file (0600 / protected DACL), synced and renamed into place; a mount without
  OS files: its write (memory of this process)

- **`fn mkdir_private(path: &str) -> bool`**
  an owner-only folder (with parents)

```text
service -- programs that run as a system service

      Windows: started by the service control manager, run() runs while the service reports

      administrator / root rights; the errors say so.
```

### `plat/watch.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/watch.rs`](../lib/plat/watch.rs)

```text
watch -- changes below folders, as they happen (continuous data protection)

  Watcher::new(&roots) -> Result<Watcher, String>   recursive; one thread watches
  watcher.take(wait_ms) -> Changes                   the paths changed since the last take
                                                     (waits up to wait_ms for the first);
                                                     overflow: events were lost, rescan
  dropping the watcher stops it

Windows: ReadDirectoryChangesW per root (subtree, overlapped, 64 KiB buffer; an empty
answer means the buffer overflowed).  Linux: inotify with a watch per folder; new folders
are added (and reported whole), a full queue or the watch limit reports an overflow.
Paths are absolute, in the form of the platform; the folder of a change is enough for a
caller that walks the tree again.
```

- **`struct Changes`**
  what changed since the last take
  - `paths: Vec<String>`
  - `overflow: bool` -- events were lost: everything below the roots may have changed

- **`struct Watcher`**

**`impl Watcher`**

- **`fn new(roots: &[String]) -> Result<Watcher, String>`**
- **`fn take(&self, wait_ms: u32) -> Changes`**
  the changes so far (waiting up to wait_ms when there are none yet)

### `plat/capabilities.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/capabilities.rs`](../lib/plat/capabilities.rs)

```text
Platform service availability, shared by app commands, agent schemas and browser hosts.
```

```rust
/// Read files through the platform's file namespace.
CAP_FILE_READ: u64 = 1 << 0
/// Write files through the platform's file namespace.
CAP_FILE_WRITE: u64 = 1 << 1
/// Confirm durable storage, rather than a temporary in-memory write.
CAP_PERSISTENT_STORAGE: u64 = 1 << 2
/// Exchange plain UTF-8 clipboard text.
CAP_CLIPBOARD_TEXT: u64 = 1 << 3
/// Exchange native/RTF/HTML rich clipboard representations.
/// Browser hosts provide an instance-local clipboard, without OS rich-format access.
CAP_CLIPBOARD_RICH: u64 = 1 << 4
/// Exchange clipboard images.
CAP_CLIPBOARD_IMAGE: u64 = 1 << 5
/// Submit a print job through the host.
CAP_PRINT: u64 = 1 << 6
/// Discover fonts installed in the operating system.
CAP_SYSTEM_FONTS: u64 = 1 << 7
/// Load native shared libraries with the platform plugin ABI.
CAP_NATIVE_PLUGINS: u64 = 1 << 8
/// Connect through a user-local IPC transport after explicit activation.
CAP_LOCAL_IPC: u64 = 1 << 9
/// Display windows, including library windows inside a browser canvas.
CAP_WINDOWING: u64 = 1 << 10
/// Run parallel operating-system threads.
CAP_THREADS: u64 = 1 << 11
/// Install operating-system shortcuts or integrations.
CAP_SHELL_INTEGRATION: u64 = 1 << 12
```

- **`struct Capabilities`**
  Snapshot of services actually provided by the current host.
  - `available: u64` -- Bit set of the `CAP_*` services.

**`impl Capabilities`**

- **`const fn supports(self, required: u64) -> bool`**
  Whether every requested service is available.
- **`fn unavailable_reason(self, required: u64) -> Option<&'static str>`**
  A concrete explanation for the first missing service, or no limitation.

- **`fn capabilities() -> Capabilities`**
  Current native service set, less what the app's permissions leave out (policy.rs).
  Browser permissions are supplied by its host adapter.

### `plat/policy.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/policy.rs`](../lib/plat/policy.rs)

```text
policy -- the app's permissions (apps/NAME/PERMISSIONS, docs/PERMISSIONS.md): parsed once at
start-up, then checked by the public file, process, shell, plugin and print functions

  install(text) -> Result<Key, String>   parse and activate a manifest (once per process);
                                         before that, and in apps without one, all is allowed
  active() -> bool
  fs_allowed(path, FS_READ | FS_WRITE) / process_allowed(program) / url_allowed(url) /
  plugin_allowed(path) / print_allowed() / secrets_allowed(service) / autostart_allowed() /
  audio_allowed()                        -> bool
  input_global_allowed() / screen_capture_allowed()
                                         -> bool
                                         a refusal is recorded (denials) and printed once
                                         per target to stderr: "PERMDENY kind target"
  audio_granted() -> bool                sound is allowed now, without asking or recording a
                                         refusal (ui's dialog sounds stay silent without it)
  net_connect_allowed(addr) / net_listen_allowed(addr) / net_name_allowed(host) -> bool
  net_resolved(host, addrs)              (resolvers) the addresses of a permitted name:
                                         connections to them follow that name's rules
  Key::grant(path, FS_*) / Key::grant_dir(dir, FS_*)   a file / folder the user handed over
                                         (file dialog, drop, command line); needs fs.user
  Key::trusted(f)                        f runs on this thread without the file checks (the
                                         library's own file dialog and test scripts)
  denials() -> Vec<Denial>               the last DENIALS_MAX refusals (audit)
  normalize(path) -> Option<String>      absolute, '/' separators, no "." / ".." / empty
                                         segments; Windows: upper-case drive letter, no
                                         device, stream or reserved names; Linux: no ".."
                                         at all (the kernel applies it after symbolic
                                         links); None = refused
  normalize_for(path, windows, cwd)      the same rules for either OS (tests, tools)
  font_dirs() -> [folder]                the system font folders in scan order (fontdb)
  cap_mask() -> CAP_* bits               what the policy leaves of capabilities()

Questions to the user ("ask" lines; one decision per line):
  questions() -> Vec<Question>           what waits for the user's answer (the UI shows it)
  Key::ask_here(on)                      this thread (the UI's) asks: an access on it is
                                         refused while its question is open (Verdict::
                                         Pending; the UI tells the app when it was answered),
                                         other threads wait up to Key::set_wait ms (env
                                         jfgui_PERM_TIMEOUT, WAIT_MS) and are refused then.
                                         Nobody asks (headless runs, console programs): refused
  Key::answer(id, Answer)                Once / Deny: until the program ends; Always / Never:
                                         also stored (Key::set_store, env jfgui_PERM_STORE,
                                         STORE in config://; the app cannot write that file)
  Key::set_answer(Some(a))               every question answered with a, without asking
                                         (scripts; env jfgui_PERM_ANSWER=once|always|deny|never)
  decisions() -> Vec<Decision>           every ask line and agent action with its answer
  forget(rule) / forget_all()            revoke: asked again on the next access
  reload()                               read the stored answers again
Plugins (their own <stem>.permissions beside the library, same syntax without ask and agent
lines, $PLUGIN = the plugin's folder; read access to that folder is implied):
  plugin_rights(lib_path) -> Result<Arc<PluginRights>, String>
  on_behalf(&rights, f)                  f on this thread for the plugin: every check must
                                         pass the plugin's rules AND the app's (nested scopes:
                                         all of them); jobs it starts on the pool keep it
  plugin_scope() -> Option<Arc<PluginRights>>   the innermost scope of this thread
Agent control (agent.confirm / agent.deny lines):
  agent_rule(action) -> AgentRule        agent_ask(action, description) -> Verdict

Manifest: one rule per line, '#' starts a comment, a key may repeat:
  fs.read PATTERN..     read files below PATTERN
  fs.write PATTERN..    write (and read) files below PATTERN
  fs.user               files the user chooses (dialog, drop, command line): read + write;
                        also every document the system hands over one at a time (Android's
                        content://, a Flatpak's documents portal mount, the browser's
                        /handles/), so they work after a restart too
  process PATTERN|NAME..   programs Command::spawn / run_elevated may start (NAME: no '/')
  url SCHEME..|*        open_url schemes (https, mailto, ...)
  plugins PATTERN..     native libraries for lib_open
  print                 plat::print
  secrets               plat::secret (the system's store for passwords, tokens and keys)
  autostart             plat::autostart_set (start the app at login; reading is free)
  audio.output          plat::audio: streams, play / play_file, the system's sounds (sound)
  input.global          plat::hotkey_register (global shortcuts: chords pressed while
                        another program has the keyboard)
  screen.capture        plat::screen::capture_start (pictures of the screen; picking one
                        pixel's colour needs nothing: the user chooses it)
  net.connect HOST:PORT..   TCP connections and UDP datagrams to HOST (a name, *.name for
                        every name below it, an IPv4 / [IPv6] address, a block 10.0.0.0/8
                        or [fd00::]/8, localhost = the loopback addresses, * = any) on PORT
                        (a number, a range 8000-8099 or *); names are checked when they are
                        resolved, their addresses then count for the name; with any name
                        rule, port 53 (DNS) is open too
  net.listen ADDR:PORT..    TCP listeners and UDP sockets with a fixed port on ADDR (an
                        address, a block, localhost or *; 0.0.0.0 / [::] = every interface)
                        and PORT (port 0 = any free one: the rule needs 0 or *)
  ask KEY ARGS.. ["reason"]   (every key but fs.user) the first access asks the user; a
                        plain rule that covers the access wins over an ask line
  agent.confirm NAME..  agent actions (glob: '*' any run) the user confirms first
  agent.deny NAME..     agent actions an agent may not run
  sandbox [strict]      ask the OS to enforce the manifest as well (Landlock + seccomp on
                        Linux, process mitigation policies on Windows; sandbox.rs); `strict`
                        refuses to start when the OS cannot enforce it
  recent                the host's list of recent files for a Flatpak (tools/pkg_linux.py:
                        --filesystem=xdg-data/recently-used.xbel, the list of every program);
                        at run time nothing changes: the system's list is always allowed
                        for files the app may read (recent.rs)
A PATTERN is an absolute path (X:/.. and //server/share/.. count on Windows only, /.. on
Linux only), or starts with $CONFIG $TEMP $HOME $EXE $FONTS, $APPIMAGE (the folder of the
running AppImage file: lib/update replaces it there; no value elsewhere), the app's own folders
$APPCONFIG $APPDATA $APPCACHE $APPLOG (vfs::app_dir) or the user's folders $DESKTOP
$DOCUMENTS $DOWNLOADS $PICTURES $MUSIC $VIDEOS (user_dir; a variable without a value
drops the pattern); '*' / '?' match inside one segment, a '**' segment any number of
segments ("dir/**" also matches dir itself); "**" alone matches every path.  Windows
compares without case.  Always readable: the font folders, the Hunspell dictionary folders
(spell::hunspell_dirs), the exe folder and on Linux /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/hosts
(netio's resolver); always writable: the app's own folders (config://, data://, cache://,
logs://; vfs::set_app_id comes first) except the file of the stored answers.  trash counts
as writing the path.

The checks are lexical: a symbolic link inside an allowed folder can point outside it.  On
Linux a path with a ".." segment is refused: "allowed/link/../x" would leave the folder.
```

```rust
/// read access ([`fs_allowed`], [`Key::grant`])
FS_READ: u32 = 1
/// write access; implies [`FS_READ`]
FS_WRITE: u32 = 2
/// refusals kept for [`denials`]
DENIALS_MAX: usize = 64
/// how long a thread other than the asking one waits for the user's answer by default (ms)
WAIT_MS: u32 = 60_000
/// where Always / Never answers are kept by default ([`Key::set_store`])
STORE: &str = "config://permission-decisions.txt"
```

- **`struct Denial`**
  one refused access
  - `kind: &'static str` -- "fs.read", "fs.write", "process", "url", "plugins", "print", "secrets", "autostart",
    "audio.output", "net.connect", "net.listen", "agent", "input.global" or "screen.capture"
  - `target: String` -- the path, program, URL, address, the service of a secret, the agent's action, the
    chord of a shortcut or "" (print, autostart, audio.output, screen.capture)
  - `plugin: String` -- the plugin the call was made for ("" = the app itself)

- **`enum Answer`**
  the user's answer to a question
  - `Once` -- allowed until the program ends
  - `Always` -- allowed, also in later runs (stored)
  - `Deny` -- refused until the program ends
  - `Never` -- refused, also in later runs (stored)

**`impl Answer`**

- **`fn allows(self) -> bool`**
  Once or Always
- **`fn stored(self) -> bool`**
  Always or Never: kept for later runs
- **`fn word(self) -> &'static str`**
  "once", "always", "deny", "never" (scripts, env, the store)
- **`fn parse(w: &str) -> Option<Answer>`**
  the answer of word

- **`enum Verdict`**
  the outcome of a check that may ask the user
  - `Allow` -- go ahead
  - `Deny` -- refused (the rules, the user's answer, nobody to ask, a timeout)
  - `Pending` -- refused for now: the question waits for the user on this (the asking) thread

- **`struct Question`**
  a question waiting for the user's answer
  - `id: u32` -- for [`Key::answer`]
  - `kind: &'static str` -- the kind of access ("fs.read", "net.connect", ..., "agent")
  - `target: String` -- what is accessed: the path, host, program, URL or the agent's action
  - `rule: String` -- the ask line the answer decides ("fs.read $DOCUMENTS/\*\*", "agent document.delete")
  - `reason: String` -- the manifest's reason ("" without one); an agent action: its description
  - `plugin: String` -- the plugin the call is made for ("" = the app)

- **`struct Decision`**
  an ask line or an agent action with its answer ([`decisions`])
  - `rule: String` -- the ask line ("url mailto") or "agent ACTION"
  - `kind: &'static str` -- its kind ("url", ..., "agent")
  - `reason: String` -- the manifest's reason or the action's description ("" when unknown)
  - `answer: Option<Answer>` -- None: not answered (asked on the next access)

- **`enum AgentRule`**
  what the manifest says about an agent action ([`agent_rule`])
  - `Free` -- no rule: the agent may run it
  - `Confirm` -- agent.confirm: the user confirms it first
  - `Deny` -- agent.deny: never for an agent

- **`struct Key(())`**
  The right to widen the installed policy for the user's own files, to run trusted library
  code and to answer questions; only [`install`] creates one (the UI runtime keeps it to
  itself).

- **`fn install(text: &str) -> Result<Key, String>`**
  parse and activate a manifest; Err names the first bad line.  Only the first call of a
  process can succeed.

- **`fn take_key() -> Option<Key>`**
  the key of a process without a manifest (it answers the questions of agent actions); only
  the first call (and none after install) gets it

- **`fn active() -> bool`**
  whether a policy restricts this process

- **`fn fs_allowed(path: &str, mode: u32) -> bool`**
  whether path may be read (FS_READ) or written (FS_WRITE)

- **`fn user_doc_allowed(uri: &str) -> bool`**
  whether the app may reach a document the user chose by its URI (Android's content://
  names; the system grants each one): with fs.user in the manifest, or without a manifest

- **`fn process_allowed(program: &str) -> bool`**
  whether Command::spawn / run_elevated may start program (a path, or a name found in PATH)

- **`fn url_allowed(url: &str) -> bool`**
  whether open_url may open url (its scheme)

- **`fn plugin_allowed(path: &str) -> bool`**
  whether lib_open may load the native library at path

- **`fn print_allowed() -> bool`**
  whether plat::print may print

- **`fn secrets_allowed(service: &str) -> bool`**
  whether plat::secret may use the system's secret store (`secrets`); a refusal names the
  service ("" for secret_available)

- **`fn autostart_allowed() -> bool`**
  whether plat::autostart_set may change the app's autostart entry (`autostart`)

- **`fn audio_allowed() -> bool`**
  whether plat::audio may play sound (`audio.output`): streams, play, play_file, the
  system's sounds

- **`fn audio_granted() -> bool`**
  whether sound is allowed now without a question or a recorded refusal: no manifest, a plain
  `audio.output` line or an ask line already answered with yes (ui's dialog sounds)

- **`fn input_global_allowed() -> bool`**
