  whether plat::hotkey_register may register global shortcuts (`input.global`)

- **`fn screen_capture_allowed() -> bool`**
  whether plat::screen::capture_start may take pictures of the screen (`screen.capture`)

- **`fn denials() -> Vec<Denial>`**
  the last refusals, oldest first

- **`fn sandbox_level() -> u8`**
  the OS sandbox the manifest asks for: 0 none, 1 `sandbox`, 2 `sandbox strict` (sandbox.rs)

- **`struct LinuxPlan`** *(Linux)*
  what the Linux OS sandbox grants, derived from the active policy ([`sandbox_plan_linux`])
  - `level: u8` -- 0 none, 1 `sandbox`, 2 `sandbox strict`
  - `fs: Vec<(String, bool)>` -- literal folders / files the manifest reaches, with whether they may be written
  - `make_dirs: Vec<String>` -- writable folders to create when missing (the app's own folders, the folders of fs.write
    rules): the kernel can only grant paths that exist
  - `exec_allowed: bool` -- the manifest names at least one program (execve is denied otherwise)
  - `connect_restrict: bool` -- restrict TCP connect to `connect_ports` (false: leave it unrestricted -- a `*` rule)
  - `connect_ports: Vec<u16>` -- the ports of net.connect (and 53 with a name rule); empty: no TCP connection at all
  - `listen_restrict: bool` -- restrict TCP bind to `listen_ports`
  - `listen_ports: Vec<u16>` -- the ports of net.listen; empty: no TCP listener at all

- **`fn sandbox_plan_linux() -> LinuxPlan`** *(Linux)*
  what the Linux OS sandbox should enforce for the active policy (no policy: nothing)

- **`struct WinPlan`** *(Windows)*
  what the Windows OS sandbox needs to know from the active policy ([`sandbox_plan_win`])
  - `level: u8` -- 0 none, 1 `sandbox`, 2 `sandbox strict`
  - `plugins_allowed: bool` -- the manifest allows native plugins (dynamic code must stay allowed for the loader)
  - `exec_allowed: bool` -- child processes may be created: the manifest names a program, or has a `url` / `print`
    rule (open_url's ShellExecute and the print dialog can start another program)

- **`fn sandbox_plan_win() -> WinPlan`** *(Windows)*
  what the Windows OS sandbox should enforce for the active policy (no policy: nothing)

- **`fn cap_mask() -> u64`**
  the CAP_\* bits the policy leaves (all without a policy)

**`impl Key`**

- **`fn grant(&self, path: &str, mode: u32) -> bool`**
  let the app read (FS_READ) or read and write (FS_WRITE) the file at path, which the
  user chose; false without fs.user or for a path normalize refuses
- **`fn grant_dir(&self, dir: &str, mode: u32) -> bool`**
  the same for a folder and everything below it
- **`fn trusted<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`**
  run f on this thread without the file checks
- **`fn ask_here(&self, on: bool)`**
  this thread (the UI's) shows the questions (on) or nobody does (off: the open
  questions are withdrawn, waiting threads are refused)
- **`fn answer(&self, id: u32, a: Answer) -> bool`**
  the user's answer to question id -> false when it is no longer open.  The answer
  decides the question's ask line; waiting threads continue.
- **`fn set_answer(&self, a: Option<Answer>)`**
  answer every question with a, without asking (None: ask; jfgui_PERM_ANSWER)
- **`fn set_wait(&self, ms: u32)`**
  how long a thread other than the asking one waits for an answer (ms)
- **`fn set_store(&self, path: Option<&str>)`**
  where Always / Never answers are kept (None: in memory only); the answers of the new
  place are read, the ones of this run stay

- **`fn questions() -> Vec<Question>`**
  the questions waiting for the user, oldest first

- **`fn decisions() -> Vec<Decision>`**
  every ask line of the manifest and every answered rule (agent actions, stored answers of
  lines the manifest no longer has) with its answer, in that order

- **`fn forget(rule: &str) -> bool`**
  revoke the answer for rule (this run's and the stored one): the next access asks again ->
  false when there was none

- **`fn forget_all()`**
  revoke every answer (this run's and the stored ones)

- **`fn reload()`**
  read the stored answers again (another program of the app changed them)

- **`fn agent_rule(action: &str) -> AgentRule`**
  agent.deny / agent.confirm of the manifest for action (Free without a manifest)

- **`fn agent_ask(action: &str, description: &str) -> Verdict`**
  ask the user whether an agent may run action (one decision per action, "agent ACTION");
  description is shown as the reason

- **`fn agent_refused(action: &str)`**
  record that an agent was refused action (agent.deny, an action the app keeps to itself)

- **`struct PluginRights`**
  the rights of a native plugin: its own manifest (None: unrestricted, the app has none and
  neither has the plugin)

**`impl PluginRights`**

- **`fn parse(name: &str, text: &str, dir: &str) -> Result<Arc<PluginRights>, String>`**
  a plugin's manifest text (the syntax of PERMISSIONS without ask and agent lines;
  $PLUGIN = dir); Err names the bad line
- **`fn none(name: &str) -> Arc<PluginRights>`**
  no rights at all (a plugin without a manifest in an app with one)
- **`fn unrestricted(name: &str) -> Arc<PluginRights>`**
  no restriction of its own (the app's rules still apply)
- **`fn name(&self) -> &str`**
  the plugin's name (its file name without extension)
- **`fn restricted(&self) -> bool`**
  whether the plugin has rules of its own

- **`fn plugin_rights(lib_path: &str) -> Result<Arc<PluginRights>, String>`**
  the rights of the native library at lib_path: its manifest "&lt;stem>.permissions" beside it;
  without one: no rights when the app has a manifest, else unrestricted.  Err: a manifest
  that does not parse (do not load the plugin).

- **`fn on_behalf<R>(rights: &Arc<PluginRights>, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R`**
  f on this thread on behalf of the plugin: every check must also pass its rules

- **`fn plugin_scope() -> Option<Arc<PluginRights>>`**
  the innermost plugin scope of this thread

- **`fn font_dirs() -> Vec<String>`**
  the system font folders in the order fontdb scans them: jfgui_FONTDIRS (';' separated,
  on Linux also ':'), else the Windows / XDG folders; on Linux then fontconfig's own folders
  (fontconfig_dirs: NixOS, TeX fonts, a &lt;dir> of the user) and in Flatpak the host's fonts

- **`fn net_connect_allowed(addr: &crate::net::SocketAddr) -> bool`**
  whether a TCP connection or a UDP datagram to addr is allowed: a net.connect rule with
  that address, an address a permitted name resolved to, or port 53 (DNS) with name rules

- **`fn net_listen_allowed(addr: &crate::net::SocketAddr) -> bool`**
  whether a TCP listener (or a UDP socket with a fixed port) may bind addr

- **`fn net_name_allowed(host: &str) -> bool`**
  whether host may be resolved: a net.connect rule names it (or allows every host)

- **`fn net_resolved(host: &str, addrs: &[crate::net::SocketAddr])`**
  (resolvers) host resolved to addrs: connections to them get the ports of host's rules

- **`fn normalize(path: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  path as an absolute, normalised path of this OS (relative paths against cwd()), or None
  for a path the policy refuses. The normalisation is lexical: junctions, symbolic links and
  8.3 names are not resolved, so rules match the path as written, not its final target.

- **`fn normalize_for(path: &str, windows: bool, cwd: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  normalize with the rules of Windows (windows = true) or Linux against the folder cwd

- **`fn pattern_matches(pattern: &str, path: &str) -> bool`**
  whether pattern (manifest syntax after variables) matches path; both normalised with the
  rules of this OS (tests)

- **`fn check(text: &str) -> Result<(), String>`**
  (build checks, tests) whether text is a valid manifest: Err names the first bad line

### `plat/sandbox.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/sandbox.rs`](../lib/plat/sandbox.rs)

```text
sandbox -- OS-level confinement that mirrors the permission manifest (docs/PERMISSIONS.md
"OS sandbox"), as defence in depth for the in-process policy (policy.rs): a bug or native
code can bypass `plat`, the kernel cannot be bypassed.  Opt in with a `sandbox` (best effort)
or `sandbox strict` (refuse to start when the OS cannot enforce it) line in the manifest.

  apply()          install the sandbox for the active policy, once, at start-up (boot.rs,
                   before the app's own code runs); nothing without a `sandbox` line
  status() -> Status   what was applied (tests, a diagnostics page)

Linux: Landlock restricts the filesystem to the folders the manifest grants plus the system
paths the library reads (ABI detected, best effort on older kernels), and TCP bind / connect
to the manifest's ports (ABI 4+); seccomp-bpf denies a list of dangerous syscalls (ptrace,
process_vm_*, kexec, module loading, mount, bpf, perf_event_open, userfaultfd, keyctl ...)
and execve when no program is allowed.  Windows: process mitigation policies (image load,
extension points, dynamic code; strict adds strict handle checks and child-process
creation).  The browser and Android have no such API; apply() does nothing there.
```

- **`struct Status`**
  what [`apply`] installed (the fields not relevant to this OS stay false / -1)
  - `level: u8` -- 0 none, 1 `sandbox`, 2 `sandbox strict`
  - `landlock_abi: i32` -- Linux: the Landlock ABI the kernel reports (-1 = no Landlock)
  - `landlock_fs: bool` -- Linux: the filesystem ruleset is enforced
  - `landlock_net: bool` -- Linux: TCP bind / connect is restricted (Landlock ABI 4+)
  - `seccomp: bool` -- Linux: the seccomp filter is installed
  - `exec_denied: bool` -- execve is denied (no program allowed): Linux seccomp, Windows child-process policy
  - `win_mitigations: bool` -- Windows: the process mitigation policies were set
  - `win_dynamic_code: bool` -- Windows: dynamic code is prohibited (no native plugins)

**`impl Status`**

- **`const NONE: Status = Status { level: 0, landlock_abi: -1, landlock_fs: false, ...`**
  nothing applied

- **`fn apply()`** *(Linux)*
  install the OS sandbox the active policy asks for (nothing without a `sandbox` line); call
  once, before the app's own code and before any worker thread is started

- **`fn apply()`** *(Windows)*
  install the OS sandbox the active policy asks for (nothing without a `sandbox` line)

- **`fn apply()`**
  the browser and Android have no such API

- **`fn status() -> Status`**
  what [`apply`] installed

- **`fn status() -> Status`**
  the browser and Android install nothing

### `plat/boot.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/boot.rs`](../lib/plat/boot.rs)

```text
boot -- what build_rs.py builds into every program of an app, set up before the program's
own code runs (docs/PERMISSIONS.md, docs/VFS.md)

  start(&rt::boot::Boot) -> Result<(), exit code>   console programs (rt::main!): the
                          process entry registers it with rt::boot; name, app://, manifest
  name_and_assets(app, assets) -> Result<(), i32>    vfs::set_app_id, the JFA1 bundle as app://
  permissions(manifest) -> Result<Option<Key>, i32>  install the manifest; with fs.user the
                          paths on the command line are the user's (read + write, folders
                          with everything below; a local file:// URI as its path); without
                          a manifest the process's key (policy::take_key: it answers the
                          questions of agent actions).  A `sandbox` line then hands the
                          manifest to the OS as well (sandbox::apply)

ui::main! calls name_and_assets and permissions itself (ui::boot, with the user's languages
in between) and keeps the key; rt::main! programs drop it, so their code cannot widen the
rules.  A refused bundle or manifest is reported on stderr: exit code 2.
```

- **`fn start(b: &rt::boot::Boot) -> Result<(), i32>`**
  (rt::main!, through rt::boot) set a console program up: name, assets, permissions

- **`fn name_and_assets(app: Option<&str>, assets: &'static [u8]) -> Result<(), i32>`**
  the app's name for its folders and its assets as app:// (Err: a damaged bundle)

- **`fn permissions(manifest: Option<&str>) -> Result<Option<Key>, i32>`**
  install the app's manifest (None: the app has none, everything stays allowed) and grant
  the command line's paths; Some(key) for the caller to keep or drop (also without a
  manifest: policy::take_key)

- **`fn grant_user(key: &Key, path: &str)`**
  a path the user handed over: a folder with everything below, else the file (with fs.user)

### `plat/vfs.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/vfs.rs`](../lib/plat/vfs.rs)

```text
vfs -- one file namespace on every platform: "scheme://path" reaches a mounted provider,
every other name is a path of the OS (or of the browser's virtual files)

  mount(scheme, provider) / unmount(scheme) -> bool / mounted(scheme) -> bool
  provider(scheme) -> Option<Arc<dyn Provider>>   a mount's provider (to build an Overlay or
                               a Sub of app://, for example)
  route(name) -> Route         Os (no scheme), Vfs(provider, path) or Bad (a scheme name
                               with ".." or an invalid scheme); "config:/" and "config:" are
                               the root like "config://"
  os_path(name) -> Option<String>   the OS path behind a name of a folder mount (for APIs
                               that need a real file); an OS path comes back unchanged
  stat(name) -> Option<Stat>   kind, size, times of a name with a scheme (Provider::stat)
  display_name(name) -> String the name to show the user (content://: the document's
                               display name; else the last segment)
  app_id() / set_app_id(id)    the name of the app's own folders (build_rs.py: the app's
                               folder name; else the exe's name)
  app_dir(APP_CONFIG | APP_DATA | APP_CACHE | APP_LOG) -> Option<String>   the app's own
                               folders: Windows %APPDATA%/<id>, %LOCALAPPDATA%/<id>,
                               %LOCALAPPDATA%/<id>/Cache, %LOCALAPPDATA%/<id>/Logs; Linux
                               the XDG config / data / cache / state homes + /<id>; browser
                               /config, /data, /cache + /<id>, /data/<id>/Logs
  Built in, mounted on first use: mem:// (one MemFs per process), config://, data://,
  cache://, logs:// (DirFs on app_dir), app:// (the app's bundle; ui::main! / rt::main! install it,
  else empty), and the user's folders desktop://, documents://, downloads://, pictures://,
  music://, videos:// (DirFs on user_dir, dirs.rs; only what the permissions allow); on
  Android content:// (the documents the user chose in the system's picker: content.rs,
  ContentFs over the ContentResolver)
  Providers: MemFs, DirFs::new(root), Overlay::new(layers) (with whiteouts),
  Sub::new(provider, folder), Bundle::new(bytes) (JFA1, tools/assetpack.py); archive::ZipFs
  (lib/archive).  Provider: kind, read, list (+ write, mkdir, delete, rename, os_path, stat,
  set_times, open -> Opened / Stream)
  pack_bundle(files) -> Vec<u8>    a JFA1 bundle (tests, tools; build_rs.py packs with
                               tools/assetpack.py)

The public file functions (guarded.rs) route names with a scheme here: read_file,
write_file, file_exists(_checked), mkdir, delete, rename (inside one mount), dir_list and
trash (folder mounts); plat::fs (stat, read_dir, links, times ...: fs.rs) too.  File::open,
create_new, open_temp and FileLock::acquire work on every mount: folder mounts open the OS
file (os_path), MemFs and Bundle (and ZipFs) hand out streams (Provider::open: Opened), other
providers get the whole file read and written back; a FileLock of a mount without OS files
holds inside this process.  Paths inside a mount use '/', have no "." or empty segments and
never "..".  Writes create missing folders.  DirFs uses the checked OS functions, so the
app's permissions apply to it; the app's own folders are always allowed (policy.rs), the
user's folders need rules ($DOCUMENTS ...).

Overlay whiteouts: deleting or renaming what a lower layer has writes ".wh.NAME" into the top
layer; a whited-out folder made again gets ".wh..wh..opq" (no lower entries below it).  The
markers live in the top layer (a DirFs keeps them on disk) and are never listed.

JFA1 bundle (little endian): "JFA1", u32 count, u32 names_len; count entries of 20 bytes
sorted by name: u32 name_off, u16 name_len, u8 codec (0 stored, 1 LZ4 block), u8 0,
u32 data_off (from the bundle start), u32 stored_len, u32 size; the names; the data.
```

```rust
/// app_dir: the app's settings folder (config://)
APP_CONFIG: u32 = 0
/// app_dir: the app's data folder (data://)
APP_DATA: u32 = 1
/// app_dir: the app's cache folder (cache://)
APP_CACHE: u32 = 2
/// app_dir: the app's log folder (logs://)
APP_LOG: u32 = 3
```

- **`struct Stat`**
  what [`Provider::stat`] reports
  - `kind: u32` -- 1 file, 2 folder
  - `size: u64`
  - `mtime_ns: i64` -- nanoseconds since 1970; 0 = unknown (bundles)
  - `atime_ns: i64`

- **`trait Stream: Send + Sync`**
  an open file of a provider without OS files (File::open on mem://, app://, zip mounts);
  offsets as in plat::File
  - `fn read_at(&self, off: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Option<usize>`
    bytes read at off (fewer at the end), None on an error
  - `fn write_at(&self, _off: u64, _buf: &[u8]) -> Option<usize>`
    bytes written at off (the file grows); None for a read-only stream
  - `fn size(&self) -> Option<u64>`
  - `fn set_len(&self, _len: u64) -> bool`
    cut or extend to len bytes
  - `fn sync(&self) -> bool`
    the data is where readers of the mount find it

- **`trait Provider: Send + Sync`**
  A file tree behind a scheme.  Paths are relative ("" is the root), '/' separated and
  normalised by route().
  - `fn kind(&self, path: &str) -> u32`
    0 missing, 1 file, 2 folder
  - `fn read(&self, path: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`
    the whole file
  - `fn list(&self, path: &str, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&str, bool, u64)) -> bool`
    f(name, is_dir, size) for every entry of a folder -> false when it is no folder
  - `fn write(&self, _path: &str, _data: &[u8]) -> bool`
    replace or create a file (missing folders are created)
  - `fn mkdir(&self, _path: &str) -> bool`
    create a folder and its parents (an existing folder is fine)
  - `fn delete(&self, _path: &str) -> bool`
    a file or an empty folder
  - `fn rename(&self, _old: &str, _new: &str) -> bool`
    a file to another name (replacing it)
  - `fn os_path(&self, _path: &str) -> Option<String>`
    the OS path of path (folder mounts only)
  - `fn stat(&self, path: &str) -> Option<Stat>`
    kind, size and times of path (None: missing); the default asks kind and the folder's
    listing, without times
  - `fn set_times(&self, _path: &str, _atime_ns: i64, _mtime_ns: i64) -> bool`
    set the access and modification times (ns since 1970) -> false where the provider
    keeps none
  - `fn open(&self, _path: &str, _mode: u32) -> Opened`
    File::open on the provider: a stream on the file (mode FO_READ, FO_WRITE: create /
    truncate, FO_RW: open or create).  The default, Generic, lets File::open use os_path,
    else read and write the whole file (written back on sync and when the File is dropped)
  - `fn display_name(&self, _path: &str) -> Option<String>`
    the name to show the user for path (None: its last segment; content:// documents:
    their display name)
  - `fn atomic_rename(&self) -> bool`
    whether a sibling renamed over a file replaces it in one step (AtomicFile commits so);
    false (content://): AtomicFile collects the bytes and writes the file in place

- **`enum Opened`**
  what [`Provider::open`] answers
  - `File(Box<dyn Stream>)` -- the provider's own stream
  - `Refused` -- missing, read-only or refused: File::open fails
  - `Generic` -- no streams of its own: File::open uses os_path, else read / write of the whole file

**`impl Opened`**

- **`fn of(f: Option<crate::File>) -> Opened`**
  a File (OS file or stream) as the answer, None as Refused

- **`enum Route`**
  where a name leads
  - `Os` -- no scheme: a path of the OS
  - `Vfs(Arc<dyn Provider>, String)` -- a mounted provider and the path inside it
  - `Bad` -- a scheme name that cannot be used (".." or no such mount)

- **`fn mount(scheme: &str, provider: Arc<dyn Provider>) -> bool`**
  mount provider under scheme (lower-case letters, digits, '+', '-', '.'; at least two
  characters); replaces an earlier mount -> false for an invalid scheme

- **`fn unmount(scheme: &str) -> bool`**
  remove a mount -> whether there was one

- **`fn mounted(scheme: &str) -> bool`**
  whether scheme is mounted (the built-in schemes count once they were used)

- **`fn clean(path: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  the normalised path inside a mount ('\\' -> '/', no "." / empty segments) or None (a "..")

- **`fn route(name: &str) -> Route`**
  where name leads (built-in schemes are mounted on first use)

- **`fn provider(scheme: &str) -> Option<Arc<dyn Provider>>`**
  the provider mounted under scheme (built-in schemes are mounted on first use)

- **`fn os_path(name: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  the OS path behind name: a folder mount's file, or name itself when it has no scheme

- **`fn stat(name: &str) -> Option<Stat>`**
  kind, size and times of a name with a scheme (Provider::stat; content://: what the
  document's provider reports) -> None for a missing one and for OS paths (plat::fs::stat)

- **`fn display_name(name: &str) -> String`**
  the name to show the user for a file or folder: a content:// document's display name,
  else the last segment of the name ("C:/a/b.txt" -> "b.txt", "config://x/y" -> "y")

- **`fn set_app_id(id: &str)`**
  set the name of the app's own folders (ui::main!, rt::main!: the app folder of build_rs.py); ignored
  unless it is a plain file name (letters, digits, '.', '-', '_', not only dots)

- **`fn app_id() -> String`**
  the name of the app's own folders: set_app_id, else the exe's name without extension

- **`fn app_dir(kind: u32) -> Option<String>`**
  the app's settings (APP_CONFIG), data (APP_DATA), cache (APP_CACHE) or log (APP_LOG) folder

- **`struct MemFs`**
  files in memory (mem://, tests, generated data); open streams share the file's bytes like
  OS files: writes are seen at once, write / delete replace or drop the name only

**`impl MemFs`**

- **`fn new() -> MemFs`**

- **`struct DirFs`**
  an OS folder as the root (config://, data://, cache://, mounts of the app); every call
  goes through the checked OS functions, so the app's permissions apply

**`impl DirFs`**

- **`fn new(root: &str) -> DirFs`**
  root: an absolute OS folder (created on the first write)

- **`struct Overlay`**
  several providers in one tree: a path comes from the first layer that has it, a folder
  lists the entries of every layer, writes go to the first layer.  Deleting or renaming what a
  lower layer has leaves a whiteout in the top layer (".wh.NAME"; a folder made again after
  that gets ".wh..wh..opq" and shows no lower entries), so a DirFs on top keeps them across
  runs; the markers are never listed, and names starting with ".wh." cannot be used.

**`impl Overlay`**

- **`fn new(layers: Vec<Arc<dyn Provider>>) -> Overlay`**
  layers[0] is on top

- **`struct Sub`**
  one folder of another provider as a root (a theme folder of app://)

**`impl Sub`**

- **`fn new(inner: Arc<dyn Provider>, dir: &str) -> Option<Sub>`**
  dir: a folder of inner ('/' separated; None for "..")

- **`struct Bundle`**
  a read-only JFA1 bundle (app://: the app's assets folder, packed by build_rs.py)

**`impl Bundle`**

- **`fn empty() -> Bundle`**
  a bundle without files
- **`fn from_static(b: &'static [u8]) -> Option<Bundle>`**
  the bundle embedded in the program (None: malformed)
- **`fn new(b: Vec<u8>) -> Option<Bundle>`**
  a bundle in memory (None: malformed)
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of files
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
  whether the bundle has no files
- **`fn names(&self) -> Vec<&str>`**
  the paths of all files, sorted

- **`fn pack_bundle(files: &[(&str, &[u8])]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  a JFA1 bundle of (name, data) pairs: LZ4 where that saves a tenth (tests, tools); None for
  a name route() would refuse, a name twice, or a bundle beyond 4 GiB

### `plat/content.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/content.rs`](../lib/plat/content.rs)

```text
content -- the documents of other apps as files: Android's Storage Access Framework
("content://" names) behind the vfs; the name logic runs on every platform, so the desktop
tests it with a host of its own

  ContentFs::new(host) -> a vfs Provider for the names after "content://".  On Android the
       vfs mounts it on first use with the ContentResolver as its host (android_host.rs,
       with_journal in the app's data folder, recover() at once); elsewhere only a test
       mounts it (apps/plattest/t_content.rs: a host in memory).
  .with_journal(dir)   writes go through a copy in dir first (below); recover() finishes the
       writes a crash interrupted -> how many
  DocHost (trait)   what the provider asks the system: query (one document), children (of a
       folder document), create, delete, rename, open (a Stream: Android a file descriptor),
       generation (a counter the system bumps when a provider reports a change)
  DocInfo           uri, display name, folder?, size, mtime, flags (DOC_*)
  uri_of(path)      "content://" + path -- the document's own URI where the name is one

Names (the path after "content://"; the file dialog hands them out, apps join names below
a chosen folder as with any other folder):
  AUTH/document/ID            one document (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT / ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT):
                              read, write, File streams, stat, display name -- no siblings
  AUTH/tree/ID                a folder the user chose (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE)
  AUTH/tree/ID/a/b.txt        below it by display names (JFLib's own form: every name is
                              looked up among the children of the folder before it)
  AUTH/tree/ID/document/ID2   Android's own form of a document inside a tree
  anything else               handed to the host as one document
Inside a tree mkdir, write (new files are created), delete (files, empty folders; never the
chosen folder itself), rename (inside one folder, replacing; to another folder: copy and
delete, files only) and dir_list work.

Names below a tree are cached: name -> the document's URI (and folder?), filled by every walk
and listing, forgotten on create / delete / rename through the provider, emptied when the
host's generation changes (Android: a ContentObserver on the provider's authority) and
unused after CACHE_TTL_US.  A cached document is asked once (query) before it is used: gone,
renamed or no longer a file / folder, the name is walked again from the nearest cached folder
(from the tree's root at worst).  So a name costs one query instead of one listing per
folder; only the leaf is checked, a folder moved elsewhere by another app stays cached until
a change is reported or its time is up.

Writing: SAF has no rename over an existing document (providers pick "name (1)", and a new
document would get a new ID, losing the grants), so the provider says atomic_rename() ==
false: AtomicFile (write_file in pieces, aio) collects the bytes and writes the document in
place.  rename replaces by deleting the target first.  write (write_file, AtomicFile's commit)
is made as safe as SAF allows:
  1. with a journal folder, the new bytes (and the URI) go there first: one file per document
     (JOURNAL, written atomically on internal storage);
  2. the document is opened truncated ("rwt" / "wt") and written, synced, then read back and
     compared (size and every byte) -- once more if that fails;
  3. the journal file goes.  A crash or a failed write leaves it: recover() (Android: when
     content:// is first used in a process) writes it again into the document if it still
     exists (else the copy is dropped).
The document keeps its URI (grants stay valid).  What remains: between the truncation and the
end of the write other readers see a part; without a journal (none set) a crash leaves that
part; File streams (File::open) write in place without any of this; opening a document for
writing, deleting or renaming it drops its pending journal copy.
```

```rust
/// DocInfo::flags: the document can be written
DOC_WRITE: u32 = 1
/// DocInfo::flags: the document can be deleted
DOC_DELETE: u32 = 2
/// DocInfo::flags: the document can be renamed
DOC_RENAME: u32 = 4
/// DocInfo::flags: the folder takes new documents
DOC_CREATE: u32 = 8
/// how long a cached name is used without a reported change (µs)
CACHE_TTL_US: u64 = 60_000_000
```

- **`fn listings() -> u64`**
  (tests) how many folder listings (DocHost::children) the walks of every ContentFs asked for

- **`fn interrupt_next_write(n: u64)`**
  (tests) the next write of a document stops after n bytes and fails, its journal copy kept
  -- what a crash in the middle of a write leaves

- **`struct DocInfo`**
  one document as the host describes it
  - `uri: String` -- the document's URI ("content://AUTH/document/ID", inside a tree
    "content://AUTH/tree/T/document/ID")
  - `name: String` -- what the user sees (OpenableColumns.DISPLAY_NAME)
  - `dir: bool`
  - `size: Option<u64>` -- bytes; None when the provider does not know
  - `mtime_ns: i64` -- ns since 1970, 0 = unknown
  - `flags: u32` -- DOC_\*

- **`trait DocHost: Send + Sync`**
  what ContentFs asks the system (Android: the ContentResolver and DocumentsContract)
  - `fn query(&self, uri: &str) -> Option<DocInfo>`
    the document behind uri (a tree's URI: its root folder) -> None when it is missing or
    not allowed
  - `fn children(&self, uri: &str) -> Option<Vec<DocInfo>>`
    the documents in the folder document uri (a URI of DocInfo::uri inside a tree)
  - `fn create(&self, parent: &str, name: &str, dir: bool) -> Option<DocInfo>`
    a new document (dir: a folder) named name in the folder parent -> its description
  - `fn delete(&self, uri: &str) -> bool`
  - `fn rename(&self, uri: &str, name: &str) -> Option<DocInfo>`
    the document under a new display name in its folder -> its description (the URI may
    change; a provider may pick another name when name is taken)
  - `fn open(&self, uri: &str, mode: u32) -> Option<Box<dyn Stream>>`
    the document opened: FO_READ, FO_WRITE (truncated) or FO_RW
  - `fn generation(&self) -> u64`
    a counter that changes when a provider reports a change of its documents (the name
    cache starts again then); 0 = never

- **`fn uri_of(path: &str) -> String`**
  "content://" + path

- **`struct ContentFs<H: DocHost>`**
  the documents of other apps behind "content://" (see the file header)

**`impl<H: DocHost> ContentFs<H>`**

- **`fn new(host: H) -> ContentFs<H>`**
- **`fn with_journal(mut self, dir: &str) -> ContentFs<H>`**
  keep a copy of every write in dir (a folder of the app's own, any plat name) until the
  document holds all of it; recover() finishes what a crash interrupted
- **`fn host(&self) -> &H`**
  the host the provider asks
- **`fn document(&self, path: &str) -> Option<DocInfo>`**
  the document a name (after "content://") means -- its own URI, display name, size
- **`fn recover(&self) -> u32`**
  finish the writes a crash (or a failure) left in the journal: each copy is written into
  its document again if that still exists, then removed; copies of documents that are gone
  or not granted any more, and damaged ones, are removed -> how many documents were
  completed

### `plat/secret.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/secret.rs`](../lib/plat/secret.rs)

```text
secret -- passwords, tokens and keys in the system's secret store instead of files

  secret_available() -> bool          a store is there and the app may use it
  secret_set(service, account, &[u8]) -> Result<(), SecretError>        create or replace
  secret_get(service, account) -> Option<Vec<u8>>                       None: missing / error
  secret_get_checked(service, account) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, SecretError>
  secret_delete(service, account) -> Result<bool, SecretError>          true: one was removed

An entry is named by the app (vfs::app_id()), a service ("github", "smtp.example.org") and
an account ("alice", or "" for one value per service), so apps do not reach each other's
entries through this API.  The app needs `secrets` in its manifest (policy.rs); without it
every call is refused (SecretError::Denied, PERMDENY secrets <service>).  Values are bytes,
at most SECRET_MAX of them.  Without a store the calls fail: nothing is ever written to a
plain file instead.

Windows (win_secret.rs): generic credentials of the Credential Manager, target
"jflib:<app>/<service>/<account>" ('%' and '/' of the names as %25 / %2F), persisted on this
computer only (CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE: tokens do not roam to other machines with the
profile).  Values above 2560 bytes (the Credential Manager's limit) go DPAPI-encrypted into
data://secrets/; the credential keeps the file's SHA-256, so neither a stale nor a foreign
file is accepted.  Linux (linux_secret.rs): items of the Secret Service on the session bus
(gnome-keyring, KWallet, KeePassXC) in the default collection, attributes app / service /
account; the values travel encrypted (dh-ietf1024-sha256-aes128-cbc-pkcs7; plain only when
the service lacks it); a locked collection is unlocked through the service's prompt.
Android (android_secret.rs): an AES-256-GCM key of the Android Keystore (one per app, made on
the first set, not exportable, no user authentication) encrypts each value into a file of
the app's no_backup folder.  Browser (web_secret.rs, web/secrets.js): a non-extractable
WebCrypto AES-GCM key per app in IndexedDB encrypts the values kept there; the host decrypts
the app's entries before it starts, plat answers from that copy and the host commits each
change asynchronously.

The OS does not separate the programs of one user: other native programs of the same user
can read these entries (the Credential Manager, an unlocked keyring); in the browser every
script of the page's origin can use the key.  The calls block -- on Linux until the user
answers a prompt (at most PROMPT_SECONDS): call them from a worker thread when the UI must
stay responsive.
```

```rust
/// the largest value secret_set stores
SECRET_MAX: usize = 64 * 1024
/// the longest service or account name (bytes of UTF-8)
SECRET_NAME_MAX: usize = 256
/// how long a call waits for the user to answer an unlock prompt (Linux)
PROMPT_SECONDS: u32 = 300
```

- **`enum SecretError`**
  why a secret call failed
  - `Unavailable` -- no secret store here (Linux: no Secret Service on the session bus; browser: no
    IndexedDB or WebCrypto, e.g. a page served over plain http)
  - `Denied` -- the app's permissions lack `secrets`
  - `Dismissed` -- the user dismissed the store's prompt (unlock, confirmation), or it timed out
  - `Invalid` -- an empty or too long service, a name with NUL, or a value above SECRET_MAX
  - `Failed(String)` -- the store refused or failed: what it said

- **`fn secret_available() -> bool`**
  whether this system has a secret store the app may use (`secrets` in its manifest)

- **`fn secret_set(service: &str, account: &str, secret: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SecretError>`**
  store secret under (service, account), replacing what was there

- **`fn secret_get(service: &str, account: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the secret of (service, account); None when there is none, and on any error

- **`fn secret_get_checked(service: &str, account: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, SecretError>`**
  the secret of (service, account): Ok(None) when there is none

- **`fn secret_delete(service: &str, account: &str) -> Result<bool, SecretError>`**
  remove the secret of (service, account) -> whether there was one

### `plat/instance.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/instance.rs`](../lib/plat/instance.rs)

```text
instance -- one running instance per app and user (ui: AppDesc AF_SINGLE_INSTANCE): a later
start hands its working folder and arguments to the running instance and ends

  claim(app) -> Claim        Primary: this process is the app's instance; the requests of
                             later starts arrive on a thread of their own (take(); each one
                             calls wake()); Forwarded: the running instance has the request,
                             end this process; Alone: no instance channel (browser, Android,
                             an error): carry on alone
  take() -> Vec<Request>     the requests that arrived, oldest first
  send(app, cwd, args) -> bool    hand a request to the running instance (claim uses it)
  Request { cwd, args }; Request::paths()   the arguments that are no options, as absolute
                             paths (local file:// URIs as paths, other names with a scheme
                             and URLs as they are)

Channel (control_ipc_win.rs / control_ipc_linux.rs): Windows the pipe
\\.\pipe\jfgui-instance-<user SID>-<app> (current user, local clients, one pipe instance:
the first process that creates it is the instance; the starting process lets it take the
foreground); Linux the abstract socket jfgui-instance-<uid>-<app>.  Both ends make sure the
other runs as the same user.  Message: "JFI1", u32 length of the rest, u32 count, count x
(u32 length, UTF-8): the working folder, then the arguments (without the program), on Linux
then "XAT1", u32 length, the start's $XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN when it has one (the running
instance's window comes forward with it on Wayland: linux_wl_act.rs; an instance of an older
version refuses the block, then the request goes again without it); answer "OK".  At most
1 MiB, 3 s per exchange.
```

- **`enum Claim`**
  what claim found
  - `Primary` -- this process is the app's instance
  - `Forwarded` -- the running instance got this start's request: end the process
  - `Alone` -- no instance channel here: carry on alone

- **`struct Request`**
  the command line of a later start
  - `cwd: String` -- the working folder of the starting process
  - `args: Vec<String>` -- its arguments, without the program

**`impl Request`**

- **`fn paths(&self) -> Vec<String>`**
  the arguments that are no options ("-..."): relative paths against cwd; local file://
  URIs as paths (Linux desktops hand files over that way for %U); other names with a
  scheme ("config://..", "https://..") as they are

- **`fn take() -> Vec<Request>`**
  the requests that arrived since the last call, oldest first

- **`fn claim(app: &str) -> Claim`**
  become the app's single instance, or hand this start's arguments to the running one

- **`fn send(app: &str, cwd: &str, args: &[String]) -> bool`**
  hand (cwd, args) to the running instance of app -> it confirmed the request

### `plat/spell.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/spell.rs`](../lib/plat/spell.rs)

```text
spell -- the system's spell checker

  sys_spell_find(lang) -> Some(tag)   the checker of the system knows the language: the tag
                                   as it names it ("de-DE"); `lang` exactly, else the same
                                   language in its main region, else any region of it
  sys_spell_languages() -> tags    every language it knows
  SysSpeller::open(tag) -> checker   language(), check(word), suggest(word, max)
  hunspell_dirs() -> folders       where Hunspell dictionaries live here (DICPATH, Linux:
                                   the XDG data folders); the spell crate reads them
  hyphen_dirs() -> folders         where hyphenation patterns live here (Linux: hyphen in
                                   the XDG data folders); spell::Hyphenator reads them
  (both always readable for the app's permissions, policy.rs)

Windows (win_spell.rs): ISpellCheckerFactory / ISpellChecker of the Spell Checking API
(Windows 8 and later; the languages are the installed language packs).  COM on the calling
thread (an apartment of its own on the UI thread): a SysSpeller stays on the thread that
opened it (it is not Send).  check() reports a word as misspelled when ISpellChecker::Check
returns any error for it (also "replace" / "delete" actions); the user's Windows word list
counts as known.  Linux, Web, Android: no system checker (None, empty) -- their Hunspell
dictionaries are files the spell crate reads itself.
```

- **`struct SysSpeller`**
  a checker of the system's spell checking service for one language

- **`fn hunspell_dirs() -> Vec<String>`**
  the folders of Hunspell dictionaries on this system, in search order: DICPATH (';'
  separated on Windows, ':' elsewhere), then on Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/hunspell
  (~/.local/share/hunspell) and hunspell, myspell, myspell/dicts below every XDG_DATA_DIRS
  folder (default /usr/local/share, /usr/share); Web / Android: none.  Always readable for
  the app's permissions (policy.rs), like the font folders.

- **`fn hyphen_dirs() -> Vec<String>`**
  the system's folders of hyphenation patterns (hyph_\*.dic, LibreOffice's format: Linux
  $XDG_DATA_HOME/hyphen (~/.local/share/hyphen), then hyphen in each of $XDG_DATA_DIRS
  (/usr/local/share, /usr/share) -- where the distributions' hyphen-\* packages put them);
  empty elsewhere (Windows: spell::Hyphenator looks in LibreOffice's extensions itself)

- **`fn sys_spell_find(lang: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  the tag of a language the system's checker knows (see the module header)

- **`fn sys_spell_languages() -> Vec<String>`**
  every language the system's checker knows

**`impl SysSpeller`**

- **`fn open(tag: &str) -> Option<SysSpeller>`**
  the checker for `tag` (a tag sys_spell_find gave), None when the system has none
- **`fn language(&self) -> &str`**
  the language tag
- **`fn check(&self, word: &str) -> bool`**
  the word is correct (an error of the service: true)
- **`fn suggest(&self, word: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String>`**
  corrections for the word (at most max)

### `plat/tray.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/tray.rs`](../lib/plat/tray.rs)

```text
tray -- the app's symbol in the notification area (system tray) and system notifications

  tray_set(&Tray) -> bool        show or update the symbol: icon (None = the program's own:
                                 Windows icon resource 1, Linux the icon named like the app),
                                 tooltip, menu (TrayItem tree; empty = no menu)
  tray_remove()                  take the symbol away
  notify(&Note) -> u32           a system notification -> its id (0: not shown); clicking
                                 it reports NoteClicked
  notify_close(id)
  tray_take() -> Vec<TrayEvent>  what happened since the last call; every event calls wake()
  tray_supported() -> bool       whether this system shows the symbol: a notification area
                                 (Linux: a StatusNotifierWatcher runs -- KDE, Xfce, ...; GNOME
                                 only with the AppIndicator extension); notifications work
                                 without one
  set_dry_run(on)                print instead of showing from now on (headless UI runs)

Windows (win_tray.rs): Shell_NotifyIconW on a message-only window of the UI thread, the menu
with TrackPopupMenuEx, notifications as the symbol's balloon (Windows 10 / 11 show it as a
toast; without a visible symbol a hidden one is added for the time it is shown).  Linux
(linux_tray.rs): StatusNotifierItem with a com.canonical.dbusmenu menu and
org.freedesktop.Notifications, on a session-bus connection of its own thread.  Elsewhere
nothing is shown.  jfgui_TRAY_DRYRUN=1 prints what would be shown instead (tests).
```

```rust
/// TrayItem flags: a check mark
TI_CHECKED: u32 = 1
/// TrayItem flags: greyed out
TI_DISABLED: u32 = 2
/// TrayItem flags: a separator line (id and label are ignored)
TI_SEPARATOR: u32 = 4
```

- **`struct TrayItem`**
  one row of the symbol's menu
  - `id: u32` -- reported by TrayEvent::Menu (0: a row without action, e.g. a submenu)
  - `label: String`
  - `flags: u32` -- TI_\*
  - `sub: Vec<TrayItem>` -- a submenu when not empty

- **`struct TrayIcon`**
  an icon: straight ARGB pixels (0xAARRGGBB), w x h
  - `w: u32`
  - `h: u32`
  - `px: Vec<u32>`

- **`struct Tray`**
  the symbol
  - `icon: Option<TrayIcon>` -- None: the program's own icon
  - `tooltip: String`
  - `menu: Vec<TrayItem>`

- **`struct Note`**
  a system notification
  - `title: String`
  - `body: String`
  - `icon: Option<TrayIcon>` -- None: the program's own icon

- **`enum TrayEvent`**
  what happened at the symbol or a notification
  - `Activate` -- the symbol was clicked (Linux: activated)
  - `SecondaryActivate` -- the symbol was double-clicked (Windows) / middle-clicked (Linux)
  - `Menu(u32)` -- a menu row was chosen: its TrayItem::id
  - `NoteClicked(u32)` -- a notification was clicked: its id
  - `NoteClosed(u32)` -- a notification went away without a click (timeout, closed): its id

- **`fn tray_take() -> Vec<TrayEvent>`**
  the events since the last call, oldest first

- **`fn set_dry_run(on: bool)`**
  print what would be shown instead of showing it (the UI's headless runs: scripts, --shot)

- **`fn tray_set(t: &Tray) -> bool`**
  show or update the symbol -> false when this system has no notification area

- **`fn tray_remove()`**
  take the symbol away

- **`fn notify(n: &Note) -> u32`**
  a system notification -> its id (0: not shown)

- **`fn notify_close(id: u32)`**
  take a notification away

- **`fn tray_supported() -> bool`**
  whether the symbol can be shown here (a notification area; Linux: a StatusNotifierWatcher
  runs -- GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension); notifications work without one

### `plat/power.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/power.rs`](../lib/plat/power.rs)

```text
power -- keep the computer awake while the app works: no standby, no screen saver

  inhibit(reason, what) -> Option<Inhibit>   ask the system not to go to sleep on its own
                                   (INHIBIT_SUSPEND: downloads, backups, long exports) or
                                   also to keep the screen on and the session active
                                   (INHIBIT_IDLE: presentations, videos; implies
                                   INHIBIT_SUSPEND).  The guard releases it when dropped.
                                   None: not possible here (no service, web, Android)
  inhibited() -> u32               the INHIBIT_* bits the live guards of this process hold

reason is shown by the system (`powercfg /requests`, the desktop's list of inhibitors);
"" names the app.  The user can still put the computer to sleep, and the opposite
direction already reaches the app: UIC_SUSPEND (the system goes to sleep / woke up) and
UIC_SESSION_END (logout, shutdown) come from win_api.rs and linux_life.rs.

Windows (win_power.rs): a power request with the reason as its text (PowerCreateRequest,
PowerSetRequest: INHIBIT_SUSPEND -> PowerRequestSystemRequired, INHIBIT_IDLE -> also
PowerRequestDisplayRequired).  Linux (linux_power.rs): the Inhibit portal
(org.freedesktop.portal.Inhibit, flags suspend 4 / idle 8; also inside Flatpak; a refusal
of its backend arrives up to 300 ms after the answer and is waited for; INHIBIT_IDLE falls
back to idle alone where a backend only inhibits idle), without it
org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver (idle) and org.freedesktop.PowerManagement.Inhibit (suspend;
only best effort beside idle) -- all on a session-bus connection of plat that stays open
while a guard lives (the desktop ends inhibitions with their connection; it is closed when
the last guard goes).  A backend may still drop an inhibition later; the guard does not
notice.  logind's Inhibit is not used: it answers with a file descriptor, which plat's
D-Bus client does not receive.
```

```rust
/// keep the system from going to sleep on its own (the screen may still turn off)
INHIBIT_SUSPEND: u32 = 1
/// keep the screen on and the session active (no screen saver, no lock); implies
/// INHIBIT_SUSPEND
INHIBIT_IDLE: u32 = 2
```

- **`struct Inhibit`**
  an inhibition; dropping it lets the system sleep again

**`impl Inhibit`**

- **`fn what(&self) -> u32`**
  the INHIBIT_\* bits this guard holds (INHIBIT_IDLE with INHIBIT_SUSPEND)

- **`fn inhibit(reason: &str, what: u32) -> Option<Inhibit>`**
  keep the system awake (INHIBIT_SUSPEND) or also the screen on (INHIBIT_IDLE) until the
  guard is dropped -> None: not possible here

- **`fn inhibited() -> u32`**
  the INHIBIT_\* bits the live guards of this process hold

### `plat/autostart.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/autostart.rs`](../lib/plat/autostart.rs)

```text
autostart -- start the app when the user logs in

  autostart_set(on, args) -> Result<(), AutostartError>   on: start this program with args
                                    at login (an existing entry is replaced); off: remove it
  autostart_get() -> bool           an entry of this app is there and switched on
  autostart_entry() -> Option<String>   the command the entry starts (Windows: the Run
                                    value, Linux: the Exec value, Flatpak: what was asked
                                    last), None without one

Changing it needs `autostart` in the app's manifest (policy.rs; else Denied and "PERMDENY
autostart"); reading needs nothing.  The entry is named after the app (vfs::app_id; Linux:
the .desktop id, linux_desk.rs) and starts the running executable -- call autostart_set
again after the program moved (autostart_entry tells where the entry points).

Windows (win_autostart.rs): the value <app id> = "exe" args of
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run (arguments quoted with the Microsoft
rules).  The Task Manager's switch (Explorer\StartupApproved\Run, an odd first byte = off)
counts for autostart_get; autostart_set(true) clears it (the user asked in the app), false
removes both; in an MSIX package (HKCU virtualized) the package's StartupTask instead,
switched through WinRT (TaskId "Autostart"; it takes no arguments, a task the user switched
off in Settings stays off: Dismissed).  Linux (linux_autostart.rs): $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/<desktop id>.desktop
(XDG autostart; Hidden=true or X-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=false count as off), Exec quoted
as the Desktop Entry spec wants, $APPIMAGE instead of the executable when set.  In Flatpak
the Background portal (RequestBackground with autostart and the command line): the desktop
may ask the user, and the call waits for the answer (at most AUTOSTART_WAIT_MS); the sandbox
cannot see the host's autostart folder, so the answer is remembered in
config://autostart.  jfgui_AUTOSTART=portal / file picks the way (tests).  Web and
Android: Unavailable.
```

```rust
/// how long autostart_set waits for the Background portal's answer (the user may be asked)
AUTOSTART_WAIT_MS: i32 = 120_000
```

- **`enum AutostartError`**
  why autostart_set failed
  - `Unavailable` -- not possible here (web, Android, no session bus for the portal, an MSIX package without
    a StartupTask)
  - `Denied` -- the app's permissions lack `autostart`
  - `Dismissed` -- the user (or the desktop) refused it, or did not answer in time (the portal)
  - `Invalid` -- an argument with NUL, or a command line beyond the system's limit
  - `Failed(String)` -- the system refused or failed: what it said

- **`fn autostart_set(on: bool, args: &[&str]) -> Result<(), AutostartError>`**
  start this program with args when the user logs in (on), or not any more (off)

- **`fn autostart_get() -> bool`**
  whether the app starts at login (an entry of it is there and switched on)

- **`fn autostart_entry() -> Option<String>`**
  the command the app's entry starts, None without one

### `plat/pkg.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/pkg.rs`](../lib/plat/pkg.rs)

```text
pkg -- the package the running program comes from, and what its package system offers for
updates (lib/update builds on it; docs/UPDATES.md "Packages")

  packaged() -> Packaged          Msix(full name) (GetCurrentPackageFullName), Flatpak(app id)
                                  (/.flatpak-info; $FLATPAK_ID), AppImage(file) ($APPIMAGE, an
                                  absolute path), Snap ($SNAP), else Plain
  msix_updates() -> Result<MsixUpdates, String>   (Windows, in an MSIX package) the App
                                  Installer file the package came from (Package
                                  .GetAppInstallerInfo: its address) and, with one, whether it
                                  offers a newer version (Package.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync);
                                  WinRT through raw COM (win_winrt.rs)
  FlatpakMonitor                  (Linux, in a Flatpak) the portal's update monitor
                                  (linux_flatpak.rs): create(), poll(ms) -> UpdateAvailable,
                                  update(progress, cancel) -> the newest version installed
  flatpak_spawn_latest(args)      (Linux) the app's newest installed version started with args
                                  (the portal's Spawn, LATEST_VERSION) -> its pid
  restart_appimage(args) -> i32   (Linux) the AppImage file started again with args (its
                                  runtime unpacks the image that is now there): 0 / -1

Elsewhere (web, Android) packaged() is Plain and the rest answers "not available".
```

- **`enum Packaged`**
  where the running program comes from
  - `Plain` -- a program file of its own: a setup, a .deb or .rpm, a portable copy
  - `AppImage(String)` -- an AppImage: the .AppImage file (the program runs from a copy its runtime unpacked)
  - `Flatpak(String)` -- a Flatpak: the app id (the program's folder is the read-only /app)
  - `Msix(String)` -- an MSIX package: its full name (the install folder is read-only)
  - `Snap` -- a Snap (snapd updates it)

- **`fn packaged() -> Packaged`**
  the package the running program comes from

- **`struct MsixUpdates`**
  what App Installer knows about the running MSIX package (msix_updates)
  - `appinstaller: String` -- the address of the .appinstaller file the package was installed from ("": none -- the
    Store, Add-AppxPackage, a developer registration)
  - `availability: u32` -- Package.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync with an .appinstaller: 0 unknown, 1 no updates,
    2 available, 3 required, 4 error; without one 0

- **`fn msix_updates() -> Result<MsixUpdates, String>`**
  the App Installer file of the running MSIX package and whether it offers an update
  (Windows 10 1809 and later) -> Err: not in a package, or WinRT failed (its HRESULT)

- **`struct FlatpakUpdate`**
  UpdateAvailable of the Flatpak portal: the commits of the running, the installed and the
  remote version (an installed one newer than the running one: restart to use it)
  - `running: String`
  - `local: String`
  - `remote: String`

- **`struct FlatpakMonitor`**
  (not Linux) there is no Flatpak portal: create() fails

**`impl FlatpakMonitor`**

- **`fn create() -> Result<FlatpakMonitor, String>`**
- **`fn poll(&mut self, _ms: i32) -> Option<FlatpakUpdate>`**
- **`fn update(&mut self, _progress: &mut dyn FnMut(u32, u32, u32), _cancel: &dyn Fn() -> bool) -> Result<(), String>`**

- **`fn flatpak_spawn_latest(args: &[&str]) -> Result<u32, String>`**
  start this app's newest installed Flatpak version with args (the portal's Spawn with
  LATEST_VERSION; the same program inside it) -> its pid

- **`fn restart_appimage(args: &[&str]) -> i32`**
  start the running AppImage's file ($APPIMAGE) again with args: its runtime unpacks the
  image the file holds now (after an update) and runs it -> 0, -1 when not an AppImage or no
  process could be started

### `plat/linux_flatpak.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_flatpak.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_flatpak.rs)

```text
linux_flatpak -- (pkg.rs) the updates of a Flatpak app through org.freedesktop.portal.Flatpak

  FlatpakMonitor::create()   CreateUpdateMonitor({handle_token}) on the session bus; the
                             handle /org/freedesktop/portal/Flatpak/update_monitor/SENDER/TOKEN
                             is known before the call, so the signals are matched first
  poll(ms)                   the newest UpdateAvailable({running-commit, local-commit,
                             remote-commit}) that arrived within ms
  update(progress, cancel)   Update("", {}) and its Progress signals ({n_ops, op, progress,
                             status: 0 running, 1 nothing to do, 2 done, 3 failed; error,
                             error_message}) until the end
  drop                       Close()
  spawn_latest(args)         Spawn(cwd, argv, {}, {}, LATEST_VERSION, {}): the app's newest
                             installed version with the same program and these arguments

The portal (flatpak-portal, outside the sandbox) checks the app's remote every few minutes
(its --poll-timeout, 300 s by default) while a monitor exists; Update only installs a
version that asks for no more permissions than the running one.
```

- **`struct FlatpakMonitor`**
  the update monitor of this app (pkg::FlatpakMonitor)

**`impl FlatpakMonitor`**

- **`fn create() -> Result<FlatpakMonitor, String>`**
- **`fn poll(&mut self, ms: i32) -> Option<FlatpakUpdate>`**
  the newest UpdateAvailable within ms (0: only what has arrived)
- **`fn update(&mut self, progress: &mut dyn FnMut(u32, u32, u32), cancel: &dyn Fn() -> bool) -> Result<(), String>`**
  install the update: progress(op, n_ops, percent) for every Progress signal, cancel()
  asked between them (the portal's transaction itself cannot be stopped: Err after it)

### `plat/taskbar.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/taskbar.rs`](../lib/plat/taskbar.rs)

```text
taskbar -- the app's button in the taskbar or dock: progress, a badge, the jump list's tasks

  taskbar_progress(TaskbarProgress) -> bool   None, Normal(f), Paused(f), Error(f) or
                                   Indeterminate (f: 0.0 ..= 1.0)
  taskbar_badge(count, icon) -> bool   count 0 = no badge; icon: the overlay Windows shows on
                                   the button (straight ARGB, 16 x 16 at 100 %; ui draws one
                                   with the number), Linux docks show the count themselves
  taskbar_tasks(&[JumpTask]) -> bool   the "Tasks" of the button's jump list (Windows): each
                                   starts this program with its arguments -- with
                                   AF_SINGLE_INSTANCE they reach the running app as
                                   UIC_OPEN; empty = the jump list removed.  Linux: false
  taskbar_state() -> (TaskbarProgress, u32)   what was set last (progress, count)
  taskbar_badge_shown(count) -> bool   that badge (with its icon) is up already (ui skips
                                   drawing it again)
  taskbar_supported() -> bool      whether this system shows any of it
  app_user_model_id() -> Option<id>   (Windows) the explicit AppUserModelID the process runs
                                   under: the taskbar button and its pins, the jump list, the
                                   recent files and the notifications all go by it.  ui::main!
                                   sets PACKAGE's app id once the setup installed the program
                                   or --register registered it (assoc::app_id_boot); None:
                                   Windows derives an id from the program's path
  set_app_user_model_id(id) -> bool   (Windows) run under id from now on: before the first
                                   window.  false elsewhere, in an MSIX package (the
                                   package's id counts) and for an id Windows refuses (more
                                   than 128 characters, blanks)

The calls keep the state and return whether the system took it (Windows: also before the
window has its button -- it is applied when the button appears).  Setting what is already
shown does nothing (progress compared in per mille), so calling them every frame is cheap.
The tray's dry run
(tray::set_dry_run, jfgui_TRAY_DRYRUN=1; the UI's headless runs) prints "taskbar: ..."
instead.

Windows (win_taskbar.rs): ITaskbarList3 on the main window (SetProgressState,
SetProgressValue, SetOverlayIcon with the count as its text), applied again on the
registered message "TaskbarButtonCreated" (the first show, Explorer restarted);
ICustomDestinationList with IShellLinkW tasks (title through IPropertyStore PKEY_Title).
COM on the UI thread: call these from the UI thread.  Linux (linux_taskbar.rs): the signal
com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry.Update(application://<desktop id>.desktop, {progress,
progress-visible, count, count-visible}) on a session-bus connection kept open (docks drop
the state when it closes; Query is answered), understood by KDE Plasma, Ubuntu's dock /
Dash to Dock and Plank.  Linux knows no paused / error / indeterminate look (paused and
error show the bar, indeterminate none) and no jump list at run time (that is the .desktop
file's Actions).  Web and Android: nothing (false).
```

- **`enum TaskbarProgress`**
  what the taskbar button's progress bar shows
  - `None` -- no bar
  - `Normal(f32)` -- done so far (0.0 ..= 1.0)
  - `Paused(f32)` -- paused at (Windows: yellow)
  - `Error(f32)` -- failed at (Windows: red)
  - `Indeterminate` -- busy without a known end (Windows: a moving bar)

**`impl TaskbarProgress`**

- **`fn value(&self) -> f32`**
  the fraction done, clamped to 0.0 ..= 1.0 (None / Indeterminate: 0.0)

- **`struct JumpTask`**
  one task of the jump list: starts this program with args
  - `title: String` -- the row's text
  - `args: Vec<String>` -- the arguments after the program
  - `desc: String` -- its tooltip ("" = none)

- **`fn taskbar_progress(p: TaskbarProgress) -> bool`**
  show progress on the app's taskbar button -> false: not shown here

- **`fn taskbar_badge(count: u32, icon: Option<&TrayIcon>) -> bool`**
  a badge on the button: count (0 = none), icon = Windows' overlay (None: no overlay there)

- **`fn taskbar_tasks(tasks: &[JumpTask]) -> bool`**
  the tasks of the button's jump list (empty: none) -> false: no jump list here

- **`fn taskbar_badge_shown(count: u32) -> bool`**
  whether a badge with count is shown already (with its icon): the UI then need not draw it
  again

- **`fn taskbar_state() -> (TaskbarProgress, u32)`**
  what was set last: the progress and the badge's count

- **`fn taskbar_supported() -> bool`**
  whether this system shows the taskbar progress and badge

- **`fn app_user_model_id() -> Option<String>`**
  (Windows) the process's explicit AppUserModelID (what the shell holds:
  GetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID); None: the one Windows derives from the program's
  path (other systems: always None)

- **`fn set_app_user_model_id(id: &str) -> bool`**
  (Windows) run the process under the AppUserModelID id: before its first window -> false
  elsewhere, in an MSIX package and for an id Windows refuses

### `plat/assoc.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/assoc.rs`](../lib/plat/assoc.rs)

```text
assoc -- the app's file types and URL schemes (apps/NAME/PACKAGE filetypes= / schemes=)
registered for the running program without a setup: developer and portable builds.  The
setup (apps/installer), the .deb, MSIX and Flatpak declare them themselves (docs/PACKAGING.md).

  package() -> Package                what build_rs.py built in (JFGUI_PACKAGE: display,
                                      app_id, categories, filetypes, schemes; ui::main! hands
                                      it over with package_set); without it: the app's name,
                                      no types
  Package::parse(text)                that text ("key=value" lines)
  parse_types(text) -> [FileType]     "ext[,ext..]|mime|description[|own]; ..." -- every
                                      extension gets the app under "Open with"; "own" types
                                      also open with it by default
  parse_schemes(text) -> [scheme]     "scheme scheme ..." (';', ',' or blanks)
  reg_entries(app, display, exe, types, schemes, app_id) -> [RegValue]   the values below
                                      HKCU\Software\Classes the setup and assoc_register write
                                      (app_id: the program's AppUserModelID in its ProgIDs,
                                      "" = none)
  app_id_boot() -> Option<id>         (ui::main!, Windows) PACKAGE's app id as the process's
                                      explicit AppUserModelID (taskbar.rs) once the setup
                                      installed this program (install.ini beside it names the
                                      id) or --register registered it (the record names it);
                                      jfgui_AUMID=ID gives one, jfgui_AUMID=off none.  Every
                                      other program keeps the id Windows derives from its path
  assoc_conflicts(&Package) -> Result<[Conflict], AssocError>   the defaults of other
                                      programs a registration would replace
  assoc_register(&Package, take) -> Result<Registered, AssocError>   register this program;
                                      take(&Conflict) decides each default of another program
                                      (false: it stays, the app is only offered under "Open
                                      with"); a registration of before is undone first
  assoc_unregister() -> Result<bool, AssocError>   undo exactly what the record lists (false:
                                      nothing was registered)
  assoc_registered() -> Option<String>   the program the record names
  file_uri_path(arg) -> Option<String>   a local file:// URI as a path (Linux desktops hand
                                      files over as URIs for Exec=... %U)
  console_print(text)                 stdout, else the console the program was started from
                                      (Windows programs of the GUI subsystem: --register)

The record (config://assoc.list) lists every key, value and file the registration added and
what it replaced; unregistering removes those (a value only while it still holds what was
written) and puts back what was there.  Windows (win_assoc.rs): the setup's entries below
HKCU\Software\Classes -- the ProgID <app>.<ext> (description, DefaultIcon, shell\open\command
= "<exe>" "%1", AppUserModelID = the app id: what Windows asks of a handler with an explicit
id for the recent files of the type), .<ext>\OpenWithProgids, for own types the default and
Content Type of .<ext>, a scheme's key (URL:<display>, URL Protocol) -- then SHChangeNotify.
A default of another program is the extension's default value (HKCU or HKLM) or a key of the
same name with another command; the user's own choice in Windows' dialog (UserChoice, hashed) is never
changed (Conflict::fixed).  Linux (linux_assoc.rs): $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/<app_id>.desktop
(Exec with %U for schemes, else %F; MimeType=), own types as shared-mime-info XML in
$XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/packages/<app_id>.xml, the defaults of own types and schemes in
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mimeapps.list [Default Applications] (written directly, no xdg-mime); the
caches are refreshed by update-mime-database / update-desktop-database when they are there
(without update-mime-database the own types are known after the next system update of the
MIME database; the .desktop file needs no cache).  A default of another program is an entry
in a mimeapps.list or, without one, another installed .desktop file with that MIME type.
In an MSIX package or a Flatpak the package declares everything: Unavailable.  Web and
Android: Unavailable.

Not a permission of the manifest: only what PACKAGE declares is written, in the user's own
part of the system (HKCU, $XDG_*_HOME).
```

- **`struct FileType`**
  one file type of PACKAGE filetypes=
  - `exts: Vec<String>` -- lower case, without the dot
  - `mime: String`
  - `desc: String`
  - `own: bool` -- the app is the default program of these extensions

- **`struct Package`**
  what the app registers (apps/NAME/PACKAGE, built in by build_rs.py)
  - `app: String` -- the app's name (vfs::app_id): Windows ProgIDs &lt;app>.&lt;ext>
  - `display: String` -- PACKAGE display=: menus, "URL:&lt;display>"
  - `app_id: String` -- the reverse-DNS id (PACKAGE app_id=, else org.jflib.&lt;App>): the Linux .desktop id
  - `categories: String` -- PACKAGE categories= (the .desktop file)
  - `types: Vec<FileType>`
  - `schemes: Vec<String>`

- **`struct Conflict`**
  a default of another program that a registration would replace
  - `what: String` -- ".ext" (an own file type), "scheme:" (a URL scheme), a ProgID or a file that is in the way
  - `holder: String` -- who has it now: a ProgID or command (Windows), a .desktop id or file (Linux)
  - `fixed: bool` -- the user chose that program in the system's dialog (Windows UserChoice): it stays,
    take is not asked

- **`struct Registered`**
  what assoc_register did
  - `exe: String` -- the program the entries start
  - `types: usize` -- file types and schemes registered
  - `schemes: usize`
  - `kept: Vec<Conflict>` -- the defaults of other programs that stayed (take said no, or fixed)
  - `notes: Vec<String>` -- hints (a missing cache tool ...)

- **`enum AssocError`**
  why a registration failed
  - `Unavailable` -- not here: web, Android, an MSIX package or a Flatpak (the package declares the types)
  - `Empty` -- PACKAGE has no filetypes= and no schemes=
  - `Declined(Conflict)` -- a file of another program is in the way and take said no (Linux: the .desktop file)
  - `Failed(String)` -- the system refused or failed: what it said

- **`fn package_set(text: Option<&str>)`**
  (ui::main!) keep the built-in PACKAGE text (JFGUI_PACKAGE)

- **`fn package() -> Package`**
  what the app registers: the built-in PACKAGE, else the app's name without types

**`impl Package`**

- **`fn parse(text: &str) -> Package`**
  "key=value" lines: display, app_id, categories, filetypes, schemes (the app is
  vfs::app_id; missing values get the defaults of tools/pkgmeta.py)
- **`fn mime_of(&self, path: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  the MIME type of a file name by its extension (own file types first), None when unknown

- **`fn parse_types(text: &str) -> Vec<FileType>`**
  "ext[,ext..]|mime|description[|own]; ..." -> the valid entries

- **`fn parse_schemes(text: &str) -> Vec<String>`**
  "scheme scheme; ..." -> the valid schemes (lower case)

- **`struct RegValue`**
  a value below HKCU (reg_entries): key, name ("" = the default value), REG_SZ value
  - `key: String`
  - `name: String`
  - `value: String`
  - `root: String` -- RV_TREE: the app's own key it lies in (a ProgID, a scheme), removed as a whole
  - `kind: u8`

```rust
/// a value in a key of the app's own (RegValue::root)
RV_TREE: u8 = 0
/// a value in a shared key (.ext\OpenWithProgids): only the value is the app's
RV_SHARED: u8 = 1
/// the default (and Content Type) of an extension: the app becomes its default program
RV_DEFAULT: u8 = 2
```

- **`fn reg_entries(app: &str, display: &str, exe: &str, types: &[FileType], schemes: &[String], app_id: &str) -> Vec<RegValue>`**
  the HKCU values of the file types and schemes for the program exe (backslashes): the setup's
  and assoc_register's.  app_id: the AppUserModelID the program runs under ("" = none, Windows
  derives one): each ProgID names it (AppUserModelID), as Windows wants for the recent files
  of an explicit id

- **`fn assoc_conflicts(pkg: &Package) -> Result<Vec<Conflict>, AssocError>`**
  the defaults of other programs a registration of pkg would replace (nothing is written)

- **`fn assoc_register(pkg: &Package, take: &mut dyn FnMut(&Conflict) -> bool) -> Result<Registered, AssocError>`**
  register this program for pkg's file types and schemes; take(conflict) -> replace that
  default of another program

- **`fn assoc_unregister() -> Result<bool, AssocError>`**
  undo the registration of the record -> Ok(false) when there was none

- **`fn assoc_registered() -> Option<String>`**
  the program a registration of this app starts (the record), None without one

- **`fn app_id_boot() -> Option<String>`**
  (ui::main!) Windows: PACKAGE's app id as the process's explicit AppUserModelID when this
  program was installed by the setup (install.ini beside it names the id) or registered with
  --register (the record names this program); jfgui_AUMID=ID gives one, =off none -> the id
  set.  Other programs (and other systems) keep the id the system derives

- **`fn file_uri_path(arg: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  a local file:// URI as a path ("file:///home/a%20b.txt" -> "/home/a b.txt", Windows
  "file:///C:/a.txt" -> "C:/a.txt"); None for anything else (another host, no URI)

- **`fn console_print(text: &str)`**
  text on stdout, else (Windows, a GUI program started from a console) on the console of
  the parent process

- **`fn hkcu_get(sub: &str, name: Option<&str>) -> Option<String>`** *(Windows)*
  (tests, Windows) HKCU\\sub: name Some(n) its string value ("" = the default value), None:
  Some("") when the key exists

### `plat/recent.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/recent.rs`](../lib/plat/recent.rs)

```text
recent -- the system's list of recently used files

  recent_add(path) -> bool        a file the user opened or saved.  Windows:
                                  SHAddToRecentDocs (Explorer's recent files; the app's jump
                                  list shows it under "Recent" when the app is a registered
                                  handler of the type: the setup, assoc_register, MSIX; with
                                  the process's explicit AppUserModelID, taskbar.rs, the
                                  item is given to that id: SHARD_APPIDINFO).
                                  Linux: a bookmark in $XDG_DATA_HOME/recently-used.xbel (the
                                  freedesktop format GTK and KDE read: href, added / modified /
                                  visited, the MIME type, this app's entry with exec and count)
  recent_list(max) -> [path]      this app's files, newest first (Windows: the jump list's
                                  recent items, IApplicationDocumentLists; Linux: the
                                  bookmarks with an entry of this app)
  recent_remove(path) -> bool     the file out of the app's list (Windows: the jump list,
                                  IApplicationDestinations -- Explorer's recent files keep it;
                                  Linux: this app's entry, the bookmark when no other app is
                                  left in it)
  recent_clear() -> bool          every file of the app (RemoveAllDestinations; every entry of
                                  this app)
  recent_os(on)                   (ui::main!) off in headless runs (--script, --shot, the
                                  agent protocols): add / remove / clear leave the system's
                                  list alone and return false
  recent_list_of(id, max) / recent_remove_of(id, path)   (Windows, tests) the jump list of
                                  another AppUserModelID (Explorer's own recent files:
                                  Microsoft.Windows.Explorer)

The path must be readable under the app's permissions (fs.read / fs.user, policy.rs; else
"PERMDENY fs.read" and false) and be an OS file (a folder mount's file counts as its OS path;
mem:// and app:// do not).  jfgui_RECENT=off: nothing is read or written; jfgui_RECENT=
/path/x.xbel: that file instead of the system's list, on every OS (tests).  The xbel file is
changed under a lock (a sidecar file in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, else beside it) and replaced
atomically; other programs' bookmarks stay byte for byte.  GLib does not lock: a write of a
GTK program between our read and our rename can be lost (as between two GTK programs).  The
MIME type of a bookmark comes from the app's PACKAGE filetypes, else a short table, else
application/octet-stream.  In a Flatpak $XDG_DATA_HOME is the app's own folder: the host's
list needs --filesystem=xdg-data/recently-used.xbel (PACKAGE flatpak_args=) and is used
then.  Web and Android: false / empty.
```

- **`fn recent_os(on: bool)`**
  (ui::main!) false: add / remove / clear leave the system's list alone (headless runs)

- **`fn recent_add(path: &str) -> bool`**
  put a file the user opened or saved into the system's list of recent files

- **`fn recent_list(max: usize) -> Vec<String>`**
  this app's recent files, newest first (at most max)

- **`fn recent_remove(path: &str) -> bool`**
  take a file out of this app's recent files

- **`fn recent_clear() -> bool`**
  forget every recent file of this app

- **`fn recent_list_of(id: &str, max: usize) -> Vec<String>`** *(Windows)*
  (Windows, tests) the recent files of the jump list of AppUserModelID id

- **`fn recent_remove_of(id: &str, path: &str) -> bool`** *(Windows)*
  (Windows, tests) a file out of the jump list of AppUserModelID id (Explorer's own:
  Microsoft.Windows.Explorer)

### `plat/audio.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/audio.rs`](../lib/plat/audio.rs)

```text
audio -- sound output: streams the app fills, short sounds from memory or files, the
system's own sounds

  Stream::open(&Config) -> Result<Stream, AudioError>   the app pushes samples into the
                          stream's ring (write / write_i16; never blocks, takes what fits),
                          the platform drains it on its audio thread
  Stream::open_fill(&Config, fill)   fill(&mut [f32]) -> bool tops up the device's buffer
                          instead (false: this was the last buffer)
  s.write(&[f32]) / s.write_i16(&[i16]) -> frames taken;  s.writable(), s.queued()
  s.start() / s.pause() / s.stop() (empties the ring) / s.finish() (ends once all is played)
  s.set_volume(0 ..= 1), s.state() -> State, s.latency_ms(), s.played(), s.underruns(),
  s.device(), s.device_changes()
  play(&Sound) -> Result<Voice, AudioError>    a short sound through the shared mixer
  play_file(path)         a WAV or Ogg Vorbis file through the VFS (app://, data://, ..)
  Sound::wav(bytes) / ogg / decode / load(path) / tone(freq, ms)
  sound(SOUND_*) -> bool  the system's own sound for an event (dialog_sounds(): whether the
                          platform plays one when a message dialog opens)
  available() -> bool     an output device / sound service exists here

Samples are f32 in -1 ..= 1, interleaved frames (WAVE channel order: 1 mono, 2 left / right,
6 = 5.1); the device side always runs in f32 at the stream's rate (the system converts the
rate and the channels where needed; the browser's context rate is converted here).

One model everywhere: the ring.  The app writes, a platform thread drains -- this works on
all four targets, where a callback on the audio thread does not: the browser's audio runs in
an AudioWorklet that cannot call into the app's WASM instance, so it is fed from a buffer
anyway.  The ring also keeps app code (allocation, locks, the UI's pace) off the real-time
thread.  open_fill is the same stream without a ring: fill runs on the audio thread
(Windows, Linux, Android) or in the browser worker's pump, and must not block.

Latency: Config::latency_ms (default 40) is split between the device buffer (half, 10 ..= 100
ms) and the ring (the rest; writable() keeps the ring within it); a fill stream gives all of it
to the device buffer.  An app that writes from UI timers (16 ms frames) wants >= 50 ms.
A stream starts playing at once (silence until data arrives); pause() first to prefill.

Platforms: Windows WASAPI shared mode, event-driven on its own thread, the default device
followed through IMMNotificationClient (win_audio.rs); Linux the PulseAudio native protocol
(pipewire-pulse on current desktops, WSLg's server), the server moves the stream to a new
default device itself (linux_audio.rs); the browser WebAudio, an AudioWorklet fed from a
SharedArrayBuffer ring or posted buffers, started after a user gesture (State::Blocked
```
