```text
before; web_audio.rs, web/audio.js); Android AAudio through the JNI host (android_audio.rs,
android/bridge.c).  No device or service: AudioError::Unavailable.

play() mixes into one stream of 48 kHz stereo that opens on demand and ends after 2 s of
silence (each sound converted to 48 kHz once, while it plays).  System sounds: Windows the
sound scheme's aliases (PlaySound: SystemAsterisk, SystemExclamation, SystemHand,
SystemQuestion, .Default, Notification.Default), Linux the freedesktop sound theme
(dialog-information, dialog-warning, dialog-error, dialog-question, bell, message-new-instant
as .oga / .ogg / .wav, the theme of org.gnome.desktop.sound, only while its event-sounds
are on), Android the notification sound and ToneGenerator beeps, the browser short generated
tones (as Linux without a theme).  jfgui_AUDIO_DRYRUN=1 / set_dry_run: sound() only prints
"sound: NAME".

Permissions: an app with a manifest needs `audio.output` (policy.rs, docs/PERMISSIONS.md) for
every sound: open / open_fill / play / play_file give AudioError::Denied, sound() false
(also in a dry run), available() false; the refusal is recorded once per run as
"PERMDENY audio.output".
```

```rust
/// the default beep (Windows ".Default", freedesktop "bell")
SOUND_DEFAULT: u32 = 0
/// information (SystemAsterisk, dialog-information)
SOUND_INFO: u32 = 1
/// a warning (SystemExclamation, dialog-warning)
SOUND_WARNING: u32 = 2
/// an error (SystemHand, dialog-error)
SOUND_ERROR: u32 = 3
/// a question (SystemQuestion, dialog-question)
SOUND_QUESTION: u32 = 4
/// a notification (Notification.Default, message-new-instant)
SOUND_NOTIFY: u32 = 5
```

- **`enum AudioError`**
  why audio is not possible
  - `Unavailable` -- no output device or sound service here
  - `Invalid` -- a rate or channel count out of range
  - `Format` -- not a sound file read here (WAV PCM / float, Ogg Vorbis) or a damaged one
  - `Io` -- the file could not be read
  - `Failed(i32)` -- the system refused (its code: an HRESULT, a PulseAudio error, an AAudio result)
  - `Denied` -- the app's permissions lack `audio.output`

- **`enum State`**
  what a stream does
  - `Starting` -- the device is being opened (browser: until its host answers)
  - `Playing`
  - `Paused`
  - `Stopped` -- stop(): the ring emptied; start() plays again
  - `Ended` -- finish() or a fill that returned false: everything was played (start() plays again)
  - `Blocked` -- the browser waits for a user gesture before it plays sound
  - `Lost` -- no device right now (the old one went away); the stream plays again when one appears

- **`struct Config<'a>`**
  what a stream plays
  - `rate: u32` -- frames per second (8000 ..= 192000)
  - `channels: u16` -- interleaved channels (1 ..= 8)
  - `latency_ms: u32` -- the latency aimed for, device buffer and ring together (10 ..= 1000 ms)
  - `name: &'a str` -- the stream's name in the system's mixer ("" = the app's name)

**`impl Config<'static>`**

- **`const fn new(rate: u32, channels: u16) -> Config<'static>`**
  rate and channels, 40 ms, the app's name

- **`struct Stream`**
  an output stream

**`impl Stream`**

- **`fn open(cfg: &Config) -> Result<Stream, AudioError>`**
  a stream the app writes into (starts playing at once: silence until data arrives)
- **`fn open_fill<F: FnMut(&mut [f32]) -> bool + Send + 'static>(cfg: &Config, fill: F) -> Result<Stream, AudioError>`**
  a stream that calls fill to top up the device's buffer (on the platform's audio thread
  or the browser worker's pump; the buffer comes zeroed); fill returns false after its
  last buffer
- **`fn rate(&self) -> u32`**
  frames per second
- **`fn channels(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn write(&mut self, samples: &[f32]) -> usize`**
  interleaved samples into the ring -> whole frames taken (at most writable(); 0 for a
  fill stream)
- **`fn write_i16(&mut self, samples: &[i16]) -> usize`**
  the same for 16-bit samples
- **`fn writable(&self) -> usize`**
  frames write() takes now
- **`fn queued(&self) -> usize`**
  frames waiting in the ring
- **`fn start(&self)`**
  play (again): after pause(), stop() or the end
- **`fn pause(&self)`**
  hold: the queued frames stay
- **`fn stop(&self)`**
  stop and drop what is queued (ring and device buffer)
- **`fn finish(&self)`**
  no more data: the stream ends (State::Ended) once the ring is played
- **`fn set_volume(&self, v: f32)`**
  0 silent ..= 1 as written (applied here, ramped over one buffer)
- **`fn volume(&self) -> f32`**
- **`fn state(&self) -> State`**
- **`fn latency_ms(&self) -> f32`**
  what is written now is heard after about this long (ring, device buffer, the device's
  own latency; ms)
- **`fn played(&self) -> u64`**
  frames played so far (handed to the device minus its buffer)
- **`fn underruns(&self) -> u32`**
  how often the ring ran dry while data was coming (and the device's own count where
  it reports one)
- **`fn device(&self) -> String`**
  the output device's name ("" not known yet)
- **`fn device_changes(&self) -> u32`**
  how often the stream followed a new default device (or the server moved it)
- **`fn server_id(&self) -> u32`**
  (tests) the server's id of the stream: PulseAudio's sink input index (u32::MAX: none)
- **`fn test_device_change(&self)`**
  (tests) act as if the default device changed (Windows: reopen on the default device)
  or the server went away (Linux: the connection is dropped and made anew); the stream
  plays on, device_changes() counts it.  Elsewhere nothing happens.

- **`struct Sound`**
  decoded PCM: interleaved f32 samples (cheap to clone: shared)

**`impl Sound`**

- **`fn new(rate: u32, channels: u16, samples: Vec<f32>) -> Result<Sound, AudioError>`**
  interleaved samples (1 ..= 8 channels, 1 kHz ..= 384 kHz)
- **`fn wav(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Sound, AudioError>`**
  a RIFF WAVE file (PCM 8 / 16 / 24 / 32 bits, float 32 / 64)
- **`fn ogg(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Sound, AudioError>`**
  an Ogg Vorbis file (.ogg, .oga)
- **`fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Sound, AudioError>`**
  WAV or Ogg Vorbis, told apart by their first bytes
- **`fn load(path: &str) -> Result<Sound, AudioError>`**
  a sound file through the VFS (app://, data://, a path, ..)
- **`fn tone(freq: f32, ms: u32) -> Sound`**
  a sine of freq Hz, ms long, 48 kHz mono, at half scale with 5 ms fades
- **`fn rate(&self) -> u32`**
- **`fn channels(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn frames(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn samples(&self) -> &[f32]`**
- **`fn duration_ms(&self) -> u32`**
- **`fn to_wav(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  as a 16-bit PCM WAVE file

- **`struct Voice`**
  a sound play() started; dropping the handle lets it play on

**`impl Voice`**

- **`fn stop(&self)`**
  end it now
- **`fn playing(&self) -> bool`**
  still playing (or waiting for the device)
- **`fn set_volume(&self, v: f32)`**
  0 ..= 1

- **`fn play(s: &Sound) -> Result<Voice, AudioError>`**
  play a sound once, mixed with the other sounds of play() (dropping the Voice lets it play
  on) -> Err(Unavailable) without an output, Err(Denied) without `audio.output`

- **`fn play_file(path: &str) -> Result<Voice, AudioError>`**
  play a WAV or Ogg Vorbis file once (see play; without `audio.output` the file is not read)

- **`fn set_dry_run(on: bool)`**
  true: sound() only prints "sound: NAME" (headless runs; also jfgui_AUDIO_DRYRUN=1)

- **`fn sound_name(kind: u32) -> &'static str`**
  the name of a SOUND_\* kind ("default", "information", "warning", "error", "question",
  "notify"; "" for others)

- **`fn sound(kind: u32) -> bool`**
  the system's sound for an event (SOUND_\*) -> false: nothing played (unknown kind, sounds
  switched off by the system, no output, no `audio.output`)

- **`fn dialog_sounds() -> bool`**
  whether message dialogs play the system's sound when they open (Windows like MessageBox;
  Linux desktops while event sounds are on; not Android, not the browser)

- **`fn available() -> bool`**
  an output device / sound service exists here (a quick probe; false without `audio.output`,
  nothing recorded)

- **`fn level(samples: &[f32], channels: usize, ch: usize, rate: u32, freq: f32) -> f32`**
  (tests) the amplitude of the sine at freq in channel ch of interleaved frames (Goertzel,
  Hann window: a full-scale sine reads 1.0)

- **`fn resample(samples: &[f32], channels: usize, from: u32, to: u32) -> Vec<f32>`**
  (tests) samples converted from one rate to another by the streams' resampler

- **`fn ring_check(n: usize, piece: usize, take: usize, threaded: bool) -> bool`**
  (tests) the ring of a push stream: n samples written in pieces of `piece` and read in
  pieces of `take`, by turns or (threaded, Windows / Linux) by a writer thread while this one
  reads -> whether every sample arrived once and in order

- **`fn theme_path(kind: u32) -> Option<String>`** *(Linux)*
  (tests, Linux) the sound theme's file for a SOUND_\* kind (".disabled": switched off)

### `plat/screen.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/screen.rs`](../lib/plat/screen.rs)

```text
screen -- the monitors, the colour of any pixel on the screen, pictures of the screen

  monitors() -> Vec<Monitor>        every monitor: id, name, rectangle and work area (desktop
                                    units), dpi, refresh rate, the primary one first; when the
                                    set or one of them changes, E_SETTINGS with SET_MONITORS
  monitor_at(x, y) -> Option<Monitor>   the monitor holding a desktop point, else the primary
  pick_available() -> bool          the user can pick a colour outside the app's windows here
  pick_start() -> Result<(), ScreenError>   the user clicks a pixel anywhere on the screen (Esc
                                    or a right click cancels); the answer is ScreenEvent::Color
  capture_available() -> bool       pictures of the screen can be taken here
  capture_start(rect) -> Result<(), ScreenError>   a picture of the whole desktop (None) or
                                    of a rectangle (desktop units); needs `screen.capture` in
                                    the manifest (else Denied, "PERMDENY screen.capture"); the
                                    answer is ScreenEvent::Shot
  screen_take() -> Vec<ScreenEvent> the answers since the last call (each one calls wake())
  pick_test_point(Some((x, y)))     (test aid) the next pick_start answers the pixel at the
                                    desktop point x, y without asking the user (Windows,
                                    X11; the portal and the browser ignore it)

One pick and one capture at a time (else Busy).  Picking needs no right: the user chooses
the one pixel the app gets, like a file in the file dialog.  Call pick_start and
capture_start from the UI thread: their answers are made there (Windows, X11) or on a thread
of their own (the portal), and arrive through the event loop.

Windows (win_screen.rs): EnumDisplayMonitors + GetMonitorInfoW (device name, work area,
primary), GetDpiForMonitor (shcore), EnumDisplaySettingsW (refresh), WM_DISPLAYCHANGE and a
changed work area -> SET_MONITORS; capture: BitBlt (CAPTUREBLT) from the screen DC into a DIB
section; pick: a topmost window over the virtual desktop showing a frozen picture of it with
a magnifier at the pointer.  Linux (linux_screen.rs): X11 RandR 1.5 (GetMonitors, the CRTC's
mode for the refresh rate, _NET_WORKAREA, RRScreenChangeNotify), GetImage of the root window,
a pointer grab for the pick; Wayland wl_output (+ zxdg_output_v1 for logical position and
size; no work area, no primary: the first output); in Wayland sessions and in Flatpak the
screenshot portal (Screenshot, PickColor: the desktop asks the user).  Browser: the host's
window.screen (getScreenDetails when the page may), the EyeDropper API (Chromium) for the
pick, no capture.  Android: the host's DisplayManager displays, no pick, no capture.
```

- **`struct Monitor`**
  one monitor
  - `id: u64` -- stable while the monitor stays connected (Windows: a hash of its device name, X11 the
    RandR monitor's name atom, Wayland the output's global name, browser / Android an index)
  - `name: String` -- the system's name ("\\\\.\\DISPLAY1", "HDMI-1", "rdp-0"); "" when unknown
  - `rect: [i32; 4]` -- x, y, w, h in desktop units: physical pixels on Windows, X11 and Android; the
    compositor's logical units on Wayland; CSS pixels in the browser
  - `work: [i32; 4]` -- the part windows should use (without taskbars, docks, panels); = rect where unknown
  - `dpi: u32` -- 96 = 100 %
  - `refresh_mhz: u32` -- refresh rate in mHz (60000 = 60 Hz), 0 = unknown
  - `primary: bool` -- the primary monitor (exactly one in a non-empty list)

- **`enum ScreenError`**
  why a pick or a capture did not happen
  - `Unavailable` -- not possible here (browser without EyeDropper, Android, no X server / portal)
  - `Denied` -- the app's permissions lack `screen.capture`, or the system / the user refused
  - `Cancelled` -- the user cancelled (Esc, a right click, the portal's dialog dismissed)
  - `Busy` -- a pick (or capture) is still running
  - `Failed(String)` -- the system failed: what it said

- **`struct Shot`**
  a picture of the screen
  - `rect: [i32; 4]` -- where it was taken: x, y, w, h in desktop units ([0, 0, w, h] when the system did not
    say: the portal)
  - `w: i32` -- size in pixels
  - `h: i32`
  - `px: Vec<u8>` -- w x h pixels B, G, R, x (rows of w \* 4 bytes); empty when `file` holds the picture
  - `file: Option<(String, Vec<u8>)>` -- the picture as the system wrote it (the screenshot portal's PNG): its name and bytes

- **`enum ScreenEvent`**
  an answer of pick_start / capture_start
  - `Color(Result<u32, ScreenError>)` -- the picked colour 0xRRGGBB
  - `Shot(Result<Shot, ScreenError>)` -- the picture

- **`fn screen_take() -> Vec<ScreenEvent>`**
  the answers since the last call, oldest first

- **`fn monitors() -> Vec<Monitor>`**
  every monitor, the primary one first (empty when nothing is known: Linux before the first
  window, headless runs)

- **`fn monitor_at(x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<Monitor>`**
  the monitor holding the desktop point x, y, else the primary one

- **`fn pick_available() -> bool`**
  whether the user can pick a colour anywhere on the screen here

- **`fn pick_start() -> Result<(), ScreenError>`**
  the user picks a pixel anywhere on the screen; the answer comes as ScreenEvent::Color

- **`fn pick_test_point(p: Option<(i32, i32)>)`**
  (test aid) the next pick_start answers the pixel at the desktop point x, y at once,
  without asking the user (Windows, X11; the portal and the browser ignore it); None: ask
  again

- **`fn capture_available() -> bool`**
  whether pictures of the screen can be taken here (the permission is checked when taking)

- **`fn capture_start(rect: Option<[i32; 4]>) -> Result<(), ScreenError>`**
  a picture of the whole desktop (None) or of the rectangle x, y, w, h (desktop units); the
  answer comes as ScreenEvent::Shot.  The screenshot portal takes the whole screen (or what
  the user chooses in its dialog) whatever rect says.

- **`fn shot_pixel(s: &Shot, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<u32>`**
  the pixel 0xRRGGBB at x, y of a shot's B, G, R, x rows (None outside)

### `plat/hotkey.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/hotkey.rs`](../lib/plat/hotkey.rs)

```text
hotkey -- global keyboard shortcuts: chords that reach the app while another program has the
keyboard

  Chord::parse("Ctrl+Alt+K") -> Option<Chord>   modifiers ctrl, alt, shift, super (win, meta,
                                    logo), one key: a-z 0-9 f1-f24, space enter tab esc
                                    backspace delete insert home end pageup pagedown left up
                                    right down print pause num0-num9 numadd numsub nummul
                                    numdiv numdec minus plus comma period (case ignored)
  chord.text() -> "Ctrl+Alt+K"      chord.trigger() -> "CTRL+ALT+k" (the XDG shortcuts
                                    notation of the GlobalShortcuts portal)
  hotkey_available() -> bool        global shortcuts work here
  hotkey_register(id, chord, description) -> Result<(), HotkeyError>   id != 0; the same id
                                    again replaces its chord; needs `input.global` in the
                                    manifest (else Denied, "PERMDENY input.global")
  hotkey_unregister(id) -> bool     hotkey_clear()   hotkey_list() -> [(id, chord)]
  hotkey_take() -> Vec<HotkeyEvent> Pressed(id) when the chord was pressed anywhere (held keys
                                    do not repeat), Refused(id, why) when the desktop refused
                                    a registration later (the portal); each one calls wake()
  set_dry_run(on)                   only record registrations (the UI's headless runs);
                                    hotkey_test_press(id) delivers a press (test aid)

Call register / unregister from the UI thread: the presses arrive through its event loop.
Windows (win_hotkey.rs): RegisterHotKey (MOD_NOREPEAT) on a message-only window of the UI
thread, WM_HOTKEY; a chord another program holds is Conflict.  X11 (linux_x11_screen.rs):
XGrabKey on the root window for every keycode of the key and every combination of Caps Lock
and Num Lock, KeyPress on the root window; BadAccess (another client grabbed it) is
Conflict.  Wayland and Flatpak (linux_hotkey.rs): the GlobalShortcuts portal on a thread of
its own: a session, BindShortcuts with the description and the preferred trigger -- the
desktop asks the user, who may choose another chord or none; what is not bound comes as
Refused(id, Dismissed); Activated -> Pressed.  Browser and Android: Unavailable.
```

- **`struct Chord`**
  a key with modifiers: VK code (the platform's E_KEY_DOWN codes) and MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL |
  MOD_ALT | MOD_SUPER
  - `vk: u32`
  - `mods: u8`

- **`enum HotkeyError`**
  why a shortcut was not registered
  - `Unavailable` -- no global shortcuts here (browser, Android, no X server / portal)
  - `Denied` -- the app's permissions lack `input.global`
  - `Invalid` -- id 0, a key without a name, a description with NUL
  - `Conflict` -- another program (or another id of this app) holds the chord
  - `Dismissed` -- the user or the desktop did not bind it (the portal's dialog)
  - `Failed(String)` -- the system failed: what it said

- **`enum HotkeyEvent`**
  what happened to a registered shortcut
  - `Pressed(u32)` -- its chord was pressed
  - `Refused(u32, HotkeyError)` -- the desktop did not bind it after all (the portal answers later)

**`impl Chord`**

- **`fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Chord>`**
  "Ctrl+Alt+K", "super+f12", "Shift+NumAdd" -> the chord (None: no key, an unknown name,
  two keys)
- **`fn text(&self) -> String`**
  "Ctrl+Alt+K" (the modifiers in the order Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Super)
- **`fn trigger(&self) -> Option<String>`**
  the XDG shortcuts notation ("CTRL+ALT+k", "LOGO+F12"): modifiers CTRL ALT SHIFT LOGO,
  the key as its xkb keysym name; None for a key without one

- **`fn hotkey_take() -> Vec<HotkeyEvent>`**
  what happened since the last call, oldest first

- **`fn set_dry_run(on: bool)`**
  only record registrations from now on (the UI's headless runs: scripts, --shot)

- **`fn hotkey_available() -> bool`**
  whether global shortcuts work here

- **`fn hotkey_register(id: u32, chord: Chord, description: &str) -> Result<(), HotkeyError>`**
  register chord as the global shortcut id (the same id again replaces it); description says
  what it does (the portal's dialog shows it)

- **`fn hotkey_unregister(id: u32) -> bool`**
  remove the shortcut id -> false when it was not registered

- **`fn hotkey_clear()`**
  remove every shortcut of the app

- **`fn hotkey_list() -> Vec<(u32, Chord)>`**
  the registered shortcuts: (id, chord)

- **`fn hotkey_test_press(id: u32) -> bool`**
  (test aid) a press of the registered shortcut id, as the system would report it -> false
  when id is not registered

### `plat/log.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/log.rs`](../lib/plat/log.rs)

```text
log -- the process's log: levels, a ring of the newest lines for crash reports, stderr
and a rotating file

  LOG_ERROR 1, LOG_WARN 2, LOG_INFO 3, LOG_DEBUG 4, LOG_TRACE 5 (LOG_OFF 0)
  log!(LOG_INFO, "net", "{} bytes from {}", n, host)   formats only when the level is on
  log_line(level, target, msg)         one line; log_error / log_warn / log_info /
                                       log_debug(target, msg) are short forms
  log_quiet(level, target, msg)        ring and file only (the text went to stderr already)
  log_enabled(level) -> bool           any sink wants this level
  log_levels(stderr, file)             the levels of the sinks (default WARN / INFO; the
                                       ring keeps everything up to DEBUG); jfgui_LOG=error |
                                       warn | info | debug | trace sets both
  log_file(Some(path), max_bytes, keep) -> bool   append the lines to path (a vfs name like
                                       logs://app.log or an OS path); when it grows
                                       beyond max_bytes it moves to path.1 (path.1 to path.2,
                                       ... up to keep files) and a new one starts; None stops
  log_recent(max_bytes) -> String      the newest whole lines of the ring (a crash report,
                                       a "copy log" button)

Lines: "2026-10-17 19:58:07.123 WARN  net: text" (Windows local time, elsewhere UTC with a
Z); line breaks inside the text become " | ".  The ring holds 64 KiB.  A crash or panic
writes the ring to stderr and to the log file before the app's crash hook runs (rt::crash
pre-hook, installed with the first line); it takes the locks only if they are free, so a
thread that crashed while logging cannot stop the report.
```

```rust
LOG_OFF: u32 = 0
LOG_ERROR: u32 = 1
LOG_WARN: u32 = 2
LOG_INFO: u32 = 3
LOG_DEBUG: u32 = 4
LOG_TRACE: u32 = 5
```

- **`fn log_levels(stderr: u32, file: u32)`**
  set the levels of stderr and the file (jfgui_LOG wins over both)

- **`fn log_enabled(level: u32) -> bool`**
  any sink wants lines of this level

- **`fn log_line(level: u32, target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  one line to every sink that wants its level

- **`fn log_quiet(level: u32, target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  one line to the ring and the file only (its text went to stderr already)

- **`fn log_error(target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  a LOG_ERROR line

- **`fn log_warn(target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  a LOG_WARN line

- **`fn log_info(target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  a LOG_INFO line

- **`fn log_debug(target: &str, msg: &str)`**
  a LOG_DEBUG line

- **`fn log_fmt(level: u32, target: &str, args: core::fmt::Arguments)`**
  (log!) a formatted line

- **`log!(...)`**
  log!(LOG_INFO, "target", "format", args...): a line, formatted only when its level is on

- **`fn log_recent(max_bytes: usize) -> String`**
  the newest whole lines of the ring, at most max_bytes

- **`fn log_file(path: Option<&str>, max_bytes: u64, keep: u32) -> bool`**
  write the lines to path (rotated at max_bytes, keep older files path.1 .. path.keep);
  None stops -> false when the file cannot be opened

### `plat/a11y.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/a11y.rs`](../lib/plat/a11y.rs)

```text
a11y -- the accessibility tree for screen readers and other assistive technology

The UI (ui/a11y.rs) turns the semantic records of every frame into a Snapshot and publishes
it here; the platform bridge serves it from threads of its own and hands the actions of the
assistive technology back to the UI thread:

  start(app)                   start the bridge (once; the UI's first window frame)
  active() -> bool             assistive technology may be listening: publish snapshots
  publish(Snapshot)            the new tree; its differences to the last one become events
                               (focus, states, names, values, text, children, windows)
  take() -> Vec<Request>       the actions asked for since the last call (UI thread)
  request(Request)             (bridges, tests) queue an action and wake the UI thread
  current() -> Option<Arc<Snapshot>>   (bridges) the tree last published
  set_translator(f) / role_name(role) / role_text(k)   the names of the roles the bridges
                               give (UIA LocalizedControlType, AT-SPI GetLocalizedRoleName) in
                               the UI language: ROLE_TEXTS holds them in German, the keys of
                               the UI's translation (ui registers i18n::tr; plat cannot ask
                               ui itself); without one they stay German

Linux: AT-SPI2 on the accessibility bus (linux_atspi.rs).  Windows: UI Automation providers
answering WM_GETOBJECT (win_uia.rs).  The browser and Android (web_a11y.rs): the host keeps
a mirror of the tree -- an ARIA shadow tree in the DOM (web/a11y.js), virtual views of an
AccessibilityNodeProvider (android/GalleryAccessibility.java) -- fed with the differences
of every published tree (a11y_wire.rs: Mirror, the wire format); the host turns the mirror
on (active() follows it) and sends the actions back.

A Snapshot holds every shown window (WinTree) with its nodes in the order of the UI's
records; Node::parent gives the hierarchy (NONE: a top-level node of the window), link()
adds the sibling links and the key index the bridges navigate with.  A node's key stays the
same from frame to frame while its widget does (the UI derives it from the widget id).
```

```rust
/// no node (Node::parent of a top-level node, WinTree::focus without a focused node)
NONE: u32 = u32::MAX
```

- **`enum Role`**
  what a node is
  - `Group` -- a container without a meaning of its own (a titled box)
  - `Label`
  - `Button`
  - `CheckBox`
  - `Radio`
  - `Switch` -- an on / off switch
  - `Slider`
  - `Progress`
  - `TextBox`
  - `Link`
  - `List` -- a selectable list and its rows
  - `ListItem`
  - `MenuBar` -- the menu bar, a menu (a menu bar entry or a popup menu) and its entries
  - `Menu`
  - `MenuItem`
  - `TabList` -- the strip of tabs and one tab
  - `Tab`
  - `Combo` -- a drop-down list (Node::text: the current choice)
  - `Image`
  - `Canvas` -- a drawing surface (charts, the app's own views)
  - `Dialog`
  - `Heading` -- a heading of a document or section (Node::value: its level, level())

```rust
/// Node::state: the keyboard focus is on the node
S_FOCUSED: u32 = 1
/// it can take the keyboard focus
S_FOCUSABLE: u32 = 2
/// greyed out: no input, no actions
S_DISABLED: u32 = 4
/// a check box, radio button or switch that is on
S_CHECKED: u32 = 8
/// a check box in the third state ("some")
S_MIXED: u32 = 16
/// a selected list row or tab
S_SELECTED: u32 = 32
/// an open drop-down, menu or dialog
S_EXPANDED: u32 = 64
/// a button shown pressed (a toggle or tool button that is on)
S_PRESSED: u32 = 128
/// a text box with several lines
S_MULTILINE: u32 = 256
/// a password box (its text: one dot per character)
S_PROTECTED: u32 = 512
/// a text box that can be read and selected but not edited
S_READONLY: u32 = 1024
/// Node::actions: press, toggle, select, open / close -- what a click on the widget does
A_CLICK: u32 = 1
/// give it the keyboard focus
A_FOCUS: u32 = 2
/// set a number (sliders)
A_VALUE: u32 = 4
/// set the text (text boxes)
A_TEXT: u32 = 8
```

- **`struct Node`**
  one element of a window
  - `key: u64` -- identity within its window, the same from frame to frame (never 0)
  - `role: Role`
  - `state: u32` -- S_\*
  - `actions: u32` -- A_\*
  - `rect: [i32; 4]` -- x, y, w, h: physical px of the window's client area
  - `name: String`
  - `text: String` -- text boxes: their text; combo boxes: the current choice; else empty
  - `caret: i32` -- text boxes: the caret in characters (-1 unknown)
  - `anchor: i32` -- text boxes: the other end of the selection in characters (== caret: nothing selected)
  - `caret_rect: [i32; 4]` -- text boxes: the caret's rectangle, physical px of the client area (w, h 0: unknown) --
    screen magnifiers follow it (char_rect)
  - `value: f64` -- sliders and progress bars: value in min ..= max (value &lt; min: progress unknown);
    headings: the level (1 ..= 9)
  - `min: f64`
  - `max: f64`
  - `step: f64`
  - `parent: u32` -- index of the parent node in WinTree::nodes (NONE: a top-level node)
  - `first: u32` -- (link) first child, next and previous sibling (NONE: none), number of children,
    position among the siblings
  - `next: u32`
  - `prev: u32`
  - `count: u32`
  - `index: u32`

- **`struct WinTree`**
  one shown window
  - `win: u8` -- the UI's window index (0 = the main window)
  - `pw: i32` -- its platform window (plat::win_\*; -1 none)
  - `title: String`
  - `dialog: bool` -- a dialog window (modal)
  - `active: bool` -- it has the keyboard
  - `origin: [i32; 2]` -- screen position of the client area (px; 0, 0 when the platform does not tell)
  - `size: [i32; 2]` -- client size (px)
  - `nodes: Vec<Node>`
  - `focus: u32` -- the focused node (NONE: the window itself)
  - `first: u32` -- (link) the first top-level node, their number
  - `count: u32`
  - `keys: Vec<(u64, u32)>` -- (link) key -> node index, sorted by key

- **`struct Snapshot`**
  the whole application
  - `app: String` -- the application's name
  - `wins: Vec<WinTree>`

**`impl Node`**

- **`fn text_str(&self) -> &str`**
  the text the text interfaces see: text boxes and drop-downs their text, labels their name
- **`fn level(&self) -> u32`**
  a heading's level 1 ..= 9 (0: not a heading)
- **`fn selection(&self) -> (i32, i32)`**
  the selection of a text box: (start, end) in characters, start == end at the caret
- **`fn char_rect(&self, k: i32) -> [i32; 4]`**
  the rectangle of character k (client px): exact at the caret of a focused text box
  (caret_rect), around it estimated from the line height (lines after '\\n', columns of
  about half a line height); without a caret the characters share the node's width
- **`fn offset_at(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32`**
  the character offset nearest to client point x, y (char_rect's inverse; -1: outside)

**`impl WinTree`**

- **`fn link(&mut self)`**
  fill the links (first / next / prev / count / index, the key index) from the parents
- **`fn find(&self, key: u64) -> Option<usize>`**
  the node with this key
- **`fn children(&self, parent: u32) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> + '_`**
  the children of a node (NONE: the top-level nodes), in order
- **`fn child(&self, parent: u32, k: usize) -> Option<usize>`**
  the child number k of a node (NONE: of the window)
- **`fn at_point(&self, x: i32, y: i32) -> Option<usize>`**
  the deepest node at a client point (px): among siblings the last one wins (drawn on top)
- **`fn on_screen(&self, n: &Node) -> bool`**
  the node lies (partly) inside the window's client area (else it is scrolled away)
- **`fn focus_key(&self) -> u64`**
  the focused node's key (0: the window itself)

**`impl Snapshot`**

- **`fn win(&self, win: u8) -> Option<&WinTree>`**
  the tree of the UI's window index win
- **`fn pw(&self, pw: i32) -> Option<&WinTree>`**
  the tree of platform window pw

- **`enum Change`**
  what changed between two snapshots (window: the UI's window index; key 0: the window)
  - `Window(u8, bool)` -- a window appeared (true) or went away
  - `Activate(u8, bool)` -- a window got (true) or lost the keyboard
  - `Focus(u8, u64)` -- the keyboard focus moved to this node (in the active window)
  - `State(u8, u64, u32, bool)` -- state bit S_\* of a node went on (true) or off
  - `Name(u8, u64)`
  - `Value(u8, u64)` -- the number of a slider / progress bar, the level of a heading
  - `Text(u8, u64, String)` -- the text of a text box / combo box (the old text)
  - `Caret(u8, u64, i32)` -- the caret of a text box (characters)
  - `Added(u8, u64, u64)` -- a node (with its subtree) appeared: parent key (0: the window), its key; in the order
    of the new tree, so its index there is right when the event arrives
  - `Removed(u8, u64, u64, u32)` -- a node (with its subtree) went away: parent key (0: the window), its key, its index
    there before; the last index of a parent first

- **`fn diff(old: &Snapshot, new: &Snapshot) -> Vec<Change>`**
  the changes from old to new

- **`enum Act`**
  an action of the assistive technology
  - `Click` -- press, toggle, select, open / close: what a click does (A_CLICK)
  - `Focus` -- the keyboard focus (A_FOCUS)
  - `Value(f64)` -- a new number (A_VALUE)
  - `Text(String)` -- a new text (A_TEXT)
  - `Select(i32, i32)` -- (text boxes, A_FOCUS) the selection from anchor to caret in characters (equal: the caret
    alone); a box without the focus gets it first

- **`struct Request`**
  an action for a node
  - `win: u8` -- the UI's window index
  - `key: u64`
  - `act: Act`

- **`fn start(app: &str)`**
  start the platform bridge (once): Linux connects to the accessibility bus when assistive
  technology is enabled (jfgui_A11Y=1 forces it, jfgui_A11Y=0 or NO_AT_BRIDGE=1 turn it off);
  Windows answers WM_GETOBJECT from now on; the browser and Android hosts turn their mirror
  on themselves (jfgui_a11y), jfgui_A11Y=0 keeps it off there too

- **`fn active() -> bool`**
  assistive technology may be listening (the UI publishes snapshots only then)

- **`fn current() -> Option<Arc<Snapshot>>`**
  the tree last published

- **`fn publish(mut s: Snapshot)`**
  publish a new tree: the links are filled, the differences to the last tree go to the bridge

- **`fn request(r: Request)`**
  (bridges, tests) queue an action and wake the UI thread (the oldest is dropped when 64 wait)

- **`fn take() -> Vec<Request>`**
  the actions asked for since the last call, oldest first (UI thread)

*the texts of the bridges*

```rust
/// what the bridges call the roles (UIA LocalizedControlType, AT-SPI GetLocalizedRoleName) in
/// Role order, then a window (AT-SPI frame), the application and an unknown role: in German,
/// the keys of their translations (set_translator; ui's i18n::tr has them in its languages)
ROLE_TEXTS: [&str; 25] = [ "Bereich", "Bezeichnung", "Schaltfläche", "Kontrollkäst ...
/// ROLE_TEXTS: a window
ROLE_WINDOW: usize = 22
/// ROLE_TEXTS: the application
ROLE_APP: usize = 23
/// ROLE_TEXTS: an unknown role
ROLE_UNKNOWN: usize = 24
```

- **`fn set_translator(f: fn(&'static str) -> &'static str)`**
  the translation of the bridges' texts into the UI language (ui sets i18n::tr with its first
  frame; it reads the language each time, so the texts follow a change of it); without one
  they stay German

- **`fn role_text(k: usize) -> &'static str`**
  ROLE_TEXTS[k] in the UI language

- **`fn role_name(r: Role) -> &'static str`**
  what the bridges call a role, in the UI language

### `plat/a11y_wire.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/a11y_wire.rs`](../lib/plat/a11y_wire.rs)

```text
a11y_wire -- the accessibility tree for hosts that keep a mirror of it (the browser's ARIA
shadow tree, Android's virtual views; web_a11y.rs): every published tree becomes its
differences to the tree the host has, in a byte format that web/a11y.js and
android/GalleryAccessibility.java read.  Compiled on every target (plattest checks it).

  Mirror::default()      nothing sent yet: the next update is a full one
  Mirror::update(&tree, &changes, place) -> Option<Vec<u8>>
                         the update for the host (None: nothing it shows changed); place
                         gives a window's client area in host px (x, y, w, h)
  Mirror::reset()        the host lost its mirror: the next update is a full one

The format: integers little-endian, str = u32 byte count + UTF-8, key = u64 (Node::key)
  u8 VERSION, u8 flags (F_FULL: the host drops its mirror first), u8 number of windows
  every shown window in the order of the snapshot (later ones lie on top):
    u8 window index, u8 flags (W_DIALOG, W_ACTIVE), i32 x, y, w, h (place),
    key of the focused node (0: none), str title,
    u32 order count (UNCHANGED: the same nodes as before), then per node in tree order:
        key, u32 parent (its position in this list; UNCHANGED: a top-level node) --
        the nodes of the window that are not in the list are gone
    u32 node count, then the nodes that are new or changed: key, u8 role (Role in
        declaration order: Group 0 .. Dialog 20, Heading 21), u32 state (S_*), u32 actions
        (A_*), i32 x, y, w, h, str name, str text, i32 caret, i32 anchor, i32 caret x, y, w,
        h, f64 value (headings: the level), min, max, step
  windows that are not listed are gone
  u32 number of events, each: u8 kind (E_*), u8 window, key, i32 a, i32 b, and for E_TEXT
    str old text -- the events of plat::a11y::diff without Added / Removed (the order
    tells those)
```

```rust
/// the first byte of an update
VERSION: u8 = 1
/// update flag: a full update (the host drops what it has)
F_FULL: u8 = 1
/// window flags
W_DIALOG: u8 = 1
W_ACTIVE: u8 = 2
/// order count: the window's nodes are the same as before; parent: a top-level node
UNCHANGED: u32 = u32::MAX
/// events: a window appeared (a 1) or went away
E_WINDOW: u8 = 1
/// the window got (a 1) or lost the keyboard
E_ACTIVE: u8 = 2
/// the keyboard focus moved to the node
E_FOCUS: u8 = 3
/// state bit a (S_*) went on (b 1) or off
E_STATE: u8 = 4
E_NAME: u8 = 5
E_VALUE: u8 = 6
/// the text changed (the old one follows)
E_TEXT: u8 = 7
/// the caret moved to character a
E_CARET: u8 = 8
```

- **`struct Mirror`**
  what the host has: the last tree sent and its window headers

**`impl Mirror`**

- **`const fn new() -> Self`**
- **`fn reset(&mut self)`**
  the host lost its mirror (or turned it off): the next update is a full one
- **`fn update(&mut self, s: &Arc<Snapshot>, changes: &[Change], place: &dyn Fn(&WinTree) -> [i32; 4]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the update that brings the host from the last tree sent to s (changes: plat::a11y::diff
  of the two); None when nothing the host shows changed

### `plat/settings.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/settings.rs`](../lib/plat/settings.rs)

```text
settings -- the user's system settings the UI follows

  sys_settings() -> SysSettings       the system's (Windows: system calls and the registry;
                                      Linux: the settings portal, at most 300 ms; elsewhere
                                      the defaults), then the jfgui_* overrides
  sys_settings_env() -> SysSettings   the defaults and the overrides only (headless runs)

Overrides (tests, shots, users): jfgui_THEME=dark|light, jfgui_ACCENT=RRGGBB,
jfgui_CONTRAST=high|normal, jfgui_REDUCE_MOTION=1|0, jfgui_TEXT_SCALE=PERCENT,

jfgui_FONT_AA=1|0, jfgui_FONT_HINTING=none|slight|medium|full,
jfgui_FONT_RGBA=none|rgb|bgr|vrgb|vbgr.

Font rendering (font_aa, font_hinting, font_rgba; None: the system says nothing): Windows
SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHING, SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGTYPE (ClearType: subpixels) and
SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGORIENTATION; Linux the portal's org.gnome.desktop.interface
```

**`impl HcColors`**

- **`const WHITE: HcColors = HcColors { bg: 0xFFFFFF, text: 0x000000, highlight: 0x370 ...`**

```rust
/// SysSettings::font_hinting
FONT_HINT_NONE: u8 = 0
FONT_HINT_SLIGHT: u8 = 1
FONT_HINT_MEDIUM: u8 = 2
FONT_HINT_FULL: u8 = 3
/// SysSettings::font_rgba: the order of a pixel's subpixels (none: greyscale smoothing)
FONT_RGBA_NONE: u8 = 0
```

- **`fn font_hint_parse(s: &str) -> Option<u8>`**

- **`struct SysSettings`**

  - `accent: Option<u32>` -- 0xRRGGBB
  - `high_contrast: bool`
  - `contrast_colors: Option<HcColors>` -- Windows: the colours of the active high-contrast scheme
  - `reduce_motion: bool`
  - `text_scale: u32` -- percent, 100 = normal
  - `double_click_ms: u32`
  - `caret_blink_ms: u32` -- one phase of the caret (on or off); 0 = steady
  - `font_aa: Option<bool>` -- font smoothing: Some(false) = off (sharp black-and-white glyphs)

  - `font_rgba: Option<u8>` -- FONT_RGBA_\* (subpixel smoothing and its order)

### `plat/guarded.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/guarded.rs`](../lib/plat/guarded.rs)

```text
guarded -- the public file functions: a name with a scheme goes to its vfs provider
(vfs.rs), any other name is checked against the app's permissions (policy.rs) and then
handed to the OS call (win_sys.rs, linux_sys.rs, web_files.rs: the *_raw functions, which
the platform layer uses for its own system files)

trash(path) moves into the trash (trash.rs) and counts as writing the path.
A refused path looks like a missing or unreadable one: 0 / None / false.
File and FileLock hold an OS file (also behind a folder mount: os_path) or a stream of a
mount (Provider::open: MemFs, Bundle, ZipFs, Overlay, Sub; other providers: the whole file,
read at the start and written back by sync and drop); a FileLock on a mount without OS
files holds inside this process only.
AtomicFile is write_file in pieces: a sibling (OS: OsAtomic of win_sys / linux_sys /
web_files / android_files; mounts: "NAME.tmp-.." in the mount) put in place by commit,
removed when dropped; content:// (no rename over a document): the bytes in memory, written
in place by commit (aio.rs builds the async writes and copies on it).
```

- **`fn file_exists(path: &str) -> u32`**
  0 missing, 1 file, 2 directory  [plat_file_exists]

- **`fn file_exists_checked(path: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Some(0) only for a missing path, Some(1/2) for file/directory, None for other errors.

- **`fn mkdir(path: &str) -> bool`**
  create a directory and its missing parents; an existing directory is fine  [plat_mkdir]

- **`fn delete(path: &str) -> bool`**
  a file or an empty directory  [plat_delete]

- **`fn trash(path: &str) -> bool`**
  move a file or folder into the trash (Windows: the recycle bin; Linux: the freedesktop
  trash) -> false: it stays where it was, never deleted for good (trash.rs).  Counts as
  writing the path; a vfs name needs a folder mount.

- **`fn rename(old: &str, new: &str) -> bool`**
  rename, replacing an existing target (both names on the OS or in the same mount)  [plat_rename]

- **`fn dir_list(path: &str, f: &mut dyn FnMut(&str, bool, u32)) -> bool`**
  f(name, is_dir, size_lo) for every entry except "." and ".."  [plat_dir_list]

- **`fn read_file(path: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the contents of a file  [plat_file_read]

- **`fn write_file(path: &str, data: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  Write an exclusively created sibling, flush it, then replace path (a mount: its own way of
  replacing a file; missing folders are created). [plat_file_write]

- **`struct File(Inner)`**
  an open file (closed when dropped): an OS file, or a stream of a vfs mount

**`impl File`**

- **`fn open(path: &str, mode: u32) -> Option<File>`**
  FO_READ (existing, read only), FO_WRITE (create / truncate), FO_RW (open or create);
  on every mount (vfs.rs)
- **`fn create_new(path: &str) -> Option<File>`**
  Create a named file exclusively; never open an existing path (a mount without OS
  files: exclusive inside this process).
- **`fn open_temp(dir: Option<&str>) -> Option<File>`**
  a new file without a lasting name in dir (None = temp_dir) that disappears when it is
  closed (also after a crash); a mount without OS files: a file in memory  [plat_file_open_temp]
- **`fn read_at(&self, off: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Option<usize>`**
  bytes read at off (fewer at the end of the file), None on an error before any byte
- **`fn write_at(&self, off: u64, buf: &[u8]) -> Option<usize>`**
  bytes written at off (the file grows as needed), None on an error before any byte
- **`fn size(&self) -> Option<u64>`**
- **`fn sync(&self) -> bool`**
  write cached data to the disk (a mount: where its readers find it)
- **`fn set_len(&self, len: u64) -> bool`**
  cut or extend the file to `len` bytes

- **`struct AtomicFile(Option<AtomicInner>)`**
  The streaming form of write_file: the bytes go into a sibling of the target, commit puts
  it in place in one step (readers see the old file or all of the new one); dropped without
  commit, the sibling is removed and the target is unchanged.  Checked and routed like
  write_file when it is created.  OS paths: an exclusive "NAME.tmp-PID-SEQ-TIME" beside the
  file, fsync and rename (Linux keeps the old file's access bits; the browser: in memory until
  commit).  Mounts: a "NAME.tmp-.." file of the mount, renamed by the provider (one without
  rename gets the whole file written); a provider whose rename cannot replace a file
  (`atomic_rename() == false`, content://) gets the bytes written in place at commit.

**`impl AtomicFile`**

- **`fn create(path: &str) -> Option<AtomicFile>`**
  a writer of path (None: refused, a folder, an invalid name, or the sibling could not be
  created)
- **`fn write_at(&self, off: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Option<usize>`**
  bytes written at off (the file grows as needed), None on an error
- **`fn commit(mut self) -> bool`**
  put the written file in place -> false: the target is unchanged, the sibling gone

- **`struct FileLock(LockInner)`**
  Nonblocking exclusive sidecar lock; drop releases it.  All cooperating writers must lock
  the same path before checking and replacing data.  OS files: across processes (Windows: an
  exclusive handle, Linux: flock); a mount without OS files: inside this process.

**`impl FileLock`**

- **`fn acquire(path: &str) -> Option<Self>`**
  Open or create without truncating. None means busy, invalid path, refused or I/O failure.

### `plat/pool.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/pool.rs`](../lib/plat/pool.rs)

```text
pool -- the worker thread pool: parallel loops and background jobs     [src/core/thread.s]

  thr_init(n) -> workers          start the pool once: n workers (0 = cpu_count), at most
                                  THR_MAX; `--threads N` on the command line wins.  Later
                                  calls return the count; every function below starts it
  thr_count() -> workers          thr_shutdown()   stop and join the workers (no job running)
  parallel_for(count, &f) -> Ok / Err(Cancelled)
       f(index, job) for 0..count on the workers AND the calling thread; returns when every
       item is done.  f may call job.cancel() to skip the remaining items.  Nested loops
       (from inside f) are fine.
  Job: a background job -- set(count, f), start() (false: still running), wait(),
       cancel(), done(), items_done().  When it finishes the pool calls wake() (E_WAKE).
  thr_self() -> slot              0..n-1 on worker k, n on any other thread: per-thread
                                  arrays of thr_count() + 1 entries

Design (as in ASMLIB): one queue of runnable jobs under a short spin lock (loops at the
head, background jobs at the tail).  A thread takes part in a job by counting itself in
`active` under the lock, then claims item indexes with fetch_add on `next`.  The thread
that sees every index handed out (or the cancel flag) unlinks the job; the last one to
leave finishes it: state DONE (from then on the owner may drop the record), wake() for
background jobs, and every thread sleeping in a job wait is woken.  Idle workers spin
briefly, then sleep on a semaphore; waiters spin, then sleep on a second one at most
WAIT_POLL_MS at a time (a semaphore post may be taken by another waiter).  Work depends
only on the item index, so results are the same for any number of threads.

The loop record lives on the caller's stack and holds a pointer to the borrowed closure:
parallel_for returns only after the last participant left, which is what makes handing
the borrow to the workers sound (the unsafe below).
```

```rust
THR_MAX: usize = 64
```

- **`struct Cancelled`**
  a loop or job ended through cancel()

- **`struct JobCtl`**
  a job as its item functions see it: cancel the rest, look at the progress

**`impl JobCtl`**

- **`fn cancel(&self)`**
  skip the items not started yet (callable from inside an item)  [thr_job_cancel]
- **`fn cancelled(&self) -> bool`**
  long items poll this
- **`fn count(&self) -> u64`**
- **`fn items_done(&self) -> u64`**
  items finished so far (progress = items_done / count)

- **`fn thr_init(n: u32) -> u32`**
  start the pool (once): the number of worker threads  [thr_init]

- **`fn thr_count() -> u32`**
  the number of worker threads (starts the pool on first use)  [thr_count]

- **`fn thr_shutdown()`**
  stop the workers once the queue is empty, join them; a later call starts a new pool

- **`fn parallel_for(count: usize, f: &(dyn Fn(usize, &JobCtl) + Sync)) -> Result<(), Cancelled>`**
  f(index, job) for every index in 0..count, on the workers and this thread  [thr_parallel_for]

- **`struct Job`**
  a background job: count items of f on the workers; wake() when it is finished

**`impl Job`**

- **`fn new() -> Job`**
- **`fn set(&mut self, count: u64, f: impl Fn(usize, &JobCtl) + Send + Sync + 'static) -> bool`**
  the work of the next start: count items of f (false while the job runs)
- **`fn set_count(&mut self, count: u64) -> bool`**
  another item count for the same function (false while the job runs)
- **`fn start(&self) -> bool`**
  run it in the background; false: it is still running  [thr_job_start]
- **`fn wait(&self) -> Result<(), Cancelled>`**
  block until the job is finished (this thread helps with items not taken yet)
- **`fn cancel(&self)`**
  skip the items not started yet; the job still finishes (wake)
- **`fn done(&self) -> bool`**
  finished (or never started)
- **`fn items_done(&self) -> u64`**
- **`fn count(&self) -> u64`**

- **`fn thr_self() -> usize`**
  the calling thread's slot: k on worker k, the worker count on any other thread  [thr_self]

### `plat/task.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/task.rs`](../lib/plat/task.rs)

```text
task -- async execution: core::future on the thread that owns an executor, blocking work on
a pool, timers, cancellation, joins                                              (task.rs)

  Executor::ui()                  the executor of the UI thread: a wake-up from another thread
                                  posts plat::wake (E_WAKE); lib/ui runs it between passes
                                  (ui.spawn), web / Android from the host's frame callback
  Executor::new()                 an executor that parks its thread (block_on, console programs)
  exec.spawn(fut) -> Task<T>      fut runs on the executor's thread (it need not be Send)
  exec.spawner() -> Spawner       spawn from inside tasks (a clone moves into them)
  exec.run() -> polled            fire the thread's due timers, run queued blocking jobs where
                                  there are no threads, poll every woken task once
  exec.accept_remote() -> bool    (Executor::ui) take the wake-ups that came from other threads;
                                  the UI calls it for E_WAKE, so headless scripts see them only
                                  at `sync` (deterministic)
  exec.has_ready() / busy() / live()   work to poll now / work in flight (`sync`) / tasks alive
  exec.block_on(fut), block_on(fut)    run until fut is done (spawned tasks run alongside)
  Task<T>: is_done / is_cancelled / take / cancel / detach; awaiting it gives Result<T,
           Cancelled>; dropping the handle cancels the task (detach keeps it running)
  spawn_blocking(f) -> Blocking<T>     f on a thread of the blocking pool (files, network,
                                  parallel_for); spawn_cancellable(f(&token)): token is
                                  cancelled once nobody awaits the result (a job not started
                                  then never starts).  A caller inside policy's trusted() keeps
                                  that on the pool thread.  blocking_pending() -> jobs in flight
  sleep(ms) / sleep_until(us)     timers of the polling thread's executor on now_us()
  now_us() / clock_set(Some(us) | None)   the task clock: time_us(), or the virtual clock of
                                  headless UI runs (scripts' `wait`)
  next_timer() -> Option<us>      the earliest timer of this thread (event loop deadlines)
  CancelToken: cancel / is_cancelled / check / cancelled() future / run(fut) -> Result<T,
               Cancelled> (fut is dropped when the token wins)
  Progress: set_total / set / add / done / total / permille / changed() future; a report
            wakes the event loop (at most every PROGRESS_WAKE_MS, always at the end)
  join(a, b) / join3(a, b, c) / join_all(v) / select(a, b) -> Either / yield_now()

Design.  An executor keeps its tasks in slots; a task's Waker (alloc::task::Wake, no unsafe)
names slot and version and queues itself once until it is polled again.  Wake-ups on the
owning thread go to the local list, those from other threads to the remote list plus a signal
(plat::wake for the UI, the park semaphore for block_on); the UI takes remote ones only with
E_WAKE.  Timers live in one list with the thread that registered them; each executor fires
its own.  Blocking jobs run on up to BLOCKING_MAX threads of their own (not the compute pool:
a job waiting for a disk must not starve parallel_for); where no thread can start (the
browser without shared memory, Android) the executors run them inline, one per run.  A panic
in a task or job ends the process like any panic (rt's handler: crash hook, exit code 3).
```

```rust
/// threads of the blocking pool at most (more jobs wait in its queue)
BLOCKING_MAX: u32 = 8
/// a Progress report wakes the event loop at most this often (the last one always)
PROGRESS_WAKE_MS: u64 = 30
```

- **`fn now_us() -> u64`**
  the task clock in microseconds: time_us(), or the virtual time clock_set gave

- **`fn clock_set(us: Option<u64>)`**
  Some(us): the task clock stands at us until the next call (headless UI runs drive it with
  the script's virtual clock); None: back to time_us()

- **`struct Executor`**
  one thread's tasks (see the head of task.rs)

**`impl Executor`**

- **`fn ui() -> Executor`**
  the UI thread's executor: other threads' wake-ups post plat::wake (E_WAKE)
- **`fn new() -> Executor`**
  an executor that parks this thread while it waits (block_on)
- **`fn spawner(&self) -> Spawner`**
  a handle that spawns onto this executor (from inside its tasks)
- **`fn spawn<F: Future + 'static>(&self, fut: F) -> Task<F::Output>`**
  run fut on this executor's thread; it starts with the next run()
- **`fn accept_remote(&mut self) -> bool`**
  take the wake-ups other threads sent (the UI calls it for E_WAKE) -> any
- **`fn run(&mut self) -> usize`**
  fire this thread's due timers, run a queued blocking job where no thread can start,
  poll every woken task once -> the number of polls
- **`fn has_ready(&self) -> bool`**
  tasks to poll now (woken or new, a blocking job to run inline)
- **`fn busy(&self) -> bool`**
  work in flight: ready tasks, wake-ups of other threads not taken yet, blocking jobs
  (the scripts' `sync` waits until it is false; tasks waiting for timers do not count)
- **`fn live(&self) -> usize`**
  tasks alive (spawned, not finished)
- **`fn block_on<F: Future>(&mut self, fut: F) -> F::Output`**
  run until fut is done; the executor's other tasks run alongside.  The thread sleeps on a
  semaphore between wake-ups (Executor::ui: it only yields)

- **`fn block_on<F: Future>(fut: F) -> F::Output`**
  run fut to its end on this thread (a parking executor; console programs, tests)

- **`struct Spawner`**
  spawns onto the executor it came from (clone it into tasks)

**`impl Spawner`**

- **`fn spawn<F: Future + 'static>(&self, fut: F) -> Task<F::Output>`**
  run fut on the executor's thread; it starts with the executor's next run

- **`struct Task<T>`**
  the handle of a spawned task; dropping it cancels the task (detach keeps it running)

**`impl<T> Task<T>`**

- **`fn is_done(&self) -> bool`**
  finished, cancelled or dropped by its executor (the future is gone or goes with the
  executor's next run)
- **`fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool`**
  it ended without a value: cancel() came first, or its executor went away
- **`fn take(&self) -> Option<T>`**
  the result, once (None: still running, cancelled or already taken)
- **`fn cancel(&self)`**
  stop the task: its future is dropped at the executor's next run (a finished task keeps
  its result)
- **`fn detach(mut self)`**
  let the task run on without a handle

- **`fn sleep(ms: u32) -> Sleep`**
  a future ready ms milliseconds of the task clock from now

- **`fn sleep_until(at_us: u64) -> Sleep`**
  a future ready when the task clock reaches at_us

- **`struct Sleep`**
  the future of sleep / sleep_until

**`impl Sleep`**

- **`fn deadline(&self) -> u64`**
  when it is ready (task clock, us)

- **`fn fire_timers(now: u64) -> usize`**
  wake this thread's timers that are due at now, earliest deadline first -> how many

- **`fn next_timer() -> Option<u64>`**
  the earliest timer of this thread (task clock, us)

- **`fn yield_now() -> YieldNow`**
  a future that lets the executor's other tasks run once

- **`struct YieldNow(bool)`**
  the future of yield_now

- **`fn blocking_pending() -> u32`**
  blocking jobs submitted and not finished yet (every executor's)

- **`struct Blocking<T>`**
  the result of spawn_blocking: a future of f's value

- **`fn spawn_blocking<T: Send + 'static>(f: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> Blocking<T>`**
  run f on the blocking pool (a thread of its own: files, network, parallel_for loops)

- **`fn spawn_cancellable<T: Send + 'static>(f: impl FnOnce(&CancelToken) -> T + Send + 'static) -> Blocking<T>`**
  run f on the blocking pool; its token is cancelled when the Blocking future is dropped
  before the result was taken (a job not started yet is skipped)

**`impl<T> Blocking<T>`**

- **`fn is_done(&self) -> bool`**
  the job has finished (polling gives its value now)

- **`struct CancelToken(Arc<CancelInner>)`**
  a shared cancel flag: cancel() from any thread, checked between chunks of work or awaited

**`impl CancelToken`**

- **`fn new() -> CancelToken`**
  a token that is not cancelled
- **`fn cancel(&self)`**
  set the flag; every cancelled() future and run() wrapper wakes up
- **`fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool`**
  cancel() was called
- **`fn check(&self) -> Result<(), Cancelled>`**
  Err(Cancelled) once the token is cancelled (`token.check()?` between chunks)
- **`fn cancelled(&self) -> WaitCancelled`**
  a future that is ready once the token is cancelled
- **`fn run<F: Future>(&self, fut: F) -> Guarded<F>`**
  fut until the token is cancelled: Ok(its value), or Err(Cancelled) (fut is dropped)

- **`struct WaitCancelled`**
  the future of CancelToken::cancelled

- **`struct Guarded<F: Future>`**
  the future of CancelToken::run

- **`struct Progress(Arc<ProgInner>)`**
  the progress of an operation: the worker reports, the UI reads (cheap clones share it)

**`impl Progress`**

- **`fn new() -> Progress`**
  nothing done, total unknown
- **`fn set_total(&self, n: u64)`**
  the amount of work (bytes, items); 0 = unknown
- **`fn set(&self, done: u64)`**
  the work done so far
- **`fn add(&self, n: u64)`**
  n more done
- **`fn done(&self) -> u64`**
  the work done so far
- **`fn total(&self) -> u64`**
  the amount of work (0: unknown)
- **`fn permille(&self) -> u32`**
  done / total in 0..=1000 (0 while the total is unknown)
- **`fn reports(&self) -> u64`**
  reports so far (changed() waits for the next one)
- **`fn changed(&self) -> Changed`**
  a future that is ready after the next report

- **`struct Changed`**
  the future of Progress::changed

- **`struct Join<A: Future, B: Future>(MaybeDone<A>, MaybeDone<B>)`**
  the future of join

- **`fn join<A: Future, B: Future>(a: A, b: B) -> Join<A, B>`**
  both futures, concurrently on the same task -> (a's value, b's value)

- **`struct Join3<A: Future, B: Future, C: Future>(MaybeDone<A>, MaybeDone<B>, MaybeDone<C>)`**
  the future of join3

- **`fn join3<A: Future, B: Future, C: Future>(a: A, b: B, c: C) -> Join3<A, B, C>`**
  three futures concurrently -> their values

- **`struct JoinAll<F: Future>(Vec<MaybeDone<F>>)`**
  the future of join_all

- **`fn join_all<F: Future>(v: impl IntoIterator<Item = F>) -> JoinAll<F>`**
  every future concurrently -> their values in order

- **`enum Either<A, B>`**
  which of two futures finished first
  - `Left(A)`
  - `Right(B)`

- **`struct Select<A: Future, B: Future>(Pin<Box<A>>, Pin<Box<B>>)`**
  the future of select

- **`fn select<A: Future, B: Future>(a: A, b: B) -> Select<A, B>`**
  the first of two futures to finish (polled in order a, b); the other one is dropped

### `plat/aio.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/aio.rs`](../lib/plat/aio.rs)

```text
aio -- files without blocking the calling thread: the work runs on the blocking pool
(task.rs) in chunks, with progress and cancellation between the chunks           (aio.rs)

  read_file(path, &ctl) -> future of Result<Vec<u8>, IoError>
  write_file(path, data, &ctl) -> future of Result<(), IoError>   atomic like write_file:
                        AtomicFile (a sibling written in chunks, put in place by the commit);
                        cancelled or failed, the sibling is removed and the old file stays
  copy_file(src, dst, &ctl) -> future of Result<u64, IoError>     src read in chunks into an
                        AtomicFile of dst -> the bytes copied
  Reader::open(path) -> reader;  reader.read(max).await -> the next chunk ([] at the end),
                        size() / pos() / seek(pos): a plat::File (OS file or a mount's stream)
                        read chunk by chunk, each chunk a job of the pool
  Writer::create(path) -> writer;  writer.write(data).await, writer.commit().await: an
                        AtomicFile filled chunk by chunk (dropped without commit: discarded)
  Ctl { progress, cancel, chunk }   what an operation reports to (bytes done / total) and
                        listens to; clones share both

Names, routing and permissions are those of the blocking functions (guarded.rs, vfs.rs): the
same calls, made on a pool thread (a caller inside policy's trusted() stays trusted there).
A cancel is seen between chunks: the operation cleans up and ends with Err(Cancelled).
Dropping one of the futures cancels it the same way.  Where no thread can start (browser,
Android) the pool's jobs run on the event loop's thread between frames.
```

```rust
/// the chunk of read_file / write_file / copy_file unless Ctl says otherwise
CHUNK: usize = 256 * 1024
```

- **`enum IoError`**
  why a file operation failed
  - `Open` -- the source is missing, refused (permissions) or no file
  - `Create` -- the target (its sibling) could not be created: refused, a folder, no such folder
  - `Read`
  - `Write`
  - `Commit` -- the finished file could not be put in place
  - `Cancelled` -- the CancelToken was cancelled (or the future dropped) before the end

- **`struct Ctl`**
  progress and cancellation of one operation (clones share them)
  - `progress: Progress` -- bytes done and the total (set when the size is known)
  - `cancel: CancelToken` -- cancel() stops the operation at the next chunk
  - `chunk: usize` -- bytes per chunk (0: CHUNK)

**`impl Ctl`**

- **`fn new() -> Ctl`**
  a fresh Progress and CancelToken, CHUNK bytes per chunk

- **`fn read_file(path: &str, ctl: &Ctl) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<u8>, IoError>> + use<>`**
  the contents of a file, read in chunks on the pool

- **`fn write_file(path: &str, data: Vec<u8>, ctl: &Ctl) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), IoError>> + use<>`**
  write data in chunks into an AtomicFile of path, then put it in place

- **`fn copy_file(src: &str, dst: &str, ctl: &Ctl) -> impl Future<Output = Result<u64, IoError>> + use<>`**
  copy src to dst (atomic like write_file) in chunks -> the bytes copied

- **`struct Reader`**
  a file read chunk by chunk on the pool

**`impl Reader`**

- **`fn open(path: &str) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Reader, IoError>> + use<>`**
  open path for reading (on the pool)
- **`fn size(&self) -> u64`**
  the size when it was opened
- **`fn pos(&self) -> u64`**
  where the next read starts
- **`fn seek(&mut self, pos: u64)`**
  the next read starts at pos
- **`async fn read(&mut self, max: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, IoError>`**
  the next chunk of at most max bytes (empty at the end of the file)

- **`struct Writer`**
  an AtomicFile filled chunk by chunk on the pool; dropped without commit, it is discarded
  (the sibling is removed by whoever drops the last reference: the dropping thread, or the
  pool when a write was still running)

**`impl Writer`**

- **`fn create(path: &str) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Writer, IoError>> + use<>`**
  a writer of path (checked and routed like write_file; on the pool)
- **`fn written(&self) -> u64`**
  bytes written so far
- **`async fn write(&mut self, data: Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), IoError>`**
  append data (on the pool)
- **`async fn commit(mut self) -> Result<(), IoError>`**
  put the written file in place (on the pool)

### `plat/win_api.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_api.rs`](../lib/plat/win_api.rs)

```text
win_api -- the window-indexed platform API on Windows: windows (records), input, the event
wait, presentation, cursors                                     [src/plat/win/win_window.s]
(popups: win_popup.rs; clipboard, IME, drops: win_clip.rs; file dialog: win_filedlg.rs;
 pens: win_pen.rs; shell, theme, home, drives, spawn_self: win_shell.rs)

  win_create(title, w_dip, h_dip, flags, owner, x, y) -> index / -1
       owner PW_NOOWNER: a top-level window (WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, preferably index 0); else
       a window owned by window `owner`: WS_POPUP | WS_CAPTION | WS_SYSMENU (+ WS_THICKFRAME
       with PWF_RESIZABLE), WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW for PWF_TOOL (no taskbar button, not in
       Alt+Tab), WS_EX_NOACTIVATE for PWF_NOACTIVATE.  Created hidden; x, y = client origin
       (PW_DEFAULT: system default / owner client origin + 32 px).  Without PWF_SYSFRAME the
       caption is removed (the library draws the frame; DWM keeps shadow and corners).
  win_destroy(w)                    win_show(w, PWS_HIDE / SHOW / SHOWNA)
  win_activate(w)                   win_enable(w, on)
  win_set_rect(w, x, y, cw, ch)     client origin (screen px) and size; PW_KEEP
  win_get_rect(w) -> [x, y, w, h]   client origin + client size (None: no window)
  win_work_area(w) -> [x, y, w, h]  work area of the window's monitor
  win_set_title(w, utf8)            win_state(w) -> WST_* (WST_ACTIVE: the app is active)
  win_cmd(w, WCMD_*)                win_begin_move(w)  win_begin_resize(w, edges)
  win_size(w) -> (w, h)             win_dpi(w) -> 96 = 100 %
  win_set_min_size(w, w_dip, h_dip) (also before the window exists)
  win_present(w, frame, rects)      rects x, y, w, h; None = all.  The window keeps a copy
                                    of the presented pixels (a DIB section the rectangles
                                    are copied into and BitBlt from): WM_PAINT repaints from
                                    it.
  win_set_cursor(w, shape)          CUR_* or a custom cursor CUR_USER0..CUR_TABLE-1
  cursor_create(px, w, h, hot_x, hot_y, dpi) -> CUR_USER0 + k / -1   a cursor from
                                    premultiplied ARGB pixels (rows of w * 4 bytes,
                                    1..CUR_MAX_PX; CreateIconIndirect)
  cursor_destroy(id)                cursor_dpi(dpi) -> the dpi to draw cursors for (the
                                    window's own on Windows)
  win_hit_hook(f)                   f(w, x, y) -> HB_* flags of the UI at a client point
                                    (WM_NCHITTEST, WM_MOUSEACTIVATE)
  win_move_hook(f)                  f(w, &mut [x, y, w, h]) may snap the client rectangle
                                    (screen px) the user drags window w to (WM_MOVING)
  wait(deadline_us) -> queued events   0 = poll, u64::MAX = forever, else plat::time_us()
  set_refresh(f)                    f() redraws during the modal move / size loop
  win_test_send(w, msg, wp, lp)     (test aid) SendMessageW to window w (input, hit test,
                                    activation, size-move messages: no pointers); more test
                                    aids in win_test.rs (win_test, file_dialog_autoclose)
(the single-window window_create / present / ... are in pwin0.rs)

Library frame (no PWF_SYSFRAME, AF_CUSTOM_TITLEBAR for the main window): the caption is
removed (WM_NCCALCSIZE) while the resize borders, shadow and rounded corners stay;
WM_NCHITTEST asks the UI hit boxes (hit hook): HB_DRAG moves the window, HB_MAX gives snap
layouts (main window), the caption buttons are drawn by the UI.
Every event carries its window (Event::win).  The window procedure never acts on input: it
only records events into the ring (evq.rs); it re-enters (SendMessage, SetWindowPos), so
the window of the events it pushes is saved and restored.
The owner keeps looking active while one of its own windows is active: WM_NCACTIVATE (FALSE)
is drawn active unless the whole app loses the activation (WM_ACTIVATEAPP).
Tool windows are not activated by clicks (WM_MOUSEACTIVATE -> MA_NOACTIVATE) unless the
click hits a text box: the keyboard stays with the main window.

State: everything lives on the UI thread (the thread that creates the windows runs their
window procedure); the records are Cells, so the re-entrant window procedure and the
callbacks (refresh, hit hook) never hold a reference across a Win32 call.
```

- **`fn win_create(title: &str, w_dip: i32, h_dip: i32, flags: u32, owner: i32, x: i32, y: i32) -> i32`**
  a hidden window (see the file header) -> index / -1  [plat_win_create]

- **`fn win_hit_hook(f: Option<fn(i32, i32, i32) -> u32>)`**
  f(w, x, y) -> HB_\* flags at a client point (None = no hit tests)

- **`fn win_move_hook(f: Option<fn(i32, &mut [i32; 4])>)`**
  f(w, &mut [x, y, w, h]) -> the client rectangle (screen px) the user drags window w to, as
  the UI wants it (snapped); called inside the modal move loop (None = no hook)

- **`fn set_refresh(f: Option<fn()>)`**
  f() redraws during the modal move / size loop

- **`fn wait_refresh(deadline_us: u64, refresh: &mut dyn FnMut()) -> u32`**
  wait() with a redraw closure for the modal move / size loop: refresh() runs (instead of the
  set_refresh hook) whenever the window must redraw before the loop returns  [main agent]

- **`fn wait(deadline_us: u64) -> u32`**
  pump the OS until an event is queued or the deadline (plat::time_us; 0 = poll without
  blocking, u64::MAX = forever) passes -> events queued (wake() makes it return at once)

- **`fn win_present(w: i32, f: &Frame, rects: Option<&[[i32; 4]]>)`**
  show the frame's dirty rectangles (x, y, w, h; None = the whole frame); the window keeps a
  copy of the pixels (WM_PAINT repaints from it; jfgui_WINPRESENT=dibits: a plain buffer and
  SetDIBitsToDevice instead of the DIB section)  [plat_win_present]

- **`fn win_destroy(w: i32)`**
  close the window (w = 0: ends the message loop)  [plat_win_destroy]

- **`fn win_show(w: i32, mode: u32)`**
  PWS_HIDE / PWS_SHOW (activates) / PWS_SHOWNA

- **`fn win_activate(w: i32)`**
  make the window the active one (keyboard focus)

- **`fn win_enable(w: i32, on: bool)`**
  a disabled window takes no input (modal dialogs disable the windows below them)

- **`fn win_set_rect(w: i32, x: i32, y: i32, cw: i32, ch: i32)`**
  client origin (screen px) and client size; PW_KEEP keeps a field

- **`fn win_get_rect(w: i32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  client origin (screen px) and client size (minimized: where it was); None: no window

- **`fn win_work_area(w: i32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  work area (without the taskbar) of the monitor the window is on: x, y, w, h (screen px)

- **`fn win_set_title(w: i32, title: &str)`**

- **`fn win_state(w: i32) -> u32`**
  WST_\* bits (WST_ACTIVE: one of the app's windows is active)

- **`fn win_cmd(w: i32, cmd: u32)`**
  WCMD_MINIMIZE / MAXIMIZE / RESTORE / CLOSE (asks, like the system menu does)

- **`fn win_begin_move(w: i32)`**
  let the system move the window (call on a button press)

- **`fn win_begin_resize(w: i32, edges: u32)`**
  let the system resize the window from an edge (EDGE_\* bits)

- **`fn win_size(w: i32) -> (i32, i32)`**
  client width, height in px ((0, 0) without a window)

- **`fn win_dpi(w: i32) -> i32`**
  96 = 100 %

- **`fn win_set_min_size(w: i32, w_dip: i32, h_dip: i32)`**
  minimum client size (also before the window exists)

- **`fn win_test_send(w: i32, msg: u32, wp: usize, lp: isize) -> isize`**
  (test aid) SendMessageW to window w -> its result (0 without the window or for a message
  that could carry a pointer)

- **`fn win_set_cursor(w: i32, shape: u32)`**
  CUR_\* shape while the pointer is over window w

- **`fn cursor_create(px: &[u8], w: i32, h: i32, hot_x: i32, hot_y: i32, _dpi: i32) -> i32`**
  a cursor from w x h premultiplied 0xAARRGGBB pixels (rows of w \* 4 bytes), hot spot in px:
  a 32-bit top-down DIB section with straight alpha + an empty AND mask -> CreateIconIndirect;
  Windows shows it at its size (dpi is not needed here) -> CUR_USER0 + k / -1

- **`fn cursor_destroy(id: i32)`**
  free a custom cursor; windows showing it fall back to the arrow (their shape is forgotten,
  so the next win_set_cursor applies even with the same id)

- **`fn cursor_dpi(dpi: i32) -> i32`**
  the dpi to draw a cursor for a window of this dpi (Windows: the window's own)

```text
win_clip -- Windows clipboard, file drops (WM_DROPFILES) and the IME caret position
                                         [src/plat/win/win_clip.s; docs/modules/CLIPBOARD_DND.md]

  clip_set(fmt, data) -> false on failure
       CLIP_TEXT: UTF-8 text (converted to CF_UNICODETEXT, "\n" -> "\r\n")
       CLIP_PNG:  PNG file bytes (registered clipboard format "PNG", the one browsers and
                  Office exchange; no CF_DIBV5 rendering)
       CLIP_IMAGE (K1): data = a CLIPIMG record (clipimg_pack: PNG + BMP file): "PNG" +
                  CF_DIBV5 (the BMP's V5 header and pixels) + CF_DIB (BITMAPINFOHEADER,
                  32 bit BI_RGB)
  clip_get(fmt) -> bytes   text as UTF-8 with "\r\n" -> "\n"; CLIP_IMAGE (K1): "PNG", else
       "image/png", else CF_DIBV5, else CF_DIB as a BMP file (clip_dib_to_bmp: header checks,
       paint.net's alpha rule)
  clip_has(fmt)            the clipboard offers the format (no data is read; K1)
  win_drop_files(hdrop) -> (files, x, y)   (K1) WM_DROPFILES: the paths go to the pending
       drop list (drop_*); shell32 (DragQueryFileW, DragQueryPoint, DragFinish) is loaded on
       the first drop.  The windows get WS_EX_ACCEPTFILES.
  win_drop_selftest(hwnd)  (K1, test aid) jfgui_TEST_DROPFILES="path|path..." posts a
       WM_DROPFILES with a real HDROP (GlobalAlloc'd DROPFILES, wide paths, point 100, 100) to
       the new main window, so the whole shell32 path runs in a real window
  ime_pos(x, y, h)         place a hidden system caret at client px (x, y) with height h in
       the window that has the keyboard, so IME composition / candidate windows open next to
       the text caret and screen magnifiers follow it (Magnifier, ZoomText: GetGUIThreadInfo
       and the caret's location events); h <= 0 removes it, so does the window's WM_KILLFOCUS
       (caret_focus_lost)

The clipboard is opened for the main window; opening is retried for a moment while another
program holds it.  Every block of another program is checked (sizes, NUL, surrogates).
```

### `plat/win_pen.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_pen.rs`](../lib/plat/win_pen.rs)

```text
win_pen -- (PN1) pen input on Windows: WM_POINTER* of pen pointers (Windows 8+)
                                                   [src/plat/win/win_pen.s; PEN_INPUT.md]

  win_pointer(hwnd, msg, wparam, w) -> true handled (the window procedure returns 0), false
       = on to DefWindowProc.  Called by the window procedure (win_api.rs) for
       WM_POINTERUPDATE .. WM_POINTERCAPTURECHANGED with the event window = w.
  pen_devices() -> pens / pen tablets attached (GetPointerDevices; -1 = the API is missing)
  pen_api_set(Some(api))   (test aid) the pointer API through the given functions instead
       of user32's (plattest's fakes); None = back to user32 (loaded again on first use)

Only pointers of type PT_PEN are handled.  EnableMouseInPointer is never called, so the
mouse keeps sending WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_*BUTTON*; touch and every pointer the API cannot
describe go on to DefWindowProc, which turns them into mouse messages as before.  A handled
pen message produces no mouse message.  With pen input off (pen_enable(false)) nothing is
handled: pens arrive as the system's mouse emulation.
  WM_POINTERUPDATE   every coalesced sample since the last message (GetPointerPenInfoHistory,
                     oldest first, at most PEN_HIST) -> E_MOVE with pen data
  WM_POINTERDOWN     tip contact -> E_DOWN BTN_LEFT, or BTN_RIGHT while the barrel button is
                     held (PEN_FLAG_BARREL / POINTER_FLAG_SECONDBUTTON), like paint.net
  WM_POINTERUP       E_UP of the button of the press
  WM_POINTERLEAVE    E_LEAVE (no button held)    WM_POINTERCAPTURECHANGED  E_UP if held
Pen data (evq_pen_data): pressure 0..1024 -> 1..PRESSURE_ONE (PEN_MASK_PRESSURE, else none),
PEN_FLAG_INVERTED / PEN_FLAG_ERASER -> PTR_ERASER, tilt x / y in degrees.  The API's results
are not trusted: counts are clamped, positions go through ScreenToClient.
```

```rust
PEN_HIST: usize = 16  // samples per WM_POINTERUPDATE
```

- **`struct PenInfo`**
  one sample of the pointer API: the POINTER_PEN_INFO fields the pen path reads
  - `flags: u32` -- POINTER_INFO.pointerFlags
  - `x: i32` -- ptPixelLocation (screen px)
  - `y: i32`
  - `pen_flags: u32` -- PEN_FLAG_\*
  - `pen_mask: u32` -- PEN_MASK_\*
  - `pressure: u32` -- 0..1024
  - `tilt_x: i32` -- -90..90 degrees
  - `tilt_y: i32`

- **`struct PenApi`**
  the pointer API (functions that are missing are None)
  - `ptype: Option<fn(u32) -> Option<u32>>` -- GetPointerType(id) -> the POINTER_INPUT_TYPE (None: failed)
  - `info: Option<fn(u32) -> Option<PenInfo>>` -- GetPointerPenInfo(id) -> the newest sample
  - `hist: Option<fn(u32, &mut u32, &mut [PenInfo]) -> bool>` -- GetPointerPenInfoHistory(id, &count, out): newest first, at most \*count (the room)
    records; \*count = the samples available -> false: failed
  - `devs: Option<fn(&mut u32, Option<&mut [u32]>) -> bool>` -- GetPointerDevices(&count, types): \*count = the devices; with Some(types) (\*count of
    them) their POINTER_DEVICE_TYPEs -> false: failed

- **`fn pen_api_set(api: Option<PenApi>)`**
  (test aid) the pointer API through `api` (None: user32's again, loaded on first use)

- **`fn pen_devices() -> i32`**
  pens / pen tablets attached, -1 = no pointer API  [plat_pen_devices]

```text
win_popup -- OS popup windows on Windows (U3)                    [src/plat/win/win_popup.s]

Popups (menus, combo lists, tooltips) of a secondary UI window that do not fit into it are
shown in borderless popup windows owned by that window (WS_POPUP, WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW |
WS_EX_NOACTIVATE, class style CS_DROPSHADOW, a rounded window region).  They never take the
keyboard; their pointer input is pushed as events of the OWNER window in owner client
coordinates, so the UI hit-tests them like the rest of the window.

  popup(slot, owner, rect, frame)
       show / move / present popup slot `slot` (0 .. PPW_MAX-1): rect = x, y, w, h in px of
       the owner's client area (popup pixel 0, 0 = owner pixel x, y); the slot keeps a copy
       of the frame's pixels (WM_PAINT repaints from it).  rect None hides it.
  popup_anchor(slot, anchor, kind, nat) / popup_placed(slot)   (§6, Wayland's placement) the
       UI places popups on Windows itself (inside the monitor's work area): nothing to do / None
  win_popup_wheel(hwnd, sx, sy, data) -> true if hwnd is one of the popups: the wheel event
       (screen point sx, sy) is pushed for its owner (win_api.rs: Windows sends the wheel to
       the focus window)
  win_popup_under(owner) -> true if the pointer is over a shown popup of owner (the owner's
       WM_MOUSELEAVE is then no leave)
```
