```text
       path: UTF-8, '/' or '\' separators.  A folder opens in Explorer (ShellExecuteW "open"
       on the folder); a file is shown selected in its folder (ShellExecuteW "open"
       explorer.exe with /select,"path").  shell32 and ole32 are loaded at run time (COM
       initialised once, as for the file dialog).  jfgui_OPEN_DRYRUN=1: nothing is started;
       the call is printed to stdout and 0 returned (tests).
  open_url(url) -> 0 / -1   a web page (http / https / mailto ...) in the default
       application (ShellExecuteW "open" on the URL); the same dry run
  theme() -> 0 light, 1 dark, -1 unknown (HKCU ... Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme)
  home() -> %USERPROFILE% (or "C:/")       drives() -> "C:/", "D:/", ...
  spawn_self(args) -> 0 / -1   this executable again: "exe" "arg1" "arg2" ... (every
       argument quoted with the Microsoft rules), no inherited handles
```

- **`fn open_url(url: &str) -> i32`**
  a web page (http / https / mailto ...) in the default application -> 0 / -1

- **`fn open_folder(path: &str) -> i32`**
  show a folder (or a file selected in its folder) in the file manager -> 0 / -1

- **`fn theme() -> i32`**
  0 light, 1 dark, -1 unknown (system setting)  [plat_theme]

- **`fn home() -> Option<String>`**
  the user's home folder (%USERPROFILE%, else "C:/")  [plat_home]

- **`fn drives() -> Vec<String>`**
  the drive roots ("C:/", "D:/", ...)  [plat_drives]

- **`fn restart_self(args: &[&str]) -> i32`**
  like spawn_self, but the program file now at this process's path (after an update a new
  file): the loader keeps the path the program was started from, also when the running exe
  was renamed since -> 0 / -1

- **`fn spawn_self(args: &[&str]) -> i32`**
  start this executable again with the arguments (no inherited handles) -> 0 / -1

### `plat/win_test.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_test.rs`](../lib/plat/win_test.rs)

```text
win_test -- test aids of the Windows platform layer (plattest --test window): they look at
and poke our own windows only (no input is injected into the system)

  win_test(op, w, a) -> i64   op:
    WT_PIXEL      0x00RRGGBB of client pixel a[0], a[1] of window w (GetPixel on its DC; -1
                  outside / no window)
    WT_REDRAW     invalidate the whole window and paint it now (WM_PAINT repaints from the
                  kept copy) -> 1
    WT_MOVE       move / size the window like the user would (SetWindowPos of the frame, not
                  win_set_rect): client origin a[0], a[1], client size a[2], a[3] -> 1
    WT_DPI        a WM_DPICHANGED of dpi a[0] with the suggested rect scaled around the
                  client origin (as Windows sends it when the window changes monitors) -> 1
    WT_CURSOR_IS  the current cursor is the one of shape a[0] (CUR_* / custom) -> 1 / 0
    WT_VISIBLE    window w is visible -> 1 / 0
    WT_POPUP_RECT popup slot w: its window rect x, y, w, h packed as 4 x i16 (-1: not shown)
    WT_POPUP_PIXEL popup slot w: 0x00RRGGBB at a[0], a[1]
    WT_ENABLED    window w takes input -> 1 / 0
    WT_CARET      the system caret's position x | y << 32 (GetCaretPos)
    WT_ACTIVE     window w is the active window -> 1 / 0
    WT_CLIP_ACCESS  0 when the clipboard can be opened, else the error (5: access denied,
                  e.g. in a sandbox that keeps processes off the clipboard)
    WT_POPUP_SEND popup slot w: SendMessageW(msg a[0], wParam a[1], lParam = point a[2], a[3])
    WT_POST_CHARS a burst: a[0] WM_CHAR messages posted to window w, the characters a[1],
                  a[1] + 1, ... a[1] + a[2] - 1 by turns (as an input method commits a long
                  text) -> the number posted
    WT_SCROLL     move the client rows a[0] .. a[0] + a[1] by a[2] rows inside the window
                  (BitBlt from its DC to itself, GdiFlush; what a scroll could cost without
                  sending the pixels again) -> microseconds taken
  win_test_image(w) -> (w, h, px)   the client area as the window shows it (BitBlt from its DC)
  file_dialog_autoclose(ms, name)   the next file_dialog is closed after ms by a timer of the
                  UI thread: name None = Cancel, Some(name) = the name typed + OK
```

```rust
WT_PIXEL: u32 = 1
WT_REDRAW: u32 = 2
WT_MOVE: u32 = 3
WT_DPI: u32 = 4
WT_CURSOR_IS: u32 = 5
WT_VISIBLE: u32 = 6
WT_POPUP_RECT: u32 = 7
WT_POPUP_PIXEL: u32 = 8
WT_ENABLED: u32 = 9
WT_CARET: u32 = 10
WT_ACTIVE: u32 = 11
WT_CLIP_ACCESS: u32 = 12
WT_POPUP_SEND: u32 = 13
WT_POST_CHARS: u32 = 14
WT_SCROLL: u32 = 15
```

- **`fn win_test(op: u32, w: i32, a: [i32; 4]) -> i64`**
  see the file header

- **`fn win_test_image(w: i32) -> Option<(i32, i32, alloc::vec::Vec<u8>)>`**
  (test aid) what window w shows: its client area read back from the window's DC (BitBlt into
  a DIB section; under DWM the window's own surface, also where other windows cover it) ->
  (w, h, rows of w \* 4 bytes B, G, R, x)

- **`fn file_dialog_autoclose(ms: u32, name: Option<&str>)`**
  (test aid) close the next file_dialog after ms: Cancel (name None) or name + OK

```text
win_inst -- the Windows calls of the setup (apps/installer): the own exe path, known
folders, .lnk shortcuts through COM IShellLinkW, the HKCU registry key of the "installed
apps" entry, starting a command line             (r12-inst)  [apps/installer/src/shell.s]

  exe_path() -> Some(path)        GetModuleFileNameW of the running exe as UTF-8 (None when
                                  it does not fit PATH_CAP wide chars)  [self_path]
  known_folder(which) -> Some(p)  0 = desktop, 1 = start menu "Programs" (SHGetKnownFolderPath,

                                  folder dir, icon 0 of the target, comment desc)  [sh_link]
  shell_link_id(lnk, target, dir, desc, app_id) -> bool   the same with the AppUserModelID
                                  app_id ("" = none) as the link's System.AppUserModel.ID
                                  (the program's explicit id, taskbar.rs: its button, jump
                                  list and notifications then belong to the link)
  link_read(lnk) -> Some((target, app_id))   a shortcut's target and System.AppUserModel.ID

  link_set_app_id(lnk, app_id) -> bool   that id written into an existing shortcut
  pins_set_app_id(dir, exe, app_id) -> usize   the shortcuts in dir and its folders that start
                                  exe and carry no id get app_id (pins made before the
                                  program ran under its id no longer match its button);
                                  Explorer is told of each (SHChangeNotify)
  pinned_dir() -> Some(path)      the user's pinned items (FOLDERID_UserPinned: TaskBar,
                                  ImplicitAppShortcuts)
  reg_create(subkey) -> Some(RegKey)   HKCU\subkey opened for writing (created when missing);

  reg_delete(subkey) -> bool      RegDeleteKeyW(HKCU, subkey)
  reg_delete_tree(subkey) -> bool RegDeleteTreeW: the key and everything below it

  assoc_changed()                 SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED): Explorer re-reads the

ole32 / shell32 / advapi32 are loaded with LoadLibraryA on the first use (inst_load, as the
asm's sh_load): only kernel32 / user32 / gdi32 are linked.  Paths are converted with the
asm's capacities (utf8_to_w with PATH_CAP wide chars, w_to_utf8 with PATH_CAP bytes).  The
```

```rust
PATH_CAP: usize = 520
```

### `plat/win_screen.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_screen.rs`](../lib/plat/win_screen.rs)

```text
win_screen -- (screen.rs) the monitors, pictures of the screen and the colour pick on Windows

  monitors() -> Vec<Monitor>   EnumDisplayMonitors; per monitor GetMonitorInfoW (MONITORINFOEXW:
                               rectangle, work area, MONITORINFOF_PRIMARY, the device name),
                               GetDpiForMonitor (shcore, effective dpi; else the system's),
                               EnumDisplaySettingsW (ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS: dmDisplayFrequency)
  capture_start(rect)          BitBlt (SRCCOPY | CAPTUREBLT) from the screen DC into a top-down
                               32-bit DIB section, answered at once (ScreenEvent::Shot)
  pick_start(test)             a frozen picture of the virtual desktop in a topmost window over
                               all monitors, a magnifier (9 x 9 pixels) beside the pointer with
                               the colour and its hex value; a left click, Enter or Space takes
                               the pixel under the pointer, the arrows move the pointer by one
                               pixel (Shift: ten), Esc / a right click cancels.  test = Some(x,
                               y): that pixel at once (1 x 1 BitBlt), no window
  (test aid) screen_test_metrics() -> (SM_CMONITORS, virtual desktop rectangle), the
                               independent figures of GetSystemMetrics

The process is made per-monitor DPI aware first (win_api.rs), so every figure is in physical
pixels of the virtual desktop.  WM_DISPLAYCHANGE and a changed work area (SPI_SETWORKAREA)
reach the app as E_SETTINGS with SET_MONITORS (win_api.rs).  The overlay belongs to the UI
thread: its messages are dispatched by wait().
```

### `plat/win_uia.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_uia.rs`](../lib/plat/win_uia.rs)

```text
win_uia -- (a11y.rs) the accessibility tree as UI Automation providers

  get_object(hwnd, pw, wp, lp)   (wndproc, WM_GETOBJECT) UiaRootObjectId: the provider of the
                                 window's root (UiaReturnRawElementProvider); assistive
                                 technology is there from now on (a11y::set_active)
  destroyed(hwnd)                (WM_DESTROY) UIA lets go of the window's providers
  changed(snapshot, changes)     the UI published a new tree: UIA events (only while clients
                                 listen: UiaClientsAreListening)
  uia_test_hwnd / uia_test_tree / uia_test_act / uia_test_listen / uia_test_events /
  uia_test_unlisten              (tests) a UI Automation client (IUIAutomation) that reads a
                                 window, acts and listens to events as a screen reader does

Every element is a small COM object of our own (Elem): the window's root (key 0) and one per
node, created on demand and identified by (platform window, node key); its methods answer
from a11y::current() on whatever thread UIA calls them (the provider is free-threaded: no
UseComThreading) and fail with UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE once the node is gone.  Interfaces:
IRawElementProviderSimple, IRawElementProviderFragment, IRawElementProviderFragmentRoot (the
root; its host provider comes from UiaHostProviderFromHwnd) and the patterns Invoke (buttons,
links, menu items), Toggle (check boxes, switches), Value (text boxes; drop-downs read-only),
RangeValue (sliders; progress bars read-only), SelectionItem (radio buttons, tabs, list rows),
ExpandCollapse (drop-downs, menus), Text / Text2 (text boxes: ranges, the caret and the
selection; win_uia_text.rs).  Headings are Text elements with HeadingLevel1 .. 9 (and the
AriaRole "heading", AriaProperties "level=N").  Dialogs, switches and headings name their
control type themselves (LocalizedControlType: a11y::role_name, in the UI language), the
others leave it to UIA.  Actions become a11y::request.  Events: focus
changed, property changes (toggle state, selected, expand state, enabled, name, value, range
value, heading level), text selection changed (the caret moved: screen readers and Magnifier
follow it), text changed, structure changed (children invalidated).  UIAutomationCore.dll
and oleaut32.dll are loaded on the first WM_GETOBJECT.
```

- **`struct UiaTestElem`**
  (tests) one element as a UI Automation client sees it
  - `name: String`
  - `control_type: i32`
  - `localized_type: String` -- LocalizedControlType (UIA's own name of the control type unless the provider gives one)
  - `depth: u32` -- below the window's element (1 = a child of it)
  - `enabled: bool`
  - `focused: bool`
  - `toggle: i32` -- Toggle state (-1: no Toggle pattern)
  - `value: Option<String>` -- Value (None: no Value pattern)
  - `range: Option<(f64, f64, f64)>` -- RangeValue: value, minimum, maximum
  - `selected: Option<bool>` -- SelectionItem: selected
  - `expand: i32` -- ExpandCollapse state (-1: no pattern)
  - `heading: i32` -- HeadingLevel 1 ..= 9 (0: HeadingLevel_None)
  - `rect: [i32; 4]` -- the bounding rectangle: x, y, w, h (screen px)

- **`enum UiaTestAct`**
  (tests) what uia_test_act does to an element
  - `Invoke`
  - `Toggle`
  - `Select`
  - `Expand`
  - `Collapse`
  - `Focus`
  - `SetValue(String)`
  - `SetRange(f64)`

- **`fn uia_test_hwnd(pw: i32) -> isize`**
  (tests; UI thread) the HWND of platform window pw

- **`fn uia_test_tree(hwnd: isize) -> Option<Vec<UiaTestElem>>`**
  (tests; not on the UI thread) the elements below window hwnd as a UI Automation client sees
  them (the raw view, depth first); None: no UI Automation

- **`fn uia_test_act(hwnd: isize, name: &str, control_type: i32, a: UiaTestAct) -> bool`**
  (tests; not on the UI thread) act on the first element with this name and control type
  through its pattern -> the call succeeded

- **`struct UiaTestCaret`**
  (tests) the caret of a text box as a UI Automation client sees it
  - `active: bool` -- GetCaretRange: the caret is active (the box has the keyboard focus)
  - `rects: Vec<[f64; 4]>` -- the caret range's bounding rectangles (screen px: x, y, w, h each)
  - `text: String` -- the text of the document range and of the selection
  - `selected: String`

- **`fn uia_test_caret(hwnd: isize, name: &str) -> Option<UiaTestCaret>`**
  (tests; not on the UI thread) the caret of the first text box with this name through
  IUIAutomationTextPattern2: GetCaretRange and its rectangles, the document's text, the
  selection's text; None: no such box / no Text pattern

- **`fn uia_test_caret_move(hwnd: isize, name: &str, chars: i32, extend: i32) -> bool`**
  (tests; not on the UI thread) move the caret of the first text box with this name: its caret
  range moved by `chars` characters (ITextRangeProvider::Move), then, with `extend` > 0, its end
  moved `extend` more characters, and Select() -> the calls succeeded

- **`fn uia_test_system_caret(hwnd: isize) -> Option<(isize, [i32; 4])>`**
  (tests; any thread) the system caret of hwnd's thread as magnifiers read it
  (GetGUIThreadInfo): its window and its rectangle on the screen (left, top, right, bottom)

- **`fn uia_test_listen(hwnd: isize) -> bool`**
  (tests; not on the UI thread) listen to focus changes everywhere, to the property changes
  below window hwnd (toggle state, selected, expand state, enabled, name, value, range value)
  and to its text events (the caret moved: TextSelectionChanged, TextChanged) -> registered

- **`fn uia_test_events() -> Vec<String>`**
  (tests) the events since the last call: "focus:&lt;name>", "prop:&lt;id>:&lt;name>=&lt;value>",
  "event:&lt;id>:&lt;name>"

- **`fn uia_test_unlisten()`**
  (tests; the thread of uia_test_listen) remove the handlers

### `plat/win_dnd.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_dnd.rs`](../lib/plat/win_dnd.rs)

```text
win_dnd -- (dnd.rs) drag and drop through OLE: every window is an IDropTarget; DoDragDrop
drags the app's content out with our own IDataObject and IDropSource

  register(hwnd, w) -> ok   (win_create) OleInitialize once, RegisterDragDrop(hwnd, a target
                            of window w); false: no OLE on this thread (WM_DROPFILES stays)
  revoke(hwnd)              (WM_DESTROY) RevokeDragDrop (releases the target)
  os_drag_start(data)       (dnd.rs drag_start) remember the drag; wait() runs it
  run_pending()             (wait, top) DoDragDrop of the remembered drag.  It is modal: the
                            UI keeps drawing from the source's QueryContinueDrag (the
                            wait_refresh closure, dnd_refresh) while events are queued, so
                            drop targets of the app highlight; then E_DRAG_END (the effect)
                            and E_UP for the buttons DoDragDrop swallowed
  dnd_test_formats(data) / dnd_test_drop(data, w, x, y, keys) / dnd_test_source(esc, keys)
                            (plattest, no user) our IDataObject read as a drop target reads
                            it; our IDropTarget fed with it (DragEnter, DragOver, Drop);
                            the IDropSource's answers

Target: DragEnter asks the data object which formats it has (QueryGetData: CF_HDROP,
CF_UNICODETEXT / CF_TEXT, "HTML Format", "UniformResourceLocatorW" / "UniformResourceLocator" /
"text/x-moz-url", "PNG" / "image/png" / CF_DIBV5 / CF_DIB), asks the UI (dnd::drag_query with
the client point and MK_SHIFT / MK_CONTROL) and answers that effect; E_DRAG goes to the UI on
enter, on every new point and on leave.  Drop reads only the kinds the UI takes (HGLOBAL
media, each at most 256 MiB): the paths of the DROPFILES block (parsed here, wide or ANSI),
text (UTF-16, else bytes), HTML (CF_HTML framing: clip_html_decode), URLs, the image (PNG, else
the DIB as a BMP file: clip_dib_to_bmp), then E_DROP (data = the number of paths).
Source: the data object offers CF_UNICODETEXT (the text, else the URLs), CF_HDROP (DROPFILES,
wide absolute paths), "HTML Format", "UniformResourceLocatorW" + "UniformResourceLocator",
"PNG", CF_DIBV5 + CF_DIB (from DragData::bmp).  GetData hands out a new HGLOBAL each time
(TYMED_HGLOBAL only), EnumFormatEtc goes through SHCreateStdEnumFmtEtc, SetData, GetDataHere
and advise sinks are refused.  ole32 / shell32 are loaded on the first window.
```

- **`fn dnd_test_formats(data: &DragData) -> Option<Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>>`**
  (plattest) our IDataObject of `data` read as a drop target reads it: EnumFormatEtc, then
  QueryGetData and GetData of every format -> (format name, bytes); None: no OLE

- **`fn dnd_test_drop(data: &DragData, w: i32, x: i32, y: i32, keys: u32) -> Option<u32>`**
  (plattest) a drop of `data` onto platform window w at client (x, y) as OLE would make it:
  DragEnter, DragOver, Drop of our IDropTarget with our IDataObject (MK_\* keys) -> the effect
  of the drop (the E_DRAG / E_DROP events are queued, the content waits in drop_data_take);
  None: no OLE

- **`fn dnd_test_source(esc: bool, keys: u32) -> u32`**
  (plattest) the IDropSource's answer to QueryContinueDrag(esc, MK_\* keys): 0 go on,
  1 drop, 2 cancel

### `plat/win_sys.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_sys.rs`](../lib/plat/win_sys.rs)

```text
win_sys -- Windows files, directories, environment, well-known paths, the date
                                        [src/plat/win/win_sys.s, win_files.s, plat_win.s]

Every function converts its paths into its own buffers, so all of them may run on any
thread.  File::read_at / write_at use explicit offsets (OVERLAPPED positions): several
threads may use one File at the same time.
```

- **`fn dev_ino(_path: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64)>`**
  (device, inode) of a path: not used on Windows (every directory is visited)

- **`fn env(name: &str) -> Option<String>`**

```text
win_thread -- Windows threads, semaphores, the wake-up of the UI thread, system information

wake(): a flag coalesces bursts.  With a window the wake-up is a posted WM_APP_WAKE (the
window turns it into E_WAKE, also inside modal loops); without one (headless, before the
window exists) an auto-reset event that wait_events waits for.  Everything here is
```

### `plat/win_print.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_print.rs`](../lib/plat/win_print.rs)

```text
win_print -- printing on Windows: PrintDlgExW (comdlg32, loaded at run time) and GDI
                                                     [src/plat/win/win_print.s; docs/modules/PRINT.md]

  print(job) -> 0 printed / ERR_CANCEL / ERR_UNSUPPORTED / ERR_IO / ERR_NOMEM / ERR_DIMS.
       The system print dialog (printer, paper, orientation, copies; the job's paper and
       PJF_LANDSCAPE preselected through a DEVMODE) returns a printer DC; the page geometry
       comes from GetDeviceCaps (PHYSICALWIDTH / -OFFSET, HORZRES, LOGPIXELS), layout()
       places the image, which goes out with StretchDIBits (HALFTONE) in bands of at most
       BAND_BYTES of 24-bit rows composited over white (row_white), clipped to the
       printable area (IntersectClipRect).
  Test variant (never a dialog, never paper):
       jfgui_PRINT_TO=FILE          output goes to FILE (DOCINFO.lpszOutput) on the printer
       jfgui_PRINT_PRINTER=NAME     (default "Microsoft Print to PDF"), opened with
                                     CreateDCW and a DEVMODE for paper / orientation
       Without a main window (headless) and without jfgui_PRINT_TO: ERR_UNSUPPORTED.
The gdi32 functions are imported directly (the assembly took ten of them with
GetProcAddress only to keep its import library small); PrintDlgExW (comdlg32),
GetDefaultPrinterW (winspool.drv) and CoInitializeEx (ole32) are loaded at run time.
```

### `plat/win_lib.rs` (Windows)

Source: [`lib/plat/win_lib.rs`](../lib/plat/win_lib.rs)

```text
win_lib -- plugin libraries and the crash guard: the Windows part
                                        [src/plat/win/win_lib.s; docs/modules/PLUGIN_LOADER.md]

  lib_open(path) -> Lib / Err(LIBE_*)   LoadLibraryExW(DONT_RESOLVE_DLL_REFERENCES): the
       image is mapped and relocated, but DllMain / TLS callbacks never run and no import
       is bound -- a plugin with an import, delay-import or TLS directory is rejected
       (LIBE_DEPS / LIBE_INIT); only x86-64 DLLs (LIBE_FORMAT).  Hard-error dialogs are
       suppressed (SetThreadErrorMode).  Segments: headers + every section.
  lib_sym(h, name) -> address | 0       own export-directory lookup (bounds checked against
       SizeOfImage, every table / name inside a readable section -- a section without
       MEM_READ is PAGE_NOACCESS; forwarders -> 0, so no other DLL is ever loaded)
  (crate) lib_unload(h)                 FreeLibrary (lib_close / drop)
  (crate) plat_tid() -> u64             thread id (TEB ClientId, gs:[0x48])
  (crate) guard_thread()                nothing on Windows
  (crate) guard_os_install()            AddVectoredExceptionHandler(first, guard_veh)

guard_veh handles access violations, in-page errors, illegal / privileged instructions,
integer and FP traps, misalignment, breakpoints and stack overflow -- only while the
faulting thread has an active guard (plib.rs); everything else goes on to the next
handler (win_crash.rs).
```

  the address of the export name, 0 when missing / forwarded  [plat_lib_sym]

### `plat/linux_disp.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_disp.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_disp.rs)

```text
linux_disp -- display backend dispatch on Linux: Wayland (linux_wl*.rs) or X11 (linux_x11*.rs)
                                                       [src/plat/linux/disp.s, lx_popup.s]

The display-dependent functions go through the backend object (trait Display).  The
first win_create (the main window, owner PW_NOOWNER) picks the backend:
  jfgui_BACKEND=wayland | x11     forces one (only the first letter counts, like disp.s)
  WAYLAND_DISPLAY set              Wayland first, then X11 if DISPLAY is set
  only DISPLAY set                 X11 first, then Wayland (default socket)
  neither                          Wayland (default socket), else an error
When no backend can open its main window the process ends with exit code 1 and a
message (as disp.s).  Before that the minimum size of window 0 and the refresh callback
are remembered and handed to the chosen backend.  wait() without a backend (headless
runs) sleeps until its deadline or a wake() (lx_wait_nodisp).

The trait is the contract between the two backend agents and with Windows (win_api.rs has
the same free functions): change it only together and say so in the report.

plat-x11 (R4): the backend choice follows disp.s exactly (first letter of
jfgui_BACKEND, the fallback order, exit 1 when every backend fails, the Wayland
backend's "quiet" flag: disp_wl_quiet()); Display::pen_devices (default -1) was added
for plat_pen_devices; cursor_dpi without a display answers the dpi (pre_cdpi); the
headless wait is lx_wait_nodisp (wake fd, E_WAKE).
```

```rust
BK_NONE: u32 = 0
BK_WAYLAND: u32 = 1
BK_X11: u32 = 2
```

  - `fn win_work_area(&mut self, w: i32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`

    the window manager's window menu at x, y (px of the window) on a button press; default

  - `fn win_size(&mut self, w: i32) -> (i32, i32)`

  - `fn popup_anchor(&mut self, _slot: u32, _anchor: [i32; 4], _kind: u32, _nat: [i32; 2])`

  - `fn cursor_create(&mut self, px: &[u8], w: i32, h: i32, hot_x: i32, hot_y: i32, dpi: i32) -> i32`

  - `fn pen_devices(&mut self) -> i32`

  - `fn drag_start(&mut self, _data: crate::DragData) -> bool`

### `plat/linux_wl.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_wl.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_wl.rs)

```text
linux_wl -- the Wayland display backend behind linux_disp::Display
                                    [src/plat/linux/wl_window.s, wl_wire.s, wl_present.s, ...]

  wl_connect() -> the backend, None when no compositor answers ($WAYLAND_DISPLAY in
       $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, /run/user/UID, /mnt/wslg/runtime-dir)
  test hooks for linuxtest (synthetic events, no compositor needed): wl_test_event,
       wl_test_setup, wl_input_service, wl_cursor_image, wl_cursor_render, wl_test_protoerr,
       wl_test_roundtrip (a compositor or tools/wlproxy/wlinject.py)
  xkb_* (linux_xkb.rs): the keymap of the Wayland keyboard, also used by X11

The modules follow the assembly files:
  linux_wl_wire.rs     connection, object table, marshalling, fd passing, dispatch,
                       roundtrips, fatal errors, the jfgui_WLDEBUG trace   [wl_wire.s]
  linux_wl_proto.rs    interface descriptors (event tables) and requests    [wl_proto.s]
  linux_wl_window.rs   globals, xdg toplevels, configure, scale, commands, the wait loop
                                                                            [wl_window.s]
  linux_wl_present.rs  wl_shm buffers, damage, frame callbacks            [wl_present.s]
  linux_wl_input.rs    wl_seat pointer / keyboard, key repeat               [wl_input.s]
  linux_wl_tablet.rs   zwp_tablet_v2 pens                                  [wl_tablet.s]
  linux_wl_popup.rs    xdg_popup windows                                    [wl_popup.s]
  linux_wl_clip.rs     wl_data_device: clipboard both ways, drag and drop in and out
                                                                            [wl_clip.s]
  linux_wl_cursor.rs   cursor-shape protocol, own cursor images, custom cursors [wl_cursor.s]
  linux_wl_act.rs      xdg-activation: the launcher's token, raising and restoring windows

State: the assembly's globals are one record (Wl) owned by this module, created on the
first use (the synthetic tests use it without a connection).  Every entry point (the
Display methods, the hooks) borrows it once for its whole call and passes `&mut Wl` down
to the event handlers; a nested borrow (re-entry) panics instead of aliasing.  Only the
UI thread calls in; wake() from other threads goes through the eventfd of linux_thread.
```

- **`fn wl_connect() -> Option<Box<dyn Display>>`**
  connect to the compositor -> the backend, None when there is no Wayland display (quiet
  unless jfgui_BACKEND=wayland forces it)  [wl_connect]

- **`fn wl_test_event(iface: &str, event: &str, args: &[u64]) -> bool`**
  call the handler of event `event` ("enter", "key", ...) of interface `iface`
  ("wl_pointer", "wl_keyboard", ...) with decoded arguments (object id 1, udata 0), as
  linuxtest --test synth does -> false when there is no such event  [hcall]

- **`fn wl_test_event_u(iface: &str, event: &str, args: &[u64], udata: u64) -> bool`**
  (main agent) wl_test_event with the handler's udata (a tablet tool's slot ...), as
  plattest --test pen does  [tcall in apps/plattest/src/pen.s]

- **`fn wl_test_scale(s120: i32)`**
  (main agent) the pointer scale while there is no window (g_wl_s120, 120ths) alone

- **`fn wl_test_setup(s120: i32, seat_ver: u32)`**
  the pointer scale while there is no window (g_wl_s120, 120ths) and the seat version
  the handlers assume (g_wl_seat_ver)

- **`fn wl_input_service(now: u64) -> u64`**
  key repeat at `now` (time_us) -> the next repeat deadline, u64::MAX = none
  [wl_input_service]

- **`fn wl_cursor_image(shape: u32) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32, u32, &'static [u8])>`**
  the built-in cursor image of a CUR_\* shape: (width, height, hot x, hot y, rows of 'X'
  black / 'o' white / '.' transparent)  [wl_cursor_image]

- **`fn wl_cursor_render(dst: &mut [u32], shape: u32, s: u32)`**
  expand a cursor image into ARGB pixels (S x S blocks, rows of width \* S pixels)
  [wl_cursor_render]

- **`fn wl_test_roundtrip() -> i32`**
  a wl_display.sync round trip: the events that arrive before its answer are dispatched
  first (linuxtest --test burst: a burst of keys while it waits) -> 0 ok / -1 timeout

- **`fn wl_test_presented(w: i32) -> Option<(i32, i32, Vec<u8>)>`**
  the pixels of window w's last committed buffer -- what the compositor shows -- as (w, h,
  rows of w \* 4 bytes B, G, R, x); None while damage waits (linuxtest --test pcheck)

- **`fn wl_test_protoerr()`**
  attach a buffer id that does not exist to the main window's surface: the compositor
  answers with wl_display.error, which ends the process (linuxtest --test protoerr)

### `plat/linux_xkb.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_xkb.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_xkb.rs)

```text
linux_xkb -- minimal XKB keymap parser and key translation (Wayland keyboard; the X11
backend fills the same table from the core keyboard mapping)        [src/plat/linux/xkb.s]

  xkb_parse(text) -> 0 ok / -1           parse an xkbcommon text keymap (format 1)
  xkb_use_fallback()                     built-in evdev -> US English table
  xkb_set_mods(depressed, latched, locked, group) -> MOD_* bits (also wl_mods())
  xkb_key(evdev) -> (VK, text codepoint)  for the current modifiers (text 0 = none)
  xkb_key_typed(evdev) -> (VK, [text; 2]) a key press with the dead keys composed (below)
  xkb_dead_reset()                       forget a pending dead key (focus change)
  xkb_dead_keysym(spacing) -> X keysym   the dead keysym of a dead key's spacing character
  xkb_is_modifier(evdev) -> bool         the key is a modifier (never auto-repeats)
  xkb_mod_bit(evdev) -> MOD_* bit the key holds (Shift / Ctrl / Alt / Super / AltGr) or 0
  xkb_dump()                             print the parsed table to stdout (tests)
  wl_mods() / wl_mods_set(m)             the MOD_* bits of the events (g_wl_mods)
  X11 backend: xkb_begin(), xkb_set_key(evdev, levels, nlev), xkb_set_roles(alt, num,
  super, level3)

Parsed: xkb_keycodes (`<NAME> = code;`, `alias <A> = <B>;`, names <= 4 chars, codes
< 264), xkb_symbols (first level list of group 1 per key, `type=`, `modifier_map`).
xkb_types / xkb_compatibility are skipped; key types are classified by name (ONE_LEVEL,
CTRL+ALT, PC_* -> one level; *KEYPAD* -> keypad; *ALPHABETIC* -> Caps Lock applies) or,
without an explicit type, like xkbcomp does (1 symbol -> one level, KP_* -> keypad, a/A
pair -> alphabetic).

Level: ONE -> 1; KEYPAD -> (Shift ^ NumLock) ? 2 : 1;
       else s = Shift ^ (ALPHA && Caps && !Level3), level = (Level3 ? 3 : 1) + s.
Text is produced for codepoints >= 0x20 (not 0x7F) unless Ctrl / Alt / Super is held
without Level3 (AltGr may arrive as Ctrl + Mod5 from Windows hosts).  Dead keys: xkb_key
gives their spacing character; xkb_key_typed composes like Windows does -- a dead key is
held back, the next letter becomes the accented one (´ e -> é, ^ o -> ô, ¨ u -> ü, ...),
Space or the same dead key gives the spacing character, anything else both; a key without
text (Backspace, Esc, a shortcut) drops it.  (An input method, IBus through text-input-v3,
composes before the keys reach us.)  VK codes: layout-following for a-z / 0-9
(level-1 symbol, like Win32) and for + , - . (VK_OEM_PLUS/COMMA/MINUS/PERIOD); otherwise
by key position; keypad keys give navigation VKs while Num Lock is off.

The table is process state behind a lock (both display backends and the tests use it).
```

```rust
// symbol values: codepoint | flags
KV_CP: u32 = 0x1FFFFF
KV_KP: u32 = 0x2000_0000
KV_DEAD: u32 = 0x4000_0000
KV_MODSHIFT: u32 = 24
```

  the MOD_\* bits the events carry (g_wl_mods)

- **`fn wl_mods_set(m: u32)`**
  set the MOD_\* bits of the events (a modifier key's own event, wl_input)

- **`fn xkb_parse(text: &[u8]) -> i32`**

- **`fn xkb_use_fallback()`**
  evdev -> US English symbols (used when no keymap parses)  [xkb_use_fallback]

- **`fn xkb_begin()`**

- **`fn xkb_set_key(evdev: u32, levels: &[u32; 4], nlev: u32)`**

  number of levels listed  [xkb_set_key]

- **`fn xkb_set_roles(alt: u32, num: u32, sup: u32, level3: u32)`**

### `plat/linux_x11.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_x11.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_x11.rs)

```text
linux_x11 -- the X11 display backend: our own X11 protocol client over a Unix socket (no
Xlib / xcb) behind linux_disp::Display
                    [src/plat/linux/x11.inc, x11_wire.s, x11_window.s, x11_present.s,
                     x11_input.s, x11_xi.s, x11_clip.s, x11_dnd.s, x11_popup.s,
                     x11_cursor.s, x11_monitor.s; docs/modules/WINDOWS_PLATFORM.md Ã‚Â§4, Ã‚Â§9, Ã‚Â§10]

  x11_connect() -> backend        $DISPLAY reachable: the backend (the main window is made
                                  by its win_create), None (no message) otherwise
  x11t::*                         the self-test entry points of linuxtest (x11synth,
                                  x11err): events without a server, keysyms, the core
                                  keymap, raw requests, the last X error

The state of the assembly's globals lives in one X11 record (module state, one UI thread):
the backend object is empty and every Display call borrows the record for its duration.
Nothing inside calls back into the plat API that would borrow it again (the refresh
callback is only stored, as on X11 in the assembly), so a re-entrant borrow would be a
bug and panics.  Files:
  linux_x11_wire.rs     connection, authentication, setup, requests, replies, errors
  linux_x11_window.rs   window records, hints, WM messages, DPI, state, events, wait
  linux_x11_present.rs  MIT-SHM (memfd / SysV) or PutImage, per window
  linux_x11_input.rs    core keyboard / pointer input, keysyms, the core keymap (built into
                        the key table of linux_xkb.rs: xkb_begin / xkb_set_key / xkb_key)
  linux_x11_xi.rs       XInput 2 pens
  linux_x11_clip.rs     CLIPBOARD (INCR both ways, images)
  linux_x11_dnd.rs      XDND 5: drops of every kind into the windows, the app's drags out
  linux_x11_misc.rs     popups (override-redirect), cursors (font / RENDER), monitors (RandR)
  linux_x11_screen.rs   the monitor list, global shortcuts (GrabKey), GetImage of the root,
                        the colour pick (pointer grab), RandR change events

Deviation from the assembly (the Rust API hands the frame over only for the call): the
MIT-SHM segments are whole frames brought up to date from the caller's frame (what each
lacks, linux_x11_present.rs), so repaints (Expose, after a map) read the segment of the
last put; the PutImage fallback keeps a shadow image of the frame, and popups keep a copy
of their pixels -- where the assembly re-read the caller's framebuffer.
```

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_portal.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_portal.rs)

```text
linux_portal -- xdg-desktop-portal over a minimal D-Bus client (raw socket, SASL EXTERNAL,
little-endian marshalling): the file dialog, OpenURI / OpenDirectory, Print
                                                           [src/plat/linux/portal.s]

  file_dialog(flags, path, exts) -> (1 chosen / 0 cancelled / -1 no portal, index of the
       chosen extension entry).  Same contract as on Windows (win_filedlg.rs): flags FD_SAVE
       | index << FD_EXT_SHIFT (FD_FOLDER: OpenFile with "directory", portal version 3),
       path in / out (UTF-8, '/'; at most PATH_CAP - 1 bytes out),
       exts ["png=PNG-Bild", "jpg;jpeg=JPEG-Bild"] (an empty entry ends the list).
  open_url(url) -> 0 / -1         a web page in the default application: OpenURI.OpenURI;
                                  jfgui_OPEN_DRYRUN=1 only prints it
  open_folder(path) -> 0 / -1     show a folder / a file in the file manager:
       OpenURI.OpenDirectory with an O_PATH descriptor (SCM_RIGHTS), fallback
       OpenURI.OpenURI("file://...").  The Response is awaited for OF_WAIT ms (the window
       keeps being serviced): code 0 -> 0, 1 / 2 -> -1; without an answer by then the
       request stays alive on its connection until the next call and 0 is returned.  No
       bus / no portal / no such path -> -1.  jfgui_OPEN_DRYRUN=1: printed, nothing sent.
  (crate) portal_print_prepare / portal_print_send / portal_print_end  org.freedesktop.portal
       .Print for linux_print.rs (PreparePrint with the job's paper / orientation, the page
       setup of the answer; Print with the PDF as a descriptor)

The dialogs belong to the portal's process.  While one is open the display keeps being
serviced (wait); input events of that time are dropped, window events (resize, close,
focus, dpi, paint) are kept and queued again afterwards.

State: the assembly's globals (receive buffer, body / message builders, token, request
path, ...) are one Bus record (module state, UI thread only).  Messages are byte-identical
to the assembly's (serials, field order, padding, token "jfgui<n>").
```

```text
linux_life -- lifecycle events on Linux

  life_start()     (the first window) the SIGTERM handler and the watcher thread, once
  life_poll()      (wait) a SIGTERM that arrived -> E_SESSION_END

SIGTERM (logout, shutdown, `kill`) sets a flag and wakes the loop: the app gets
E_SESSION_END (UIC_SESSION_END), saves, and ends.  The watcher thread has connections of
its own (linux_dbus.rs): logind's PrepareForSleep(b) on the system bus -> E_POWER (1
sleep, 0 woke up); the settings portal's SettingChanged(namespace, key, value) on the
session bus -> E_SETTINGS with SET_THEME (color-scheme, accent-color, gtk-theme),
SET_CONTRAST (contrast, high-contrast), SET_FONTS (font names, text-scaling-factor),
SET_LOCALE (region); other keys are ignored.  Without a bus the thread ends quietly;
jfgui_LIFE=0 turns it off.
```

### `plat/linux_thread.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_thread.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_thread.rs)

```text
linux_thread -- Linux threads (clone + futex), semaphores, the wake-up of the UI thread,
system information, the date                       [src/plat/linux/lx_thread.s, plat_linux.s]

A thread's stack is an mmap with a PROT_NONE guard page below it; the thread record sits
at its top.  The kernel clears the record's tid word and wakes it (a shared futex wake)
when the thread ends, which is what join waits for.  Semaphores are process-private
futex counters.  The wake-up is an eventfd: the display backends poll it next to their
socket, wait_events polls it alone (headless).
```

### `plat/linux_elfload.rs` (Linux)

Source: [`lib/plat/linux_elfload.rs`](../lib/plat/linux_elfload.rs)

```text
linux_elfload -- plugin libraries on Linux: a small ELF loader without libc
                                       [src/plat/linux/elfload.s; docs/modules/PLUGIN_LOADER.md]

  lib_open(path) -> Lib / Err(LIBE_*)
  lib_sym(h, name) -> address | 0       .dynsym lookup (count from DT_HASH nchain or the
                                        DT_GNU_HASH chains)
  (crate) lib_unload(h)                 munmap (lib_close / drop)

Accepted: ELFCLASS64, little endian, ET_DYN, EM_X86_64, program headers of 56 bytes
(1..64), at most LH_SEGMAX PT_LOAD segments in ascending, page-disjoint order, never
writable AND executable, one PT_DYNAMIC; relocations R_X86_64_NONE / RELATIVE and
R_X86_64_64 / GLOB_DAT / JUMP_SLOT against symbols the object defines itself (RELA only).
Rejected: DT_NEEDED or undefined symbols (LIBE_DEPS), PT_INTERP / PT_TLS / DT_INIT /
DT_INIT_ARRAY / DT_PREINIT_ARRAY (LIBE_INIT: nothing of the object runs while loading),
DT_REL and other relocation types (LIBE_RELOC), everything malformed (LIBE_FORMAT).
The file is untrusted input: every header value, offset, size and address is checked in
64-bit arithmetic against the file size or the mapped span (LIB_SPAN_MAX) before use.
Mapping: one anonymous read-write reservation of the whole span, the segments copied in,
relocations applied, then mprotect per segment (gaps PROT_NONE, PT_GNU_RELRO read-only).
While loading, the mapping is accessed as a slice (every access bounds-checked on top of
the assembly's checks); lib_sym reads the protected image like the assembly.
```

- **`fn lib_open(path: &str) -> Result<Lib, u32>`**
  open a plugin ELF object (see the file header)  [plat_lib_open]

- **`fn lib_sym(h: &Lib, name: &str) -> usize`**
  the address of the defined dynamic symbol name, or 0  [plat_lib_sym]

### `plat/web.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/web.rs`](../lib/plat/web.rs)

```text
Shared browser/Android host adapter. The host exchanges bounded buffers and queued events;
app state stays in the same Rust UI/runtime used by native applications.
Android differs where its system offers more: real files on internal storage
(android_files.rs), the documents of other apps as content:// names, the system clipboard and
the persisted grants (android_host.rs), the system's file picker behind file_dialog
(FD_PENDING, file_dialog_poll), download() as "save a copy" through the picker.
The browser with the File System Access API (Chromium; the host says so, HOST_HANDLES):
file_dialog shows the system's pickers too and answers later; the chosen file is the user's
own, bound to a path /handles/ID/NAME (web/handles.js keeps the handle in IndexedDB), and every
change of it is written back (write_back: the request of persist); reopen() reads it again
after a reload.  Without the API: the library's own dialog over the virtual files, export
through download().
```

```rust
/// Persist a virtual file to browser storage; payload: u32 path byte count, path, file bytes.
REQUEST_PERSIST: u32 = 1
/// Export/download a file; same payload framing as persistence.
REQUEST_DOWNLOAD: u32 = 2
/// Open a browser file picker; payload is a UTF-8 extension filter.
REQUEST_OPEN: u32 = 3
/// Read browser clipboard text asynchronously.
REQUEST_CLIP_READ: u32 = 4
/// Write browser clipboard text; payload is UTF-8.
REQUEST_CLIP_WRITE: u32 = 5
/// Update the DOM composition element's caret rectangle (three little-endian i32 values).
REQUEST_IME: u32 = 6
/// Update the browser pointer shape (one little-endian u32 CUR value).
REQUEST_CURSOR: u32 = 7
/// Update the document title (UTF-8).
REQUEST_TITLE: u32 = 8
/// Open an explicitly requested HTTP(S)/mailto URL; payload is UTF-8.
REQUEST_URL: u32 = 9
/// Mirror explicit in-app control activation/revocation to the host (one boolean byte).
REQUEST_AGENT: u32 = 10
/// The differences of the accessibility tree for the host's mirror (web_a11y.rs, a11y_wire.rs).
REQUEST_A11Y: u32 = 11
/// (Android) the system's file picker for file_dialog: u32 flags, the suggested name, the
/// content:// URI it starts at (may be empty), u32 count, the extensions (one string each,
/// "png"); answered by jfgui_file_result with the chosen content:// URI
REQUEST_FILE_DIALOG: u32 = 12
/// (browser) commit a change of the secret store (secret.rs, web_secret.rs): u32 op (1 set,
/// 2 delete), app, service, account and for set the value, each as u32 length + bytes; the
/// host encrypts and stores it in order and completes with 2, or an error
REQUEST_SECRET: u32 = 13
/// (browser) read a file of the user's own (/handles/..) again: the path (UTF-8); the host asks
/// for the permission the handle needs (from the user's gesture), imports the file and
/// completes with 2
REQUEST_REOPEN: u32 = 20
/// (browser) sound output (audio.rs, web_audio.rs, web/audio.js): five u32, op (1 open, 2 close,
/// 3 play, 4 pause, 5 flush), stream id, rate, channels, latency frames; no completion
REQUEST_AUDIO: u32 = 14
/// (browser) the app holds unsaved work (one byte, 1 / 0): the page asks before the tab is
/// closed or reloaded (loader.js beforeunload)
REQUEST_UNSAVED: u32 = 22
```

- **`fn set_unsaved(on: bool)`**
  set_unsaved(on) -- tell the page whether closing the tab would lose unsaved work

- **`enum RequestStatus`**
  Completion state of one browser operation; durable and exported are distinct outcomes.
  - `Pending` -- The host has not completed the operation.
  - `Durable` -- Browser storage confirmed this exact file revision was committed.
  - `Exported` -- The host completed a download/export, not an origin-storage commit.
  - `Completed` -- A transient operation such as clipboard access completed.
  - `Denied` -- The user or browser denied access.
  - `Quota` -- Browser storage quota was exhausted.
  - `Unsupported` -- This browser lacks the requested service.
  - `Cancelled` -- User cancellation.
  - `Failed` -- Other host I/O failure.

- **`trait WebApplication`**
  An owned app runtime registered once when the browser entrypoint returns.
  - `fn frame_delay(&self) -> u32`
    Milliseconds until a timer or animation needs a host tick; input wakes immediately.
  - `fn input(&mut self, time_ms: u32)`
    Drain queued input without presenting intermediate frames; default runtimes may tick.
  - `fn tick(&mut self, time_ms: u32)`
    Process queued input, advance timers and render one frame.
  - `fn control(&mut self, line: &[u8]) -> Option<String>`
    Process one explicitly enabled agent request, returning its UTF-8 response.
  - `fn set_control_enabled(&mut self, _enabled: bool)`
    Synchronize runtime visibility and command state when the host changes activation.

- **`fn install(app: Box<dyn WebApplication>) -> bool`**
  Install the owned runtime. Returns false if an app is already registered.

- **`fn persist(path: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Request durable origin storage for the current virtual-file revision.  A file of the user's
  own (/handles/.., chosen in the system's picker) is written back to that file instead
  (Durable once the browser closed the write); its change already started that request, which
  is returned while it is pending or done.

- **`fn reopen(path: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Read a file of the user's own (/handles/.., chosen in the system's picker before) again,
  e.g. after a reload: the host asks for the permission the browser wants again (call it from
  the user's click or key), imports the file's current bytes and completes (Completed; Denied,
  Failed when the file is gone, Unsupported without such a file).  None: refused by the
  permissions or no request slot.

- **`fn persist(path: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Android: the file is on internal storage already; its data is synced (fsync) and the
  request is Durable (Failed for a missing file) at once.

- **`fn download(path: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Request a browser download; success means export, not durable origin storage.  Android:
  "save a copy" through the system's picker (the user chooses where).

- **`fn pick_file(extensions: &str) -> Option<u32>`**
  Request file selection. The host imports selected files before completing the request.
  Android: the chosen document arrives as its content:// name in a drop (E_DROP).

- **`fn request_status(id: u32) -> Option<RequestStatus>`**
  Query an operation. Old terminal results expire when the 256-entry history fills.

- **`fn forget_request(id: u32) -> bool`**
  Remove a completed operation once its result has been consumed.

- **`fn capabilities() -> Capabilities`**
  Services supplied by this browser session, including dynamically granted host services.

- **`fn args() -> Vec<String>`**
  App start arguments copied from the host, with a synthetic executable name first.

- **`fn time_us() -> u64`**
  Monotonic microseconds from the host's performance clock.

- **`fn sleep_ms(_ms: u32)`**
  No blocking sleep occurs in the browser; callers must return to their step loop.

- **`fn env(name: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  Read a per-instance virtual environment setting.

- **`fn getenv(name: &str) -> Option<String>`**
  Alias for the shared environment API.

- **`fn setenv(name: &str, value: Option<&str>) -> bool`**
  Set a per-instance environment value without changing the browser or OS environment.

- **`fn date() -> (Date, bool)`**
  Host-supplied UTC calendar, updated independently from the monotonic clock.

- **`fn unix_time_ns() -> i64`**
  Wall-clock time from the host calendar: nanoseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC.

- **`fn theme() -> i32`**
  Theme requested by the host: 0 light, 1 dark, or -1 unspecified.

- **`fn cpu_count() -> u32`**
  Available compute workers in a shared-memory bundle, otherwise one app worker.

- **`fn mem_total() -> u64`**
  Current WASM linear-memory allocation; zero when the embedded host does not report RAM.

- **`fn thread_yield()`**
  Cooperative yield is achieved by returning from the current runtime step.

- **`struct Thread`**
  Browser thread handle placeholder; spawning native threads is unsupported.

**`impl Thread`**

- **`fn join(self)`**
  No thread was started.

- **`fn thread_spawn(_stack: usize, _f: Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>) -> Option<Thread>`**
  Reject native thread creation. Use Job for cooperative background work.

- **`struct Sem(AtomicU32)`**
  Nonblocking counting semaphore used only by portable try-wait paths.

**`impl Sem`**

- **`fn new(initial: u32) -> Option<Self>`**
  Create a logical semaphore inside this worker.
- **`fn post(&self, count: u32)`**
  Add available units.
- **`fn wait(&self, _timeout: i32) -> bool`**
  Try to take a unit; browser execution never blocks on another thread.

- **`fn wake()`**
  Coalesce job/repaint notifications without occupying the bounded input ring.

- **`fn wait(_deadline_us: u64) -> u32`**
  Poll available events; the host schedules future ticks.

- **`fn wait_events(_deadline_us: u64, on_event: &mut dyn FnMut(&Event)) -> u32`**
  Dispatch already queued events without blocking the browser worker.

- **`fn read_stdin(_bytes: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, u32>`**
  Browser MessagePort replaces process stdin.

- **`fn file_dialog(flags: u32, path: &mut String, extensions: &[&str]) -> (i32, u32)`**
  The browser: with the File System Access API (Chromium) the system's pickers --
  FD_OPEN showOpenFilePicker, FD_SAVE showSaveFilePicker (the suggested name from path, the
  types from the extensions; a /handles/.. path starts beside that file).  They answer later:
  (FD_PENDING, 0) now, file_dialog_poll() once the user is done; the answer is a path
  /handles/ID/NAME bound to the chosen file (opened: imported already), whose changes are
  written back.  One picker at a time ((0, 0) while one is open).  FD_FOLDER and browsers
  without the API: (-1, 0), the library's own dialog over the virtual files.

- **`fn file_dialog(flags: u32, path: &mut String, extensions: &[&str]) -> (i32, u32)`**
  Android: the system's picker (Storage Access Framework) -- FD_OPEN ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT,
  FD_SAVE ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT (the suggested name from path, the type of the selected
  extension), FD_FOLDER ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE.  It answers later: (FD_PENDING, 0) now,
  file_dialog_poll() once the user is done (the UI wakes up then); the chosen document comes
  as its content:// name, its grant kept across restarts.  One picker at a time: a second
  call while one is open answers (0, 0).  (-1, 0) when the host has no picker.

- **`fn file_dialog_poll() -> Option<(i32, u32, String)>`**
  The answer of the picker file_dialog opened: None while it is open (or there is none),
  then once (1, 0, the content:// name / the /handles/ path) or (0, 0, "") for cancelled /
  failed.

- **`fn print(_job: &mut crate::PrintJob<'_>) -> i32`**
  Native printing is disabled until a browser print adapter has been connected.

- **`fn open_folder(_path: &str) -> i32`**
  Operating-system folder launch is unavailable.

- **`fn open_url(url: &str) -> i32`**
  Request an explicitly selected web URL; the host still enforces user-gesture restrictions.

- **`fn spawn_self(_args: &[&str]) -> i32`**
  Process spawning is unavailable in the browser.

- **`fn restart_self(_args: &[&str]) -> i32`**
  Process spawning is unavailable in the browser.

- **`fn pen_devices() -> i32`**
  Number of pen devices is not exposed by browser pointer events.

- **`fn ime_pos(x: i32, y: i32, height: i32)`**
  Update the DOM IME/composition caret position in physical pixels.

- **`fn clip_set_many(entries: &[(u32, &[u8])]) -> bool`**
  Set the local multi-format clipboard; browser system text writes are asynchronous requests.
  Android: text and HTML (an image: its PNG) go to the system's clipboard at once; the richer
  forms stay in the app and count while the system's clip is still this one.

- **`fn clip_set(format: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  Set one instance-local clipboard representation.  Android: CLIP_IMAGE (the record of
  ui::clip_set_image) and CLIP_PNG go to the system's clipboard as a PNG.

- **`fn clip_get(format: u32) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  Read an available clipboard representation; the host refreshes text before paste input.
  Android: text, HTML and images from the system's clipboard; the app's own richer forms
  while the system's clip is the one it set.

- **`fn clip_has(format: u32) -> bool`**
  Whether an instance-local clipboard representation is present (Android: on the system's
  clipboard, or the app's own form of its clip).

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_buffer(len: u32) -> usize`**
  Reserve the reusable host input buffer (at most 256 MiB); zero means allocation failure.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_start(width: i32, height: i32, dpi: i32, args_len: u32) -> i32`**
  Start once. Inbox contains newline-separated arguments, excluding the synthetic program name.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_present_us() -> f64`**
  Microseconds spent presenting so far (present_time: the windows' copies, the composition,
  the hand-over to the host); for measurements.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_tick(time_ms: u32)`**
  Advance the owned runtime and cooperative jobs, then submit the composed framebuffer.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_input(time_ms: u32)`**
  Drain input in order, deferring expensive rasterization until the batch's next tick.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_frame_delay() -> u32`**
  Idle host scheduling hint. The host must still wake immediately for new input.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_event( typ: u32, button: u32, mods: u32, window: u32, x: i32, y: i32, data: u32, ) -> u32`**
  Enqueue a bounded platform event; pointer/resize events update virtual window routing.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_env(len: u32) -> u32`**
  Set a per-instance environment value from the host before jfgui_start; inbox: UTF-8
  "NAME=value" (the host's languages arrive as LANGUAGE=de-DE:en-US).  1 = set.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_text(len: u32) -> u32`**
  Enqueue committed UTF-8 from the host composition element; uncommitted IME text stays in the DOM.
  The text goes as commits (whole strings, not one ring slot per character) -> the characters
  queued: fewer when the queue is full (the host calls again with the rest after jfgui_input),
  none without a window that takes text.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_control(len: u32) -> u32`**
  Process one MessagePort/JavaScript agent request only after explicit activation.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_response() -> usize`**
  Address of the current response, valid until the next control request.

- **`fn set_agent_enabled(enabled: bool)`**
  Disable browser control immediately; reactivation must be explicit in application UI/startup.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_agent(enabled: u32) -> u32`**
  Explicitly enable or revoke browser automation after app startup.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_capabilities(bits: u32)`**
  Grant only browser-supported dynamic services; native plugins/IPC/threads cannot be granted.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_date( year: u32, month: u32, day: u32, hour: u32, minute: u32, second: u32, millis: u32, weekday: u32, ) -> u32`**
  Refresh UTC calendar fields, validated before replacing the last host value.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_import(path_len: u32, total_len: u32, dropped: u32, durable: u32) -> u32`**
  Import path + file bytes from the inbox. Selected files can be announced through E_DROP.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_clipboard(format: u32, len: u32) -> u32`**
  Update a browser clipboard representation before delivering the corresponding paste key.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_file_result(id: u32, status: i32, len: u32) -> u32`**
  The answer of the system's picker: the inbox holds the chosen content:// URI (Android) or
  the /handles/ path bound to the chosen file (browser; an opened file was imported first)
  (status 2), a negative status as in jfgui_complete (-4 cancelled).  A file_dialog request
  keeps the name for file_dialog_poll; pick_file's becomes a drop (E_DROP).  1 = taken.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_complete(id: u32, status: i32) -> u32`**
  Confirm a host operation: 0 durable, 1 exported, 2 completed; negatives are explicit errors.

### `plat/web_files.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/web_files.rs`](../lib/plat/web_files.rs)

```text
Worker-local virtual files. File codecs use their existing byte and streaming APIs;
durable storage is a separate asynchronous request confirmed by the browser host.
Files below /handles/ are the user's own files: the host keeps a FileSystemFileHandle for
each (web/handles.js) and every change is written back to it (web.rs write_back: write_file,
AtomicFile's commit, rename onto it, a File stream's sync and drop); imports never are.
```

- **`fn cwd() -> String`**
  Current browser virtual directory; it is unrelated to the host operating system.

- **`fn config_dir() -> Option<String>`**
  Configuration namespace in virtual storage.

- **`fn data_dir() -> Option<String>`**
  Application data namespace in virtual storage.

- **`fn cache_dir() -> Option<String>`**
  Cache namespace in virtual storage.

- **`fn temp_dir() -> Option<String>`**
  Temporary virtual namespace.

- **`fn home() -> Option<String>`**
  Home namespace for user documents imported or created in this app instance.

- **`fn drives() -> Vec<String>`**
  Browser virtual roots; no native drives are exposed.

- **`fn dev_ino(_path: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64)>`**
  Stable filesystem device/inode identity is not available in browser storage.

### `plat/android_host.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/android_host.rs`](../lib/plat/android_host.rs)

```text
android_host -- what Android's Java host does for plat while Rust waits: the
ContentResolver behind content:// (content.rs: ContentFs over AndroidDocs), the system
clipboard (ClipboardManager), the persisted grants of the user's documents.

Rust asks synchronously on the UI thread: jfgui_host_call(kind, bytes) in bridge.c calls
GalleryHost.call(kind, byte[]) (android/GalleryHost.java) and copies its answer into the
buffer jfgui_reply hands out; null / an exception = None.  The file picker and the export of
download() answer later (web.rs: REQUEST_FILE_DIALOG / REQUEST_OPEN / REQUEST_DOWNLOAD,
jfgui_file_result).  A provider whose tree the app listed reports changes through
jfgui_content_changed (DocHost::generation: content.rs's name cache starts again).

Wire (little endian): u32 numbers, i64 times, strings and byte blocks as u32 length + bytes.
  CALL_QUERY     uri -> DocInfo, or nothing (missing / not allowed)
  CALL_CHILDREN  uri -> u32 count, DocInfo..
  CALL_CREATE    u32 dir, parent, name -> DocInfo
  CALL_DELETE    uri -> u32 ok
  CALL_RENAME    uri, name -> DocInfo
  CALL_OPEN      u32 mode (FO_*), uri -> i32 file descriptor (detached: ours to close)
  CALL_CLIP_GET  u32 format (CLIP_TEXT / CLIP_HTML / CLIP_IMAGE) -> u32 found, bytes
  CALL_CLIP_SET  text, html, png (each may be empty) -> i64 stamp of the new clip
  CALL_CLIP_HAS  u32 format -> u32
  CALL_CLIP_STAMP -> i64 (ClipDescription.getTimestamp of the current clip, 0 = none or no
                 access: Android lets only the focused app read the clipboard)
  CALL_CLIP_OURS -> u32 (the clip's first item is a file of the app's GalleryFiles)
  CALL_GRANTS    -> u32 count, (uri, u32 read, u32 write)..
  CALL_RELEASE   uri -> u32 ok
  CALL_SECRET_*  the secret store (android_secret.rs, android/GallerySecrets.java)
  DocInfo: uri, display name, u32 dir, u64 size (u64::MAX unknown), i64 mtime ms, u32 DOC_*

The clipboard: text (and HTML) go to the system; the library's richer forms (RTF, DOCX)
stay in the process and count while the system's clip is still the one we set (its
timestamp; when the app had no focus while setting it -- right after the picker -- the
contents decide once it can read them); images go as a PNG through the app's GalleryFiles
provider when the manifest has one (else only inside the app).
```

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_reply(len: u32) -> usize`**
  (bridge.c) a buffer of len bytes for the answer of a host call; 0 = no memory

- **`struct AndroidDocs`**
  the ContentResolver as ContentFs's host

- **`fn content_fs() -> Arc<dyn Provider>`**
  the provider of content:// (mounted by vfs::route on first use): writes go through a copy
  in the app's data folder (.content-journal), and what a crash left there is finished now

- **`fn content_grants() -> Vec<(String, bool, bool)>`**
  the documents and folders the app keeps access to across restarts (the system's
  persisted grants): (content:// URI, read, write)

- **`fn content_release(uri: &str) -> bool`**
  give up the lasting access to a document or folder the user chose (Android keeps at most
  128 / 512 of them per app) -> whether there was one

### `plat/web_windows.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/web_windows.rs`](../lib/plat/web_windows.rs)

```text
Library windows and popups composited into one browser canvas. Every surface is drawn
by the existing software renderer; the browser host receives pixels, not another UI.
The windows keep their pixels as R, G, B, A rows (the order of the browser's ImageData and
Android's Bitmap): the frames' B, G, R, x is swapped once, while copying the dirty
rectangles in, and the host copies rows without touching pixels.  One window over the
whole canvas without popups is the canvas itself (no composition); otherwise the windows
and popups are composited into the canvas buffer.
```

- **`fn win_create( title: &str, width: i32, height: i32, _flags: u32, _owner: i32, x: i32, y: i32, ) -> i32`**
  Create a window within the app canvas; window zero uses the host viewport.

- **`fn win_destroy(id: i32)`**
  Destroy a library surface and return focus to the main window.

- **`fn win_show(id: i32, mode: u32)`**
  Show or hide a library surface.

- **`fn win_activate(id: i32)`**
  Set keyboard focus to an enabled library window.

- **`fn win_enable(id: i32, enabled: bool)`**
  Enable or disable window input, including modality established by the UI runtime.

- **`fn win_set_rect(id: i32, x: i32, y: i32, width: i32, height: i32)`**
  Change a library surface rectangle, preserving fields equal to PW_KEEP.

- **`fn win_get_rect(id: i32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  Current canvas-relative client rectangle.

- **`fn win_work_area(_id: i32) -> Option<[i32; 4]>`**
  The browser canvas is the available work area.

- **`fn win_set_title(id: i32, title: &str)`**
  Update a library title and the browser document title for window zero.

- **`fn win_state(id: i32) -> u32`**
  Current library state flags; browser surfaces use library-owned chrome.

- **`fn win_cmd(id: i32, command: u32)`**
  Apply library-window commands; close is delivered to the normal app close workflow.

- **`fn win_begin_move(id: i32)`**
  Begin a pointer-driven move of a non-main library window.

- **`fn win_begin_resize(id: i32, edges: u32)`**
  Begin resizing a library surface inside the browser canvas.

- **`fn win_size(id: i32) -> (i32, i32)`**
  Physical client dimensions.

- **`fn win_dpi(id: i32) -> i32`**
  Current host DPI of a library surface.

- **`fn win_set_min_size(id: i32, width: i32, height: i32)`**
  Minimum drag-resize dimensions in DIP.

- **`fn win_present(id: i32, frame: &Frame<'_>, rects: Option<&[[i32; 4]]>)`**
  Copy the dirty rectangles of a software-renderer frame into the window's surface (R, G,
  B, A); the next flush shows them.

- **`fn win_set_cursor(_id: i32, shape: u32)`**
  Request one of the shared browser pointer shapes.

- **`fn win_hit_hook(_hook: Option<fn(i32, i32, i32) -> u32>)`**
  Hit testing remains inside the shared UI; no OS nonclient callback is installed.

- **`fn win_move_hook(_hook: Option<fn(i32, &mut [i32; 4])>)`**
  Dragged library surfaces are not snapped in the browser yet.

- **`fn set_refresh(_callback: Option<fn()>)`**
  Native modal resize callbacks are unnecessary for host-stepped browser rendering.

- **`fn cursor_create( _pixels: &[u8], _width: i32, _height: i32, _x: i32, _y: i32, _dpi: i32, ) -> i32`**
  Custom native cursor handles are unavailable; use the shared system-shape cursor mapping.

- **`fn cursor_destroy(_id: i32)`**
  No native custom cursor handle exists.

- **`fn cursor_dpi(dpi: i32) -> i32`**
  Cursor scale follows the canvas DPI.

- **`fn popup_anchor(_slot: u32, _anchor: [i32; 4], _kind: u32, _nat: [i32; 2])`**
  The canvas shows popups where the library put them (inside the canvas).

### `plat/web_screen.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/web_screen.rs`](../lib/plat/web_screen.rs)

```text
web_screen -- (screen.rs) the monitors the browser / Android host reports, the browser's
EyeDropper

  jfgui_screens(len) -> count      the host's monitors from the inbox: one line per monitor,
                                   "x y w h wx wy ww wh dpi refresh_mhz primary name" (name:
                                   the rest of the line, may be empty); sent at start and on
                                   every change (then E_SETTINGS with SET_MONITORS).  Browser
                                   (web/loader.js): window.screen (CSS pixels, availLeft /
                                   availTop / availWidth / availHeight, devicePixelRatio) or,
                                   where the page may already (permission "window-management"
                                   granted), getScreenDetails() with every screen; Android
                                   (android/GalleryActivity.java): DisplayManager.getDisplays()
                                   with their bounds, density and refresh rate
  monitors()                       that list; before it arrives one monitor of the viewport
  pick_start()                     REQUEST_PICK_COLOR: the browser's EyeDropper (Chromium,
                                   from the user's gesture), answered by jfgui_color(id, status,
                                   rgb); without EyeDropper (the host's capability bit
                                   HOST_EYEDROPPER) and on Android Unavailable
  capture_*                        Unavailable (no picture of the screen here)
```

```rust
/// (browser) open the EyeDropper; no payload; answered by jfgui_color
REQUEST_PICK_COLOR: u32 = 21
```

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_screens(len: u32) -> u32`**
  The host's monitors (inbox: one line per monitor, see the module header) -> how many were
  taken; a different list once the app runs is a change (E_SETTINGS with SET_MONITORS; the
  first one after the start too: the app saw the viewport until then).

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_color(id: u32, status: i32, rgb: u32) -> u32`**
  The EyeDropper's answer to the pick request id: status 2 = picked (rgb 0xRRGGBB), -4
  cancelled, -1 refused, -3 not supported, else failed.  1 = taken.

### `plat/android_ime.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/android_ime.rs`](../lib/plat/android_ime.rs)

```text
Android editor snapshots and edits. UTF-8 byte offsets cross JNI; Java owns UTF-16.
This adapter shares the host's single UI thread and never invokes Android under a lock.
```

- **`fn android_ime_publish(id: u32, text: &[u8], anchor: usize, caret: usize, flags: u32)`**
  Publish the focused editor's actual text, flags and UTF-8 selection to Android's IME.

- **`fn android_ime_clear()`**
  Close the Android input session when library focus leaves an editor.

- **`fn android_ime_take(id: u32) -> Option<(Vec<u8>, usize, usize)>`**
  Consume one host edit for the focused widget, including the requested UTF-8 selection.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_editor_snapshot() -> u32`**
  Build a JNI snapshot: id, flags, anchor, caret (little-endian u32), then UTF-8 text.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_editor_data() -> usize`**
  Snapshot address, valid until the next snapshot call on this same host thread.

- **`extern "C" fn jfgui_editor_replace(id: u32, len: u32, anchor: u32, caret: u32) -> u32`**
  Queue a bounded, valid editor replacement from the shared JNI input buffer.

### `plat/web_threads.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/web_threads.rs`](../lib/plat/web_threads.rs)

```text
OS primitives for the existing pool.rs scheduler. Each Worker instantiates the
same module and shared memory, with its own __stack_pointer. Only the app worker
enters the UI. LLD's atomic memory initializer runs once across all instances.
```

- **`struct Thread`**
  A browser worker with an exclusively owned stack and a join completion word.

**`impl Thread`**

- **`fn join(self)`**
  Wait until JavaScript has returned from WASM before releasing its stack.

- **`fn spawn(stack: usize, f: Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>) -> Option<Thread>`**
  Start a closure on a compute worker; return None if the host cannot start it.

- **`struct Sem(AtomicU32)`**
  Counting semaphore backed by WebAssembly atomics and worker-only Atomics.wait.

**`impl Sem`**

- **`fn new(initial: u32) -> Option<Self>`**
  Construct a semaphore with the specified number of available units.
- **`fn post(&self, count: u32)`**
  Publish work and wake up to count sleeping workers.
- **`fn wait(&self, timeout: i32) -> bool`**
  Take a unit; negative timeout waits indefinitely, zero only tries once.

### `plat/clipdrop.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/clipdrop.rs`](../lib/plat/clipdrop.rs)

```text
clipdrop -- the shared helpers of the clipboard image formats and file drops (every OS)
                                    [src/plat/clipdrop.s; docs/modules/CLIPBOARD_DND.md]

  drop_reset()                 start a new pending drop (the old list and data are dropped)
  drop_add(path) -> bool       one path (empty, too long, NUL inside or too many: false)
  drop_uri_list(data) -> n     text/uri-list: every file:// URI (host empty or "localhost"),
                               %XX decoded, '#' lines skipped
  drop_take() -> paths         hand the pending list over (E_DROP data = its count)
  clip_dib_to_bmp(dib) -> BMP file   a clipboard DIB (BITMAPCOREHEADER / INFO / V4 / V5
       header, masks, colour table, pixels) as a BMP file, None when the header is
       invalid.  32-bit BI_RGB / BI_BITFIELDS / BI_ALPHABITFIELDS DIBs are rewritten with
       a V5 header (BI_BITFIELDS, the source masks) and paint.net's alpha rule: the alpha
       channel (the 4th byte of BI_RGB, else the header's alpha mask) is used when any
       pixel has a non-zero alpha, else the image is opaque (alpha mask 0).  Other depths
       are copied with a BITMAPFILEHEADER in front.
  clip_bmp_fix(bmp) -> BMP file   the same rule for a BMP file (image/bmp of other programs)

Every length is checked: clipboard / drop data come from other programs.  The pending
list keeps raw bytes (a decoded URI need not be UTF-8); drop_take converts lossily.
```

- **`fn drop_reset()`**
  forget the pending list (and the rest of the pending drop: dnd.rs)

- **`fn drop_add(path: &str) -> bool`**
  one path (copied) -> false when it is empty, too long, has a NUL or the list is full

- **`fn drop_uri_list(data: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  text/uri-list -> paths added

- **`fn drop_take() -> Vec<String>`**
  hand the pending list over (it starts empty again)

- **`fn clip_dib_to_bmp(dib: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  a clipboard DIB as a BMP file (None: invalid header)

- **`fn clip_bmp_fix(bmp: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  a BMP file of another program with the same alpha rule

- **`fn clipimg_pack(png: &[u8], bmp: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the CLIPIMG bytes of a PNG file and a BMP file (either may be empty)

- **`fn clipimg_split(data: &[u8]) -> Option<(&[u8], &[u8])>`**
  (PNG, BMP) of CLIPIMG bytes (an absent part is empty; None: malformed)

### `plat/dnd.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/dnd.rs`](../lib/plat/dnd.rs)

```text
dnd -- drag and drop between programs: what a drag carries, the target hook, the pending
drop and the app's own outgoing drag (the parts every OS shares)       (docs/GUIDE.md §7)

  DT_FILES / DT_TEXT / DT_URL / DT_HTML / DT_IMAGE   kinds of content (bits, DT_STD = all);
                               DT_USER0 << k: the app's own kinds (internal drags only)
  DE_COPY / DE_MOVE / DE_LINK  effects (bits)
  DragData                     the content of one drag (paths, text, URLs, HTML, an image, the
                               app's own bytes) and the effects
  drag_hook(Some(f))           f(pw, x, y, types) -> (accepted types, accepted effects): what the
                               UI takes at a point (px) of platform window pw.  The OS layers
                               ask it synchronously while something is dragged over a window
                               (IDropTarget::DragOver, XdndPosition, wl_data_device.motion).
  drag_query(pw, x, y, types, allowed, mods) -> (types, effect)   (OS layers) the hook's answer
                               with one effect picked; without a hook: files, copy (as before).
                               Files are never moved: a source deletes what it moved, and
                               the app gets only the paths (copy or link instead)
  drag_effect_pick(allowed, mods) -> effect   Ctrl copy, Shift move, Ctrl+Shift link; else
                               the first of copy / move / link the mask allows
  drop_data_take() -> DragData the pending drop of E_DROP: the paths of drop_take and the rest
  drop_set_text / drop_set_html / drop_add_url / drop_set_image / drop_set_effect
                               (OS layers) fill the pending drop (drop_reset empties it)
  drop_text_from(bytes, utf16) / drop_url_list(text)   decoding helpers of the OS layers
  drag_start(data) -> bool     drag data out of the app while the left button is held (the UI
                               calls it when an internal drag leaves its window); false when
                               the platform cannot (headless, browser) or a drag runs.
                               E_DRAG_END follows (data = the effect, 0 = cancelled / refused).
  drag_running() -> bool       an outgoing drag runs

Events: E_DRAG (x, y = position in window px, data = DT_* offered | DE_* allowed << 8; data 0:
the drag left the window, was dropped or cancelled) while another program's drag (or our
own outgoing one) is over a window; E_DROP (x, y, data = the number of paths) when it is
dropped there; E_DRAG_END when our own outgoing drag ended.
Windows: OLE (win_dnd.rs: IDropTarget per window, DoDragDrop with our IDataObject / IDropSource);
X11: Xdnd 5 target and source (linux_x11_dnd.rs); Wayland: wl_data_device (linux_wl_clip.rs).
Everything that comes from another program is bounded (sizes, counts) and checked.
```

*kinds of content (bits)*

```rust
DT_FILES: u32 = 1  // paths (file:// URIs, CF_HDROP)
DT_TEXT: u32 = 2  // UTF-8 text
DT_URL: u32 = 4  // URLs that are not local files
DT_HTML: u32 = 8  // a UTF-8 HTML fragment
DT_IMAGE: u32 = 16  // an image file (PNG; a DIB arrives as BMP)
DT_STD: u32 = 31  // every kind other programs know
DT_USER0: u32 = 1 << 8  // the app's own kinds: DT_USER0 << k, k = 0..23
```

*effects (bits)*

```rust
DE_COPY: u32 = 1  // the target copies (DROPEFFECT_COPY, XdndActionCopy)
DE_MOVE: u32 = 2  // the target moves: the source deletes its original
DE_LINK: u32 = 4  // the target links to it (not on Wayland)
DE_ALL: u32 = 7  // every effect
```

- **`struct DragData`**
  the content of one drag (a drop that arrives, or what the app drags)
  - `files: Vec<String>` -- paths of files and folders
  - `text: Option<String>` -- plain text
  - `urls: Vec<String>` -- URLs (not local files)
  - `html: Option<String>` -- an HTML fragment (UTF-8)
  - `image: Option<Vec<u8>>` -- an image file: PNG (a drop of a DIB / image/bmp arrives as a BMP file)
  - `bmp: Option<Vec<u8>>` -- (drag out) the same image as a BMP file, offered as DIB / image/bmp too (optional)
  - `app: u32` -- the app's own kind (DT_USER0 &lt;&lt; k bits) and bytes: internal drags only
  - `bytes: Vec<u8>`
  - `label: String` -- what the drag shows next to the pointer inside the app (empty: from the content)
  - `effects: u32` -- drag out: the DE_\* effects the source allows (0 = copy | move); a drop: the effect chosen

**`impl DragData`**

- **`fn types(&self) -> u32`**
  the DT_\* kinds it carries (the app's own kinds included)
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
  nothing to drag
- **`fn of_text(s: &str) -> DragData`**
  text only
- **`fn of_files(paths: &[&str]) -> DragData`**
  paths only
- **`fn of_app(kind: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> DragData`**
  the app's own kind (DT_USER0 &lt;&lt; k) and bytes
- **`fn allowed(&self) -> u32`**
  the effects a drag out allows (0 means copy | move)

- **`type DragHook = fn(i32, i32, i32, u32) -> (u32, u32)`**
  what the UI takes at a point: f(platform window, x, y px, offered DT_\*) -> (accepted DT_\*,
  accepted DE_\*)

- **`fn drag_hook(f: Option<DragHook>)`**
  install (Some) or remove (None) the drop target hook (the UI does it for its windows)

- **`fn drag_effect_pick(allowed: u32, mods: u8) -> u32`**
  the effect of a drop: the modifier keys choose (Ctrl copy, Shift move, Ctrl+Shift link),
  else the first of copy / move / link that `allowed` has (0: none)

- **`fn drag_query(pw: i32, x: i32, y: i32, types: u32, allowed: u32, mods: u8) -> (u32, u32)`**
  (OS layers) what platform window pw takes at (x, y) px of a drag offering `types` with the
  effects `allowed` (0 = copy | move) -> (accepted types, the effect); (0, 0) = refused

- **`fn drop_set_text(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  (OS layers) the pending drop's text (UTF-8 bytes; cut at a NUL) -> false when too large

- **`fn drop_set_html(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  (OS layers) the pending drop's HTML fragment (UTF-8 bytes) -> false when too large

- **`fn drop_add_url(url: &str) -> bool`**
  (OS layers) one URL of the pending drop ("scheme:...", no blanks or control characters,
  bounded, no duplicates) -> added

- **`fn drop_set_image(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> bool`**
  (OS layers) the pending drop's image file (PNG or BMP bytes) -> false when too large

- **`fn drop_set_effect(effect: u32)`**
  (OS layers) the effect the drop was made with (DE_\*)

- **`fn drop_data_take() -> DragData`**
  the pending drop (E_DROP): its paths (drop_take) and the rest; both start empty again

- **`fn drop_text_from(bytes: &[u8], utf16: bool) -> Vec<u8>`**
  (OS layers) text in other programs' encodings -> UTF-8 bytes: UTF-16 LE (utf16, up to a
  NUL unit) or bytes as they are (up to a NUL)

- **`fn drop_url_list(text: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  (OS layers) the lines of a URL list (text/uri-list, text/x-moz-url, UniformResourceLocator):
  '#' lines skipped, every other line one URL; local files are left to drop_uri_list -> URLs
  added (also used for the URL a browser drags)

- **`fn drag_start(data: DragData) -> bool`**
  drag `data` out of the app (call while the left button is held) -> started; E_DRAG_END
  (data = the effect, 0 = cancelled or refused) follows.  Only the standard kinds leave
  the app.

- **`fn drag_running() -> bool`**
  an outgoing drag runs (until its E_DRAG_END is queued)
