### `plat/evq.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/evq.rs`](../lib/plat/evq.rs)

```text
evq -- the platform event ring (shared by every platform and the script runner)
                                                                       [src/plat/evq.s]

  evq_push(ev) -> false when the event was dropped (ring and overflow full)
  evq_pop() -> Some(event)        evq_count()        evq_clear()
  evq_dropped() -> events dropped so far (tests)
  evq_pen_data(pressure, type, tilt_x, tilt_y) -> u32   (PN1) Event::data of a pointer
       event: pressure -1 = the device has none (-> 0), else clamped to 1..PRESSURE_ONE;
       type PTR_*; tilts in degrees, clamped to -63..63.  0 for PTR_MOUSE and while pen
       input is off.
  pen_enable(on)    pen input on (default) / off: off = pens report plain mouse events
  pen_enabled() -> bool

The OS layer pushes from its message handlers, the UI core pops between frames (one
thread; the lock only makes the static safe).

A burst larger than the ring (one socket read of synthetic keys on X11 / Wayland, a client
flooding input: their dispatch must read on to an awaited reply, so it cannot stop at a
full ring) waits in a second-level queue on the heap, in order; the ring takes from it as
it drains.  Only beyond EVQ_MORE_MAX is an event dropped: counted (evq_dropped) and
logged once per burst.  Windows keeps WM_CHAR bursts in its own message queue instead
(wait() stops pumping at EVQ_CAP - 64).
```

```rust
PD_PRESSURE: u32 = 0xFFFF  // bits 0..15 pressure 1..PRESSURE_ONE, 0 = none (full)
PD_TYPE_SHIFT: u32 = 16  // bits 16..17 PTR_*
PD_TILTX_SHIFT: u32 = 18  // bits 18..24 i7 tilt x in degrees (-63..63, + = right)
PD_TILTY_SHIFT: u32 = 25  // bits 25..31 i7 tilt y in degrees (+ = towards the user)
PRESSURE_ONE: i32 = 65535
```

- **`fn evq_push(e: Event) -> bool`**
  append an event (behind a full ring: the overflow queue) -> false when it was dropped
  (more than EVQ_MORE_MAX events wait)

- **`fn evq_pop() -> Option<Event>`**
  the oldest queued event

- **`fn evq_count() -> u32`**
  events queued (the ring and the overflow queue)

- **`fn evq_clear()`**

- **`fn evq_dropped() -> u32`**
  events dropped since the start because more than EVQ_MORE_MAX waited (tests)

- **`fn evq_pen_data(pressure: i32, typ: u32, tilt_x: i32, tilt_y: i32) -> u32`**
  Event::data of a pen pointer event (0 for a mouse or while pen input is off)

- **`fn pen_enable(on: bool)`**
  pen input on (default) / off (pens become plain mouse events)

- **`fn pen_enabled() -> bool`**

```text
icc -- the colour profile of the monitor a window is on
         [src/plat/win/win_icc.s, src/plat/linux/lx_icc.s; docs/modules/COLOR_MANAGEMENT.md]

  monitor_icc(w) -> profile bytes / None
       Windows: the ICC profile of the monitor that shows window w (0 = the main window;
       other windows use the main window's monitor; ICC_MON_PRIMARY (-1) = the primary
       monitor, no window needed): GetMonitorInfoW -> CreateDCW(device) -> GetICMProfileW
       -> the file.  No window (headless) -> None.
       Linux X11: the root window property _ICC_PROFILE (ICC Profiles in X Specification;
       set by colord / xiccd / dispwin for screen 0); profiles above 1 MB are ignored.
       Wayland: None -- the core protocol has no colour management (the compositor shows
       sRGB), so callers assume sRGB.  No display (headless): None.
       Every profile is validated (icc_check: header, 'acsp', version 2..5, tag table).
  monitor_key(w) -> u64   Windows: the HMONITOR of that monitor (0 = none) -- cheap; poll
       it every frame and query the profile again when it changes (window moved to another
       monitor).  Linux: 0 (the X11 property is per screen, not per monitor).

icc_check is a private copy of img_core::icc::icc_check (plat does not depend on the image
crates).  Linux: the X11 requests go through linux_x11.rs (x11s::root_property, marked
plat-shared there).
```

```rust
/// monitor_icc / monitor_key: the primary monitor instead of a window's
ICC_MON_PRIMARY: i32 = -1
```

- **`fn monitor_icc(w: i32) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the ICC profile of the monitor showing window w (validated), None = assume sRGB
  [plat_monitor_icc]

- **`fn monitor_key(w: i32) -> u64`**
  a cheap key of the monitor showing window w (poll it every frame; 0 = unknown)
  [plat_monitor_key]

### `plat/plib.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/plib.rs`](../lib/plat/plib.rs)

```text
plib -- plugin libraries and the crash guard: the portable part
                                       [src/plat/plib.s; docs/modules/PLUGIN_LOADER.md]

  lib_open(path) -> Lib / Err(LIBE_*)    Windows: LoadLibraryExW without DllMain / imports
                                         (win_lib.rs); Linux: own ELF ET_DYN loader
                                         (linux_elfload.rs)
  lib_sym(h, name) -> address | 0        exported symbol (own export / .dynsym lookup)
  lib_close(h)                           unload (also when a Lib is dropped)
  lib_seg(h, addr) -> (end of the image segment holding addr (0 = outside), LIBA_*)
                                         -- check every pointer a plugin hands over (data:
                                         LIBA_R, code: LIBA_X) before dereferencing it
  guard_init()                           install the OS fault handler once (VEH on
                                         Windows, SIGSEGV / SIGBUS / SIGILL / SIGFPE /
                                         SIGTRAP on Linux; linux_guard.rs)
  guard_call(f, a1, a2, a3, a4, info) -> (rax, rdx)
       calls the code at address f with the Win64 ABI (on Linux too: the plugin ABI) as
       f(a1, a2, a3, a4); a fault inside it on this thread (also in nested host code)
       resumes here with rax = rdx = ERR_FAULT and info (GuardInfo) filled; otherwise
       info.kind = 0 and rax / rdx are those of f.  Nested calls are allowed.  ERR_LIMIT
       when the thread table is full (GT_MAX threads).
  guard_tag() -> u64                     info.tag of this thread's innermost active guard
                                         (0 = none)

guard_call pushes a guard record (rsp / rbp of its trampoline, xmm6-15, MXCSR, x87
control word, tag) and links it as the innermost guard of the calling thread in a table
{OS thread id -> record} (thread id = TEB ClientId on Windows, gettid on Linux).  The
handlers find the thread's entry by its id, unlink the innermost record (a second fault
goes to the enclosing guard), store the fault into it and resume the thread at
jfgui_guard_fault_ip with rsp / rbp of the trampoline's body.  That code restores x87,
MXCSR, DF and xmm6-15 and returns through the epilogue, which restores the caller's
callee-saved registers.  NOT a sandbox: the guard catches faults, nothing else (see the
docs: corrupt state stays corrupt, hangs are not detected).

Safety contract: guard_call runs untrusted machine code at an arbitrary address; it is a
safe function only in the sense the assembly API is: the caller hands it addresses of
loaded plugin code (lib_sym) or of its own `extern "win64"` functions.  Pointers a plugin
returns are checked with lib_seg before the host reads through them.
```

```rust
ERR_FAULT: i32 = -64  // the guarded call faulted (plugin disabled)
LIBA_R: u32 = 1  // lib_seg flags
LIBA_W: u32 = 2
LIBA_X: u32 = 4
LIBE_IO: u32 = 1  // file missing / unreadable / larger than LIB_FILE_MAX
LIBE_FORMAT: u32 = 2  // not an x86-64 ELF shared object / PE DLL, or damaged
LIBE_DEPS: u32 = 3  // needs other libraries / undefined symbols
LIBE_RELOC: u32 = 4  // unsupported relocation
LIBE_NOMEM: u32 = 5
LIBE_INIT: u32 = 6  // TLS, initialisers or an interpreter (not supported)
LIBE_MAP: u32 = 7  // mmap / mprotect failed
LIB_FILE_MAX: u64 = 64 << 20
LH_SEGMAX: usize = 16
GK_NONE: u32 = 0
GK_ACCESS: u32 = 1  // access violation / SIGSEGV
GK_ILLEGAL: u32 = 2  // illegal / privileged instruction / SIGILL
GK_ARITH: u32 = 3  // division by zero, overflow, FP trap / SIGFPE
GK_BUS: u32 = 4  // misalignment / SIGBUS
GK_BREAK: u32 = 5  // breakpoint (int3) / SIGTRAP
GK_STACK: u32 = 6  // stack overflow (Windows)
GT_MAX: usize = 128
```

- **`struct LibSeg`**
  one segment of a loaded image: [start, end), LIBA_\*
  - `start: usize`
  - `end: usize`
  - `flags: u32`

- **`struct Lib`**
  a loaded plugin library (LIBH)

**`impl Lib`**

- **`fn base(&self) -> usize`**
  the image base
- **`fn span(&self) -> usize`**
  bytes mapped from the base
- **`fn segs(&self) -> &[LibSeg]`**
  the segments (Windows: the headers, then every section)

- **`fn lib_close(h: Lib)`**
  unload a library (dropping the Lib does the same)  [plat_lib_close]

- **`fn lib_seg(h: &Lib, addr: usize) -> (usize, u32)`**
  the end of the segment of h holding addr (0 = none) and its LIBA_\* flags  [plat_lib_seg]

- **`struct GuardInfo`**
  GUARDINFO: what a guarded call hit; tag is an input (guard_tag)
  - `kind: u32` -- GK_\* (0 = no fault)
  - `code: u32` -- NTSTATUS (Windows) / signal number (Linux)
  - `pc: u64` -- faulting instruction
  - `addr: u64` -- faulting data address (access faults) or 0
  - `tag: u64` -- in: tag of this guard (guard_tag)

- **`fn guard_init() -> i32`**
  install the fault handler (idempotent, thread safe)  [plat_guard_init]

- **`fn guard_tag() -> u64`**
  info.tag of the innermost active guard of this thread (0 = none)  [plat_guard_tag]

- **`fn guard_call(f: usize, a1: u64, a2: u64, a3: u64, a4: u64, info: Option<&mut GuardInfo>) -> (u64, u64)`**
  f(a1, a2, a3, a4) under the crash guard (see the file header)  [plat_guard_call]

- **`fn guard_run<R, F: FnOnce() -> R>(f: F, info: Option<&mut GuardInfo>) -> Result<R, i32>`**
  run the Rust closure f under the crash guard -> Ok(result), Err(ERR_FAULT) when it faulted
  (info filled), Err(ERR_LIMIT) when the thread table is full (f did not run).  A fault
  abandons f's frames without running destructors (what they own leaks): meant for host
  code that may touch plugin memory (the loader fuzz runs lib_open / lib_sym under it).

- **`fn guard_read(addr: usize, len: usize) -> Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>`**
  copy len bytes at any address under the crash guard -> None when addr is 0, the copy
  faulted or the memory for the copy is missing  (pn-sys)

- **`fn guard_write(addr: usize, data: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  write data at any address under the crash guard -> false when addr is 0 or it faulted
  (pn-sys)

- **`fn lib_read(h: &Lib, addr: usize, len: usize) -> Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>`**
  copy len bytes at addr of the image of h -- only when they lie in one readable segment
  (lib_seg), else None (pointers a plugin hands over)

- **`fn guard_test_code(k: u32) -> usize`**
  (test aid) the address of guard test function k (see above), 0 for an unknown k

- **`fn guard_test_state() -> (u32, u32, bool)`**
  (test aid) this thread's MXCSR, x87 control word and direction flag

### `plat/print.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/print.rs`](../lib/plat/print.rs)

```text
print -- printing, the OS-independent part: paper sizes, page layout, rows over white, the
job as a one-page PDF  [src/plat/print.s, src/img/pdfwrite.s; docs/modules/PRINT.md]

  print(job) -> 0 printed / ERR_CANCEL / ERR_UNSUPPORTED / ERR_IO / ERR_NOMEM / ERR_DIMS
       the OS part: win_print.rs (PrintDlgExW + GDI), linux_print.rs (portal Print + PDF)
  page_init(paper, flags) -> PPage         the paper PAPER_* in pt (PJF_LANDSCAPE swaps
                                           width / height), no unprintable edge
  layout(job, page) -> Place               the image rectangle and the printable area on
                                           the page (pt, from the top-left)
  row_white(dst, src, n, mode)             n pixels (B, G, R, A) -> n * 3 bytes composited
                                           over white (PRW_* mode bits)
  print_pdf(job, page) -> PDF bytes / ERR_*  the job laid out on page as a one-page PDF
                                           (job.page_w / page_h set)
  print_dpi(unit, dpu) -> f64              pixels per inch from a resolution in unit (0 none
                                           -> 96, 1 inch, 2 cm)
  pdf_write_image(src, opt) -> PDF bytes / ERR_*   one image on one PDF page (pdfwrite.s)
  set_print_deflate(f)                     the zlib compressor of the PDF streams

Deviation (plat-shared): plat must not depend on the image crates, so pdfwrite.s is ported
here and the one thing it took from img -- zlib_deflate -- comes through a hook.  An app
sets it to img_core::deflate::zlib_deflate (then the PDF is byte-identical to the
assembly's); without a hook the streams are zlib "stored" blocks (a valid, uncompressed
PDF).  The source is a PrintSrc (rows of B, G, R, A bytes; the gfx::Surface fields)
instead of a SURFACE pointer.
```

*results (the ERR_\* of jfgui.inc / plugin.inc that plat returns)*

```rust
ERR_UNSUPPORTED: i32 = -9
ERR_DIMS: i32 = -12
ERR_IO: i32 = -13
ERR_CANCEL: i32 = -14
```

*the source formats (FMT_\* of jfgui.inc)*

```rust
PRINT_PARGB: u8 = 1  // premultiplied
PRINT_ARGB: u8 = 3  // straight
```

```rust
PJF_LANDSCAPE: u32 = 1  // Querformat
PJF_CENTER: u32 = 2  // centre in the printable area (else its top-left corner)
PJF_SMASK: u32 = 4  // PDF only: straight colours + alpha as /SMask (no white)
```

*PrintJob::scale*

```rust
PJS_FIT: u32 = 0  // as large as the printable area allows (aspect kept)
PJS_DPI: u32 = 1  // original size: pixels / DPI inches
PJS_PERCENT: u32 = 2  // PrintJob::percent of the original size
```

*paper*

```rust
PAPER_A4: u32 = 0
PAPER_LETTER: u32 = 1
PAPER_A5: u32 = 2
PAPER_LEGAL: u32 = 3
PAPER_A3: u32 = 4
```

```rust
PRW_PREMUL: u32 = 2  // source is premultiplied
```

- **`struct PrintSrc<'a>`**
  the pixels of a print job: rows of 32-bit B, G, R, A (the fields of gfx::Surface)
  - `px: &'a [u8]`

  - `h: i32`
  - `stride: i32`

  - `dpi_x: f64` -- image pixels per inch (&lt;= 0: 96)
  - `dpi_y: f64` -- (&lt;= 0: dpi_x)
  - `flags: u32` -- PJF_\*
  - `scale: u32` -- PJS_\*
  - `percent: u32` -- PJS_PERCENT: 1..10000 % of the size by DPI
  - `margin: u32` -- on every side, 1/100 mm (the printer's unprintable edge wins when larger)
  - `paper: u32` -- PAPER_\* suggested to the dialog / used without one
  - `copies: u32` -- copies (informative, 0 = unknown)
  - `page_w: f64` -- page size in pt the job was laid out on
  - `page_h: f64`

### `plat/modhost.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/modhost.rs`](../lib/plat/modhost.rs)

```text
modhost -- loadable modules, the host side (jxl-module): the JPEG XL writer module jxlenc
                                                                      [jxl-module: no asm]

  jxlenc_set_path(Some(path) | None)   the module file: None = <exe folder>/jxlenc.dll
                             (Linux jxlenc.so); "off" = none.  Before the first use.
  jxlenc_ready() -> bool     the module is loaded (loads it on the first call and keeps it;
                             a missing / refused file stays missing for the process)
  jxlenc_file() -> path      the file the module was (or would be) loaded from
  jxlenc_encode(req) -> Some(file / ERR_*) | None (no module)
  module_at(addr) -> Some((file name, image base))   the loaded module holding addr (crash
                             reports: offsets into its .map; allocation-free)

The module (modules/jxlenc) is a no_std cdylib without imports, loaded with the plugin
loader (lib_open / lib_sym: win_lib.rs, linux_elfload.rs -- the same checks), its one export
jxlenc_module(&HostTable) -> &ModTable (modabi.rs: the records, the memory and thread rules).
It is our own code, called without a guard: a fault inside it is a crash with the normal
report, a panic comes back through HostTable::panic into rt::crash::report.  The JPEG XL
specifics (what JxlReq carries) are img_jxl::writer's; this file only moves the bytes.
jfgui_JXLENC_TEST=panic | fault (tests) makes the module panic / fault in its encode.
```

```rust
/// the module's file name next to the exe
JXLENC_FILE: &str = "jxlenc.dll"
/// the module's file name next to the exe
JXLENC_FILE: &str = "jxlenc.so"
```

- **`fn jxlenc_set_path(path: Option<String>)`**

### `plat/modabi.rs`

Source: [`lib/plat/modabi.rs`](../lib/plat/modabi.rs)

```text
modabi -- the ABI of loadable modules (jxl-module): the records the host (modhost.rs) and a
module (the module runtime modules/modrt, which includes this file) exchange
                                                                      [jxl-module: no asm]

A module is a no_std cdylib linked against nothing (no imports; built and checked like a
Rust PaintCraft plugin, build_rs.py section jxl-module) that exports exactly one function

    <name>_module(host: *const HostTable) -> *const ModTable          extern "win64"

(`jxlenc_module` for the JPEG XL writer).  The host keeps the module loaded for the rest of
the process; the module keeps the HostTable pointer.  Null = the module refuses the host
(another MOD_VERSION).  Every function pointer is extern "win64" on both systems (as the
plugin ABI), so the records are the same on Windows and Linux.

Memory: the module's global allocator is the host's (HostTable::alloc / free = the host's
GlobalAlloc with the same Layout), so blocks move between both sides as Vec<u8> raw parts
(JxlReq::rgba to the module, JxlRes to the host) without a copy.
Threads: parallel_for runs item(ctx, index, job) on the host's worker pool (and the calling
thread); thr_count / thr_self are the pool's, so per-thread arrays of the module work as in
the host.  A panic of the module ends in HostTable::panic: the host's normal crash report
(stderr "panic: jxlenc: ...", the crash hook, exit code 3); a fault inside the module code
goes to the host's crash handlers like any other.

Version 1.  Layouts are asserted below.
```

```rust
/// ModTable::magic ("MODM" little endian)
MOD_MAGIC: u32 = 0x4D44_4F4D
/// the ABI version of this file
MOD_VERSION: u32 = 1
/// ModTable::kind of the JPEG XL writer
MOD_JXLENC: u32 = 1
/// JxlReq::blobs: which of the blobs are present (None vs Some)
JXB_ICC: u32 = 1
JXB_EXIF: u32 = 2
JXB_XMP: u32 = 4
/// JxlReq::test: crash tests of the module (plat::jxlenc_*: jfgui_JXLENC_TEST=panic / fault)
JXT_PANIC: u32 = 1
JXT_FAULT: u32 = 2
```

- **`type ItemFn = extern "win64" fn(ctx: *const c_void, index: usize, job: *const c_void)`**
  one item of a parallel loop: item(ctx, index, job)

- **`struct HostTable`**
  the host's functions (the module keeps the pointer)
  - `size: u32` -- size_of::&lt;HostTable>()
  - `version: u32` -- MOD_VERSION
  - `cpu: u32` -- the host's rt::cpu::features() (--simd sse2: 0, the module then uses SSE2 too)
  - `threads: u32` -- workers of the host's pool
  - `alloc: extern "win64" fn(size: usize, align: usize, zeroed: u32) -> *mut u8` -- a block of `size` bytes aligned to `align` from the host's allocator (zeroed != 0:
    cleared), null when out of memory
  - `free: extern "win64" fn(p: *mut u8, size: usize, align: usize)` -- free a block of alloc with its size and alignment
  - `parallel_for: extern "win64" fn(count: usize, ctx: *const c_void, item: ItemFn) -> u32` -- item(ctx, i, job) for i in 0..count on the pool; 0 = done, 1 = cancelled
  - `job_cancel: extern "win64" fn(job: *const c_void)` -- job.cancel() of the job an item got
  - `job_cancelled: extern "win64" fn(job: *const c_void) -> u32` -- job.cancelled()
  - `thr_count: extern "win64" fn() -> u32` -- the pool's thr_count() / thr_self()
  - `thr_self: extern "win64" fn() -> usize`
  - `yield_now: extern "win64" fn()` -- give the time slice away (spin locks)
  - `log: extern "win64" fn(msg: *const u8, len: usize)` -- one line on stderr ("&lt;module>: msg")
  - `panic: extern "win64" fn(msg: *const u8, len: usize) -> !` -- a panic of the module (UTF-8 message): the host's crash report, exit code 3

- **`struct ModTable`**
  what a module offers
  - `size: u32` -- size_of::&lt;ModTable>()
  - `version: u32` -- MOD_VERSION
  - `magic: u32` -- MOD_MAGIC
  - `kind: u32` -- MOD_JXLENC
  - `jxl_encode: extern "win64" fn(req: *const JxlReq, res: *mut JxlRes) -> i32` -- the JPEG XL writer: 0 and res filled, or ERR_\* (res empty)

- **`struct JxlReq`**
  a JPEG XL encode: the samples of img_jxl::writer::image_of and the writer's options
  - `size: u32` -- size_of::&lt;JxlReq>()
  - `w: u32`
  - `h: u32`
  - `gray: u32` -- Px::gray
  - `alpha: u32` -- Px::alpha
  - `effort: u32`
  - `quality: u32`
  - `flags: u32` -- IO_FLAGS
  - `blobs: u32` -- JXB_\*: which blobs are present
  - `test: u32` -- JXT_\* (0)
  - `rgba: *mut u8` -- Px::rgba (R, G, B, A per pixel) as Vec raw parts: the module owns it from now on
  - `rgba_len: usize`
  - `rgba_cap: usize`
  - `icc: *const u8`
  - `icc_len: usize`
  - `exif: *const u8`
  - `exif_len: usize`
  - `xmp: *const u8`
  - `xmp_len: usize`
  - `cancel: *const u32` -- the cancel flag (an AtomicU32), null = none

- **`struct JxlRes`**
  the file the writer made, as Vec raw parts (the host owns it from now on)
  - `data: *mut u8`
  - `len: usize`
  - `cap: usize`

```text
features and files are in plat (they need unsafe).
```

### `base/ini.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/ini.rs`](../lib/base/ini.rs)

```text
ini -- settings files: UTF-8 "[section]" / "key=value" text              [src/core/ini.s]

  Ini::new() / Ini::load(path) / Ini::parse(bytes)    a missing or unreadable file is empty
  ini.save(path) -> bool       plat::write_file, creates missing directories
  ini.to_bytes()               the text save writes
  ini.get(sec, key) -> Option<&str>   (get_bytes for values that are not UTF-8)
  ini.get_int(sec, key, def)   decimal (+/-), 0x hex, true/false/yes/no/on/off; else def
  ini.get_f64(sec, key, def)   '.' decimal point only; else def
  ini.set(sec, key, value) / set_int / set_f64 -> bool   add or replace (false: bad name)
  ini.remove(sec, key) -> bool
  ini.section(sec) -> Vec<(&str, &str)>   the keys of a section and their values, in order
  ini.sections() -> Vec<&str>   the section names in file order (each once; not "")
  ini.items() -> Vec<Item>      headers, keys and malformed lines with their line numbers
                                (files that are checked: a theme names a mistake's line)

Format: one entry per line; sec "" = the keys before the first [section].  Section and
key names compare ASCII case-insensitively; values are stored as written (blanks around
names and values trimmed; no quoting, no inline comments, so values may contain ';' and
'#').  Lines starting with ';' or '#', blank lines and malformed lines (no '=', "[" without
"]", NUL bytes, longer than LINE_MAX) are kept verbatim and written back unchanged, as are
all lines not touched by set (the original spacing survives).  New keys go after the
last key of their section, new sections to the end.  A UTF-8 BOM is skipped.  Files are
read up to FILE_MAX bytes; after LINES_MAX lines the rest is kept as one verbatim block.
Line ends: LF, CRLF (any number of CRs before the LF are dropped) when reading; written as
CRLF on Windows, LF on Linux.  Key names must not contain '=', NUL, CR or LF nor start with
';' '#' '['; section names must not contain ']', NUL, CR or LF; neither may start or end with
a blank (set -> false).  CR / LF inside a value are written as blanks.
```

- **`struct Ini`**
  a settings object (one thread at a time)

- **`enum Item<'a>`**
  a line of the file as Ini::items lists it (line numbers from 1)
  - `Section { line: usize, name: &'a str }` -- a "[name]" header
  - `Key { line: usize, sec: &'a str, key: &'a str, value: &'a str }` -- "key = value" of section sec ("" before the first header)
  - `Bad { line: usize, text: &'a [u8] }` -- neither blank, a comment, a header nor a key (or not UTF-8)

**`impl Ini`**

### `base/settings.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/settings.rs`](../lib/base/settings.rs)

```text
settings -- typed settings: a schema of keys (type, default, limits, label) over a settings
file (Ini) with a format version and migrations

  const DARK: Key<bool> = Key::bool("view.dark", false).label("Dunkles Design");
  const ZOOM: Key<i64> = Key::int("view.zoom", 100, 10, 800).label("Zoom (%)").step(10);
  static SCHEMA: Schema = Schema::new(2, &[DARK.d, ZOOM.d]).sections(&[("view", "Ansicht")])
      .migrate(migrate);
  let mut s = Settings::open("config://settings.ini", &SCHEMA);
  let zoom: i64 = s.get(&ZOOM);   s.set(&ZOOM, 120);   s.save();

Key types: Key<bool> (Key::bool), Key<i64> (Key::int: min..max, step), Key<f64> (Key::num:
min..max, decimals), Key<String> (Key::text: at most max bytes of UTF-8), Key<usize>
(Key::choice: an index into (stored word, label) items; the file keeps the word),
Key<u32> (Key::color: 0xRRGGBB; the file "#RRGGBB").  Builders: label(s), help(s),
hidden() (not on the settings page), restart() (takes effect after a restart: the page
says so), step(n) (int: the number box's step).

  Settings::open(path, &schema)   load, migrate, read (a missing file: the defaults)
  Settings::new(&schema)          only in memory (save does nothing)
  Settings::from_ini(ini, &schema)  in memory, from an Ini (tests)
  s.get(&key) -> T   s.text(&key) -> &str   s.set(&key, v) -> changed   s.reset(&key)
  s.reset_all()   s.is_default(&key)   s.save() -> ok   s.dirty()   s.revision()
  s.ini() / s.ini_mut()   the file for free-form data the schema does not describe (a
                          list of recent files); ini_mut marks the settings dirty
  s.file_version()        the version the file had (0: none or older than versions)
  s.schema(), s.at(i), s.set_at(i, val), s.default_at(i)   by schema index (the page)
  rename(&mut ini, "old.key", "new.key")   for migrations

Names are "section.key" (no '.': the top of the file).  The file keeps only values that
differ from the default (setting the default removes the line), so a new default reaches
users who never changed it; comments, unknown keys and other sections survive (Ini).
The format version is "version=N" at the top: a file of an older version (no line: 0)
runs migrate(from, &mut ini) once before its values are read (rename keys, convert units)
and is saved with the new version by the next save; a missing file needs no migration; a
file of a newer version is read as far as the schema goes and keeps its number.  A value
the schema cannot use (not a number, an unknown choice, a bad colour) reads as the default
and a WARN goes to the log; numbers out of range are clamped, texts cut to their maximum.
Keys that are not in the schema still work through get / set (read from the file each
time) but are not on the page.
```

```rust
/// Desc::flags: not on the settings page
KF_HIDDEN: u32 = 1
/// Desc::flags: takes effect after a restart (the page says so)
KF_RESTART: u32 = 2
```

### `base/rng.rs`

```text
rng -- deterministic pseudo-random numbers for simulations, tests and games (NOT for keys:
those come from plat::fill_random)

  SplitMix64::new(seed)      next_u64; derives seeds (Vigna's splitmix64)
  Pcg32::new(seed, stream)   PCG-XSH-RR 64/32 (O'Neill), the reference pcg32_srandom_r: the

  chance(num, den) / chance_ppm(ppm) / fill(bytes) / shuffle(slice) / advance(delta)
```

### `base/metrics.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/metrics.rs`](../lib/base/metrics.rs)

```text
metrics -- measurements of running systems without keeping single values: counters, gauges,
log-linear histograms and a sliding window of them (simulators, servers, benchmarks)

  Counter        inc / add / get (saturating u64)
  Gauge          set / add / get / max (i64; max is the highest value seen)
  Hist           log-linear buckets: values below 2^b exactly, above in 2^b linear steps
                 per power of two (b = 5: at most 1/32 = 3.1 % bucket width, the midpoint
                 is off by half of that); record / record_n / count / sum / min / max /
                 mean / quantile(per_mille) / p50 / p95 / p99 / merge / clear / buckets
  Window         n slots of `span` time units each (Window::new(300, 1_000_000_000): five
                 minutes in 1 s slots of nanoseconds); record(t, v) / quantile(t, pm) /
                 p50 / p95 / p99 / count / sum / mean / min / max over the slots still in
                 the window at t / per_slot(t, pm) for charts / hist(t)
                 hist_between(from, to): the slots that start in [from, to) as one
                 histogram (a time series: one point per interval, quantiles of any span);
                 bytes(): the heap memory it holds -- its slots come with the first value,
                 so a window that never got one costs nothing (a simulator keeps one per
                 device and copies them often)

Quantiles use the nearest rank (rank = ceil(pm * n / 1000)) and give the midpoint of that
rank's bucket, clamped to the smallest and largest value seen (the first and the last rank
are those values), so a run of equal values reports that value exactly.  A window slot keeps a sparse histogram (bucket, count) and its
own count, sum, min and max; nothing stores the values themselves.  All integer arithmetic:
the same values give the same results on every target.
```

### `base/cmdtree.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/cmdtree.rs`](../lib/base/cmdtree.rs)

```text
cmdtree -- command trees for IOS-like command lines: unique prefix abbreviations ("sh ip int
br"), "?" help with descriptions, Tab completion, modes with prompts, the "no" form, typed
parameters and the position of an error for the IOS-like messages ("% Invalid input detected at
'^' marker.", "% Incomplete command.", "% Ambiguous command:")

  Tree::new()                          an empty tree of commands of type C (an app's enum)
  mode(prompt, title, parent, no_help) a mode: its prompt after the host name ("(config)#"),
                                       the title of its "?" list, the mode its commands fall
                                       back to, the help of its "no" (None: no "no")
  add(mode, path, help, cmd, flags)    a command path; shared prefixes merge, the last word
                                       gets the help text, `cmd` makes the path complete
  also(mode, path, target)             the words after `target` may follow `path` too
                                       (options in any order)
  parse(mode, line, &dyn Names)        -> Result<Parsed<C>, Error>
  help(mode, line, &dyn Names)         -> Help: the answer to "?" typed after `line`
  complete(mode, line, &dyn Names)     -> Completion (Tab)
  Error::render / Help::render         the text an IOS-like console shows
  find_mode(prompt)                    a mode by its prompt (modes that parts of an app add
                                       need no fixed number)

Paths are words separated by spaces.  A keyword stands for itself ("shutdown"; "access=mode"
stores it under the key "mode").  A parameter is TYPE or TYPE=key (a later value of a key
hides an earlier one, so "mode access=mode" reads as "access"):

  <lo-hi>      a decimal number in the range          Val::Num
  A.B.C.D      an IPv4 address                         Val::Ipv4
  MASK         a contiguous dotted netmask              Val::Mask (its length)
  A.B.C.D/nn   an address with a prefix length          Val::Prefix
  X:X:X:X::X   an IPv6 address (every RFC 4291 form)    Val::Ipv6
  X:X:X:X::X/<0-128>   an IPv6 address with a prefix length   Val::Prefix6
  H.H.H        a MAC address (H.H.H or with colons)     Val::Mac
  WORD         one word                                 Val::Word
  LINE         the rest of the line, spaces included    Val::Line
  NAME, NAME1 .. NAME9   one of the caller's names (lists 0 .. 9, interfaces): a type and a
               number ("gi0/0/0", "Gi 0/0/0", "lo0"), the type abbreviated like a keyword,
               also as two words                       Val::Name (the full name)

Matching is IOS-like: keywords ignore case and may be shortened to any prefix that no other
word of that place shares; a word that is a whole keyword wins; numbers, addresses and names
must be valid; WORD and LINE take what no keyword takes.  The error position is the first
character no candidate accepts (the "^" marker).  "no" is a keyword of every mode that has
it; it leads to the commands added with F_NO, and a no-form may end early where add_no says.
Help lists keywords and parameters in ASCII order (parameters and capitalised interface
types first) with "<cr>" when the command may end there.
```

- **`type NodeId = u32`**
  the index of a node of a tree

- **`type ModeId = u16`**
  the index of a mode

```rust
/// a command may be negated ("no shutdown"); set on its first word
F_NO: u8 = 1
/// not listed by help and completion (aliases, commands of the configuration file only)
F_HIDDEN: u8 = 2
```

  a typed parameter
  - `Num(i64, i64)`
  - `Ipv4`
  - `Mask`
  - `Prefix`
  - `Mac`
  - `Word`
  - `Line`
  - `Name(u8)`
  - `Ipv6`
  - `Prefix6`

**`impl Param`**

- **`fn label(&self) -> String`**
  what help shows for it ("&lt;1-4094>", "A.B.C.D", "WORD")

- **`enum Val`**
  a value of a parsed command
  - `Key(String)` -- a keyword, written out in full
  - `Num(i64)`
  - `Ipv4([u8; 4])`
  - `Mask(u8)`
  - `Prefix([u8; 4], u8)`
  - `Mac([u8; 6])`

- **`trait Names`**

  - `fn type_help(&self, _list: u8, ty: &str) -> String`

    configuration); the caller decides whether it tries there

- **`struct Parsed<C>`**
  a parsed command line
  - `cmd: C`
  - `no: bool` -- the line started with "no"

**`impl<C> Parsed<C>`**

  - `Invalid(usize)` -- no command goes on at this byte of the line (the "^" marker)

  - `List { title: Option<String>, items: Vec<(String, String)>, cr: bool }` -- what may follow: (label, description) in display order; `cr` when the command may end

  - `Words(Vec<String>)` -- the keywords a partly typed word may become
  - `Unrecognized` -- nothing starts like the partly typed word

- **`struct Completion`**

  - `choices: Vec<String>` -- what the last word may become

- **`struct Tree<C>`**

**`impl<C: Copy> Tree<C>`**

### `base/hashring.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/hashring.rs`](../lib/base/hashring.rs)

```text
hashring -- consistent hashing: a ring of tokens with virtual nodes per member; a key belongs
to the member of the first token at or after its hash (going round at the end), and its
preference list is the next n distinct members from there (sharded stores, load balancers
with sticky keys).  Adding or removing a member moves only the keys of its own tokens.

  hash64(bytes) -> u64                    FNV-1a (64 bit) with a final mix; the same on every
                                          target
  Ring::new() / add(member, key, vnodes) / remove(&member) / members() / tokens()
  owner(h) -> Option<&M>                  the member of the first token at or after h
  preference(h, n) -> Vec<M>              the first n distinct members from h on
  preference_by(h, n, ok)                 the same, skipping members ok() refuses
  shares() -> Vec<(M, u32)>               each member's part of the ring in parts per million

The tokens of a member come from its key and the vnode number ("10.0.4.11#3"), so every
device that knows the members builds the same ring.
```

- **`fn hash64(b: &[u8]) -> u64`**
  FNV-1a over the bytes, then the finaliser of SplitMix64 (spreads close keys over the ring)

- **`struct Ring<M: Ord + Clone>`**
  a ring of tokens; M names a member (an address, a backend)

**`impl<M: Ord + Clone> Ring<M>`**

- **`fn new() -> Ring<M>`**
- **`fn add(&mut self, m: M, key: &str, vnodes: u32)`**
  adds a member with `vnodes` tokens made from `key` (a member that is there already gets
  its tokens again)
- **`fn remove(&mut self, m: &M) -> bool`**
  removes a member and its tokens
- **`fn members(&self) -> &[M]`**
  the members, sorted
- **`fn tokens(&self) -> &[(u64, M)]`**
  the tokens with their members, sorted by token
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn owner(&self, h: u64) -> Option<&M>`**
  the member a hash belongs to
- **`fn preference(&self, h: u64, n: usize) -> Vec<M>`**
  the first `n` distinct members from h on, in ring order
- **`fn preference_by(&self, h: u64, n: usize, ok: impl Fn(&M) -> bool) -> Vec<M>`**
  the first `n` distinct members from h on that `ok` accepts
- **`fn shares(&self) -> Vec<(M, u32)>`**
  the part of the hash space each member owns, in parts per million (sorted by member)

### `base/lru.rs`

Source: [`lib/base/lru.rs`](../lib/base/lru.rs)

```text
lru -- a map that forgets the least recently used entries: a limit on the number of entries
and one on their weight (bytes), ordered maps only (deterministic, no hashing); caches of
simulators and servers

  Lru::new(max_len, max_weight)          0: no limit
  get(k) (counts as a use) / peek(k) / contains(k) / get_mut(k)
  insert(k, v, weight) -> evicted        the entries that had to go, oldest first (the new
                                         one itself when it alone is too heavy)
  remove(k) / pop_lru() / clear() / len() / weight() / keys() (oldest first)

Every use moves an entry to the young end; eviction takes from the old end until both
limits hold.  Costs are O(log n) per call.
```

- **`struct Lru<K: Ord + Clone, V>`**
  a least-recently-used map
  - `max_len: usize` -- entries at most (0: no limit)
  - `max_weight: u64` -- summed weight at most (0: no limit)

**`impl<K: Ord + Clone, V> Lru<K, V>`**

- **`fn new(max_len: usize, max_weight: u64) -> Lru<K, V>`**
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn weight(&self) -> u64`**
  the summed weight of the entries
- **`fn contains(&self, k: &K) -> bool`**
- **`fn peek(&self, k: &K) -> Option<&V>`**
  an entry without counting it as a use
- **`fn get(&mut self, k: &K) -> Option<&V>`**
  an entry; it becomes the most recently used
- **`fn get_mut(&mut self, k: &K) -> Option<&mut V>`**
  an entry to change in place; it becomes the most recently used
- **`fn insert(&mut self, k: K, v: V, weight: u64) -> Vec<(K, V)>`**
  stores an entry (replacing one with the same key) as the most recently used; the
  entries that had to go for the limits, oldest first
- **`fn remove(&mut self, k: &K) -> Option<V>`**
- **`fn pop_lru(&mut self) -> Option<(K, V)>`**
  takes the least recently used entry
- **`fn clear(&mut self)`**
- **`fn keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &K>`**
  the keys, least recently used first
- **`fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&K, &V)>`**
  the entries in key order (no use counted)

## datetime

*timestamps, civil dates, RFC 3339, IANA time zones with DST, cron schedules* -- crate root [`lib/datetime/lib.rs`](../lib/datetime/lib.rs)

```text
datetime -- calendar time: timestamps, civil dates, RFC 3339, time zones, cron schedules

  Timestamp { secs, nanos }          seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC
  Civil { year .. second, nanos }    a calendar date and wall time (no zone)
  days_from_civil / civil_from_days / days_in_month / is_leap / weekday (0 = Monday)
  rfc3339(ts) / rfc3339_offset(ts, offset) / parse_rfc3339(s)
  format_date_time(ts, &zone, en) / format_date / format_time / format_duration(secs, en)
  tz::Zone                           IANA zones with their current DST rule (zones.rs from
                                     tools/gen_tz.py), Windows zone keys, POSIX TZ strings;
                                     offset_at / to_local / from_local (Single, Ambiguous,
                                     Gap)
  cron::Cron                         5-field cron expressions: next_after in a zone (a time
                                     in a DST gap runs right after the gap, a repeated time
                                     runs once), next_n, describe (de / en)

No clock here: plat::unix_time_ns gives "now"; datetime only computes.
```

### `datetime` crate root

- **`struct Timestamp`**
  a point in time: seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and nanoseconds
  - `secs: i64`
  - `nanos: u32`

**`impl Timestamp`**

### `datetime/cron.rs`

Source: [`lib/datetime/cron.rs`](../lib/datetime/cron.rs)

```text
cron -- 5-field cron schedules evaluated in a time zone

  Cron::parse("30 2 * * 1-5")   minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week; fields: *, n,
                                a-b, a-b/n, */n, lists a,b; month names jan..dec, weekday
                                names sun..sat (0 and 7 = Sunday); @hourly @daily @midnight
                                @weekly @monthly @yearly @annually.  Day of month and day of
                                week restricted both: either matches (Vixie cron).
  cron.next_after(ts, &zone)    the first run after ts: a wall time in a DST gap runs at the
                                jump (right after the gap), a repeated wall time runs once
                                (its first occurrence); None when nothing matches within
                                5 years
  cron.next_n(ts, &zone, n)     the next n runs
  cron.describe(en)             "Täglich um 02:00", "Werktags um 02:00", "Alle 15 Minuten" …
  Schedule helpers: daily(h, m), weekly(mask, h, m), monthly(day, h, m), hourly(m) build
  the expressions of the usual choices (mask bit 0 = Monday)
```

### `datetime/tz.rs`

Source: [`lib/datetime/tz.rs`](../lib/datetime/tz.rs)

```text
tz -- time zones from POSIX TZ rules ("CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3")

  Zone::utc() / Zone::by_name("Europe/Berlin") / Zone::from_windows("W. Europe Standard Time")
  Zone::from_posix(name, rule) / Zone::fixed(name, offset_secs)
  Zone::names() -> every IANA name of the table (sorted)
  zone.offset_at(secs) -> UTC offset (seconds east), zone.abbrev_at(secs), zone.is_dst(secs)
  zone.to_local(ts) -> Civil;  zone.from_local(&civil) -> LocalResult:
       Single(ts) | Ambiguous(first, second) (the repeated hour) | Gap { after } (the skipped
       hour: `after` is the instant the clocks jumped, the first valid time after the gap)

A rule describes the zone from its last change on (the TZif footer of tools/gen_tz.py), so
times before that change use today's rule.
```

- **`enum LocalResult`**

  - `Gap { after: Timestamp }` -- the wall time does not exist (the clocks jumped forward): the jump's instant
