## script

*the JFNetworker scripting language (.jfs): lexer, parser, editor diagnostics, compiler, a VM with fuel and a garbage collector, the standard library (str, list, map, bytes, math, json), float arithmetic and math in software* -- crate root [`lib/script/lib.rs`](../lib/script/lib.rs)

```text
script -- the JFNetworker scripting language (.jfs): lexer, parser, syntax tree, editor
diagnostics, compiler, VM with fuel and a garbage collector

  parse(name, src) -> Result<ast::Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>   the syntax tree, or the syntax
                               errors (the parser goes on at the next statement after an
                               error and reports the first error of each line)
  parse_partial(name, src)     the tree of what parsed plus the errors (editor features)
  check(src)                   syntax errors plus name resolution against GLOBALS: unknown
                               names (warnings), duplicate declarations, break / continue
                               outside a loop, return outside a function (errors);
                               check_with(src, globals) with other predeclared names
  resolve(&program, globals)   the resolution part alone (for the compiler)
  tokens(src)                  (byte start, length, TokKind) of every token, covering every
                               byte, for syntax highlighting; never fails
  outline(src)                 the top-level fns and lets with their lines
  compile(src) -> Result<Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>   bytecode (code.rs, compile.rs), or the
                               errors of parse() and check() (warnings do not stop it);
                               compile_named(name, src) names the file; compile_with(name,
                               src, globals) for a host with other names (the standalone
                               runner apps/jfs): unknown names are errors there
  Vm::new(&program, limits)    a VM (vm.rs): run(host, fuel) -> Done | Yielded | Error,
                               call(name, args), call_value, global / set_global, pin,
                               output; Value (16 bytes, heap.rs), Host and Cx for native
                               functions; num: float arithmetic in software
  library()                    the standard library every host gets (stdlib.rs: str, list,
                               map, bytes, math, json, int / float.parse; math.rs: exp, log,
                               pow, sin, cos .. in software), found by name before the host

The language: small, dynamically typed, JS/Lua-like.  Values: nil, bool, int (i64), float
(f64), str (immutable UTF-8), bytes, list, map (insertion ordered; keys str, int, bool),
fn (closures).  Statements: let x = e, fn name(a, b) { }, if c { } else if c { } else { },
while c { }, for x in list { }, for k, v in map { }, for i in 0..n { }, break, continue,
return [e], try { } catch e { }, throw e, assignments = += -= *= /= %= to names, fields
(m.k) and indexes (a[i]), expression statements.  Expressions: literals (1_000, 0xFF,
0b101, 1.5e3, "text" with \n \t \r \0 \" \\ \$ \u{..} and ${expr}, true, false, nil),
[a, b], {k: v, "s": v, 1: v, [e]: v}, fn(a) { }, calls, .field, [index], methods
s.split(","), unary - !, binary operators from loose to tight: ?? || && (== !=)
(< <= > >=) (+ -) (* / %).  Comments // and /* */.  A line break ends a statement once
its expression is complete (parse.rs has the details); a string stays on one line.
Positions: lines and columns from 1, columns count characters, end_col is exclusive.
The messages are German.  The scope rules are in ast.rs.
```

### `script` crate root

- **`struct Diagnostic`**
  a message for the editor: position (1-based; columns count characters, end_col is
  exclusive and on the same line), error or warning, German text
  - `line: u32`
  - `col: u32`
  - `end_col: u32`
  - `error: bool`
  - `msg: String`

```rust
/// the names a script may use without declaring them: the host API of the simulator and the
/// standard library (check warns about other unknown names)
GLOBALS: &[&str] = &[ "print", "log", "len", "str", "int", "float", "type", ...
```

- **`fn library() -> Vec<&'static str>`**
  the functions and constants of the standard library ("str.split", "math.pi", "bytes"),
  for completion in an editor; methods are listed under their type (s.split(",") is
  str.split(s, ","))

- **`fn parse(name: &str, src: &str) -> Result<ast::Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>`**
  the syntax tree of a script, or its syntax errors; name: a file name for later messages

- **`fn parse_partial(name: &str, src: &str) -> (ast::Program, Vec<Diagnostic>)`**
  the tree of everything that parsed and the syntax errors (empty when parse() succeeds)

- **`fn check(src: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic>`**
  syntax errors and the findings of resolve() with GLOBALS, sorted by position

- **`fn check_with(src: &str, globals: &[&str]) -> Vec<Diagnostic>`**
  check() with other predeclared names

- **`fn tokens(src: &str) -> Vec<(u32, u32, TokKind)>`**
  (byte start, length, kind) of every token in source order, covering every byte; the
  `${` and `}` of interpolations are TokKind::Interp, the text around them Str

- **`fn outline(src: &str) -> Vec<(String, u32)>`**
  the top-level declarations with their lines: "fn key(id)", "let hits" (also while the
  script has syntax errors)

- **`fn compile(src: &str) -> Result<Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>`**
  compile a script for the VM; the errors of parse() and check() (not the warnings) when it
  has some

- **`fn compile_named(name: &str, src: &str) -> Result<Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>`**
  compile() with a file name (Program::name)

- **`fn compile_with(name: &str, src: &str, globals: &[&str]) -> Result<Program, Vec<Diagnostic>>`**
  compile_named() for a host with names of its own instead of GLOBALS: `globals` are the
  names it answers (Host::call, set_global; "log", "timer", "config"), the built-ins and the
  standard library are known without them.  Unlike compile(), a name that is neither
  declared nor known is an error ("Unbekannter Name prnt – meinst du print?"), so a typing
  error stops the script before it runs; the other warnings still do not

### `script/ast.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/ast.rs`](../lib/script/ast.rs)

```text
ast -- the syntax tree of a .jfs script (parse() builds it, the compiler reads it)

  Program { name, body }   the top-level statements
  Stmt { span, kind }      StmtKind: Let, Fn, If, While, For, Break, Continue, Return, Try,
                           Throw, Expr, Assign, Block
  Expr { span, kind }      ExprKind: literals, Interp, List, Map, Fn, Var, Unary, Binary,
                           Call, Method, Field, Index
  Span                     bytes start..end plus line and column of the start (1-based,
                           columns count characters); a name's span.start is unique per
                           source, a key for side tables of later passes
  x.sexpr()                the tree as S-expressions: (+ 1 (* 2 3)), (call f a), (. m k) ..

Scopes (check::resolve and the compiler follow the same rules):
  * top-level let and fn are the script's globals: visible in every function wherever they
    are declared (functions run later, as callbacks); top-level code itself reads a let
    only after it ran (check warns otherwise)
  * a block { } is a scope: its fn declarations are visible in the whole block (local
    functions may call each other), a let from the next statement on; a second let of a
    name in one block is an error, an inner block may shadow it
  * parameters form a scope around the function body; the for variables and the catch
    variable a scope around their block
  * fn declarations and fn literals are closures: they capture the locals they use
  * && || ?? evaluate their right side only when needed; a..b exists only in for and
    counts a, a + 1 .. b - 1
```

- **`struct Span`**
  a source range: bytes start..end, line and column of start (1-based; columns count characters)
  - `start: u32`
  - `end: u32`
  - `line: u32`
  - `col: u32`

**`impl Span`**

- **`fn to(self, other: Span) -> Span`**
  from the start of self to the end of other

- **`struct Name`**
  a name where it is written: declarations, parameters, field and method names
  - `text: String`
  - `span: Span`

- **`struct Program`**
  - `name: String` -- the name given to parse() (a file name for messages)
  - `body: Vec<Stmt>`

- **`struct Block`**
  { statements }
  - `span: Span`
  - `stmts: Vec<Stmt>`

- **`struct FnDef`**
  a function: fn name(params) { body }, or the literal fn(params) { body } without a name
  - `span: Span`
  - `name: Option<Name>`
  - `params: Vec<Name>`
  - `body: Block`

- **`struct Stmt`**
  - `span: Span`
  - `kind: StmtKind`

- **`enum StmtKind`**
  - `Let { name: Name, init: Option<Expr> }` -- let name = init (no init: nil)
  - `Fn(FnDef)` -- fn name(params) { } (the FnDef has a name)
  - `If { arms: Vec<(Expr, Block)>, els: Option<Block> }` -- if c { } else if c { } else { }: the (condition, block) arms in order
  - `While { cond: Expr, body: Block }`
  - `For { a: Name, b: Option<Name>, src: ForSrc, body: Block }` -- for a in src / for a, b in src (key and value of a map, index and item of a list)
  - `Break`
  - `Continue`
  - `Return(Option<Expr>)`
  - `Try { body: Block, var: Option<Name>, catch: Block }` -- try { body } catch var { catch }
  - `Throw(Expr)`
  - `Expr(Expr)`
  - `Assign { op: Option<BinOp>, target: Expr, value: Expr }` -- target = value, or target op= value (op Some(Add) for +=); target is Var, Field or Index
  - `Block(Block)` -- a bare { } block

- **`enum ForSrc`**
  what a for loop runs over
  - `Each(Expr)` -- a list, map, str or bytes value
  - `Range(Expr, Expr)` -- lo..hi

- **`struct Expr`**
  - `span: Span`
  - `kind: ExprKind`

- **`enum ExprKind`**
  - `Nil`
  - `Bool(bool)`
  - `Int(i64)`
  - `Float(f64)`
  - `Str(String)`
  - `Interp(Vec<Expr>)` -- "a${x}b": the pieces in order, Str for the text (empty pieces left out)
  - `List(Vec<Expr>)`
  - `Map(Vec<(Expr, Expr)>)` -- {k: v, "s": v, 1: v, [e]: v}: (key, value) in order; a bare name key is a Str
  - `Fn(Box<FnDef>)`
  - `Var(String)`
  - `Unary(UnOp, Box<Expr>)`
  - `Binary(BinOp, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>)`
  - `Call(Box<Expr>, Vec<Expr>)` -- f(args)
  - `Method(Box<Expr>, Name, Vec<Expr>)` -- obj.name(args)
  - `Field(Box<Expr>, Name)` -- obj.name
  - `Index(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>)` -- obj[index]

- **`enum UnOp`**
  the unary operators: minus and not (!)
  - `Neg`
  - `Not`

- **`enum BinOp`**
  binary operators; And, Or and Coalesce (??) short-circuit
  - `Mul`
  - `Div`
  - `Rem`
  - `Add`
  - `Sub`
  - `Lt`
  - `Le`
  - `Gt`
  - `Ge`
  - `Eq`
  - `Ne`
  - `And`
  - `Or`
  - `Coalesce`

**`impl BinOp`**

- **`fn text(self) -> &'static str`**
  the operator as written: "\*", "&&", "??" ..

**`impl Program`**

- **`fn sexpr(&self) -> String`**
  one S-expression per top-level statement, one per line

**`impl Stmt`**

- **`fn sexpr(&self) -> String`**
  (let x 1), (fn f (a) (block ..)), (if c (block ..) else (block ..)), (= x 1) ..

**`impl Expr`**

- **`fn sexpr(&self) -> String`**
  (+ 1 (\* 2 3)), (call f a), (method s split ","), (. m k), (index a 0), (interp "a" x) ..

### `script/check.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/check.rs`](../lib/script/check.rs)

```text
check -- name resolution over the syntax tree, with the scope rules of ast.rs

  resolve(&program, globals) -> Vec<Diagnostic>
    errors:   a name declared twice in one block (also parameters, the two for
              variables, top-level declarations), break / continue outside a loop (a
              function body starts outside of any loop), return outside a function, two
              variables over a range a..b
    warnings: a name that is neither declared nor in globals (with a suggestion for a
              typing error), a top-level let read by top-level code before it ran
  globals: the predeclared names (crate::GLOBALS for check())
  resolve_strict(&program, globals)   the same with unknown names as errors
              (crate::compile_with: the host says which names it has)
```

- **`fn resolve(prog: &Program, globals: &[&str]) -> Vec<Diagnostic>`**
  see the module comment

### `script/lex.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/lex.rs`](../lib/script/lex.rs)

```text
lex -- the tokens of .jfs scripts

  lex(src) -> (Vec<Tok>, Vec<Diagnostic>)   every byte in exactly one token (Space, Newline
                                            and Comment included), then Eof; never fails: an
                                            unknown character or a bad number becomes an
                                            Error token plus a diagnostic
  significant(&toks, src)                   the tokens the parser reads: no Space, Newline,
                                            Comment; Tok::nl marks a line break before one
  Strings stay on one line.  "a${x}b" is StrHead `"a${`, the tokens of x, StrTail `}b"`;
  between two interpolations StrMid `}..${`.  Braces inside ${..} nest, so do strings.
  int_value / float_value / str_value decode literal tokens; TokKind::class() groups the
  kinds for syntax highlighting.
```

- **`enum TokKind`**
  the kind of a token; the keywords are Let .. Nil, the other names are the punctuation
  and operator characters
  - `Space` -- spaces, tabs and other white space
  - `Newline` -- \\n or \\r\\n
  - `Comment` -- // to the line end, /\* .. \*/
  - `Error` -- a character or number that is no token (lex() reported it)
  - `Eof` -- the end of the source (lex() only, never in tokens())
  - `Ident`
  - `Int`
  - `Float`
  - `Str` -- a whole string; in tokens() also the text pieces of an interpolated one
  - `StrHead` -- "..${ (lex() only: tokens() splits it into Str and Interp)
  - `StrMid` -- }..${ (lex() only)
  - `StrTail` -- }.." (lex() only)
  - `Interp` -- the ${ or } of an interpolation (tokens() only)
  - `Let`
  - `Fn`
  - `If`
  - `Else`
  - `While`
  - `For`
  - `In`
  - `Break`
  - `Continue`
  - `Return`
  - `Try`
  - `Catch`
  - `Throw`
  - `True`
  - `False`
  - `Nil`
  - `LParen`
  - `RParen`
  - `LBracket`
  - `RBracket`
  - `LBrace`
  - `RBrace`
  - `Comma`
  - `Dot`
  - `Colon`
  - `Semi`
  - `DotDot` -- ..
  - `Plus`
  - `Minus`
  - `Star`
  - `Slash`
  - `Percent`
  - `PlusEq`
  - `MinusEq`
  - `StarEq`
  - `SlashEq`
  - `PercentEq`
  - `Assign` -- =
  - `EqEq` -- ==
  - `NotEq` -- !=
  - `Not` -- !
  - `Lt`
  - `Le`
  - `Gt`
  - `Ge`
  - `AndAnd` -- &&
  - `OrOr` -- ||
  - `Coalesce` -- ??

- **`enum TokClass`**
  what a token is for syntax highlighting
  - `Space`
  - `Comment`
  - `Keyword`
  - `Constant` -- true, false, nil
  - `Number`
  - `Str`
  - `Ident`
  - `Op`
  - `Punct`
  - `Error`

**`impl TokKind`**

- **`fn class(self) -> TokClass`**
  the highlighting class
- **`fn is_keyword(self) -> bool`**
  let, fn, .. nil
- **`fn keyword(word: &str) -> Option<TokKind>`**
  the keyword for a word

- **`struct Tok`**
  one token: kind, byte range, 1-based line and column (columns count characters) of its
  start; nl: a line break stands between it and the previous significant token
  - `kind: TokKind`
  - `start: u32`
  - `end: u32`
  - `line: u32`
  - `col: u32`
  - `nl: bool`

- **`fn lex(src: &str) -> (Vec<Tok>, Vec<Diagnostic>)`**
  tokenize a whole source (see the module comment)

- **`fn significant(toks: &[Tok], src: &str) -> Vec<Tok>`**
  the tokens the parser reads (see the module comment); a /\* \*/ comment with a line break
  counts as a line break

- **`fn int_value(text: &str) -> Option<i64>`**
  the value of an Int token: decimal up to i64::MAX, 0x / 0b with up to 64 bits (two's
  complement), `_` between digits

- **`fn float_value(text: &str) -> Option<f64>`**
  the value of a Float token (`_` between digits)

- **`fn str_inner(kind: TokKind, text: &str) -> &str`**
  the text between the delimiters of a Str / StrHead / StrMid / StrTail token

- **`fn str_value(kind: TokKind, text: &str) -> String`**
  the value of a string token: its inner text with the escapes decoded (bad escapes, which
  lex() reported, are dropped)

### `script/parse.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/parse.rs`](../lib/script/parse.rs)

```text
parse -- the parser of .jfs scripts: statements by recursive descent, expressions by
precedence climbing (Pratt), with error recovery

  parse_program(name, src) -> (Program, Vec<Diagnostic>)   the tree of everything that parsed
                              and the errors of lexer and parser (the first of each line)
  Line breaks: a statement ends at a line break once its expression is complete; `;` is
  optional.  Inside ( ) [ ] map { } and ${ } line breaks are ignored; after an operator,
  `=` or `,` the expression goes on.  A line that starts with `.` or a binary operator other
  than `-` continues the line above; `-x`, `(..)` and `[..]` at the start of a line begin a
  new statement (inside brackets they continue).  `else` and `catch` may start a line.
  Recovery: an error ends the statement; the parser skips to the next line break outside
  the statement's brackets (or to the `}` of its block) and goes on there.  A closing
  bracket missing at a line end is reported and taken as given when the next line starts
  at or left of the statement's column, or when the token closes an outer bracket.
  Stack: nesting deeper than MAX_DEPTH (blocks, brackets, operands; the links of an operator
  or call chain count too, since every pass over the tree recurses) is an error.  The
  parser needs up to about 2 KB of stack per level in development builds, so the deepest
  script fits in a 256 KB thread (coretest checks that on Linux).
```

```rust
/// nesting limit of blocks and expressions (the links of operator and call chains count)
MAX_DEPTH: u32 = 100
```

### `script/code.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/code.rs`](../lib/script/code.rs)

```text
code -- the bytecode of compiled scripts: instructions, functions, the compiled Program

  Op        one instruction of the stack machine (12 bytes); the comments give the stack
            effect.  Slots count from the frame base: the parameters, then the locals of
            the blocks, then the temporaries.  A local that a closure captures holds a
            cell; closures keep the cells (Up::Local from the enclosing frame, Up::Up from
            the enclosing closure).
  Proto     a function: code, the line and column of every instruction, the exception
            table (try ranges with their handler and stack height), the upvalue sources,
            the most stack it needs
  Program   what compile() returns: functions (0 is the top-level code), constants, the
            names of the globals and of the host names the script uses; cheap to clone
            (shared), Send + Sync
  disasm()  the code as text, for tests and debugging
```

- **`struct Program`**
  a compiled script (see compile()); clones share the code

**`impl Program`**

- **`fn name(&self) -> &str`**
  the name given to compile_named()
- **`fn globals(&self) -> Vec<&str>`**
  the script's globals (top-level let and fn) in the order of the source
- **`fn host_names(&self) -> Vec<&str>`**
  the names the script takes from the host (print, http.serve, config ..)
- **`fn instructions(&self) -> usize`**
  the number of instructions of all functions
- **`fn disasm(&self) -> String`**
  the code as text: per function a header, then "pc line:col instruction"

### `script/heap.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/heap.rs`](../lib/script/heap.rs)

```text
heap -- the values of the script VM and the arena they live in

  Value       16 bytes: nil, bool, int, float, or a typed reference into the heap (str,
              bytes, list, map, fn) or to a native function by name
  Heap        a Vec of objects addressed by index; free slots form a list; mark bits and the
              sweep for the VM's mark-and-sweep collector (the VM marks from its roots)
  Map         insertion ordered hash map (keys str, int, bool): entries in order plus an
              open-addressing index once it has more than 8 entries; removing leaves a hole
              that the next compaction closes
  sizes       every object has an accounted size computed from its contents (lengths, never
              capacities), so the heap limit and the collector's timing are the same on
              every target

Hashes are fixed functions (FNV-1a for text): iteration order is insertion order anyway.
```

- **`struct Ref(pub(crate) u32)`**
  a reference to an object of the VM's heap (only meaningful for the VM that made it)

- **`enum Value`**
  a value of a script; strings, bytes, lists, maps and functions live on the VM's heap.  A
  value that refers to the heap stays valid while the script can still reach it (or it is
  pinned): keep values the host holds across runs with Vm::pin.
  - `Nil`
  - `Bool(bool)`
  - `Int(i64)`
  - `Float(f64)`
  - `Str(Ref)`
  - `Bytes(Ref)`
  - `List(Ref)`
  - `Map(Ref)`
  - `Func(Ref)` -- a function of the script (a closure)
  - `Native(u32)` -- a function of the host, by the index of its name in the VM's name table
  - `Cell(Ref)` -- a captured variable (inside the VM only; scripts and hosts never see one)

**`impl Value`**

- **`fn type_name(self) -> &'static str`**
  the type name scripts see: nil bool int float str bytes list map fn
- **`fn truthy(self) -> bool`**
  false for nil and false, true for everything else (also 0, "" and [])

### `script/num.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/num.rs`](../lib/script/num.rs)

```text
num -- IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic in software, so float results of scripts are
bit-identical on every target

  add sub mul div sqrt     correctly rounded (to nearest, ties to even)
  rem                      fmod: exact, with the sign of the dividend
  from_i64(i)              correctly rounded; to_i64(x) truncates (None for NaN, infinity and
                           values outside i64)
  cmp / eq / lt / le       comparisons: NaN is unordered, -0 == +0
  cmp_int(i, x)            an i64 against a float, exactly (i is not rounded first)
  neg abs trunc floor ceil
  NAN                      the one NaN every operation returns (0x7FF8_0000_0000_0000)
  fmt(x, out)              shortest text that reads back as the same bits: 1.0, 0.1, 1e21,
                           -0.0, inf, -inf, nan

Only integer arithmetic: the floating-point unit is never used, so modes such as flush to
zero and the NaN bits of different processors cannot change a result.  (For finite values
x86-64, ARM64 and wasm hardware would agree with these functions; the NaN bits do not.)
```

```rust
/// the NaN every operation of this module returns
NAN: f64 = f64::from_bits(0x7FF8_0000_0000_0000)
```

- **`fn is_nan(x: f64) -> bool`**
  whether x is a NaN

- **`fn add(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  a + b

- **`fn sub(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  a - b

- **`fn mul(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  a \* b

- **`fn div(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  a / b

- **`fn rem(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  the remainder of a / b truncated (C's fmod): exact, with the sign of a

- **`fn sqrt(a: f64) -> f64`**
  the square root (NaN for negative numbers, sqrt(-0) = -0)

- **`fn from_i64(i: i64) -> f64`**
  i as a float, correctly rounded

- **`fn to_i64(x: f64) -> Option<i64>`**
  x truncated towards zero; None for NaN, infinity and values outside i64

- **`fn neg(x: f64) -> f64`**
  -x (NaN stays the one NaN)

- **`fn abs(x: f64) -> f64`**
  |x|

- **`fn trunc(x: f64) -> f64`**
  x without its fraction (towards zero)

- **`fn floor(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the largest integer &lt;= x

- **`fn ceil(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the smallest integer >= x

- **`fn cmp(a: f64, b: f64) -> Option<Ordering>`**
  the order of a and b; None when one of them is NaN

- **`fn eq(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool`**
  a == b (false for NaN, true for -0 == +0)

- **`fn lt(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool`**
  a &lt; b

- **`fn le(a: f64, b: f64) -> bool`**
  a &lt;= b

- **`fn cmp_int(i: i64, x: f64) -> Option<Ordering>`**
  the order of the integer i and the float x, exactly; None when x is NaN

- **`fn fmt(x: f64, out: &mut String)`**
  the shortest text that reads back as the same bits: 1.0, 0.1, 0.30000000000000004, 1e21,
  1.5e-7, -0.0, inf, -inf, nan

### `script/math.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/math.rs`](../lib/script/math.rs)

```text
math -- the transcendental functions of the script library in software: exp, log, log2,
log10, pow, sin, cos and round, bit-identical on every target

  exp(x) log(x) log2(x) log10(x)   ports of fdlibm (as in FreeBSD and musl), error below
  pow(x, y) sin(x) cos(x)          1 ulp; exact where the result is exact: log2(8) = 3,
                                   pow(2, 10) = 1024, pow(x, 0.5) = sqrt(x), exp(0) = 1
  round(x)                         to the nearest integer, halves away from zero
  scalbn(x, n)                     x * 2^n, rounded once

Every float operation is one of num's correctly rounded integer routines (through the F
wrapper below, so the ports read like the C originals), so the results depend on nothing
but the input bits.  sin and cos reduce their argument exactly: integer Payne-Hanek with
1280 bits of 2/pi (computed with Python's integers from Machin's formula), so sin(1e300) is
as good as sin(1).  NaN results are num::NAN; special values follow C99 Annex F (pow(x, 0)
= 1 even for NaN, pow(-1, inf) = 1, log(0) = -inf, sin(inf) = NaN).
```

- **`fn scalbn(x: f64, n: i32) -> f64`**
  x \* 2^n, rounded once (musl's scalbn)

- **`fn round(x: f64) -> f64`**
  to the nearest integer, halves away from zero (C's round); keeps -0 and the sign of
  results that round to zero

- **`fn exp(x: f64) -> f64`**
  e^x

- **`fn log(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the natural logarithm

- **`fn log2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the logarithm to base 2 (exact for powers of two)

- **`fn log10(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the logarithm to base 10

- **`fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64`**
  x to the power y

- **`fn sin(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the sine

- **`fn cos(x: f64) -> f64`**
  the cosine

### `script/vm.rs`

Source: [`lib/script/vm.rs`](../lib/script/vm.rs)

```text
vm -- the stack machine that runs compiled scripts: fuel, limits, exceptions, the
mark-and-sweep collector, the host interface

  let mut vm = Vm::new(&program, Limits::default());   the top-level code is pending
  match vm.run(&mut host, 10_000) {                     run it with up to 10 000 fuel
      Status::Done(v) => ..                             finished with the value v
      Status::Yielded => ..                             fuel used up, or a native asked to
                                                        yield: run() again continues
      Status::Error(e) => ..                            an uncaught exception or a limit; the
                                                        invocation is gone, globals stay
  }
  vm.call("on_request", &[arg])?;  then run() as above   (only while idle)
  vm.call_value(f, &args)?                               a function value, e.g. a pinned
                                                         callback
  vm.global("hits") / set_global("config", v)            globals of the script; a name the
                                                         script takes from the host gets its
                                                         value here
  vm.output() / take_output()                            what print() wrote
  vm.resume(host, fuel)                                  the same as run(), after Yielded

Fuel is virtual CPU time: one unit per instruction, more for instructions that copy (string
and list concatenation, literals, iterating a map), plus what natives charge.  run(host,
fuel) stops before the next instruction once `fuel` is used, so a run may use a little more
than asked (the extra of its last instruction); last_fuel() tells how much.  Splitting an
invocation into runs of any size never changes its result, its output or its total fuel:
all state lives in the VM, and the collector runs at allocations only.

Values: nil and false are falsy, everything else is truthy.  int is i64 with wrapping +, -,
* and unary minus; / and % truncate (like C, Go, Rust), x / 0 and x % 0 throw.  An int
meeting a float becomes a float; float arithmetic is num.rs (bit-identical everywhere).  ==
compares numbers exactly across int and float, str and bytes by content, lists, maps and
functions by identity.  + also joins str, bytes and lists.  Map keys are str, int or bool;
a missing key or field reads as nil; lists throw on an index outside 0..len.  for over a map
visits the keys it had when the loop started (in insertion order, skipping removed ones);
over a list it reads the length each round.  Calls pass missing arguments as nil and drop
extra ones.

Names the script does not declare come from the host: print, len, type, str, int and float
are built in, the standard library (stdlib.rs: str.split, list.sort, math.sqrt, json.encode,
math.pi ..) comes next; f(..) and obj.method(..) on any other host name call Host::call with
the name ("log", "http.serve"); obj.m(..) on a value calls a function stored under m in a
map, the built-in list.push / list.pop, the library's type.m, or Host::call("list.m", [obj,
args..]).  set_global gives a host name a value (config), which then takes precedence.
Reading a host name as a value (let f = log) needs Host::knows (library names need none);
an unknown one throws "Unbekannter Name".  A native can call a function value back to its
end with Cx::call (sort, map); a yield it asks for then waits until the native returns, and
an exception that leaves the callback keeps the position it was thrown at.  cancel() drops
a pending invocation.

Runtime errors (wrong types, division by 0, a bad index) throw a str with a German message
that try/catch can catch; an uncaught one ends the invocation with an Error (message,
line and column, a stack trace).  The limits (fuel per invocation, heap, call depth, stack)
end it at once and cannot be caught.

Collector: mark and sweep over the heap arena, from the stack, the globals, host values,
pinned values, the last result and objects a native made during its call.  It runs only in
run(), when an allocation crosses the threshold (twice the live bytes after the last
collection, at least 256 KiB, at most the heap limit).  Values the host keeps between runs
must be pinned (pin / unpin) or be reachable from the script.  Values the host passes in
are checked (valid()): a stale value of a freed object gives an error or None, not a crash.
```

- **`struct Limits`**
  the limits of a VM; crossing one ends the invocation (scripts cannot catch it)
  - `heap: u64` -- heap bytes, counted the same way on every target (default 16 MiB)
  - `stack: u32` -- values on the stack: parameters, locals and temporaries of all calls (100 000)
  - `depth: u32` -- calls inside each other (500)
  - `fuel: u64` -- fuel of one invocation (the top-level code, call, call_value) over all its runs
    (10 000 000)
  - `output: u32` -- bytes of print output kept; more is dropped (1 MiB)

- **`enum ErrorKind`**
  what an Error is about
  - `Uncaught` -- an exception nobody caught: throw, or a runtime error such as a division by 0
  - `Fuel` -- the invocation used more fuel than Limits::fuel
  - `Heap` -- the heap would grow beyond Limits::heap
  - `Depth` -- more nested calls than Limits::depth
  - `Stack` -- more stack values than Limits::stack
  - `Host` -- a native function failed for good (Fail::Fatal)
  - `Usage` -- the request does not fit the VM's state: busy, nothing to run, no such function
  - `Internal` -- a bug of the VM or the compiler

- **`struct TraceLine`**
  a function and the position it was at when the error happened
  - `func: String` -- "" for the top-level code, "fn" for an anonymous function
  - `line: u32`
  - `col: u32`

- **`struct Error`**
  why an invocation ended without a result
  - `kind: ErrorKind`
  - `msg: String` -- German text; for an uncaught throw the thrown value as text
  - `line: u32` -- where it happened (0 when not in the script)
  - `col: u32`
  - `trace: Vec<TraceLine>` -- the calls, innermost first

- **`enum Status`**
  the outcome of run()
  - `Done(Value)` -- the invocation returned this value (valid until the next run)
  - `Yielded` -- fuel used up, or a native asked to yield; run() again continues
  - `Error(Error)`

- **`enum Fail`**
  why a native function returned no value
  - `Unknown` -- the host has no function of that name
  - `Throw(Value)` -- throw this value in the script (catchable); Cx::error makes one from a message
  - `Fatal(String)` -- end the invocation with this message (not catchable)

- **`trait Host`**
  the functions a script can call besides its own: Host::call gets the name as the script
  wrote it ("log", "http.serve"), or "type.method" with the object as args[0] for methods of
  the built-in types ("list.sum", "map.json"); return Err(Fail::Unknown) for names you do
  not have.  The built-ins (print, len, type, str, int, float, list.push, list.pop) and the
  standard library (script::library(): str.split, list.sort, json.encode ..) never get here.
  - `fn call(&mut self, cx: &mut Cx, name: &str, args: &[Value]) -> Result<Value, Fail>`
  - `fn knows(&self, name: &str) -> bool`
    whether `name` ("log", "http", "http.serve") may be read as a value (a native function
    value), as in `let f = log` or `list.each(log)`; reading an unknown name throws
    "Unbekannter Name".  Calls do not ask.

- **`struct Pin(u32)`**
  a value the host keeps alive (see Vm::pin)

- **`struct Vm`**
  a running script; Clone copies the whole state (heap included), Send moves it to another
  thread

**`impl Vm`**

- **`fn new(prog: &Program, limits: Limits) -> Vm`**
  a VM for the program with its top-level code pending (run() runs it)
- **`fn busy(&self) -> bool`**
  whether an invocation is pending (started or yielded)
- **`fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[Value]) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  start a call of the script's global function `name` (run() runs it)
- **`fn call_value(&mut self, f: Value, args: &[Value]) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  start a call of a function value (run() runs it)
- **`fn run(&mut self, host: &mut dyn Host, fuel: u64) -> Status`**
  run the pending invocation with up to `fuel` fuel (see the module comment)
- **`fn resume(&mut self, host: &mut dyn Host, fuel: u64) -> Status`**
  continue an invocation after Status::Yielded: the same as run(), named for readers of
  host code
- **`fn cancel(&mut self)`**
  drop the pending invocation (a yielded callback of a device that was switched off, say);
  globals keep what it changed so far
- **`fn last_fuel(&self) -> u64`**
  fuel used by the last run()
- **`fn call_fuel(&self) -> u64`**
  fuel used by the current (or last) invocation so far
- **`fn limits(&self) -> Limits`**
  the limits the VM was made with
- **`fn output(&self) -> &str`**
  what print() wrote since the last take_output()
- **`fn take_output(&mut self) -> String`**
  what print() wrote, emptying the buffer
- **`fn global(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Value>`**
  a global of the script, or the value the host gave a host name
- **`fn set_global(&mut self, name: &str, v: Value) -> bool`**
  set a global of the script, or give a name the script takes from the host a value (a
  map for config, say); false when the script uses no such name
- **`fn valid(&self, v: Value) -> bool`**
  whether a value belongs to this VM and is alive: a value of an object the collector
  freed (not pinned between runs), of another VM, or a cell is not
- **`fn str(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&str>`**
  the text of a str
- **`fn bytes(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&[u8]>`**
  the content of a bytes value
- **`fn list(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&[Value]>`**
  the items of a list
- **`fn map_get(&self, m: Value, key: Value) -> Option<Value>`**
  m[key]; None when m is no map, the key is missing or of a type maps do not have
- **`fn map_get_str(&self, m: Value, key: &str) -> Option<Value>`**
  m.key
- **`fn map_entries(&self, m: Value) -> Vec<(Value, Value)>`**
  the entries of a map in order
- **`fn new_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<Value, Error>`**
  a new str (valid until the next run unless the script keeps it or it is pinned)
- **`fn new_bytes(&mut self, b: &[u8]) -> Result<Value, Error>`**
  a new bytes value
- **`fn new_list(&mut self, items: Vec<Value>) -> Result<Value, Error>`**
  a new list of these items
- **`fn new_map(&mut self) -> Result<Value, Error>`**
  a new empty map
- **`fn map_set(&mut self, m: Value, k: Value, v: Value) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  m[k] = v (k: str, int or bool)
- **`fn map_remove(&mut self, m: Value, k: Value) -> Option<Value>`**
  remove m[k]; the old value
- **`fn list_push(&mut self, l: Value, v: Value) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  append v to the list l
- **`fn list_set(&mut self, l: Value, i: usize, v: Value) -> bool`**
  l[i] = v (false when l is no list or i is out of range)
- **`fn list_replace(&mut self, l: Value, items: Vec<Value>) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  replace the items of a list (sorting, filtering in place)
- **`fn native(&mut self, name: &str) -> Value`**
  a native function value for a host name ("timer.cancel")
- **`fn pin(&mut self, v: Value) -> Pin`**
  keep a value alive while the host holds it (a callback, say); an invalid value pins nil
- **`fn pinned(&self, p: Pin) -> Value`**
  the pinned value (nil after unpin)
- **`fn unpin(&mut self, p: Pin)`**
  let the collector have the value again
- **`fn display(&self, v: Value) -> String`**
  the value as print() shows it (strings as they are, inside lists and maps quoted)
- **`fn equal(&self, a: Value, b: Value) -> bool`**
  == of the script
- **`fn json_encode(&mut self, v: Value, indent: u32) -> Result<String, Error>`**
  v as JSON text like json.encode (indent 0: compact, else spaces per level); an Error
  (kind Uncaught, the German message) for data JSON cannot hold
- **`fn json_decode(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<Value, Error>`**
  the value of a JSON text like json.decode (valid until the next run unless the script
  keeps it or it is pinned)
- **`fn collect(&mut self)`**
  collect garbage now: everything the script cannot reach, except pinned values and the
  last result, is freed
- **`fn heap_bytes(&self) -> u64`**
  accounted bytes of the collectable objects
- **`fn heap_objects(&self) -> u32`**
  objects on the heap (without the program's constants)
- **`fn collections(&self) -> u32`**
  collections so far

- **`struct Cx<'a>`**
  the context of a native function: values, allocation, fuel, yielding

**`impl Cx<'_>`**

- **`fn str(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&str>`**
  the text of a str (Vm::str)
- **`fn bytes(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&[u8]>`**
  the content of a bytes value
- **`fn list(&self, v: Value) -> Option<&[Value]>`**
  the items of a list
- **`fn map_get(&self, m: Value, key: Value) -> Option<Value>`**
  m[key]
- **`fn map_get_str(&self, m: Value, key: &str) -> Option<Value>`**
  m.key
- **`fn map_entries(&self, m: Value) -> Vec<(Value, Value)>`**
  the entries of a map in order
- **`fn display(&self, v: Value) -> String`**
  the value as print() shows it
- **`fn equal(&self, a: Value, b: Value) -> bool`**
  == of the script
- **`fn new_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  a new str (alive until the native returns; return it or store it in the script's data)
- **`fn new_bytes(&mut self, b: &[u8]) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  a new bytes value
- **`fn new_list(&mut self, items: Vec<Value>) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  a new list of these items
- **`fn new_map(&mut self) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  a new empty map
- **`fn map_set(&mut self, m: Value, k: Value, v: Value) -> Result<(), Fail>`**
  m[k] = v (k: str, int or bool)
- **`fn map_remove(&mut self, m: Value, k: Value) -> Option<Value>`**
  remove m[k]; the old value
- **`fn list_push(&mut self, l: Value, v: Value) -> Result<(), Fail>`**
  append v to the list l
- **`fn list_set(&mut self, l: Value, i: usize, v: Value) -> bool`**
  l[i] = v (false when l is no list or i is out of range)
- **`fn list_replace(&mut self, l: Value, items: Vec<Value>) -> Result<(), Fail>`**
  replace the items of a list
- **`fn native(&mut self, name: &str) -> Value`**
  a native function value (for maps of functions the host returns)
- **`fn call(&mut self, host: &mut dyn Host, f: Value, args: &[Value]) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  call a function value (a callback the script passed) to its end and return its result;
  Err(Fail::Throw(v)) when it throws (return it to pass the exception on).  Pass the host
  itself (`cx.call(self, f, &args)`): the callback may call natives too.  It cannot yield
  in between (a yield request waits until the native returns); fuel and the limits count
  as usual, and calls nest at most 20 deep.
- **`fn error(&mut self, msg: &str) -> Fail`**
  an exception with a message, for `return Err(cx.error("…"))`
- **`fn charge(&mut self, fuel: u64)`**
  add fuel for the work of this call (the call itself costs 1); spend() also stops at the
  fuel limit
- **`fn fuel(&self) -> u64`**
  the fuel of the current invocation so far, over all its runs and this call included:
  the moment of its CPU time a host gives what the native does (JFNetworker's scripts)
- **`fn spend(&mut self, fuel: u64) -> Result<(), Fail>`**
  charge fuel for work and end the invocation with ErrorKind::Fuel once Limits::fuel is
  used up: a long operation calls this as it goes, so a huge job stops in the middle
- **`fn keep(&mut self, v: Value)`**
  keep v alive until the native returns, for values it holds while it calls back (the
  callback may change the list they came from, and the collector may run)
- **`fn json_encode(&mut self, v: Value, indent: u32) -> Result<String, Fail>`**
  v as JSON text like json.encode (indent 0: compact, else spaces per level); data that
  JSON cannot hold (nan, bytes, functions, cycles) throws
- **`fn json_decode(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<Value, Fail>`**
  the value of a JSON text like json.decode (maps in the order of the members); a syntax
  error throws "json.decode: … (Zeile 1, Spalte 5)"
- **`fn yield_now(&mut self)`**
  end the run after this call returns (Status::Yielded; run() continues after the call)
- **`fn print(&mut self, s: &str)`**
  add text to the print output
- **`fn pin(&mut self, v: Value) -> Pin`**
  keep a value alive beyond this call (a callback, say); see Vm::pin
- **`fn pinned(&self, p: Pin) -> Value`**
  the pinned value
- **`fn unpin(&mut self, p: Pin)`**
  let the collector have the value again

## crypto

*hashes, MACs, KDFs, Argon2id, AEAD, X25519, Ed25519, sealed boxes (no randomness inside)* -- crate root [`lib/crypto/lib.rs`](../lib/crypto/lib.rs)

```text
crypto -- the primitives BackupCraft (and anything else) builds on, in plain Rust

  sha2      Sha256 / Sha384 / Sha512, sha256 / sha384 / sha512(data)         (FIPS 180-4)
  hmac      Hmac<H>, hmac_sha256 / hmac_sha512, hkdf_sha256 / hkdf_sha512,
            pbkdf2_sha256 (import of foreign key files only)                (RFC 2104/5869/8018)
  blake2b   Blake2b (keyed, 1..64 byte digests)                             (RFC 7693)
  blake3    Blake3 (hash, keyed_hash, derive_key, any output length)
  argon2    argon2id(password, salt, params, out), PHC strings hash / verify (RFC 9106)
  chacha    ChaCha20 (IETF), HChaCha20, XChaCha20                           (RFC 8439)
  poly1305  Poly1305 one-time authenticator                                 (RFC 8439)
  aead      ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 seal / open            (RFC 8439)
  x25519    Diffie-Hellman over Curve25519                                  (RFC 7748)
  ed25519   signatures, strict verification                                 (RFC 8032)
  sealbox   anonymous public-key encryption: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + XChaCha20-Poly1305
  aes, gcm  AES-128/256 (bitsliced, constant time; both directions), AES-GCM seal / open
            (FIPS 197, SP 800-38D)
  bn        big integers modulo odd numbers (public values: variable time; pow_ct for a
            secret exponent)
  rsa       RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and PSS verification                            (RFC 8017)
  ecdsa     ECDSA verification on P-256 / P-384                              (FIPS 186-4)
  p256      Diffie-Hellman on P-256 in constant time (complete formulas)      (SEC 1)
  b64       Base64 (standard and URL alphabet, with or without padding)
  ct_eq / zeroize / hex
  sha1      Sha1, sha1(data); with hmac_sha1, pbkdf2 (any Hash) and pbkdf2_sha1 in hmac:
            only for protocols defined with SHA-1 (WPA2-Personal)          (FIPS 180-4)
  keywrap   aes_wrap / aes_unwrap: the AES key wrap                         (RFC 3394)
  cmac      cmac_aes: AES-CMAC                                              (RFC 4493)

No randomness here: callers pass random bytes in (plat::fill_random), so everything is
deterministic and testable.  Secret-dependent work avoids branches and table lookups
(field arithmetic with 51-bit limbs, masked conditional swaps and selects).
```

    the digest into out[..OUT]

### `crypto/aead.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/aead.rs`](../lib/crypto/aead.rs)

```text
aead -- ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) and XChaCha20-Poly1305 (192-bit nonces: random nonces
are safe)

  seal_in_place(key, nonce, aad, buf) -> tag          open_in_place(.., buf, &tag) -> ok
  seal(key, nonce, aad, plain) -> ciphertext ‖ tag    open(.., sealed) -> Some(plain)
  (x_* : the same with a 24-byte nonce)
```

```rust
KEY_LEN: usize = 32
NONCE_LEN: usize = 12
XNONCE_LEN: usize = 24
TAG_LEN: usize = 16
```

- **`fn seal_in_place(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], aad: &[u8], buf: &mut [u8]) -> [u8; 16]`**
  encrypt buf in place -> the tag

- **`fn open_in_place(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], aad: &[u8], buf: &mut [u8], t: &[u8; 16]) -> bool`**
  check the tag and decrypt buf in place -> false (buf unchanged) on a wrong tag

- **`fn seal(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], aad: &[u8], plain: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  ciphertext ‖ tag

- **`fn open(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 12], aad: &[u8], sealed: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the plaintext of ciphertext ‖ tag (None: too short or forged)

- **`fn x_seal_in_place(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 24], aad: &[u8], buf: &mut [u8]) -> [u8; 16]`**
  XChaCha20-Poly1305: encrypt buf in place -> the tag

- **`fn x_open_in_place(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 24], aad: &[u8], buf: &mut [u8], t: &[u8; 16]) -> bool`**
  XChaCha20-Poly1305: check and decrypt in place

- **`fn x_seal(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 24], aad: &[u8], plain: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  XChaCha20-Poly1305: ciphertext ‖ tag

- **`fn x_open(key: &[u8; 32], nonce: &[u8; 24], aad: &[u8], sealed: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  XChaCha20-Poly1305: the plaintext of ciphertext ‖ tag

### `crypto/aes.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/aes.rs`](../lib/crypto/aes.rs)

```text
aes -- AES-128 / AES-256 (FIPS 197) in constant time

  Aes::new(key) (16 or 32 bytes)    aes.encrypt4(&mut [[u8; 16]; 4])    aes.encrypt(&mut block)
                                    aes.decrypt4(&mut [[u8; 16]; 4])    aes.decrypt(&mut block)

Bitsliced: four blocks at a time in eight 64-bit words, word i holding bit i of all 64 bytes
(bit position = row * 16 + column * 4 + block).  SubBytes inverts in GF(2^8) with
multiplications on those bit planes (x^254 by four multiplications and seven squarings),
then applies the affine map; ShiftRows rotates inside the 16-bit row fields, MixColumns
rotates whole rows.  No table lookups, no branches on data or key: what GCM needs for
TLS.  The inverse cipher (CBC of the Secret Service, plat::secret) undoes the affine map
before the same inversion; InvMixColumns is MixColumns after a_r ^= 4 (a_r ^ a_(r+2)).
```

- **`struct Aes`**

**`impl Aes`**

- **`fn new(key: &[u8]) -> Option<Aes>`**
  a 16-byte (AES-128) or 32-byte (AES-256) key
- **`fn encrypt4(&self, blocks: &mut [[u8; 16]; 4])`**
  encrypt four blocks in place
- **`fn encrypt(&self, block: &mut [u8; 16])`**
  encrypt one block in place
- **`fn decrypt4(&self, blocks: &mut [[u8; 16]; 4])`**
  decrypt four blocks in place
- **`fn decrypt(&self, block: &mut [u8; 16])`**
  decrypt one block in place

### `crypto/argon2.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/argon2.rs`](../lib/crypto/argon2.rs)

```text
argon2 -- Argon2id (RFC 9106, version 0x13) and PHC strings

  argon2id(password, salt, &Params, out)          raw tag (secret / associated data empty)
  argon2id_ex(password, salt, secret, ad, &Params, out)
  hash(password, salt, &Params) -> "$argon2id$v=19$m=..,t=..,p=..$salt$hash"
  verify(phc, password) -> bool                   (constant-time comparison)

Lanes are filled one after the other in each slice (the result is the same as with
threads); memory is m KiB, allocated per call.
```

- **`struct Params`**
  cost parameters
  - `m_kib: u32` -- memory in KiB (at least 8 \* lanes)
  - `t: u32` -- passes over the memory
  - `p: u32` -- lanes (parallelism)
  - `out_len: u32` -- tag length in bytes

**`impl Params`**

- **`const INTERACTIVE: Params = Params { m_kib: 19 * 1024, t: 2, p: 1, out_len: 32 }`**
  the OWASP recommendation for interactive logins: 19 MiB, 2 passes, 1 lane
- **`const KEY: Params = Params { m_kib: 64 * 1024, t: 3, p: 1, out_len: 32 }`**
  for keys that protect data at rest (passphrases): 64 MiB, 3 passes, 1 lane

- **`fn argon2id(password: &[u8], salt: &[u8], params: &Params, out: &mut [u8]) -> bool`**
  Argon2id with an empty secret and no associated data

- **`fn argon2id_ex(password: &[u8], salt: &[u8], secret: &[u8], ad: &[u8], params: &Params, out: &mut [u8]) -> bool`**
  Argon2id: false for invalid parameters (out.len() must equal params.out_len)

- **`fn parse(phc: &str) -> Option<(Params, Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>`**
  the parameters, salt and tag of a PHC string

### `crypto/bn.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/bn.rs`](../lib/crypto/bn.rs)

```text
bn -- unsigned big integers for checking signatures (RSA, ECDSA)

  from_be / to_be                     big-endian bytes <-> little-endian 64-bit limbs
  Mont::new(n)                        arithmetic modulo an odd n: mul (Montgomery), add, sub,
                                      to_mont / from_mont, pow, inv (n prime); pow_ct for a
                                      secret exponent (finite-field Diffie-Hellman)

Variable time on purpose: everything here is public (keys, signatures, digests).  Never use
it for secrets -- except pow_ct, which neither branches on nor indexes by the exponent.
```

- **`type Limbs = Vec<u64>`**

- **`fn from_be(b: &[u8], k: usize) -> Limbs`**
  big-endian bytes -> limbs (at least `k` of them)

- **`fn to_be(a: &[u64], len: usize) -> Vec<u8>`**
  limbs -> exactly `len` big-endian bytes (higher bytes dropped)

- **`fn cmp(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Ordering`**

- **`fn is_zero(a: &[u64]) -> bool`**

- **`fn bits(a: &[u64]) -> usize`**
  the number of significant bits

- **`struct Mont`**
  arithmetic modulo an odd number
  - `n: Limbs`

**`impl Mont`**

- **`fn new(n: &[u64]) -> Option<Mont>`**
- **`fn limbs(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn mul(&self, a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
  a b R^-1 mod n (a, b &lt; n)
- **`fn to_mont(&self, a: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
- **`fn from_mont(&self, a: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
- **`fn add(&self, a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
  (a + b) mod n (a, b &lt; n)
- **`fn sub(&self, a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
  (a - b) mod n (a, b &lt; n)
- **`fn reduce_once(&self, a: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
  a mod n for a &lt; 2 n
- **`fn pow(&self, base: &[u64], exp: &[u8]) -> Limbs`**
  base^exp mod n (normal form in and out; exp big-endian)
- **`fn pow_ct(&self, base: &[u64], exp: &[u8]) -> Limbs`**
  base^exp mod n for a secret exponent (Diffie-Hellman; base public): windows of four
  bits, the table entry picked with masks, masked reductions -- the time depends on the
  lengths only
- **`fn inv_mont(&self, a: &[u64]) -> Limbs`**
  a^-1 mod n for a prime n (a != 0; Montgomery form in and out)

### `crypto/ed25519.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/ed25519.rs`](../lib/crypto/ed25519.rs)

```text
ed25519 -- Ed25519 signatures (RFC 8032), strict verification

  Keypair::from_seed(&seed) -> Keypair { public }     sign(&msg) -> [u8; 64]
  verify(&public, &msg, &sig) -> bool

Verification is strict: the public key and R must be canonical points, S must be below the
group order, and [S]B == R + [k]A must hold exactly (no cofactor), so a signature is valid
or not the same way everywhere.  The curve constants (d, sqrt(-1), the base point) are
computed from their definitions instead of copied as long numbers.
Scalar multiplication: double and add-always with masked selects (no branches on bits).
```

### `crypto/gcm.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/gcm.rs`](../lib/crypto/gcm.rs)

```text
gcm -- AES-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D) with 12-byte nonces and 16-byte tags, in constant time

  AesGcm::new(key)                          16 (AES-128-GCM) or 32 bytes (AES-256-GCM)
  seal_in_place(nonce, aad, data) -> tag    open_in_place(nonce, aad, data, tag) -> bool

GHASH runs on the bit-reversed form of the blocks, where multiplication in GF(2^128) is a
plain carry-less product modulo x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1.  The carry-less products come from
integer multiplications of operands with three-bit holes (32-bit halves: at most eight
partial products meet in one position, so no carry reaches the next used bit).
```

### `crypto/p256.rs`

Source: [`lib/crypto/p256.rs`](../lib/crypto/p256.rs)

```text
p256 -- Diffie-Hellman on NIST P-256 (SEC 1, RFC 8446 4.2.8.2) in constant time

  public_key(&secret) -> [u8; 65]          (panics on an invalid secret) 04 || x || y of secret * G
  shared(&secret, &peer_point) -> Option<[u8; 32]>   the x coordinate of secret * peer;
                                           None for a point that is not on the curve
  secret_from(random) -> Option<[u8; 32]>  a scalar in [1, n - 1] from 32 random bytes

Field elements in Montgomery form with four 64-bit limbs; multiplication, addition and
subtraction without branches on the values (masked final corrections).  Points in projective
coordinates with the complete addition formulas of Renes, Costello and Batina (2016,
algorithm 4, a = -3): no exceptional cases, so doubling uses the same formula.  Scalar
multiplication by four-bit windows with a table read in full for every window.
```

- **`fn secret_from(random: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<[u8; 32]>`**
  a scalar in [1, n - 1] from random bytes (None: draw again)

- **`fn public_key(secret: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 65]`**
  the public key of a secret scalar: 04 || x || y

```text
compress -- lossless compression for backup data

  lz4::compress(data) -> Vec<u8>                  LZ4 block (greedy, 64 KiB window)
  lz4::decompress(block, max_out) -> Option<Vec>  bounds-checked; None on any corruption

```

### `compress/lz4.rs`

Source: [`lib/compress/lz4.rs`](../lib/compress/lz4.rs)

```text
lz4 -- the LZ4 block and frame formats

  compress(data) -> block                greedy matcher, 16K-entry hash table, skip
                                         acceleration on incompressible data
  decompress(block, max_out)             None on truncation, a bad offset, or more than
                                         max_out bytes; never reads or writes out of bounds
  decompress_into(block, &mut out, limit) appends (back references may reach into the
                                         earlier contents of out: linked frame blocks)
  frame_compress(data) / frame_decompress(frame, max_out)

Block rules kept by the compressor: the last 5 bytes are literals, no match starts in the
last 12 bytes, offsets 1..=65535.
```

- **`const fn bound(n: usize) -> usize`**
  the largest block compress() can produce for n input bytes

- **`fn compress(src: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  compress into one LZ4 block

- **`fn decompress_into(src: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>, limit: usize) -> bool`**
  decode one block, appending to out (out.len() stays &lt;= limit) -> false on corrupt input

- **`fn decompress(src: &[u8], max_out: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  decode one block of at most max_out bytes

- **`fn frame_compress(src: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  an LZ4 frame: independent 4 MiB blocks, content size and content checksum

- **`fn frame_decompress(src: &[u8], max_out: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  decode one or more concatenated LZ4 frames (skippable frames are skipped) of at most
  max_out bytes in total; None on corruption, an unsupported feature (dictionary ids), a
  checksum mismatch, or too much output

### `compress/zstd/mod.rs`

Source: [`lib/compress/zstd/mod.rs`](../lib/compress/zstd/mod.rs)

```text
zstd -- the Zstandard format (RFC 8878), interoperable with the zstd tool both ways

  compress(data, level) -> frame        levels 1..=19 (LEVEL_DEFAULT 3); content size and
                                        checksum in the frame; window up to 8 MiB
  decompress(frames, max_out)           any conforming frames without a dictionary,
                                        concatenated and skippable ones too; None on
                                        corruption, a checksum mismatch or > max_out bytes
  content_size(frame)                   the size a frame header declares

```

```rust
LEVEL_DEFAULT: i32 = 3
LEVEL_MAX: i32 = 19
```

### `compress/zstd/dec.rs`

Source: [`lib/compress/zstd/dec.rs`](../lib/compress/zstd/dec.rs)

```text
dec -- the zstd frame decoder (RFC 8878): frames and skippable frames, raw / RLE /
compressed blocks, raw / RLE / Huffman / treeless literals with 1 or 4 streams, sequences
with predefined / RLE / FSE / repeat tables, repeat offsets, content size and checksum.
Dictionaries are not supported (a frame that names one is refused).  Every length, offset
and table is checked: corrupt input gives None, never a panic or more than max_out bytes.
```

- **`fn decompress(src: &[u8], max_out: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  decode all frames of src -> None on corruption, unsupported features or > max_out bytes

- **`fn content_size(src: &[u8]) -> Option<u64>`**
  the content size a frame header declares (None: not stated or not a zstd frame)

### `compress/zstd/enc.rs`

Source: [`lib/compress/zstd/enc.rs`](../lib/compress/zstd/enc.rs)

```text
enc -- the zstd encoder: one frame with content size and checksum, blocks of 128 KiB.

Matches come from a hash-chain finder over a window of up to 8 MiB (levels 1..=19 set the
search depth and how many positions ahead a lazy match may be preferred); the three repeat
offsets are tried first.  Literals are Huffman coded when that is smaller; each of the three
sequence codes takes the cheapest of RLE, the predefined distribution and its own table.
A block that does not get smaller is stored raw; a run of one byte value becomes an RLE
block.  The decoder's repeat offsets do not move on raw blocks, so the encoder rolls them back.
```

- **`const fn bound(n: usize) -> usize`**
  the largest frame compress() makes from n bytes

- **`fn compress(src: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8>`**
  one zstd frame

## datastore

*an embedded journal database: JSON collections, transactions, snapshots, crash recovery* -- crate root [`lib/datastore/lib.rs`](../lib/datastore/lib.rs)

```text
datastore -- an embedded, crash-safe store for one server process: collections of JSON
records (id -> value) kept in memory, made durable by a write-ahead log and snapshots, plus
append-only journals for logs that grow without bound (audit, session logs)

  Store::open(dir) / open_with(dir, Options) -> Result<Store, StoreError>
  get(coll, id) / list(coll) / count(coll) / ids(coll)          (clones of the values)
  write(|tx| { tx.put(coll, id, v); tx.delete(coll, id); }) -> Result<seq>
  update(coll, id, |v| ...)                                     read-modify-write in one txn
  compact()                                                     snapshot now
  Journal::open(dir) / append(name, &value) / tail(name, n) / read_month(name, yyyymm)

Files in `dir`: LOCK, snap-<seq>.bcs, wal-<first seq>.log; journal/<name>/<yyyymm>.jl.
  snapshot: "BCS1" seq:u64 | colls:u32 | per collection name, records:u32 | per record id,
            JSON | BLAKE3 of everything before (32 bytes)
  WAL frame: "BCW1" len:u32 seq:u64 payload BLAKE3(len ‖ seq ‖ payload)[..16]; the payload is
            a JSON array of ["put", coll, id, value] / ["del", coll, id]
A transaction is one frame, written and fsynced before it becomes visible.  Opening loads the
newest valid snapshot and replays the frames after it.  A torn frame at the very end (a crash
during a write) is cut off; a damaged frame with intact data behind it stops the open with
StoreError::Corrupt unless Options::repair is set (then the log is cut there).
Values are plain JSON: secrets are sealed by the caller (crypto::aead) before they get here.
```

### `datastore` crate root

- **`fn record_limits() -> Limits`**
  the limits of one stored record

- **`enum StoreError`**
  - `Locked` -- another process holds the store
  - `Io(String)` -- reading or writing a file failed
  - `Corrupt(String)` -- a damaged log frame with intact data behind it (open with repair to cut the log there)
  - `TooLarge` -- a record or transaction over the size limits

- **`type StoreResult<T> = Result<T, StoreError>`**

- **`struct Options`**
  - `snapshot_bytes: u64` -- write a snapshot (and start a new log) when the log grows beyond this
  - `repair: bool` -- cut a damaged log at the damage instead of refusing to open
  - `durable: bool` -- fsync every transaction (off only for tests and bulk imports)

- **`struct Recovery`**
  what open() found
  - `snapshot_seq: u64`
  - `frames_replayed: u64`
  - `truncated_bytes: u64` -- bytes cut from the end of the log (a torn last write)
  - `repaired: Option<String>` -- the damage that was cut away with Options::repair

- **`struct Tx`**
  the changes of one transaction

**`impl Tx`**

- **`fn put(&mut self, coll: &str, id: &str, v: Value)`**
- **`fn delete(&mut self, coll: &str, id: &str)`**
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**

- **`type Data = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Value>>`**
  the records of every collection: collection -> id -> value

- **`struct Store`**
  the store (share it between threads by reference or Arc)

**`impl Store`**

- **`fn open(dir: &str) -> StoreResult<Store>`**
- **`fn open_with(dir: &str, opts: Options) -> StoreResult<Store>`**
- **`fn recovery(&self) -> &Recovery`**
  what open() found and repaired
- **`fn seq(&self) -> u64`**
  the sequence number of the last transaction
- **`fn get(&self, coll: &str, id: &str) -> Option<Value>`**
- **`fn contains(&self, coll: &str, id: &str) -> bool`**
- **`fn list(&self, coll: &str) -> Vec<(String, Value)>`**
  every record of a collection, ordered by id
- **`fn filter(&self, coll: &str, mut f: impl FnMut(&str, &Value) -> bool) -> Vec<(String, Value)>`**
  the records for which `f` holds
- **`fn ids(&self, coll: &str) -> Vec<String>`**
- **`fn count(&self, coll: &str) -> usize`**
- **`fn write<E: From<StoreError>>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&Data, &mut Tx) -> Result<(), E>) -> Result<u64, E>`**
  run a transaction: the changes `f` records become durable and visible together
  (f sees the current data; nothing is written when it returns Err or records nothing)
- **`fn put(&self, coll: &str, id: &str, v: Value) -> StoreResult<u64>`**
  put one record
- **`fn delete(&self, coll: &str, id: &str) -> StoreResult<u64>`**
  delete one record
- **`fn update(&self, coll: &str, id: &str, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Value)) -> StoreResult<Option<Value>>`**
  change one record in place (None: it does not exist)
- **`fn compact(&self) -> StoreResult<()>`**
  write a snapshot now and start a new log

## netio

*HTTP/1.1 server and client, TLS 1.3 subset, X.509 of a private CA, SSH-2, DNS* -- crate root [`lib/netio/lib.rs`](../lib/netio/lib.rs)

```text
netio -- network protocols on top of plat::net

  dns        host names to addresses (Linux: /etc/hosts, resolv.conf, UDP / TCP queries;
             Windows: the system resolver)
  url        Url::parse("https://host:9443/api?x=1"), percent_encode / percent_decode,
             query_pairs
  http       Request, Response, Body (bytes or a stream sent chunked), Headers, status texts;
             the HTTP/1.1 wire format (bounded parsing, chunked transfer, keep-alive)
  server     Server::start(addr, ServerConfig, handler): accept thread + worker pool
  client     Client::request(...): blocking, timeouts, size limit
  tls        TLS 1.3 for own deployments (ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519, Ed25519, mutual auth)
             and a client for public servers (AES-GCM, RSA / ECDSA, TLS 1.2 fallback):
             connect / accept -> TlsStream (a Stream)
  x509 / der / pem   certificates: Ed25519 of a private CA (parse, build, verify chains) and
             the RSA / ECDSA certificates of the web PKI
  roots      the system's certificate authorities (Windows: CryptoAPI; Linux: the bundle)
  ssh        SSH-2 client (curve25519, ssh-ed25519, chacha20-poly1305): run commands with
             stdin; the server side of the transport for tests
  trust      https to a server with its own CA: known CA, pinned fingerprint or trust on
             first use (the presented CA comes back for the user's decision); https to
             public servers with the system's CAs
  smtp       sending mail: STARTTLS / TLS, AUTH PLAIN / LOGIN, UTF-8 messages
  Stream     what HTTP runs over (plat::net::TcpStream, tls::TlsStream)

Everything is blocking with timeouts and size limits on every read; a malformed peer gets an
error answer or a closed connection, never a panic.
```

### `netio` crate root

- **`trait Stream: Send + Sync`**
  a byte stream HTTP runs over (shared between a reader and a writer: &self methods)
  - `fn read(&self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> NetResult<usize>`
    up to buf.len() bytes; Ok(0) at the end
  - `fn write_all(&self, buf: &[u8]) -> NetResult<()>`
  - `fn set_timeouts(&self, read_ms: Option<u32>, write_ms: Option<u32>)`
    timeouts for the following reads / writes (None: block)
  - `fn shutdown(&self)`
    no more writes from this side
  - `fn wait_readable(&self, _ms: u32) -> bool`
    whether bytes (or the end) can be read within `ms`

### `netio/client.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/client.rs`](../lib/netio/client.rs)

```text
client -- a blocking HTTP/1.1 client: one connection per request, timeouts, a size limit,
an optional connector for https (TLS wraps the TCP connection)

  Client::new().request("GET", &url, &headers, body) -> Result<Response, HttpError>
  client.get_to(&url, &headers, max, on)   a download piece by piece (Part::Head, Part::Data)
  client.with_connector(Arc<dyn Fn(&Url, TcpStream) -> Result<Box<dyn Stream>, HttpError>>)
  client.request_async(method, &url, &headers, body) -> future of the answer (the request on
  plat::task's blocking pool: ui.spawn / block_on await it without blocking)
  client.download(&url, &headers, path, &ctl) -> future of the status: the body into the file
  (plat::AtomicFile: replaced only by a whole 2xx body), progress and cancel in ctl
```

- **`enum HttpError`**
  - `Url(String)` -- not an http(s) URL, or https without a connector
  - `Net(NetError)`
  - `Tls(String)` -- the TLS layer refused (certificate, handshake)
  - `Bad` -- a malformed answer
  - `TooLarge` -- an answer over the size limit
  - `File` -- (download) the target file could not be created, written or put in place
  - `Cancelled` -- (download) cancelled through the Ctl, or the future was dropped

- **`type Connector = Arc<dyn Fn(&Url, TcpStream) -> Result<Box<dyn Stream>, HttpError> + Send + Sync>`**

- **`enum Part<'a>`**
  a piece of an answer that Client::get_to streams
  - `Head(u16, &'a Headers)` -- the status and the headers (first)
  - `Data(&'a [u8])` -- the next bytes of the body

- **`struct Client`**
  - `connect_ms: u32`
  - `timeout_ms: u32` -- the longest wait for any read or write
  - `max_body: usize`
  - `user_agent: String`

**`impl Client`**

- **`fn new() -> Client`**
- **`fn with_connector(mut self, c: Connector) -> Client`**
  the TLS layer for https URLs
- **`fn connect(&self, url: &Url) -> Result<Box<dyn Stream>, HttpError>`**
  open the connection a request to `url` goes over
- **`fn request(&self, method: &str, url: &Url, headers: &Headers, body: &[u8]) -> Result<Response, HttpError>`**
  send one request and read the whole answer
- **`fn get_to(&self, url: &Url, headers: &Headers, max: u64, on: &mut dyn FnMut(Part<'_>) -> bool) -> Result<(u16, Headers), HttpError>`**
  a GET whose answer goes piece by piece to `on` (downloads larger than memory): first
  Part::Head (false: skip the body), then Part::Data for every piece of the body (false:
  stop, Err(HttpError::Bad)).  The body may have up to `max` bytes.  -> the status and the
  headers
- **`fn get(&self, url: &Url, headers: &Headers) -> Result<Response, HttpError>`**
- **`fn request_async(&self, method: &str, url: &Url, headers: &Headers, body: Vec<u8>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Response, HttpError>> + use<>`**
  request() on the blocking pool (plat::task::spawn_blocking): a future of the answer
- **`fn download(&self, url: &Url, headers: &Headers, path: &str, ctl: &Ctl) -> impl Future<Output = Result<u16, HttpError>> + use<>`**
  A GET whose body goes into the file at path, on the blocking pool.  The file is replaced
  like plat::write_file (plat::AtomicFile) and only by the whole body of a 2xx answer;
  other answers leave it alone.  ctl.progress counts the bytes (the total from
  Content-Length); ctl.cancel, or dropping the future, stops between pieces:
  Err(Cancelled), the file unchanged.  -> the status

- **`struct Session`**
  requests over one kept-alive connection (reconnected when the server closed it)

**`impl Session`**

- **`fn new(client: Client, url: Url) -> Session`**
- **`fn url(&self) -> &Url`**
- **`fn request(&mut self, method: &str, target: &str, headers: &Headers, body: &[u8], max_body: usize) -> Result<Response, HttpError>`**
  one request (an answer of at most `max_body` bytes)

- **`fn json_headers(token: &str) -> Headers`**
  "Bearer &lt;token>" headers plus JSON content type

### `netio/dns.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/dns.rs`](../lib/netio/dns.rs)

```text
dns -- host names to addresses

  resolve(host, port) -> NetResult<Vec<SocketAddr>>   numeric addresses and "localhost"
                    directly; Windows: the system resolver (plat); Linux: /etc/hosts, then
                    the name servers of /etc/resolv.conf (search domains, ndots)
  resolve_with(host, port, &Config)   the same with a given configuration (tests)
  Config::system()                    /etc/hosts + /etc/resolv.conf

Queries: A and AAAA over UDP (2 s per server and attempt, two rounds), over TCP when the answer
is truncated; an answer must come from the server asked and carry the query's id and question.
IPv4 addresses come first.  Not here: DNSSEC validation, mDNS, caching.

The app's permissions: a name its net.connect rules do not cover fails with
NetErrorKind::Denied before any query; the addresses of a covered name are registered
(plat::policy::net_resolved), so connections to them follow that name's ports.
```

  a query for one name and type

- **`enum Answer`**

  - `Found(Vec<IpAddr>)` -- the addresses of the asked type (maybe none: the name exists without them)
  - `NoName` -- the name does not exist
  - `Truncated` -- too large for UDP: ask over TCP
  - `Bad` -- a server failure or an answer that does not fit the question

    buffer and returns false after the last one (Content-Length when `len` is known)

  - `BodyTooLarge` -- body over the limit (413)

**`impl<'a> Reader<'a>`**

  reads fail with TimedOut once plat::time_us() is past this (a limit for a whole head,
  where the stream's timeout counts each read)
- **`fn has_buffered(&self) -> bool`**
  whether unread bytes are buffered (a pipelined next request)

  a message body by Content-Length or chunked transfer (`until_close`: a response without

- **`fn body_to(&mut self, h: &Headers, max: u64, until_close: bool, sink: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u8]) -> bool) -> Result<u64, ReadError>`**
  the body like body(), but each piece goes to `sink` as it arrives (downloads of any
  size); `sink` returning false stops reading with Err(Bad) -> the number of body bytes

### `netio/server.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/server.rs`](../lib/netio/server.rs)

```text
server -- a blocking HTTP/1.1 server: one accept thread, a pool of worker threads, each
worker serves one connection at a time (keep-alive, pipelined requests in order)

  Server::start(&addr, ServerConfig, handler) -> NetResult<Server>
  Server::start_with(.., Some(wrap))   wrap turns an accepted TcpStream into the Stream HTTP
                                       runs over (TLS) and the identity it proved
  server.local_addr() / server.stop()

The handler runs on a worker thread; it must not panic (panics abort the process).
Requests with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding are refused (request smuggling).
```

- **`struct ServerConfig`**
  - `threads: usize` -- worker threads (connections served at once)
  - `max_body: usize` -- the largest request body
  - `idle_ms: u32` -- how long an idle keep-alive connection stays open
  - `read_ms: u32` -- the longest wait for the next bytes of a request in progress
  - `write_ms: u32`
  - `max_requests: usize` -- requests per connection

- **`type Handler = Arc<dyn Fn(&Request) -> Response + Send + Sync>`**

- **`type Wrap = Arc<dyn Fn(TcpStream) -> Option<(Box<dyn Stream>, Option<String>)> + Send + Sync>`**
  turns an accepted connection into the stream HTTP runs over and the identity it proved
  (None: drop the connection, e.g. a failed TLS handshake)

### `netio/ssh.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/ssh.rs`](../lib/netio/ssh.rs)

```text
ssh -- SSH-2 for running commands on a machine (RFC 4253 / 4252 / 4254)

  Client::connect(stream, HostKeyCheck) -> Client      version, key exchange, host key check
  client.host_key()                                    type, blob, "SHA256:..." fingerprint
  client.auth_password(user, pw) / auth_key(user, &Keypair)
  client.exec(command, stdin, max_out) -> Exec { status, stdout, stderr }
  Transport::accept(stream, &host_key)                 the server side of the transport
                                                       (tests drive it with OpenSSH's client)
  private_key(text) -> Keypair      an unencrypted Ed25519 key ("OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY")
  public_key_line(&Keypair, comment) -> "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment" (authorized_keys)
  fingerprint(blob) -> "SHA256:..." the way ssh-keygen -l shows it

Algorithms: curve25519-sha256 (also @libssh.org) with OpenSSH's strict key exchange (against
the Terrapin prefix truncation), ssh-ed25519 host and user keys, chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com.
The host key is checked by the caller's rule: HostKeyCheck::Pinned(fingerprint) or Any (only
to learn the fingerprint).  Not here: RSA / ECDSA keys, compression, port forwarding, PTYs,
rekeying (a peer that starts a new key exchange ends the session; commands here are short).
```

### `netio/tls/mod.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/tls/mod.rs`](../lib/netio/tls/mod.rs)

```text
tls -- TLS for BackupCraft's own servers and agents and for public servers (RFC 8446, 5246)

  Own deployments (both sides): TLS 1.3, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 · X25519 · Ed25519
  certificates (own CA) · mutual authentication · HelloRetryRequest · KeyUpdate.
  Public servers (client side, Trust::System): also TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, RSA / ECDSA
  certificates of the system's CAs, and TLS 1.2 with ECDHE (X25519) and AEAD suites.
  Not here: PSK / resumption, 0-RTT, renegotiation, revocation checks.

  connect(stream, ClientConfig) -> TlsStream     accept(stream, ServerConfig) -> TlsStream
  TlsStream implements Stream (HTTP runs over it unchanged); peer_certs() after the handshake
  Trust::Anchors(CAs) / Pinned(SHA-256 of the leaf) / Any (trust on first use: the caller
  shows the fingerprint and pins it) / System(extra CAs) (the operating system's CAs)

conn.rs is the I/O-free core (feed bytes, take bytes); this file drives it over a Stream.
```

- **`struct Identity`**
  a certificate chain (DER, leaf first) and the leaf's private key
  - `chain: Vec<Vec<u8>>`
  - `key: Keypair`

- **`enum Trust`**
  - `Anchors(Vec<Cert>)` -- certificates issued by one of these CAs
  - `Pinned(Vec<[u8; 32]>)` -- exactly these leaf certificates (SHA-256 of the DER)
  - `Any` -- anything (only to read the fingerprint for a trust decision)
  - `System(Vec<Cert>)` -- the operating system's certificate authorities, and these as well (a company CA);
    allows TLS 1.2 and the public suites (crate::roots)

- **`struct ClientConfig`**
  - `trust: Trust`
  - `identity: Option<Identity>`
  - `server_name: String` -- the name the certificate must carry (DNS name or IP address); may be empty only with
    Trust::Pinned / Trust::Any, which do not check it

- **`struct ServerConfig`**
  - `identity: Identity`
  - `client_auth: Option<Trust>` -- ask for a client certificate trusted like this
  - `client_auth_optional: bool` -- a client without a certificate is accepted too (one that sends one must pass the
    check); for a port that consoles and agents share

- **`enum TlsError`**
  - `Alert(u8, &'static str)` -- we ended the connection with this alert
  - `PeerAlert(u8)` -- the peer ended it with this alert
  - `Net(NetError)`
  - `Closed`

- **`fn alert_name(a: u8) -> String`**

- **`struct TlsStream`**
  TLS over a stream

**`impl TlsStream`**

- **`fn peer_certs(&self) -> Vec<Cert>`**
  the peer's certificate chain (leaf first)
- **`fn last_error(&self) -> Option<TlsError>`**
- **`fn version(&self) -> (&'static str, u16)`**
  "TLS 1.3" / "TLS 1.2" and the cipher suite number

- **`fn connect(inner: Box<dyn Stream>, cfg: ClientConfig) -> Result<TlsStream, TlsError>`**
  client side: handshake over `inner`

- **`fn accept(inner: Box<dyn Stream>, cfg: ServerConfig) -> Result<TlsStream, TlsError>`**
  server side: handshake over `inner`

### `netio/tls/conn.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/tls/conn.rs`](../lib/netio/tls/conn.rs)

```text
conn -- the TLS handshake and the record stream, without I/O

  Conn::client(cfg) / Conn::server(cfg)
  feed(bytes)          bytes from the peer (any split)
  take_out() -> bytes  to send to the peer
  read_plain / write_plain / close
  established(), peer_cert(), version(), suite()

Our own servers and agents (private PKI): TLS 1.3 with TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, X25519,
Ed25519 signatures and certificates, a HelloRetryRequest when the client offered X25519
without a key share (or a cookie), mutual authentication.  The server side speaks only that.

A client that trusts the system's certificate authorities (Trust::System: mail servers,
update servers, web hooks) also offers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, RSA (PKCS #1 v1.5 / PSS) and
ECDSA (P-256 / P-384) signatures and the P-256 key exchange (after a HelloRetryRequest),
and falls back to TLS 1.2 with ECDHE (X25519 or P-256) and AEAD suites (AES-128-GCM,
ChaCha20-Poly1305), the extended master secret and the TLS 1.3 downgrade check.  Private
connections never fall back.

No PSK, no 0-RTT, no session tickets (a client ignores them), no renegotiation;
post-handshake KeyUpdate is supported.  Every protocol error ends the connection with the
matching alert.
```

```rust
AL_CLOSE_NOTIFY: u8 = 0
AL_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE: u8 = 10
AL_BAD_RECORD_MAC: u8 = 20
AL_RECORD_OVERFLOW: u8 = 22
AL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE: u8 = 40
AL_BAD_CERTIFICATE: u8 = 42
AL_UNSUPPORTED_CERTIFICATE: u8 = 43
AL_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED: u8 = 45
AL_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER: u8 = 47
AL_UNKNOWN_CA: u8 = 48
AL_DECODE_ERROR: u8 = 50
AL_DECRYPT_ERROR: u8 = 51
AL_PROTOCOL_VERSION: u8 = 70
AL_INTERNAL_ERROR: u8 = 80
AL_NO_RENEGOTIATION: u8 = 100
AL_MISSING_EXTENSION: u8 = 109
AL_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED: u8 = 116
```

- **`fn client(cfg: ClientConfig) -> Conn`**
- **`fn server(cfg: ServerConfig) -> Conn`**

- **`fn closed(&self) -> bool`**
