### `netio/tls/record.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/tls/record.rs`](../lib/netio/tls/record.rs)

```text
record -- the TLS record layer: TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446) and, for public servers, TLS 1.2 (RFC
5246 with AEAD suites only: RFC 5288 AES-GCM, RFC 7905 ChaCha20-Poly1305)

  plaintext record    type | 0x0303 | length | fragment          (handshake before keys,
                                                                   alerts, CCS)
  TLS 1.3 protected   23 | 0x0303 | length | AEAD(content ‖ type ‖ zero padding)
                      nonce = IV xor sequence number, additional data = the record header
  TLS 1.2 protected   type | 0x0303 | length | [explicit nonce (GCM)] AEAD(content)
                      additional data = sequence ‖ type ‖ 0x0303 ‖ content length;
                      GCM nonce = 4-byte salt ‖ explicit 8 bytes (we send the sequence),
                      ChaCha20 nonce = IV xor sequence number
```

```rust
CHANGE_CIPHER_SPEC: u8 = 20
ALERT: u8 = 21
HANDSHAKE: u8 = 22
APPLICATION_DATA: u8 = 23
/// the largest plaintext fragment
MAX_PLAIN: usize = 1 << 14
/// the largest record body on the wire (protected: plaintext + type + tag, some slack)
MAX_RECORD: usize = MAX_PLAIN + 256
/// the cipher suites (TLS 1.3, then TLS 1.2 ECDHE)
TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256: u16 = 0x1301
TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256: u16 = 0x1303
ECDHE_ECDSA_AES128_GCM: u16 = 0xC02B
ECDHE_RSA_AES128_GCM: u16 = 0xC02F
ECDHE_RSA_CHACHA20: u16 = 0xCCA8
ECDHE_ECDSA_CHACHA20: u16 = 0xCCA9
```

- **`fn key_iv_len(suite: u16) -> Option<(usize, usize)>`**
  key and IV lengths of a suite (TLS 1.2: the IV is the implicit part)

- **`struct Cipher`**

**`impl Cipher`**

- **`fn new(key: [u8; 32], iv: [u8; 12]) -> Cipher`**

  the keys of a suite (key and IV of key_iv_len); None for an unknown suite

```text
trust -- https to a server with its own private CA (Ed25519): the client either has the CA

the user decide (trust on first use, like SSH host keys)
```

### `netio/x509.rs`

Source: [`lib/netio/x509.rs`](../lib/netio/x509.rs)

```text
x509 -- certificates (RFC 5280): the private PKI of BackupCraft (Ed25519, RFC 8410; built
and signed here) and the public web PKI (RSA and P-256 / P-384 keys; RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 / PSS
and ECDSA signatures with SHA-256 / 384 / 512), parsed strictly

  Cert::parse(der) -> Option<Cert>        subject / issuer, validity, key, CA flag, names,
                                          key and extended key usage, name constraints,
                                          unknown critical extensions noticed
  cert.fingerprint() -> SHA-256 (hex)     cert.signed_by(&issuer) -> bool
  cert.verify(alg, data, sig)             a signature made with the certificate's key
  verify_chain(&[leaf, ...], &anchors, now, name, usage) -> Result<(), String>   builds a
                                          path through the given intermediates to an anchor
  CertBuilder { .. }.sign(&issuer_cert_or_self, &issuer_key) -> DER

Not checked: revocation (CRL / OCSP), certificate policies; name constraints cover DNS
names and IP addresses (the names a TLS server is reached by).
```

```rust
OID_ED25519: &[u64] = &[1, 3, 101, 112]
/// key usage bits as they appear in the first byte
KU_DIGITAL_SIGNATURE: u8 = 0x80
KU_KEY_CERT_SIGN: u8 = 0x04

```

## netpkt

*network packets byte for byte: addresses, checksums, Ethernet to TCP codecs, DHCP, DNS, NTP, syslog, a dissector, pcapng* -- crate root [`lib/netpkt/lib.rs`](../lib/netpkt/lib.rs)

```text
netpkt -- network packets byte for byte: addresses, checksums, header codecs, a dissector
and capture files.  No I/O, no clock, no randomness: everything is deterministic and works
on every target (simulators, packet tools, tests).

  addr      Mac, Ipv4, Ipv6, IpAddr, Prefix4, Prefix6, wildcard_match
  checksum  Internet checksum (sum / finish / verify / pseudo_v4 / pseudo_v6 / update16),
            crc32 (Ethernet FCS)
  pkt       Pkt: a buffer with headroom, headers are prepended in place
  eth       Ethernet II (EthView, EthHdr), 802.1Q tags (VlanTag, tag_of, tagged, untagged,
            L2), 802.2 LLC
  arp       ArpView, Arp (request / reply / probe / announce)          (RFC 826, 5227)
  ipv4      Ipv4View, Ipv4Hdr, dec_ttl, fragment, Reassembly           (RFC 791, 1624)
  ipv6      Ipv6View, Ipv6Hdr, upper_layer / ext_headers (extension header walk),
            FragHdr, fragment, Reassembly6                             (RFC 8200, 5722)
  icmp      IcmpView, Icmp, error_quote, name                          (RFC 792, 1191)
  udp       UdpView, UdpHdr (push_v4 / push_v6 with checksum)          (RFC 768)
  tcp       TcpView, TcpHdr, TcpOpts (MSS, WS, SACK, TS), seq_lt ...   (RFC 9293, 7323, 2018)
  dhcp      DhcpView, Dhcp with typed options (Opt), MsgType           (RFC 2131, 2132, 3046)
  dns       Message, Header, Question, Rr, RData, names with compression   (RFC 1035, 3596)
  ntp       NtpView, Ntp, Ts (32.32 timestamps), offset_delay           (RFC 5905)
  syslog    pri / bsd / ios formatting, parse                           (RFC 3164, IOS)
  decode    stack / proto_mask / layers / info: layers with fields and byte ranges for
            packet inspectors, P_* bits for filters, one-line summaries
  pcapng    Writer (section, interfaces, enhanced packets), read
  http      HTTP/1.1 without I/O: Parser (fed as bytes arrive, says when it needs more),
            Head, Headers, framing, encode_request / encode_response / chunks (RFC 9112)
  stp       BPDUs of STP and RSTP: Configuration, TCN and RST BPDUs with their flags,
            BridgeId, PortId, path_cost, the 802.3 / LLC frame (802.1D-1998, 802.1D-2004)
  rip       RipView, Rip, Rte, Auth: RIP requests and responses, version 2 and 1, the
            authentication entry recognised                       (RFC 2453, 1058)
  nat       address and port translation in place: Flow (what translation and filters look
            at), rewrite / rewrite_quoted with incremental checksums (RFC 3022, 1624, 5508)
  icmpv6    Icmp6View, Icmp6 (echo and the errors with their quote), Nd: router and neighbor
            solicitations and advertisements, redirects, their options (link-layer
            addresses, prefix information, MTU); error_quote, name   (RFC 4443, 4861, 4862)
  ospf      OspfView, Packet (Hello, Database Description, Link State Request, Update,
            Acknowledgment), LsaHeader, Lsa (router, network, summary, AS-external) with the
            Fletcher checksum, compare (which instance is newer)      (RFC 2328, RFC 905)
  addrsel   destination address selection: scope, the default policy table (precedence,
            label), Dest and sort, the order getaddrinfo tries addresses in   (RFC 6724)
  eapol     EapolView, Key: EAPOL-Key frames of the 4-way handshake (Key Information bits,
            replay counter, nonces, MIC field, key data), the RSN element, KDEs (GTK,
            IGTK); mic_input / set_mic for the caller's MIC (802.1X-2004, 802.11-2020 12.7)
  bgp       BGP-4 messages: frame (a message out of a TCP stream), BgpView, Message (OPEN with
            capabilities, UPDATE with its path attributes, NOTIFICATION, KEEPALIVE,
            ROUTE-REFRESH), BgpErr (the NOTIFICATION a receiver sends)   (RFC 4271, 5492,
            6793, 2918, 1997, 4486)
  tftp      TftpView, Packet (RRQ, WRQ, DATA, ACK, ERROR, OACK) with their options, error
            codes, netascii, looks_like (a transfer away from port 69)  (RFC 1350, 2347-2349)
  ftp       Command, Reply (multi-line), Lines, ReplyReader, host_port (PORT, 227), eprt,
            epsv_port (229), the reply texts as the server's own words  (RFC 959, 2428, 2389)

Views (XxxView::parse) check lengths once and then read fields without copying; records
(XxxHdr, Arp, Icmp) write headers, usually with push_onto / push_v4 into a Pkt.  Multi-byte
fields are big endian (network order); be16 / be32 / put16 / put32 below read and write them.
```

```text
addr -- link and network addresses: MAC, IPv4, IPv6, prefixes

  Mac([u8; 6])        parse "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff" / "aa-bb-.." / "aabb.ccdd.eeff"; Display with
                      colons, cisco() with dots; broadcast / multicast / local bits; EUI-64
  Ipv4([u8; 4])       strict dotted decimal (no leading zeros); masks <-> prefix lengths;
                      class tests (private, loopback, link local, multicast, broadcast)
  Ipv6([u8; 16])      every RFC 4291 text form in, RFC 5952 out; solicited-node and

  IpAddr              V4 | V6
  Prefix4 / Prefix6   an address with a prefix length ("10.0.0.1/24"): network, broadcast,
                      contains, host range (/31 and /32 per RFC 3021); masks and wildcards
  wildcard_match      ACL matching with any (also non-contiguous) wildcard mask

These are value types for packets, not OS socket addresses (those are plat::net's).
```

### `netpkt/checksum.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/checksum.rs`](../lib/netpkt/checksum.rs)

```text
checksum -- the Internet checksum (RFC 1071, 1624) and the Ethernet CRC-32

  sum(acc, data) -> u32          ones' complement sum of 16-bit big-endian words; only the
                                 last piece of a message may have an odd length
  finish(acc) -> u16             the checksum to write (complement of the folded sum)
  checksum(data) -> u16          finish(sum(0, data))
  verify(data) -> bool           a block that contains its checksum sums to 0xFFFF
  pseudo_v4 / pseudo_v6          the pseudo-header sums of UDP, TCP and ICMPv6
  update16(ck, old, new) -> u16  incremental update after a 16-bit field changed (RFC 1624)
  crc32(data) -> u32             IEEE 802.3 FCS (reflected 0x04C11DB7, as zlib)
  update(ck, old, new) -> u16    incremental update after a run of bytes changed (an address,
                                 a whole quoted packet): update16 for every word that differs
```

- **`fn sum(acc: u32, data: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  adds `data` to a running ones' complement sum (the result is folded to 17 bits at most)

- **`fn fold(acc: u32) -> u16`**
  folds a sum to 16 bits (without the final complement)

- **`fn finish(acc: u32) -> u16`**
  the checksum value to store: the complement of the folded sum

- **`fn checksum(data: &[u8]) -> u16`**
  the Internet checksum of a block

- **`fn verify(data: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  a block that includes its checksum field is intact

- **`fn pseudo_v4(src: Ipv4, dst: Ipv4, proto: u8, len: u16) -> u32`**
  the IPv4 pseudo header of UDP / TCP: addresses, protocol, length of the segment

- **`fn pseudo_v6(src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6, next: u8, len: u32) -> u32`**
  the IPv6 pseudo header (RFC 8200 8.1): addresses, upper-layer length, next header

- **`fn update16(ck: u16, old: u16, new: u16) -> u16`**
  the new checksum after one 16-bit word changed from `old` to `new` (RFC 1624 eqn. 3)

- **`fn crc32(data: &[u8]) -> u32`**
  CRC-32 of IEEE 802.3 (the Ethernet frame check sequence; also zlib's and PNG's)

- **`fn update(ck: u16, old: &[u8], new: &[u8]) -> u16`**
  the new checksum after the bytes `old` became `new` (of the same length, starting at an even
  offset of the data the checksum covers; an odd last byte is the high byte of its word, as
  in sum): RFC 1624 eqn. 3 for every 16-bit word that changed

### `netpkt/decode.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/decode.rs`](../lib/netpkt/decode.rs)

```text
decode -- dissects a frame into layers for packet inspectors and event filters

  stack(frame) -> Stack          the protocol layers and their header ranges, no allocation
  proto_mask(frame) -> u32       P_* bits of every layer present (for event filters)
  stack_ip / ip_mask(packet)     the same for a bare IP packet (serial lines, tunnels)
  layers(frame) -> Vec<Layer>    per layer: title, fields with byte ranges (for a hex view),
                                 problems (bad checksum, truncated header, ...)
  info(frame) -> (Proto, String) the top protocol and a one-line summary like a capture tool
                                 ("Echo (ping) request id=0x0001, seq=1, ttl=64")

Application protocols are recognised by their well-known ports.  DHCP (fixed fields and
every option), DNS (header, questions and records, also over TCP), NTP and syslog have
dissectors; the payload of the others shows as one field.
BPDUs of STP and RSTP (LLC SAP 0x42) show every field and flag (stp.rs).
Field names and values follow the usual capture-tool wording (English protocol terms).
HTTP (ports 80, 8080, 8000, and any TCP segment that starts like a request or a response)
shows the start line, the header lines and the body bytes of every message the segment
holds; a segment in the middle of a message is a "Continuation".
RIP (port 520) shows its header and one field per entry (route, authentication, the request
for the whole table) with the problems a receiver would refuse (RFC 2453, RFC 1058).
IPv6 shows its extension headers as fields of its layer (a later fragment carries data only);
ICMPv6 every field of echo, the errors (with the quoted packet) and Neighbor Discovery (RS, RA,
NS, NA, redirect and one field per option) with what a receiver refuses: a checksum over the
pseudo header that does not fit, an ND message whose hop limit is not 255 (RFC 4443, 4861).
OSPF (IP protocol 89) shows the common header, the fields of the five packet types, every LSA
header and the links, routers and metrics of the LSAs an update carries, with what a receiver
refuses: another version, a wrong packet or LSA checksum, bodies that do not fit (RFC 2328).
EAPOL (ethertype 0x888E) shows its header and an EAPOL-Key body field by field: the Key
Information bits, replay counter, nonce, MIC and the key data (the RSN element and, when it is
not encrypted, the KDEs); the summary names the message of the 4-way handshake (eapol.rs).
BGP (TCP port 179) shows every message a segment holds: the header, the fields of OPEN with each
capability, UPDATE with each withdrawn route, path attribute (its flags and value) and NLRI,
NOTIFICATION with the names of its code and subcode, ROUTE-REFRESH; what a receiver would answer
with a NOTIFICATION is a problem with that code; a segment that does not start with the marker
is the rest of a message of an earlier one (bgp.rs; AS numbers of 2 or 4 octets as
bgp::as_path_4 guesses).
TFTP (port 69, and the DATA, ACK, ERROR and OACK packets of a transfer between two ports
above 1023 by their shape: RFC 1350 moves a transfer to new ports) shows its opcode, file,
mode, options, block, data and error (tftp.rs).  FTP (TCP port 21) shows each command line
with its verb and argument and each reply line with its code; FTP-DATA (port 20, the active
data connections) its bytes; passive data connections run between two free ports and show
as TCP data (ftp.rs).
```

```rust
P_ETH: u32 = 1 << 0
P_VLAN: u32 = 1 << 1
P_LLC: u32 = 1 << 2
P_ARP: u32 = 1 << 3
P_IPV4: u32 = 1 << 4
P_IPV6: u32 = 1 << 5
P_ICMP: u32 = 1 << 6
P_ICMPV6: u32 = 1 << 7
P_IGMP: u32 = 1 << 8
P_UDP: u32 = 1 << 9
P_TCP: u32 = 1 << 10
P_DHCP: u32 = 1 << 11
P_DNS: u32 = 1 << 12
P_HTTP: u32 = 1 << 13
P_TLS: u32 = 1 << 14
P_SSH: u32 = 1 << 15
P_STP: u32 = 1 << 16
P_RIP: u32 = 1 << 17
P_OSPF: u32 = 1 << 18
P_NTP: u32 = 1 << 19
P_SYSLOG: u32 = 1 << 20
P_TFTP: u32 = 1 << 21
P_SNMP: u32 = 1 << 22
P_LLDP: u32 = 1 << 23
P_DHCPV6: u32 = 1 << 24
P_EAPOL: u32 = 1 << 25
/// BGP (TCP port 179); a bit far from the next free ones, which other protocols take in order
P_BGP: u32 = 1 << 30
/// FTP's control connection and its active data connections (FTP-DATA)
P_FTP: u32 = 1 << 26
P_DATA: u32 = 1 << 31
```

**`impl Proto`**

- **`struct Stack`**
  the layers of a frame: protocol, header offset and header length (the application layer
  and Data cover their payload)

### `netpkt/dhcp.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/dhcp.rs`](../lib/netpkt/dhcp.rs)

```text
dhcp -- the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv4 (RFC 2131; options RFC 2132, long
options RFC 3396, relay agent information RFC 3046)

  DhcpView::parse(b)     the fixed BOOTP part (236 bytes) and the magic cookie; fields
                         without copying; options() walks the options (pad skipped, end
                         stops; with option 52 the file and sname fields follow); opt(code)
                         the first instance of an option; msg_type()
  Dhcp { op, htype, hlen, hops, xid, secs, flags, ciaddr, yiaddr, siaddr, giaddr, chaddr,
         sname, file, opts: Vec<Opt> }
                         read(&view) (repeated options are joined, RFC 3396) / to_bytes(min)
                         (options in their order, long ones split, end, zero padding up to
                         `min` bytes: BOOTP_MIN for the 300 bytes most clients and servers
                         send) / new(op, xid, chaddr) / get(code) / set(opt) / mac()
  Opt                    MsgType, SubnetMask, Routers, DnsServers, HostName, DomainName,
                         RequestedIp, LeaseTime, ServerId, Params, Message, MaxSize, T1, T2,
                         ClientId, RelayInfo, BroadcastAddr, NtpServers, Other(code, bytes)
  MsgType                Discover .. Inform; name()
  option_name(code)      "Subnet Mask", "Router", ... for dissectors

An option whose length does not fit its type is kept as Other(code, bytes), so reading and
writing a message gives the same bytes.
```

  - `T2(u32)` -- rebinding time in seconds

### `netpkt/dns.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/dns.rs`](../lib/netpkt/dns.rs)

```text
dns -- the Domain Name System message format (RFC 1035; AAAA RFC 3596; negative answers
RFC 2308; the EDNS(0) OPT record of RFC 6891 is kept as raw data)

  Header { id, qr, opcode, aa, tc, rd, ra, ad, cd, rcode }   flags() / from_flags(id, f)
  Question { name, qtype, qclass }
  Rr { name, rtype, class, ttl, data: RData }      Rr::new(name, ttl, data)
  RData            A, Aaaa, Ns, Cname, Ptr, Mx { pref, host }, Soa(Soa), Txt(strings),
                   Other(bytes); rtype() / text()
  Message { header, questions, answers, authority, additional }
                   parse(b) (names with compression pointers; loops, forward pointers and
                   names over 255 bytes are refused) / to_bytes() (names compressed against
                   earlier ones, RFC 1035 4.1.4) / to_bytes_max(limit) -> (bytes, truncated):
                   whole records only, TC set when something was left out /
                   query(id, name, qtype, rd) / reply_to(&query)
  read_name(msg, off) -> Option<(String, usize)> / write_name(out, name, &mut Compressor)
  name_eq / is_subdomain(name, zone) / parent(name) / reverse_v4(ip) / parse_reverse_v4
  TYPE_* / CLASS_IN / RCODE_* / OPCODE_QUERY; type_name / type_by_name / rcode_name

Names are text without the final dot ("www.example.com"; the root is ""); a dot or a
backslash inside a label and bytes outside printable ASCII are written \. \\ \DDD as in
zone files.  Comparisons ignore ASCII case (RFC 4343).
```

```rust
DNS_HDR: usize = 12
/// the largest answer over UDP without EDNS (RFC 1035 4.2.1)
UDP_MAX: usize = 512
TYPE_A: u16 = 1
TYPE_NS: u16 = 2
TYPE_CNAME: u16 = 5
TYPE_SOA: u16 = 6
TYPE_PTR: u16 = 12
TYPE_MX: u16 = 15
TYPE_TXT: u16 = 16
TYPE_AAAA: u16 = 28
TYPE_SRV: u16 = 33
TYPE_OPT: u16 = 41
TYPE_ANY: u16 = 255
CLASS_IN: u16 = 1
OPCODE_QUERY: u8 = 0
RCODE_NOERROR: u8 = 0
RCODE_FORMERR: u8 = 1
RCODE_SERVFAIL: u8 = 2
RCODE_NXDOMAIN: u8 = 3
RCODE_NOTIMP: u8 = 4
RCODE_REFUSED: u8 = 5
```

- **`fn type_name(t: u16) -> String`**
  "A", "MX", ... ("TYPE99" for others, RFC 3597)

- **`fn type_by_name(s: &str) -> Option<u16>`**
  the type of a mnemonic ("a", "MX", "TYPE99")

- **`fn rcode_name(r: u8) -> &'static str`**
  "NOERROR", "NXDOMAIN", ...

- **`enum DnsErr`**
  why a message could not be read
  - `Short` -- it ends inside a header, a name or a record
  - `BadName` -- a label, a pointer or the length of a name is wrong
  - `BadRecord` -- the data of a record does not fit its type or length

- **`struct Header`**
  the fixed header
  - `id: u16`
  - `qr: bool` -- a response
  - `opcode: u8`
  - `aa: bool` -- authoritative answer
  - `tc: bool` -- truncated
  - `rd: bool` -- recursion desired
  - `ra: bool` -- recursion available
  - `ad: bool` -- authentic data (DNSSEC)
  - `cd: bool` -- checking disabled (DNSSEC)
  - `rcode: u8`

**`impl Header`**

- **`fn flags(&self) -> u16`**
  the 16 flag bits
- **`fn from_flags(id: u16, f: u16) -> Header`**

- **`struct Question`**
  - `name: String`
  - `qtype: u16`
  - `qclass: u16`

- **`struct Soa`**
  the data of a start of authority record
  - `mname: String` -- the primary name server
  - `rname: String` -- the mailbox of the responsible person (the first dot is the @)
  - `serial: u32`
  - `refresh: u32`
  - `retry: u32`
  - `expire: u32`
  - `minimum: u32` -- the TTL of negative answers (RFC 2308)

- **`enum RData`**
  the data of a resource record
  - `A(Ipv4)`
  - `Aaaa(Ipv6)`
  - `Ns(String)`
  - `Cname(String)`
  - `Ptr(String)`
  - `Mx { pref: u16, host: String }`
  - `Soa(Soa)`
  - `Txt(Vec<Vec<u8>>)` -- character strings of up to 255 bytes each
  - `Other(Vec<u8>)` -- any other type, as it was on the wire

**`impl RData`**

- **`fn rtype(&self) -> Option<u16>`**
  the record type of the data (None for Other)
- **`fn text(&self) -> String`**
  the data in zone-file form ("10.0.0.1", "10 mail.example.com", "\\"text\\"")

- **`struct Rr`**
  a resource record
  - `name: String`
  - `rtype: u16`
  - `class: u16`
  - `ttl: u32`
  - `data: RData`

**`impl Rr`**

- **`fn new(name: &str, ttl: u32, data: RData) -> Rr`**
  a record of class IN; the type follows the data

- **`struct Message`**
  a whole message
  - `header: Header`
  - `questions: Vec<Question>`
  - `answers: Vec<Rr>`
  - `authority: Vec<Rr>`
  - `additional: Vec<Rr>`

- **`fn labels(name: &str) -> Option<Vec<Vec<u8>>>`**
  the labels of a name in text form (None: empty label, label over 63 bytes, name over 255
  bytes on the wire, bad escape)

- **`fn read_name(msg: &[u8], off: usize) -> Option<(String, usize)>`**
  the name at `off` of a message and the offset after it (where the name ends in place, not
  where a pointer led)

- **`struct Compressor`**
  remembers where names were written so later names can point there (RFC 1035 4.1.4)
  - `off: bool` -- off: every name is written in full

**`impl Compressor`**

- **`fn new() -> Compressor`**
- **`fn forget_from(&mut self, off: usize)`**
  forgets the names written at `off` or later (the output was cut back there)

- **`fn write_name(out: &mut Vec<u8>, name: &str, c: &mut Compressor) -> bool`**
  appends a name in wire form (with pointers to earlier names when the compressor allows);
  false when the name is not valid

- **`fn name_eq(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool`**
  two names are the same (ASCII case ignored)

- **`fn is_subdomain(name: &str, zone: &str) -> bool`**
  `name` is `zone` or lies below it ("www.lab" in "lab"; every name lies in the root "")

- **`fn parent(name: &str) -> &str`**
  the name without its first label ("lab" for "www.lab", "" for "lab")

- **`fn reverse_v4(ip: Ipv4) -> String`**
  the PTR name of an address ("4.3.2.1.in-addr.arpa")

- **`fn parse_reverse_v4(name: &str) -> Option<Ipv4>`**
  the address of a PTR name ("4.3.2.1.in-addr.arpa" -> 1.2.3.4)

**`impl Message`**

- **`fn query(id: u16, name: &str, qtype: u16, rd: bool) -> Message`**
  a query for one name
- **`fn reply_to(q: &Message) -> Message`**
  an empty response to a query: same id, opcode, question and recursion wish
- **`fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Message, DnsErr>`**
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the message in wire form, names compressed
- **`fn to_bytes_max(&self, limit: usize) -> (Vec<u8>, bool)`**
  at most `limit` bytes: records that do not fit are left out whole and TC is set
  (RFC 2181 9: true when something was left out); a record with an invalid name is
  skipped

### `netpkt/eth.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/eth.rs`](../lib/netpkt/eth.rs)

```text
eth -- Ethernet II frames, IEEE 802.1Q tags and 802.2 LLC

  EthView::parse(frame)       dst, src, ethertype (or 802.3 length), payload
  EthHdr { dst, src, ethertype }  write / push_onto(&mut Pkt)
  VlanTag { pcp, dei, vid }   tag_of(frame), tagged(frame, tag), untagged(frame)
  L2::parse(frame)            dst, src, the 802.1Q tag if any, the inner ethertype and where
                              the payload starts
  Llc                         802.2 LLC header of 802.3 frames (STP uses DSAP/SSAP 0x42)
  pad(frame)                  pads to the 60-byte minimum (without FCS)

Frames here never carry the FCS; checksum::crc32 computes it when someone wants to see it.
```

```rust
ETH_HDR: usize = 14
VLAN_TAG: usize = 4
/// the shortest frame without FCS
ETH_MIN: usize = 60
/// the largest payload of a standard frame
ETH_MTU: usize = 1500
ET_IPV4: u16 = 0x0800
ET_ARP: u16 = 0x0806
ET_VLAN: u16 = 0x8100
ET_IPV6: u16 = 0x86DD
ET_QINQ: u16 = 0x88A8
ET_LLDP: u16 = 0x88CC
/// IEEE 802.1X (EAPOL: the 4-way handshake of WPA2 and WPA3)
ET_EAPOL: u16 = 0x888E
```

### `netpkt/ipv4.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/ipv4.rs`](../lib/netpkt/ipv4.rs)

```text
ipv4 -- the IPv4 header (RFC 791), fragmentation and reassembly

  Ipv4View::parse(b)     version 4, IHL >= 5, total length within the buffer (trailing bytes,
                         e.g. Ethernet padding, are ignored by payload())
  Ipv4Hdr { .. }         write(out, payload_len) fills length and checksum; push_onto(&mut Pkt)
  dec_ttl(hdr) -> u8     TTL - 1 in place with an incremental checksum update (RFC 1624)
  fragment(pkt, mtu)     splits a packet into fragments of at most `mtu` bytes (None when DF
                         is set and the packet is too large); options with the copy flag go
                         into every fragment
  Reassembly             collects fragments of one datagram (no timers: the caller expires
                         it after its own timeout)
```

```rust
IPV4_MAX_OPTS: usize = 40

PROTO_TCP: u8 = 6

PROTO_ESP: u8 = 50
PROTO_AH: u8 = 51
PROTO_ICMPV6: u8 = 58
PROTO_OSPF: u8 = 89
PROTO_VRRP: u8 = 112
```

### `netpkt/ipv6.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/ipv6.rs`](../lib/netpkt/ipv6.rs)

```text
ipv6 -- the IPv6 fixed header (RFC 8200), the walk over extension headers, the fragment
header, fragmentation and reassembly

  Ipv6View::parse(b)    version 6, payload length within the buffer
  Ipv6View::parse_truncated(b)   a packet that may be cut after its header (the quote inside
                        an ICMPv6 error): payload() ends at the end of the buffer
  Ipv6Hdr { .. }        write(out, payload_len), push_onto(&mut Pkt)
  upper_layer(v)        (next header, offset in the payload) after hop-by-hop, routing,
                        fragment and destination options headers
  ext_headers(v)        the extension headers in order (type, offset, length, next header);
                        None for a malformed chain
  FragHdr / frag(v)     the fragment header (offset in bytes, more fragments, identification)
                        and where it sits
  fragment(pkt, mtu, id)  fragments of at most `mtu` bytes with a fragment header (RFC 8200
                        4.5: the unfragmentable part -- the header, hop-by-hop and routing
                        headers -- in front of each); None when even one 8-byte unit does
                        not fit
  Reassembly6           collects the fragments of one packet; overlapping fragments drop the
                        whole packet (RFC 5722); no timers: the caller expires it after 60 s
  dec_hop_limit(pkt)    hop limit - 1 in place (IPv6 has no header checksum)

ICMPv6 and Neighbor Discovery are in icmpv6.rs; the addresses of ND (solicited-node groups,
EUI-64 interface identifiers, multicast MACs) in addr.rs.
```

```rust
IPV6_HDR: usize = 40
/// the minimum link MTU of IPv6 (RFC 8200 5)
MIN_MTU: usize = 1280
/// the length of the fragment header
FRAG_HDR: usize = 8
NH_HOPOPT: u8 = 0
NH_TCP: u8 = 6
NH_UDP: u8 = 17
NH_ROUTING: u8 = 43
NH_FRAGMENT: u8 = 44
NH_ESP: u8 = 50
NH_AH: u8 = 51
NH_ICMPV6: u8 = 58
NH_NONE: u8 = 59
NH_DSTOPTS: u8 = 60
```

- **`fn ext_name(nh: u8) -> Option<&'static str>`**
  a name for an extension header type ("Hop-by-Hop Options", "Fragment", ...)

  the payload up to the payload length (or the end of a truncated quote)
- **`fn packet(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
  header and payload, without trailing padding

- **`fn upper_layer(v: &Ipv6View) -> Option<(u8, usize)>`**
  the upper-layer protocol and its offset in the payload, after the extension headers;
  None for a malformed chain

- **`struct ExtHdr`**
  one extension header of a packet
  - `kind: u8` -- its type (the Next Header value that announced it)
  - `off: usize` -- offset and length in the payload

  - `next: u8` -- the Next Header field it carries

  the extension headers of a packet in order; None for a malformed chain

- **`struct FragHdr`**
  the fragment header of a packet
  - `next: u8`

**`impl FragHdr`**

- **`fn read(b: &[u8]) -> FragHdr`**

- **`fn frag(v: &Ipv6View) -> Option<(FragHdr, usize)>`**

- **`fn fragment(packet: &[u8], mtu: usize, id: u32) -> Option<Vec<Vec<u8>>>`**
  splits a packet into fragments of at most `mtu` bytes (RFC 8200 4.5); a packet that fits
  comes back alone.  None when the packet is malformed, is a fragment already, or not even
  one 8-byte unit of data fits.

- **`fn dec_hop_limit(pkt: &mut [u8]) -> u8`**
  lowers the hop limit by one in place; the new value

- **`enum ReasmErr`**
  why a fragment could not be taken (the receiver answers the first two with a Parameter
  Problem, RFC 8200 4.5)
  - `BadLength` -- a fragment with more to come whose data is not a multiple of 8 bytes (pointer: the
    Payload Length field)
  - `TooLong` -- offset and length go beyond 65535 bytes (pointer: the Fragment Offset field)
  - `Overlap` -- it overlaps a fragment already held: the whole packet is dropped (RFC 5722)

- **`struct Reassembly6`**
  the fragments of one packet (key: source, destination, identification)

- **`fn reassembly_key(v: &Ipv6View, f: &FragHdr) -> (Ipv6, Ipv6, u32)`**
  the reassembly key of a fragment

  adds a fragment (`at`: the offset of its fragment header in the payload); Ok(Some(the
  complete packet)) when all parts are there
- **`fn has_first(&self) -> bool`**
  the first fragment (offset 0) is here: a timeout is answered with Time Exceeded
- **`fn first_packet(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the source and header of the first fragment (what a timeout's error quotes)

  bytes collected so far

  an IPv6 fixed header to write

  - `hop_limit: u8`
  - `src: Ipv6`
  - `dst: Ipv6`

- **`const LEN: usize = IPV6_HDR`**

- **`fn read(v: &Ipv6View) -> Ipv6Hdr`**

```text
  MODE_* / LI_*; mode_name
```

### `netpkt/pcapng.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/pcapng.rs`](../lib/netpkt/pcapng.rs)

```text
pcapng -- capture files in the pcapng format (IETF draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng), as Wireshark
reads them

  Writer::new(app)                 section header block (little endian, "app" as shb_userappl)
  add_interface(name, link, snap)  interface description block with nanosecond timestamps;
                                   returns the interface id
  packet(iface, t_ns, data)        enhanced packet block (with an optional comment)
  finish() -> Vec<u8>              the file
  read(bytes) -> Result<Capture>   section header, interfaces and enhanced / simple packet
                                   blocks of either byte order; other blocks are skipped

Timestamps are whatever the caller counts in nanoseconds (a simulator's virtual clock).
Link types: LINKTYPE_ETHERNET, LINKTYPE_C_HDLC (serial lines), LINKTYPE_RAW (bare IP).
```

```rust
LINKTYPE_ETHERNET: u16 = 1
/// bare IPv4 / IPv6 packets without a link header
LINKTYPE_RAW: u16 = 101
/// Cisco HDLC (address, control, an ethertype, the packet), as on serial lines
LINKTYPE_C_HDLC: u16 = 104
```

### `netpkt/pkt.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/pkt.rs`](../lib/netpkt/pkt.rs)

```text
pkt -- a packet buffer with headroom: headers are prepended in place

  Pkt::new(headroom, payload)     the payload behind `headroom` free bytes
  push(n) -> &mut [u8]            n more bytes at the front (the new header to fill in);
                                  grows the headroom when it runs out (a copy, still correct)
  pull(n) -> bool                 drops n bytes at the front (a header that was read)
  bytes() / bytes_mut() / len()   the packet from the current front
  extend(data) / truncate(len)    the tail
  into_vec()                      the packet alone

A segment is built once: payload first, then TCP, IP, VLAN and Ethernet headers in front of
it, without moving the payload.
```

```rust
/// room for Ethernet + 802.1Q + IPv4 with options + TCP with options (14 + 4 + 60 + 60)
HEADROOM: usize = 144
```

### `netpkt/http.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/http.rs`](../lib/netpkt/http.rs)

```text
http -- HTTP/1.1 messages byte for byte without I/O: an incremental parser that takes the
bytes as they arrive and says when it needs more, and the encoders of requests, responses
and chunks (RFC 9110, 9112), with the wire rules of lib/netio/http.rs

  Headers              header lines in order; names compare case-insensitively: get / set /
                       add / remove / has_token / content_length / chunked
  Version, Head        a start line with its headers: a request (method, target) or a
                       response (status, reason); Head::keep_alive / path
  Parser::requests() / responses()
                       push(bytes) -> Event: More (more bytes are needed), Head, Data (body
                       bytes as they came), End (the message is complete, with the trailers
                       of a chunked body); poll() gives the next event of bytes pushed before
                       (pipelined messages), finish() at the end of the connection (a
                       response body without a length ends there); expect(method) tells a
                       response parser which request it answers (HEAD: no body); idle,
                       buffered, framing, max_body
  Framing              how a body is delimited: None, Length(n), Chunked, UntilClose;
                       request_framing / response_framing after RFC 9112 6.3
  keep_alive(version, headers)   the connection stays open: HTTP/1.1 unless "Connection:
                       close", HTTP/1.0 only with "Connection: keep-alive"
  encode_request / encode_response / encode_head / encode_chunk / encode_chunked /
  encode_last_chunk    Content-Length or chunked as netio writes them; lines whose value has
                       CR or LF (or whose name has CR, LF or ':') are left out
  parse_head(bytes, request)  one head on its own (the dissector): Ok(Some(head)), Ok(None)
                       while it is incomplete; start_kind(bytes) tells a request from a
                       response from anything else
  reason(status), http_date(unix seconds) ("Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:00:00 GMT")

Limits: a head of at most 16 KiB (start line and header lines with their line ends) and 100
header lines (431), a request target of at most 8 KiB (414), chunk-size lines of at most 1024
bytes, bodies up to max_body (413).  Obsolete line folding, a header name with spaces or
control characters, a line that is not UTF-8, a Content-Length that is no number or differs
from another one, a request with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length, and a
Transfer-Encoding other than chunked are errors (400); a request of a version other than
HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 is 505.  Up to four empty lines before a start line are skipped; LF
alone ends a line too.  A response to HEAD, a 1xx, 204 or 304 response has no body; a
response without a length runs until the connection ends; a request without one has none.
```

```rust
MAX_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024
MAX_HEADERS: usize = 100
MAX_TARGET: usize = 8 * 1024
MAX_CHUNK_LINE: usize = 1024
/// the body limit of a new parser
MAX_BODY: u64 = 64 << 20
/// the last chunk of a chunked body without trailers
LAST_CHUNK: &[u8] = b"0\r\n\r\n"
```

- **`struct Headers(pub Vec<(String, String)>)`**
  header lines; names compare case-insensitively

**`impl Headers`**

- **`fn new() -> Headers`**
- **`fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str>`**
  the first value of a header
- **`fn set(&mut self, name: &str, value: &str)`**
  replaces (or adds) a header
- **`fn add(&mut self, name: &str, value: &str)`**
- **`fn remove(&mut self, name: &str)`**
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn has_token(&self, name: &str, token: &str) -> bool`**
  whether a comma-separated header names a token ("Connection: close")
- **`fn content_length(&self) -> Result<Option<u64>, HttpErr>`**
  the Content-Length: None without one, an error when it is no number or two differ
- **`fn chunked(&self) -> bool`**
  the body is chunked (Transfer-Encoding)

- **`enum Version`**
  the protocol version of a message
  - `Http10`
  - `Http11`

**`impl Version`**

- **`fn as_str(self) -> &'static str`**

- **`enum HttpErr`**
  why a message could not be read
  - `Bad(&'static str)` -- malformed (400), with what was wrong
  - `HeadTooLarge` -- a head over 16 KiB or with more than 100 header lines (431)
  - `UriTooLong` -- a request target over 8 KiB (414)
  - `Version` -- a request of a version other than HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 (505)
  - `BodyTooLarge` -- a body over the limit (413)
  - `Truncated` -- the connection ended in the middle of a message

**`impl HttpErr`**

- **`fn status(self) -> u16`**
  the status a server answers with
- **`fn text(self) -> &'static str`**
  what was wrong, in a few English words (dissector, notes)

- **`struct Head`**
  a start line and its headers
  - `method: String` -- a request: its method and target ("GET", "/index.html?x=1"); empty in a response
  - `target: String`
  - `status: u16` -- a response: the status and its reason phrase; 0 in a request
  - `reason: String`
  - `version: Version`
  - `headers: Headers`
  - `len: usize` -- the bytes of the head up to and including the empty line (with skipped empty lines
    before the start line)

**`impl Head`**

- **`fn is_request(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str>`**
- **`fn keep_alive(&self) -> bool`**
  the connection stays open after this message
- **`fn path(&self) -> &str`**
  the target without its query
- **`fn start_line(&self) -> String`**
  the start line ("GET / HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/1.1 200 OK")

- **`fn keep_alive(v: Version, h: &Headers) -> bool`**
  whether the connection stays open after a message

- **`enum Framing`**
  how a body is delimited
  - `None` -- no body
  - `Length(u64)`
  - `Chunked`
  - `UntilClose` -- until the connection ends (responses only)

- **`fn request_framing(h: &Headers) -> Result<Framing, HttpErr>`**
  the framing of a request body (RFC 9112 6.3; netio's server rejects TE with CL)

- **`fn response_framing(status: u16, h: &Headers, method: &str) -> Result<Framing, HttpErr>`**
  the framing of a response to a request of `method` (RFC 9112 6.3)

- **`fn start_kind(b: &[u8]) -> Option<bool>`**
  what a message starts with: Some(true) a request ("GET "), Some(false) a response
  ("HTTP/1."), None something else (a continuation, another protocol); empty lines before it
  are skipped

- **`fn parse_head(b: &[u8], request: bool) -> Result<Option<Head>, HttpErr>`**
  a head at the start of `b` (Ok(None): incomplete); `request` picks the kind of start line

- **`enum Event`**
  what the bytes so far make up
  - `More` -- more bytes are needed
  - `Head(Head)` -- the start line and the headers of a message
  - `Data(Vec<u8>)` -- body bytes as they came (chunk framing removed)
  - `End(Headers)` -- the message is complete; the trailers of a chunked body

- **`struct Parser`**
  an incremental parser of the messages of one connection, in one direction
  - `max_body: u64` -- the largest body it takes (BodyTooLarge beyond)
  - `messages: u64` -- messages completed

**`impl Parser`**

- **`fn requests() -> Parser`**
  a parser of requests (a server reads them)
- **`fn responses() -> Parser`**
  a parser of responses (a client reads them)
- **`fn expect(&mut self, method: &str)`**
  a response parser: a request of `method` went out; its response is next after the
  ones before (a response to HEAD has no body)
- **`fn outstanding(&self) -> usize`**
  requests sent and not answered yet
- **`fn buffered(&self) -> usize`**
  bytes pushed and not used yet
- **`fn idle(&self) -> bool`**
  between messages with nothing buffered
- **`fn in_message(&self) -> bool`**
  inside a message (its head came, its end not yet)
- **`fn framing(&self) -> Framing`**
  the framing of the message being read
- **`fn body_len(&self) -> u64`**
  body bytes of the current message so far
- **`fn push(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Event, HttpErr>`**
  takes more bytes and gives the first event they complete (More: nothing yet)
- **`fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Event, HttpErr>`**
  the next event of the bytes pushed so far
- **`fn finish(&mut self) -> Result<Event, HttpErr>`**
  the connection ended: a body that runs until the close is complete (End); between
  messages with nothing buffered More (a clean end); inside a message Truncated

- **`fn encode_head(h: &Head) -> Vec<u8>`**
  a head exactly as given: a request when `status` is 0, else a response

- **`fn encode_request(method: &str, target: &str, version: Version, h: &Headers, body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  a request; Content-Length when it has a body or the method is POST, PUT or PATCH (unless
  the headers say chunked: then the body goes as one chunk)

- **`fn encode_response(version: Version, status: u16, h: &Headers, body: &[u8], head_only: bool) -> Vec<u8>`**
  a response with its body (only the head for HEAD requests): Content-Length for every status
  from 200 on but 204 and 304, unless the headers say chunked (then the body goes as one
  chunk and the last chunk)

- **`fn encode_chunk(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  one chunk; nothing for empty data (an empty chunk would end the body)

- **`fn encode_last_chunk(trailers: &Headers) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the last chunk with trailers

- **`fn encode_chunked(body: &[u8], size: usize) -> Vec<u8>`**
  a whole body as chunks of `size` bytes and the last chunk

- **`fn reason(status: u16) -> &'static str`**
  the reason phrase of a status code

- **`fn http_date(unix: i64) -> String`**
  the date of a Date header (IMF-fixdate) for seconds since 1970

### `netpkt/stp.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/stp.rs`](../lib/netpkt/stp.rs)

```text
stp -- Bridge Protocol Data Units of the spanning tree protocols: Configuration and Topology
Change Notification BPDUs (IEEE 802.1D-1998 clause 9) and RST BPDUs (IEEE 802.1D-2004 9.3.3,
RSTP of 802.1w) with their flags, bridge and port identifiers, the recommended path costs,
and the 802.3 frames with LLC that carry them to 01:80:c2:00:00:00

  BridgeId(u64)            priority (16 bits: 4 settable, 12 system ID extension) and MAC:
                           new(priority, mac), priority(), ext(), mac(); Display
                           "4096/0/02:4a:00:00:01:00" as capture tools write it
  PortId(u16)              priority (4 bits, in steps of 16) and port number (12 bits):
                           new(priority, number), priority(), number(); Display "128.1"
  path_cost(kbps)          the recommended Port Path Cost of 802.1D-2004 Table 17-3:
                           20 000 000 000 / speed in kbit/s, 1 .. 200 000 000 (100M 200 000,
                           1G 20 000, 2.5G 8 000, 10G 2 000, 25G 800, 100G 200)
  Role                     the port role of an RST BPDU (Unknown, AltBackup, Root, Designated)
  F_TC, F_PROPOSAL, F_ROLE, F_LEARNING, F_FORWARDING, F_AGREEMENT, F_TCA   the flag bits
  Bpdu { kind, version, flags, root, cost, bridge, port, msg_age, max_age, hello, fwd_delay }
                           times in 1/256 s (TIME_UNIT per second); config / tcn / rst build
                           one from whole seconds (Times), with_role sets the role bits,
                           times() reads them back in seconds
  Bpdu::parse(b)           the BPDU after the LLC header, validated as 802.1D-2004 9.3.4 says
                           (protocol identifier 0, type and length); Err with the reason
  Bpdu::to_bytes()         35 (Configuration), 4 (TCN) or 36 bytes (RST)
  Bpdu::frame(src)         the whole frame: 01:80:c2:00:00:00, the 802.3 length, LLC
                           42 42 03, the BPDU, padded to 60 bytes
  of_frame(frame)          the BPDU of a received frame (untagged or tagged), None for any
                           other frame or a BPDU that does not validate
  flags_text(kind, flags)  "Forwarding, Learning, Port Role: Designated" (dissectors)
  summary(&Bpdu)           a one-line summary like a capture tool's ("RST. Root =
                           4096/0/02:4a:00:00:01:00  Cost = 0  Port = 0x8001")

Multi-byte fields are big endian.  The receiver checks what needs its own state (a Message Age
that is not below Max Age, its own BPDU looped back); the codec only reads and writes.
```

```rust
/// BPDU timer values count in 1/256 s
TIME_UNIT: u16 = 256
/// the lengths of the three BPDUs
CONFIG_LEN: usize = 35
TCN_LEN: usize = 4
RST_LEN: usize = 36
TYPE_CONFIG: u8 = 0x00
TYPE_RST: u8 = 0x02
TYPE_TCN: u8 = 0x80
/// Protocol Version Identifiers: 802.1D STP, RSTP (802.1w), MSTP (802.1s)
VERSION_STP: u8 = 0
VERSION_RSTP: u8 = 2
VERSION_MSTP: u8 = 3
/// flag bits: Topology Change (both BPDUs), the RST BPDU's own ones, and the Topology Change
/// Acknowledgment of Configuration BPDUs
F_TC: u8 = 0x01
F_PROPOSAL: u8 = 0x02
F_ROLE: u8 = 0x0C
F_LEARNING: u8 = 0x10
F_FORWARDING: u8 = 0x20
F_AGREEMENT: u8 = 0x40
F_TCA: u8 = 0x80
```

  extension, 0 for one spanning tree) and the bridge's MAC address; lower is better

**`impl PortId`**

- **`fn number(&self) -> u16`**

- **`fn path_cost(kbps: u32) -> u32`**
  the recommended Port Path Cost of a link speed (802.1D-2004 Table 17-3: 20 000 000 000
  divided by the speed in kbit/s, within 1 .. 200 000 000)

- **`enum Role`**
  the port role an RST BPDU conveys (flag bits 3 and 4)
  - `Unknown`

**`impl Role`**

  - `Config`

- **`struct Times`**
  the four timer values of a BPDU in whole seconds
  - `msg_age: u16`
  - `max_age: u16`
  - `hello: u16`
  - `fwd_delay: u16`

- **`struct Bpdu`**
  a BPDU; the times count in 1/256 s
  - `kind: Kind`

  - `flags: u8`
  - `root: BridgeId`

  - `bridge: BridgeId`

  - `msg_age: u16`

  - `fwd_delay: u16`

  why bytes are no BPDU
  - `Short` -- shorter than its type needs
  - `Protocol` -- the Protocol Identifier is not 0
  - `Type` -- a BPDU type (or type and version) this codec does not know

**`impl BpduErr`**

**`impl Bpdu`**

  a Configuration BPDU (only the TC and TC acknowledgment flags count)
- **`fn tcn() -> Bpdu`**
  a Topology Change Notification BPDU
- **`fn rst(flags: u8, root: BridgeId, cost: u32, bridge: BridgeId, port: PortId, t: Times) -> Bpdu`**
  an RST BPDU (the port role is part of the flags: Role::bits, with_role)
- **`fn with_role(mut self, r: Role) -> Bpdu`**
  the same BPDU conveying another port role
- **`fn role(&self) -> Role`**

- **`fn tca(&self) -> bool`**

- **`fn learning(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn forwarding(&self) -> bool`**

  the timer values in whole seconds (rounded down)
- **`fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Bpdu, BpduErr>`**
  the BPDU in `b` (the bytes after the LLC header), as 802.1D-2004 9.3.4 validates it
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the bytes of the BPDU
- **`fn frame(&self, src: Mac) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the frame that carries the BPDU from a port with MAC `src`: IEEE 802.3 to the bridge
  group address, LLC with SAP 0x42, padded to the 60-byte minimum

- **`fn of_frame(frame: &[u8]) -> Option<Bpdu>`**
  the BPDU a received frame carries: to 01:80:c2:00:00:00 (tagged or not), an 802.3 length,
  LLC with SAP 0x42; None for any other frame and for one that does not validate
