  Cost = 20000  Port = 0x8002", "RST. Root = ...", "Topology Change Notification")

### `netpkt/rip.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/rip.rs`](../lib/netpkt/rip.rs)

```text
rip -- Routing Information Protocol messages (UDP port 520): version 2 after RFC 2453 and
version 1 after RFC 1058; requests and responses with their route entries, and the
authentication entry of RFC 2453 4.1 (recognised; simple passwords read and written)

  RipView::parse(b)          command, version, must-be-zero field, the complete 20-byte
                             entries (entry(i), entries(), routes() without the
                             authentication entry), auth(), trailing() bytes after them
  Rte { afi, tag, addr, mask, next_hop, metric }   one entry; Rte::v2 / Rte::v1 build route
                             entries, prefix() is the destination with a version 2 mask,
                             mbz_clear() checks the fields version 1 leaves zero
  Auth { kind, data }        the first entry with AFI 0xFFFF: AUTH_PASSWORD (16 bytes of
                             plain text: Auth::password, text()), AUTH_MD5 (RFC 4822: kind and
                             bytes only, not checked)
  Rip { command, version, auth, entries }   read / to_bytes / response / request_all /
                             is_request_all (one entry, address family 0, metric 16)
  CMD_REQUEST, CMD_RESPONSE, AFI_INET, AFI_AUTH, AUTH_*, INFINITY (16), MAX_ENTRIES (25),
  GROUP (224.0.0.9, RIPv2's multicast address), command_name

The view reads whatever is there: more than 25 entries, bytes after the last entry, a version
1 message with a must-be-zero field set or an unknown command are for the receiver to judge
(decode.rs reports them as problems).  Version 1 entries carry no mask; the receiver infers it
from the address class and its own interfaces (RFC 1058 3.7).
```

```rust
/// the header: command, version, two bytes that must be zero
RIP_HDR: usize = 4
/// one entry (route or authentication)
RTE_LEN: usize = 20
/// entries a message holds at most (RFC 2453 3.6); 24 routes with an authentication entry
MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 25
CMD_REQUEST: u8 = 1
CMD_RESPONSE: u8 = 2
/// the address family of IPv4 routes
AFI_INET: u16 = 2
/// the address family that marks the authentication entry (RFC 2453 4.1)
AFI_AUTH: u16 = 0xFFFF
/// a plain-text password of 16 bytes (RFC 2453 4.1)
AUTH_PASSWORD: u16 = 2
/// keyed MD5 (RFC 4822)
AUTH_MD5: u16 = 3
/// the metric of an unreachable destination
INFINITY: u32 = 16
/// where version 2 sends its updates (RFC 2453 4.5)
GROUP: Ipv4 = Ipv4([224, 0, 0, 9])
```

- **`fn command_name(c: u8) -> &'static str`**
  the name of a command as capture tools show it

- **`struct Rte`**
  one 20-byte entry; for the authentication entry `tag` holds the type and the 16 bytes from
  `addr` on hold the authentication data (Auth reads them)
  - `afi: u16`
  - `tag: u16` -- the route tag (version 2; zero in version 1)
  - `addr: Ipv4`
  - `mask: Ipv4` -- the subnet mask (version 2; zero: not given)
  - `next_hop: Ipv4` -- where to send packets for the destination (version 2; 0.0.0.0: to the sender)
  - `metric: u32`

**`impl Rte`**

- **`fn read(b: &[u8]) -> Rte`**
  an entry from its 20 bytes (the caller has checked the length)
- **`fn write(&self, b: &mut [u8])`**
  writes the entry into 20 bytes
- **`fn v2(prefix: Prefix4, next_hop: Ipv4, metric: u32, tag: u16) -> Rte`**
  a version 2 route: the destination with its mask, the next hop (0.0.0.0: the sender
  itself), the metric and the route tag
- **`fn v1(addr: Ipv4, metric: u32) -> Rte`**
  a version 1 route: the address alone
- **`fn prefix(&self) -> Option<Prefix4>`**
  the destination with its version 2 mask (None: no mask, or one with gaps)
- **`fn mbz_clear(&self) -> bool`**
  the fields version 1 leaves zero are zero (route tag, mask, next hop)

- **`struct Auth`**
  the authentication entry of a version 2 message
  - `kind: u16`
  - `data: [u8; 16]`

**`impl Auth`**

- **`fn password(pw: &[u8]) -> Auth`**
  a plain-text password: left-justified, padded with zero bytes, cut at 16 bytes
- **`fn text(&self) -> Option<String>`**
  the password of a plain-text entry (up to the first zero byte)

- **`struct RipView<'a>`**
  a received RIP message

**`impl<'a> RipView<'a>`**

- **`fn parse(b: &'a [u8]) -> Option<RipView<'a>>`**
  at least the header
- **`fn command(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn version(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn mbz(&self) -> u16`**
  the two header bytes that must be zero
- **`fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn count(&self) -> usize`**
  complete entries
- **`fn trailing(&self) -> usize`**
  bytes after the last complete entry
- **`fn entry(&self, i: usize) -> Option<Rte>`**
  entry `i` (authentication entries included)
- **`fn entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Rte> + '_`**
- **`fn auth(&self) -> Option<Auth>`**
  the authentication entry: only the first entry may be one (RFC 2453 4.1)
- **`fn routes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Rte> + '_`**
  the entries after a leading authentication entry

- **`struct Rip`**
  a RIP message to write (or one read)
  - `command: u8`
  - `version: u8`
  - `auth: Option<Auth>` -- written as the first entry
  - `entries: Vec<Rte>`

**`impl Rip`**

- **`fn response(version: u8, entries: Vec<Rte>) -> Rip`**
- **`fn request_all(version: u8) -> Rip`**
  the request for the whole routing table: a single entry with address family 0 and
  metric 16 (RFC 2453 3.9.1)
- **`fn is_request_all(&self) -> bool`**
  this is the request for the whole table
- **`fn read(v: &RipView) -> Rip`**
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the message as bytes (no limit on the number of entries: the sender splits at 25)

### `netpkt/nat.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/nat.rs`](../lib/netpkt/nat.rs)

```text
nat -- address and port translation of IPv4 packets in place (RFC 3022): addresses, TCP and
UDP ports and the identifiers of ICMP queries change, and every checksum that covers them
follows incrementally (RFC 1624); ICMP errors take the packet they quote along (RFC 5508)

  Flow::of(packet) -> Option<Flow>      protocol, addresses, ports (the identifier of an ICMP
                                        query in both), ICMP type and code, TCP flags; a
                                        fragment after the first has no ports (`ports`
                                        false)
  Flow::quoted(packet) -> Option<Flow>  the packet an ICMP error quotes (its header and at
                                        least 8 bytes of its payload)
  rewrite(pkt, side, addr, port)        the source or destination address of a packet and,
                                        with Some, its port (an ICMP query: its identifier);
                                        the IPv4 header checksum, the TCP or UDP checksum
                                        (pseudo header and port; a UDP checksum of 0 means
                                        none and stays 0) and the ICMP checksum follow; a
                                        later fragment changes its address only
  rewrite_quoted(pkt, side, addr, port) the same for the packet inside an ICMP error: its
                                        header checksum, its TCP or UDP checksum when the
                                        quote holds it, an ICMP query's checksum, and the
                                        error's own ICMP checksum over every changed byte
                                        (the outer header stays; rewrite() changes it)
  is_query(type) / reply_of(type)       ICMP queries that carry an identifier (echo,
                                        timestamp, information, address mask) and the type
                                        of their answers

Translation needs no full recomputation: the segment of a first fragment is not complete,
yet its checksum covers all of it, and an ICMP error quotes only the start of a packet.
Every field these functions change lies on a 16-bit boundary of the data its checksum
covers, so the old and new words are enough (checksum::update).
```

- **`enum Side`**
  which address and port of a packet a translation changes
  - `Src`
  - `Dst`

- **`struct Flow`**
  what translation and filters look at in a packet
  - `proto: u8`
  - `src: Ipv4`
  - `dst: Ipv4`
  - `sport: u16` -- TCP and UDP ports; an ICMP query's identifier in both; 0 when unknown
  - `dport: u16`
  - `ports: bool` -- the ports (or the identifier) are known: not a later fragment, and the transport header
    is there
  - `icmp: Option<(u8, u8)>` -- ICMP type and code
  - `flags: u8` -- TCP flags (netpkt::tcp::SYN ...)
  - `later: bool` -- a fragment after the first (no transport header)
  - `mf: bool` -- more fragments follow
  - `id: u16` -- the identification field (fragments of one datagram share it)

- **`fn is_query(typ: u8) -> bool`**
  ICMP queries with an identifier: echo, timestamp, information, address mask (requests and
  replies)

- **`fn reply_of(typ: u8) -> Option<u8>`**
  the type of the answer to an ICMP query request (None: not a request)

**`impl Flow`**

- **`fn of(packet: &[u8]) -> Option<Flow>`**
  the flow of a whole packet
- **`fn quoted(packet: &[u8]) -> Option<Flow>`**
  the flow of the packet an ICMP error quotes (`packet`: the error's whole IPv4 packet)

- **`fn rewrite(pkt: &mut [u8], side: Side, addr: Ipv4, port: Option<u16>) -> bool`**
  sets the source or destination address of an IPv4 packet and, with `port`, its TCP / UDP
  port or ICMP query identifier, with every checksum updated; false when it is no IPv4 packet

- **`fn rewrite_quoted(pkt: &mut [u8], side: Side, addr: Ipv4, port: Option<u16>) -> bool`**
  sets the source or destination address (and port or query identifier) of the packet an
  ICMP error quotes, with the quote's checksums and the error's ICMP checksum; false when
  `pkt` is no ICMP error with a quoted IPv4 header

### `netpkt/icmpv6.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/icmpv6.rs`](../lib/netpkt/icmpv6.rs)

```text
icmpv6 -- ICMP for IPv6 (RFC 4443) and the messages of Neighbor Discovery (RFC 4861)

  Icmp6View::parse(b)     type, code, checksum (checksum_ok over the IPv6 pseudo header, RFC
                          4443 2.3), the 4 bytes after it, the body; quoted() for the packet
                          an error message carries
  Icmp6                   EchoRequest / EchoReply { id, seq }, DestUnreach { code },
                          PacketTooBig { mtu }, TimeExceeded { code }, ParamProblem { code,
                          pointer }, Other; encode(src, dst, body) and push_v6(&mut Pkt, src,
                          dst) with the checksum
  Nd { msg, opts }        RouterSolicit, RouterAdvert(Ra), NeighborSolicit { target },
                          NeighborAdvert { router, solicited, override_, target },
                          Redirect { target, dst } with their options (NdOpt: source / target
                          link-layer address, prefix information, redirected header, MTU, any
                          other kept as bytes); Nd::parse checks what RFC 4861 asks a receiver
                          to check in the message itself (code 0, lengths, no option of length
                          0, no group as target); hop limit 255, the checksum and the rules
                          that need the addresses are the caller's (check_ip)
  Nd::encode(src, dst)    the message with its checksum
  error_quote(packet)     what an error quotes: as much of the offending packet as fits into
                          an ICMPv6 packet of the minimum MTU (1280 bytes, RFC 4443 2.4 (c))
  name(type, code)        "Echo (ping) request", "Neighbor Solicitation", "Time Exceeded (hop
                          limit exceeded in transit)", ... (the wording of capture tools)

The multicast addresses and MACs of ND are Ipv6::solicited_node, Ipv6::ALL_NODES,
ALL_ROUTERS and Mac::of_ipv6_multicast (addr.rs); interface identifiers Mac::eui64.
```

```rust
/// type, code, checksum and the 4 bytes every message has after them
ICMPV6_HDR: usize = 8
T_DEST_UNREACH: u8 = 1
T_PACKET_TOO_BIG: u8 = 2
T_TIME_EXCEEDED: u8 = 3
T_PARAM_PROBLEM: u8 = 4
T_ECHO_REQUEST: u8 = 128
T_ECHO_REPLY: u8 = 129
T_MLD_QUERY: u8 = 130
T_MLD_REPORT: u8 = 131
T_MLD_DONE: u8 = 132
T_ROUTER_SOLICIT: u8 = 133
T_ROUTER_ADVERT: u8 = 134
T_NEIGHBOR_SOLICIT: u8 = 135
T_NEIGHBOR_ADVERT: u8 = 136
T_REDIRECT: u8 = 137
T_MLD2_REPORT: u8 = 143
/// codes of Destination Unreachable
UNREACH_NO_ROUTE: u8 = 0
UNREACH_ADMIN: u8 = 1
UNREACH_BEYOND_SCOPE: u8 = 2
UNREACH_ADDR: u8 = 3
UNREACH_PORT: u8 = 4
UNREACH_POLICY: u8 = 5
UNREACH_REJECT: u8 = 6
/// codes of Time Exceeded
EXCEEDED_HOP_LIMIT: u8 = 0
EXCEEDED_REASSEMBLY: u8 = 1
/// codes of Parameter Problem
PARAM_HEADER: u8 = 0
PARAM_NEXT_HEADER: u8 = 1
PARAM_OPTION: u8 = 2
/// ND option types (RFC 4861 4.6)
OPT_SRC_LLA: u8 = 1
OPT_TGT_LLA: u8 = 2
OPT_PREFIX: u8 = 3
OPT_REDIRECTED: u8 = 4
OPT_MTU: u8 = 5
/// the lifetime that never ends (prefix information, RFC 4861 4.6.2)
INFINITE: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF
```

- **`struct Icmp6View<'a>`**
  a received ICMPv6 message

**`impl<'a> Icmp6View<'a>`**

- **`fn parse(b: &'a [u8]) -> Option<Icmp6View<'a>>`**
  at least type, code and checksum
- **`fn typ(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn code(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn checksum(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn checksum_ok(&self, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6) -> bool`**
  the checksum over the pseudo header of `src` and `dst` and the whole message
- **`fn checksum_want(&self, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6) -> u16`**
  the checksum the message should carry (for a dissector's "should be")
- **`fn rest(&self) -> [u8; 4]`**
  the 4 bytes after the checksum (zeros when the message is shorter)
- **`fn id(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn seq(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn value(&self) -> u32`**
  the MTU of Packet Too Big, the pointer of Parameter Problem
- **`fn body(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
  what follows the first 8 bytes (an error's quote, an echo's data)
- **`fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn is_error(&self) -> bool`**
  an error message (types 0 to 127, RFC 4443 2.1)
- **`fn is_nd(&self) -> bool`**
  a message of Neighbor Discovery
- **`fn quoted(&self) -> Option<Ipv6View<'a>>`**
  the packet an error message quotes (cut where the quote ends)

- **`fn error_quote(packet: &[u8]) -> &[u8]`**
  as much of the offending packet as an error may quote: the error packet stays within the
  minimum MTU of 1280 bytes (40 bytes IPv6, 8 bytes ICMPv6, at most 1232 of the packet)

- **`enum Icmp6`**
  an ICMPv6 message with the 8-byte header (echo and the errors) to write
  - `EchoRequest { id: u16, seq: u16 }`
  - `EchoReply { id: u16, seq: u16 }`
  - `DestUnreach { code: u8 }`
  - `PacketTooBig { mtu: u32 }`
  - `TimeExceeded { code: u8 }`
  - `ParamProblem { code: u8, pointer: u32 }`
  - `Other { typ: u8, code: u8, rest: [u8; 4] }`

**`impl Icmp6`**

- **`fn read(v: &Icmp6View) -> Icmp6`**
- **`fn type_code(&self) -> (u8, u8)`**
- **`fn is_error(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn encode(&self, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6, body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  header + body with the checksum over the pseudo header
- **`fn push_v6(&self, p: &mut Pkt, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6)`**
  prepends the header (the packet's content is the body) with the checksum

- **`struct Ra`**
  the fixed fields of a Router Advertisement (RFC 4861 4.2; the preference bits of RFC 4191)
  - `hop_limit: u8` -- 0: unspecified
  - `managed: bool` -- addresses from DHCPv6 (M) / other settings from DHCPv6 (O)
  - `other: bool`
  - `prf: u8` -- default router preference: 0 medium, 1 high, 3 low (2 is reserved, read as medium)
  - `lifetime: u16` -- seconds; 0: not a default router
  - `reachable: u32` -- milliseconds; 0: unspecified
  - `retrans: u32`

- **`struct PrefixInfo`**
  a prefix information option (RFC 4861 4.6.2)
  - `len: u8`
  - `on_link: bool` -- the prefix is on the link (L)
  - `auto: bool` -- addresses may be formed from it (A, RFC 4862)
  - `valid: u32` -- seconds, INFINITE for ever
  - `preferred: u32`
  - `prefix: Ipv6`

- **`enum NdOpt`**
  an option of an ND message
  - `SrcLla(Mac)`
  - `TgtLla(Mac)`
  - `Prefix(PrefixInfo)`
  - `Redirected(Vec<u8>)` -- what a redirect carries of the redirected packet
  - `Mtu(u32)`
  - `Other(u8, Vec<u8>)` -- any other option: its type and its bytes after type and length

**`impl NdOpt`**

- **`fn kind(&self) -> u8`**

- **`enum NdMsg`**
  the message of ND
  - `RouterSolicit`
  - `RouterAdvert(Ra)`
  - `NeighborSolicit { target: Ipv6 }`
  - `NeighborAdvert { router: bool, solicited: bool, override_: bool, target: Ipv6 }`
  - `Redirect { target: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6 }`

- **`enum NdErr`**
  why a receiver drops an ND message (RFC 4861 6.1, 7.1, 8.1)
  - `Code(u8)` -- the ICMP code is not 0
  - `Short` -- shorter than the message's fixed part
  - `BadOption` -- an option with length 0, or one that runs past the end
  - `Multicast` -- a group address as the target of NS / NA or as the destination of a redirect
  - `NotNd` -- not an ND type
  - `HopLimit` -- the hop limit is not 255: the message did not come from this link
  - `Source` -- a router advertisement or redirect from an address that is not link-local
  - `DadDest` -- an address detection probe (unspecified source) not sent to a solicited-node group
  - `SourceLla` -- an unspecified source with a source link-layer address option
  - `SolicitedToGroup` -- a solicited advertisement sent to a group

**`impl NdErr`**

- **`fn text(&self) -> &'static str`**
  the reason in the words of capture tools (English)

- **`struct Nd`**
  a Neighbor Discovery message with its options
  - `msg: NdMsg`
  - `opts: Vec<NdOpt>`

- **`fn options(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<(NdOpt, usize, usize)>, NdErr>`**
  the options of `b` (the bytes after the fixed part): each with its offset and length in
  `b`; Err when one has length 0 or runs past the end

- **`fn fixed_len(typ: u8) -> Option<usize>`**
  the length of the fixed part of an ND message type

**`impl Nd`**

- **`fn new(msg: NdMsg, opts: Vec<NdOpt>) -> Nd`**
- **`fn rs(src_lla: Option<Mac>) -> Nd`**
  a Router Solicitation (with the sender's MAC unless it has no address yet)
- **`fn ns(target: Ipv6, src_lla: Option<Mac>) -> Nd`**
  a Neighbor Solicitation (DAD probes carry no source link-layer address)
- **`fn na(target: Ipv6, router: bool, solicited: bool, override_: bool, tgt_lla: Option<Mac>) -> Nd`**
  a Neighbor Advertisement
- **`fn parse(v: &Icmp6View) -> Result<Nd, NdErr>`**
  reads an ND message (the checks RFC 4861 makes on the message itself)
- **`fn typ(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn encode(&self, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the message with its checksum
- **`fn src_lla(&self) -> Option<Mac>`**
  the source link-layer address option
- **`fn tgt_lla(&self) -> Option<Mac>`**
  the target link-layer address option
- **`fn prefixes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &PrefixInfo>`**
  the prefix information options
- **`fn mtu(&self) -> Option<u32>`**
  the MTU option
- **`fn check_ip(&self, src: Ipv6, dst: Ipv6, hop_limit: u8) -> Option<NdErr>`**
  the rules of RFC 4861 that need the packet's addresses and hop limit: hop limit 255 for
  every message, a link-local source for RA and redirect, an unspecified source only with a
  solicited-node destination and without a source link-layer address (NS) or without it
  (RS), solicited NA never to a group; None when the message may be taken

- **`fn name(typ: u8, code: u8) -> &'static str`**
  a name of an ICMPv6 type and code as capture tools write it

### `netpkt/ospf.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/ospf.rs`](../lib/netpkt/ospf.rs)

```text
ospf -- OSPF version 2 packets and LSAs byte for byte (RFC 2328 appendix A): the 24-byte
header with its checksum and authentication field, the five packet types, LSA headers with
the Fletcher checksum of RFC 2328 12.1.7 (RFC 905 annex B), router-, network-, summary- and
AS-external-LSAs, and how two instances of an LSA compare (13.1)

  OspfView::parse(b)       version, kind, length, router ID, area, checksum, authentication
                           type and field, body(); checksum_ok() (the IP checksum of the
                           packet without the authentication field, A.3.1); None when the
                           bytes are shorter than the header or than its length field
  Header { kind, router, area, autype, auth }   the common header
  Packet { hdr, body }     read(&view) (Err with the reason: OspfErr::text) / to_bytes()
                           (length and checksum filled in; with AU_CRYPTO the checksum stays
                           0 and no digest is appended)
  Body::Hello(Hello)       network mask, HelloInterval, options, priority, RouterDeadInterval,
                           DR, BDR, the neighbours seen
       Dd(Dd)              interface MTU, options, the I / M / MS flags, DD sequence number,
                           LSA headers
       Lsr(Vec<LsaKey>)    the LSAs asked for (type, Link State ID, advertising router)
       Lsu(Vec<Vec<u8>>)   whole LSAs as they travel (flooding forwards them byte for byte)
       Ack(Vec<LsaHeader>) the LSA headers acknowledged
  LsaHeader                age, options, type, Link State ID, advertising router, sequence
                           number, checksum, length; read / write / of(lsa) / key()
  Lsa { hdr, body }        parse(lsa) (Err: LsaErr) / to_bytes() (length and Fletcher
                           checksum filled in); LsaBody::Router (flags V / E / B and links
                           with metrics), Network (mask, attached routers), Summary (types 3
                           and 4: mask and metric), External (mask, type 1 or 2, metric,
                           forwarding address, route tag), Other (bytes of an unknown type)
  lsa_checksum(lsa) / lsa_checksum_ok(lsa)   the Fletcher checksum over the LSA without its
                           age, C0 and C1 both zero for a correct one
  set_age(lsa, age)        a new LS age (outside the checksum)
  compare(a, b)            which instance is more recent: sequence number (signed), checksum,
                           MaxAge, an age difference beyond MaxAgeDiff (13.1)
  type_name, lsa_name, options_text, dd_flags_text, area_text   names for dissectors

Constants: VERSION, the packet types T_*, ALL_SPF_ROUTERS (224.0.0.5), ALL_D_ROUTERS
(224.0.0.6), authentication types AU_*, option bits OPT_*, the DD flags DD_I, DD_M, DD_MS,
LSA types LSA_*, router-LSA link types LINK_* and flags RTR_B / RTR_E / RTR_V, the
architectural constants of appendix B (MAX_AGE, LS_REFRESH_TIME, MIN_LS_INTERVAL, ...),
INITIAL_SEQ / MAX_SEQ and LS_INFINITY.

The codec reads and writes; what a receiver refuses because of its own state (mismatched
timers, the area, the neighbours) is the protocol's business.  TOS metrics other than TOS 0
are read and written but carry no meaning (RFC 2328 dropped TOS routing).
```

```rust
/// OSPF version 2
VERSION: u8 = 2
/// the common header, an LSA header, an entry of a Link State Request
HDR_LEN: usize = 24
LSA_HDR_LEN: usize = 20
LSR_ENTRY_LEN: usize = 12
/// the fixed part of a Hello and of a Database Description packet
HELLO_LEN: usize = 20
DD_LEN: usize = 8
/// packet types
T_HELLO: u8 = 1
T_DD: u8 = 2
T_LSR: u8 = 3
T_LSU: u8 = 4
T_ACK: u8 = 5
/// every OSPF router listens to AllSPFRouters, the DR and the BDR to AllDRouters (A.1)
ALL_SPF_ROUTERS: Ipv4 = Ipv4([224, 0, 0, 5])
ALL_D_ROUTERS: Ipv4 = Ipv4([224, 0, 0, 6])
/// authentication types (appendix D)
AU_NULL: u16 = 0
AU_SIMPLE: u16 = 1
AU_CRYPTO: u16 = 2
/// option bits (A.2; DN and O came later: RFC 4576, RFC 5250)
OPT_E: u8 = 0x02
OPT_MC: u8 = 0x04
OPT_NP: u8 = 0x08
OPT_EA: u8 = 0x10
OPT_DC: u8 = 0x20
OPT_O: u8 = 0x40
OPT_DN: u8 = 0x80
/// the flags of a Database Description packet: Init, More, Master/Slave
DD_I: u8 = 0x04
DD_M: u8 = 0x02
DD_MS: u8 = 0x01
/// LSA types
LSA_ROUTER: u8 = 1
LSA_NETWORK: u8 = 2
LSA_SUMMARY: u8 = 3
LSA_ASBR: u8 = 4
LSA_EXTERNAL: u8 = 5
/// the links of a router-LSA
LINK_P2P: u8 = 1
LINK_TRANSIT: u8 = 2
LINK_STUB: u8 = 3
LINK_VIRTUAL: u8 = 4
/// the flags of a router-LSA: area border router, AS boundary router, virtual link endpoint
RTR_B: u8 = 0x01
RTR_E: u8 = 0x02
RTR_V: u8 = 0x04
/// architectural constants (appendix B), in seconds
LS_REFRESH_TIME: u16 = 1800
MIN_LS_INTERVAL: u16 = 5
MIN_LS_ARRIVAL: u16 = 1
MAX_AGE: u16 = 3600
CHECK_AGE: u16 = 300
MAX_AGE_DIFF: u16 = 900
/// the metric of an unreachable destination in summary- and AS-external-LSAs
LS_INFINITY: u32 = 0xFF_FFFF
/// LS sequence numbers are signed: the first one, the largest one (12.1.6)
INITIAL_SEQ: u32 = 0x8000_0001
MAX_SEQ: u32 = 0x7FFF_FFFF
```

- **`fn type_name(t: u8) -> &'static str`**
  the name of a packet type as capture tools show it

- **`fn lsa_name(t: u8) -> &'static str`**
  the name of an LSA type

- **`fn options_text(o: u8) -> String`**
  the set option bits: "E, MC" ("none" without any)

- **`fn dd_flags_text(f: u8) -> String`**
  the flags of a Database Description packet: "I, M, MS" ("none")

- **`fn area_text(a: u32) -> String`**
  an area ID as dissectors show it: "0.0.0.0 (Backbone)", "0.0.0.1"

- **`fn lsa_checksum(lsa: &[u8]) -> u16`**
  the Fletcher checksum of an LSA (RFC 2328 12.1.7): over the bytes from the options field to
  the end of the LSA (the LS age left out), the checksum field taken as zero; the two check
  bytes X and Y of RFC 905 B.4 that make C0 and C1 zero, a zero byte written as 255

- **`fn lsa_checksum_ok(lsa: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  an LSA's checksum is correct: C0 and C1 over the bytes after the age are both zero (RFC 905
  B.2); a checksum of 0 is never correct

- **`fn set_age(lsa: &mut [u8], age: u16)`**
  writes a new LS age into an LSA (the checksum does not cover it)

- **`struct LsaKey`**
  what identifies an LSA: its type, Link State ID and advertising router (12.1)
  - `kind: u8`
  - `id: Ipv4`
  - `adv: Ipv4`

- **`struct LsaHeader`**
  the 20-byte header of an LSA
  - `age: u16` -- seconds since it was originated
  - `options: u8`
  - `kind: u8`
  - `id: Ipv4`
  - `adv: Ipv4`
  - `seq: u32` -- signed: INITIAL_SEQ (0x80000001) is the smallest one used
  - `checksum: u16`
  - `len: u16` -- the whole LSA with this header

**`impl LsaHeader`**

- **`fn read(b: &[u8]) -> LsaHeader`**
  a header from its 20 bytes (the caller has checked the length)
- **`fn of(lsa: &[u8]) -> Option<LsaHeader>`**
  the header of an LSA (None when it is shorter than a header)
- **`fn write(&self, b: &mut [u8])`**
  writes the header into 20 bytes
- **`fn key(&self) -> LsaKey`**

- **`fn compare(a: &LsaHeader, b: &LsaHeader) -> Ordering`**
  which of two instances of the same LSA is more recent (RFC 2328 13.1): Greater when `a` is,
  Equal when they are the same instance

- **`struct RouterLink`**
  one link of a router-LSA (A.4.2)
  - `id: Ipv4` -- LINK_P2P: the neighbour's router ID; LINK_TRANSIT: the DR's interface address;
    LINK_STUB: the network
  - `data: Ipv4` -- the router's interface address (LINK_P2P, LINK_TRANSIT; an interface index when
    unnumbered) or the network mask (LINK_STUB)
  - `kind: u8`
  - `metric: u16` -- the TOS 0 metric
  - `tos: Vec<(u8, u16)>` -- further TOS metrics: (TOS, metric)

- **`struct RouterLsa`**
  the body of a router-LSA
  - `flags: u8` -- RTR_V, RTR_E, RTR_B
  - `links: Vec<RouterLink>`

- **`struct NetworkLsa`**
  the body of a network-LSA (A.4.3)
  - `mask: Ipv4`
  - `routers: Vec<Ipv4>` -- the routers fully adjacent to the DR, the DR itself included

- **`struct SummaryLsa`**
  the body of a summary-LSA of type 3 or 4 (A.4.4; type 4 has the mask 0)
  - `mask: Ipv4`
  - `metric: u32` -- 24 bits; LS_INFINITY: unreachable
  - `tos: Vec<(u8, u32)>`

- **`struct ExternalLsa`**
  the TOS 0 part of an AS-external-LSA and its further TOS entries (A.4.5)
  - `mask: Ipv4`
  - `e2: bool` -- the E bit: a type 2 metric (larger than any path inside the AS)
  - `metric: u32` -- 24 bits
  - `fwd: Ipv4` -- where traffic for the destination should go (0.0.0.0: to the AS boundary router)
  - `tag: u32`
  - `tos: Vec<(u8, u32, Ipv4, u32)>` -- further TOS entries: (E bit and TOS, metric, forwarding address, tag)

- **`enum LsaBody`**
  what an LSA says
  - `Router(RouterLsa)`
  - `Network(NetworkLsa)`
  - `Summary(SummaryLsa)`
  - `External(ExternalLsa)`
  - `Other(Vec<u8>)` -- an LSA of another type: its bytes after the header

- **`enum LsaErr`**
  why an LSA cannot be read
  - `Short` -- fewer bytes than its header or its length field
  - `Length` -- the length field does not fit what the body needs

**`impl LsaErr`**

- **`fn text(self) -> &'static str`**

- **`struct Lsa`**
  an LSA as a record
  - `hdr: LsaHeader`
  - `body: LsaBody`

**`impl Lsa`**

- **`fn new(kind: u8, id: Ipv4, adv: Ipv4, seq: u32, options: u8, body: LsaBody) -> Lsa`**
  a new instance: age 0; to_bytes fills in length and checksum
- **`fn key(&self) -> LsaKey`**
- **`fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Lsa, LsaErr>`**
  reads an LSA (the bytes may go on after it: its length field says where it ends)
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the LSA as bytes: the header with the length and the Fletcher checksum filled in (the
  record's age stays as it is)

- **`struct Header`**
  the common header (A.3.1)
  - `kind: u8`
  - `router: Ipv4` -- the sender's router ID
  - `area: u32`
  - `autype: u16`
  - `auth: [u8; 8]` -- the authentication field: zeros (AU_NULL), the password (AU_SIMPLE), key ID, length and
    sequence number (AU_CRYPTO)

- **`struct Hello`**
  a Hello packet (A.3.2)
  - `mask: Ipv4`
  - `interval: u16` -- HelloInterval in seconds
  - `options: u8`
  - `priority: u8`
  - `dead: u32` -- RouterDeadInterval in seconds
  - `dr: Ipv4` -- the interface addresses of the DR and the BDR as the sender sees them (0.0.0.0: none)
  - `bdr: Ipv4`
  - `neighbors: Vec<Ipv4>` -- the router IDs it heard Hellos from within RouterDeadInterval

- **`struct Dd`**
  a Database Description packet (A.3.3)
  - `mtu: u16` -- the largest IP datagram the interface sends without fragmentation
  - `options: u8`
  - `flags: u8` -- DD_I, DD_M, DD_MS
  - `seq: u32`
  - `lsas: Vec<LsaHeader>`

- **`enum Body`**
  the body of a packet
  - `Hello(Hello)`
  - `Dd(Dd)`
  - `Lsr(Vec<LsaKey>)`
  - `Lsu(Vec<Vec<u8>>)` -- whole LSAs (each as long as its length field)
  - `Ack(Vec<LsaHeader>)`

- **`enum OspfErr`**
  why a packet cannot be read
  - `Version(u8)` -- not version 2
  - `Kind(u8)` -- not one of the five packet types
  - `Body` -- the body is shorter than its fixed part, or its entries do not fill it
  - `Lsa` -- an LSA of an update is cut or longer than the packet

**`impl OspfErr`**

- **`fn text(self) -> String`**

- **`struct Packet`**
  an OSPF packet as a record
  - `hdr: Header`
  - `body: Body`

- **`struct OspfView<'a>`**
  a received OSPF packet (the bytes are cut to its length field)

**`impl<'a> OspfView<'a>`**

- **`fn parse(b: &'a [u8]) -> Option<OspfView<'a>>`**
  at least the header, and as many bytes as its length field says (more are ignored)
- **`fn version(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn kind(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`**
- **`fn router(&self) -> Ipv4`**
- **`fn area(&self) -> u32`**
- **`fn checksum(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn autype(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn auth(&self) -> [u8; 8]`**
- **`fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn body(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn computed_checksum(&self) -> u16`**
  the checksum the packet should carry
- **`fn checksum_ok(&self) -> bool`**
  the checksum is right (with cryptographic authentication there is none: always true)
- **`fn header(&self) -> Header`**
- **`fn lsu_spans(&self) -> Option<Vec<(usize, usize)>>`**
  where the LSAs of an update start and end within the packet: (offset, length); None when
  one does not fit

**`impl Packet`**

- **`fn kind(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn read(v: &OspfView) -> Result<Packet, OspfErr>`**
  reads a packet; the checksum and the authentication are for the receiver to judge
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the packet as bytes: version 2, the type of the body, the length, the checksum (none with
  AU_CRYPTO)

### `netpkt/addrsel.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/addrsel.rs`](../lib/netpkt/addrsel.rs)

```text
addrsel -- destination address selection after RFC 6724: the scope of an address, the
default policy table (precedence and label) and the order in which the addresses a name
resolves to are tried (what getaddrinfo sorts), given the source address each one would use

  scope(a) -> u8            RFC 6724 3.1 and 3.2: the scope of an IPv6 multicast address,
                            2 (link-local) for fe80::/10 and ::1, 5 for the old site-local
                            fec0::/10, 14 (global) for the other unicast addresses (unique
                            local ones included); IPv4: 127/8 and 169.254/16 link-local, the
                            rest global (private addresses too)
  precedence(a) / label(a)  the default policy table of RFC 6724 2.1 (an IPv4 address as
                            ::ffff:a.b.c.d)
  Dest { addr, src, src_len, src_deprecated }   a destination and what source address
                            selection gave it (src None: unusable, no route or no source)
  compare(a, b) / sort(&mut [Dest])   the rules of RFC 6724 6: 1 (unusable last), 2 (matching
                            scope), 3 (no deprecated source), 5 (matching label), 6 (higher
                            precedence), 8 (smaller scope), 9 (longest matching prefix, as
                            glibc only between two IPv6 destinations), 10 (else the order as
                            given: the sort is stable)

Rules 4 (home addresses) and 7 (native transport) decide nothing without Mobile IPv6 and
tunnels and are left out.  The default table makes 2001:db8::/32 and other global IPv6
destinations (precedence 40) come before IPv4 ones (35), and IPv4 before unique local IPv6
addresses (3): a host with a global IPv6 address tries IPv6 first, one with only a link-local
IPv6 address IPv4 first (rule 2).
```

```rust
/// RFC 6724 3.1: link-local scope (fe80::/10, ::1, IPv4 127/8 and 169.254/16)
SCOPE_LINK: u8 = 2
/// the deprecated site-local fec0::/10
SCOPE_SITE: u8 = 5
/// global scope
SCOPE_GLOBAL: u8 = 14
```

- **`fn precedence(a: IpAddr) -> u8`**
  the precedence of the default policy table (higher is preferred)

- **`fn label(a: IpAddr) -> u8`**
  the label of the default policy table (a source and a destination with the same label
  belong together)

- **`fn scope(a: IpAddr) -> u8`**
  the scope of an address (RFC 6724 3.1, 3.2)

- **`struct Dest`**
  a destination to sort and the source address it would leave with
  - `addr: IpAddr`
  - `src: Option<IpAddr>` -- the source address selection gave it; None: it cannot be reached (no route, no source)
  - `src_len: u8` -- the prefix length of the source (the part before its interface identifier: rule 9
    counts common bits up to it)
  - `src_deprecated: bool` -- the source is deprecated (its preferred lifetime ended)

**`impl Dest`**

- **`fn new(addr: IpAddr, src: Option<IpAddr>) -> Dest`**

- **`fn compare(a: &Dest, b: &Dest) -> Ordering`**
  which of two destinations comes first (Less: `a`); Equal leaves their order

- **`fn sort(d: &mut [Dest])`**
  sorts destinations by RFC 6724 (stable: rule 10 keeps the given order)

### `netpkt/eapol.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/eapol.rs`](../lib/netpkt/eapol.rs)

```text
eapol -- EAPOL frames (IEEE 802.1X-2004 clause 11) with the EAPOL-Key body of IEEE 802.11-2020
12.7.2: the four messages of the 4-way handshake, the RSN element a station and an access
point put into them, and the key data elements (KDEs) of message 3.  No cryptography here:
the caller computes the MIC over mic_input() (HMAC-SHA1-128 or AES-128-CMAC by the key
descriptor version) and wraps the key data (the AES key wrap of RFC 3394)

  ET_EAPOL (eth.rs)              0x888E
  EapolView::parse(pdu)          version, packet type, body length, body
  Key { info, key_len, replay, nonce, iv, rsc, mic, data }     the EAPOL-Key body
  Key::parse(body) / Key::pdu(version) -> Vec<u8>   read one, write the whole EAPOL PDU
  Key::message() -> Option<u8>   1 .. 4 of the 4-way handshake by its Key Information bits
  mic_input(pdu) -> Vec<u8>      the PDU with the MIC field zero (what the MIC covers)
  set_mic(pdu, mic)              puts the MIC into a written PDU
  Rsne { akm, caps }             the RSN element (CCMP for group and pairwise, one AKM):
                                 to_bytes / parse
  kde_gtk(id, gtk) / kde_igtk(id, ipn, igtk) / kdes(data)   KDEs and the elements of key
                                 data (with the padding of 12.7.2 j: 0xdd 0x00 ...)
  pad_key_data(data)             the padding for the key wrap (a multiple of 8, at least 16)
  KI_* (Key Information), AKM_* and CIPHER_CCMP (the suites of 00-0F-AC)

The fields are big endian; the key replay counter is a 64-bit number.  Lengths are checked
once by parse; a body shorter than the 95 fixed bytes is no Key.
```

```rust
/// EAPOL packet types (802.1X-2004 11.3.2)
T_EAP: u8 = 0
T_START: u8 = 1
T_LOGOFF: u8 = 2
T_KEY: u8 = 3
/// the version 802.1X-2004 writes
VERSION_2004: u8 = 2
/// the RSN key descriptor type (802.11-2020 12.7.2)
DESC_RSN: u8 = 2
/// Key Information bits (802.11-2020 Figure 12-33)
KI_VERSION: u16 = 0x0007
KI_PAIRWISE: u16 = 0x0008
KI_INSTALL: u16 = 0x0040
KI_ACK: u16 = 0x0080
KI_MIC: u16 = 0x0100
KI_SECURE: u16 = 0x0200
KI_ERROR: u16 = 0x0400
KI_REQUEST: u16 = 0x0800
KI_ENCRYPTED: u16 = 0x1000
/// key descriptor versions: 2 HMAC-SHA1-128 MIC with the AES key wrap (AKM 2, PSK), 3 AES-128-CMAC
/// (AKM 6), 0 what the AKM defines (AKM 8, SAE: AES-128-CMAC)
KDV_AKM: u16 = 0
KDV_SHA1: u16 = 2
KDV_CMAC: u16 = 3
/// the fixed part of an EAPOL-Key body with a 16-byte MIC
KEY_FIXED: usize = 95
/// where the MIC sits in the body, its length
MIC_OFF: usize = 77
MIC_LEN: usize = 16
/// the OUI of IEEE 802.11 suites and KDEs
OUI: [u8; 3] = [0x00, 0x0F, 0xAC]
/// cipher suite: CCMP-128
CIPHER_CCMP: u8 = 4
/// AKM suites: PSK (WPA2-Personal), PSK-SHA256, SAE (WPA3-Personal)
AKM_PSK: u8 = 2
AKM_PSK_SHA256: u8 = 6
AKM_SAE: u8 = 8
/// RSN capabilities: management frame protection capable / required
RSN_MFPR: u16 = 0x0040
RSN_MFPC: u16 = 0x0080
/// the element id of the RSN element, the id of a vendor element (KDEs)
EID_RSN: u8 = 48
EID_VENDOR: u8 = 0xDD
/// KDE types (802.11-2020 Table 12-10)
KDE_GTK: u8 = 1
KDE_PMKID: u8 = 4
KDE_IGTK: u8 = 9
```

- **`struct EapolView<'a>`**
  the EAPOL header and body of a PDU

**`impl<'a> EapolView<'a>`**

- **`fn parse(b: &'a [u8]) -> Option<EapolView<'a>>`**
  the 4-byte header and a body as long as it says
- **`fn version(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn kind(&self) -> u8`**
- **`fn body_len(&self) -> usize`**
- **`fn body(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn pdu(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
  header and body without what follows (Ethernet padding)

- **`fn kind_name(t: u8) -> &'static str`**
  the name of a packet type ("EAPOL-Key")

- **`struct Key`**
  an EAPOL-Key body (RSN descriptor, a 16-byte MIC)
  - `info: u16`
  - `key_len: u16`
  - `replay: u64`
  - `nonce: [u8; 32]`
  - `iv: [u8; 16]`
  - `rsc: [u8; 8]`
  - `mic: [u8; 16]`
  - `data: Vec<u8>`

**`impl Key`**

- **`fn parse(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Key>`**
  a key body; None when it is shorter than its fixed part or its key data, or is no RSN
  descriptor
- **`fn body(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the body bytes
- **`fn pdu(&self, version: u8) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the whole EAPOL PDU (header with `version`, packet type EAPOL-Key, the body)
- **`fn version(&self) -> u16`**
  the key descriptor version (KDV_\*)
- **`fn has(&self, bits: u16) -> bool`**
- **`fn message(&self) -> Option<u8>`**
  which message of the 4-way handshake: 1 (Ack), 2 (MIC), 3 (Ack, MIC, Install), 4 (MIC,
  Secure); None for a group key message or a request

- **`fn mic_input(pdu: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`**
  the PDU with the MIC field set to zero: what the MIC covers (None when it holds no key
  body)

- **`fn set_mic(pdu: &mut [u8], mic: &[u8; 16])`**
  writes the MIC into a PDU made by Key::pdu

- **`struct Rsne`**
  the RSN element of a personal network: CCMP for group and pairwise traffic, one AKM
  - `akm: u8`
  - `caps: u16`

**`impl Rsne`**

- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the element with its id and length (22 bytes)
- **`fn parse(elems: &[u8]) -> Option<Rsne>`**
  the first RSN element of a list of elements (key data); one pairwise and one AKM suite
  of 00-0F-AC are read, the counts are little endian as in every element

- **`fn elements(b: &[u8]) -> Vec<(u8, &[u8])>`**
  the elements of a list: (id, contents); stops at one that does not fit

- **`fn kde_gtk(id: u8, gtk: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the GTK KDE: key id (0..3), transmit bit clear, the key

- **`fn kde_igtk(id: u16, ipn: u64, igtk: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  the IGTK KDE (management frame protection): key id (4 or 5), its packet number, the key

- **`fn kdes(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<(u8, &[u8])>`**
  the KDEs of key data: (type, contents after the type); other elements are left out

- **`fn pad_key_data(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  key data padded for the key wrap: 0xdd and zeros up to a multiple of 8, at least 16 bytes

### `netpkt/bgp.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/bgp.rs`](../lib/netpkt/bgp.rs)

```text
bgp -- BGP-4 messages byte for byte (RFC 4271): the 19-byte header with its marker, OPEN with
its optional parameters and the capabilities of RFC 5492 (multiprotocol IPv4 unicast of RFC
4760, route refresh of RFC 2918, 4-octet AS numbers of RFC 6793), UPDATE with withdrawn routes,
path attributes and NLRI, NOTIFICATION with the codes and subcodes of RFC 4271 and the Cease
subcodes of RFC 4486, KEEPALIVE and ROUTE-REFRESH; the checks of RFC 4271 6.1 to 6.3 as the
NOTIFICATION a receiver sends

  frame(stream)            the length of the first message of a TCP byte stream once it is
                           complete (Ok(None): more bytes needed) after the header checks of
                           6.1 (marker, length, type and the length of the type)
  BgpView::parse(b)        one message: kind(), len(), body(), marker_ok(); None when the
                           bytes are shorter than the header or than its length field
  Message::read(b, as4)    a whole message as a record (Err: the BgpErr whose NOTIFICATION a
                           receiver sends); to_bytes(as4) writes it with marker and length.
                           `as4`: the session negotiated 4-octet AS numbers (AS_PATH and
                           AGGREGATOR carry them)
  Open { version, asn, hold, id, params }   `asn` as on the wire (AS_TRANS for a 4-octet AS);
                           Open::new(asn, hold, id, caps) fills it in; caps(), as4(),
                           peer_as(), has_cap(code)
  OptParam::Caps(Vec<Cap>) / Other;  Cap::Mp { afi, safi }, RouteRefresh, As4(asn), Other
  Update { withdrawn, attrs, nlri }; Attr { flags, val } with Attr::new(val) (the flags the
                           RFCs give the type) and kind(); AttrVal::Origin, AsPath (segments),
                           NextHop, Med, LocalPref, AtomicAggregate, Aggregator, Communities,
                           As4Path, As4Aggregator, Other (unknown types byte for byte);
                           Update::get(kind), origin(), as_path(), next_hop(), med(),
                           local_pref(), communities()
  Segment { set, asns }    an AS_SET or AS_SEQUENCE; path_len(segs) counts a set as one AS
                           (9.1.2.2), path_text(segs) "65002 65003 {65010,65011}"
  Notification { code, sub, data };  error_name(code, sub), code_name(code)
  BgpErr { code, sub, data }   what a receiver refuses and the NOTIFICATION it sends for it;
                           text() in English
  prefix_len(p) / write_prefix / read_prefixes   NLRI: the length in bits, then the bytes needed
  as_path_4(value)         a dissector's guess whether an AS_PATH carries 4-octet numbers
  origin_code(o) / origin_name(o) / community_text(c) / afi_name / cap_name   for dissectors

Constants: PORT (179), VERSION, HDR_LEN, MAX_LEN, MARKER, the minimum lengths OPEN_MIN,
UPDATE_MIN, NOTIFICATION_MIN, ROUTE_REFRESH_LEN, the types T_*, OPT_CAPS, the capability codes
CAP_*, AFI_IPV4 / SAFI_UNICAST, AS_TRANS, the attribute flags F_* and types A_*, ORIGIN_*,
SEG_*, the error codes E_* with their subcodes (HE_*, OE_*, UE_*, CE_*).

The codec reads and writes; what needs the session (the peer's AS, its BGP identifier against
the own one, the hold time a speaker accepts, NEXT_HOP semantics, AS path loops, LOCAL_PREF
from an internal peer) is the speaker's business.  Attributes keep their flags and order, so a
message read and written again is the same bytes (the unused low four flag bits too); a
malformed AS4_PATH or AS4_AGGREGATOR is kept as Other (RFC 6793 6: attribute discard).  RFC
7606 (treat-as-withdraw) is not here: every error is a NOTIFICATION as RFC 4271 says.
```

```rust
/// the TCP port of BGP
PORT: u16 = 179
/// BGP version 4
VERSION: u8 = 4
/// the header (marker, length, type) and the longest message (RFC 4271 4)
HDR_LEN: usize = 19
MAX_LEN: usize = 4096
/// sixteen bytes of ones
MARKER: [u8; 16] = [0xFF; 16]
/// the shortest OPEN, UPDATE and NOTIFICATION, the length of ROUTE-REFRESH
OPEN_MIN: usize = 29
UPDATE_MIN: usize = 23
NOTIFICATION_MIN: usize = 21
ROUTE_REFRESH_LEN: usize = 23
/// message types
T_OPEN: u8 = 1
T_UPDATE: u8 = 2
T_NOTIFICATION: u8 = 3
T_KEEPALIVE: u8 = 4
T_ROUTE_REFRESH: u8 = 5
/// the optional parameter that carries capabilities (RFC 5492)
OPT_CAPS: u8 = 2
/// capability codes: multiprotocol (RFC 4760), route refresh (RFC 2918), 4-octet AS (RFC 6793)
CAP_MP: u8 = 1
CAP_ROUTE_REFRESH: u8 = 2
CAP_AS4: u8 = 65
/// the address family and sub-family of IPv4 unicast
AFI_IPV4: u16 = 1
SAFI_UNICAST: u8 = 1
/// the 2-octet AS a 4-octet one shows as to an old speaker (RFC 6793)
AS_TRANS: u16 = 23456
/// attribute flags
F_OPTIONAL: u8 = 0x80
F_TRANSITIVE: u8 = 0x40
F_PARTIAL: u8 = 0x20
F_EXTENDED: u8 = 0x10
/// attribute types
A_ORIGIN: u8 = 1
A_AS_PATH: u8 = 2
A_NEXT_HOP: u8 = 3
A_MED: u8 = 4
A_LOCAL_PREF: u8 = 5
A_ATOMIC_AGGREGATE: u8 = 6
A_AGGREGATOR: u8 = 7
A_COMMUNITIES: u8 = 8
A_AS4_PATH: u8 = 17
A_AS4_AGGREGATOR: u8 = 18
/// ORIGIN values
ORIGIN_IGP: u8 = 0
ORIGIN_EGP: u8 = 1
ORIGIN_INCOMPLETE: u8 = 2
/// AS_PATH segment types
SEG_SET: u8 = 1
SEG_SEQUENCE: u8 = 2
/// error codes (RFC 4271 4.5)
E_HEADER: u8 = 1
E_OPEN: u8 = 2
E_UPDATE: u8 = 3
E_HOLD: u8 = 4
E_FSM: u8 = 5
E_CEASE: u8 = 6
/// Message Header Error subcodes
HE_SYNC: u8 = 1
HE_LENGTH: u8 = 2
HE_TYPE: u8 = 3
/// OPEN Message Error subcodes (7: RFC 5492)
OE_UNSPECIFIC: u8 = 0
OE_VERSION: u8 = 1
OE_PEER_AS: u8 = 2
OE_ID: u8 = 3
OE_OPT_PARAM: u8 = 4
OE_HOLD: u8 = 6
OE_CAPABILITY: u8 = 7
/// UPDATE Message Error subcodes
UE_ATTR_LIST: u8 = 1
UE_UNRECOGNIZED: u8 = 2
UE_MISSING: u8 = 3
UE_FLAGS: u8 = 4
UE_LENGTH: u8 = 5
UE_ORIGIN: u8 = 6
UE_NEXT_HOP: u8 = 8
UE_OPTIONAL: u8 = 9
UE_NETWORK: u8 = 10
UE_AS_PATH: u8 = 11
/// Cease subcodes (RFC 4486)
CE_MAX_PREFIXES: u8 = 1
CE_SHUTDOWN: u8 = 2
CE_DECONFIGURED: u8 = 3
CE_RESET: u8 = 4
CE_REJECTED: u8 = 5
CE_CONFIG: u8 = 6
CE_COLLISION: u8 = 7
CE_RESOURCES: u8 = 8
```

- **`struct BgpErr`**
  what a receiver refuses: the code, subcode and data of the NOTIFICATION it sends
  - `code: u8`
  - `sub: u8`

**`impl BgpErr`**

- **`fn text(&self) -> String`**

  the name of a subcode ("Bad Peer AS"); the code's name where it has none

  bytes needed); Err with the NOTIFICATION of 6.1 for a bad header

- **`struct BgpView<'a>`**

**`impl<'a> BgpView<'a>`**

  the length are left out)

- **`fn len(&self) -> usize`**

  the prefixes of a withdrawn-routes or NLRI field; Err(Invalid Network Field) for a length
  above 32 or bytes that end early.  Bits after the length are dropped (the network form).

- **`enum Cap`**
  a capability (RFC 5492)

  - `RouteRefresh` -- route refresh (RFC 2918)
  - `As4(u32)` -- 4-octet AS numbers with the speaker's AS (RFC 6793)

- **`fn code(&self) -> u8`**

  an optional parameter of an OPEN
  - `Caps(Vec<Cap>)` -- capabilities (parameter type 2)
  - `Other { kind: u8, data: Vec<u8> }` -- another type, byte for byte (a receiver refuses it: Unsupported Optional Parameter)

- **`struct Open`**
  an OPEN message (RFC 4271 4.2)

  - `hold: u16`
  - `id: Ipv4`

- **`fn new(asn: u32, hold: u16, id: Ipv4, caps: Vec<Cap>) -> Open`**

  capabilities (none when `caps` is empty)
- **`fn caps(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Cap>`**
  every capability, in order
- **`fn has_cap(&self, code: u8) -> bool`**
- **`fn as4(&self) -> Option<u32>`**

- **`fn ipv4_unicast(&self) -> bool`**

  the body of an OPEN (6.2): the version, the optional parameters as their lengths say

- **`enum AttrVal`**

  - `LocalPref(u32)`
  - `AtomicAggregate`

  - `Communities(Vec<u32>)`

  - `As4Aggregator { asn: u32, id: Ipv4 }`
  - `Other { kind: u8, data: Vec<u8> }` -- a type this codec does not know (or a malformed AS4 attribute), byte for byte

- **`struct Attr`**

  - `flags: u8`

- **`fn as_path_4(v: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  a dissector's guess: the AS_PATH value reads as 4-octet numbers (a session between speakers
  with the capability) and not as 2-octet ones, or as both and the 2-octet reading gives AS 0
  (the high halves of 4-octet numbers)

  appends flags, type, length (two bytes with the extended length bit) and value

### `netpkt/tftp.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/tftp.rs`](../lib/netpkt/tftp.rs)

```text
tftp -- Trivial File Transfer Protocol packets (UDP port 69, RFC 1350) with the option
extension of RFC 2347 (OACK, error 8) and the options blksize (RFC 2348), timeout and tsize
(RFC 2349)

  TftpView::parse(b)        the opcode and the fields of each kind: file / mode / options
                            (RRQ, WRQ, OACK as NUL-terminated strings with their offsets),
                            block and data (DATA), block (ACK), code and message (ERROR)
  Packet                    Rrq / Wrq { file, mode, opts } | Data { block, data } |
                            Ack { block } | Error { code, msg } | Oack { opts }:
                            read(view) / parse(b) / to_bytes / opcode / opt(name)
  Packet::error_of(code)    an ERROR with the RFC's text of the code
  OP_* (1 .. 6), ERR_* (0 .. 8), op_name, error_name, BLOCK (512), BLKSIZE_MIN / _MAX,
  mode_known ("octet", "netascii", "mail"), to_netascii / from_netascii (RFC 764 line ends)
  looks_like(b)             the shape of a packet of a running transfer (DATA, ACK, ERROR,
                            OACK): RFC 1350 moves a transfer to new ports at once, so a
                            dissector without state knows it only by its bytes

A transfer is lock-step: every DATA block waits for its ACK, a block shorter than the block
size ends it (an empty one when the size is a multiple), block numbers count from 1 and roll
over after 65535.  Option names compare case-insensitively; values are decimal text.  Errors
of parse name what is wrong for a dissector (Bad).
```

```rust
OP_RRQ: u16 = 1
OP_WRQ: u16 = 2
OP_DATA: u16 = 3
OP_ACK: u16 = 4
OP_ERROR: u16 = 5
/// option acknowledgment (RFC 2347)
OP_OACK: u16 = 6
/// opcode and block number (DATA, ACK) or error code (ERROR)
TFTP_HDR: usize = 4
/// data bytes in a block without the blksize option
BLOCK: usize = 512
/// the block sizes RFC 2348 allows
BLKSIZE_MIN: u16 = 8
BLKSIZE_MAX: u16 = 65464
/// "Not defined, see error message (if any)."
ERR_UNDEFINED: u16 = 0
ERR_NOT_FOUND: u16 = 1
ERR_ACCESS: u16 = 2
ERR_DISK_FULL: u16 = 3
ERR_ILLEGAL: u16 = 4
ERR_UNKNOWN_TID: u16 = 5
ERR_EXISTS: u16 = 6
ERR_NO_USER: u16 = 7
/// option negotiation failed (RFC 2347)
ERR_OPTION: u16 = 8
```

- **`fn op_name(op: u16) -> &'static str`**
  the name of an opcode as capture tools show it

- **`fn error_name(code: u16) -> &'static str`**
  the meaning of an error code (RFC 1350 appendix, RFC 2347)

- **`fn mode_known(mode: &str) -> bool`**
  a transfer mode RFC 1350 defines (case-insensitive)

- **`fn to_netascii(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  bytes as netascii: LF becomes CR LF, a lone CR becomes CR NUL (RFC 764)

- **`fn from_netascii(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`**
  netascii back to bytes: CR LF is LF, CR NUL is CR

- **`enum Bad`**
  why bytes are no TFTP packet
  - `Short` -- shorter than its opcode and fixed fields
  - `Opcode(u16)` -- an opcode RFC 1350 and 2347 do not define
  - `Unterminated` -- a string field without its NUL
  - `OddOptions` -- an option name without a value

- **`type Span = (usize, usize)`**
  a NUL-terminated string field: its offset, its length without the NUL

- **`struct TftpView<'a>`**
  a received TFTP packet

**`impl<'a> TftpView<'a>`**

- **`fn parse(b: &'a [u8]) -> Result<TftpView<'a>, Bad>`**
  at least an opcode RFC 1350 or 2347 defines and the fields its kind has
- **`fn bytes(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
- **`fn opcode(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn block(&self) -> u16`**
  the block number of DATA and ACK
- **`fn data(&self) -> &'a [u8]`**
  the data of a DATA packet
- **`fn error_code(&self) -> u16`**
  the code of an ERROR
- **`fn error_msg(&self) -> String`**
  the message of an ERROR (up to its NUL)
- **`fn fields(&self) -> Vec<Span>`**
  the string fields after the opcode (RRQ, WRQ: file, mode, then option pairs; OACK: the
  pairs), offsets relative to the packet
- **`fn text(&self, s: Span) -> String`**
  a field as text

- **`enum Packet`**
  a TFTP packet to write (or one read)
  - `Rrq { file: String, mode: String, opts: Vec<(String, String)> }`
  - `Wrq { file: String, mode: String, opts: Vec<(String, String)> }`
  - `Data { block: u16, data: Vec<u8> }`
  - `Ack { block: u16 }`
  - `Error { code: u16, msg: String }`
  - `Oack { opts: Vec<(String, String)> }`

**`impl Packet`**

- **`fn read(v: &TftpView) -> Packet`**
- **`fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Packet, Bad>`**
  bytes as a packet
- **`fn error_of(code: u16) -> Packet`**
  an ERROR with the meaning of its code as the message
- **`fn opcode(&self) -> u16`**
- **`fn opt(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str>`**
  an option of a request or an OACK (the name ignores case)
- **`fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>`**

- **`fn looks_like(b: &[u8]) -> bool`**
  the bytes of a packet of a running transfer: a DATA block (at most BLKSIZE_MAX bytes), an
  ACK of exactly four bytes, an ERROR with a known code and a printable message, an OACK of
  option names and values

### `netpkt/ftp.rs`

Source: [`lib/netpkt/ftp.rs`](../lib/netpkt/ftp.rs)

```text
ftp -- the control connection of the File Transfer Protocol (TCP port 21, RFC 959): command
lines, replies with their multi-line form, the host-port of PORT and of the 227 reply to PASV,
EPRT and the 229 reply to EPSV (RFC 2428), FEAT's list (RFC 2389)

  Command { verb, arg }     Command::parse(line) (the verb in capitals, the argument as
                            typed), Command::new(verb, arg), to_line() ("USER anna\r\n")
  Reply { code, lines }     to_bytes(): one line "220 text", or "211-first" ... "211 last"
                            (the inner lines start with a space when they could look like
                            the end); is_final / is_ok (1xx preliminary, 2xx done, 3xx more)
  Lines                     cuts the bytes of a control connection into lines (CRLF, a lone
                            LF too), in any pieces as they arrive
  ReplyReader               the replies of a server from its bytes: push(bytes) -> Vec<Reply>
                            (a multi-line reply ends with a line of the same code and a space)
  host_port(text) / fmt_host_port(ip, port)   "h1,h2,h3,h4,p1,p2" (PORT's argument, 227's
                            numbers: host_port finds them anywhere in a reply's text)
  eprt(arg) / fmt_eprt(addr, port)            "|1|10.0.0.5|40001|", "|2|2001:db8::5|40001|"
  epsv_port(text) / fmt_epsv(port)            the "(|||port|)" of a 229 reply
  PORT_FTP (21), PORT_FTP_DATA (20), verb_known

Lines are UTF-8 or ASCII; RFC 959 allows Telnet sequences, which nobody sends here.  The
reply texts are the server's own words: clients go by the codes and the numbers of 227 and
229 only.
```

```rust
PORT_FTP: u16 = 21
/// the server's port of active data connections
PORT_FTP_DATA: u16 = 20
```

**`impl Reply`**

- **`fn is_ok(&self) -> bool`**

- **`fn is_intermediate(&self) -> bool`**
  3xx: the command waits for another (PASS after USER)

## cas

*content-addressed backup repositories: chunking, packs, signed encrypted snapshots, GC* -- crate root [`lib/cas/lib.rs`](../lib/cas/lib.rs)

```text
cas -- a content-addressed, deduplicating, encrypted chunk store (BackupCraft's repository
format "bcrepo-1")

  Repo::create(path, &CreateOptions) / Repo::open(path, Unlock::{Master, Passphrase,
       Recovery})                       one process holds a repository at a time (LOCK)
  repo.writer() -> Writer               put(kind, bytes) / put_stream(reader) -> chunk ids,
                                        finish() (packs and indexes are durable);
                                        .codec(c, level): this writer's compression
                                        (the repository's own is the default)
  repo.read_chunk(id) / read_tree(id)   repo.save_snapshot / load_snapshot / snapshot_ids /
                                        delete_snapshot (refused while immutable)
  repo.check(read_data, progress)       snapshots, signatures, references, every blob
  repo.gc(progress)                     mark & sweep, repack sparse packs
  repo.add_passphrase / set_recovery / set_immutable_days / trust_signer

Layout:  repo.json  data/<xx>/<pack>.pack  index/<pack>.idx  snapshots/<id>.snap  LOCK
Keys:    one random repository key, wrapped in repo.json for the server's master key, for
         passphrases (Argon2id) and for the recovery kit (sealed box); per purpose keys are
         derived from it with BLAKE3 derive_key (chunk ids, data, index, snapshots, gear).
Chunks:  id = BLAKE3-keyed(id key, plain) -> identical data is stored once, the ids reveal
         nothing without the key.  Commit order of a backup: packs (fsync) -> indexes
         (fsync) -> snapshot (atomic rename, directory sync); a crash leaves at most
         unreferenced packs, which gc removes.
```


### `cas/chunker.rs`

Source: [`lib/cas/chunker.rs`](../lib/cas/chunker.rs)

```text
chunker -- content-defined chunking (FastCDC with normalized chunking, level 2)

Boundaries depend on the content only, so an insertion early in a file moves one boundary
and leaves the later chunks (and their deduplication) intact.  The gear table is derived
from the repository key: chunk sizes do not reveal known files to someone who sees the
repository without its key.
```

- **`struct Chunker`**
  - `min: usize`
  - `avg: usize`
  - `max: usize`

**`impl Chunker`**

- **`fn new(gear_key: &[u8; 32], avg: usize) -> Chunker`**
  avg must be a power of two; min = avg / 4, max = avg \* 4
- **`fn cut(&self, data: &[u8], last: bool) -> Option<usize>`**
  the length of the first chunk of `data` (`last`: no more data follows)
- **`fn split(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<usize>`**
  split a whole buffer into chunk lengths

### `cas/pack.rs`

Source: [`lib/cas/pack.rs`](../lib/cas/pack.rs)

```text
pack -- blobs, pack files and their indexes

  blob     kind:u8 codec:u8 | nonce:24 | XChaCha20-Poly1305(data key, nonce,
           aad = chunk id ‖ kind ‖ codec, payload)       payload: plain, an LZ4 block or a
                                                         zstd frame (the codec byte says which)
  pack     "BCK1" | blobs ... | sealed index (as below) | len:u32 | "BCKI"
           (the trailer repeats the index: a lost index file can be rebuilt from the pack)
  index    "BCI1" | nonce:24 | XChaCha20-Poly1305(index key, aad = pack id, JSON
           [[id hex, offset, length, kind, raw length], ...])

Pack files are written to a temporary name, synced, renamed; then their index.  A crash
leaves at most a pack without an index (garbage that check reports and gc removes).
```

```rust
PACK_MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"BCK1"
PACK_TRAILER: &[u8; 4] = b"BCKI"
INDEX_MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"BCI1"
/// a pack is closed when it reaches this size
PACK_TARGET: usize = 32 << 20
BLOB_OVERHEAD: usize = 2 + 24 + 16
```

- **`type PackId = [u8; 16]`**
