## update

*signed app updates: check, download, apply at the next start, health marker, rollback* -- crate root [`lib/update/lib.rs`](../lib/update/lib.rs)

```text
update -- signed updates of an app: check, download, put in place at the next start, roll
back a version that does not start

  Config::new(app, version, url, keys)   the app's id and running version, the address of
                               its update.json and the trusted Ed25519 public keys (hex);
                               then dir (default data://update), exe, target, attempts,
                               restart, max_size, ca_pem, timeout_ms
  startup(&cfg) -> Startup     first thing in main (before ui::launch): puts a downloaded
                               update in place and restarts into it, counts the starts of a
                               new version, rolls back one that never reported healthy
  healthy(&cfg) -> bool        the health marker: the new version works (after its first
                               frame, for example); without it the next start rolls back
  Updater::new(cfg)            check() / download() / apply() (blocking), start_check() /
                               start_download() (a background thread, plat::wake() when
                               done), status() (phase, progress, error), cancel(), staged()
  state(&cfg), newer(a, b), target(), Manifest::parse, verify
  install(&cfg) -> Packaged     how the program is installed (plat::pkg::packaged; cfg.exe
                               set: Plain), which decides what an update is:
    Plain     exe / bundle / package entries of update.json (below)
    AppImage  the "appimage" entry: the .AppImage file ($APPIMAGE) is replaced as a whole
              (copied next to it, checked, renamed over it; the old file is the backup, the
              trial and the rollback as for an exe; restarted through the AppImage); a folder
              the user cannot write: check() fails with Error::ReadOnly.  A signed AppImage
              (.sha256_sig / .sig_key, appimagetool --sign) only takes an update signed by a
              key of its own key block (appimage.rs, pgp.rs)
    Flatpak   no update.json: the portal's update monitor (plat::pkg::FlatpakMonitor) --
              check() reports what it found (Kind::Flatpak), download() installs it
              (Update, Progress), apply() starts the newest version (Spawn) and ends this
              one; without the portal: Check::Managed(Manager::Flatpak, None)
    Msix      Check::Managed: App Installer (an .appinstaller: updated at the next start,
              with whether it knows of a newer version) or whoever installed the package
    Snap      Check::Managed(Manager::Snap, None)
  appimage_signature(path)     the embedded signature of an AppImage file (Signed)

The channel: update.json (UTF-8 JSON) and update.json.sig beside it (the Base64 Ed25519
signature over the exact bytes of update.json); tools/update_manifest.py writes both:
  {"format": 1, "app": "Kritzel", "version": "1.2.0", "date": 1760000000,
   "expires": 1762600000, "notes": "...",
   "files": [{"target": "windows-x86_64", "kind": "exe", "url": "Kritzel-1.2.0.exe",
              "size": 123456, "sha256": "<64 hex digits>"}, ...]}
kind "exe" replaces the program file, "bundle" is a JFA1 bundle of files relative to the
program's folder (the program and its modules), "package" an installer (.deb, setup) that
is only downloaded and checked (Updater::staged), "appimage" a whole AppImage (only for a
program running as one; entries of unknown kinds are left out).  A relative url is resolved
against the address update.json came from; redirects are followed (at most 5).

Checks: the signature against cfg.keys; "app" must be cfg.app; "expires" (unix seconds) not
passed; a version older than one a signed manifest named before is refused (replay); only a
newer version than cfg.version that was not rolled back is offered; the file's size and
SHA-256 while it downloads, and all of it again before it is put in place.  Connections go
through netio and plat::net, so the app's net.connect rules apply (a refused host:
Error::Denied and PERMDENY on stderr); https checks the server against the system's CAs
(plus cfg.ca_pem).  The signature protects the content, so http works too.

cfg.dir holds state (stage, version, from, starts, bad, seen), lock, partial/<sha256> (an
interrupted download, continued with a Range request), staged/ (update.json, its signature
and the file) and backup/ (the replaced files of the last update).  Putting an update in
place writes the program's folder: in an app with a PERMISSIONS manifest that needs
fs.write $EXE/** (an AppImage: fs.write $APPIMAGE/**); a folder of the system (/usr/lib,
Program Files) needs a "package" update.
```

### `update` crate root

Re-exports: `plat::pkg::Packaged`

- **`struct Config`**
  what the updater needs to know about the app
  - `app: String` -- the app's id as the manifest names it ("app")
  - `version: String` -- the running version
  - `url: String` -- the address of update.json (https://... or http://...)
  - `keys: Vec<[u8; 32]>` -- the trusted Ed25519 public keys (built into the app)
  - `dir: String` -- the folder of the updater's files (default "data://update")
  - `exe: String` -- the program file an update replaces ("" = the running exe)
  - `target: String` -- the system whose package is taken (default target())
  - `attempts: u32` -- starts of a new version without healthy() before it is rolled back (default 1)
  - `restart: bool` -- startup() and apply() restart the program after a change (default true; false: they
    return Startup::Applied / RollingBack and the caller restarts)
  - `max_size: u64` -- the largest package accepted (default 1 GiB)
  - `ca_pem: String` -- further CA certificates (PEM) for an https channel with its own CA
  - `timeout_ms: u32` -- the longest wait for the server (ms; default 60000)

**`impl Config`**

- **`fn new(app: &str, version: &str, url: &str, keys: &[&str]) -> Config`**
  the app's id and version, the address of update.json and the trusted public keys (64
  hex digits each; others are left out, so a channel without a valid key fails with
  Error::Config) -- the other fields at their defaults

- **`enum Error`**
  why a step failed
  - `Config(String)` -- no channel, no valid key or an invalid address
  - `Denied(String)` -- the app's PERMISSIONS do not allow the host (net.connect)
  - `Net(String)` -- connection, TLS or protocol failure
  - `Http(u16)` -- the server answered with another status than 200 / 206
  - `Signature` -- the signature of update.json matches no trusted key
  - `Manifest(String)` -- update.json is malformed or for another app
  - `Expired` -- the manifest's "expires" has passed
  - `Replay(String)` -- the manifest is older than one seen before (its version)
  - `Size { expected: u64, got: u64 }` -- the file has not the size of the manifest
  - `Hash` -- the file's SHA-256 is not the manifest's
  - `Incomplete { done: u64, total: u64 }` -- the connection ended early; what arrived is kept and the next download continues it
  - `Cancelled` -- stopped by cancel()
  - `Busy` -- another check, download or apply runs (this process or another one)
  - `Nothing` -- nothing to download or to apply
  - `Unsupported(String)` -- a package that is not put in place by the updater
  - `Io(String)` -- files could not be read or written
  - `ReadOnly(String)` -- the AppImage lies in a folder the user cannot write (the folder): it is not replaced
  - `Rejected(String)` -- the downloaded package is not taken: not an AppImage, or its signature does not follow
    the running one's (why)

- **`struct Offer`**
  a newer version the channel offers
  - `version: String`
  - `notes: String`
  - `date: i64` -- unix seconds (0: not given)
  - `size: u64` -- the package's size in bytes
  - `kind: Kind`
  - `staged: bool` -- it is downloaded already (staged)

- **`enum Check`**
  the answer of a check
  - `UpToDate` -- no newer version (or only one that was rolled back)
  - `NoPackage(String)` -- a newer version without a package for this system and installation (its version): an
    AppImage takes only "appimage" entries, a plain program none of them
  - `Available(Offer)` -- a newer version to download
  - `Managed(Manager, Option<bool>)` -- this installation is updated by its package system, not through update.json: who, and
    whether it knows of a newer version (None: it does not say)

- **`enum Manager`**
  who updates an installation that lib/update does not update itself (Check::Managed)
  - `AppInstaller` -- App Installer: the MSIX package came from an .appinstaller file and is updated as that
    file says (tools/pkg_msix.py: at the next start)
  - `Msix` -- an MSIX package without an .appinstaller (the Store, Add-AppxPackage): updated by
    whoever installed it
  - `Flatpak` -- Flatpak (flatpak update, a software centre): the portal's update monitor is missing
  - `Snap` -- snapd

- **`enum Startup`**
  what startup() did
  - `Normal` -- nothing to do
  - `Applied(String)` -- the staged version is in place; the program must restart into it (only with
    cfg.restart = false or when the restart failed)
  - `Trial(String)` -- this is a new version on trial: call healthy() once the app works
  - `RollingBack(String)` -- the new version never reported healthy and the old one is back; the program must
    restart (only with cfg.restart = false or when the restart failed)
  - `RolledBack(String)` -- the old version runs again because this new one failed (reported once)
  - `Failed(Error)` -- putting the staged update in place failed (a damaged one is dropped)

- **`enum Phase`**
  what an Updater is doing
  - `Idle`
  - `Checking`
  - `UpToDate` -- the last check found nothing newer
  - `Available` -- a newer version can be downloaded (Status::version)
  - `Downloading`
  - `Ready` -- downloaded and checked: put in place at the next start or by apply()
  - `Failed` -- the last step failed (Status::error)

- **`struct Status`**
  the state for a dialog or a status line
  - `phase: Phase`
  - `version: String` -- the offered or downloaded version
  - `notes: String`
  - `done: u64` -- bytes downloaded and the file's size
  - `total: u64`
  - `error: Option<Error>`

- **`struct Updater`**
  checks and downloads for one Config; clones share the same state

**`impl Updater`**

- **`fn new(cfg: Config) -> Updater`**
  an updater for cfg; a downloaded update (stage Staged) starts it in Phase::Ready
- **`fn config(&self) -> &Config`**
  the configuration it was made with
- **`fn status(&self) -> Status`**
  the current phase, progress and last error
- **`fn cancel(&self)`**
  stop a running download (it ends with Error::Cancelled; what arrived is kept)
- **`fn check(&self) -> Result<Check, Error>`**
  fetch update.json and its signature and check them (blocking)
- **`fn download(&self) -> Result<String, Error>`**
  download the package the last check() offered, check it and stage it for the next
  start (blocking; progress in status()) -> its version
- **`fn start_check(&self) -> bool`**
  check() on a background thread; plat::wake() (UIC_WAKE / E_WAKE) when it is done ->
  false while another background step runs
- **`fn start_download(&self) -> bool`**
  download() on a background thread; plat::wake() when it is done -> false while another
  background step runs
- **`fn busy(&self) -> bool`**
  whether a background step runs
- **`fn staged(&self) -> Option<(String, Kind, String)>`**
  the downloaded update: its version, kind and the OS path of its file (a "package" is
  installed from there by the app or the user)
- **`fn apply(&self) -> Result<Startup, Error>`**
  put the downloaded update in place now and restart into it (with cfg.restart the
  process ends here); a Flatpak: start the newest installed version (the portal's Spawn)
  and end this one

- **`fn install(cfg: &Config) -> Packaged`**
  how the running program is installed, which decides what an update is (cfg.exe set:
  Plain -- an explicit program file)

- **`fn startup(cfg: &Config) -> Startup`**
  at the start of the program, before its UI: a staged update is put in place and the
  program restarted into it; a new version on trial counts its start, and one that already
  had cfg.attempts starts without healthy() is rolled back (the old version restarted).
  Another process holding the updater's lock: Normal.

- **`fn healthy(cfg: &Config) -> bool`**
  the health marker: the new version on trial works.  Call it once the app is up (after its
  first frame, for example); true when it ended a trial.  Cheap when no trial runs.

### `update/appimage.rs`

Source: [`lib/update/appimage.rs`](../lib/update/appimage.rs)

```text
appimage -- an AppImage file as an update: the type-2 header, its embedded signature (the
sections .sha256_sig and .sig_key appimagetool --sign writes) and whether a new file may
follow the running one

  is_type2(path) -> bool             ELF with "AI\x02" at byte 8
  signature(path) -> Result<Signed, String>   No (no or empty sections), By(the signing key
                                     of the embedded key block, its fingerprints), Err: a
                                     signature that does not check
  follows(old, new) -> Result<(), String>   the rule of an update: a signed AppImage only
                                     takes one signed by a key of its own key block

The signed text is the SHA-256 of the whole file, with the bytes of both sections taken as
zeros, as 64 lower-case hex digits (appimagetool's digest; AppImageUpdate's validate checks
the same).  The armored signature and key stand NUL-padded in their sections.
```

- **`enum Signed`**
  what an AppImage's signature sections say
  - `No` -- not signed (no sections, or empty ones)
  - `By { signer: [u8; 20], keys: Vec<[u8; 20]> }` -- signed by `signer` (a key of the embedded block, whose fingerprints are `keys`)

- **`fn signature(path: &str) -> Result<Signed, String>`**
  the embedded signature of the AppImage at path

### `update/apply.rs`

Source: [`lib/update/apply.rs`](../lib/update/apply.rs)

```text
apply -- the state of an update in cfg.dir, putting a staged update in place, the trial of
the new version and the way back

  state(cfg) -> State          the file cfg.dir/state (key=value lines)
  startup(cfg) -> Startup      (lib.rs) first thing at program start
  healthy(cfg) -> bool         (lib.rs) the health marker

Every file of an update is written next to its target as NAME.jfupd-new; the old file is
copied to backup/files/ (backup/list: "R path" replaced, "N path" new), renamed away
(NAME.jfupd-old-<n>: Windows can rename a running exe, not replace it) and the new file takes
its name.  Leftover .jfupd-* files are removed at a later start, once no process uses them.
An AppImage update has one file, the .AppImage itself ($APPIMAGE): copied (and hashed on the
way) from staged/ as NAME.jfupd-new, checked as an AppImage whose signature follows the
running one's (appimage.rs), renamed over the old file (atomic on Linux); the old file is
the backup.  Large files are copied in pieces, never read whole.
```

- **`enum Stage`**
  where an update stands
  - `None` -- nothing pending
  - `Staged` -- downloaded and checked: put in place at the next start (or by Updater::apply)
  - `Trial` -- the new version runs on trial until healthy()
  - `Ok` -- the new version reported healthy() (the backup of the old one is kept)
  - `RolledBack` -- the new version failed and the old one is back; reported once by startup()

- **`struct State`**
  the file cfg.dir/state
  - `stage: Stage`
  - `version: String` -- the staged, new or rolled-back version
  - `from: String` -- the version that was running before it
  - `starts: u32` -- starts of the new version without healthy()
  - `kind: String` -- what the staged file is
  - `file: String` -- the staged file's name in staged/
  - `bad: Vec<String>` -- versions that were rolled back: never offered again
  - `seen: String` -- the newest version a signed manifest named (older manifests are refused: replay)

- **`fn state(cfg: &Config) -> State`**
  the state of cfg.dir (a missing or unreadable file: nothing pending)

### `update/fetch.rs`

Source: [`lib/update/fetch.rs`](../lib/update/fetch.rs)

```text
fetch -- the updater's HTTP(S): small files with redirects, and downloads that hash while
they write and resume an interrupted file with a Range request

  join(base, href) -> Option<Url>   a manifest's file address
  get(cfg, url, max) -> (final url, bytes)
  download(cfg, url, part, size, sha256, progress) -> Ok when part holds the whole file
```

- **`fn join(base: &Url, href: &str) -> Option<Url>`**
  href relative to base: an absolute http(s) address, "//host/..", "/path" or a name
  relative to base's folder

### `update/manifest.rs`

Source: [`lib/update/manifest.rs`](../lib/update/manifest.rs)

```text
manifest -- update.json: parse, check the signature, pick the package of this system,
compare versions

  Manifest::parse(bytes) -> Result<Manifest, String>   (no signature check; entries of a
                                          kind this version does not know are left out)
  Manifest::package_for(target, appimage) the entry for this system and installation
  verify(bytes, sig_text, keys) -> bool   the Base64 Ed25519 signature of update.json.sig
  target() -> "windows-x86_64" | "linux-x86_64" | "linux-aarch64" | ...
  newer(a, b) -> bool                     "1.10.0" > "1.9.2", "2.0.0" > "2.0.0-rc1"
```

```rust
/// the largest update.json read
MAX_MANIFEST: usize = 1 << 20
/// the largest update.json.sig read
MAX_SIG: usize = 4096
```

- **`enum Kind`**
  what a package of the manifest is
  - `Exe` -- the program file itself
  - `Bundle` -- a JFA1 bundle (tools/assetpack.py) of files relative to the program's folder
  - `Package` -- an installer (.deb, setup): downloaded and checked, installed by the app or the user
  - `AppImage` -- a whole AppImage: replaces the running AppImage's file ($APPIMAGE); only offered to a
    program that runs as an AppImage, which is offered nothing else
  - `Flatpak` -- an update of a Flatpak from its repository, through the Flatpak portal (never in a
    manifest: Offer::kind of a Flatpak)

**`impl Kind`**

- **`fn name(self) -> &'static str`**
  "exe", "bundle", "package", "appimage" or "flatpak"
- **`fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Kind>`**
  the kind of a name (name())

- **`struct Package`**
  one file of a manifest
  - `target: String` -- the system it is for (target())
  - `kind: Kind`
  - `url: String` -- as written in the manifest: relative to update.json's address, or absolute
  - `size: u64`
  - `sha256: [u8; 32]`

- **`struct Manifest`**
  a parsed update.json
  - `app: String` -- the app it is for (Config::app)
  - `version: String`
  - `date: i64` -- unix seconds (0: not given)
  - `expires: i64` -- unix seconds after which the manifest is refused (0: never)
  - `notes: String` -- release notes for the user
  - `files: Vec<Package>`

**`impl Manifest`**

- **`fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Manifest, String>`**
  parse update.json (format 1; the signature is not checked here) -> the reason when
  it is malformed
- **`fn package(&self, target: &str) -> Option<&Package>`**
  the package for a target (the first one)
- **`fn package_for(&self, target: &str, appimage: bool) -> Option<&Package>`**
  the package for a target and the way the program is installed: the first "appimage"
  entry for an AppImage (appimage = true), else the first entry of another kind

- **`fn verify(bytes: &[u8], sig_text: &[u8], keys: &[[u8; 32]]) -> bool`**
  whether sig_text (update.json.sig: the Base64 Ed25519 signature, blanks around it ignored)
  signs bytes with one of keys

- **`fn target() -> &'static str`**
  the system this program runs on, as the manifest names it: "windows-x86_64",
  "linux-x86_64", "linux-aarch64", "android-aarch64", "web-wasm32"

- **`fn newer(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool`**
  a is newer than b: the numbers before a '-' compared part by part ("1.10" > "1.9",
  missing parts are 0, a leading 'v' is ignored); with equal numbers a release is newer than
  a pre-release ("2.0.0" > "2.0.0-rc1"), pre-releases compare by SemVer's rules (numeric
  parts as numbers, lower than text parts; more parts win); "+build" is ignored; a version
  that does not parse is never newer and nothing is newer than it

## archive

*bounded ZIP32 containers (stored and DEFLATE)* -- crate root [`lib/archive/lib.rs`](../lib/archive/lib.rs)

```text
In-memory ZIP32 interchange. New native library code, independent of document/UI code.
Raw DEFLATE and CRC reuse the existing safe codec primitives; no paths are extracted.
ZipFs shows an archive as a read-only plat::vfs tree:
  plat::vfs::mount("pack", Arc::new(archive::ZipFs::new(&bytes, Limits::default())?))
  -> plat::read_file("pack://textures/a.png"), plat::File::open("pack://..", FO_READ),
  plat::fs::stat (size; mtime: the entry's DOS time, read as UTC)
```

### `archive` crate root

- **`struct Entry`**
  One decoded archive part with a normalized, relative UTF-8 name.
  - `name: String`
  - `data: Vec<u8>`

- **`struct Limits`**
  Bounds are checked before decompression or allocation of advertised sizes.
  - `entries: usize`
  - `part_bytes: usize`
  - `total_bytes: usize`
  - `archive_bytes: usize`

- **`enum Error`**
  Structural, integrity, feature or resource-limit failure.
  - `Invalid`
  - `Unsupported`
  - `Checksum`
  - `Limit`

- **`fn read(b: &[u8], limits: Limits) -> Result<Vec<Entry>, Error>`**
  Read stored/DEFLATE ZIP32 files. Reject encryption, multi-disk/ZIP64, ambiguous names,
  duplicate parts, overlapping local records, trailing payloads and CRC mismatches.

- **`fn write(entries: &[Entry], limits: Limits) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Deterministic stored ZIP32 writer (UTF-8 names, fixed DOS date 1980-01-01).

- **`struct ZipFs(plat::vfs::MemFs)`**
  A ZIP archive as a read-only plat::vfs provider (mount it under a scheme of its own). The
  parts are checked and decompressed once, within `limits`.

**`impl ZipFs`**

- **`fn new(b: &[u8], limits: Limits) -> Result<ZipFs, Error>`**
  Read every part of the archive; Invalid also for names that collide as file and folder.

## doc_core

### `doc_core` crate root

- **`type Id = u64`**
  Stable identity inside a document. IDs are never reused by an editing session.

- **`enum ParagraphChange`**
  A paragraph command applied atomically to a selection. Individual properties preserve
  each paragraph's other overrides; Format replaces the complete set of overrides.
  - `Style(ParagraphStyle)`
  - `Format(ParagraphFormat)`
  - `Properties(ParagraphFormat)`
  - `Tabs(TabStops)` -- Replace the effective tab list, preserving explicit suppression of inherited stops.
  - `Alignment(Alignment)`
  - `PageBreakBefore(bool)`

- **`enum ParagraphStyle`**

  - `Normal`
  - `Title`
  - `Heading1`
  - `Heading2`
  - `Named(u32)`

- **`enum Inline`**
  Text or a structured citation; a citation remains linked to a source after edits.
  - `Text(String)`
  - `StyledText { text: String, format: TextFormat, }`
  - `Citation { source: Id, locator: String, }`
  - `CitationCluster(Vec<CitationItem>)`
  - `Formula(Formula)` -- Bounded live arithmetic, using the containing table for cell references.
  - `Bibliography`
  - `NoteReference(Id)` -- Stable note identity; a note has exactly one anchor, in the main body.

**`impl Inline`**

- **`fn text(&self) -> Option<&str>`**
  Editable text, excluding generated citation and bibliography fields.
- **`fn format(&self) -> TextFormat`**
  Character overrides; plain text and fields inherit the paragraph style.
- **`fn with_format(text: String, format: TextFormat) -> Self`**
  Canonical text node: inherited formatting uses the compact plain-text variant.

- **`struct Paragraph`**
  A paragraph with stable identity and structured inline content.
  - `id: Id`
  - `style: ParagraphStyle`
  - `format: ParagraphFormat`
  - `content: Vec<Inline>`

- **`struct Document`**
  Document data. Public for codecs; validate() is mandatory at trust boundaries.
  - `tables: Vec<Table>`
  - `table_styles: Vec<TableStyle>`
  - `styles: Vec<StyleDefinition>`
  - `paragraphs: Vec<Paragraph>`
  - `sources: Vec<Source>`
  - `notes: Vec<Note>`
  - `page: PageSettings`

- **`enum Error`**
  Invalid structure, dangling citation, source in use, or a resource budget exceeded.
  - `Invalid`
  - `Missing`
  - `InUse`
  - `Limit`

**`impl Document`**

- **`fn source(&self, id: Id) -> Option<&Source>`**
  Lookup by stable source identity.
- **`fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  Validate identities, source references, XML-compatible text and conservative budgets.
- **`fn byte_size(&self) -> usize`**
  Approximate retained payload size for history budgets (including node overhead).
- **`fn citation_text(&self, source: Id, locator: &str) -> String`**
  Cached display text for a citation; this basic author/year rendering is not CSL/APA.
- **`fn paragraph_text(&self, p: &Paragraph) -> String`**
  Paragraph text including live citation labels.
- **`fn plain_text(&self) -> String`**
  Plain-text view used for counts and explicit text exports.
- **`fn bibliography(&self) -> Vec<String>`**
  Deterministic basic list of cited sources, including notes at their anchor position.

- **`enum Edit`**
  One atomic edit; invalid edits leave document, redo history and dirty state untouched.
  - `InsertFormula { paragraph:Id, inline:usize, offset:usize, formula:Formula }` -- Insert a live formula at a UTF-8 caret, retaining adjacent text and formatting.
  - `SetFormula { paragraph:Id, inline:usize, formula:Formula }` -- Replace a calculation field without touching its neighbours, as one undo step.
  - `InsertTable { paragraph: Id, offset: usize, rows: usize, columns: usize }`
  - `ChangeTable { table: Id, change: TableChange }`
  - `SetTableStyle { style: TableStyle, table: Option<Id> }`
  - `SetStyleDefinition(StyleDefinition)` -- Create or replace one definition; validation rejects cycles and dangling bases atomically.
  - `RemoveField { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, }` -- Remove one generated field by native position, including zero-width bibliography.
    Removing a note anchor removes its body in the same undo transaction.
  - `ReplaceStoryFragment { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, fragment: DocumentFragment, }` -- Replace a rich selection, including complete fields, in one atomic transaction.
    Imported identities are remapped and exactly identical sources are reused.
  - `FormatStoryParagraphs { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, change: ParagraphChange, }` -- Change all paragraphs touched by a story selection without changing their inline
    objects. An end caret at the beginning of the next paragraph excludes that paragraph.
  - `ReplaceStoryText { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, text: String, paragraph_breaks: bool, }` -- Replace a UTF-8 selection in one complete story (main body or one note). Newlines
    optionally create paragraphs; false keeps them as soft line breaks inside a run.
    Crossing generated fields is rejected atomically, including the paragraph structure.
  - `FormatStoryText { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, format: TextFormat, }` -- Apply character overrides over several paragraphs as a single history step.
  - `ReplaceStoryFormat { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, format: TextFormat, }` -- Replace all character overrides in a story range as one undoable edit.
    Default formatting clears overrides and restores paragraph-style inheritance.
    Text, paragraph styles and generated fields retain their original structure;
    selections intersecting generated fields are rejected before committing.
  - `ReplaceParagraphText { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, text: String, }` -- Replace a UTF-8 range across adjacent formatted runs; generated fields are protected.
  - `FormatParagraphText { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, format: TextFormat, }` -- Apply explicit character overrides across adjacent formatted runs as one transaction.
  - `SplitParagraphText { paragraph: Id, start: usize, end: usize, }` -- Split a selection across adjacent formatted runs into a new paragraph atomically.
  - `SplitParagraph { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, start: usize, end: usize, }` -- Replace a selection in one text run with a paragraph boundary. Formatting and all
    following fields/notes move intact; returns the new paragraph identity. A heading
    split at its end continues in Normal style. The new half never repeats a page break.
  - `JoinParagraphs { first: Id, second: Id, }` -- Join adjacent paragraphs in one story, retaining the first identity/style and every
    inline object. Matching character overrides at the seam coalesce into one text run.
  - `InsertNote { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, offset: usize, kind: NoteKind, text: String, }` -- Insert one note at a main-body UTF-8 text caret, preserving both text formatting and suffix.
  - `SetNoteKind { note: Id, kind: NoteKind, }` -- Convert a note without changing its identity, anchor or body.
  - `RemoveNote(Id)` -- Remove a note and its sole anchor in one undo transaction.
  - `FormatText { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, start: usize, end: usize, format: TextFormat, }` -- Format a UTF-8 range in one text run, preserving its prefix/suffix and field neighbors.
  - `SetParagraphFormat { paragraph: Id, format: ParagraphFormat, }`
  - `SetPage(PageSettings)`
  - `ReplaceMatch { found: TextMatch, expected: String, replacement: String, }` -- Replace a previously found range only if its text still matches the expected value.
  - `ReplaceAll { query: String, replacement: String, options: SearchOptions, }` -- One undo transaction for all matching text, excluding generated fields.
  - `SetText { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, text: String, }` -- Replace an editable run. An empty paragraph exposes virtual run zero; writing a
    nonempty value creates its first text run, while an empty value preserves the structure.
  - `SetStyle { paragraph: Id, style: ParagraphStyle, }`
  - `AddParagraph { after: Id, }`
  - `InsertBibliography { after: Id, }`
  - `RemoveParagraph(Id)`
  - `PutSource(Source)`
  - `ImportSources(Vec<Source>)` -- Import a complete list atomically, allocating IDs and skipping exact content duplicates.
  - `MergeSources(SourceMerge)` -- Merge two existing sources and redirect all citation occurrences in one transaction.
  - `RemoveSource(Id)`
  - `Cite { paragraph: Id, source: Id, locator: String, }`
  - `InsertCitation { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, offset: usize, items: Vec<CitationItem>, }` -- Insert a citation at a UTF-8 caret inside one editable run, preserving its formatting.
    The suffix is always retained as editable text, including insertion at the run end.
  - `UpdateCitation { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, items: Vec<CitationItem>, }` -- Replace an existing citation's items in a single undo transaction.
  - `ConvertCitationToText { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, }` -- Replace one citation field by its current display text, disconnecting its sources.
  - `RemoveCitation { paragraph: Id, inline: usize, }`

- **`struct Editor`**
  Editing session with a saved checkpoint and bounded snapshot history.

**`impl Editor`**

- **`fn new(doc: Document) -> Result<Self, Error>`**
  Create a validated editing session; loading starts with an empty history.
- **`fn document(&self) -> &Document`**
  Current immutable document.
- **`fn revision(&self) -> u64`**
  Changes on every successful content edit/undo/redo; suitable for a layout cache.
- **`fn state_id(&self) -> u64`**
  Identity of this history state. Unlike revision(), undo/redo restore this identity,
  allowing a view to restore transaction-associated caret positions without model data.
  Identities are local to one Editor session; no-op/failed edits do not change them.
- **`fn dirty(&self) -> bool`**
  Content differs from the last successfully saved checkpoint.
- **`fn mark_saved(&mut self)`**
  Call only after a successful durable write.
- **`fn can_undo(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether an undo step exists.
- **`fn can_redo(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether a redo step exists.
- **`fn undo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Undo a complete model edit, including source/citation changes.
- **`fn redo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Redo a complete model edit.
- **`fn apply(&mut self, edit: Edit) -> Result<Id, Error>`**
  Apply an edit; returns the created/affected identity. New sources use id=0.
- **`fn apply_checked(&mut self, edit:Edit,check:impl FnOnce(&Document)->Result<(),Error>)->Result<Id,Error>`**
  Validate an additional shared constraint before committing a transaction.
  A rejected edit leaves identities, history, saved state and revision untouched.

- **`fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), Error>`**

  - `paragraph: Id` -- Stable paragraph ID containing the field.
  - `inline: usize` -- Zero-based inline index of the field within its paragraph.

**`impl Inline`**

- **`fn citation(items: Vec<CitationItem>) -> Result<Self, Error>`**
  Create a bounded citation field, keeping simple single references in the legacy form.
  Source existence is checked when validating or applying the containing document.
- **`fn citation_items(&self) -> Option<Vec<CitationItem>>`**
  Owned edit draft for either citation representation; other inline nodes return None.

**`impl Document`**

- **`fn citation_cluster_text(&self, items: &[CitationItem]) -> String`**
  Basic author/year rendering of an ordered multi-source field; this is not CSL/APA.
  Prefixes/suffixes are literal. Author suppression hides people/corporations; title
  suppression hides the title fallback of anonymous sources. Locators use "S. ".
- **`fn cited_source_ids(&self) -> Vec<Id>`**
  Distinct cited source IDs in first-use order, scanning the document only once.
  Bibliography fields and unreferenced sources do not add IDs. Validate the document
  at trust boundaries; for valid documents at most 1,024 IDs are returned.
- **`fn source_uses(&self, source: Id) -> Vec<CitationLocation>`**
  Citation fields using a source, once per field in document order.

- **`enum SourceIssueKind`**

  - `MissingCreators` -- Neither personal authors nor a corporate author were supplied.
  - `MissingYear` -- The publication year is blank.
  - `MissingPublisher` -- A book has no publisher.

**`impl Document`**

- **`fn audit_sources(&self) -> Vec<SourceIssue>`**
  Inspect all sources, including uncited ones, without changing document or history.
  Hints never block source saving, mark the document dirty or claim style compliance.
  Results follow source order, then creators, year, type-specific field and access date.
  Whitespace-only fields are blank. Access dates are checked only for missing preceding
  components, not calendar validity; year-only and year/month dates are accepted.
  A valid document has at most 1,024 sources and fewer than 6,144 returned hints.

    Returns the final record's existing or new library ID, or zero for an empty import.
  - `Put(Source)` -- ID zero explicitly creates a source; a nonzero ID updates an existing source.
    Unlike import, explicit creation preserves intentionally identical records.
  - `Remove(Id)` -- Remove an existing library source without affecting copies in documents.

- **`fn can_undo(&self) -> bool`**

- **`fn can_redo(&self) -> bool`**

- **`fn undo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Undo one transaction without making any previously issued identity reusable.
- **`fn redo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Redo one transaction, preserving the same source identities and allocation watermark.

  The validated document contains at most 1024 sources, so at most 1023 are returned.

## doc_layout

*typographic paragraph flow and page layout* -- crate root [`lib/doc_layout/lib.rs`](../lib/doc_layout/lib.rs)

```text
Bounded paragraph flow and pagination in twips. New native functionality; no legacy counterpart.
Font measurement is supplied by the caller, so pagination is independent of zoom and GUI DPI.
```

### `doc_layout` crate root

- **`struct Metrics`**
  Font metrics in twips (1/20 point). Positive ascent/height and nonnegative descent.
  - `ascent: i32`
  - `descent: i32`
  - `height: i32`

- **`trait Measure`**
  A reusable measurement interface. Widths must be nonnegative, metrics positive and bounded.
  - `fn width(&mut self, text: &str, format: ResolvedFormat) -> i32`
    Measure a fragment at `format.display_size_half_points()`, without GUI zoom.
  - `fn metrics(&mut self, format: ResolvedFormat) -> Metrics`
    Return glyph metrics at `format.display_size_half_points()`, in twips.
    The layout itself accounts for the script baseline displacement.

- **`struct Fragment`**
  A text fragment positioned on a page in twips, ready for the caller's renderer.
  - `leader: doc_core::TabLeader` -- Visual fill for a tab; `text` remains empty and its source is the original tab.
  - `source: Option<(usize, usize)>` -- UTF-8 range in Document::text_projection; None for generated note-number prefixes.
  - `text: String`
  - `format: ResolvedFormat`
  - `x: i32`
  - `baseline: i32`
  - `width: i32`

- **`struct Line`**
  A line with a stable paragraph target for navigation and hit testing.
  - `cell: Option<Id>` -- Owning table cell, or `None` for body and note text.
  - `bar_tabs: Vec<i32>` -- Absolute page x positions of bar tab rules, in twips.
  - `start: usize` -- Start/end in the paragraph's displayed UTF-8 text, excluding an explicit line break.
  - `end: usize`
  - `paragraph: Id` -- Document paragraph ID, or zero for a generated non-editable heading.
  - `x: i32` -- Aligned start in twips, including an empty line's insertion point.
  - `top: i32`
  - `height: i32`
  - `fragments: Vec<Fragment>`

- **`struct Page`**
  One page; an empty document still produces one page.
  - `cells: Vec<CellBox>`
  - `lines: Vec<Line>`
  - `separators: Vec<Separator>` -- Page-bottom rules above footnotes; empty on pages without footnotes.

- **`struct CellBox`**
  A table cell rectangle in page twips, shared by paint, hit testing and resizing.
  - `edges: Vec<CellEdge>` -- Shared edges resolved per adjacent grid segment; offsets are relative to this box.
  - `repeated: bool` -- Display instance of an existing header cell; never a second document cell.
  - `table: Id`
  - `cell: Id`
  - `row: usize`
  - `column: usize`
  - `paragraph: Id`
  - `row_span: usize`
  - `column_span: usize`
  - `last_row_height: u32`
  - `row_end: bool` -- False for a cell fragment ending at a page break instead of its grid row boundary.
  - `rect: [i32;4]`
  - `fill: Option<u32>`
  - `border_width: u16`
  - `border_color: u32`

- **`struct Separator`**
  A horizontal rule separating footnote content from the main page text, in twips.
  - `x: i32`
  - `y: i32`
  - `width: i32`

- **`struct Layout`**
  Laid-out document; page coordinates do not change when the view zoom changes.
  - `settings: PageSettings`
  - `pages: Vec<Page>`

- **`enum Error`**
  Invalid model/measurements or exceeded expansion, fragment or page budget.
  - `Model(doc_core::Error)`
  - `Metrics`
  - `Limit`

**`impl Layout`**

- **`fn paragraph_at(&self, page: usize, y: i32) -> Option<Id>`**
  Hit-test the vertical extent of a line on a page, in page-relative twips.

- **`fn paginate(d: &Document, measure: &mut impl Measure) -> Result<Layout, Error>`**
  Paginate a validated document. Handles formatting runs, whitespace, tabs, line/page breaks,
  paragraph spacing/indents, alignment and heading keep-with-next when it fits on one page.
  Footnotes reserve page-bottom space with continuations; endnotes follow the main text.
  An anchor line and the first line of every note it references must fit on the same page.
  A same-line group that cannot meet that requirement without reordering note bodies fails
  with `Error::Limit`; notes are never silently omitted.
  Rectangular tables flow by rows. No shaping, bidirectional algorithm or Word-identical pagination is claimed.

## doc_io

*conservative DOCX interchange and bounded file I/O* -- crate root [`lib/doc_io/lib.rs`](../lib/doc_io/lib.rs)

```text
Conservative DOCX interchange for the initial document model. New native library code.
Unrepresentable content is rejected before exposing an editable document. No VBA support.
```

### `doc_io` crate root

- **`enum Error`**
  Failure with the unsupported part/element included for a useful UI explanation.
  - `Io`
  - `Limit`
  - `Invalid`
  - `Archive(archive::Error)`
  - `Xml(xml::Error)`
  - `Unsupported(String)`
  - `Model(doc_core::Error)`

- **`fn encode_docx(d: &Document) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Serialize a validated document to a deterministic DOCX package. Sources are native
  bibliography custom XML; citations are CITATION fields with cached display text.
  Footnotes and endnotes use their standard parts and continuous decimal numbering.

- **`fn decode_docx(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Document, Error>`**
  Read the initial editable DOCX profile. Unknown package parts, layout, formatting,
  relationships, fields and source fields are rejected, never silently discarded.
  Full Word interoperability is deliberately not claimed by this early codec.

- **`fn read_file(path: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Bounded whole-file read; refuses oversized files before allocation, including short reads.

- **`fn load_docx(path: &str) -> Result<Document, Error>`**
  Load a DOCX without altering the caller's current editing session on failure.

- **`fn save_docx(path: &str, d: &Document) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  Encode completely before the platform's temporary-file/rename write.

```text
Shared Word bibliography XML codec: used by DOCX and standalone source lists.
```

- **`fn encode_sources(sources: &[Source]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Encode supported sources as Word Sources.xml, with document-local jf&lt;ID> tags.
  Input IDs must be unique and nonzero. Output is UTF-8, without external resources.

- **`fn decode_sources(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Source>, Error>`**
  Decode a complete standalone Word source list. External tags are validated but remapped
  to sequential IDs; use Edit::ImportSources to allocate identities in an existing document.
  Unrepresented fields/types abort the whole import; no partial or silent content import.

- **`fn load_sources(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Source>, Error>`**

- **`fn save_sources(path: &str, sources: &[Source]) -> Result<(), Error>`**

### `doc_io/bibtex.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/bibtex.rs`](../lib/doc_io/bibtex.rs)

```text
Bounded, explicit Unicode BibTeX interchange subset. New native library code.
Syntax reference: Oren Patashnik, BibTeXing, https://texdoc.org/serve/btxdoc/0.
This is a metadata codec, not a TeX interpreter or a BibLaTeX style processor.
```

- **`fn decode_bibtex(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Source>, Error>`**
  Decode a bounded Unicode BibTeX subset (@book, @article, @online and web @misc).
  Values may be braced, quoted or numeric. Names use Family, Given, single-token
  family names, or one braced corporation. UTF-8 and BOM-marked UTF-16 are accepted.
  Entry keys are validated and remapped to sequential IDs, not retained as metadata.
  Unsupported fields, TeX commands, case protection, macros and suffixes abort the
  entire import. Limits: 4 MiB input, 1024 sources, 64 authors, 4096 bytes per scalar,
  2 MiB retained model. ASCII field whitespace follows BibTeX normalization.

- **`fn encode_bibtex(sources: &[Source]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Encode the representable Source subset as deterministic UTF-8 BibTeX.
  Keys are jf&lt;ID>; IDs must be nonzero, unique and below 0x7fff_ffff. Separate middle
  names, external IDs, language, short titles and other unmapped metadata are errors.
  Export validates the entire list and refuses values whose meaning/spacing would
  change. Unicode is emitted directly; no TeX commands, resource loading or execution.

### `doc_io/clipboard.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/clipboard.rs`](../lib/doc_io/clipboard.rs)

```text
Bounded rich clipboard interchange. New native code, no assembly counterpart.
RTF control syntax follows Microsoft's RTF specification; this is a supported profile,
not a general RTF file editor. Internal structured fragments use the DOCX codec instead.
```

- **`fn clipboard_rtf_encode(d: &Document) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Encode body paragraphs as RTF 1 with explicit resolved character formatting, RGB colors,
  paragraph alignment, twip spacing/indents and Unicode. Hard paragraphs and soft breaks
  remain distinct. Fields and note anchors become their visible text; source/note metadata
  and style identities are not transferred. Font families and effective formatting remain.
  Use DOCX for a structured internal copy including the style graph.
  CRLF and lone CR inside text normalize to a single soft break.
  The output is bounded to 16 MiB and color tables to 1024 entries.

- **`fn clipboard_html_encode(d: &Document) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Encode a raw UTF-8 HTML clipboard fragment with inline CSS for resolved character and
  paragraph formatting. No CF_HTML envelope is included: that belongs to the platform
  clipboard layer. Font families use escaped CSS names; fields/anchors become visible text and
  source/note metadata stays in the private DOCX format. The result is bounded to 16 MiB.
  Floating tables carry versioned exact anchors plus CSS float fallback; page units are twips.

- **`fn clipboard_rtf_decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Document, Error>`**
  Decode the bounded RTF clipboard profile into validated, directly formatted paragraphs.
  Accepts group-scoped formatting, Windows single-byte text (874/1250–1258), Unicode/surrogate escapes, colors,
  relative line spacing, twip paragraph metrics, font family names and cached field results.
  Language, style identities and metadata map to model defaults. Unknown ignorable destinations are
  skipped; unsupported visible content (including pictures, lists and objects),
  unsupported encodings or typography and malformed input are rejected atomically.
  Only direct formatting is read: implicit Normal-style/default-character properties in
  metadata are not resolved and fall back to RTF defaults (12pt, automatic color). Other
  named-style references are rejected. This profile is intended for resolved rich selections.
  Rectangular and nested table grids, row/column merges, headers, fills and cell borders are read.
  Limits: 16 MiB input, 2 MiB expanded text, 64 groups, 1024 colors, 256 fonts, 4M tokens.

### `doc_io/html_import.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/html_import.rs`](../lib/doc_io/html_import.rs)

- **`fn clipboard_html_decode(bytes:&[u8])->Result<Document,Error>`**
  Decode a UTF-8 HTML clipboard fragment into editable paragraphs and nested tables.
  Handles inline text/CSS, table grids, merged cells, headers, borders and table positions.
  JFLib's versioned data attributes retain exact twip anchors and document page settings.
  Input is bounded to 16 MiB, 2 MiB text, 64 element levels and eight table levels.
  Active content and metadata are ignored; external resources are never requested.

### `doc_io/library.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/library.rs`](../lib/doc_io/library.rs)

```text
Native source-library persistence: strict XML, optimistic conflict detection and recovery.
New shared functionality; no user-profile policy or application UI belongs in this layer.
```

- **`fn encode_source_library(library: &SourceLibrary) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Encode the native version-one source library, preserving source IDs and their high-water mark.

- **`fn decode_source_library(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<SourceLibrary, Error>`**
  Decode the complete native source-library format; future versions and unknown data fail closed.

- **`enum LibraryStoreError`**
  Persistent-library failures distinguish stale content, a held lock and codec rejection.
  - `Io` -- A path could not be inspected, read, backed up or atomically replaced.
  - `Busy` -- The cooperative lock could not be acquired (busy or unavailable).
  - `Conflict` -- The file has changed since this store's successful open, reload or save.
  - `Codec(Error)` -- The current file, backup or proposed model is outside the supported native format.

- **`struct LibraryStore`**
  A validated source library and the exact file snapshot used for optimistic concurrency.
  Opening and reloading never write. Saving uses a sibling lock and atomic platform writes.

- **`struct LibraryRecovery`**
  A recovery preview with exact current-file and backup snapshots, safe to keep across a dialog.
  Restoring fails if either reviewed file changes before the caller confirms the operation.

**`impl LibraryRecovery`**

- **`fn library(&self) -> &SourceLibrary`**
  The planned restored model, retaining the greater ID high-water mark of valid current XML.
- **`fn restore(&self) -> Result<LibraryStore, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Restore the reviewed backup under the library lock, preserving replaced bytes in `.damaged`.

**`impl LibraryStore`**

- **`fn open(path: &str) -> Result<Self, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Open an existing valid library, or an empty in-memory library when the path is absent.
  A malformed existing file is an error and is never replaced by an empty model.
- **`fn library(&self) -> &SourceLibrary`**
  The last successfully opened, reloaded or saved library.
- **`fn path(&self) -> &str`**
  The configured native library filename.
- **`fn save(&mut self, library: &SourceLibrary) -> Result<(), LibraryStoreError>`**
  Validate fully, acquire the sibling lock, compare the original bytes, then save atomically.
  An existing valid version is backed up to `.bak` before replacement; backup failure aborts.
- **`fn reload(&mut self) -> Result<(), LibraryStoreError>`**
  Read and validate the current file; on any failure this store keeps its previous state.
- **`fn restore_backup(&mut self) -> Result<(), LibraryStoreError>`**
  Restore the validated `.bak` only if the current file still matches this store's snapshot.
  The replaced bytes are retained in `.damaged`; the good `.bak` is never overwritten.
- **`fn inspect_backup(path: &str) -> Result<SourceLibrary, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Read a backup for review without changing the current file or creating any paths.
- **`fn prepare_recovery(path: &str) -> Result<LibraryRecovery, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Read a valid backup and current bytes for explicit recovery, including malformed current XML.
  This read-only preview can later restore exactly those reviewed snapshots.
- **`fn restore_backup_if(&mut self, expected: &SourceLibrary) -> Result<(), LibraryStoreError>`**
  Restore only the backup model the caller previously inspected; changes return `Conflict`.
- **`fn recover(path: &str) -> Result<Self, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Recover from a malformed current file by restoring a validated `.bak` under the same lock.
  Current bytes are retained in `.damaged` before replacement; neither an unreadable nor an
  oversized current file is overwritten because an exact comparison cannot be established.
  Valid current XML retains its ID high-water mark. A malformed file cannot supply that mark.
- **`fn recover_if_backup( path: &str, expected: &SourceLibrary, ) -> Result<Self, LibraryStoreError>`**
  Recover only the backup model the caller previously inspected, preventing a stale preview.

### `doc_io/preservation.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/preservation.rs`](../lib/doc_io/preservation.rs)

```text
Bounded OPC inspection and original-byte preservation for foreign Word documents.
New native library code. Unrepresented content is never exposed as an editable model.
```

- **`enum DocxMode`**
  Whether the entire document is represented by the editable model.
  - `Editable` -- Every supported package component has passed the strict editable codec.
  - `Preserved` -- The original package is retained; the text excerpt is not an editable conversion.

- **`struct DocxReport`**
  Deterministic inspection results for a bounded, structurally checked DOCX package.
  - `mode: DocxMode` -- Editing capability; preservation does not imply rendering or editing compatibility.
  - `main_part: String` -- Main document part resolved through the package relationship.
  - `part_count: usize` -- Number of ZIP parts, including content types and relationships.
  - `diagnostics: Vec<String>` -- Human-readable reasons and feature descriptions, capped at 64 distinct entries.
  - `preview_truncated: bool` -- The reading excerpt reached its independent paragraph or text limit.

- **`struct DocxFile`**
  A DOCX session retaining its exact original archive alongside an optional full model.
  Unknown features remain intact; individually proven text leaves may be edited without
  model conversion. Saving without edits returns the original bytes, including compression,
  ordering, metadata, images, fields and unknown extension parts.

**`impl DocxFile`**

- **`fn open(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, Error>`**
  Inspect a conventional, unencrypted DOCX with bounded ZIP/XML processing.
  Macro-enabled main parts or VBA payloads are rejected. External relationships are
  retained as data only; this library never follows links or executes embedded content.
- **`fn load(path: &str) -> Result<Self, Error>`**
  Read and inspect a file, refusing archives over 32 MiB before allocation.
- **`fn document(&self) -> Option<&Document>`**
  Entire editable document, or `None` when any unsupported content must be preserved.
- **`fn preview(&self) -> &[String]`**
  Main-story plain-text excerpt, excluding separate headers, footers and note parts.
  This deliberately does not claim layout fidelity.
  Field instructions, deleted revisions and unsupported alternate representations
  are omitted; cached visible field text and table-cell paragraphs may be included.
- **`fn report(&self) -> &DocxReport`**
  Original package's capability and compatibility diagnostics.
- **`fn text_runs(&self) -> &[crate::DocxTextRun]`**
  Safe individual text leaves in the preserved main story and related headers, footers,
  footnotes and endnotes. Parts resolve through OPC relationships and content types.
  Signed/protected packages, fields, revisions and content controls are not editable;
  a complex field or tracked revision disables its whole containing story part.
- **`fn replace_text( &mut self, index: usize, expected: &str, replacement: &str, ) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  Replace exactly one eligible text leaf, verifying its current text first.
  Paragraph/run structure and every other package payload remain unchanged.
- **`fn dirty(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether preserved text differs from the last saved checkpoint.
- **`fn revision(&self) -> u64`**
  Monotonic preserved-text revision, including successful undo and redo operations.
  Saving and replacing text with identical text leave the revision unchanged.
- **`fn mark_saved(&mut self)`**
  Establish the saved checkpoint after a successful save, retaining undo history.
- **`fn undo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Undo the most recent preserved text edit, within the bounded history.
- **`fn redo(&mut self) -> bool`**
  Redo the next preserved text edit.
- **`fn can_undo(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether an earlier preserved text edit is available.
- **`fn can_redo(&self) -> bool`**
  Whether an undone preserved text edit is available.
- **`fn encode(&self, document: Option<&Document>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Produce original bytes for unchanged content, or serialize a changed fully
  represented model. Passing a model to a preservation-only session is an error.
  None saves preserved text edits if present, otherwise copies the original exactly.
- **`fn save(&self, path: &str, document: Option<&Document>) -> Result<(), Error>`**
  Encode before atomic temporary-file/rename writing; a failed edit cannot overwrite
  a destination. Copying a preserved document retains every original archive byte.

### `doc_io/preserved_text.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/preserved_text.rs`](../lib/doc_io/preserved_text.rs)

```text
Provenance-preserving edits of individual Word text leaves, independent of the model.
Original XML syntax, run properties and every unrelated package payload are retained.
```

- **`struct DocxTextRun`**
  An individually editable text leaf in an original Word story part.
  - `index: usize` -- Stable zero-based identifier accepted by DocxFile::replace_text.
  - `part: String` -- Original OPC part path; shared headers are exposed only once.
  - `story: DocxStory` -- The containing story, resolved from the main part's relationship and content type.
  - `note_id: Option<i64>` -- OOXML note identity, not its rendered number. None for the main story and headers/footers.

### `doc_io/ris.rs`

Source: [`lib/doc_io/ris.rs`](../lib/doc_io/ris.rs)

```text
Bounded RIS bibliography interchange. New native codec, no legacy counterpart.
Tag semantics: Clarivate RIS / primary Zotero RIS translator mapping; see public API scope.
```

- **`fn decode_ris(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Source>, Error>`**
  Decode a complete bounded RIS list: BOOK/JOUR/ELEC, people in AU/A1 order,
  TI/T1 (BOOK: BT), PY/Y1 year only, PB/CY/ET, JOUR JF/JO/T2, ELEC T2,
  VL/IS/SP/EP (not ELEC), UR/DO, SN/ST/N1/LA and Y2 access date.
  UTF-8/BOM and BOM UTF-16, LF/CRLF and multiline values are accepted. Continuations
  strip one six-space indent; other continuation text is preserved with LF.
  ID is validated then remapped sequentially; use Edit::ImportSources for document IDs.
  No corporate/suffix inference, role conversion, abstract/keyword/attachment dropping,
  or publication-date truncation. Unknown or duplicate scalar tags abort the whole list.
  DOI occupies the URL only when a safe doi.org URL and any UR agree. LA is kept verbatim.
  Limits: 4 MiB encoded/decoded input, 4096 tags, 1024 records, 4096 bytes per field,
  64 authors per record and 2 MiB retained model. No input causes filesystem/network access.

- **`fn encode_ris(sources: &[Source]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`**
  Export deterministic UTF-8 RIS with CRLF and indented continuation lines.
  Only fields represented by decode_ris are accepted; source IDs are local and omitted.
  Corporate authors, separately stored middle names, external GUIDs, incompatible
  type-specific fields and non-year publication dates produce record/tag diagnostics.
  People with commas or outer whitespace in name components cannot be emitted faithfully.
  Validation includes decoding the complete result and model equality (except source IDs),
  so no partial output or silently omitted metadata is ever returned.

*the runtime parts apps use: SSE / x87 float semantics, CPU features, locks, crash records* -- crate root [`lib/rt/lib.rs`](../lib/rt/lib.rs)

```text
rt -- the runtime under everything: allocator, memory intrinsics, exact SSE float
semantics, the minimal OS calls the runtime itself needs, panic handling.

  rt::os::{pages_alloc, pages_free, write_stdout, write_stderr, exit, yield_now}   (and on
  Linux the raw syscall helpers plat builds on)
  rt::fx   cvtt / cvt / sqrt / minss / maxss / floor_i / ceil_i / div255
  rt::x87  the extended-precision steps of f64 <-> decimal text (ini.s), fpatan
  rt::sync SpinLock
  rt::cpu  CPU feature bits (CPUID, cached; force_baseline for --simd sse2)
  rt::crash the crash hook, CrashInfo, report (exit 3) -- also for panics
  rt::boot  what build_rs.py builds into a program (name, manifest, assets) for plat's start
  rt::main!(body)  the entry symbol of console programs (boot first, then body)
  rt::VERSION, VERSION_MAJOR / _MINOR / _PATCH   the library's version (lib/VERSION, SemVer;
           docs/VERSIONING.md), also as plat::VERSION and ui::VERSION
  rt::app_version!()  the app's own version (version= of apps/NAME/PACKAGE)

One of the four crates that may contain `unsafe` (rt, simd, plat, plugin).
```

### `rt` crate root

```rust
/// the library's version, "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH" (lib/VERSION; docs/VERSIONING.md says what a
/// change of each part promises).  Not the app's version: that is `rt::app_version!()`.
VERSION: &str = include_str!("../VERSION").trim_ascii()
/// the first number of VERSION (incompatible API changes; while 0, the MINOR number counts them)
VERSION_MAJOR: u32 = version_part(VERSION, 0)
/// the second number of VERSION
VERSION_MINOR: u32 = version_part(VERSION, 1)
/// the third number of VERSION
VERSION_PATCH: u32 = version_part(VERSION, 2)
```

- **`app_version!(...)`**
  The app's own version: `version=` of apps/NAME/PACKAGE, which build_rs.py hands to rustc as
  JFGUI_VERSION (every program of the app); "0.0.0" without one.  An expression of type
  \\`&'static str\\`: \\`const APP_VERSION: &str = rt::app_version!();\\`, \\`update::Config::new(app,
  rt::app_version!(), ..)\\`.

- **`main!(...)`**
  Define the common app entry symbol without requiring the GUI crate in headless tools.  It
  first hands what build_rs.py built in (boot.rs: the app's name, its manifest, its assets)
  to the platform layer, which installs them as ui::main! does; a refused manifest ends the
  program with exit code 2.

**`mod portable`**

Portable arithmetic, available on native targets for exact backend comparisons.

```text
boot -- what build_rs.py builds into a program, handed to the platform layer before the
program's own code runs

                                   folder name), JFGUI_PERMISSIONS (apps/NAME/PERMISSIONS or
```

### `rt/cpu.rs`

Source: [`lib/rt/cpu.rs`](../lib/rt/cpu.rs)

```text
cpu -- CPU feature detection for SIMD dispatch                             [src/core/cpu.s]

  features() -> CPU_* bits     cached; SSE2 is the baseline and has no bit
  force_baseline()             report 0 from now on (plat calls it at process start for
                               `--simd sse2`: baseline kernels only, to compare results)
  cpuid(leaf) -> CpuidResult

CPU_AVX2 and CPU_FMA are only reported when the OS saves the YMM state (CPUID.1:ECX.OSXSAVE
and XGETBV(0) bits 1 and 2).  Thread safe: every caller computes the same cached value.
Lives in rt so that simd (which may not depend on plat) dispatches on the same bits.
```

```rust
CPU_SSE41: u32 = 1
CPU_AVX2: u32 = 2  // AVX2 + OS-enabled YMM state
CPU_FMA: u32 = 4  // FMA3 + OS-enabled YMM state
CPU_POPCNT: u32 = 8
CPU_BMI2: u32 = 16
```

- **`fn cpuid(leaf: u32) -> CpuidResult`**

- **`fn features() -> u32`**
  CPU_\* bits (cached)  [cpu_features]

- **`fn force_baseline()`**
  report no optional features from now on (`--simd sse2`)

### `rt/crash.rs`

Source: [`lib/rt/crash.rs`](../lib/rt/crash.rs)

```text
crash -- crash reports: the hook an app installs, the record the platform fills  [docs/modules/CRASH.md]

  set_hook(Some(f))      f(&CrashInfo) runs once when the process crashes or panics, after
                         the stderr line and before the process ends with exit code 3.  A
                         crash inside it (or a second crashing thread) ends the process at
                         once; a stack overflow skips it.
  set_pre_hook(Some(f))  the library's part (plat::log: the newest log lines), before the
                         app's hook; the same rules
  report(&info) -> !     the end of every crash (the platform's fault handlers, the panic
                         handler): the pre-hook, the hook, then exit(3)
  StackText<N>           a fixed buffer for core::fmt -- crash paths do not allocate (the
                         allocator lock may be held by the crashing thread)

Rust adds one kind, CK_PANIC: the panic message is in CrashInfo::msg.
```

```rust
CK_ACCESS: u32 = 1  // access violation / SIGSEGV
CK_ILLEGAL: u32 = 2  // illegal or privileged instruction
CK_DIVIDE: u32 = 3  // integer division by zero / overflow, SIGFPE
CK_BUS: u32 = 4  // SIGBUS, misalignment, in-page error
CK_STACK: u32 = 5  // stack overflow (no hook: there is no stack left)
CK_OTHER: u32 = 6
CK_PANIC: u32 = 7  // a Rust panic (msg)
FRAMES_MAX: usize = 32
```

- **`struct CrashInfo<'a>`**
  what the crash handler knows (the CRASHINFO record of ASMLIB)
  - `code: u32` -- Windows exception code / Linux signal number (panic: 0)
  - `kind: u32` -- CK_\*
  - `access: u32` -- access violations: 0 read, 1 write, 8 execute, 2 unknown
  - `addr: u64` -- data address of an access violation / bus error (0 = none)
  - `ip: u64` -- instruction pointer
  - `base: u64` -- image base: offset = address - base (Linux 0: the .map lists addresses)
  - `code0: u64` -- the executable code: code0..code1
  - `code1: u64`
  - `regs: [u64; 17]` -- rax rbx rcx rdx rsi rdi rbp rsp r8 .. r15 rip
  - `frames: [u64; FRAMES_MAX]` -- the call chain: return addresses, innermost first (plat)
  - `nframes: u32`
  - `msg: &'a str` -- CK_PANIC: the message

**`impl CrashInfo<'_>`**

- **`const fn empty() -> Self`**

- **`type CrashHook = fn(&CrashInfo)`**

- **`fn set_hook(f: Option<CrashHook>)`**
  install (Some) or remove (None) the crash hook  [plat_crash_hook]

- **`fn set_pre_hook(f: Option<CrashHook>)`**
  install (Some) or remove (None) the library's hook that runs before the app's

- **`fn busy() -> bool`**
  a crash is being reported (a second one ends the process at once)

- **`fn report(info: &CrashInfo) -> !`**
  run the hook once, then exit(3)

- **`struct StackText<const N: usize>`**
  formatting into a fixed buffer (overflow is cut off)

**`impl<const N: usize> StackText<N>`**

- **`const fn new() -> Self`**
- **`fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8]`**
- **`fn as_str(&self) -> &str`**

### `rt/fx.rs`

Source: [`lib/rt/fx.rs`](../lib/rt/fx.rs)

```text
fx -- scalar SSE float operations with exactly the semantics the assembly uses
(cvttss2si, cvtss2si with round-half-even, sqrtss, minss, maxss), so float results
are bit-identical to ASMLIB.  Rust never fuses a multiply and an add into an FMA.
```

- **`fn cvtt(x: f32) -> i32`**
  cvttss2si: truncate towards zero (0x80000000 for NaN / out of range)

- **`fn cvt(x: f32) -> i32`**
  cvtss2si: round to nearest, ties to even (the default MXCSR mode)

- **`fn sqrt(x: f32) -> f32`**

- **`fn minss(a: f32, b: f32) -> f32`**
  minss a, b: a &lt; b ? a : b (b when unordered)

- **`fn maxss(a: f32, b: f32) -> f32`**
  maxss a, b: a > b ? a : b (b when unordered)

- **`fn floor_i(x: f32) -> i32`**
  floor / ceil the way f_floor / f_ceil do it: truncate, then step if needed

- **`fn ceil_i(x: f32) -> i32`**

- **`fn div255(x: u32) -> u32`**
  round(x / 255) for x in 0..=65025: ((x + 128) \* 257) >> 16 (pmulhuw), equal to
  (x + 128 + ((x + 128) >> 8)) >> 8

- **`fn sqrtd(x: f64) -> f64`**
  sqrtsd

- **`fn maxsd(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  maxsd a, b: a > b ? a : b (b when unordered)

- **`fn minsd(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64`**
  minsd a, b: a &lt; b ? a : b (b when unordered)

- **`fn cvttd(x: f64) -> i32`**
  cvttsd2si (32-bit): truncate towards zero (0x80000000 for NaN / out of range)

- **`fn cvtd(x: f64) -> i32`**
  cvtsd2si (32-bit): round to nearest even (0x80000000 for NaN / out of range)

- **`fn cvtd64(x: f64) -> i64`**
  cvtsd2si (64-bit): round to nearest even (i64::MIN for NaN / out of range)

- **`fn cvttd64(x: f64) -> i64`**
  cvttsd2si (64-bit): truncate (i64::MIN for NaN / out of range)

### `rt/x87.rs`

Source: [`lib/rt/x87.rs`](../lib/rt/x87.rs)

```text
x87 -- the extended-precision steps of the decimal <-> double conversions   [src/core/ini.s]

  scale(m, e) -> f64          m * 10^e (e < 0: m / 10^-e), one rounding to double  (f64_parse)
  scale_round(v, k) -> i64    round(v * 10^k) (k < 0: v / 10^-k), to nearest       (f64_format)
  log10_round(v) -> i32       round(log10 v) as fyl2x computes it                  (f64_format)
  pow(x, y) -> f64            x^y as fx_pow computes it (R6-icc)       [src/fx/fx_lut.s]
  exp2 / log2 / cos / sin     fx_exp2 / fx_log2 / fx_cos / fx_sin (r10-fx)  [src/fx/fx_lut.s]
  rz_exp2 / rz_log2           PaintCraft's rz_exp2 / rz_log2 (pn-ui; other rounding)  [dlg_rotzoom.s]

ASMLIB computes these on the x87 unit with 64-bit precision and round to nearest (the
control word is saved and restored in every call), 10^n as fld1 times the double table
1e0..1e22 (1e22 repeated for larger n).  The same instructions run here, so the text a
double is written as and the double a text reads as are bit-identical to the assembly.
```

- **`fn scale(m: u64, e: i32) -> f64`**
  m \* 10^e or m / 10^-e (m &lt; 2^63), rounded once to double  [f64_parse .fp_calc]

- **`fn scale_round(v: f64, k: i32) -> i64`**
  frndint(v \* 10^k) or frndint(v / 10^-k) as a 64-bit integer  [f64_format .ff_scale]

- **`fn log10_round(v: f64) -> i32`**
  fldlg2 / fyl2x / fistp: log10 v rounded to the nearest integer  [f64_format]

- **`fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64`**
  fpatan: atan2(y, x) on the x87 unit, rounded once to double (the precision control does
  not apply to fpatan)  [pathdata.s pd_atan2, dash.s dc_atan2]

- **`fn sincos(x: f64) -> (f64, f64)`**
  fsincos: (cos x, sin x) on the x87 unit, each rounded once to double (the precision
  control does not apply to fsincos)  [ui_value.s deg_sincos]

- **`fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64`**
  fx_pow: x^y -- NaN when x or y is NaN, 1 for y == 0, 0 for x &lt;= 0, x for y == 1, else
  2^(y log2 x) on the x87 unit with 64-bit precision and round to nearest (fyl2x, then
  frndint / f2xm1 / fscale), rounded once to double  [fx_lut.s fx_pow]

- **`fn rz_log2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  fyl2x with y = 1: log2(x) on the x87 unit, rounded once to double (fyl2x is not subject
  to the precision control)  [PaintCraft dlg_rotzoom.s rz_log2]

- **`fn rz_exp2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  2^x as rz_exp2 computes it (|x| &lt; 2^30): i = cvtsd2si x, f = x - i (SSE), then on the x87
  unit f2xm1 f, + 1 (faddp: rounded by the process's precision control, as in the
  assembly), fscale by i, rounded to double  [PaintCraft dlg_rotzoom.s rz_exp2]

```text
Scalar IEEE-754 operations matching the native SSE conversion and operand-selection
rules. Integer square root avoids libm imports and gives correctly rounded results.
```

### `rt/portable/math.rs`

Source: [`lib/rt/portable/math.rs`](../lib/rt/portable/math.rs)

```text
Portable replacement for the native x87 entry points. Decimal scaling emulates the
x87 64-bit significand after each multiply/divide. Transcendentals use explicit scalar
binary64 series; native x87 remains unchanged and is the comparison reference.
```

- **`fn scale(m: u64, e: i32) -> f64`**
  Decimal scaling with the same 64-bit significand intermediate rounding as x87.

- **`fn scale_round(v: f64, k: i32) -> i64`**
  Nearest-even integer after decimal scaling, including native indefinite overflow.

- **`fn log10_round(v: f64) -> i32`**
  Nearest integer decimal logarithm; nonpositive inputs produce the SSE indefinite value.

- **`fn log2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Binary logarithm using a normalized mantissa and a convergent atanh series.

- **`fn exp2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Platform-independent base-two exponent; finite underflow rounds into subnormals.

- **`fn rz_log2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Existing rotation/zoom base-two logarithm API.

- **`fn rz_exp2(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Existing rotation/zoom base-two exponent API.

- **`fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64`**
  Effect power contract: y=0 yields 1, nonpositive bases yield 0, NaNs propagate canonically.

- **`fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64`**
  Quadrant-aware arctangent, including signed zeros and infinite operands.

- **`fn sincos(x: f64) -> (f64, f64)`**
  Cosine and sine with shared quadrant reduction; return order matches the x87 API.

- **`fn cos(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Scalar cosine using the common angle reduction.

- **`fn sin(x: f64) -> f64`**
  Scalar sine using the common angle reduction.

## plugin

*the PaintCraft plugin ABI for plugins written in Rust* -- crate root [`lib/plugin/lib.rs`](../lib/plugin/lib.rs)

```text
plugin -- the PaintCraft plugin ABI for plugins written in Rust (no_std cdylib, no imports)
                    [ASMLIB/inc/plugin.inc; docs apps/PaintCraft/docs/PLUGINS.md, plugins/README.md]

A plugin is a library exporting one function, pn_plugin_query(PNAPI*) -> PLUGININFO*, that
PaintCraft (the Rust and the assembly build alike) loads from <root>/Effects, FileTypes or
Shapes.  It is linked against nothing: no rt, no plat, no system library -- the host's
functions come through the PNAPI table.  This crate is all a plugin depends on (+ core):

  abi       the records of plugin.inc / fx.inc / img.inc as #[repr(C)] types (layouts
            asserted): PnApi, PluginInfo, FxDesc, FxProp, FtDesc, ShapeDesc, FxArgs,
            Surface, Job, ImgDec, ImgMeta, ImgOpt; their const constructors
  api       the host table after pn_plugin_query (api()): Block (a PA_ALLOC buffer),
            parallel_for, hash32, log / log!, nthreads; PnAlloc (opt-in global allocator)
  fx        Effect (render / prepare of an effect or adjustment) and its safe view Fx
            (source rows, the destination rows of the ROI, parameters, cancel polling)
  ft        FileType (probe / decode / encode of a file type): Decoder, Image
  mem       memcpy / memmove / memset / memcmp / bcmp (and the MSVC support symbols) for
            core, in assembly so that they never become exports

The unsafe parts (raw host records, the trampolines the host calls) live here; a plugin's
own code stays safe: `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, with entry!() as its one exception (the
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] export).  Minimal plugin (see plugins/sepiastr):

  #![no_std]
  #![deny(unsafe_code)]
  use plugin::*;
  struct Sepia;
  impl Effect for Sepia {
      type Aux = ();
      fn render(fx: &mut Fx, _: Option<&()>) -> Result<(), i32> { ... }
  }
  static PROPS: [FxProp; 1] = [FxProp::int(0, c"Stärke", 0.0, 100.0, 60.0)];
  static FX: FxDesc = FxDesc::new::<Sepia>(c"Sepia-Stärke", FXF_ADJ, FXC_ADJUST, &PROPS);
  static FX_LIST: [&FxDesc; 1] = [&FX];
  static INFO: PluginInfo = PluginInfo::new(c"Sepia-Stärke (Beispiel)", c"1.0").effects(&FX_LIST);
  fn query(_: &'static PnApi) -> Option<&'static PluginInfo> { Some(&INFO) }
  plugin::entry!(query);
  #[panic_handler]
  fn panic(info: &core::panic::PanicInfo) -> ! { plugin::panic(info) }

Panics: `plugin::panic` logs "panic at FILE:LINE" through PA_LOG and executes ud2,
`plugin::trap` only executes ud2 -- the host's crash guard catches it and disables the plugin
("Absturz in render (ungültiger Befehl ...)"), like any other fault inside plugin code.

Build: python build_rs.py plugin [NAME] (section rust-plugin: cdylib, panic=abort, fat LTO,
linked against nothing, checked like PaintCraft's loader checks it).
```
